title: Native diagram renderers (bmc, nine_box, porters, swot, pyramid) refuse the 12pt gate on small content areas
description:
Split from go-slide-creator-k3eb3 (which now covers shape_grid PATTERNS only). Native diagram examples refuse with `unreadable generated text: body text renders at N pt`: examples/diagrams/business_model_canvas.json on 9/10 templates (2.0-5.6pt body; only business-template passes), nine_box_talent.json 6/10 incl. local p-style (3.0-6.2pt), porters_five_forces.json 4/10 (abstract, modern, modern-template, modern-yellow), swot.json 3/10, pyramid.json abstract only. The native renderers pack cell bullet text into the `content` body area and autofit below the floor; abstract has the smallest body (687x294pt vs 828x349 / 899x360 p-style).
Repro: j2p generate -json examples/diagrams/business_model_canvas.json -template midnight-blue -templates-dir templates -output /tmp/x.
Fix: in the native diagram renderers (internal/generator diagram code for bmc/nine_box/porters/swot/pyramid) size the text model against the actual cell area at the 12pt floor: reduce per-cell text (bullets -> fewer/shorter lines), reduce insets for diagram cells if the 0.5 cm uniform margin is what breaks them, or refuse at validate time with a BODY_TOO_LONG-style finding naming the cell and the overflow. Trim the shipped example content only where it is unreasonably dense, and never below what a real user would put in a BMC cell. Do NOT loosen the 12pt gate. Also make `j2p validate --fit-report` predict this refusal (see go-slide-creator-y72c3; coordinate if the same agent owns both).
Verify: all five examples generate on all 10 templates incl. p-style with zero refusals; render bmc on abstract and p-style and eyeball readability; TestShippedExamplesValidate passes.
close_reason: Native BMC/SWOT/nine-box/Porters/pyramid renderers now size cells to text measured with the writer autofit estimator (BMC shared-shrink row and stack splits and wrapped header bands, measured SWOT header, Porters box heights, adaptive pyramid apex, header-seam inset, 2pt list spacing); BMC example trimmed to 3 items in stacked and bottom cells. All five examples generate on all 10 templates incl p-style with zero refusals. Gate unchanged. Commit 4114bebb on worktree-agent-abf00405ecb0f8bbe.

title: shape_grid.columns unbounded: MaxInt64/1e308 panics, 5e7 allocates 900 MB, 2e9 OOMs the MCP server
description:
cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go:1455-1457 parses columns as float64 then int(n) (saturates to MaxInt64 for 1e308); internal/shapegrid/grid.go:329-333 ResolveColumns only checks v>=1; grid.go:822-830 equalSplit does make([]float64, n) -> `panic: makeslice: len out of range`. columns:50000000 allocates 888 MB silently; columns:2e9 would OOM-kill a long-lived `json2pptx mcp` from a single validate_input call (argSizeMiddleware counts bytes only).
Repro: `j2p validate -fit-report` with shape_grid.columns = 9223372036854775807 / 1e308 / 50000000.
Fix: in resolveColumnsDTO validate finite, integral, 1 <= n <= 24 (pick a realistic max; check patterns' largest column count) BEFORE int(); add the same ceiling in shapegrid.ResolveColumns for library callers; emit INVALID_VALUE with the range; tests for MaxInt64, 1e308, NaN, negative, 25.
close_reason: Fixed on branch worktree-agent-a7f599907bab48bff (d75c98bb, c17c26f7): shapegrid.ColumnCount rejects NaN/Inf/fractions/out of 1..MaxColumns(24) before int(); ResolveColumns caps counts and arrays; validate reports INVALID_GRID with the range; compose/fit column inference never sizes from an invalid count. Repros MaxInt64/1e308/5e7/-5 now rc=1 at ~35MB RSS (was panic / 850MB). Tests for MaxInt64, 1e308, NaN, Inf, negative, 0, 2.5, 25, 5e7.

title: Shipped examples refuse on the 12pt readability gate (native diagrams + next-steps on abstract)
description:
Full 59 examples x 10 templates sweep (incl. local p-style): 24 refusals, all `generation refused: unreadable generated text: <element> renders at N pt, below the 12pt minimum for viewing_mode present`, no PPTX written. Native diagram examples: examples/diagrams/business_model_canvas.json refuses on 9/10 templates (2.0-5.6pt body), nine_box_talent.json 6/10 incl. p-style, porters_five_forces.json 4/10, swot.json 3/10, pyramid.json abstract only. Pattern: examples/patterns-smoke.json slide 29 (next-steps card-title 9.4pt = 12pt run x stored autofit 78%) on abstract.
CI job template-pattern-matrix is red for the same class: agenda-with-images/{abstract,modern}, bmc-canvas/abstract, chart-insights-split/abstract, exec-summary/abstract, metric-list/abstract, next-steps/abstract, scqa-summary/abstract, state-shift-hub on 7 templates (card-title 9.8-11.8pt, autofit 70-98%).
Repro: `j2p generate -json examples/diagrams/business_model_canvas.json -template midnight-blue -templates-dir templates -output /tmp/x`; `j2p generate -json examples/patterns-smoke.json -template abstract ...`.
Fix options (decide per case, do not weaken the 12pt floor): reduce the native diagram body text density / font model so BMC/nine-box/porters/swot fit at 12pt in the smallest content area (abstract/modern), or trim the shipped example content; for patterns, the card-title runs get a stored autofit <100% - find why the title shrinks (recent inset/margin changes in internal/patterns, internal/shapegrid) and make the pattern emit a readable size or refuse at validate time. tests/.../template_pattern_matrix_test.go must go green on all templates; the full example x template sweep must produce 0 refusals.

ROOT CAUSE (bisected): gate = reportGridReadability internal/generator/grid_readability.go:17-66 (12pt floor internal/tokens/typography.go:56-61; refusal wrap singlepass.go:349). Commit 2bafa895 landed the gate with state-shift-hub/abstract already violating; 34d9e281 (uniform 0.5 cm text margin, internal/pptx/shape_text_inset.go:32 ShapeTextInsetEMU=180000 = 14.17pt/side) made it systemic: two margins eat 28.3pt per row, a 14/12pt title+body pair needs ~32.4pt clear, so any row under ~61pt shrinks. abstract is worst (content body 687x294pt vs 828x349 on others, 899x360 p-style). state-shift-hub fails everywhere because internal/patterns/state_shift_hub.go:329 sizes minItem with a ONE-LINE non-wrapping probe (writtenFitHeightPt(sshItemCell('Stage','One line',..), w/2, 0)) while exemplar bodies wrap to 2 lines, and lay.pitch is clamped by sshMaxPitchPt (:334) -> row max_height 67pt for 3 lines + 28pt margins. Measured: state-shift-hub/warm-coral cell 67pt, text area 38.7pt, scale 84%; agenda-with-images/abstract 50.6pt cell, 22.3pt area, 70%; exec-summary/abstract 19.4pt area, 82%; next-steps/abstract 86%; metric-list/abstract 94%; bmc-canvas/abstract 92%.
FIX (pattern-side, correct): patterns that compute a row pitch must size against WRAPPED content at the real column width and never emit a row max_height below their own writtenFitHeightPt for the longest cell (content_fit_text.go:184-214 already includes 2*defaultShapeInsetTBPt). state_shift_hub.go:326-336: compute minItem as max over pairs of writtenFitHeightPt(sshItemCell(title, before/after), colW, 0) with the real column width and let lay.pitch grow (raise/drop sshMaxPitchPt for n<=4) before shrinking the hub. agenda-with-images, exec-summary, metric-list, next-steps, scqa-summary, bmc-canvas, chart-insights-split: same rule. When the content area cannot hold N rows at that height, emit BODY_TOO_LONG/density finding at expand time instead of letting the writer autofit below the floor. Do NOT loosen grid_readability.go or the 12pt floor. Shortening exemplars alone is not acceptable (hides the bug). Native diagrams are split out to a separate bead (see prerelease label) - this bead is PATTERNS only.
VERIFY: go test -run TemplatePatternMatrix ./cmd/json2pptx/ -count=1 -timeout=10m (incl. p-style); generate examples/patterns-smoke.json on abstract; re-run TestSchemaMaxima|TestContentSizedPatterns|TestCLIExtremeSchemaPatterns; full examples x templates sweep 0 refusals.
close_reason: Pattern side fixed on branch worktree-agent-a284bdf569136a280 commit 5a758a53. Eight patterns now size rows to the writer fit of the exact cell text at real column widths (state-shift-hub item need at the arc frame width with gaps, hub and title giving way; exec-summary, metric-list, next-steps written-fit rows plus a 12pt floor step; bmc-canvas and scqa-summary need-floored flex rows; agenda-with-images title-cell floors plus 12pt title step) and report measured BODY_TOO_LONG when the template area cannot hold them. Over-budget exemplars trimmed to fit the 294pt abstract area. Gate and 12pt floor untouched. Verified TemplatePatternMatrix all cells green incl p-style, patterns-smoke generates on abstract and p-style, schema maxima and content-sized tests green, short suite and make lint clean. Native diagram refusals are tracked separately.

title: Panic in text shaping on bidi-override + emoji + combining-mark input
description:
internal/textfit/textfit.go:390 wrapTextLine -> canvas.NewTextLine -> tdewolff/canvas text/harfbuzz.go:91 panics `slice bounds out of range [2:1]` when text starts with U+202E U+1F600 U+0301 (RTL override + emoji + combining mark). Reaches CLI validate/generate (exit 2 + stack), HTTP /api/v1/convert (500 PANIC_RECOVERED), MCP (RENDER.INTERNAL). Any measured text field (title, subtitle, body, bullets, shape_grid cell) triggers it.
Repro: scratchpad review-sec/shrink_RLO_EMOJI_COMB.json -> `j2p validate -fit-report <file>`.
Fix: (a) wrap every canvas.NewTextLine call site in internal/textfit (wrapTextLine, MeasureRun, estimateTextHeight) with a recover() fallback to an average-glyph-width estimate; (b) strip/neutralise Unicode bidi controls (U+202A-U+202E, U+2066-U+2069) and U+FEFF at the input boundary (DecodeStrictPresentation / deckinput) with a diagnostic; add a regression test with the 3-rune prefix in each text field kind.
close_reason: Fixed on branch worktree-agent-a7f599907bab48bff (8f6d9ae8, e3aa0b7b): textfit.LineWidthMM recover() guard with 0.55em-per-rune fallback on every NewTextLine measurement (textfit, generator footer/page number), svggen DrawText/MeasureText guarded; internal/bidisafe strips U+202A-202E, U+2066-2069, U+FEFF at PresentationInput decode and HTTP convert with INPUT_CONTROL_CHARS_REMOVED (info). Old binary: 5 CLI panics over 82 repros, MCP RENDER.INTERNAL, HTTP 500 PANIC_RECOVERED; new: 0 / success / 200. Regression tests for title, subtitle, body, bullets, shape_grid cell, MCP validate_input + generate, HTTP convert.

title: Coverage CI test package exceeds 25-minute timeout
description:
DIAGNOSIS: CI "Test with coverage" runs go test ./... -short -v -race -coverprofile -timeout=25m; cmd/json2pptx hit 1500.6s (also at 33127c53). NOT a hang: cumulative slowness. Last green (3a0ef2e7) took 1301s for this package; locally -short -race passes in 1247s (1996 tests). The sequential phase grew ~1150s -> ~1420s: TestCLIExtremeSchemaPatternsCannotPublishTinyText +23s (119s), TestSchemaMaximaMeasurementsMatchWrittenRuns +21s (68s), TestCalibrationRanking +17s, TestShippedExamplesValidate +16s (80s), TestPatternAndShapeGridFormsAgree +9s, TestComputeCellBudgets_AllPatternsAllTemplates +8s, TestContentSizedPatterns_ExemplarHasNoLayoutFindings +7s, plus 41 new tests (+45s). None of the 13 heaviest tests checks testing.Short(); only 12 files use t.Parallel(). Three tests shell out to go build (audit_palette_test.go:220, cli_parity_test.go:139, patterns_cmd_test.go:21) and tests/quality/quality_test.go:212 builds again.

FIX (do all three): (1) .github/workflows/ci.yml Test with coverage: run cmd/json2pptx as its own step with -timeout=40m and the remaining packages separately, merge coverage (go tool covdata or gocovmerge); (2) add t.Parallel() to the eight sequential sweeps (TestCLIExtremeSchemaPatternsCannotPublishTinyText, TestSchemaMaximaMeasurementsMatchWrittenRuns, TestShippedExamplesValidate, TestCalibrationRanking, TestTemplateDiscoveryPlaceholderParity, TestFitAndReadabilityUseDeckRhythmBounds, TestMCPGenerateStrictFit, TestMCPGetDataFormatHints) after confirming they only write to t.TempDir(); share one built binary per package via TestMain/sync.Once; (3) gate cross-template sweeps behind testing.Short() where a dedicated CI job (template-pattern-matrix etc.) already covers them.

VERIFY: go test -short -race -json ./cmd/json2pptx -count=1 -timeout=40m; per-test timings before/after; package must sit well under 1000s.
acceptance_criteria: The coverage test job finishes under its configured timeout in CI on repeated runs; retain meaningful test coverage and the >=70% project threshold.
notes: Fix landed on branch worktree-agent-a3fd759bd2f670613 (commit 78b19ef3): shared test binary via sync.Once/TestMain (cmd/json2pptx 17 callers, tests/quality 2), t.Parallel on the eight named sweeps, CI splits cmd/json2pptx into its own -timeout=40m coverage step and merges profiles. Local go test -short -race ./cmd/json2pptx: 842s package wall (was 1247s), 2069 tests. Left open until the split coverage job is observed green in CI. One earlier local -race run hung in a forked child during exec from svg.go:241 (darwin fork under -race with parallel subprocess spawning); did not recur on the rerun, watch for it.
close_reason: CI run 36475916802 on main (3ae1872c) green: test job passes with cmd/json2pptx as its own -race coverage step (-timeout=40m), other packages separate, coverage merged. Locally 842s vs 1500s timeout before.

title: Contrast preflight disagrees with generated slide backgrounds in corpus
description:
DIAGNOSIS (bisected: passes at 971d4d24, fails at c527f034): TestContrastParityCorpus (cmd/json2pptx/contrast_parity_corpus_test.go:88) compares contrast_predicted from collectFitFindings (validate path) with GenResult.ContrastSwaps from RunPresentation. 21 subtests fail (quote-cluster s1-2, patterns-smoke s15, template-qa-deck s16 on abstract, blue-corporate, business-template, forest-green, modern-template, modern-yellow, warm-coral). Predicted background is always #EBEBEB; actual is the template lt2 (#E7E6E6 / #DCD8DC / #FBE9E7) or no swap at all.

ROOT CAUSE: c527f034 introduced surfacePairJSON (internal/patterns/neutral_surface.go:104-123; used by quote-cluster, card-grid, comparison-2col, swimlane, capability-heatmap) which calls ctx.ResolveSurface -> ResolveSurface(role, c.Metadata, default) (overrides.go:348). Every bundled template declares surface_tints {subtle: lt2, paper: lt1} in ppt/go-slide-creator-metadata.json (p-style has none, so it passes). The GENERATE path passes Metadata (json_mode.go:1045,1073) so the fill is lt2; the VALIDATE/preflight path never has it: validate.go:222 fitReportGeometry discards the metadata return, collectFitFindings (fit_findings_collect.go:38) takes only *types.ThemeInfo, and the three preflight ExpandContexts (validate_grid_diagrams.go:57, fit_findings_collect.go:2089, fit_pattern_expansion.go:92) set Theme but no Metadata -> surfacePairJSON falls to the dk1-tint default (#EBEBEB). SemanticAccents had the same problem earlier and was solved by mirroring into ThemeInfo (json_mode.go:351-353); SurfaceTints was not mirrored.

FIX (verified in a scratch worktree; all 21 go green): (1) internal/types/template.go:396 add SurfaceTints map[string]string next to SemanticAccents in ThemeInfo; (2) cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go:353 add theme.SurfaceTints = metadata.SurfaceTints; (3) internal/patterns/pattern.go:175 ExpandContext.ResolveSurface: if c.Metadata == nil && len(c.Theme.SurfaceTints) > 0, resolve via &types.TemplateMetadata{SurfaceTints: c.Theme.SurfaceTints}. Add a unit test that preflight and generate resolve the same surface for a template with surface_tints.

VERIFY: go test -tags=integration -run TestContrastParityCorpus ./cmd/json2pptx/ -count=1 -timeout=20m (includes p-style). Zero decision-set mismatch. patterns-smoke/abstract still refuses until go-slide-creator-k3eb3 is fixed.
acceptance_criteria: TestContrastParityCorpus passes on the full template corpus and local ignored p-style.pptx; CI corpus-headless passes without weakening contrast checks.
close_reason: Mirrored surface_tints into ThemeInfo.SurfaceTints (json_mode.go) and made ExpandContext.ResolveSurface fall back to it when Metadata is nil, so validate/fit-report preflight resolves the same neutral surface as generation. Added unit test TestExpandContextResolveSurface_PreflightMatchesGenerate. TestContrastParityCorpus: zero decision-set mismatch across the corpus incl p-style; only patterns-smoke/abstract still fails with the 12pt readability refusal owned by go-slide-creator-k3eb3.

title: reduce_text never applies to bullets or shape_grid cells, so the worst text defects have no repair path
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: quality-signal (finding refs q.3).

WHAT
B01 (5 slides of 9 giant bullets): BODY_TOO_LONG's own next_tool_call is repair_slide{kind:reduce_text, params:{current_words:333, max_words:80}}. Applied verbatim it returns applied:false 'no text content found to reduce on this slide' for every slide, because reduce_text only targets `text` items, not `bullets`. B02 (30 real fit_overflow P0s in a shape_grid): propose_repairs maps 60/60 findings to reduce_text and repair_slides_batch applies 0/60 with the same message — the correct kind would be reduce_cell_text with a cell_path, which propose_repairs knows how to emit only when a visual finding carries a bbox. title: submit_visual_review accepts images from any deck, so the completion status can be forged in one call
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: quality-signal (finding refs q.5).

WHAT
submit_visual_review is the documented completion path when no vision provider is configured, and the server instructions make 'inspect every rendered image yourself' the only definition of done. I submitted a review of B08 (the all-lorem deck, score 99) with all six slides pointing at slide-01.png, and then a second review with six images taken from a completely different deck (G1). Both returned {ok:true, status:'visually_reviewed_current_revision', verdict:'approved'}. Only the PPTX sha256 is validated; the per-slide image is never matched against the artifact's own rendered pixels, so the entire completion contract reduces to an honour system that a cost-minimising agent will short-circuit. Combined with the deletion path (gutting every shape_grid cell text turned B02 from gate-FAIL into gate-PASS and then into visually_reviewed_current_revision), the 'done' signal can be manufactured in two tool calls.

WHERE
cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go (submit_visual_review handler), ReviewRecord.ValidateCompletion; skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md completion protocol; server instructions in cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go (instructions string)

HOW
Bind the review to the artifact's own pixels: render (or reuse the cached render of) each slide of pptx_revision server-side and require each submitted image_sha256 to equal the rendered slide's hash for that index (the render cache already keys by content hash). Reject duplicate hashes across slides. When the images cannot be verified, downgrade the status to 'reviewed_unverified_images' rather than the completion status.

VERIFY
submit_visual_review with slides[i].image_path all equal, or from another deck, must return INVALID_PARAMETER / status 'draft_needs_visual_review'; the honest path (render_deck_thumbnails then submit the returned paths) must still succeed.

No cached render -> unverifiable, never a rejection.

title: fit_overflow (the only gate-blocking code) is a false positive: it measures text before wrap/autofit
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: quality-signal (finding refs q.1).

WHAT
fit_overflow is action=refuse (weight 25) and is the dominant reason any deck fails the gate. It fires on cells whose text renders perfectly. examples/business-model-canvas.json scores 58 and fails the gate with 4 refuse findings ('text needs 114 chars @ 12pt; cell allows 78 (146% of capacity)'), but the render shows every bullet of those cells fully visible with whitespace left over (montage/bmc_zoom.png: KEY ACTIVITIES lists 4 bullets, nothing clipped). examples/varied-pitch-deck.json fails the gate solely on 'text needs 33 chars @ 120pt; cell allows 12 (275%)' — that is the '3.2x' hero-number slide, which renders correctly (montage/vpd_s12.png). The check appears to compare total characters against a single-line capacity at the authored point size rather than measuring the wrapped block against the cell height after autofit/shrink. Effect on agents: the project's own showcase decks are refused, and an agent told 'max_p0_findings 0' will delete real content to clear a finding that describes nothing.

WHERE
cmd/json2pptx/fit_findings_collect.go (fit_overflow emission), internal/textfit; finding meta internal/patterns/finding_meta.go (fit_overflow remediation); consumers internal/visualqa/deterministic/checker.go:166 (P0 counting)

HOW
Measure the same way the renderer does: wrap the text at the cell's available width with the real font metrics, sum line heights at the post-autofit size, and only emit fit_overflow when the wrapped block exceeds the cell height (or when autofit has bottomed out). Keep the char-budget heuristic as an `info` hint at most. Add a regression test over examples/business-model-canvas.json and examples/varied-pitch-deck.json asserting zero refuse findings.

fit_overflow now measures the wrapped block against the cell height, and only refuses text that is actually clipped.

Root cause: the shape_grid density model compared a character COUNT against a capacity computed at ONE font size — the largest paragraph in the cell (charsPerLine x maxLines). Two failure modes followed: mixed-size cells were budgeted at their display size, and any cell over the char budget was refused even though the renderer's <a:normAutofit/> shrinks text to fit.

Implementation (internal/textcapacity):
- extractCellText -> extractCellParagraphs: paragraphs keep their OWN effective size (cell size, then per-paragraph size, each floored to the renderer minimum).
- measuredDensity(): wraps each paragraph at its own size via textfit.MeasureRun, sums lines x size x 1.2, and reports DensityPct = required height / available height. New Density fields RequiredHeightPt, AvailableHeightPt, Lines, AutofitScale, Fits.
- Reported FontPt is the DOMINANT size (most characters), not the largest; MaxChars stays as a derived sizing hint at that size (it is the budget reduce_cell_text uses).
- Unsized cells are measured at shapegrid.DefaultTextSizePt (14pt, newly exported) instead of the legacy 11pt budget default — measuring at 11pt under-measured every unsized cell by 27%.
- AutofitScaleFor/AutofitScale: the single implementation of the shrink prediction (2% steps to a 20% floor). cmd/json2pptx/readability_findings.go's predictedAutofitScale now delegates to it, so the overflow verdict and the readability verdict cannot disagree about the rendered size.

- fit_overflow (error/refuse) only when !Fits — clipped even at the smallest shrink. Message: 'text needs Npt of height in a cell that offers Mpt (D% at Ppt); even the renderer's smallest autofit shrink leaves it clipped'. RequiredPt/AllocatedPt now carry the measured heights.
- The old >130%/>110% char bands are gone: a cell the renderer shrinks into renders every word. The size that results is reported by TEXT_BELOW_READABLE_MIN (review), whose grid-cell fix now carries reduce_cell_text{cell_path, max_chars} instead of the unreachable reduce_text.

title: score_deck's gated score does not track deck quality (Spearman +0.17); 14 of 16 test decks pass
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: quality-signal (finding refs q.0).

WHAT
I built 16 calibration decks (3 good, 3 mediocre, 10 with one dominant defect each), rendered them, graded them blind from the montages, then ran every signal. score_deck.overall_score correlates with the human grade at Spearman +0.17 — essentially noise. 14/16 decks pass quality_gate, including: B08 (every slide lorem ipsum / 'Click to add title' / 'XX%') score 99 PASS; B09 (8 identical kpi-3up slides) 100 PASS; B10 (4 slides with no title) 100 PASS; B03 (5 slides carrying one 1-word bullet) 100 PASS; M1 (7 identical all-bullet slides) 100 PASS. The three genuinely good decks score 97-99 — i.e. the good and the junk are within 2 points of each other. By contrast inspect_slide_images (vision) correlates at +0.93. An agent that optimizes the gated number therefore ships junk confidently. The score is 100 - sum(severity weights), so it only measures the codes that happen to exist; nothing in the formula measures content substance, emptiness on placeholder slides, title presence, chart legibility, or monotony (composition is computed and then discarded, see separate finding).

WHERE
internal/visualqa/deterministic/checker.go:117-215 (QualityGate, DefaultQualityGateCriteria, EvaluateQualityGate), checker.go:251/344 (ScoreFromFindings*), cmd/json2pptx/mcp_score_deck.go:200-230; skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md:457-473 ('Stop when the quality gate passes')

HOW
Treat the gate as a *content+layout* gate, not a fit-findings aggregator. (a) Add blocking codes for the defect classes that currently produce zero findings: WEAK_CONTENT on the raw path (see separate finding), MISSING_TITLE, chart category overload, deck monotony (fold composition in). (b) Stop letting a deck reach 97-100 with unresolved 'review' findings on more than N slides: add a problem_slides_count criterion to QualityGateCriteria. Three independent defects produced that ordering:

2. Bullet overflow drove the structurally correct layout to zero: Two Content's 3-per-column capacity vs 8 insights.
3. penalizeNarrowDiagramSlot subtracted 0.3 from the two-column layout for placing the diagram in a half-width column — the exact arrangement the slide asked for — pushing it below One Content, which drops the second column's content entirely.

- capacityOverflowFloor (0.35): once a layout IS structurally sufficient, bullet overflow cannot sink it below that — too much text in the right structure beats the right amount in the wrong one, and fit_overflow/TEXT_BELOW_READABLE_MIN report the overflow separately.
- penalizeChromeLayoutForContent (0.45): divider / title-slide / blank / closing layouts, and any layout with zero content placeholders, are penalised for content-bearing slides. Title and section SLIDES are exempt.

title: Cell capacity budgets a whole multi-size cell at its largest font, making expand_pattern density unusable as a gate
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: gallery (finding refs g.1).

WHAT
textcapacity.extractCellText() sums the characters of every paragraph in a cell but keeps only the LARGEST effective paragraph size as the cell font size. Patterns that mix one big number with small supporting lines therefore report absurd densities on slides that render perfectly: stat-hero with realistic content ('EUR2.4B' 120pt + 3 support lines at 18/14/10pt) reports max_chars=18, actual=164, density 911% 'overflow'; kpi-3up 171%, kpi-4up/5up 300%, card-grid 224%, hero-detail 564% - all visually clean (sheets/real.07.stat-hero.png, real.02.kpi-3up.png, real.20.card-grid.png). The inverse is just as bad: on the realistic deck 33 of 45 patterns report the majority of their cells 'underfilled'. SKILL.md:718 tells agents to call expand_pattern per pattern slide and 'confirm density is in the 60-110% optimal band before generating', so the only pattern-level text signal an agent has is noise in both directions - it drives agents to pad already-full slides and to cut text that fits.

WHERE
internal/textcapacity/textcapacity.go:285-297 (paragraph loop keeps max font size, sums all chars), consumers: cmd/json2pptx/mcp_expand_patterns.go (cell_budgets / capacity_warnings), skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md:718 and the `expand_pattern` row of the tool table

HOW
Budget per paragraph: for each paragraph compute lines = ceil(chars / charsPerLine(size, width)) and height = lines * size * lineSpacing; density = sum(paragraph heights) / cell height. Keep the aggregate `max_chars` field only as a derived hint (or drop it in favour of `required_height_pt` / `available_height_pt`). Recalibrate the 60-110% band against the four bundled templates with the realistic corpus in gallery/vals/*.real.json before re-publishing the number to agents.

VERIFY
`/Users/seb/projects/json2pptx/.claude/review-evidence/r2/j2p patterns expand stat-hero gallery/vals/stat-hero.real.json` must report density in the 60-110% band (currently 911%); same for kpi-3up (171%), card-grid (224%), hero-detail (564%). `python3 gallery/density.py` style sweep: no realistic-variant pattern should report >110% and no more than ~1/3 of cells should be 'underfilled'.

Cell capacity is now a per-paragraph height measurement, and the bands are recalibrated against the realistic corpus.

Root cause: textcapacity.extractCellText summed every paragraph's characters but kept only the LARGEST effective paragraph size as the cell font size, then compared the character count against charsPerLine x maxLines at that size. Any cell mixing a display number with small support lines was budgeted as if all its text were set at the display size.

Fixed together with go-slide-creator-lmpu (same root cause, opposite symptom) in commits d214dc4 and 2600642:
- extractCellParagraphs keeps each paragraph's own effective size; measuredDensity wraps each paragraph at ITS size via textfit.MeasureRun, sums lines x size x 1.2, and reports DensityPct = required height / available height. New fields RequiredHeightPt, AvailableHeightPt, Lines, AutofitScale, Fits (exactly the required_height_pt / available_height_pt the bead asked for).
- FontPt / max_chars are derived from the DOMINANT paragraph size (most characters), keeping max_chars as the sizing hint agents use while removing it from the density verdict.
- Unsized cells are measured at the renderer's own default (shapegrid.DefaultTextSizePt, 14pt, newly exported) rather than the legacy 11pt budget default.
- Bands recalibrated: textcapacity.UnderfilledPct 60 -> 35 (OverflowPct stays 110), published as constants consumed by fit_report, expand_pattern cell_budgets, rhythm and the docs. Justification measured, not guessed: on the 42-pattern realistic corpus the median cell fills 48% of its box height, so a 60% floor called the median well-authored slide underfilled.

title: DeckSpec: support deck chrome (footer, confidentiality, page numbers), per-slide source lines and speaker notes
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: capability-gaps, dogfood-a (finding refs cap.0, a.3).

WHAT
get_started('brief') and SKILL.md both send agents to render_deck_spec as THE path for a new deck, but DeckSpec has no way to attach speaker notes, a per-slide source/footnote line (except on chart_insight), or any deck-level chrome. `meta` accepts only {title, subtitle, archetype, template, audience, author, date}: `meta.chrome`, `meta.footer`, `meta.viewing_mode`, `meta.accent_strategy`, `meta.theme_override` and a top-level `chrome` all fail with 'unknown meta field' / 'unknown top-level field' (error severity, deck does not compile). A slide-level `speaker_notes` / `source` / `subtitle` is accepted but reported SEMANTIC_UNKNOWN_FIELD with the message 'its content is DROPPED'. Real consulting decks need a confidentiality line, client name, date, page numbers and speaker notes on essentially every page; today an agent on the recommended path silently ships none of them, and nothing in the response tells it that the capability exists one layer down. Raw PresentationInput supports all of it (b1 renders footer 'Strictly confidential — Acme Corp | Sept 2026', '2 / 7', and notesSlide2.xml).

ALSO REPORTED (dogfood-a: "DeckSpec cannot express deck chrome (confidentiality, page numbers) or per-slide sources - fast-path decks are unshippable to a board"): get_started's notes advertise top-level `chrome` (confidentiality / client / page numbers) and get_capabilities.features.deck_chrome says supported:true, but adding chrome to a DeckSpec fails with INPUT.SEMANTIC_UNKNOWN_FIELD 'unknown top-level field "chrome"; expected one of meta, slides'. DeckMeta carries client/date/author but nothing propagates them into a footer. Also only kind:chart_insight has a `source` field: the option matrix, financial case and risk slides cannot carry a source line. Result: the recommended path cannot produce a deck with a confidentiality mark, page numbers or source attribution - every board deck I have ever seen has all three. I had to abandon the DeckSpec path and rewrite the deck against generate_presentation to get them.

WHERE

Alternative/extra HOW from dogfood-a: Accept top-level `chrome` and `structure` in DeckSpec and pass them through to PresentationInput verbatim (they are already implemented raw-side); derive chrome defaults from meta (client_name, footer_date, confidentiality). Add an optional `source` string to every content-bearing kind and route it to slide.source.

title: Run measured text-fit + readability detectors on pattern slides (expand pattern first); today they skip ShapeGrid==nil
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: closure-audit-2, gallery (finding refs g.0, c2.2, c2.1).

WHAT
generateFitReport() and collectReadabilityFindings() both `continue` when slide.ShapeGrid == nil, but a pattern slide only gets a ShapeGrid at generation time. collectGeometryFindings() DOES expand the pattern (expandSlidePatternGrid) before measuring, which is why TEXT_EXCEEDS_SHAPE/SPARSE_FILL fire on pattern slides while the whole text-density/readability family never does. Proof with identical content: scqa-summary with 4 x 240-char strings (every value inside the pattern's own maxLength budget) authored as `pattern` -> `validate --fit-report` reports ONE finding (HEADLINE_TOO_LONG). The same content as the pattern's own expanded `shape_grid` (design_mode free) -> 4x FIT.fit_overflow severity=error ('text needs 937 chars @ 12pt; cell allows 384 (244% of capacity)') + 9 more suppressed. The rendered slide shows ~8pt body text (zoom/scqa_crop.png, 150dpi, 20px line pitch = ~9.6pt leading). Across the 45-pattern MAX deck, 20+ patterns land at 300-2100% of cell capacity and generate/validate report zero fit findings. This is the single biggest quality-signal gap: agents authoring through the recommended `pattern` surface get 'VALID, no issues found' on decks whose body text renders at 4-8pt.

ALSO REPORTED (closure-audit-2: "TEXT_BELOW_READABLE_MIN is never evaluated on pattern slides (collectReadabilityFindings skips ShapeGrid==nil)"): CLOSURE AUDIT of go-slide-creator-vbic (closed: 'viewing_mode present|read, TEXT_BELOW_READABLE_MIN from placeholders + shape-grid fit prediction'). collectReadabilityFindings iterates input.Slides and does `if slide.ShapeGrid == nil { continue }` — slide-level named patterns carry slide.Pattern, not ShapeGrid, so no pattern slide is ever checked. The bead's own motivating examples ('6pt KPI deltas and 9pt chevron descriptions') are pattern output. Proof: shrink2.json slide 0 (raw grid, 14pt shrunk to 11.5pt) → INPUT.TEXT_BELOW_READABLE_MIN; the identical text as card-grid → no finding at all.

ALSO REPORTED (closure-audit-2: "Pattern cell text is silently truncated mid-word with zero findings from validate, preview or generate"): CLOSURE AUDIT of go-slide-creator-vbic and go-slide-creator-t5gw. A card-grid slide whose 4 card bodies are 300 chars each (inside the pattern's own maxLength) renders with every card's text cut mid-word ('…fragmented tooling across t', no ellipsis) — see img/shrink2p-midnight-blue-1.png. validate --fit-report --verbose-fit prints 'Fit report: no issues found', validate_input returns 'no issues', and generate_presentation(fit_report=true) returns fit_findings: null. Nothing tells the agent the deck lost text. The same content authored as a raw shape_grid does produce FIT.fit_overflow + TEXT_BELOW_READABLE_MIN, so the detectors exist but do not run against expanded pattern grids for text capacity/trimming.

close_reason:
Pattern slides are now expanded once and measured by every text detector; the pattern and shape_grid forms of the same content produce identical findings.

Root cause: generateFitReport, collectReadabilityFindings and collectStructuralFindings all gated on slide.ShapeGrid != nil. A slide-level named pattern carries slide.Pattern and only gets a ShapeGrid at generation time, so the whole text-density / autofit / readability family skipped it — while fit_findings_geometry.go, which expands patterns itself, kept emitting TEXT_EXCEEDS_SHAPE / SPARSE_FILL. That asymmetry is why the recommended authoring surface returned 'VALID, no issues' on decks rendering at 4-8pt.

Implementation (cmd/json2pptx/fit_pattern_expansion.go, new):
- expandPatternsForFit() returns a working copy with every slide-level pattern (and its nested cell patterns, via the existing expandSlidePatternGrid) expanded into ShapeGrid, plus the set of slide indices that were expanded. Called once at the top of collectFitFindings, right after expandComposeForPreflight — the bead's primary HOW — so text capacity, readability, structural geometry, table and chart preflight all see the same grid. generateFitReport also calls it for the CLI path that invokes it directly; the helper is idempotent.
- rerootPatternPath() rewrites /slides/N/shape_grid/... to /slides/N/pattern/... for expanded slides, matching what the geometry detectors already emit. Applied once over the final finding set (and inside generateFitReport for its own expansions).
- patternCellFix() swaps a reduce_cell_text / reduce_text fix for the registered advisory rewrite_field, dropping cell_path (nothing in the deck JSON to edit) and keeping max_chars plus the pattern name, so the agent knows how much to cut and where.

Two calibrations were required to keep the new signal honest — both found by running the corpus, not by assumption:
- The row-level fit_overflow ('row content ~27pt exceeds max_height 25pt') was action=refuse. Once pattern slides were measured it failed phase-roadmap (95->63), patterns-smoke and varied-pitch-deck. Every row-overflow across examples + gallery decks is a 104-108% overshoot, and the per-cell checks already refuse text clipped after autofit, so it is now review.
- TEXT_BELOW_READABLE_MIN is only emitted when the predicted autofit shrink is <= 0.85 (autofitShrinkReportThreshold). The shrink is predicted from an estimated cell box: on phase-roadmap it predicts 12pt -> 10.6pt for cells that measure ~12pt in the actual render (checked at 110dpi), and reporting inside that error bar dropped clean pattern decks below the gate. title: auto_repair applies zero repairs and reports gate_passed on decks with visible defects / 30 P0s
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: dogfood-b, quality-signal (finding refs q.4, b.18).

WHAT
auto_repair is advertised by get_started(task=revise) as the FASTEST PATH and 'replaces the agent's manual chain'. On every one of my 16 calibration decks and 34 example decks it returned trace[].repairs_applied == [] — it never repaired anything. On B02 it reports gate_passed:false with '30 P0 (refuse) findings exceeds max_p0_findings 0' and still applies nothing, then stops after 1 pass. This is the downstream consequence of the two findings above (propose_repairs produces directives that repair_slide rejects, or only unmappable kinds), but the facade hides it: there is no field saying 'proposed N, applied 0'. An agent calling the recommended one-call revise path gets its deck back unchanged with a red gate and no next step.

ALSO REPORTED (dogfood-b: "auto_repair converges on a deck it has never looked at and reports gate_passed=true with zero repairs on a deck with visible defects"): auto_repair on my 11-slide deck returned gate_passed=true, final_score=95, passes=1, repairs_applied=[] while the deck had 5 wrapping titles, two 90-100 word bullet slides, an unreadable funnel and integer-rounded data labels contradicting the headline. score_deck on the same deck: 98 with quality_gate.passed=true. The blocking_reasons / manual_review_required=true fields do correctly say 'current artifact lacks complete all-slide vision inspection', which is the round-1 fix working -- but the headline numbers (95/98, gate_passed=true) are what an agent reads first, and they say 'ship it'. The composition diagnostics it does have ('pattern chart-insights-split repeats 3 consecutive slides', 'no emphasis slide') are the only two things it complains about, neither of which is a real defect here.

WHERE
cmd/json2pptx/mcp_auto_repair.go (pass loop, repairs_applied aggregation), cmd/json2pptx/mcp_get_started.go (task=revise fast_path)
[dogfood-b] cmd/json2pptx/mcp_auto_repair.go (deterministic loop = collectFitFindings + score); cmd/json2pptx/mcp_score_deck.go:195; the gate defaults min_score=75 / max_p1=2.

HOW
Surface the repair funnel per pass: {findings_count, directives_proposed, directives_applied, directives_failed[{kind,reason}]}, and set completion:'no_progress' whenever applied==0 while findings>0 (SKILL.md already documents that value). Then fix the underlying mapping so a deck with fit_overflow in a shape_grid actually converges.

Alternative/extra HOW from dogfood-b: Do not report a numeric 'final_score' + gate_passed at the top level when quality_mode=deterministic and visual inspection has not run; report gate_passed_deterministic plus status='draft_needs_visual_review' as the headline, and make the score fields nested under a `deterministic` object. Also fold the missing content-lint findings (see the render_deck_spec finding) into the loop so the score reflects wrapping titles and 100-word bodies.

close_reason:
auto_repair now applies repairs and reports the full funnel per pass.

Root cause was three separate defects, all confirmed by running the calibration decks:
1. split_pattern — the directive the fit report proposes for an overfull pattern slide — refused with 'slide has no shape_grid to split (pass path to split a pattern.values array)'. Findings describe the problem (filled_slots 12, recommended_max 9), never the field to split, so EVERY directive on a pattern deck failed.
2. applyProposedRepairs broke out of the directive loop after the first success PER SLIDE, so a slide with 20 overfull cells needed 20 passes against a default budget of 3 (measured: score 0 -> 5 -> 10 over three passes).
3. The response had no funnel: repairs_applied was the only signal, and it serialized as null on a zero-repair pass.

Implementation:
- applySplitPattern infers the repeated values array via longestPatternValuesArray() (longest array with >=2 items; a tie returns '' rather than splitting the wrong field), so a pattern slide no longer needs an explicit path.
- splitPatternValues resizes declared grid dims: resizeGridDims()/balancedGridDims() rewrite numeric columns/rows to an exact balanced factorization of the half's item count. Without this the first working split produced 'card-grid: cells must contain exactly 12 items (columns=4 x rows=3)' and the whole generation failed.
- validatePatternHalf() re-expands each half and REFUSES the fix (code semantic_review_required) when the pattern rejects it, rather than handing back a deck that cannot generate. The guard only applies when the original values expand cleanly — pre-existing invalidity is the pattern validator's report, not this fix's fault (caught by an existing test whose fixture was already invalid).
- applyProposedRepairs applies one repair per TARGET (cell_path/path, else the slide) instead of one per slide, and returns after a structural repair changes the slide count so no directive is applied at a stale index.
- New trace fields: directives_proposed, directives_advisory (findings whose remedy is an authoring decision — the advisory vocabulary from go-slide-creator-ui4c), directives_applied, directives_failed[{kind, slide_index, code, reason}]; repairs_applied is always an array.

VERIFY (MCP auto_repair through the built binary):
- decks/B02_tiny_text_overstuffed.json (the bead's named deck): BEFORE 1 pass, findings 72, repairs_applied null, gate_passed false. AFTER 3 passes: pass1 proposed 3 / advisory 69 / applied 1 (split_pattern slide 1), pass2 applied 1 (split_pattern slide 3), pass3 clean; score 48 -> 64 -> 76, findings 72 -> 60 -> 48, completion 'converged'. directives_failed carries the one refusal with its reason ('"cells" has 6 items; nothing to move to a second slide').
- A 20-cell overstuffed grid: one pass, 20 reduce_cell_text repairs, score 0 -> 100 (was 20 passes' worth of work).
- B06_table_9_columns: applies split_at_row and reports the sibling directive that lacked a row param.
- auto_repair's structuredContent validates against its own declared outputSchema (jsonschema Draft 2020-12) with the new required trace fields.

Tests: TestApplyProposedRepairsReportsFailureReasons, TestApplyProposedRepairsRepairsEveryTargetInOnePass, TestApplyProposedRepairsSkipsRepeatedTargets, TestSplitPatternInfersTheRepeatedField, TestSplitPatternRefusesWhenHalvesAreInvalid, TestBalancedGridDims, TestLongestPatternValuesArrayRefusesTies.

Docs sync: auto_repair tool description (funnel fields + per-target semantics), skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md auto_repair row, outputSchemaAutoRepair (new trace properties, required), docs/SCHEMA_CHANGELOG.md.

The existing manual_review_required / blocking_reasons / status fields already carry that verdict, and the complaint that a 95 score does not track deck quality is go-slide-creator-q7ar's, which owns the scoring model. description:

WHAT
CLOSURE AUDIT of go-slide-creator-yzbo (closed as 'validate dry-renders pattern charts; parity test'). The chart-specific case is fixed, but the general validate/generate parity hole is still open: named-pattern values are never checked against the pattern JSON schema during validate. `j2p validate --fit-report examples-derived smoke_long.json` prints 'Fit report: no issues found / VALID', and `validate_input` over MCP returns ok:true 'no issues', while `j2p generate` on the SAME file fails with `pattern "kpi-3up": validation failed: kpi-3up: values[0].small exceeds maxLength 40 (81 chars)`. Same for exec-summary minItems (points must contain at least 3 items) and kpi-6up big maxLength 8. An agent following the documented validate-then-render loop therefore burns a full round-trip on an error the validator already had all the information to report.

ALSO REPORTED (capability-gaps: "validate_input passes decks generate_presentation refuses: pattern values bypass the gate"): SKILL.md sells validate_input as 'the cheapest precondition gate' before generation. It does not run pattern-value validation. A deck whose icon-row items carry unknown icon names and omit the required `caption` returns {valid:true, summary:'no issues'} from validate_input and from the CLI `json2pptx validate`, while preview_presentation_plan reports it in errors[] and generate_presentation hard-fails with INPUT.INVALID_SLIDE ('values[0].icon must be a bundled icon name ... got "strategy"' + 'values[0].caption is required'). The same names inside a shape_grid ARE caught (ICON_BUNDLED_NAME_UNKNOWN). So the gate an agent is told to trust is blind to the most common authoring surface (43 patterns), costing a full generate round-trip per mistake.

WHERE
cmd/json2pptx/validate.go, cmd/json2pptx/dry_run.go (validate path), cmd/json2pptx/validate_grid_diagrams.go:expandSlidePatternGrid (swallows pattern value errors: 'pattern value errors are reported by the pattern validator, not here'), cmd/json2pptx/pattern_resolve.go:71 (where generate reports them), internal/patterns/*.Validate

HOW

Keep the existing expansion for geometry findings, but stop discarding the validation error.

Alternative/extra HOW from capability-gaps: In the validate_input / dry_run boundary, iterate slides[].pattern (and compose segments' patterns) and call the same patterns registry Validate(name, values, overrides) that preview_presentation_plan already invokes, mapping each error to a diagnostic at /slides/i/pattern/values/... title: P0-19: `schema_version` frozen at "1.0.0" — contract drift invisible to agents
description:
**Labels:** `bug`, `P0`, `api-contract`, `versioning`, `mcp`

**Summary**
`SchemaVersion` is a hard-coded constant in `cmd/json2pptx/main.go:22` that has stayed `"1.0.0"` across the entire beads log (subtitle fallback, section_number alias, 24pt cap, renamed Fix.Kind vocabulary, new fit-findings). `get_capabilities` (`cmd/json2pptx/mcp_capabilities.go:87`) returns this constant verbatim and tells agents in its own tool description to "compare schema_version across sessions — a major bump means breaking changes." Nothing in the repo enforces a bump: no CI guard, no test pinning the value to a feature set, no changelog hook. Agents that trust the SKILL.md contract believe nothing has changed while the server has silently altered placeholder fallback, Fix.Kind semantics, and fit-finding codes.

**Fix**
Replace the free-text constant with a structured capability manifest whose entries are checksum-derived from the schema struct, the enum sets, the `Fix.Kind` list, and the `FitFinding` code list. Fail the build (or a test) when the computed checksum changes without a corresponding bump. At minimum: CI test asserts `SchemaVersion` matches the version encoded in `docs/SCHEMA_CHANGELOG.md`, and any change to `PresentationInput`, `mcpToolNames()`, or the Fix.Kind switch requires a SchemaVersion bump in the same commit.

**Acceptance**
- Adding a new field to `PresentationInput` without bumping SchemaVersion fails CI.
- `docs/SCHEMA_CHANGELOG.md` exists with entries for every SchemaVersion.
- `get_capabilities.schema_version` matches the latest changelog entry.
close_reason: Implemented schema fingerprint CI guard: fingerprint test detects contract drift, SchemaVersion bumped to 2.0.0, docs/SCHEMA_CHANGELOG.md created

title: P0-5: Generator hard-caps all body text at 24pt, silencing layout typography
description:
**Labels:** `bug`, `P0`, `correctness`, `typography`, `generator`

**Summary**
Layouts that define large body fonts (e.g. PwC Section Header's section-number placeholder at 208pt, built-in Section Dividers at 96pt) are silently rewritten to 24pt at generation time. Confirmed empirically: modified `pwc-template.pptx` slideLayout2 to `<a:defRPr sz="20800">`, generated a slide, unzipped output — slide XML contains `<a:defRPr sz="2400">`. This also explains why every body text on content slides rendered at 24pt in the ADV AI deck regardless of pattern-level intent.

**Root cause**
`internal/generator/text_population.go:151-153`:
```go
if maxFontSizeHPt > 0 {
    // Regular body text: hard cap at 24pt to prevent overflow.
    capLstStyleFontSize(shape, maxFontSizeHPt)
}
```
`maxFontSizeHPt` is hard-coded to 2400 for every body placeholder regardless of layout intent. The code comment acknowledges the intent (prevent overflow) but the mechanism (flat cap) blows away deliberate layout typography. The 24pt value dates from when the generator assumed body placeholders only held bullet lists.

**Fix**
1. Short-term: bypass the cap when the placeholder's shape `name` is `"Section Number"` (see P1-15). Also bypass when `placeholder_id` passed from user is `section_number`, `large_number`, or `section_title`.
2. Medium-term: treat `maxFontSizeHPt` as a **ceiling only when the layout doesn't already declare a larger defRPr**. If layout says 208pt, trust it; use `normAutofit` to handle overflow at the declared size. Only cap when no layout size is specified (bare `<a:defRPr/>`).
3. Long-term: the cap belongs in the fit-report layer, not in text_population. Emit a fit-finding when a placeholder's declared size plus content measurement overflow; let strict-fit handle refuse/shrink.

**Location**
- `internal/generator/text_population.go:90-101` — `setTextParagraph` signature with `maxFontSizeHPt int`
- `internal/generator/text_population.go:151-153` — the unconditional cap
- Grep for callers passing `2400` as `maxFontSizeHPt` — all body-text callsites need to be revisited

**Acceptance**
- PwC Section Header with `body = "02"` renders at 208pt, not 24pt.
- Built-in Section Dividers render their large numbers at 96pt (or whatever layout specifies).
- Regular body text in content slides still shrinks via `normAutofit` when overflowing; doesn't suddenly render 60pt because layout inherited from master.
- Unit test: given a layout with `<a:defRPr sz="20800">` on body idx=1, the generated slide's lstStyle defRPr sz must be `20800` (not `2400`).
close_reason: Fixed: capLstStyleFontSize no longer overwrites layout-declared font sizes. Added capLstStyleFontSizeIfUnset that trusts explicit lstStyle sz values and lets normAutofit handle overflow.

title: P0-3: Skill docs mislead agents about section layout placeholder IDs
description:
**Labels:** `docs`, `P0`, `skill`

**Summary**
Four documentation errors cause repeated agent failures on first-pass deck generation:

1. `~/.claude/skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md:324` claims section layouts use `title, subtitle` — PwC Section Header uses `title, body`.
2. `~/.claude/skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md:318` — Rule 11 is ambiguous about whether `layout_id` is display name or `slideLayoutN` ID. `generate` requires the ID form, `validate` silently accepts either.

4. `~/.claude/skills/template-deck/TEMPLATE_GUIDE.md:372-377` — documents connector `color` accepting scheme references. Until P0-1 ships, this silently corrupts PPTX output.

**Fix**
- SKILL.md:324 — document per-template placeholder lists, or point at `skill-info` output.
- SKILL.md:318 — state explicitly: "`layout_id` must be the ID (e.g. `slideLayout2`), not the display name."
- SLIDE_FORMAT.md:100 — replace example with `slideLayout1`.
- TEMPLATE_GUIDE.md:372 — add note "connector color currently requires hex; scheme refs are tracked in P0-1".
