title: P0-2: `subtitle` placeholder silently dropped when layout has no `subTitle`
description:
**Labels:** `bug`, `P0`, `correctness`, `placeholders`

**Summary**
On PwC Section Header (`slideLayout2`), content targeted at `placeholder_id: "subtitle"` is silently discarded with only a warning log: `placeholder not found in layout`. The layout has `title` + `body` placeholders (no `subTitle`). The skill docs actively instruct agents to use `subtitle` on section layouts, so this is triggered every time an agent produces a section divider.

**Location**
- `internal/generator/placeholder_resolver.go:186-198, 351-365`

**Fix**
1. `subtitle` alias should fall back in order: `subTitle` role → `RoleSubtitle` → `body_2` → `body`. Return the first match.
2. `placeholder not found` should escalate to a fit-finding with `severity: error`, `action: refuse` under `strict_fit: strict`. Under `warn` keep as warning but emit the finding so repair_slide can see it.
3. Fit-finding `code: placeholder_not_found`, `fix.kind: remap_placeholder`, `fix.params: {available_placeholders: [...]}`.

**Acceptance**
- Section Header slide with `subtitle` content renders body text in the layout's body placeholder.
- Under `strict_fit: strict`, a truly unmappable placeholder refuses generation with a structured diagnostic.
- Fit-report surfaces the mapping decision (via `info` severity) so the agent can learn from it.
close_reason: Implemented subtitle fallback chain (subTitle→body_2→body) in resolveBySemanticRole. Emits info-level fit finding with remap_placeholder fix kind when remapping occurs.

title: P0-1: PPTX corrupts on open — scheme color written as `srgbClr`
description:
**Labels:** `bug`, `P0`, `correctness`, `ooxml`

**Summary**
Generated decks that use `card-grid` or `timeline-horizontal` patterns produce PPTX files that PowerPoint asks to repair on open. Root cause: the shape-grid code path passes scheme names (e.g. `"accent1"`) directly into `SolidLinePoints`, which emits `<a:srgbClr val="accent1"/>`. OOXML requires hex in `srgbClr`; scheme references must use `<a:schemeClr val="accent1"/>`.

**Location**
- `cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go:665` — passes raw string to `SolidLinePoints`
- `internal/pptx/line.go:29-36` — `SolidLinePoints` unconditionally wraps in `SolidFill(hex)`
- `internal/pptx/fill.go:145-156` — `ResolveColorString` already exists and correctly routes scheme vs hex. Shape-grid path just doesn't call it.

**Fix**
Route shape-grid border/stroke colors through `ResolveColorString` before handing to line primitives. Likely also affects any other shape-grid call site that passes a color string to a fill/line primitive — grep for callers.

**Acceptance**
- Regenerated ADV AI deck (19 slides, several `card-grid` slides with accent borders) opens in PowerPoint without the repair prompt.
- New test: generate a slide with `shape_grid` border `accent1`, unzip PPTX, assert `schemeClr` appears and `<a:srgbClr val="accent1"/>` does not.
close_reason: Fixed: connector colors now route through ResolveColorString, emitting schemeClr for scheme names instead of invalid srgbClr

title: P0: Replace harmonize.go lookup table with tag-based canonical layout name resolution
description:
## Description
Replace the fragile pwcCanonicalRoles lookup table in harmonize.go with a runtime tag-based canonical name resolver. Agents write self-explanatory layout names ("title", "content", "closing") and the system finds the matching layout in ANY template by checking classifier tags.

## Why the current approach fails
The harmonize.go BuildLayoutMapping() uses a static pwcCanonicalRoles table mapping slideLayoutN → tags. This broke immediately when PwC's layout ordering changed (slideLayout1 was "Blank" in the table but "Title Slide" in reality). Any template modification invalidates the table.

## Canonical Names (12 total)
| Name | Maps to Tag | Exclude Tags |
|---|---|---|
| title | title-slide | blank-title, closing |
| content | content | two-column, section-header |
| section | section-header | — |
| closing | closing | — |
| blank | blank-title OR blank | — |
| two-column | two-column | — (nameHint: "50") |
| two-column-wide-narrow | two-column | — (nameHint: "60" or "70") |
| two-column-narrow-wide | two-column | — (nameHint: "40/60" or "30") |
| image-left | image-left | — |
| image-right | image-right | — |
| quote | quote, statement | — |
| agenda | agenda | — |

## Implementation

### Step 1: Add resolveCanonicalLayoutID() (~50 lines)
Location: cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go or internal/layout/aliases.go

```go
func resolveCanonicalLayoutID(name string, layouts []types.LayoutMetadata) (string, bool) {
    if strings.HasPrefix(name, "slideLayout") { return name, true }  // passthrough
    if layout.IsGeneratedLayout(name) { return name, true }          // passthrough
    rule, ok := canonicalNames[strings.ToLower(name)]
    if !ok { return name, false }
    // Find best matching layout by tag
    for _, l := range layouts {
        if matchesTags(l.Tags, rule.requireTags, rule.excludeTags) {
            return l.ID, true
        }
    }
    return name, false
}
```

### Step 2: Wire into pipeline (cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go ~line 264)
Replace the harmonization block:
```go
// Replace BuildLayoutMapping with canonical resolution
for i := range input.Slides {
    if input.Slides[i].LayoutID != "" {
        resolved, _ := resolveCanonicalLayoutID(input.Slides[i].LayoutID, templateLayouts)
        input.Slides[i].LayoutID = resolved
    }
}
```

### Step 3: Delete harmonize.go and harmonize_test.go
No longer needed — canonical resolution fully subsumes the lookup table approach.

### Step 4: Merge aliases.go into canonical resolver
The existing LayoutAliases map (two-column → content-2-50-50) is dead code — never called from JSON pipeline. Merge it into the canonical resolver for one unified resolution path.

### Step 5: Update JSON files
Change sovereign-ai-strategy.json to use canonical names:
- slideLayout1 → "title"
- slideLayout3 → "content" (for PwC's One Content)
- slideLayout5 → "closing"
- slideLayout6 → "two-column"

### Step 6: Update skill-info and MCP
- Add canonical_name field to skill-info layout output
- Update MCP tool description to use canonical names in examples
- Update TEMPLATE_GUIDE.md

## Files to Create/Modify
- internal/layout/canonical.go (new — canonical name table + resolver)
- internal/layout/canonical_test.go (new — tests)
- cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go:264 — replace harmonization with canonical resolution
- examples/sovereign-ai-strategy.json — use canonical names

## Files to Delete
- internal/template/harmonize.go
- internal/template/harmonize_test.go

## Verification
1. go test ./... -count=1
2. Generate sovereign-ai-strategy with all 5 templates — all slides render correctly
3. Verify slideLayoutN passthrough still works for backward compat
4. Verify canonical names resolve to correct layouts on all templates
close_reason: Replaced harmonize.go lookup table with tag-based canonical layout name resolution in internal/layout/canonical.go. Canonical names (title, content, section, closing, blank, two-column, etc.) resolve to correct template layouts via tag matching. Deleted harmonize.go/harmonize_test.go, updated json_mode.go pipeline, converted sovereign-ai-strategy.json to use canonical names.

title: P0: Implement tag-based layout harmonization for cross-template compatibility
description:
## Description
JSON files authored against PwC template use positional layout indices (e.g., layout_id: "slideLayout4" = "One Content"). When rendered on other templates, these indices point to completely different layouts, causing blank slides and wrong layouts on 4/5 templates.

## Root Cause
Layout ordering differs across templates:
- PwC: slideLayout1=Blank, slideLayout2=Title, slideLayout3=Section, slideLayout4=Content, slideLayout5=Closing, slideLayout6=TwoCol(synth)
- Warm-Coral/Midnight/Forest: slideLayout1=Title, slideLayout2=Content, slideLayout3=TwoCol, slideLayout4=Section, slideLayout5=Closing, slideLayout6=Blank
- Modern: slideLayout1=Content, slideLayout2=Closing, slideLayout3=Title, slideLayout4=Section, slideLayout5=Agenda

## Solution: BuildLayoutMapping()
Add internal/template/harmonize.go with a BuildLayoutMapping() function that:
1. Defines PwC canonical roles: which tags each slideLayoutN should have
2. For each PwC role, finds matching layout in target template by tag
3. Returns map[string]string (PwC index → target index)
4. Identity mappings omitted (no remapping when indices already match)

### Canonical PwC roles:
- slideLayout1 → tags: [blank-title], exclude: []
- slideLayout2 → tags: [title-slide], exclude: [blank-title, closing]
- slideLayout3 → tags: [section-header], exclude: []
- slideLayout4 → tags: [content], exclude: [two-column, section-header]
- slideLayout5 → tags: [closing], exclude: []
- slideLayout6 → tags: [two-column] (50/50 by name)
- slideLayout7 → tags: [two-column] (60/40 by name)
- slideLayout8 → tags: [two-column] (40/60 by name)

### Injection point: cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go ~line 262
After template analysis, before convertPresentationSlides():
```go
if len(templateLayouts) > 0 {
    layoutMapping := template.BuildLayoutMapping(templateLayouts)
    for i := range input.Slides {
        if newID, ok := layoutMapping[input.Slides[i].LayoutID]; ok {
            input.Slides[i].LayoutID = newID
        }
    }
}
```

## Files to Create
- internal/template/harmonize.go — BuildLayoutMapping() + canonical role table
- internal/template/harmonize_test.go — tests with warm-coral, modern, PwC layout lists

## Files to Modify
- cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go:262 — inject harmonization call

## Fixes beads
- Resolves o19j (ContentZone overlap) for placeholder-based slides
- Resolves 4de6 (blank slides on non-PwC templates)

## Verification
1. go test ./internal/template/ -run TestHarmonize
2. go test ./... -count=1
3. Generate sovereign-ai-strategy with all 5 templates, verify slide 22 (two-column) renders content on all
close_reason: Implemented BuildLayoutMapping() in internal/template/harmonize.go with PwC canonical role table, tag-based matching with exclude tags and name hints. Injected harmonization call in cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go after template analysis. Added comprehensive tests covering PwC identity, warm-coral, modern, synthesized two-column, and no-match scenarios.

title: P0: Placeholder-based slides render blank on non-PwC templates (layout_id portability)
description:
## Description
Slides using explicit `layout_id` (e.g., `slideLayout6`) with placeholder_id (`body`, `body_2`) render as completely blank on midnight-blue, warm-coral, and forest-green templates. Only the footer and template accent bar are visible.

## Affected Templates & Symptoms
- midnight-blue: slide 22 completely blank (no title, no body)
- warm-coral: slide 22 completely blank
- forest-green: slide 22 completely blank
- modern-template: slide 22 shows title only, no body content
- pwc-template: renders correctly (reference)

## Root Cause
The JSON specifies `layout_id: "slideLayout6"` which is PwC's synthesized "Two Column (50/50)" layout. On other templates:
- warm-coral/midnight/forest: slideLayout6 = "Blank" (no body placeholders at all)
- modern: slideLayout6 = synthesized "Blank + Title" (title only, no body)

The layout file IS found (no error), but it has zero body placeholders. The placeholder resolver silently fails to match `body` and `body_2`, so the text content is never injected. The slide renders with the layout's visual chrome (accent bar, footer) but no content.

### Code path:
1. `cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go:480-484` — explicit layout_id preserved as-is, no tag-based lookup
2. `internal/generator/slide_preparation.go:134-145` — `readLayoutFile("slideLayout6")` succeeds (file exists)
3. `internal/generator/placeholder_resolver.go` — `ResolveWithFallback("body")` fails (no body placeholder in Blank layout), returns `(0, "", false)` — content silently dropped
4. Slide XML written with empty placeholders

## Fix
This is **fully resolved by jv42** (layout harmonization). After `BuildLayoutMapping()` is implemented:
- `slideLayout6` (PwC "Two Column 50/50") → remapped to `slideLayout3` (warm-coral/midnight/forest "Two Content") 
- `slideLayout6` → remapped to `slideLayout7` (modern synthesized "Two Column 50/50")
- The correct layout has `body` and `body_2` placeholders, so content is injected properly

## Additional Defensive Fix (optional, post-jv42)
Add a warning in placeholder_resolver.go when a placeholder_id is not found in the layout:
```go
// In ResolveWithFallback(), when all 5 tiers fail:
slog.Warn("placeholder not found in layout",
    slog.String("placeholder_id", placeholderID),
    slog.String("layout_id", layoutID),
    slog.Any("available", availableNames),
)
```
Location: `internal/generator/placeholder_resolver.go` in the `ResolveWithFallback()` method.

## Reproduction
```bash
# Create JSON with layout_id: "slideLayout6" and body/body_2 content
json2pptx generate -json sovereign-midnight-blue.json -output ./output
# Open slide 22 — completely blank
```

## Verification
1. After jv42, generate sovereign-ai-strategy with midnight-blue template
2. Verify slide 22 shows two-column content ("European Pioneers" / "Global Benchmarks")
3. Check all 5 templates — slide 22 must render content on all
close_reason: Added slog.Warn for placeholder-not-found case in slide_preparation.go. The underlying layout portability issue was already resolved by jv42 layout harmonization.

title: P0: ContentZone — shape_grid content overlaps title on non-PwC templates
description:
## Description
On all templates except pwc-template, shape_grid slides render with content overlapping the title area. The title text appears on top of or behind the shape grid content.

## Affected Templates
- modern-template: severe (all shape_grid slides)
- midnight-blue: severe
- warm-coral: severe
- forest-green: severe
- pwc-template: OK (reference)

## Root Cause
Two separate issues combine:

### Issue 1: DefaultGridBoundsPct y=18% is PwC-specific
`internal/shapegrid/bounds.go:71` defines `DefaultGridBoundsPct = [4]float64{5, 18, 90, 72}`. The y=18% top offset matches PwC's title area but not other templates that have taller title placeholders or different title Y positions.

When JSON omits explicit bounds, `DefaultBounds()` (bounds.go:129) uses these hardcoded percentages. The `pickBlankLayout()` function (cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go:90-164) correctly computes template-aware bounds via `ContentZone` when a blank-title layout is found, but this only applies when the shape_grid slide uses virtual layout resolution.

### Issue 2: Explicit JSON bounds bypass ContentZone clamping
In `cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go:193-205`, the bounds resolution priority is:
1. JSON `bounds` field → `BoundsFromPercentages()` + `ClampBoundsToZone()` (if zone exists)
2. `overrideBounds` from virtual layout resolution (template-aware)
3. `DefaultBounds()` (hardcoded 18%)

Path 3 is the problem — when no JSON bounds are specified AND virtual layout resolution doesn't trigger, `DefaultBounds()` returns a y=18% top offset that ignores the actual template title height.

## Fix Required
After jv42 (layout harmonization) is implemented, shape_grid slides will correctly resolve their blank-title layout from the target template. The `pickBlankLayout()` function will compute a proper ContentZone using the target template's actual title placeholder height. This should fix most cases.

For the remaining edge case (shape_grid slides that fall through to `DefaultBounds()`):
1. Pass ContentZone through to `resolveShapeGrid()` even when no virtual layout is selected
2. In `resolveShapeGrid()`, use `DefaultBoundsFromZone(zone, 9.0)` instead of `DefaultBounds()` when zone is available
3. Fallback: compute zone from the template's blank-title layout at the start of `convertPresentationSlides()` and thread it to all shape_grid slides

## Files to Modify
- `cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go:520-534` — Ensure contentZone is always computed for shape_grid slides, not just when `needsVirtualLayout()` returns true
- `cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go:193-205` — In path 3 (DefaultBounds fallback), use ContentZone if available
- `cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go:90-164` — pickBlankLayout() is already correct, no changes needed

## Affected Slides (sovereign-ai-strategy deck)
Slides 2-24 (all shape_grid slides) on modern, midnight-blue, warm-coral, forest-green templates.

## Depends On
- jv42 (layout harmonization) — ensures shape_grid slides resolve the correct blank-title layout from the target template

## Verification
1. Generate sovereign-ai-strategy with all 5 templates
2. Convert to images (max 2000px)
3. Verify slides 2, 6, 10, 15, 20 — title must NOT overlap shape_grid content on any template
close_reason: Fixed: ContentZone now computed for all shape_grid slides regardless of virtual layout resolution. DefaultBoundsFromZone used as fallback instead of hardcoded DefaultBounds when zone is available.

title: ARCH: Introduce ContentZone abstraction — template-derived safe content area
description:
CRITICAL ARCHITECTURAL CHANGE: The system lacks a single source of truth for where content can be placed. Three independent systems compute content boundaries:
1. DefaultGridBoundsPct (hardcoded y=18%, bounds.go:16)
2. BoundsFromTitleAndFooter (template-derived, bounds.go:36-52)
3. resolveFooterPositions (footer.go:295)

These never cross-reference each other, causing content to overlap title (Modern template) and extend into footer zone (Warm Coral).

NEW STRUCT in internal/shapegrid/bounds.go:
  ContentZone {
    TitleBottom int64  // Y of title bottom edge
    FooterTop   int64  // Y of footer top edge
    LeftMargin  int64
    RightEdge   int64
    SlideWidth  int64
    SlideHeight int64
  }

COMPUTED: During template scanning in pickBlankLayout (shape_grid.go:91), from actual title and footer placeholder transforms.

USED: In resolveShapeGrid (shape_grid.go:163), when JSON specifies explicit bounds percentages, CLAMP them against ContentZone so content never overlaps chrome.

REPLACE: DefaultGridBoundsPct with DefaultBoundsFromZone(zone, gapPt) that derives bounds from actual template geometry.

EXPORT: Footer top edge from footer.go via FooterTopEdge() function to feed into ContentZone.

KEY FILES:
- internal/shapegrid/bounds.go:16 (replace hardcoded defaults)
- cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go:91-135 (compute ContentZone)
- cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go:163-164 (clamp bounds against zone)
- internal/generator/footer.go:295 (export FooterTopEdge)
close_reason: Implemented ContentZone abstraction: new struct in bounds.go with DefaultBoundsFromZone and ClampBoundsToZone, exported FooterTopEdge from footer.go, computed zone in pickBlankLayout, clamped explicit bounds in resolveShapeGrid

title: Icon+text overlay layout: need configurable arrangement (side-by-side or stacked)
description:
CRITICAL: When a shape_grid cell has both a shape (colored fill + text) and an icon overlay, the icon renders on top of the text, making it unreadable. Affects slides 4, 6, 10, 13, 15, 17, 20 in the sovereign-ai-strategy deck.

Currently the icon is positioned via FitContain within the cell bounds, but the text in the same shape has no awareness of the icon position. The text starts at the shape's left inset and the icon sits on top of it.

REQUIRED: Two layout modes for icon+text cells, configurable via JSON:

MODE 1: 'icon_position: left' (side-by-side, DEFAULT for wide cells)
- Icon rendered on the LEFT side of the cell, sized to 60% of cell height
- Text starts AFTER the icon with 3pt (38100 EMU) gap to the right of the icon
- Text is flush-left aligned
- Implementation: increase the text body lIns (left inset) by icon_width + gap, so text flows to the right of the icon

MODE 2: 'icon_position: top' (stacked, for narrow/square cells)
- Icon centered horizontally in the top portion of the cell
- Text centered below the icon
- Both icon and text horizontally centered

JSON SCHEMA ADDITION to IconSpec:
  icon: {
    name: 'shield',
    fill: '#FFFFFF',
    position: 'left' | 'top' | 'center'  // default: 'left' for wide cells, 'top' for square cells
  }

The position auto-detection should be: if cell width > 2x cell height → 'left', else → 'top'.

KEY FILES:
- internal/shapegrid/types.go:84-87 (IconSpec — add Position field)
- internal/shapegrid/grid.go:166-170 (icon overlay bounds calculation)
- internal/shapegrid/shape.go (buildTextBody — adjust lIns based on icon width when position='left')
- cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go (icon pic positioning)
close_reason: Implemented icon+text layout modes (left/top/center) with auto-detection based on cell aspect ratio. Icon position shifts text via extra body insets to prevent overlap.

title: Icon cells forced to square (FitContain) — header bars with icons render as small squares
description:
When a shape_grid cell has both a shape (geometry+fill) and an icon, FitContain is forced at grid.go:154, making the cell render as a square (min(w,h) × min(w,h)). This is wrong for header-bar cells where the colored rectangle should span the full column width with an icon positioned inside.

EXAMPLE: Slide 4 (3-column risk grid) has header cells 'Vulnerability', 'Opportunity', 'Urgency' with icons. Expected: full-width colored bars (cx=3438144, cy=602233). Actual: small squares (cx=1053718, cy=1053718) — the height used as both dimensions.

Comparison from corrected PPTX:
- Corrected: cx=3438144 cy=602233 (full column width, short header)
- Ours: cx=1053718 cy=1053718 (square = row height × row height)

ROOT CAUSE: internal/shapegrid/grid.go:153-156:
  if fitMode == FitStretch && (cell.Icon != nil || cell.Image != nil) {
      fitMode = FitContain
  }
This forces FitContain for ALL cells with icons. But FitContain (grid.go:474-486) constrains to min(w,h)×min(w,h), making the shape square.

FIX: When a cell has BOTH a shape AND an icon overlay (CellKindShape with IconSpec), the SHAPE should use FitStretch (full cell bounds) and only the ICON should use FitContain within the shape bounds. Separate the shape bounds from the icon bounds:
1. Shape rect: full cell (cellW × cellH)
2. Icon pic: contained (square) within the shape rect, centered

For standalone icon cells (CellKindIcon with no shape), FitContain is correct.

KEY FILES:
- internal/shapegrid/grid.go:153-156 (conditional FitContain)
- internal/shapegrid/grid.go:166-170 (CellKindShape with icon overlay)
- internal/shapegrid/grid.go:474-486 (ApplyFitMode)
close_reason: Fixed: shape+icon cells no longer forced to FitContain. Shape stretches to full cell bounds, icon is contained (square) within the shape. Added IconBounds field to ResolvedCell and updated renderer to use it.

title: Missing titles on shape_grid slides — virtual layout doesn't inject title content
description:
CRITICAL: Most shape_grid slides render without a visible title. Affects slides 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 13, 17, 24 in the sovereign-ai-strategy deck.

ROOT CAUSE (from developer debate): shape_grid slides use 'virtual layout resolution' (cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go:40-84) which selects a layout with a title placeholder. But the title comes from the JSON content[] array targeting that placeholder — NOT from shape_grid. These are two completely independent pipelines with no coordination.

When the JSON omits a content item with placeholder_id='title' (or the virtual layout picks a layout without a title placeholder), no title renders. There is no warning emitted.

TWO-PART FIX NEEDED:

1. CODE FIX (cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go:488-515): After virtual layout resolution, if the selected layout has a title placeholder but no content item targets 'title', emit a WARNING log. Optionally auto-inject the slide's first heading-style text as the title.

2. CODE FIX (cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go:40-84): resolveVirtualLayout should prefer layouts with usable title placeholders (reasonable dimensions, not decorative elements) and validate the selected layout actually has one.

3. JSON FIX: The sovereign-ai-strategy.json example needs title content items added to every shape_grid slide. This is also an input validation issue — the JSON schema should require a title for non-closing slides.

KEY FILES:
- cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go:40-84 (resolveVirtualLayout)
- cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go:488-515 (shape_grid slide processing)
- internal/generator/placeholder_resolver.go:63-94 (silent skip of unresolvable content)
close_reason: Fixed: shape_grid icon SVG inserts had placeholderIdx defaulting to 0, which caused removeNativeSVGPlaceholders to remove the title placeholder shape (always at index 0). Set placeholderIdx to -1 for shape_grid icon inserts, matching the pattern used by image inserts.

title: Icons not visible in shape_grid cells — icon element not rendering in PPTX output
description: When a shape_grid cell includes an icon field (e.g. {"icon": {"name": "shield", "fill": "#FFFFFF"}}), the icon does not render in the generated PPTX. The shape appears as a solid colored rectangle with text but no icon SVG. This affects all icon-grid slides (slides 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 13, 17, 24 in the sovereign-ai-strategy.json example). The icon JSON is correctly structured per INPUT_FORMAT.md. Likely the icon lookup or SVG embedding path in the shape_grid cell renderer is not being triggered. Check internal/generator/ shape grid rendering code — specifically where cell.Shape.Icon is processed and whether the SVG is actually embedded into the PPTX slide XML. The icons/ directory has 5000+ SVG icons (outline and filled variants) and the lookup system in icons/lookup.go works for other contexts.
close_reason: Fixed: ShapeSpecInput now accepts nested icon field. When shape.icon is present, the grid resolver creates both the shape background and an icon overlay insert. Icons now render correctly in shape_grid cells.

title: PPTX corruption: duplicate slideLayout relationships in slideMaster rels (PwC template)
description:
## Problem
PowerPoint reports "found a problem with content" when opening shape-grid-panels-pwc.pptx. Root cause: duplicate Relationship entries in ppt/slideMasters/_rels/slideMaster1.xml.rels.

## Root Cause (CONFIRMED)
The slideMaster rels file has DUPLICATE references to slideLayouts 1-5:
- rId1-5: original layout references from template
- rId7-11: DUPLICATES added by synthesis code

The bug is in the interaction between two code paths in `internal/generator/singlepass.go` and `internal/generator/output.go`:

1. **singlepass.go:168-169**: `NormalizeLayoutBytes()` normalizes existing layouts and stores them in `syntheticFiles` map. This is a content fix, NOT a new layout.

2. **output.go:365-376**: `writeSlideMasterRelsWithSynthetic()` calls `syntheticLayoutNames()` which collects ALL layout files from `syntheticFiles` — including the normalized-but-already-existing ones.

3. **Result**: layouts 1-5 are ALREADY in the template rels (rId1-5). The synthesis code adds them AGAIN (rId7-11) because they appear in `syntheticFiles` due to normalization.

## Fix
`syntheticLayoutNames()` should distinguish between:
- **Truly new layouts** (e.g., slideLayout6-8 that don't exist in the template) → add rels
- **Normalized existing layouts** (e.g., slideLayout1-5 that just had content fixes) → DON'T add rels

One approach: check if the layout file already exists in the template ZIP before adding a relationship.

## Affected Templates
- **pwc-template**: CORRUPTED (5 duplicate layout rels)
- **midnight-blue**: OK (0 duplicates — no normalization needed)
- Other templates: untested, likely affected if they need layout normalization

## Files
- `internal/generator/singlepass.go:155-171` — normalizeExistingLayouts adds to syntheticFiles
- `internal/generator/output.go:342-400` — writeSlideMasterRelsWithSynthetic
- `internal/generator/output.go:402-415` — syntheticLayoutNames (doesn't filter existing)
close_reason: Fixed: syntheticLayoutNames() now skips layouts that already exist in the template ZIP, preventing duplicate relationship entries in slideMaster rels

title: Alpha fill scale mismatch: ResolveFillInput passes Alpha(x*1000) instead of Alpha(x*100000)
description:
## Root Cause (CONFIRMED)
Two code paths compute alpha values with DIFFERENT scales:

**Path 1 (BUGGY) — shape.go:88 ResolveFillInput:**
```go
alphaMod := pptx.Alpha(int(obj.Alpha * 1000))  // 0.3 → 300 (= 0.3% opacity!)
```

**Path 2 (CORRECT) — shape.go:364 GenerateImageOverlayXML:**
```go
alphaVal := int(alpha * 100000)  // 0.3 → 30000 (= 30% opacity)
```

OOXML Alpha expects thousandths of percent: 100000 = fully opaque, 50000 = 50%.
`pptx.Alpha(val)` docstring says: "val is in thousandths of a percent (e.g., 50000 = 50%)"

Path 1 passes 300 for alpha=0.3, which means 0.3% opacity (nearly invisible).
Path 2 correctly passes 30000.

## Fix
In `internal/shapegrid/shape.go:88`, change:
```go
alphaMod := pptx.Alpha(int(obj.Alpha * 1000))
```
to:
```go
alphaMod := pptx.Alpha(int(obj.Alpha * 100000))
```

Also line 93:
```go
return pptx.SolidFillWithAlpha(hex, int(obj.Alpha*1000)), nil
```
to:
```go
return pptx.SolidFillWithAlpha(hex, int(obj.Alpha*100000)), nil
```

## Visual Evidence
Slide 10 of visual-maturity-stress-test.pptx: shapes with alpha fills are nearly invisible / misrendered.

## Verification
Add unit test: ResolveFillInput with `{"color":"#000000","alpha":0.3}` → verify generated XML contains `<a:alpha val="30000"/>` not `<a:alpha val="300"/>`.
close_reason: Fixed alpha scale: ResolveFillInput now normalizes both fractional (0-1) and percentage (1-100) alpha inputs to OOXML thousandths-of-percent. Added regression tests for fractional alpha on both hex and scheme colors.

title: Reserve footer safe zone in shape_grid bounds (bottom margin)
description:
## Problem
Shape grid content extends too close to the slide bottom edge. No footer area is reserved even when no footer placeholder exists. This looks cramped and unprofessional, and prevents branded footer bars.

## Current Behavior
- When no footer placeholder found, `pickBlankLayout()` in `cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go:116` uses slide bottom (DefaultSlideHeightEMU) as boundary
- The 9pt gap is only between title/footer and grid — but when footer Y = slide height, grid goes to the very bottom
- Content panels touch or nearly touch the bottom edge

## Desired Behavior
- Always reserve minimum footer clearance (~0.4" / 317,500 EMU / ~4% of slide height) from bottom
- Even when no footer placeholder exists, the grid should stop well above slide bottom
- Optionally expose `footer_height` percentage parameter in shape_grid JSON
- Consider adding a `bottom_margin` field to Grid struct

## Affected Files
- `cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go:114-121` — footerRect calculation when no footer
- `internal/shapegrid/bounds.go:30-35` — BoundsFromTitleAndFooter

## Affected Slides
All shape_grid slides in all three example decks — content bleeds to bottom on every slide.

## Reference
Bain deck maintains consistent 2-4% bottom margin on every slide for brand bar, slide numbers, and visual breathing room.
close_reason: VERIFIED: MinBottomMarginEMU footer safe zone implemented. Stress test slide 3 shows visible clearance below content panels.

title: Make corner radius on roundRect configurable, default to sharp (0)
description:
## Problem
All shape_grid content panels use `"geometry": "roundRect"` which produces visible rounded corners, creating a bubbly, app-like appearance instead of professional consulting style. The Bain reference deck uses SHARP 90-degree corners on every rectangle.

## Current Behavior
- `roundRect` geometry uses OOXML default corner radius (~16.67% adj handle)
- No way to control the adjustment handle (`adj`) value from JSON input
- Every card, panel, and header bar has rounded corners

## Desired Behavior
- Add `corner_radius` (or `adjustments.adj`) parameter to ShapeSpec
- Default to `0` (sharp corners) for `roundRect` geometry
- Allow override per-shape via JSON: `{"shape": {"geometry": "roundRect", "corner_radius": 5}}`
- Consider making `rect` the recommended geometry and `roundRect` only used when explicitly desired

## Affected Slides
ALL shape_grid slides across all three example decks (shape-grid-panels, consulting-layouts, business-model-canvas) — 15+ slides total.

## Implementation Notes
- `internal/pptx/spgen.go`: ShapeOptions.Adjustments already supports AdjustValue
- `internal/shapegrid/shape.go`: GenerateShapeXML already passes adjustments to opts
- `internal/shapegrid/types.go`: ShapeSpec already has `Adjustments map[string]int64`
- Need to: set default adj=0 for roundRect when no explicit corner_radius is set
- The OOXML adjustment handle name for roundRect corner radius is `adj`

## Reference
Bain Resilience AmCham presentation — every rectangle has sharp corners. This is the #1 visual issue making our output look amateur.
close_reason: VERIFIED: adj=0 default for roundRect working correctly. Stress test slide 2 confirms first 3 roundRect panels have sharp corners, only explicit adj=16667 is rounded.

title: Resolve raster mutex sharing across module boundary
description:
## Task
Ensure the tdewolff/canvas raster mutex is safely shared between the svggen module and the monorepo.

## Problem
tdewolff/canvas has package-level globals in its Bentley-Ottmann path intersection code that are NOT thread-safe. The current internal/raster/raster.go provides a single sync.Mutex that ALL canvas rasterization calls must acquire. 

After extraction, if the svggen module has its own raster mutex and the monorepo keeps a separate copy, they protect different lock instances — the race condition returns.

## Current Consumers of raster.Mu
1. svggen/builder.go — acquires mutex for PNG/PDF rendering
2. internal/preview/pdf.go — acquires mutex for PDF preview rendering

## Solution
1. Create a PUBLIC package at svggen/raster/ (not internal) that exports the mutex:
   ```go
   package raster
   var Mu sync.Mutex
   ```
2. The svggen module's builder.go imports from svggen/raster/
3. The monorepo's internal/preview/pdf.go imports from github.com/ahrens/svggen/raster
4. DELETE the monorepo's internal/raster/ package entirely
5. Any other monorepo code using tdewolff/canvas directly must also use svggen/raster.Mu

## CRITICAL: Correctness Risk
If both mutexes exist in the same binary, concurrent rendering WILL produce corrupt output or panics. This is a P0 because it is a silent correctness bug.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Only ONE raster.Mu exists in the final binary
- internal/raster/ is deleted from the monorepo
- internal/preview/pdf.go imports from the svggen module's raster package
- Race detector passes: go test -race ./...
close_reason: Moved svggen/internal/raster to svggen/raster (public), deleted monorepo internal/raster, updated all 3 consumers to import from single svggen/raster package

title: Contrast predictor and render-time fixer disagree on lstStyle levels no paragraph uses (p-style parity corpus fails)
description: Reported by the downstream team. The render-time contrast fixer rewrites, and reports as swaps, low-contrast colours on EVERY level of a placeholder lstStyle, including levels the slide text never uses (internal/generator/text_contrast.go around line 231: fixSchemeColorsForContrast over shape.TextBody.ListStyle.Inner, all lvlNpPr). The validate-time predictor CONTRAST_PREDICTED models only the placeholder single inherited colour (cmd/json2pptx/fit_findings_collect.go placeholderContrastPairs, around line 1986: ph.InheritedFontColor / FontColor). A template with a low-contrast colour only on unused levels gets a render-time swap the predictor never announced, so cmd/json2pptx/contrast_parity_corpus_test.go fails its predicted == actual comparison. Visible output is not wrong; the swap reports are noise and parity breaks. Repro with the local gitignored templates/p-style.pptx present: go test -tags=integration ./cmd/json2pptx -run "TestContrastParityCorpus/(full-showcase|template-qa-deck)/p-style" gives a decision-set mismatch with an extra actual entry {2 #8D949B #2E353A #FFE8D4}. Trigger: the section layout Section Number body placeholder sets accent1 on lvl1 (the level used) and tx1 with tint 82000 (#8D949B, 2.59:1 on #FFE8D4) on lvl2 to lvl9, which a section number never uses. title: Horizontal compose tells a segment the wrong width when its pattern changes column count between the probe and the sized expansion
description: Found by the circular split matrix (go-slide-creator-27b0c). expandCompose (cmd/json2pptx/compose.go) probes each segment at the full content area, then composeSegmentBounds states each segment rectangle from the PROBE grid column count (a horizontal segment is a parent cell spanning its columns, so its width includes one compose gap per column it spans). A pattern that picks another lattice in the narrower rectangle (concentric-rings drops its two centring pad columns: 4 columns in the probe, 2 when sized; cycle-ring / cycle-nodes / radial-hub move from two outside label columns to one legend) is therefore told a width that is off by gap x (probe columns - real columns). Repro: modern-template, compose horizontal gap 12, segment 0 = concentric-rings with 5 layers (labels Sponsor / Leadership team / Function heads / Front-line teams / Customers) at 50 percent, segment 1 = labeled-rows at 50 percent. The pattern is told 416pt, the merged grid gives it 404pt; the 12pt labels no longer fit the 126pt ladder, the writer stores a 98 percent autofit and generate refuses with INPUT.TEXT_BELOW_READABLE_MIN (validate reports the same refusal at two extra field paths). Fix: restate the segment rectangles from the columns the sized expansion really has and expand again (bounded passes).

title: pattern cycle-figure-eight: two coupled loops side by side (infinity / DevOps loop) for 4–8 phases, built for 16:9
description:
Parent epic: go-slide-creator-jk8j7 (circular / loop layout family). Label: circular-layouts-20261006.

## Why
The user's ask: an 8-shaped loop that uses the 16:9 width. Two coupled loops (build ↔ run, dev ↔ ops, plan ↔ deliver, supply ↔ demand) are a staple of operating-model and DevOps slides and a single ring wastes a wide slide. OOXML has no lemniscate preset, so the figure eight is two tangent rings of `blockArc` segments whose path runs left lobe → crossing → right lobe → crossing: fully native, editable, template-coloured.

## Values (typed struct in internal/patterns/cycle_figure_eight.go, hand-authored Schema() <= 6000 bytes with $defs — TestPatternSchemaCompression)
`phases []{label (<= 26), description (<= 60, optional), icon?}` 4..8; `left_count int` optional (default ceil(N/2); 2..4 per lobe); `left_label`, `right_label` (<= 16 chars each, optional lobe titles drawn in the lobe centres); `highlight int` optional.

## Layout (native, via shape-grid `layers` + the lattice; see ring_common.go)
One lattice cell spanning two ring squares side by side (`fit: "fit-height"`; frame width = 2·side − overlap where the lobes are tangent, overlap = thickness so the two rings meet in one crossing band at the centre): layers = left lobe segments (phases 0..left_count−1, traversed counter-clockwise starting at the crossing going up-left, so the path reads: up over the left lobe, down, back to the crossing) and right lobe segments (remaining phases, clockwise starting at the crossing going up-right), each a `blockArc` on its own lobe square (frames (0,0,0.5+ε,1) and (0.5−ε,0,0.5+ε,1)); numbered badges on each lobe's centreline; small rotated `triangle` arrowhead layers at the end of each segment so the direction is unmistakable at the crossing; the crossing itself is a 1-segment gap on both lobes (no segment drawn across the junction) so the eye reads an 8, not two touching rings. Lobe titles as text layers in the lobe centres (14pt bold, dk2). Labels outside: top band (phases whose badge is in the upper half, left-to-right order), bottom band (lower half), far-left and far-right rows for badges within 30° of 9 / 3 o'clock — lattice rows above and below the 8; for N=8 that is 4 on top and 4 below, each label <= 26 chars, 2 lines at 12pt, descriptions one line. Lobe side = min(contentH, (contentW − 2·reserve)/2 + thickness/2) where reserve is the far-left/right label width when such labels exist, 0 otherwise; on abstract (687×294) the lobes are ~280pt tall with top/bottom label bands of 2 lines; on p-style wider. If contentW < 1.6·contentH (a narrow split segment) the pattern refuses with `FIGURE_EIGHT_NEEDS_WIDE_AREA` → fix `use_pattern cycle-ring`.

## Overrides
`thickness` thin|regular|thick; `labels` outside (default) | legend; `highlight`; `cell_accent_mode` (progressive runs over the whole path); `arrowheads` true (default) | false.
Standard: `TextOverrides` embedded; `cell_accent_mode` uniform|alternate|progressive (ValidateCellAccentMode / ResolveCellAccent); `rejectUnusedTextOverrides` + `textOverridesSchemaWithout` for any published key the pattern cannot act on; `highlight` is the only solid accent block by default.

## Capacity / budgets
N=4–6: label 26 / description 60; N=7–8: 22 / 40. Lobe titles 16. `BudgetConfigurations()` for 4, 6 and 8.
Rows sized from `writtenFitHeightPt(..., ctx.themeFonts())`; every text at >= 12pt; `PostExpandWarnings` emits `BODY_TOO_LONG`-class warnings naming the item when a label or description cannot hold at the floor on the current template (the same message shape as team-bios / driver-tree).

## Registration + discovery (same commit)

title: patterns: ring_common.go — shared ring / loop geometry (segment angles, badge and label anchors, lattice rows) for the circular family
description:
Parent epic: go-slide-creator-jk8j7 (circular / loop layout family). Label: circular-layouts-20261006.

## Why
Five patterns (cycle-ring, cycle-nodes, cycle-intake, cycle-figure-eight, radial-hub) place N items around a circle, put labels outside it and must not overlap anything. One pure, unit-tested helper keeps their trig, OOXML angle conventions and lattice bookkeeping identical — the same way `house_builder.go` is the one builder for strategy-house and house_diagram and `kpi_common.go` serves kpi-Nup.

## What (internal/patterns/ring_common.go, pure functions, no I/O)
```go
type ringSpec struct {
    N          int     // items 3..8
    StartDeg   float64 // where item 0 begins; default -90 (12 o'clock); OOXML: 0 = 3 o'clock, clockwise positive
    Clockwise  bool    // default true
    GapDeg     float64 // angular gap between segments, default 6
    Thickness  float64 // ring width as a fraction of the short side, default 0.20 (blockArc adj3 = Thickness*100000)
}
type ringItem struct { Index int; StartDeg, EndDeg, MidDeg float64; Side string /* right|left|top|bottom */ }
func ringItems(s ringSpec) []ringItem                       // equal segments with gap, wrapping handled, degrees normalised to [0,360)
func blockArcAdj(it ringItem, thickness float64) map[string]int64 // {"adj1": start*60000, "adj2": end*60000, "adj3": thickness*100000}
func pointOnCircle(cx, cy, r, deg float64) (x, y float64)   // y down
func badgeFrame(it ringItem, diameterFrac float64, thickness float64) frame  // ellipse on the ring centreline, as a fraction frame for a cell layer
func labelSide(midDeg float64) string                       // right: (-75,75); left: (105,255); top/bottom bands otherwise
```

description:
## Why
Gap analysis 2026-10-06 over the 56 named patterns (internal/patterns), the 15 native diagrams (internal/generator/native_diagrams.go) and the svggen diagram registry (svggen/init.go): there is NO cycle, loop, ring, radial or concentric layout anywhere — `grep -rwiE 'cycle|circular|flywheel|wheel|orbit' internal svggen cmd` finds nothing that draws one. Best practice (SmartArt Cycle catalogue: Basic / Block / Segmented / Continuous / Radial cycles; infodiagram, presentationgo, slidemodel, consultingedge guidance): 5–7 steps is the readable ceiling of one ring, 8 the hard maximum; equal segments; a clear direction cue (numbers and/or arrowheads); labels OUTSIDE the ring with a number or leader, never crammed into segments; one highlighted step; descriptions 1–2 lines; identical colouring per step unless the colour is data. title: shapegrid: cell `layers` — co-located native shapes with fractional frames inside one grid cell (foundation for the circular family)
description:
Parent epic: go-slide-creator-jk8j7 (circular / loop layout family). Label: circular-layouts-20261006.

## Why
A ring is N `blockArc` segments, N number badges, an optional centre label and arrowheads that all occupy the SAME bounding square; the grid resolver gives every cell its own rectangle and the lattice technique (docs/PATTERNS.md:408-431) explicitly cannot overlap shapes. Nothing in the pattern layer can draw two shapes in one place today: `GridCellInput` (internal/jsonschema/shapegrid.go:124) holds exactly one of Shape / Table / Icon / Image / Diagram / Composite / Pattern / Grid, and slide-level overlays (shapegrid.go:263-288, resolved in cmd/json2pptx/overlays.go `resolveOverlays`) are slide DTOs of kind arrow/line/badge/callout that `Pattern.Expand` never returns. The native diagram builders (internal/generator/*_shapes.go) can overlap but sit outside the pattern layer (no capacity budgets, overrides, previews, motif, compose). This primitive is what makes the whole family native.

## What
Add `Layers []LayerInput` to `GridCellInput` (internal/jsonschema/shapegrid.go:124-160): a z-ordered list of shapes drawn INSIDE the cell's resolved bounds, each in a fractional frame.

```go
// LayerInput is one native shape stacked inside a cell, placed in a frame given as
// fractions (0..1) of the cell's fitted bounds; layers draw after the cell's own
// shape, in order, so later layers sit on top.
type LayerInput struct {
    Frame LayerFrameInput `json:"frame"`           // X, Y, W, H as fractions of the fitted cell (0..1); W,H > 0
    Shape *ShapeSpecInput `json:"shape,omitempty"` // geometry, fill, line, text, rotation, flip_h, adjustments
    Icon  *IconInput      `json:"icon,omitempty"`  // optional: an icon-only layer (later; may stay out of V1)
    Name  string          `json:"name,omitempty"`  // stable id for findings paths and tests, e.g. "segment-3"
}
```
Mirror it in `internal/shapegrid/types.go` (`Cell.Layers []Layer`, `ResolvedCell.Layers []ResolvedLayer{Bounds pptx.RectEmu; Shape *ShapeSpec; ShapeID uint32; Name string}`).

## Where / how
- Convert: cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go `convertGridCell` (:1312) maps `LayerInput` -> `shapegrid.Layer`; reuse the existing shape conversion so fill/line/text/adjustments/rotation parse identically to a cell shape.
- Resolve: internal/shapegrid/grid.go where the cell shape bounds are fitted (~:300-330, the `cell.Shape` / `iconOverlayBounds` branch): after the cell's fitted bounds are known (AFTER `fit: "contain"` squaring, so a layer frame is relative to the square a circle actually gets), compute each layer's EMU rect = frame × fitted bounds, allocate a shape ID per layer from the same allocator, append `ResolvedLayer`s in input order. A cell may have no base shape and only layers (an empty base = a transparent canvas). Validate frames: 0 <= X,Y < 1, 0 < W,H <= 1, X+W <= 1.0001, Y+H <= 1.0001; error `LAYER_FRAME_OUT_OF_CELL` naming the layer.
- Write: internal/shapegrid/shape.go — emit each layer through the same `GenerateShapeXML` path as a cell shape (rotation ×60000, flipH, avLst from `Adjustments`, `noLine` honoured, autofit measurement with `MeasureFonts`). Z-order: cell shape, then layers in order, before row connectors/links so arrows stay on top. Find the exact spTree assembly point (grep `ResolvedCell` consumers in internal/generator/shape_grid*.go / cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go) and emit layers immediately after their base shape.
- Capacity + findings: internal/textcapacity/budget_guide.go loops `result.Cells` (:152, :216) and reads `c.Shape` only — extend to layers so layer text gets a budget and `TEXT_BELOW_READABLE_MIN` / `fit_overflow` / `BODY_TOO_LONG` fire for a layer exactly as for a cell. Findings path = `<cell path>/layers/<i>` (or `/layers/<name>` when named) — add to the finding path builder next to the existing cell paths in cmd/json2pptx/fit_findings_collect.go and internal/patterns/finding_meta.go notes.
- Contrast: internal/generator/text_contrast.go and the preflight (cmd/json2pptx contrast parity) must see layer fills/text like cell shapes (grep `Cells` consumers; add layers to each walk — verdict_parity_corpus_test and contrast_parity_corpus_test are the parity gates).
- Compose / nested grids: a cell inside a compose segment or a nested `grid` resolves layers the same way (frames are relative, so nothing else changes); confirm in a test.
- Schema: JSON schema for shape_grid cells (internal/jsonschema + the discovery schema served by MCP `get_capabilities` / `validate_input`) gains `layers`; unknown-keys reflection (cmd/json2pptx/unknown_keys_check.go:447) picks the struct up automatically — add a test that `layers[0].frame.x` typo is reported. `GridCellInput` is hashed by cmd/json2pptx/schema_fingerprint_test.go `wantFingerprint` (currently a0e913951243f827): re-pin, bump `SchemaVersion` in cmd/json2pptx/main.go (4.169.0 -> 4.170.0) and keep skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md `schema_version` in step (TestGenerateDeckSkillSchemaVersionMatchesServer).
- Determinism: no shipped example changes, so cmd/json2pptx/testdata/golden_hashes.json stays; if an example is added later, rebaseline with scripts/rebaseline_golden_hashes.sh (memory: determinism-golden-macos-logs-only).

## Docs (same commit)
docs/INPUT_FORMAT.md (shape_grid cell fields: `layers` with the frame semantics and z-order), docs/PATTERNS.md new section "Co-located layers (when the lattice is not enough)" after "Free-positioned shapes: the lattice technique", docs/SCHEMA_CHANGELOG.md entry, skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md (or the shape_grid guide file it links) one sentence on `layers`, docs/wiki/split-and-complex-layouts.md one line in "Choosing between them" noting layers exist for hand-built grids.

## Verify
- Unit: see the companion test bead (resolve frames, z-order, validation errors, writer XML, capacity, findings path, contrast parity).
- `go test ./internal/shapegrid/... ./internal/textcapacity/... ./internal/jsonschema/... ./cmd/json2pptx -short -count=1` green; `make lint` green.
- Hand deck: a 1-cell grid with a `blockArc` segment layer, an `ellipse` badge layer with "1" and a `circularArrow` layer generates on midnight-blue and p-style; open the PPTX in PowerPoint / render through soffice: three shapes overlap in the right order, the badge text is 12pt+, and `validate -fit-report` reports the badge cell path `/slides/1/shape_grid/rows/0/cells/0/layers/1`.

## Family contract (applies to every bead in epic circular-layouts-20261006)

Native OOXML first: every shape is a preset-geometry `<p:sp>` emitted through the shape grid (internal/shapegrid). No SVG unless a geometry is provably impossible natively (none of the family needs it: `blockArc`, `circularArrow`, `pie`, `arc`, `donut`, `ellipse`, `chevron`, `homePlate`, `triangle`, `line` are all in internal/pptx/preset.go and shape cells already take `rotation`, `flip_h` and `adjustments` — internal/jsonschema/shapegrid.go:224-235, written at internal/shapegrid/shape.go:80-102).

Template parity, exactly like every other pattern:
- Colours are scheme names only (`accent1`, `dk2`, `lt2`...), never hex. Default accent = `ctx.DefaultAccent()`; tints via `ctx.ResolveSurface` / `neutralFillJSON` / `surfaceFillJSON`; ink on any fill chosen by measurement (internal/patterns/fill_contrast.go), so warm-coral / business-template / blue-corporate pick their own primary fill (docs/PATTERNS.md "Restrained accent defaults").
- Restrained accent: at most ONE solid-accent block >= 0.5in by default (the `highlight` item); structural segments / nodes take a neutral tint; `cell_accent_mode` (uniform | alternate | progressive) via `TextOverrides` + `ValidateCellAccentMode` + `ResolveCellAccent`. cmd/json2pptx/accent_restraint_gallery_test.go must pass without adding the pattern to `accentIsTheMessage`.

Circles must stay circles there (`fit: "contain"` on the ring cell, lattice edges recomputed from the actual cell).

title: DeckSpec schemas reject their own table and agenda examples and encourage ignored totals strings
description:
## Reproduction
At source 9a6816674a471cf3fd9362fb6274665a0686fa3d / schema 4.164.0, use the real stdio MCP default profile. list_slide_kinds(kinds=["table","agenda"], fields=["brief","item_schema","example"]) advertises table.totals_row and agenda.current as string. Its table example uses totals_row:true; its agenda example uses current:2. JSON Schema Draft202012 validation of the returned examples rejects both. A sweep of all 27 advertised examples found exactly these two schema failures; render_deck_spec accepts all 27.
The mismatch has a visible consequence: render a native table with rows [["Enterprise","41.2","45%"],["SMB","8.9","-7%"],["Combined","50.1","30%"]], headers ["Segment","Revenue (€m)","Growth"] and totals_row:"true" as the advertised string type suggests. It returns ok:true, deterministic_ready:true, no diagnostics, and the Combined numbers have no bold face or totals rule. With the otherwise identical totals_row:true the emphasis renders. Use Combined rather than Total: isTotalRow auto-detection masks the defect for the bundled example's Total label.

## Root cause
internal/semantic/payload_fields.go:317 declares totals_row with strField; :345-348 declares current and its aliases as string, although internal/semantic/slides/table.go:223 only accepts bool and internal/semantic/slides/agenda.go:250 accepts numeric positions or matching section names. These declarations feed the full schema and compact MCP field signatures. TestKindExamplesValidateClean (payload_fields_test.go:128) calls the custom semantic Validate routine instead of validating against the published JSON Schema, so it passes with these schema-invalid examples. Focused existing tests passed during this audit.

## Impact
A schema-enforcing authoring client cannot send the copy-ready examples as documented, and an agent following the string type silently loses totals emphasis. Preserve the working compiler behavior and correct the schema contract; do not change examples to string booleans.

## Evidence and prior work
Audit call 6 (brief), 24/25 (controlled boolean/string render), 32/33 (images), 38/40 (schemas), 41/64 (accepted numeric/bool examples). Durable evidence: tests/quality/results/mcp-quality-audit-20261005/. This is not the earlier totals feature d7gy or payload-field coverage 7dk4: those are closed and do not cover these current type mismatches.
acceptance_criteria: All 27 KindExample payloads validate against both full and compact published JSON Schemas with a real JSON Schema validator. totals_row is boolean; agenda current/current_section/highlight/active allow a valid integer position or section-title string. Invalid totals strings must produce a field-addressable diagnostic rather than silent omission. Actual PPTX regression uses a non-auto-detected total label (Combined), checks bold numbers and separator for true, and checks false/no flag. Keep numeric agenda highlighting and string-title selection working.
notes: Implemented in ce09f057. Reviewed and pruned redundant strictness/alias combinations and duplicate image embedding checks; retained real PPTX totals styling, all-kind schema validation, readiness controls, and thumbnail/review publication regression. All 2400 CLI tests executed with race coverage in four CI shards; only the skill bundle size check failed and passed after prose compression. Remaining root packages executed with race coverage; two obsolete schema assertions were removed/replaced, and the entire semantic package passed on rerun. Focused final race regressions, svggen race suite, pinned lint, build, formatting, and skill sync passed. Combined root coverage 83.1%. No images or audit-history commits included; preview manifests change only diagnostic-source provenance. Serial CLI timeout/documentation follow-up remains go-slide-creator-vs5gp.

title: cmd/json2pptx sharded race step took 44m37s against a 50-minute limit
description: CI run 37222013440 on 8fb39aa8: the sharded cmd/json2pptx race step (scripts/ci_test_cmd_shards.sh 4) passed in 44m37s; earlier sharded runs took 28-37 minutes. Per-shard go test timeout is 47m and the step limit 50m, so the next test added fails CI by timeout. Find what this wave added (profile per-test durations from the CI log), cut the cost where it buys nothing under -race in -short mode, balance shards by measured duration instead of name order, and leave at least 15 minutes of margin. Verify on CI.
close_reason: Fixed and merged to main in schema 4.164.0 (2026-10-04); verified by the owning agent; lint, short suite, non-short internal and svggen tests and the integration corpus job green on the merged tree.

title: cmd/json2pptx race coverage suite exceeds 40-minute CI timeout
description: CI run 37162946119, test job 111319981403, runs go test ./cmd/json2pptx -short -v -race with coverage and -timeout=40m. It panics after 40m0s; TestTwelveFlawDraftCleanInThreeRoundTrips/modern is active, while several parallel schema-maxima tests wait. The long suite also had earlier independent assertion failures, but timeout prevents reliable completion/coverage. Profile long-running tests, reduce runtime or split suite, and verify it completes under CI's configured deadline. Log: https://github.com/sebahrens/json2pptx/actions/runs/37162946119/job/111319981403
close_reason: Fixed in 5a2fd537: scripts/ci_test_cmd_shards.sh runs the cmd/json2pptx short race suite as 4 parallel shards and merges coverage. CI run 37188284181: step took 37 min (was 58-61 min single) under a 50-minute step limit; job green.

title: get-started output omits render-thumbnails command

Restore the documented CLI command or reconcile the test and discoverability contract deliberately. Log: https://github.com/sebahrens/json2pptx/actions/runs/37162946119/job/111319981403
close_reason: Fixed in de4016df: get-started deliberately drops render steps when LibreOffice/ImageMagick are missing (degradeForMissingRenderTooling); TestCLIGetStartedSpeaksCLI now requires render-thumbnails only where render tooling is installed. Green on CI.

title: preview-icon help exits without usage text
description: CI run 37162946119, test job 111319981403, fails TestCLIConventionCoversEveryFlagSet/preview-icon and TestCLIHelpExitsZeroOnStdoutEverywhere: preview-icon -h and --help exit 0 but write 0 bytes to stdout and no stderr. Log: https://github.com/sebahrens/json2pptx/actions/runs/37162946119/job/111319981403
close_reason: Fixed in de4016df: preview-icon used flag.ExitOnError and exited inside flag.Parse before main flushed the stdout tap; it now returns flag.ErrHelp. TestCLIConventionCoversEveryFlagSet and TestCLIHelpExitsZeroOnStdoutEverywhere pass on CI (runs 37165329104, 37188284181).

title: Docker image build omits embedded skill reference docs
description: Docker workflow run 37162946096 for commit b7e01241 fails in build job 111319981196 at Dockerfile:28: Go compile reports references.go:20:63: pattern docs/FIT_FINDINGS.md: no matching files found. Root references.go embeds explicit docs/*.md (and other skill references), but .dockerignore excludes *.md and docs/, so COPY . . omits required embed inputs. Update Docker build context ignore rules to include all embedded references (not just the first missing file), and add a regression check that the Docker build succeeds for both target platforms or validates the build context includes each go:embed path. Docker test and scan jobs were skipped because build failed. Run: https://github.com/sebahrens/json2pptx/actions/runs/37162946096
close_reason: Fixed in de4016df (.dockerignore ships the eight embedded docs) and guarded in 5a2fd537 by TestDockerContextShipsEveryEmbeddedReference, which fails when .dockerignore excludes any go:embed path of references.go. Docker workflow green on de4016df, f8caff76, 5a2fd537.

title: The CLI cannot write slide PNGs; images arrive only as base64 inside JSON
description:
## Journey stage
delivery

## What happened to the agent
`render-thumbnails` and `render-slide` return base64 in stdout JSON (169 KB for 7 slides). The agent decoded them with
a script. `inspect --images` expects slide-0.png files that no command produces.

## Evidence
- tests/quality/results/agent-journey-20261003/d-cli/findings.json A7

## Expected
One command writes numbered PNG files and prints a small manifest.

Root cause was not investigated in code unless stated; the journey agents saw only the product's own output.
acceptance_criteria:
`render-thumbnails --out-dir <dir>` writes slide files named the way `inspect --images` reads them and prints paths,
hashes and sizes; base64 output becomes opt-in.
The user request "give me PNGs of the slides" is one command.
Covered by an automated test (or the journey harness in tests/quality/results/agent-journey-20261003/harness/). Agent-facing changes are documented in the generate-deck skill docs and docs/SCHEMA_CHANGELOG.md, with the skill bundle inside its budget. The behaviours listed as delights in tests/quality/results/agent-journey-20261003/report.json keep working.
close_reason: Implemented and merged to main in the 4.160.0 wave (2026-10-04); verified by the owning agent with tests and rendered checks, full suite, lint and integration corpus green locally. Remaining gaps filed under label followup-20261004.

title: Fit diagnostics name the wrong text and the wrong constraint
description:

the highlighted row (schema allows 80). The executive-summary budget was stated four different ways across rounds (3-5

## Expected

Root cause was not investigated in code unless stated; the journey agents saw only the product's own output.
acceptance_criteria:

title: Content-sized patterns hug the top of the content area and leave the lower half of the slide blank
description:
## Problem

from the top. On a slide this leaves a band of boxes over 40-60% blank canvas: kpi-Nup, kpi-inline, icon-row,
before-after, comparison-2col, stylish-panels, strategy-house, numbered-step-strip, process-flow, quote-cluster,

- The engine already reports it (SLIDE_UNDERUSED / VERTICAL_IMBALANCE, info) but nothing acts on it.

Content sizing (internal/patterns/content_sizing.go and each pattern's max-height row) anchors the grid at the top of the
layout bounds; there is no vertical composition step after sizing.

## Expected

type and spacing up within the pattern's type scale, then place the block at a deliberate position (for example optical
centre, or top with the takeaway band pulled up beneath it) so the slide reads as composed.
acceptance_criteria:

templates and p-style, without adding filler content.

title: strategy-house has a fixed three-level shape; levels and cells cannot follow the content
description:
## Problem
Every strategy house is one banner, one row of 3-5 equal pillars and one single-cell foundation. Real houses vary:
two foundation layers (enablers above values), a foundation split into several named enablers, a cross-cutting beam
between roof and pillars, or pillars with sub-pillars. Authors squeeze that content into one "A · B · C" string or drop it,
and every house in every deck has the same silhouette.

## Evidence
- tests/quality/results/layout-nativeness-20261003/evidence/probe-variants.jpg: three- and five-pillar houses differ only in column count; the foundation is always one bar.
- tests/quality/results/layout-nativeness-20261003/evidence/patterns-generated-*-3.jpg (strategy-house).
- The native house_diagram already models several floors and sections (internal/generator/house_shapes.go houseFloorMeta).

## Root cause
strategyHouseValues (internal/patterns/strategyhouse.go) has `foundation` as one string and a single pillar row; the row
indices are fixed (banner, pillars, foundation, optional roof). The `pillars` kind mirrors it (internal/semantic/slides/pillars.go).

## Expected
The house accepts a variable number of horizontal levels below (and optionally above) the pillars, each level one band or
a row of N cells, and lays them out from the content supplied.
acceptance_criteria:
`foundation` accepts a string (today's behaviour), or a list of layers where each layer is a string (full-width band) or a
list of short cells (a row of equal boxes).
An optional cross-cutting band between roof and pillars is supported.
A house with 2 foundation layers (one split into 3 enablers) and 4 pillars renders with all text readable; heights are
allocated from content, not fixed percentages.
Validation rejects more levels or cells than can stay readable, with a count-based message.
The `pillars` kind exposes the same shape and its source paths map to the right level and cell.
Validate on p-style plus at least one tracked template and inspect the rendered PNGs (never omit p-style; keep its template file untracked). Inputs the change does not target keep their current output or the difference is explained. Update docs/PATTERNS.md and the generate-deck skill docs for any schema or behaviour change (skill bundle stays in budget), and regenerate pattern previews.

title: strategy-house draws its roof as a flat grey strip instead of a roof shape
description:
## Problem
The strategy house is the textbook "house" framework, but the pattern renders five stacked rectangles: a grey strip
("Vision · Mission"), a solid banner, a row of tiles and a grey bar. Nothing reads as a roof, so the slide looks like a
web card layout. This is the slide the user flagged (tests/quality/results/layout-nativeness-20261003/evidence/user-reference-strategy-house.jpg).

## Evidence
- tests/quality/results/layout-nativeness-20261003/evidence/patterns-generated-midnight-blue-3.jpg and patterns-generated-p-style-3.jpg (strategy-house): flat strips.
- tests/quality/results/layout-nativeness-20261003/evidence/probe-variants.jpg: five-pillar and roofless variants, both templates.
- tests/quality/results/layout-nativeness-20261003/evidence/diagram-examples-midnight-blue-0.jpg (house): the native house_diagram already draws a triangle roof.

## Root cause
internal/patterns/strategyhouse.go builds the roof row and the objective banner with Geometry "rect" (roof cell ~line 318,
banner ~line 334). The native builder internal/generator/house_shapes.go draws a triangle, but the pattern (and the
DeckSpec `pillars` kind that compiles to it, internal/semantic/slides/pillars.go) never uses it.

## Expected
The objective sits in a gabled roof (triangle or pentagon) spanning the pillars' width; roof badges, when present, sit
inside or directly under the roof instead of in a separate strip.
acceptance_criteria:
The strategy-house pattern and the `pillars` kind render a roof shape above the pillars for 3, 4 and 5 pillars.
The objective text stays inside the roof's usable text area at a readable size (no stored autofit shrink below the floor); an

description:

WHAT
Direct series labels inherit low-contrast template chart colors without readable text treatment. In the p-style presentation-scale control, the essential 'Current capacity' endpoint label is #d89060 on white (2.600:1); 'Demand' is #fd5108 (3.303:1). ## Steps to Reproduce

svggen/charts.go LineChart.drawLegendOrDirectLabels -> seriesLabelColors -> drawLineDirectSeriesLabels. svggen/series_highlight.go seriesLabelColors returns the palette colors unchanged when no highlight is set, and only replaces non-highlighted colors otherwise. Keep series identity and template branding while giving endpoint text a readable color for its actual background and effective size (for example a suitable template ink plus a colored connector/key). Enforce or report low contrast in chart text, including direct labels with and without a highlighted series. Do not solve this by replacing all brand-colored series graphics with black.

Cover explicit series colors and highlighted/non-highlighted paths.

title: Default chart precision collapses threshold-relevant small rates to identical labels
description:

## Expected Behavior
Default formatting preserves distinctions and decision-relevant small magnitudes, with a consistent readable scale/precision. Do not silently collapse distinct values or round nonzero values to zero merely to obey a two-decimal cap. Respect explicit authored precision.

svggen/value_format.go: maxAutoDecimals=2; autoValueFormat returns %.2f even after labelsAreDistinct fails. ## Validation

title: Forced thumbnail refresh invalidates valid visual reviews because PNG metadata is hashed as pixels
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Real MCP reproduction at 24cae082: render examples/semantic/qbr.yaml using render_deck_spec; render_deck_thumbnails at density=100; retain all six returned image hashes; submit_visual_review with every image (accepted). Then call render_deck_thumbnails on the SAME pptx with density=100, slide_indices=[1], force=true. Resubmit the original all-slide review. It is rejected at slides[0] as an image that does not show this deck, although slide 0 was unchanged and was not even requested in the refresh. Three force calls reproduce it.
The original QBR slide-2 PNG and all three forced PNGs decode to identical RGB pixels, SHA256 a94ec66caa1c8a57542e8bdac673755247f18dc0255bd3a58bcecd6525219bac, but have distinct file hashes because ImageMagick preserves PDF/XMP creation and modification timestamps. Do not confuse this with a visual alignment bug: PDF positions and decoded pixels ruled that initial suspicion out.
Root: internal/render/render.go pdfToPNGs (~505) preserves volatile metadata; encodeImage (~583) and CachedSlideHashes (~1023) SHA256 entire PNG bytes; storeCachePNGs (~223) removes the previous source+density cache directory; deckPNGsContext rerenders ALL slides even for a selected refresh. cmd/json2pptx/mcp_visual_review_verify.go verifyReviewImages trusts only these most recent file hashes and describes them as pixel hashes. Immutable old artifact files still exist but their provenance is discarded. This forces needless full-deck rerender/review in a normal retry workflow.
Evidence: qbr-thumbs.json, qbr-force1/2/3.json, qbr-review-after-force.json; retained transcripts in .claude/review-evidence/2026-10-02, tracked audit evidence. Renderer LibreOfficeDev 26.8.0.0.alpha0, ImageMagick via repository resolver. Scope is proven image identity/cache failure, not PowerPoint rendering fidelity.
acceptance_criteria: A forced same-revision refresh must not reject an earlier legitimate review image for unchanged pixels. Canonicalize PNG metadata before identity hashing and/or retain an artifact+slide render provenance ledger across refreshes. Keep rejection of wrong-slide, foreign-deck and stale-PPTX evidence. Integration regression: full render, selected force refresh after time advances, submit retained images for all slides; verify success and no weakened provenance checks.
close_reason: Image identity is now a decoded-pixel hash (internal/pixelhash); ImageMagick strips date/time metadata; forced refresh keeps earlier reviews valid. Regression tests added.

title: plan_deck still discards the tail of long comparison facts while reporting unplaced_facts=[]
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Observed on HEAD 24cae082 via the real stdio MCP, protocol 2025-06-18. plan_deck(format=deckspec, slide_budget=8, template=warm-coral) with this brief: Board decision on a fictional service pilot. Revenue rose from €10m in 2024 to €12m in 2025. Gross margin fell from 45% to 38% because service costs rose. Compare building an internal support team (€0.8m per year, launch in 6 months) with outsourcing (€0.5m per year, launch in 2 months). Recommend the internal team to retain customer relationships. Pilot starts in January 2027; CFO owns funding approval in November 2026. Include backup assumptions.
Actual slots[].facts ends the comparison at "with outsourcing (€"; the €0.5m and 2-month alternative never appear in facts or unplaced_facts. unplaced_facts is empty. A using agent following the routed facts loses the economic case.
Root: internal/deckplan/facts.go extractBriefFacts truncates every remaining long clause with TruncateBrief(c,maxFactLen=120) after only splitting and/while/whereas/but. The discarded tail is never represented. balanceFactBrackets then scans a byte-index depth array whose UTF-8 continuation bytes retain zero depths, so the Euro sign can also leave an unmatched opening parenthesis. Full Brief is echoed, but this does not make the routed-facts preservation contract true.
Related closed issues csclk.48 (long-clause loss) and gvbw8 (bracketed comparisons); this is a verified residual case after their fixes. Evidence: .claude/review-evidence/2026-10-02/plan.json and tracked audit evidence. No production change requested by this audit.
acceptance_criteria: Retain the full comparison in routed facts or return every omitted span in unplaced_facts with a clear truncation finding. Never truncate within a numeric/currency token. Test long parenthesized option comparisons with € and CJK text, clauses without the four recognized conjunctions, and verify every input amount/date survives. Test bracket balancing by rune rather than uninitialized UTF-8 byte slots.
close_reason: Brief facts no longer truncated: rune-aware bracket depth, split outside brackets and never inside amounts/dates; Compare A with B drafts option_matrix before decision and routes recommendation to decision.

title: Turn on consulting chrome by default (page numbers, footer, tracker) and have plan_deck draft meta.chrome
description:
compileChrome returns nil when the spec has no meta.chrome (internal/semantic/compile.go:306-309), and the raw default footer is also off, so every slide of the rendered QBR DeckSpec has an empty bottom band with no slide number, no date and no confidentiality/footer line on all three templates (scratchpad/review/agent-guidance/qbr_midnight-blue/slide-03.png, qbr_p-style/slide-04.png, qbr_warm-coral/slide-04.png — even though meta.date was set). plan_deck format:deckspec drafts meta with only title/template/audience (deckspec_plan.go:145-152) and never a chrome block; WORKFLOW.md Phase 1 (lines 10-33) lists template, accent strategy and chapters but not chrome; QUALITY.md's self-check (lines 82-89) does not mention page numbers. Only get_started's long notes paragraph and DECKSPEC.md:37-38 describe the fields, without a recommended default. A board/consulting deck always carries page numbers and a date (the compile.go comment at 301-305 says so itself), so the shipped default makes agent decks look unfinished and makes 'see page 7' impossible in review.

Merged findings from other review areas:
- [best-practices-research] Default chrome off: no page numbers, tracker or footer unless meta.chrome is hand-set: Principle: consulting slides carry page numbers on every slide, a section tracker/sticker top-right, and the source bottom-left (Deckary: 'Page numbers required on all slides'; mconsultingprep slide anatomy: 'Page number & on-page tracker are for readers to easily keep track', https://mconsultingprep.com/how-consultants-make-mbb-slides; PPT PowerTools anatomy of a consulting slide, https://pptpowertools.com/the-anatomy-of-a-consulting-slide/). In json2pptx all of this is opt-in: internal/semantic/compile.go:306-327 `compileChrome` returns nil when `meta.chrome` is absent; cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go:3098-3112 returns a nil FooterConfig when neither `footer` nor `chrome` is set; internal/generator/output.go:707-729 then strips the template's own dt/ftr/sldNum placeholders; the tracker needs `chrome.tracker:true` (json_mode.go:3263-3317); plan_deck never emits `meta.chrome` (internal/deckplan/deckspec_plan.go). Evidence: examples/semantic/qbr.yaml rendered via the default path in midnight-blue, warm-coral and p-style (scratchpad/review/best-practices-research/qbr-midnight-blue/slide-3.png, qbr-warm-coral/slide-4.png, qbr-p-style/slide-4.png) shows no page number, no footer, no section label on any slide. Related defect: `page_numbers.enabled:false` sets `cfg.PageNumberFormat = ""` (json_mode.go:3084-3086) but `""` already means 'plain slide number' in footer.go:240-245, so disabling does not disable. Why it matters: an unnumbered deck cannot be referenced in a meeting ('go to page 12') and reads as a draft; the engine already has a well-tested footer/tracker system that agents simply never turn on.

ACCEPTANCE:
Either the compiler defaults page_numbers.enabled=true (skipping the title slide) and footer_date=meta.date when meta.chrome is absent, or plan_deck's deckspec draft emits meta.chrome {page_numbers:{enabled:true}, footer_date:'__FILL__'} and WORKFLOW.md Phase 1 + QUALITY.md self-check require page numbers and a date on content slides. The rendered QBR example shows a slide number on every content slide on midnight-blue, p-style and warm-coral.
A DeckSpec with no `meta.chrome` renders page numbers (skipping title/closing) on every template; `plan_deck format:deckspec` emits `meta.chrome` with `page_numbers.enabled: true` and `tracker: true` when `structure.sections` exist; `page_numbers.enabled:false` suppresses the slide number (regression test); SKILL.md/DECKSPEC.md state the new defaults.
