title: Setting table header_background flips the whole table to the legacy look: 18pt text, 1pt black grid, zebra
description:
An agent that adds the single most common table tweak — `style.header_background: "accent1"` — loses the consulting default entirely. IsEngineDefaultTableStyle (internal/generator/table_defaults.go:55-59) returns false as soon as header_background is set, so: (a) TableBaseFontSize falls back to the legacy defaultFontSize 18pt (table_defaults.go:62-70) and the header becomes 19.8pt (headerFontSize 110%, table_defaults.go:129-131); (b) borders default to 'all' — 1pt tx1 lines on every side of every cell (table.go:1314-1318 -> generateBorderXMLWithOverrides default case table.go:1397-1410, borderWidth=12700 table.go:65) plus table-level solid borders (table.go:292-294, 1414-1452); (c) tableStriped returns true because Striped is nil (table_defaults.go:118-125), painting accent1 15% stripes (table.go:1348). Rendered OOXML confirms: sz 1800/1980, lnL w=12700, four stripe fills (x/abstract/ppt/slides/slide10.xml) versus sz 1100/1200 and w=0 rules on the default table (slide9.xml). PNG evidence: review/typography-color/out-abstract/slide-10.png, out-p-style/slide-10.png, out-forest-green/slide-10.png, out-modern-template/slide-10.png vs the default look in out-*/slide-09.png. RULES.md:111 tells agents header_background is for 'a deliberate exception', but nothing warns that it also changes type size, borders and banding. Expected: header_background (and borders/striped set individually) should be additive on top of the engine default — 12pt rows / 11pt header, horizontal hairline rules only, no stripes, white or dk1 header text chosen by contrast — unless the author also set borders/striped/style_id. Why it matters: a heavy 18pt gridded zebra table is the single most 'PowerPoint-default' artefact on a consulting slide and it appears from a one-field change agents make constantly.

ACCEPTANCE:
Given a table_value whose style sets only header_background, the rendered table keeps engine-default sizes (12pt rows, 11pt header), engine-default borders (1pt rule under header, 0.5pt 15% row rules, no vertical rules, no outer frame) and no zebra stripes; only the header fill and header text colour change. An explicit `borders: "all"` or `striped: true` still opts in. Golden tests cover header_background alone and header_background+borders. docs/STYLE_DEFAULTS.md and RULES.md describe header_background as additive.

description:

On modern-yellow the third candidate is the title-less 'Statement' layout (slideLayout4, body idx=10 only) which wins for slide index 4 (gen.log `layout_name=Statement score=0.58`) — see separate finding on the dropped title. title: plan_deck format:deckspec is brief-insensitive and flat: one fixed storyline, no agenda/sections/appendix
description:
internal/deckplan/deckspec_plan.go:67-137 hard-codes the slot list cover/answer/problem/cause/evidence*N/plan/roadmap/ask/closing with fixed kinds (executive_summary, kpi_snapshot|stat|comparison, pillars, chart_insight, process, roadmap, decision, next_steps). The brief only changes the problem slot (by number of numeric facts) and how many chart_insight slots fill the budget. Evidence: three real briefs produced identical kind sequences — QBR (plan_qbr.json), board strategy recommendation with three options scored on cost/time/risk (plan_strategy.json) and a customer product update (plan_product.json, 8 slides: title, executive_summary, kpi_snapshot, pillars, process, roadmap, decision, next_steps). The strategy brief explicitly describes an option evaluation yet no option_matrix slot is drafted; the product update gets a 'cause: Why it is happening' pillars slot and a 'decision' ask that make no sense for a customer-facing update; every brief gets 'pillars' as the cause slide. With --slides 16 the draft is title, executive_summary, comparison, pillars, then FOUR consecutive chart_insight slides, process, roadmap, decision, next_steps (12 slides) — a visual-family run of 4 that the tool's own rhythm rule ('no 3 consecutive slides with the same pattern', mcp_plan_deck.go:19) forbids, and chart_insight evidence slots are drafted even when the brief carries no series data (guidance says 'never invent data'). No draft ever uses structure.sections, agenda or section kinds, so a 12-16 slide board deck is drafted without chapters. Audience is stored in meta but never changes the plan. The storyline is therefore not 'a kind per narrative slot routed from the brief' as SKILL.md:38-41 and get_started promise; an agent trusting it ships a problem/cause/plan arc on a product update.

Merged findings from other review areas:
- [best-practices-research] plan_deck never plans agenda, dividers or appendix; no appendix kind or A-numbering: Principle: a consulting deck has five parts — cover, executive summary, body in sections with dividers/tracker, next steps, appendix of backup pages (Slideworks, https://slideworks.io/resources/how-mckinsey-consultants-make-presentations; Winning Presentations on the executive appendix, https://winningpresentations.com/executive-appendix-backup-slides/); agenda + dividers give the audience the horizontal logic. Repo: `plan_deck --format deckspec` output for a 10-slide board brief (run in this review) contained no `structure.sections`, no `agenda`, no `section` and no appendix slot — internal/deckplan/deckspec_plan.go:68-76 is a flat cover→answer→…→next_steps list; `auto_agenda` is opt-in and only works with 2+ hand-written sections (internal/semantic/sections.go:33); `SEMANTIC_RHYTHM_SECTIONING` nudges only above 10 body slides (internal/semantic/rhythm.go:21-37); there is no `appendix` kind (internal/semantic/kinds.go:12-67 — 'appendix' appears only in a title-exemption list at cmd/json2pptx/fit_findings_balance.go:196), dividers are auto-numbered 01/02 with no A1/A2 restart, and page numbering cannot distinguish backup pages. QUALITY.md:13 tells agents to 'put backup material in an appendix section' with no way to express it. Why it matters: the planner is the recommended entry point; whatever it omits, agents omit.

ACCEPTANCE:

title: Enforce action titles: weight TITLE_NOT_ACTION, add length/topic-title checks, exempt closers
description:
A 9-slide raw deck alternating 7-bullet 'content' slides with kpi-4up/chart slides, every content title a topic label ('Revenue Overview', 'Margin Analysis', 'Pipeline', 'Churn'), no source on any of the 3 data slides, no executive summary, and a 'Thank you / Questions?' closing scores 99/100 and quality_gate.passed=true with reasons=[] (scratchpad/review/agent-guidance/mixed.json -> score_mixed.json). The scorer did emit 5x TITLE_NOT_ACTION, 3x DATA_WITHOUT_SOURCE and 1x MISSING_ALT_TEXT, but all are severity info, and info weighs 0 (tool description cmd/json2pptx/mcp_score_deck.go:31 'Weights: refuse=25, shrink_or_split=15, review=5, info=0'). DefaultQualityGateCriteria (internal/visualqa/deterministic/checker.go:212-222) checks only min_score, P0/P1 counts, substantive reviews, takeaway-on-charts, accent_overload, composition and problem-slide share; nothing about action titles, sources, an executive summary, a next-steps closer, or walls of bullets below the 6-in-a-row DECK_MONOTONY threshold (the all-bullets deck bullets.json failed only via DECK_MONOTONY, score 96). Meanwhile the same gate blocks a well-formed QBR DeckSpec for four exec-summary BODY_TOO_LONG 'substantive review' findings (score_qbr.json: 92, gate false). The gate therefore steers agents toward structurally clean but consulting-poor decks and away from good ones: TOOLS.md:69 tells agents 'A passing quality_gate stops score-driven repair'.

Merged findings from other review areas:
- [best-practices-research] Enforce action titles: topic titles and 20-word titles pass validate and the score gate: Principle: a consulting slide title is a full-sentence conclusion, max ~15 words / 2 lines, carrying its number (Deckary consulting slide standards: 'Maximum 15 words', 'Never exceed two lines', https://deckary.com/blog/consulting-slide-standards; Slideworks on McKinsey action titles; Minto Pyramid 'the point above summarises those below', https://modelthinkers.com/mental-model/minto-pyramid-scqa). QUALITY.md:15-31 states the same rule (<=15 words, full sentence, number). Enforcement in code is near-zero: `TITLE_NOT_ACTION` (cmd/json2pptx/fit_findings_balance.go:191-289) fires only when the title has FEWER than 4 words, no digit and no verb from a ~70-word lexicon, and its action is `info` (0 points, excluded from the breadth penalty at checker.go:377-406); `HEADLINE_TOO_LONG` (>12 words, fit_findings_content_lint.go:18-27) fires only when the title was NOT measured against a real placeholder (:96-98), so on every normal render it is skipped; `TITLE_TOO_LONG` is 'more than 2 rendered lines' (-5). Evidence: scratchpad/review/best-practices-research/topic-titles.yaml with titles 'Executive Summary', 'Key Metrics', a 20-word/105-char topic title and a 'Thank you' closer: `json2pptx semantic validate` returned `ok: true` with only three SEMANTIC_TAKEAWAY_REQUIRED warnings (no title finding at all); `score` gave 96 and passed the gate, with TITLE_NOT_ACTION as info only. plan_deck's `__FILL__` titles carry no word/verb constraint (internal/deckplan/deckspec_plan.go:68-76). Why it matters: the title is the single highest-leverage element of a consulting slide; the skill tells agents the rule, but nothing in the loop pushes back when they ignore it.
- [agent-guidance] TITLE_NOT_ACTION fires on the next_steps closer ('Next steps') although QUALITY.md exempts closing slides: QUALITY.md:30 says 'Cover, section and closing slides may keep short labels' and the next_steps kind is documented as 'the closer a consulting deck ends on' (kinds.go:248). Yet every render of the review QBR reports info TITLE_NOT_ACTION at slides[9].title for 'Next steps' (qbr_midnight-blue/render.json; also in score_qbr.json). An agent following the rubric (WORKFLOW.md Phase 4 check 1, P1) rewrites the closer title into a sentence, which is not how consulting decks close; the finding is noise on the recommended path.

ACCEPTANCE:
score_deck's gate (or at minimum its overall_score) penalises: (a) TITLE_NOT_ACTION on content slides, (b) DATA_WITHOUT_SOURCE on chart/KPI/table slides, (c) a deck of >=6 slides without an executive_summary/exec-summary slide, (d) a closing that is a plain 'Thank you' title/closing with no next-steps, (e) a bullets-only slide with >=6 bullets ('wall of bullets') even when the run is shorter than 6. The mixed.json deck in the review scratchpad must fail the gate with at least one of these reasons; the rendered QBR DeckSpec (qbr_raw.json) must still pass. SKILL.md/FINDINGS.md updated to list the new gate reasons.
A content-slide title (a) >15 words, or (b) with no finite verb AND no digit regardless of word count, or (c) matching a stock label (Overview, Summary, Key Metrics, Next Steps, Thank you) draws a `review`-weighted finding (not `info`) in validate_input, validate_deck_spec and score_deck, with fix hints; cover/section/agenda titles are exempt; `next_steps` is recommended over a 'Thank you' closing via a finding. Tests cover the four shipped examples in QUALITY.md's do/don't table.
TITLE_NOT_ACTION skips slides whose kind is next_steps/closing/section/title/agenda (and raw slides using the next-steps pattern); the review QBR renders with zero TITLE_NOT_ACTION findings.

title: Native chart path parity: labelled/decluttered defaults, sort option and horizontal bars like the pattern path
description:
The same bar data rendered two ways on one deck: in a `body` placeholder (raw chart path) and inside `chart-insights-split`. The placeholder version has no value labels, a full y-axis with ticks and 6 gridlines, 10pt tick labels and an 11pt centred bold title (.../charts-diagrams/out/charts-deck-midnight-blue/slide-01.png, slide-02.png, slide-03.png; same on p-style slide-01.png and abstract slide-01.png). The pattern version of the identical data is labelled mode: values on every bar, no value axis, a thin baseline, 12pt category labels and a 14pt title (.../out/charts-deck-midnight-blue/slide-16.png, slide-17.png). Root cause: internal/patterns/chart_insights_split.go:756-779 `chartWithDataLabels` turns `Style.ShowValues` on by default for label-friendly chart types with few points, and svggen's `applyLabelledMode` (svggen/charts.go:343-359) then drops the axis and gridlines. The raw placeholder path (internal/generator/chart_render.go builds the RequestEnvelope from `spec.Style` only; DefaultChartConfig in svggen/charts.go:224-239 sets ShowValues:false, ShowGrid:true, ShowLegend:true) never applies that default, and neither SKILL.md nor RULES.md/RAW_PATH.md mention `show_values`/`data_labels` (grep returns nothing), so a raw-path agent ships the weaker chart every time. Every examples/*.json chart and examples/diagrams/*.json uses this path. Expected (consulting standard): single-series bars and short lines carry direct value labels and drop the value axis by default on both paths; the raw path should share `dataLabelsByDefault`. Why it matters: it is the default on the most common data slide and is visibly inferior to what the same engine already produces one pattern away.

Merged findings from other review areas:
- [best-practices-research] Bar charts: no sort, no horizontal form, native path defaults to gridlines/axis/no labels: Principles: Zelazny's item comparison ('larger than / smaller than') is drawn as a HORIZONTAL bar chart sorted by value (Say It With Charts, https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/say-it-with/9780071369978/); Knaflic's declutter list: remove gridlines, label data directly, order categories by value (Storytelling with Data, https://www.shortform.com/blog/cole-nussbaumer-knaflic-storytelling-with-data/); Tufte's data-ink ratio. Repo state: (1) no sort option anywhere — svggen/chart_schemas.go:102-111 exposes only `highlight`; the only `sort` call in svggen/charts.go (line 1731) orders line-end labels; (2) `BarChartConfig.Horizontal` (svggen/charts.go:297) is never set by any diagram and only read at :630, so ranked horizontal bars cannot be produced even though svggen/capabilities.go:79 recommends 'horizontal-bar-with-callouts'; (3) `DefaultChartConfig` is `ShowAxes:true, ShowGrid:true, ShowValues:false` (charts.go:240-246), so a native `bar_chart` renders gridlines + value axis + no labels, whereas the chart-insights-split pattern turns labels on by default for <=16 points (internal/patterns/chart_insights_split.go:172, :755-778) and gets the clean 'labelled layout' (no gridlines, zero baseline, 60% bars, charts.go:350-404). Evidence: scratchpad/review/best-practices-research/charts/slide-1.png (7 countries in alphabetical order, gridlines, axis, no value labels — the title says 'Germany is largest, ahead of France' but the eye has to hunt) vs qbr-midnight-blue/slide-4.png (same engine, pattern path: labelled, decluttered). Why it matters: the two most common evidence charts in a deck — a ranking and a time series — look like Excel defaults on the raw/native path and inconsistent with pattern slides in the same deck.
- [charts-diagrams] Bar chart schema advertises a horizontal variant that no field can request: svggen/chart_schemas.go:107 describes bar data as 'Supports grouped, stacked, and horizontal variants' and BarChartConfig has a `Horizontal` flag (svggen/charts.go:296-297, honoured in fallBackFromCollidingDirectLabels :630), but neither `style` nor `data` exposes it: `style.horizontal` is rejected as an unknown field (probe .../charts-diagrams/probe.json slide 2: `unknown field "horizontal" at /slides/1/content/1/chart_value/style/horizontal`) and get_data_format_hints lists no such key. The only horizontal bars an agent can get are via the `horizontal-bar-with-callouts` pattern. Ranked category comparisons with long labels (e.g. the 7 cost functions in .../out/charts-deck-midnight-blue/slide-02.png, whose labels wrap to two 10pt lines) are the textbook case for horizontal bars. Why it matters: the capability text sends agents looking for a knob that does not exist, and long-label rankings stay vertical.

ACCEPTANCE:
1) A raw `slide_type: chart` bar with <= cisDataLabelMaxPts points and no explicit style renders in labelled mode (values on bars, no value axis/gridlines) identical to the chart-insights-split version of the same data; 2) the same default applies to single-series line/area with <= 12 points; 3) `style.show_values:false` or `data.data_labels:false` still opts out; 4) SKILL.md/RULES.md state the default and the opt-out; 5) a golden/parity test compares raw vs pattern rendering of one dataset.
`data.sort: "desc"|"asc"|"none"` exists for single-series bar/horizontal bar and defaults to `desc` when categories are not time-like (reuse `timeCategoryRe`), keeping `highlight` by name; `type: horizontal_bar` (or `orientation: horizontal`) renders and is recommended by recommend_visual for 'rank/largest/top N' intents; native bar/line charts with <=16 points use the labelled layout by default on all paths (gridlines off, direct labels on), matching the pattern path; SKILL.md/RULES.md and docs/FIT_FINDINGS.md updated.
1) Either `style.orientation: "horizontal"` (or `data.horizontal: true`) is accepted for bar/grouped_bar/stacked_bar and renders horizontal bars with labelled mode, or the schema text and capability hints stop claiming the variant; 2) get_data_format_hints and SKILL.md document the chosen option; 3) DensityBehavior for bar recommends horizontal orientation when category labels exceed ~14 chars.

title: Readable-ink fix paints pattern text pure black on accent fills instead of darkening the fill
description:
Patterns write lt1 text on accent fills (value-chain, process-flow, pyramid, stylish-panels headers, strategy-house banner, numbered-step-strip badges, swimlane, timeline...). ApplyReadableInk (internal/patterns/ink_fix.go:51-75) and readableInkOn (internal/patterns/fill_contrast.go:254, 269-292) try lt1 -> dk2 -> dk1 against WCAG 4.5:1 for any text under 14pt bold / 18pt. For 12-13pt labels (numbered-step-strip labelSize 13pt numbered_step_strip.go:420/753, stylish-panels body 14pt, pyramid/process-flow 11-13pt) this fails on the primary accent of 5 of 10 shipped templates: abstract 8E8172 white=3.8 -> dk1; warm-coral E64A19 white=3.9 -> dk1; blue-corporate 55BC7E 2.4 -> dk1; business-template AD84C6 3.0 -> dk1; p-style FD5108 3.3 -> dk2 (=000000). With accent_strategy rotate, accent2-6 flip to black on nearly every template (midnight-blue D4463A/43A047 -> dk1, modern E89756/7E7E7E -> dk1, modern-template 4A7AB5/C06B3F/9E8520 -> dk1). Full ratio table in review/typography-color/contrast.py output. Result is bold black type on saturated orange/taupe boxes — exactly the 'off-brand black' the fixer's own comment (text_contrast.go:270-274, fill_contrast.go:249-253) says it wants to avoid; dk2 only helps when dk2 is dark and the accent is light. PNG evidence: acc-abstract/slide-2.png (process-flow, black on taupe), acc-abstract/slide-3.png (pyramid), acc-abstract/slide-5.png (strategy-house banner), acc-abstract/slide-6.png (badges), acc-warm-coral/slide-4.png, acc-warm-coral/slide-5.png, acc-warm-coral/slide-6.png (black on E64A19), acc-p-style/slide-3.png, acc-p-style/slide-4.png, acc-p-style/slide-5.png (black on FD5108). Expected (consulting-grade): the fill is engine-drawn, so when lt1 misses the bar the engine should first shade the FILL (a:shade / darker lumMod) until lt1 clears 4.5:1 — keeping the hue and white type — and only then fall back to a dark ink; pure dk1 #000000 should never be chosen when dk2 is distinct, and label text that is 14pt bold already clears 3:1 so patterns could also lift sub-14pt bold labels to the 14pt subhead step before recolouring.

ACCEPTANCE:
On abstract, warm-coral, blue-corporate, business-template and p-style, value-chain / process-flow / pyramid / stylish-panels / strategy-house / numbered-step-strip default renders show no #000000 text on an accent fill: either white text on a shaded accent that measures >= 4.5:1 (or >= 3:1 for >= 14pt bold), or dk2 where dk2 is not black. A unit test asserts readableInkOn / the shape-grid fixer never returns dk1 for a saturated accent (chroma above a threshold) while a fill shade exists that lets lt1 pass. SKILL.md/RULES.md describe the behaviour.

title: decision / executive_summary kinds render two stacked near-duplicate conclusion callouts (examples and qbr.yaml author b
description:
The built-in list_slide_kinds examples (internal/semantic/kind_examples.go) give executive_summary both bottom_line AND takeaway, and decision both recommendation AND takeaway; examples/semantic/qbr.yaml does the same for its decision slide. SplitConclusion (internal/semantic/slides/conclusion.go:15-25) only collapses them when they are near-duplicates (>=85% overlap), so the pattern renders its own callout band (recommendation / bottom line) AND the generator adds the slide takeaway band beneath it (decision.go:133-147, content.go:39). Result: two bold accent-bar one-liners stacked 50px apart saying almost the same thing, at DIFFERENT x indents (abstract: 78px vs 118px; midnight-blue 113 vs 108). Evidence: abstract/slide-04.png, abstract/slide-12.png, abstract/slide-32.png (QBR decision), modern-yellow/slide-12.png, warm-coral/slide-32.png, p-style/slide-04.png (second bar pushed to the slide bottom with a 100px gap). An agent copying the example as recommended produces this on every decision and exec-summary slide. A consulting slide has one bottom line.

Merged findings from other review areas:
- [best-practices-research] Decision / exec-summary kinds render two near-duplicate conclusion bands on one slide: Principle: one message per slide; redundant ink lowers the signal-to-noise ratio (McKinsey one-message rule, https://deckary.com/blog/consulting-slide-standards; Reynolds SNR; Tufte redundant data-ink). Repo: internal/semantic/slides/decision.go:133-147 places `recommendation` in the callout band and, unless `DuplicateConclusion` says they are the same, the `takeaway` in a second identical-style band; `DuplicateConclusion` (internal/semantic/slides/conclusion.go:27-50) only treats them as duplicates when the shorter is >= 85% the length of the longer AND a verbatim substring — ordinary paraphrases pass. content.go:129,207 does the same for `executive_summary` `bottom_line` + `takeaway`. Evidence: the shipped example examples/semantic/qbr.yaml renders slide 5 with two stacked accent-bar bands: 'Stand up a dedicated SMB customer-success pod in Q3 to arrest churn before it compounds.' and 'Fund a dedicated SMB success pod now to protect net retention.' (scratchpad/review/best-practices-research/qbr-midnight-blue/slide-5.png; same in warm-coral and p-style). The title already says 'Fund an SMB success pod in Q3…', so the message appears three times. Why it matters: the flagship example teaches agents that doubling the so-what is correct, and the two bands eat the whitespace the options need.

ACCEPTANCE:
(1) kind_examples and qbr.yaml carry either a takeaway or a bottom_line/recommendation, not both, and SKILL.md says takeaway is the fallback when the kind has its own conclusion field. (2) When both are present, the compiler emits a single band (the pattern's) or the takeaway as a muted second line inside it; validation warns SEMANTIC_DUPLICATE_CONCLUSION (or similar) when both are authored. (3) Rendered decision/exec-summary slides show exactly one accent-bar callout.
When a decision/executive_summary carries both a kind-level conclusion and a `takeaway`, the compiler renders one band by default (recommendation wins; takeaway is kept as speaker note or merged) unless `takeaway` differs by a token-overlap test (e.g. Jaccard < 0.4 after stopword removal); otherwise emit `SEMANTIC_DUPLICATE_CONCLUSION` (warning) at `slides[N].takeaway`; examples/semantic/qbr.yaml is updated so the decision slide renders a single band.

title: Quadratic autofit trimming: a 14 KB deck with 2000 bullets pins a core for 3+ minutes
description:
internal/generator/text_autofit.go:486 trimOverflowParagraphs drops ONE trailing paragraph per iteration and re-runs textfit.Calculate over all remaining paragraphs (each call re-shapes every word and rebuilds the harfbuzz shape plan). O(n^2): 500 bullets 13 s, 1000 51 s, 2000 196 s, 4000 >300 s (CLI generate; MCP generate_presentation/make_deck/auto_repair). Not interruptible by ctx within a slide (singlepass.go:217-235). HTTP /convert is unaffected (paginates).
Fix: binary-search the paragraph count or measure per-paragraph heights once and cumulative-sum (O(n log n) / O(n)); reuse one shaper/face per placeholder; add a validation cap (e.g. 200 paragraphs per placeholder -> BODY_TOO_LONG). Add a benchmark/regression test with 2000 bullets asserting < 5 s.

title: Every chart/diagram inside a shape_grid cell (i.e. every named pattern) ships a 128px PNG fallback at 17–22 DPI with ALL text dropped — Google Slides/Keynote/older PowerPoint/thumbnail pipelines show an unlabelled blob
description: chart-insights-split: image1.svg 700x419 -> fallback image2.png 128x77 placed at 7.29x4.36in (17.6 DPI, no axis labels/ticks/categories). Full-slide charts are fine (1875x775, 163 DPI). Output validator warns below 96 DPI. Real chart-insights-split before/after inspected: 128px no labels vs 1094px with Q1-Q4, values, axis labels. Unit/e2e tests cover pixel labels and DPI warning. Full suite, lint, build pass; deterministic basic-deck hashes unchanged. Follow-up preflight parity: go-slide-creator-542qg.

title: process-flow-compact with type:"chevron" renders every label one character per line (B/a/s/e/l/i/n/e) on all templates — the compact variant never got the chevronMaxAspectH cap (go-slide-creator-czk4 fixed process-flow only) and the chevron insets stack on top of the preset's own text rect, leaving ~3pt of text width
description: OOXML: prst=chevron cx=156pt cy=122pt adj=30000, bodyPr lIns/rIns=39.7pt each side (+ preset notch 36.7pt) => ~3pt. process-flow emits cy=78 (height <= width/2). Fix: apply the pointed cap in the compact variant (cap Bounds.Height to cellW*0.5 in zone %) and subtract the preset text rect before adding insets. Evidence: /tmp/review/pattern-render/pfc-all.png (3-way proof), z-pfc-mb45.png; copied to .claude/review-evidence/r3/pattern-render/.
notes: Fixed compact pointed process-flow geometry: when any step is chevron/rightArrow, the band is capped at half a resolved step width; both process-flow variants now emit only 3pt bodyPr padding because the preset text rectangle already reserves the notch/point width. Removed the obsolete notch helper. Added unit regression for all-pointed and mixed rows and an integration check of resolved cell aspect, centering, and emitted XML insets. Verification: focused tests, full internal/patterns suite, TemplatePatternMatrix, full golangci-lint (0 issues), go test ./... -short -race (pass; cmd/json2pptx 481s). Adversarial and testing reviews found no remaining high-confidence issue in this change.
close_reason: Closed

title: LibreOffice ignores the SVG CSS `font:` shorthand, so every render-based QA surface (render_slide_image, inspect, audit_palette, pptx2jpg) shows chart text at one default size/weight — agents chase label collisions PowerPoint will not have and never see the real 9pt ticks

Any bead in this epic whose only evidence is a soffice PNG of SVG text fit should be re-verified with rsvg/resvg before closing.
close_reason: Emitted explicit SVG font-size/font-weight/font-family alongside CSS shorthand, covered normal/bold/multi-family cases, regenerated goldens with declaration-only diffs, and passed both Go module short suites, lint, and builds.

title: generate ships a deck whose only section divider is labelled "02": evaluateStrictFit never sees refuse-class substance findings that validate reports
description:
Why: a real host-agent deck (outputs/…/state-of-agentic-ai-mid-2026.json, slide 4 `layout_id: section` with authored Section Number "02" and no "01") passes `generate --strict-fit=strict` (success:true, finding absent) while `validate --json --fit-report` reports INPUT.SECTION_NUMBER_SEQUENCE_MISMATCH severity=error action=refuse (envelope ok:false) and top-level valid:true. Three verdicts for one input; the shipped deck is mis-numbered — a no-go for a client deck.
Root cause: cmd/json2pptx/fit_report.go:48 evaluateStrictFit() gates on generateFitReport() + two ad-hoc local preflights (tablePreflightLocalFindings, chartDryRenderLocalFindings — each added after an earlier escape, oaif/rrjj) instead of collectFitFindings() (fit_findings_collect.go:33) which carries collectSectionNumberSequenceFindings (fit_findings_substance.go:37), exemplar-copy refuse findings, contrast prediction etc. MCP generate_presentation uses the same gate (mcp.go:418). docs/FIT_FINDINGS.md:146 claims "Emitted at: … generate" — false.
Fix (atomic): gate evaluateStrictFit on collectFitFindings and delete the two local appends; in warn mode auto-correct an authored numeric divider label to the injected sequence (injectSectionNumber, json_mode.go:886) and emit `section_number_renumbered` (info); make validate `valid:false` whenever any action=refuse finding exists so valid and ok agree. Test: for every examples/*.json, refuse-class findings from validate also refuse under generate --strict-fit=strict.
Evidence: .claude/review-evidence/r3/orchestrator-ledger.md O5; .claude/review-evidence/r3/pattern-render/real_grid.png (slide 4).

Seven parallel reviewers (mcp-contract, semantic-dogfood, advisory-tools, quality-signals, template-portability, charts-diagrams, layout-sweep) plus a real host-agent deck from outputs/. Close children only with rendered before/after evidence where the finding is visual.

title: BUG: semantic validate and explain must surface template resolution failures
description:
Location: cmd/json2pptx/semantic_layout_coverage.go semanticTemplateLayouts, cmd/json2pptx/semantic_cmd.go validate/explain, and cmd/json2pptx/mcp_semantic.go validate/explain compiledSpecFindings.

Problem: semanticTemplateLayouts returns ok=false for every template resolution or analysis error. Callers silently skip template-aware checks, so a DeckSpec that pins a nonexistent or unreadable template can pass json2pptx semantic validate and validate_deck_spec, and explain reports a normal plan. Rendering then fails later. The same silence also suppresses required-layout availability diagnostics.

Change: return a structured TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND or TEMPLATE_ERROR diagnostic at meta.template when template resolution or analysis fails. CLI validate and MCP validate_deck_spec must include it as blocking. CLI and MCP explain must fail with the shared diagnostic envelope rather than claiming a usable plan. Keep valid template behavior and required-layout coverage unchanged.

Verification: tests cover missing registered name and template analysis failure where feasible across CLI validate/explain and MCP validate/explain; assert exact code/path and non-success. Existing valid template and required-layout tests pass.
acceptance_criteria: Unknown or unreadable templates can no longer pass semantic validate or explain; CLI and MCP emit path-scoped template diagnostics; valid templates retain current coverage behavior.
close_reason: Semantic CLI/MCP validate and explain now emit blocking TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND/TEMPLATE_ERROR diagnostics at meta.template; optional deferred templates remain supported.

title: DEFECT: publish discoverable required layout enums and closed structured MCP schema
description:
Location: internal/semantic/schema.go deckMetaSchema, CompactInlineSchema, compactStructuredSlideSchemas, and cmd/json2pptx/mcp_semantic.go withDeckSpecSchema.

Problem: meta.required_layouts is described as canonical IDs but its item schema accepts any string, so agents cannot discover allowed values. In addition, CompactInlineSchema replaces cover, closing, and section slide payloads with a kind-only open outline even on validate_deck_spec, despite that tool claiming the full closed contract. Typos can pass MCP client-side validation on the structured path while equivalent flat slides are rejected.

Change: expose the canonical layout enum from the layout registry in required_layouts items. Preserve the complete closed per-kind payload contract for structured slides in validate_deck_spec while remaining inside tools/list budget, preferably by retaining local defs and rewriting refs to the nested spec path instead of duplicating unions. Keep outline schemas only on tools that intentionally advertise an outline.

Verification: schema tests assert the enum exactly matches canonical layout IDs, structured slide payloads reject unknown fields through the MCP input schema, all local refs resolve, and tools/list payload budget plus schema fingerprint tests pass.
acceptance_criteria: Agents can discover all canonical required layout IDs from schema; validate_deck_spec has equally closed flat and structured slide contracts; every ref resolves and MCP payload budgets remain green.
close_reason: Published required_layouts enum now follows the canonical registry; validate_deck_spec uses a rebased closed $defs schema for flat and structured payloads within the 100 KiB core tools budget.

title: BUG: headline only satisfies title checks when it renders on a blank canvas
description:
Location: cmd/json2pptx/fit_findings_substance.go collectSubstanceFindings and collectSlideSubstanceFindings.

Problem: any non-empty slide.headline suppresses MISSING_TITLE on every layout, but headline is rendered only when isBlankCanvasLayout is true. Conversely, after layout resolution a real blank layout can have a concrete slideLayoutN ID and the suggested repair path incorrectly says title instead of headline because validation calls isBlankCanvasLayout with nil layout metadata.

Change: pass resolved layout metadata into substance validation and count headline only when the slide resolves to a true blank canvas. Use the same resolved predicate for the fix path. A headline on content/title layouts must not hide a missing rendered title.

Verification: add tests for a nonblank slide with headline but no title, a canonical blank-canvas slide, and a concrete layout tagged as blank. Assert finding presence and fix path. Run raw validate_input and score_deck parity tests.
acceptance_criteria: Only headlines that the renderer will draw satisfy the visible-title requirement; canonical and concrete blank layouts suggest headline; nonblank layouts still report MISSING_TITLE.
close_reason: Missing-title validation now treats headline as visible only on resolved blank canvases and gives the correct repair path for concrete blank layouts.

title: BUG: expanded structured renders must report accurate slide metadata
description:
Location: cmd/json2pptx/semantic_cmd.go runSemanticRender, cmd/json2pptx/mcp_semantic.go renderDeckSpecHandler, and internal/pipeline manifest helpers.

Problem: both surfaces read len(spec.Slides) after compiling a structure-only DeckSpec. The source slice is empty even though compilation expands cover, agenda, section dividers, section content, and closing slides. CLI authoring manifests therefore contain slides: [] while the PPTX contains slides, and MCP render-start telemetry reports slide_count: 0.

Change: derive rendered slide metadata from the normalized or compiled expanded sequence. Generate stable manifest payloads and one logical entry for every generated slide, retaining source-map paths. Log the expanded count for MCP start and completion events.

Verification: CLI integration test renders a structure-only spec and asserts manifest slide count equals PPTX/result slide count with unique stable IDs; MCP logging test asserts the start event uses the expanded count. Flat-spec metadata must remain unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Structure-only render manifests and MCP telemetry report the actual expanded slide count; logical slide IDs are stable; flat decks retain current behavior.
close_reason: Structured manifest payloads now cover every expanded slide; CLI integration asserts seven manifest entries and MCP telemetry uses expanded counts.

title: BUG: diagnose unknown keys inside semantic structure blocks
description:
Location: internal/semantic/yaml.go alongside checkUnknownTopLevel and checkUnknownMeta.

Problem: unknown keys in structure and structure.sections[] are silently dropped by typed unmarshalling. Examples include structure.typo_field and structure.sections[0].slidez. This disagrees with additionalProperties:false in the published schema and can turn authored content into an apparently empty section.

Change: define the supported structure and section key sets, scan the generic document before building DeckSpec, emit SEMANTIC_UNKNOWN_FIELD at exact paths, and provide close-spelling suggestions where useful.

Verification: JSON and YAML tests for unknown structure and section fields, including a slidez typo suggestion; assert known fields do not report findings and CLI validate exposes the paths.
acceptance_criteria: Unknown structure and section keys are never silently discarded; diagnostics identify exact paths and likely spelling fixes; valid structured specs remain clean.
close_reason: Structured and section unknown keys now emit SEMANTIC_UNKNOWN_FIELD with exact paths and typo suggestions.

title: BUG: reject explicit empty slides together with semantic structure
description:
Location: internal/semantic/yaml.go buildDeckSpec, internal/semantic/spec.go DeckSpec, and internal/semantic/validate.go Validate.

Problem: the structured DeckSpec XOR check tests len(spec.Slides) > 0. A parsed document containing slides: [] and structure: {...} therefore bypasses STRUCTURE_AND_SLIDES even though both top-level forms are present and the JSON Schema rejects that shape.

Change: retain top-level field presence during parsing and validate mutual exclusion by presence, including an explicit empty slides array. Keep programmatic DeckSpec construction behavior compatible where field presence is unknowable.

Verification: add JSON and YAML Parse plus Check tests with valid metadata and a valid structured section alongside slides: []; assert one path-scoped mutual-exclusion error and CLI validate failure. Confirm structure-only and flat-only specs still pass.
acceptance_criteria: Parsed JSON and YAML with both slides and structure fail even when slides is empty; structure-only and flat-only inputs remain valid; CLI and semantic package tests pass.
close_reason: Parser now preserves explicit slides field presence and validation rejects slides: [] plus structure in JSON and YAML.

title: BUG: return path-scoped diagnostics for malformed structured containers
description:
Location: internal/semantic/yaml.go validateContainerShapes and structured parsing.

Problem: malformed nested structure containers such as structure.sections: wrong, a scalar section entry, section.slides: wrong, or scalar cover/closing values fall through to typed decoding and return an opaque root INPUT.INVALID_JSON message with Go decoder type names. Agents cannot identify or repair the failing path.

Change: extend the generic shape pass to validate structure.cover, structure.closing, structure.sections, every section object, and every section.slides array before typed decoding. Emit stable path-scoped semantic parse diagnostics with friendly JSON shape names.

Verification: table-driven JSON and YAML tests for every malformed nested container; assert exact evidence paths and that messages do not expose semantic.rawSection or Go type names. Exercise json2pptx semantic validate for at least one YAML case.
acceptance_criteria: All malformed nested structure containers fail with their exact source path and friendly expected/actual shapes; no opaque typed-unmarshal error remains for these cases.
close_reason: Generic parse gate now reports exact paths for malformed cover, closing, sections, section entries, and section slides containers, including null.

title: BUG: use complete matching for required layout coverage
description:
Location: internal/semantic/layout_coverage.go applyRequiredLayoutCoverage and internal/semantic/layout_coverage_test.go.

Problem: required layout assignment greedily takes the first compatible unused slide. When one slide can satisfy multiple layouts and another can satisfy only one, request order can report SEMANTIC_REQUIRED_LAYOUT_MISSING even though a complete assignment exists. Example: requested [content, blank-title], slides [pattern KPI, table]. The KPI can satisfy either layout and the table can satisfy content only. Greedy assigns KPI to content and falsely misses blank-title.

Change: replace first-fit assignment with deterministic bipartite matching or an augmenting-path algorithm. Preserve requested order in LayoutCoverage.Assigned, keep one slide per requested layout, and apply Visual.Layout mutations only from the final match.

Verification: add a regression test for the counterexample and a permutation test showing request and slide order cannot create a false missing result. Run go test ./internal/semantic -count=1 and semantic validate/explain coverage tests.
acceptance_criteria: A compatible complete assignment produces no missing layouts; assignments remain deterministic and one-to-one; the counterexample and existing coverage tests pass.
close_reason: Replaced greedy first-fit with deterministic augmenting-path matching; regression proves content/blank-title counterexample assigns completely.

title: Section dividers: prevent wrapped titles from clipping the number placeholder
description:
## What

A section-divider title that wraps in the shipped midnight-blue and warm-coral layouts destabilizes the neighbouring large section-number placeholder in LibreOffice rendering. A short title renders 02 centered and fully visible; What leaders should do wraps and moves 02 upward/right so it is clipped by the slide edge. The generated XML uses the same layout and number bounds as the clean first divider, isolating the trigger to title fit.

## Steps to Reproduce

Render skills/generate-deck/examples/layout-coverage-deckspec.md to PPTX and JPG. Slide 3 (Where the market is / 01) is clean. Slide 6 (What leaders should do / 02) wraps and clips. Replacing the second title with Leadership actions makes 02 render correctly. Reproduces on midnight-blue and warm-coral.

## Where

- internal/generator/text_population.go section-title sizing order
- internal/generator/text_helpers.go maxFontForWordFit and boostSectionTitleFont
- internal/generator/text_population_test.go
- section-divider rendered regression fixture on two templates

## How

Keep section headings within the horizontal title band when they can remain readable on one line. Apply prominence boosting before the final width cap so boostSectionTitleFont cannot undo a safe cap. Add a conservative full-line estimate in addition to longest-word protection, with the section-title readability floor and normal autofit retained for genuinely long copy. Do not change ordinary slide titles or the decorative number size.

## Verification

- What leaders should do is fitted inside the title placeholder without wrapping into the number region.
- 01 and 02 remain fully visible and centered on midnight-blue and warm-coral JPG renders.
- Short section titles preserve the template's prominent size.
- Extremely long titles retain readable autofit behavior and emit existing fit findings when necessary.
- Unit tests cover sizing order and whole-line cap; generator, CLI render, and full regression tests pass.
acceptance_criteria: Readable section titles fit the title band without causing the adjacent section number to move or clip; short titles stay prominent; two-template rendered evidence shows complete 01/02.
close_reason: Implemented the specified schema, compiler, validation, rendering, MCP/CLI, documentation, and skill changes. Verified with go test ./..., go build ./..., golangci-lint (0 issues), skill canonical check, bead lint, all-seven-layout semantic render, template-missing coverage unit test, and midnight-blue/warm-coral JPG inspection for divider numbers and blank-canvas strategy-house headline clearance.

title: Semantic structure: preserve planned native layout on every generated divider
description:
## What

Generated structural slides drop the planner's canonical Layout field during semantic lowering. In the worked structured DeckSpec, Explain reports both dividers as layout: section, but compiled JSON gives layout_id: section only to the divider selected by required_layouts; the other carries only slide_type: section and relies on heuristic selection. Title and closing structural compilers have the same explain-to-compile gap.

## Steps to Reproduce

Compile skills/generate-deck/examples/layout-coverage-deckspec.md with --envelope. Compare explanation_summary / semantic explain with compiled_json: the second section divider is planned as section but omits layout_id.

## Where

- internal/semantic/slides/structural.go
- internal/semantic/compile.go required-layout override precedence
- internal/semantic/sections.go generated structural slides
- semantic explain/compile parity tests

## How

Structural compilers should copy Input.Layout into layout_id when the structural form is compatible: title, section, and non-bulleted closing. A required-layout assignment remains authoritative after compilation. A bulleted closing that deliberately lowers to content must retain its content fallback. raw_json2pptx concrete layout IDs remain untouched.

## Verification

- Two structured dividers both compile with layout_id: section.
- Title and simple closing compile with title/closing layout IDs.
- Bulleted closing retains its content fallback.
- Required-layout coverage can still override a compatible slide.
- raw_json2pptx concrete layout IDs are unchanged.
- Explain and compile layout parity tests pass, plus CLI/MCP semantic tests.
acceptance_criteria: Structural semantic slides preserve compatible planned layouts; deliberate content fallbacks and raw concrete layouts remain unchanged; required-layout overrides still win; explain and compile agree.
close_reason: Implemented the specified schema, compiler, validation, rendering, MCP/CLI, documentation, and skill changes. Verified with go test ./..., go build ./..., golangci-lint (0 issues), skill canonical check, bead lint, all-seven-layout semantic render, template-missing coverage unit test, and midnight-blue/warm-coral JPG inspection for divider numbers and blank-canvas strategy-house headline clearance.

title: generate-deck skill: add narrative-first layout-coverage workflow and visual-quality rubric
description:
## What
Add a dedicated workflow and review rubric to the generate-deck skill for prompts that require both a substantive narrative and coverage of template layouts or pattern types.

Current failure mode: the author maps one requested layout to one slide, producing a seven-slide fixture rather than a complete presentation. Pixel review then checks clipping and overlap but accepts weak hierarchy, large dead zones, unsupported section numbering, and a narrow visual vocabulary.

## Where
- skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md: planning, semantic-default path, completion protocol
- skills/generate-deck/WORKFLOW.md: Plan, Vary, Render, Repair
- skills/generate-deck/RULES.md: content/layout and blank-canvas rules
- skills/generate-deck/examples or examples/four-phase-workflow.md
- mirrored/generated skill copies if enforced by repository sync tests

## How
Document a `layout coverage` branch of the workflow:
1. Build the story and section outline first, independently of coverage.
2. Choose a slide budget appropriate to the word "complete"; do not equate layout count with slide count.
3. Map required layouts into compatible narrative roles and allow repeated content layouts.
4. Use DeckSpec by default; use raw JSON only for the minimum unsupported coverage requirement.
5. Never manually author a numeric section placeholder when automatic numbering is available.
6. A content-bearing blank canvas must include an authored, visible headline inside its composition.
7. Require evidence diversity appropriate to the topic: data visuals, diagrams, screenshots/images when they explain something, and purposeful structural slides.
8. Treat composition, underfill, title, and rhythm findings as review inputs even when informational.

Expand final visual review beyond defect detection. title: Validation: require a visible headline on content-bearing blank-canvas slides
description:
## What
Require a visible headline on a blank-canvas slide when that slide carries a pattern, shape grid, compose tree, chart, diagram, image, or other argument content. The current missing-title detector classifies all blank slides as chrome and exempts them, even when the blank canvas contains a substantive visual.

## Steps to Reproduce
Create a slide with `layout_id: blank-canvas`, no content items, and a `strategy-house` pattern. Run `json2pptx validate --fit-report`. The slide passes without `MISSING_TITLE` and renders a large visual with no audience-facing headline.

## Where
- cmd/json2pptx/fit_findings_substance.go: slideCarriesArgument, extractTitleText, patternTitleValue
- raw SlideInput/schema if a universal canvas headline field is needed
- pattern and shape-grid title semantics
- cmd/json2pptx validation, preview, score, and repair paths
- docs/INPUT_FORMAT.md, docs/FIT_FINDINGS.md, skills/generate-deck/RULES.md and FINDINGS.md

## How
Refine `slideCarriesArgument`: an explicitly blank slide is exempt only when it contains no argument content. A blank canvas with pattern/grid/compose/media is content-bearing.

Define one supported way to satisfy the headline requirement without relying on a nonexistent template placeholder. Preferred contract: an optional slide-level `headline` for blank-canvas slides, rendered as a theme-aware title overlay whose reserved bounds are passed to the grid/pattern layout. Alternatively, standardize a machine-readable title role inside pattern/grid content. Do not infer arbitrary bold text as a title.

Emit `MISSING_TITLE` with a fix targeting the supported headline field. Include headline bounds in fit/collision checks so the fix cannot overlap the visual.

## Verification
- Blank canvas + strategy-house without headline emits `MISSING_TITLE` and fails the strict quality gate.
- Adding the supported headline renders it visibly and shifts/resizes the visual into the remaining content zone.
- Intentionally empty interstitial blank slides remain exempt.

- Tests cover pattern, raw shape_grid, compose, image, and truly empty blank cases.

title: Validation: reject numeric section labels that contradict automatic sequence
description:
## What
Detect and refuse numeric section labels that contradict the divider's automatic sequence. Today section numbers are computed in `convertPresentationSlides`, but `injectSectionNumber` is a no-op when the author has already populated the section-number slot. A first divider explicitly containing `02` therefore validates and renders as `02` even though the generator's expected number is `01`.

## Steps to Reproduce
Create a raw PresentationInput with one `layout_id: section` slide whose content targets `Section Number` with text `02`; run `json2pptx validate --fit-report` and generate it. Validation currently passes and the rendered first divider shows 02.

## Where
- cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go: sectionNumbers computation, contentTargetsSectionSlot, injectSectionNumber
- cmd/json2pptx/fit_findings_collect.go or substance/narrative findings
- internal/patterns finding code and metadata
- docs/FIT_FINDINGS.md, skills/generate-deck/FINDINGS.md, docs/SCHEMA_CHANGELOG.md

## How
When a section slide already targets `section_number`, `section_no`, `large_number`, `Section Number`, or the resolved fallback body slot, compare a numeric authored value with the expected sequential number. Normalize leading zeroes for comparison, retain the deck's configured display format, and emit `SECTION_NUMBER_SEQUENCE_MISMATCH` with expected, actual, and slide/section indices. Treat the finding as refuse under strict validation.

Non-numeric labels such as `A`, `PART II`, or custom text must remain supported and should be reported as an explicit custom-numbering mode rather than coerced. Do not silently overwrite authored content.

## Verification
- Repro: one section slide with authored `02` produces a blocking finding expecting `01`.
- Authored `1`, `01`, and the auto-injected value pass for the first divider according to normalization/format rules.
- Two dividers authored `01`, `03` flag only the second and expect `02`.
- Alias IDs and a template that falls back to `body` are covered.
- Custom non-numeric labels retain current behavior.
- Validate, dry-run, generate, CLI JSON, and MCP envelopes expose the same finding.
- Run `go test ./cmd/json2pptx/... ./internal/patterns/...` and `golangci-lint run ./...`.
acceptance_criteria: A first divider authored as 02 fails strict validation with expected 01; aliases and fallback slots are covered; matching numeric values pass; custom non-numeric section labels remain supported; validate and generate diagnostics agree.

description:

title: timeline-horizontal gantt/chevron paints lt1 text on the lightest gradient bar (1.5:1)
description:
WHAT
timeline-horizontal's gantt and chevron styles tint each bar across the chain (buildChevronGradientFill, internal/patterns/timelinehorizontal.go:501) from shade 70000 at the first stop to tint 40000 at the last, but the text inside every bar is hardcoded "color":"lt1" (expandGantt ~line 452, buildChevronTextContent ~line 535). On the lightest bars white-on-tint is unreadable.

EVIDENCE (measured, midnight-blue, 3 gantt stops)
Sampled the rendered PNG inside each bar:
  bar 1 rgb(39,68,123)   vs white = 9.55:1  OK
  bar 2 rgb(46,80,144)   vs white = 7.88:1  OK
  bar 3 rgb(205,208,219) vs white = 1.54:1  FAILS WCAG AA (needs 4.5)
The third bar's date label is effectively invisible. With 5-7 stops more bars land in the failing range.

WHY IT SURVIVED
internal/patterns/fill_contrast.go already has readableTextOn(ctx, tone, fallback) for exactly this, but fillTone models alpha/lumMod/lumOff only — not the tint/shade modifiers this pattern uses. So the pattern could not ask, and the shape-grid contrast pass is warn-only for grid text.

HOW
1. Extend fillTone with Tint/Shade and teach effectiveFillColor the DrawingML a:tint / a:shade transforms (they are not lumMod/lumOff; tint moves toward white, shade toward black, both on luminance).
2. Have expandGantt and buildChevronTextContent (and buildChevronGradientFill's callers generally) pick the text colour with readableTextOn against the bar's own tone instead of hardcoding lt1.
3. The dots style is unaffected (text sits on the slide background).

VERIFY
Render a 7-stop gantt and a 7-stop chevron on all four templates, sample every bar's fill and its text colour, and assert >= 4.5:1 for each; add a table test over the gradient positions so a future gradient change cannot reintroduce it.

FOUND BY
go-slide-creator-wrsb while rendering the new DeckSpec timeline kind, which routes any payload carrying an end_date into gantt.
close_reason:
Fixed (9d943040).

ROOT CAUSE
Two bugs, one symptom. timeline-horizontal's gantt and chevron styles tint each bar across the chain (shade 70000 at the first stop through tint 40000 at the last) and hardcoded "color":"lt1" inside every one of them. The helper for choosing text by measurement already existed — readableTextOn in internal/patterns/fill_contrast.go — but fillTone modelled alpha/lumMod/lumOff only, so a pattern built from tint/shade had no way to ask. tint and shade were simply ignored by the effective-colour model, which is why nothing caught it.

THE COLOUR MODEL
tint and shade are LINEAR-LIGHT mixes toward white and black; they are not the HSL lightness that lumMod/lumOff act on. Both formulas were derived from rendered pixels and then verified against them: midnight-blue accent1 #2E5090 renders rgb(38,67,122) under shade 70000 and rgb(205,208,219) under tint 40000, and only the linear-light model reproduces both (sRGB mixing gives (171,185,211), HSL lightness gives (158,181,224) — out by 30-50 per channel, which is exactly the difference between readable and invisible). EffectiveColorMods now models all four modifiers; EffectiveColor stays as a thin wrapper so no caller changed.

WHAT CHANGED
- internal/patterns/fill_contrast.go: ColorMods + EffectiveColorMods, with applyLinearMix and the sRGB<->linear conversions. fillTone gains Tint/Shade and fillJSON emits them.
- internal/patterns/icon_color.go: parseFillTone reads tint/shade, so every existing contrast assertion sees them.
- internal/patterns/timelinehorizontal.go: buildChevronGradientFill becomes chevronGradientTone, returning the tone rather than the JSON, so the fill painted and the fill measured cannot drift. Both expandGantt and buildChevronTextContent take their text colour from readableTextOn against that tone.
- cmd/json2pptx/contrast_fill_tone.go: the fit report's own fill reader was blind to tint/shade for the same reason, so its contrast preflight judged a near-white bar by its untinted accent. Fixed.
- docs/PATTERNS.md: a new "Text on a tinted fill must be chosen by measurement too" authoring rule beside the existing highlight-fill one.

EVIDENCE
Before, sampled from a real midnight-blue render: bars 9.55 / 7.88 / 1.54 against their white labels — the third failing AA by a factor of three. After, sampled from a warm-coral render of the same deck: 5.16 / 5.36 / 14.68, the picker having switched the two light bars to dk1. Test: TestTimelineGradientTextStaysReadable walks all seven stops (the pattern's own maximum) in both gantt and chevron on both bundled palettes and asserts >= 4.5:1 for every paragraph against its own bar. TestEffectiveColorModsMatchesRenderedTintAndShade pins the two transforms to the measured pixels, so a future "simplification" of the colour model fails loudly.

GATES
golangci-lint 0 issues in both modules; go test ./... passes in both; TemplatePatternMatrix passes; build clean.

PATTERN_UNKNOWN_FIELD does NOT read the schema and guess. It decodes the payload with the pattern's OWN decoder, re-marshals, and reports a key only when the text written under it is demonstrably absent from the decoded value. That matters because the schemas are not honest about the tolerances: KPICell accepts {value,number,label,caption,delta,trend,change} and the string shorthand '$4.2M | ARR', none of which the schema lists. A schema-driven checker would refuse all of them. The content-survival test passes every one.

did_you_mean prefers a property the caller has NOT already filled (a key whose content did land cannot be the one they meant), scored by synonym class, whole-word containment, edit distance, plus a bonus for a still-missing required property. title: shorten_title truncates mid-word into nonsense titles; its params disagree with repair_slide's schema
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: quality-signal (finding refs q.13).

WHAT
Applying HEADLINE_TOO_LONG's own next_tool_call verbatim on B01 rewrote titles to 'Digital Transformation Programme: A Comprehensive' and 'Workstream 1: Our comprehensive enterprise-wide di' — the latter cut mid-word — and the score went UP (92→96, input 67→92) for a deck that now has meaningless titles (montage/B01_after_repair.jpg). The fix directive also carries params {current_words, max_words} while repair_slide's own description documents shorten_title params as {path, max_length}; the call happens to work, but an agent reading the tool description and constructing the call itself will pass max_length and get different behaviour. Any deterministic truncation of a title is the wrong remedy — it turns a long-but-meaningful headline into a broken fragment while making the number look better, which is precisely the reward-hacking shape to avoid.

WHERE
cmd/json2pptx/mcp_repair.go (shorten_title), internal/patterns/finding_meta.go (HEADLINE_TOO_LONG / TITLE_OVERFLOW remediation + next_tool_call template), skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md:837

HOW
(1) Never cut mid-word or mid-clause: truncate at the last word boundary within budget and append no ellipsis, or better (2) change the remediation to advisory — 'rewrite this headline to <= N words; here is the measured max_chars' — and remove the auto-applicable directive for titles, keeping automatic shorten_title only for machine-generated labels. (3) Align the params schema between the emitted fix and repair_slide's documented schema (accept both, document one).

VERIFY
repair_slide(shorten_title) on a long title must not produce a token that is a prefix of a word; unit test asserting the output ends on a word boundary. Re-run the B01 loop: no title ends mid-word.

(1) NEVER CUT MID-WORD: new shortenTitleAtWordBoundary() drops whole words from the end until the budget is met, counting RUNES not bytes (the old code byte-sliced, so multi-byte text could be split mid-character — asserted by a test with 'Programme für die nächste Generation'), then strips a dangling colon/dash and any trailing function word from a 26-word list, so a cut never lands on '... despite the'. title: Heuristic inspect_slide_images is noise: more findings on the best deck than the worst; fires on chrome
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: quality-signal (finding refs q.10).

WHAT
With ANTHROPIC_API_KEY unset, inspect_slide_images falls back to a pure-Go heuristic. Run over my decks it emitted 14 text_overflow P3 findings on G1 (the best deck, zero real defects) and 10-11 on B08/B05 (the worst) — inverted. Every finding is an edge-band false positive; the most common description is '100.0% of pixels in the left edge contain non-background content', which is the midnight-blue template's own decorative accent bar, and '16.7% of pixels in the right edge', which is the takeaway band. It fires on blank 'Thank You' slides. Since get_started's NO VISION PROVIDER path routes agents to this tool, an agent without a key gets a stream of noise and learns to ignore the visual channel — the only channel that actually correlates with quality (+0.93 in vision mode).

WHERE
internal/visualqa/ (heuristic checker: blank-slide, edge-band, aspect-ratio checks), cmd/json2pptx/mcp_visual_qa.go (fallback selection + mode='heuristic')

HOW
Exclude the layout's own decorative chrome from the edge-band test: resolve the layout/master background shapes and accent bars and mask them out before sampling, and only report an edge band when the ink is text-like (high-frequency, dark-on-light) rather than a solid fill. Failing that, remove the edge-band check entirely and keep only the blank-slide detector — an empty finding list is a far better signal than a uniform one. Also state in the tool description that heuristic mode cannot approve a deck.

title: Contrast autofix targets 3:1 at any font size: 11pt text lands at 3.0:1, illegible; findings weigh 0
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: quality-signal (finding refs q.8).

WHAT
B05 authors six low-contrast card colour pairs. The engine detects all of them (18 contrast_predicted + 36 contrast_autofixed) and rewrites them, but always to the WCAG AA *large text* threshold of 3.0:1 — the code comment says 'presentation text is almost always >= 18pt or >= 14pt bold', which is false for the 11pt supporting line these cards carry. The swaps land at exactly ratio 3.0 (#CCCCCC→#7D7D7D on #DDDDDD, #444444→#7C7C7C on #333333, #9ACD9A→#4B644B on #8FBC8F) and the rendered slide shows 'Supporting detail text that the audience must read' as barely-visible grey-on-grey (montage/B05_low_contrast_grid.jpg, slides 2-4). Both codes are severity info / weight 0, so the deck's contrast problem contributes nothing to the score; B05 fails the gate only because of unrelated cell_underfilled noise, and auto_repair passes it.

WHERE
internal/generator/text_contrast.go:388-411 contrastReplacementScheme (svggen.WCAGAALarge), :692-712 (large-text threshold comment), svggen/contrast.go:9-13; severity mapping in internal/patterns/finding_meta.go:792 (contrast_predicted)

HOW
Pass the run's effective point size into the contrast check and require 4.5:1 for text below 18pt (or below 14pt bold); keep 3:1 only for genuinely large runs. Emit contrast_predicted/contrast_autofixed at `review` severity (weight 5) when the *authored* ratio was below 3:1 so an authoring mistake is visible in the score, and add a `contrast_unfixable` refuse finding when even the replacement cannot reach the required ratio.

title: Set real tool annotations: all 52 tools ship mcp-go defaults (destructiveHint=true, no title)
description:

WHAT
tools/list shows identical annotations for every tool in both profiles: {"readOnlyHint":false,"destructiveHint":true,"idempotentHint":false,"openWorldHint":true} and no `title`. So get_started, get_capabilities, list_templates, list_patterns, show_pattern, describe_finding, list_slide_kinds, validate_* — all pure reads — are advertised as destructive, non-idempotent, open-world. Hosts that gate destructive tools behind user confirmation (or that auto-approve read-only ones) will prompt on every discovery call, and planners that avoid destructive tools will avoid the very tools the workflow starts with. HOW
In registerMCPTools (mcp_registry.go), after building each mcp.Tool, apply annotations derived from its classification: readOnlyHint = !(MutatesState || WritesFiles); destructiveHint = MutatesState (only delete_template_setting / register_template_setting); idempotentHint = true for pure reads and for content-addressed renders; openWorldHint = false (the server touches only its own templates/output dirs); title = a short human label (e.g. 'List templates'). Add a test asserting annotations match classification for all registered tools.

`tools/list` shows readOnlyHint:true for get_started/get_capabilities/list_*/show_pattern/describe_finding/validate_*/score_deck/analyze_deck_rhythm/recommend_visual/preview_presentation_plan/plan_deck/expand_pattern, destructiveHint:true only for delete_template_setting; new TestToolAnnotationsMatchClassification.

title: Add MCP resources/resource_link: the .pptx is only deliverable as a server-local filesystem path
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: mcp-surface (finding refs m.10).

WHAT
resources/list, resources/templates/list, prompts/list, logging/setLevel and completion/complete all return -32601 (verified on both profiles); initialize advertises capabilities {experimental:{compact_responses:true}, tools:{}} only. The only deliverable of the whole workflow — the .pptx — is returned as `pptx_path: /abs/path/on/the/server`. There is no resource_link content block, no resources/read, and no base64/blob route (grep: no BlobResourceContents, no pptx_base64 anywhere). On stdio+same-host that works; on Claude Desktop with a containerized server, on a remote/HTTP deployment, or in any sandbox where the model's file tools cannot see the server's output dir, the agent literally cannot give the user the deck it just made. The PNG side already solved the equivalent problem with ImageContent, which shows the pattern is understood.

cmd/json2pptx/mcp_server.go:98-106 newMCPServer (no server.WithResourceCapabilities), internal/api/mcp_result.go (no ResourceLink builder), render/generate handlers in cmd/json2pptx/mcp_semantic.go and mcp.go.

1) Enable resources (server.WithResourceCapabilities(true,true)) and register a resource template `json2pptx://deck/{content_hash}` whose resources/read returns the .pptx as a base64 BlobResourceContents with mimeType application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation. 2) Append an mcp.ResourceLink content block (uri + name + mimeType + size) to render_deck_spec / generate_presentation results alongside the existing JSON so hosts can offer a download without reading the blob. 3) Expose read-only resources for the things agents currently pay tool calls for: json2pptx://templates (catalog), json2pptx://patterns (catalog), json2pptx://schema/deckspec, json2pptx://skill (SKILL.md) — all cacheable by the host and free of per-call tokens.

VERIFY
resources/list returns the four static resources; resources/read on json2pptx://deck/<hash> returns a blob whose sha256 equals the response's content_hash; render_deck_spec's content array contains a resource_link.

description:

title: cell_underfilled fires per-cell with no cap and sinks 10 of 34 bundled examples below the gate
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: quality-signal (finding refs q.6).

WHAT
cell_underfilled ('cell content is 13 chars (10% of capacity)') is a review finding (weight 5) emitted once per cell with no per-slide aggregation, so a slide of KPI cards can accumulate 20+ and bottom out at 0. It is by far the most emitted finding in the whole system (395 occurrences over 50 decks). Consequence: 10 of 34 decks in examples/ fail the project's own gate, 8 of them purely on score, and the dominant code is cell_underfilled — examples/consulting-layouts.json 53×, examples/visual-maturity-stress-test.json 81×, examples/sovereign-ai-strategy.json 71×, examples/kpi-big-numbers.json 26×. I looked at those renders: they are presentable decks (montage/ex_kpi-big-numbers.jpg, montage/ex_consulting-layouts.jpg). A KPI card containing '$12.4M' is *correct*, not underfilled. Meanwhile the one genuinely broken thing on consulting-layouts (chevron labels rendered as vertically stacked single letters) costs 5 points via a single TEXT_EXCEEDS_SHAPE — a 53:1 severity inversion.

WHERE
internal/patterns (cell_underfilled emission + capacity model), internal/visualqa/deterministic/checker.go:18-27 (SeverityWeight), cmd/json2pptx/fit_findings_geometry.go (aggregation precedent: 'aggregated to one per code per slide' is already done for geometry findings)

title: Deck monotony is measured then discarded: composition score never enters overall_score or the gate
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: quality-signal (finding refs q.11).

WHAT
score_deck computes ds.Composition (composition score + diagnostics like pattern_run, missing_emphasis, density_monotony) and then evaluates the quality gate purely on fit findings. So B09 (8 consecutive identical kpi-3up slides) scores 100 / gate PASS with composition 55 and diagnostics ['pattern_run','missing_emphasis']; M1 (7 identical bullet slides) scores 100 / PASS with composition 50; B10 (4 title-less identical slides) 100 / PASS with composition 60. The information needed to catch the single most common LLM deck failure (everything looks the same) is already in the response and has no consequence. analyze_deck_rhythm repeats the same score, also advisory.

WHERE
cmd/json2pptx/mcp_score_deck.go:220-228 (composition computed, then EvaluateQualityGate called with fit findings only), internal/visualqa/deterministic/checker.go:166-215 EvaluateQualityGate

HOW
Add a MinCompositionScore criterion (suggest 65) to QualityGateCriteria and include it in Reasons with a stable position after accent_overload; or blend composition into overall_score as a separate axis (e.g. overall = 0.75*correctness + 0.25*composition) and document the change in SKILL.md §'Stop when the quality gate passes' plus docs/SCHEMA_CHANGELOG.md.

The composition axis now gates the deck, and two things that would have made
that gate harmful were fixed first.

1. THE GATE (the bead's ask). QualityGateCriteria gains MinCompositionScore,
default DefaultQualityGateMinCompositionScore = 65, evaluated in
EvaluateQualityGate after accent_overload and before the problem-slide share —
the stable position the bead asked for. The reason names the diagnostics rather
than only the number:
  "composition 55 < min_composition_score 65 (missing_emphasis, pattern_run)"
0 disables it, and it is skipped when ds.Composition is nil (the slide_indices
subset path, where a rhythm verdict over three slides is meaningless).
65 is between the graded monotony decks (50 / 55 / 60) and every well-built deck
(100).

VERIFY, over live MCP score_deck calls on the bead's own decks:
  B09_same_layout_x8      composition 55  gate PASS -> FAIL (missing_emphasis, pattern_run)
  M1_all_bullets          composition 50  gate PASS -> FAIL (pattern_run)
  B10_titleless           composition 60  FAIL, now with a composition reason too
  G2_legacy_strategy_review composition 100  PASS, unchanged

2. THE BEAD'S VERIFY SAID "G1/G3 (composition 100) still pass". THEY DO NOT
SCORE 100 — they score 35 and 40, and that number is an artifact. G1 and G3 are
DeckSpecs (`_kind: "spec"`, slides carrying `kind`). score_deck unmarshals a
spec into a PresentationInput whose slides are all EMPTY and grades that,
answering overall_score 99 / quality_gate PASS for a deck it never read, with a
composition score describing its own misreading ("pattern \"content\" repeats 8
consecutive slides" — because every slide looked like empty content). Adding the
gate on top would have converted a silent wrong answer into a confident WRONG
REFUSAL on two good decks.
So score_deck now detects DeckSpec-shaped input (looksLikeDeckSpec: declared
`_kind: "spec"`, or every slide has `kind` and none has content/shape_grid/
pattern/compose) and refuses it with INVALID_PARAMETER naming validate_deck_spec
and compile_deck_spec. G1 / G3 / M3 are refused rather than mis-scored; no false
block.

3. THE RHYTHM ANALYZER CONFLATED EVERY HAND-BUILT GRID. fingerprint() named any
raw shape_grid slide the literal string "shape_grid", so six structurally
DIFFERENT grids in a row read as a six-slide pattern_run.
examples/sovereign-ai-strategy.json — 25 slides of hand-authored grids, the
showcase deck — scored composition 15 on three such phantom runs and would have
been blocked as monotonous. shapeGridFingerprint() now names a raw grid by its
shape ("shape_grid:2-2" vs "shape_grid:3"), so identical layouts still count as
a run and different ones do not. sovereign-ai-strategy now scores 100.

BLAST RADIUS, measured over all 34 bundled examples through score_deck:
  before: 29 pass / 5 fail
  with the gate alone: 24 pass / 7 composition failures (4 of them phantom runs)
  with the grid fingerprint: 27 pass / 3 composition failures
The three that fail are genuinely repetitive — basic-deck (7 consecutive content
slides), charts (a chart-type showcase), template-qa-deck (a QA fixture). No
test asserted the examples pass the gate; the full suite is green.

internal/visualqa/deterministic/composition_gate_test.go — fails at 55, passes
at 100 and exactly at the floor, skipped when Composition is nil, disabled at 0,
reason order, and compositionCodes dedupes/sorts.
internal/rhythm/shape_grid_fingerprint_test.go — a 3-cell row and a 2x2 grid do
not share a fingerprint, two identical grids do, the CellCount and bare
fallbacks, and five varied grids score better than five identical ones.
cmd/json2pptx/score_deck_input_shape_test.go — nine shapes of input through
looksLikeDeckSpec (including "a kind slide that also has content is raw"), the
tool refusing a spec with the right pointers, and the guard that a raw deck is
still graded.

overall_score (0.75*correctness + 0.25*composition)". I took the criterion
option. Blending would have made overall_score mean two different things at
once and moved every deck's number; a criterion is separable, reportable, and
the reason says exactly what to fix.

description:

The rendered slide is a 3-bullet text page with ~60% empty space - the weakest slide in an otherwise decent deck - while card-grid(columns=3) renders the same content as three proper panels (I verified this by hand on the raw path).

ALSO REPORTED (dogfood-b: "comparison kind is hard-capped at 2 columns, so a 3-4 way competitor comparison degrades to a bullet list"): 'Compare us to 3 competitors' is the single most common QBR/strategy slide. kind=comparison with 4 columns validates ok=true with a warning ('a comparison renders exactly two columns as a comparison-2col visual; found 4 (otherwise it degrades to a bullet list)') and renders four run-on bullets -- 'Helio: ARR EUR 86M, +31% YoY; NRR 117%; CAC payback 14 months; Gross churn 6.2%' -- with no column structure, no header row and no highlight of 'us'. internal/semantic/slides/visual.go:41-83 CompileComparison / ComparisonPatternFeasible (len(cols)!=2 -> fallback); internal/semantic/validate.go SEMANTIC_DENSITY rule

description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: capability-gaps (finding refs cap.12).

WHAT
list_icons offers only a case-insensitive substring filter on the icon name. Have list_icons match against concept ∪ name and return `matched_via:'synonym'`; have the ICON_BUNDLED_NAME_UNKNOWN suggester consult the same map before falling back to Levenshtein. Surface a `concepts` listing in the tool description so an agent knows the vocabulary exists.
