title: Shrink get_capabilities (183KB): add projection args and drop the duplicated tool descriptions
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: dogfood-a, mcp-surface (finding refs m.1, a.13).

WHAT
get_started(brief).sequence step 1 is get_capabilities with when_to_call "First — detect schema_version drift and feature flags before doing anything else", and SKILL.md repeats it. One call returns 183,242 wire bytes (93,731 text + 83,822 structuredContent) ≈ 46K tokens. Breakdown of structuredContent: tool_list 55,475 B (name+description of all 52 tools — a verbatim duplicate of what tools/list already sent), mcp_tools_available 13,689 B, vocabularies 3,734, features 3,673, cli_only_commands 1,935 (CLI-only, useless to an MCP agent), error_codes 1,623, registry 1,284. Its inputSchema is {"type":"object","properties":{}} — there is no way to ask for less. The single most useful field for an MCP agent (runtime.render_available / output_dir, 326 B) is buried behind those 46K tokens.

ALSO REPORTED (dogfood-a: "Discovery payloads cost ~250KB before a single slide is authored (tools/list 69KB in the core profile, get_capabilities 183KB)"): Measured wire bytes for a first-time agent on the DEFAULT core profile: tools/list 69,254 B; list_slide_kinds 55,259 B (11 kinds, each carrying a full JSON Schema with the same 12-key item object repeated); list_templates (single template, read_only) 50,409 B; get_capabilities 182,704 B; list_patterns compact 30,579 B; show_pattern 11-20 KB each. That is ~250 KB of discovery before authoring, and get_capabilities alone duplicates the same array under both `deprecated_fields` and `deprecations` and inlines the entire tool_list (55 KB) that tools/list already returned. list_templates additionally defaults to `full` and returns a deprecation warning telling you to pass fields explicitly - a wasted round-trip by design.

WHERE
cmd/json2pptx/mcp_capabilities.go (capabilities payload assembly, ToolList/MCPToolsAvailable/CLIOnlyCommands fields), cmd/json2pptx/mcp_output_schemas.go (outputSchemaGetCapabilities), cmd/json2pptx/mcp_get_started.go:129 (the 'call this first' step).
[dogfood-a] cmd/json2pptx/mcp*.go tool registry (core profile); get_capabilities handler (tool_list, deprecated_fields+deprecations duplication); internal/semantic/schema.go per-kind item_schema generation; list_templates default projection

HOW
1) Add a `sections` arg (enum: runtime, features, vocabularies, registry, tools, deprecations; default [runtime, features, deprecations] ~8KB) and a `fields=compact|full` projection like list_templates. 2) Drop tool_list and cli_only_commands from the default payload entirely for MCP callers — tools/list is the authoritative list and the CLI table is not callable over MCP. 3) Keep schema_version + schema_fingerprint + runtime in every projection so drift detection still works in <1KB. 4) Update get_started's step hint to `get_capabilities {sections:["runtime","features"]}`.

Alternative/extra HOW from dogfood-a: (a) drop tool_list from get_capabilities (tools/list is the source of truth) and emit `deprecations` only; (b) in list_slide_kinds hoist the shared item-object schema into a $defs and $ref it per kind; (c) flip list_templates/list_patterns defaults to compact now that the warning has shipped; (d) consider a `fields` projection on get_capabilities.

VERIFY

description:

title: Merged table cells omit hMerge continuation cells, so two-tier headers render blank
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: capability-gaps (finding refs cap.6).

WHAT
A row using col_span produces one <a:tc gridSpan="N"> and nothing for the covered grid columns: row 1 of the test table emits 3 <a:tc> against 5 <a:gridCol>. ECMA-376 requires the covered cells to be present as <a:tc hMerge="1"/>. LibreOffice renders the consequence: the second merged cell ('Plan') loses its text entirely and is painted as an empty blue block. Output validation (strict) passes it. The generator already knows how to emit continuation cells (generateDataCell / generateHeaderRowWithMerges handle cell.IsMerged) but NOTHING ever sets types.TableCell.IsMerged from JSON input, so the branch is dead. Merged headers ('FY24 Actuals | FY25 Plan') are standard in any financial table.

WHERE
internal/generator/table.go:663-690 generateDataCell (IsMerged branch) and :559-585 generateHeaderRowWithMerges; internal/types/table.go:20 IsMerged (no producer); conversion from jsonschema.TableCellInput lives in the deckinput→types table conversion

HOW
When converting TableCellInput rows to types.TableCell, expand spans: after a cell with ColSpan=N insert N-1 synthetic cells {IsMerged:true, ColSpan:0}, and for RowSpan=M insert {IsMerged:true, RowSpan:0} into the M-1 following rows at the same column index. Add an OOXML output-validation rule: for every <a:tr>, count(<a:tc>) must equal count(<a:gridCol>) (spans are expressed by gridSpan on the origin PLUS hMerge placeholders).

VERIFY
Regenerate capability-gaps/b1/deck.json slide 5; python: every <a:tr> has 5 <a:tc>; the render shows 'Segment | Actuals (2 cols) | Plan (2 cols)' with both labels visible; validate-output flags a hand-crafted row with a missing placeholder.

Root cause confirmed exactly as reported: the generator's cell.IsMerged branches (internal/generator/table.go generateDataCell :666 and generateHeaderRowWithMerges :566) were dead because nothing set types.TableCell.IsMerged from JSON input. New expandCellSpans() in internal/jsonschema/table.go, wired into TableInput.ToTableSpec(), materialises the continuation cells: horizontal spans get ColSpan-0 cells (=> hMerge), vertical spans push RowSpan-0 cells into each row they cover (=> vMerge), and a rectangle (col+row) merge is covered at every grid position it occupies. New slide kind 'table' compiles to a native table content block (1d1f48e).

WHAT WAS WRONG
A plain data table — the financials, the segment split, the pricing tiers — had no kind. capability-gaps probed kind=table and got 'unknown slide kind', so the most ordinary business slide there is needed kind=raw_json2pptx.

SHIPPED
- kind table: headers (<=6, alias columns) + rows (<=6 so the table stays within the renderer's 7-row logical budget including the header). A row is a list of cell values OR an object keyed by header label — both shapes an author writes. Short rows pad with blank cells rather than dropping a column; cells keep the author's own numeric literal (1000000, not 1e+06).
- column_alignments (left/center/right, the shape-grid codes l/ctr/r accepted and normalized), highlight_column (a header NAME or a 0-based index; an unknown name highlights nothing rather than guessing), totals_row, column_types. With NO emphasis fields set, no style block is emitted and the template's own table style renders verbatim.
- Compiles to a content slide with table_value, so it inherits the engine's table machinery rather than reimplementing any of it: banding, totals emphasis, font scaling, conditional fills, and the fit report's density findings.
- validateTable reports the 6-column / 7-row budget and any row whose cell count does not match the headers, at authoring time instead of after a render. Without a header row there is no table to build, so the rows degrade to bullets labelled by whatever headers exist (never silent, never dropped).
- Registered across kinds.go / kind_examples.go / payload_fields.go / validate.go (takeaway + field shapes + rules) / ir.go (plan + compositionCandidates, which point at option_matrix for a scored matrix) / compile.go / slides/table.go.

The first cut emitted the shape-grid alignment codes (l/ctr/r). generator.alignmentToOOXML reads the WORDS left/center/right and falls through to left for anything else, so every 'right' column came out silently left-aligned — visible in the first render, fixed, and pinned by TestTableAlignmentUsesTheRendererVocabulary.

title: Chart legend is drawn on top of the x-axis title on every Cartesian chart type
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: charts-diagrams (finding refs ch.0).

WHAT
With a realistic 3-series dataset and an x_label, the legend row and the x-axis title are drawn at the same vertical band, so the axis title sits inside the legend text. Measured in the emitted SVG (all-midnight-blue.pptx slide 5, grouped_bar/real): the axis title 'Quarter' is at y=379.85 and the legend labels 'Enterprise'/'Mid-market'/'SMB' at y=384.99 with the same centre x — they overprint. Visible on all 4 templates and in every Cartesian family: bar, grouped_bar, stacked_bar, line, area, stacked_area, scatter, bubble. Root cause is a 2-line discrepancy: svggen/charts.go computes legendBounds.Y with `xAxisLabelSpace = TickSize + TickPadding + SizeSmall + Spacing.SM`, while svggen/axes.go drawTitle places the axis title at `TickSize + TickPadding + SizeSmall + Spacing.LG`; since SM < LG the legend lands above the title. Neither the x-axis title height nor rotated/wrapped tick label height is accounted for, so with long categories the title also lands in the middle of the rotated labels. Nothing in validate --fit-report mentions it, so an agent that never renders ships the defect.

WHERE
svggen/charts.go:553-563 (bar) and the identical blocks at :1377, :2000, :2757, :3258; svggen/axes.go:509-535 (Axis.drawTitle, titleOffset); svggen/cartesian_layout.go:55-64 (legendHeight reservation)

HOW
Make the legend offset derive from the same measured stack as the axis title: bottom-of-plot + tick + padding + actual x-label block height (including AdaptXLabels rotation/wrap) + axis-title height (SizeBody + Spacing) + Spacing.SM. Extract a single helper `xAxisFooterHeight(style, xLayout, hasTitle)` used by both drawTitle and every legendBounds site so the two can never drift again. Add a golden test asserting legend top > axis-title bottom for a chart with x_label and 3 series.

VERIFY
python3 - <<'P'\nimport re;s=open('ppt/media/image9.svg').read()\nP  — after the fix, in the SVG for `charts-diagrams/single/grouped_bar__real.json` the y of the 'Quarter' text must be strictly less than the y of the first legend label, and `magick` inspection of sheets/05_grouped_bar__real.png must show no overlap on any of the 4 templates.

description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: gallery (finding refs g.2).

WHAT
resolveIconOverlay sets ResolvedCell.TextInsets to {iconWidth+gap,0,0,0} (icon left) or {0,iconZoneH,0,0} (icon top). Those four values are written verbatim as lIns/tIns/rIns/bIns, so every other side loses PowerPoint's default 0.1in/0.05in padding. WHERE
internal/shapegrid/grid.go:965 and :987 (iconOverlayLayout.TextInsets), consumed in internal/shapegrid/grid.go:249 and written by internal/pptx/text.go:82-85

Seed TextInsets with the renderer's default insets (91440 L/R, 45720 T/B) and only ADD the icon reservation on the icon axis, e.g. {defaultL + iconW + gap, defaultT, defaultR, defaultB}. Alternatively keep 0 as 'unset' and merge with defaults in buildTextBody instead of emitting an explicit 0.

description:

WHAT

description:

Rewrite the theme part at package time: in the output stage, when ThemeOverride is non-nil, patch ppt/theme/theme<N>.xml — replace the <a:srgbClr val> inside each overridden <a:accentK>/<a:dk*>/<a:lt*> and the <a:latin typeface> of majorFont/minorFont — before the zip is written (the file is already streamed through internal/generator/output.go). title: render_deck_spec: add output_filename and never overwrite output.pptx (content_hash stops matching the file)
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: dogfood-a, mcp-surface (finding refs a.11, m.9).

WHAT
generate_presentation takes output_filename; render_deck_spec does not, so every DeckSpec render writes <output-dir>/output.pptx. Iterating (render v1, keep it, render v2 to compare) is impossible without shell access to copy the file between calls - which an MCP-only agent does not have. It also makes two concurrent decks in one session collide silently, and breaks submit_visual_review's revision matching if anything re-renders in between.

ALSO REPORTED (mcp-surface: "render_deck_spec always writes output.pptx: renders overwrite and content_hash stops matching the file"): render_deck_spec has no output_filename argument (inputSchema: output_validation, spec, strict, template) and RunPresentation writes to mc.outputDir/output.pptx. Two different decks rendered in one session both returned pptx_path .../output.pptx with different content_hash values — the second silently destroyed the first (verified: render1 hash 39f556ae..., render2 hash c880c0a5..., same path). Worse under concurrency: two in-flight render_deck_spec calls both returned success with distinct content_hash values and the same path, but the file on disk contained only deck A (sha256 = A's hash, slide1 title DECK-AAAA, 15 slides) — so B's reported content_hash matches nothing on disk. Since submit_visual_review requires pptx_revision == the current file's sha256 and render_deck_thumbnails keys its cache on file content, the agent's completion path is then unfixable except by re-rendering. generate_presentation does have output_filename (path components stripped — verified '../../escape.pptx' -> escape.pptx in the output dir), so the gap is specific to the recommended tool.

WHERE
render_deck_spec MCP tool input schema (params: spec, template, strict, output_validation) in cmd/json2pptx/mcp*.go; cmd/json2pptx/semantic_cmd.go:570 OutputPath
[mcp-surface] cmd/json2pptx/mcp_semantic.go:403 (RenderOptions{OutputDir: mc.outputDir}), RunPresentation in cmd/json2pptx (output naming), tool definition mcpRenderDeckSpecTool in mcp_semantic.go.

HOW
Add output_filename (same sanitisation as generate_presentation) to render_deck_spec, defaulting to a slug of meta.title plus a short content hash.

Alternative/extra HOW from mcp-surface: Add an `output_filename` arg to render_deck_spec with the same sanitation as generate_presentation, and default the name to something collision-free (e.g. slugify(meta.title) + '-' + content_hash[:8] + '.pptx', or output.pptx only when the dir has no colliding deck). Return `overwrote: true` in the response when an existing file was replaced. Serialize writes to the same target path with a mutex so a concurrent pair cannot report a hash that never hits disk.

title: Server-side deck handle (deck_id + patch ops + per-slide re-render) so revisions don't resend the whole spec
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: dogfood-b, mcp-surface (finding refs m.20, b.4).

WHAT
Measured on a 15-slide deck: the DeckSpec loop (validate -> render -> thumbs -> fix -> validate -> render -> thumbs -> one slide) resent the 3,695-byte spec on 5 of 8 calls (15,555 request bytes total) and received 863,592 bytes back, of which 32,963 was JSON — and every render re-echoes explanation_summary (15 slides x ~200 B) plus a 15-entry quality_summary.slide_scores array the agent already has. The raw path is worse: the compiled deck is 5,359 bytes and a validate/preview/generate/score/repair/generate/score loop resent 37,718 request bytes and got 131,585 back, with preview_presentation_plan alone at 61,885 B. A one-line title fix therefore costs a full spec re-upload plus a full-deck re-render plus 15 re-inspected images. The infrastructure for a handle already exists: cmd/json2pptx/mcp_loop_state.go has a per-process TTL'd session store with resume tokens (used by auto_repair/make_deck), and mcp_idempotency.go has a keyed response cache.

ALSO REPORTED (dogfood-b: "No deck state for revisions: a 4-item edit forces resending the whole spec, and get_started(revise) points at tools hidden in the core profile"): Phase-1b revise ('slide 4 chart -> line, insert a competitor slide after 6, shorten titles, switch to midnight-blue') required re-sending the entire 7.9 KB DeckSpec and re-rendering all 11 slides; there is no deck handle, no session state, and no slide-level re-render from a spec. get_started(task=revise) makes it worse: its fast_path is auto_repair and its sequence is read_presentation -> validate_input -> repair_slide -> generate_presentation -- a RAW-deck workflow. Two of those (auto_repair, read_presentation) are not advertised in the default core profile (the notes admit this and tell the agent to ask the operator to restart the server), and none of them mentions the DeckSpec the brief task just told the agent to author. A DeckSpec-authored deck has no documented revise path at all. The right primitive, apply_deck_patch, exists, works (4 ops applied atomically, patched_deck + findings back in one 53 KB call) and is hidden in `all`.

title: Stop sending every MCP response twice (indented text + structuredContent); compact JSON by default
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: dogfood-b, mcp-surface (finding refs m.3, b.15).

WHAT
api.MCPSuccessResult always emits the full payload as a pretty-printed TextContent AND as structuredContent. One pass over the 18 callable core tools = 221,206 B of text + 168,072 B of structuredContent = 389KB (~97K tokens) for data worth 168KB. 53,134 B of the text copy is pure two-space indentation (list_slide_kinds alone: 34,633 B text vs 17,124 B compact — a 100% overhead). Compaction only happens if the client sends experimental.compact_responses:true (a json2pptx-specific capability no mainstream client sends) or the deprecated MCP_COMPACT_RESPONSES=1 env var; verified: opting in drops list_slide_kinds from 55,311 to 36,565 wire bytes. Payload bloat is proportional to input too: a 1MB title produced a 2,003,105 B response because the text and the structuredContent each echo it.

ALSO REPORTED (dogfood-b: "Every MCP response ships its full JSON twice (content text + structuredContent), roughly doubling response tokens"): api.MCPSuccessResult puts the same object in both Content[0].text and StructuredContent. Measured on the wire: get_started -> content 7,471 B + structuredContent 7,420 B (14.9 KB total for 7.4 KB of information); list_slide_kinds 18.3 KB + 18.3 KB = 55 KB on the wire; list_templates 153 KB; render_deck_spec 13.1 KB for a 6.4 KB payload. The compact_responses capability only removes indentation -- it does not remove the duplicate. Over my ~45-call session this is tens of thousands of wasted tokens, and it fights the round-1 payload work (go-slide-creator-vdxa).

WHERE
internal/api/mcp_encode.go: MarshalMCPResponse / isCompactSession; internal/api/mcp_result.go: MCPSuccessResult; cmd/json2pptx/mcp_server.go:179-190 (the AfterInitialize hook advertising experimental.compact_responses).
[dogfood-b] internal/api/mcp_result.go:19-35 MCPSuccessResult; internal/api/mcp_encode.go MarshalMCPResponse / isCompactSession; cmd/json2pptx/mcp_server.go:184 (advertises experimental.compact_responses).

HOW
Make json.Marshal (compact) the DEFAULT in MarshalMCPResponse and keep indentation only behind an explicit opt-in (env JSON2PPTX_MCP_PRETTY=1) — the text block is a machine-read fallback, not a human document. Then add a server flag/arg `text_fallback=auto|always|never` (default auto: omit the TextContent entirely when the negotiated protocolVersion >= 2025-06-18, i.e. when structuredContent is guaranteed to be understood). That halves every response again.

Alternative/extra HOW from dogfood-b: When the session negotiated compact_responses (or structuredContent support), emit a one-line human summary in Content ('render_deck_spec ok: 11 slides, score 100, 3 diagnostics') and keep the full object only in StructuredContent. Keep today's behaviour for clients that negotiate neither.

VERIFY
Wire: `list_slide_kinds {}` with no client capabilities < 20KB; with protocolVersion 2024-11-05 the TextContent is still present. Tests: TestMarshalMCPResponseCompactByDefault, TestTextFallbackOmittedOnModernProtocol.
[dogfood-b] With experimental.compact_responses negotiated, the tools/call wire size for get_started drops to ~7.5 KB and structuredContent still carries the full object; a client reading only Content still gets an actionable summary.

close_reason:
MCP responses no longer ship every payload twice.

TWO CHANGES, both from the bead's HOW.

1. COMPACT BY DEFAULT. MarshalMCPResponse returns json.Marshal unconditionally;
JSON2PPTX_MCP_PRETTY=1 indents it for reading raw transcripts by hand. The text
block is a machine-read fallback, not a human document — 53,134 B of one pass
over the core tools was pure two-space indentation.

2. NO DUPLICATE ON A MODERN PROTOCOL. MCPSuccessResult omits the
content[0].text copy when the session negotiated protocol 2025-06-18 or later,
where structuredContent is part of the tool-result contract. The mcp-go session
interface exposes client info and capabilities but NOT the negotiated version,
so the server records it in AddAfterInitialize (keyed by session ID) and drops
it in AddOnUnregisterSession. An unknown version keeps the copy — the safe
direction, and what every direct handler call in the test suite gets.

VERIFY (both clauses, measured on the wire with a real stdio session)
                         BEFORE            AFTER (2025-06-18)   AFTER (2024-11-05)
  list_slide_kinds       61,606 B          19,620 B             41,705 B
  get_started            16,728 B           7,919 B             16,012 B
- "list_slide_kinds {} with no client capabilities < 20KB": 19,620 B. MET.
- "with protocolVersion 2024-11-05 the TextContent is still present": present,
  19,550 B of text — and still 49% smaller than the 38,195 B it was, from
  compaction alone. MET.
Also verified --text-fallback=always restores the copy on 2025-06-18 (41,705 B),
--text-fallback=never drops it on 2024-11-05 (19,620 B), and
JSON2PPTX_MCP_TEXT_FALLBACK=always has the same effect as the flag.

A JUDGEMENT CALL, stated plainly. The MCP spec says a tool returning structured
content SHOULD also return the serialized JSON in a TextContent block for
backwards compatibility. `auto` deviates from that SHOULD on the grounds that a
client which negotiated 2025-06-18 can be relied on to read structuredContent —
which is what the bead specifies and what its VERIFY demands. If a client reads
content[0].text anyway, one flag (--text-fallback=always, or the env var)
restores the old behaviour for every response. That escape hatch is documented
in SKILL.md next to the measurement, not buried.

TESTS internal/api/mcp_text_fallback_test.go: the copy is omitted on
2025-06-18, kept on 2024-11-05 and 2025-03-26, kept when the protocol is
unknown, the three modes behave as named, an unrecognised mode leaves the
current one alone, and the protocol registry is per-session (forgetting one does
not disturb another).

FOUR EXISTING TESTS encoded the behaviour being fixed and were updated
deliberately, each with the reason:
TestMarshalMCPResponse_Default and TestMCPSuccessResult_IndentedByDefault
(renamed _CompactByDefault) asserted indentation; _EnvNotOne and

existing clients do not break.

title: Native OOXML diagrams emit <a:normAutofit/> with no fontScale, so LibreOffice renders a shrunk deck that PowerPoint will overflow
description:

WHAT

in PowerPoint as in our own thumbnails.

ROOT CAUSE confirmed on the bead's own deck. swot__stress.json produced five
`<a:normAutofit/>` with no fontScale. LibreOffice recomputes the shrink;
PowerPoint applies the stored scale (100% when absent) and only recomputes on

would have overflowed for the reader.

measures the body and writes fontScale / lnSpcReduction on the element. Placing
it in GenerateShape rather than at the 20 `AutoFit: "normAutofit"` call sites

forgotten by the next builder.

52000; the three quadrants that fit keep the bare element (which means "no
shrink" to every renderer).

not. It ignored paragraph spcAft and predicted 66%. I verified it the only way
that actually proves anything: pinned the text at the predicted scale with
<a:noAutofit/> and re-rendered, so LibreOffice could not recompute and hide the
error. /tmp/wvr0b/pinned.png shows four bullets spilling out of two quadrants at
66% — the prediction was optimistic and would have handed PowerPoint an
overflowing deck. Cause: twelve bullets at spcAft 6pt carry 72pt of spacing the
glyph measurement never sees. With spacing counted the prediction drops to 28%,
and the same pinned-render test (/tmp/wvr0c/pinned.png) puts every bullet inside

internal/textcapacity.AutofitScale now delegates to it, so the number the engine

WHAT
The recommended new-deck path (get_started task=brief -> render_deck_spec) is the blindest tool in the server. cmd/json2pptx/mcp_semantic.go handleRenderDeckSpec (calls RunPresentation only); cmd/json2pptx/semantic_cmd.go buildSemanticRenderSuccess (fit := rr.SynthesisFindings + rr.GenResult.FitFindings + rr.StrictFitFindings + rr.GridVisualFindings); the missing collectors are cmd/json2pptx/fit_findings_collect.go collectFitFindings -> collectTitleFitFindings (title_measure.go) + collectContentLintFindings (fit_findings_content_lint.go), which mcp.go:545 (generate_presentation) and mcp.go:1019 (validate_input) both run.

title: internal/render.pptxToPDF must use a private LibreOffice -env:UserInstallation per conversion (concurrent renders fail)
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: closure-audit-1, dogfood-b, mcp-surface, quality-signal (finding refs c1.4, b.5, m.18, q.19).

WHAT
Closure audit spillover from go-slide-creator-71kj (pptx2jpg got a private profile; internal/render did not). internal/render.pptxToPDF invokes soffice with no -env:UserInstallation, so it uses the shared default profile. Its mutex only serialises within one process. Running 4 json2pptx MCP servers concurrently (the normal case when several agents / a lane runner share a machine, or when the user has LibreOffice open), 2 of 4 render_slide_image calls failed with RENDER.RENDER_FAILED 'PDF not created at …'; the other 2 succeeded. Serial calls always pass, so the failure looks random to an agent and it cannot complete the mandatory visual-review step.

ALSO REPORTED (dogfood-b: "Concurrent renders collide: render_deck_thumbnails fails with 'PDF not created' whenever another LibreOffice render is running"): internal/render invokes LibreOffice without a private -env:UserInstallation profile, so two render calls (different server processes, or a host that also renders) fight over the default user profile. Reproduced deterministically: two MCP servers each rendering a different deck, 3 rounds -> 3 of 6 calls returned isError with 'RENDER.RENDER_FAILED: PDF not created at /var/folders/.../render-deck-*.pdf'. I hit the same failure twice during the normal workflow (runs/r12, runs/r15) and both times a bare retry succeeded. The message does not mention concurrency or suggest a retry, so an agent reasonably concludes the deck is broken and starts editing content that is fine. cmd/pptx2jpg, internal/layoutpreview and internal/qualitybench all already pass -env:UserInstallation; only the MCP render path does not.

ALSO REPORTED (mcp-surface: "Isolate LibreOffice per conversion: 1 of 3 parallel render_deck_thumbnails failed with 'PDF not created'"): Three json2pptx MCP server processes (the realistic case: several agents/sessions on one machine, or one agent with parallel subagents) each called render_deck_thumbnails on the same PPTX at the same time. Two returned 15 images; the third returned RENDER.RENDER_FAILED 'PDF not created at /var/folders/.../render-deck-*/output.pdf'. The same failure appeared once in the single-process nasty-input run. Cause: internal/render/render.go serializes LibreOffice with an in-process `var mu sync.Mutex` only, and internal/render/render.go's soffice invocation passes no -env:UserInstallation profile, so concurrent soffice processes share ~/Library/Application Support/LibreOffice/4 and one of them exits without producing the PDF. The repo already knows the fix: cmd/pptx2jpg/main.go:188 and internal/layoutpreview/preview.go:48 both pass a private -env:UserInstallation profile, and internal/qualitybench/render.go:90 does too — the MCP render path is the one that does not. The error is also uninformative (no hint that a concurrent render is the likely cause, no retry).

ALSO REPORTED (quality-signal: "render_deck_thumbnails fails under concurrent LibreOffice use: pptxToPDF omits -env:UserInstallation"): 3 of 34 example decks (gear-process-chain, patterns-smoke, sovereign-ai-strategy) and one calibration deck returned RENDER.RENDER_FAILED 'PDF not created at /var/folders/.../render-deck-NNN/<name>.pdf' and then rendered fine on a sequential retry. internal/render/render.go:184 pptxToPDF is the only LibreOffice call site in the repo that does not pass -env:UserInstallation — layoutpreview/preview.go:35-48, qualitybench/render.go:90 and cmd/pptx2jpg/main.go:188 all use a private profile, and preview.go's own comment says it exists 'so concurrent renders do not collide'. The in-process mutex only serialises one server; a second MCP server, a parallel agent, or the user's own soffice collides. Because the server instructions make 'render ALL slides and inspect every image' the definition of done, a flaky render blocks completion, and the error carries no retry hint.

WHERE
internal/render/render.go:184 pptxToPDF (compare cmd/pptx2jpg/main.go:188, internal/layoutpreview/preview.go:48, internal/qualitybench/render.go:90 which all pass -env:UserInstallation)
[dogfood-b] internal/render/render.go:184 pptxToPDF (args: --headless --convert-to pdf --outdir; no -env:UserInstallation) and render.go:214 'PDF not created at %s'; contrast internal/layoutpreview/preview.go:48 and cmd/pptx2jpg/main.go:188.
[mcp-surface] internal/render/render.go:180-215 pptxToPDF (missing -env:UserInstallation, in-process mutex only), compare cmd/pptx2jpg/main.go:188 and internal/layoutpreview/preview.go:35-48.
[quality-signal] internal/render/render.go:184-215 pptxToPDF (mu.Lock + officeCommand + args); contrast with internal/layoutpreview/preview.go:35-48, internal/qualitybench/render.go:90, cmd/pptx2jpg/main.go:188

HOW
Give every soffice invocation in internal/render a per-process (or per-call) profile dir: `-env:UserInstallation=file://<tmp>/lo-<pid>` under os.TempDir, created once per process and reused; keep the mutex for CPU fairness. Also turn a missing PDF into a retryable error with the soffice stderr attached.

Alternative/extra HOW from dogfood-b: Give each render a per-process (or per-call) profile dir: append "-env:UserInstallation=file://"+filepath.ToSlash(profileDir) with profileDir under os.MkdirTemp, as layoutpreview already does. Add one bounded retry on 'PDF not created' and make the finding text say 'LibreOffice produced no PDF (often a concurrent soffice instance); retry once'.

Alternative/extra HOW from mcp-surface: Give each conversion a private LibreOffice profile dir under the temp dir (same helper layoutpreview already has) and add a cross-process lock (an O_EXCL lockfile or flock in os.TempDir()) around the soffice invocation, with a bounded wait. On failure, retry once and, if it still fails, return RENDER_FAILED with a message naming the likely cause ('another LibreOffice conversion was running; retry').

Alternative/extra HOW from quality-signal: Give pptxToPDF a private per-process (or per-call) UserInstallation directory under os.TempDir(), exactly as layoutpreview does, and retry once on 'PDF not created' with a fresh profile before surfacing RENDER_FAILED. Add the retry count and the profile path to the finding's evidence.

VERIFY
Run the 4-way concurrency repro (mcp/batch5f.log script): four independent `j2p mcp` processes each calling render_slide_image on the same pptx must all return an image block. Also run with a foreground `soffice --headless` on the default profile held open.

[mcp-surface] mcp-surface/twoservers.py (3 processes, same pptx) must return 15 images from all three, repeated 5x; go test ./internal/render -run TestConcurrentConversion.
[quality-signal] Run two MCP servers concurrently, each calling render_deck_thumbnails on a different deck 5 times: zero RENDER_FAILED. Re-run NOVISION=1 OUTROOT=ex_results run_signals.py over examples/*.json → 34/34 decks produce slide images.

ROOT CAUSE (reproduced, not inferred): internal/render/render.go pptxToPDF was

title: Chart number formatting: decimal-aware default data labels + agent-controllable number format (currency, %, M/bn)
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: charts-diagrams, dogfood-a, dogfood-b (finding refs a.7, b.2, ch.19).

WHAT
chart-insights-split turns data labels on by default. With the real series [4.6,4.9,5.2,5.5,5.8,6.2,6.5] every bar was labelled 5 or 6 - seven bars, three distinct labels, directly contradicting the axis and the '+6% a year' headline. I only noticed by looking at the render; nothing in validate/score/fit findings flags it. I had to rescale the data to millions (4600...) to get honest labels. svggen auto-detects fractional values for waterfall (waterfall.go:142) but not for bar/line, whose default ValueFormat is hardcoded '%.0f'.

ALSO REPORTED (dogfood-b: "Chart data labels are hard-formatted %.0f, printing 86 where the headline says EUR 86.4M; no reachable format knob"): svggen/series.go formatValue defaults to "%.0f". My ARR series [61.2 ... 86.4] renders data labels 61, 64, 65, 66, 71, 75, 81, 86 on a slide titled 'ARR grew eight straight quarters to EUR 86.4M' whose insight bullet says 'from EUR 66.0M to EUR 86.4M'. The chart therefore contradicts the narrative on the same slide -- an instant credibility failure at a board review. The only formatter is data.data_labels.format, which every category+series chart schema REJECTS: render_slide_image_from_json with data_labels on a line_chart returns 'line_chart does not accept field "data_labels"; allowed fields: categories, colors, footnote, labels, series, x_axis_title, x_label, x_labels, y_axis_title, y_label'. So there is no way for an agent to get one decimal, a thousands separator or a EUR/% suffix. The funnel has the same issue: it prints 'Leads: 12400', not '12,400'.

ALSO REPORTED (charts-diagrams: "Number formatting is inconsistent inside one chart and cannot be controlled by the agent"): In a single bar chart the axis uses compact notation ('1.2M', '800K') while `show_values` data labels print raw numbers ('1240', '865', '413'); funnel prints raw integers ('Website visitors: 48200 (100.0%)'); pie prints percentages only; gauge prints the raw value plus a free-text unit that collides with its label. There is no thousands separator anywhere, no currency/unit suffix, no decimals control and no agent-facing knob — an EUR deck therefore shows '1240' where a consultant needs '€1.24m'. The unit has to be smuggled into y_label or the chart title.

WHERE

title: Title autofit bakes 64-76% line spacing so multi-line titles overlap; emit TITLE_OVERFLOW instead of crushing leading
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: closure-audit-1, gallery (finding refs c1.3, g.4).

WHAT
Closure audit of go-slide-creator-6cjs. Measured autofit is genuinely wired (fitted size lands in the runs: sz=2700 for a 103-char title on modern-template, TITLE_OVERFLOW fires at 312 chars), but the same path emits `<a:lnSpc><a:spcPct val="64000"/>` while keeping sz=2700 — a 17.3pt line pitch for 27pt all-caps text. LibreOffice renders the four title lines physically overlapping, which is the exact defect the bead claims to have fixed (bead text: 'LibreOffice squashes lines together'). midnight-blue writes 72% on the same content and is merely tight. The line-spacing floor is therefore below the glyph height.

ALSO REPORTED (gallery: "Title autofit bakes 76% line spacing, so 3-line titles collide on modern-template - and no TITLE_OVERFLOW is emitted"): bakeTitleFit multiplies the template's own line spacing by (1 - LnSpcReduction) with maxLnSpcReductionPct=20. On modern-template a 137-char title is written as <a:lnSpc><a:spcPct val="76000"/></a:lnSpc> at sz=2700 - 20.5pt of line pitch for 27pt all-caps glyphs. The rendered result has line 1's umlaut touching line 2's ascenders and line 3's 'Q' descender crossing line 2 (zoom/title_crop.png at 200dpi). Every max-variant slide on modern-template shows it (45/45). validate --fit-report reports only FIT.HEADLINE_TOO_LONG (a word count lint); neither TITLE_OVERFLOW nor title_wraps fires, so an agent has no signal that its title is unreadable. Round-1 bead go-slide-creator-6cjs claimed to fix colliding title lines and add TITLE_OVERFLOW - on this template it is still reproducible.

WHERE
internal/generator/text_autofit.go (measured-fit line-spacing reduction), internal/textfit (line spacing candidates)
[gallery] internal/generator/title_fit.go:261-278 (bakeTitleFit lnSpc computation), internal/textfit/textfit.go:101 (maxLnSpcReductionPct = 20), internal/generator/title_fit.go:39-40 (template LineSpacingPct multiplier), cmd/json2pptx/fit_findings_collect.go:53 (collectTitleFitFindings)

HOW
Floor the line-spacing reduction at ~0.9 of the font's line height (e.g. spcPct >= 90000, or >= ascender+descender for the resolved font) and spend the remaining deficit on font size / TITLE_OVERFLOW instead of on leading.

Alternative/extra HOW from gallery: Floor the baked spcPct at ~90% of single spacing (or derive the floor from font ascent+descent so the pitch never drops below ~1.05em) and take the remaining shrink out of font size. When even the minimum size + floor spacing does not fit, emit TITLE_OVERFLOW instead of silently overlapping.

title: svggen LinearScale.TickFormat prints '%!(NOVERB)' for flat/all-zero series (step==0 precision overflow)
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: charts-diagrams, mcp-surface (finding refs ch.2, m.8).

WHAT
A legitimately all-zero series (incidents = 0,0; a filtered dataset; a null coerced to 0) renders a Go format-verb error string onto the slide. Minimal repro: `{"type":"bar","data":{"categories":["Q1","Q2"],"series":[{"name":"s","values":[0,0]}]}}` -> the SVG contains `<tspan>%!(NOVERB)%!(EXTRA float64=0)</tspan>` (charts-diagrams/probe/p_flat_zero.json). Same output for a series containing `null` (probe/p_nan.json, which the engine silently coerces to 0) and for a single-category zero bar (single/bar_single_point__stress.json). Root cause: LinearScale.TickFormat computes `precision = int(max(0, -floor(log10(|step|))))`; with a degenerate domain step is 0, log10(0) = -Inf and the resulting `fmt.Sprintf("%%.%df", precision)` produces an invalid verb. validate reports only an info-level all_zero_series and says nothing about the corrupted label.

ALSO REPORTED (mcp-surface: "svggen TickFormat prints '%!(NOVERB)' onto slides for flat chart data; render still reports success/100"): A chart whose values collapse to a single value (all zeros, or non-numeric strings coerced to 0) renders the literal Go format-error string as the axis label. Repro through MCP: render_deck_spec with slides[0].chart = {type:"bar_chart",data:{categories:["a","b"],series:[{name:"s",values:["1","two"]}]}} -> success=true, quality_summary.score=100, diagnostics=[]; the rendered slide shows '(NOVERB)%!(EXTRA float64=0)' where the axis labels belong and an empty plot (see out_chart/m.jpg, right panel). Root cause: svggen/scales.go:211 LinearScale.TickFormat computes precision = int(math.Max(0, -math.Floor(math.Log10(math.Abs(step))))) — with step==0, log10(0) = -Inf so precision = 9223372036854775807 and the format becomes "%.9223372036854775807f" (reproduced standalone: fmt.Sprintf on that format yields exactly "%!(NOVERB)%!(EXTRA float64=0)"). It is consumed at svggen/axes.go:147 and svggen/cartesian_layout.go:291.

WHERE
svggen/scales.go:211-222 (LinearScale.TickFormat); consumers svggen/axes.go:130-145 and svggen/cartesian_layout.go:275-292 (AdaptYLabels)
[mcp-surface] svggen/scales.go:211-222 LinearScale.TickFormat; consumers svggen/axes.go:147, svggen/cartesian_layout.go:291; MCP surface cmd/json2pptx/mcp_semantic.go (no diagnostic emitted).

HOW
Guard TickFormat: if step is 0, NaN or Inf (degenerate domain), fall back to precision 0 and a nice symmetric domain (e.g. [0,1]). Additionally reject/flag nulls in series values instead of coercing to 0 (emit INPUT.chart_value_coerced). Add a unit test for domains (0,0), (5,5) and values containing null.

Alternative/extra HOW from mcp-surface: In TickFormat, guard the degenerate domain: `if step == 0 || math.IsNaN(step) || math.IsInf(step,0) { return "%.0f" }` and clamp precision to [0,6]. Additionally emit a chart finding (chart.flat_series / chart.no_variance) when domainMin==domainMax so render_deck_spec reports it instead of scoring 100, and coerce non-numeric series values to a CHART finding rather than 0.

VERIFY
go test ./svggen -run TickFormat; then `j2p generate --json charts-diagrams/probe/p_flat_zero.json` and assert no tspan matching `NOVERB` in ppt/media/*.svg.
[mcp-surface] cd svggen && go test ./... -run TestTickFormat (new case: TickFormat on a zero-span domain returns "%.0f"); end-to-end: render the repro spec and grep the produced SVG/EMF for 'NOVERB' (must be absent); MCP: the same call returns a chart.* diagnostic and score < 100.

WHAT

ALSO REPORTED (quality-signal: "table_rows_truncated drops data rows at review severity: 12-row table ships 9 rows, gate still passes"): B06 puts a 9-column, 12-row table on a slide. The engine renders 9 rows plus a literal '…and 3 more rows' cell and reports table_rows_truncated at action=review (weight 5). Deck score 88, quality_gate.passed true, auto_repair gate passed. Dropping three rows of financial data is content loss, not a styling nit — any deck that reaches a reviewer with silently missing rows is wrong regardless of how it looks. The correct fix (split_at_row) is already computed in the finding's params, so the deck is trivially repairable; there is no reason to let it pass.

WHERE
internal/generator/table.go:178 (`fmt.Sprintf("...and %d more rows", overflow)`) and table.go:1165 row-capacity check; finding emission mapped to code table_rows_truncated; cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go fit_report default false.

Emit the same finding from the PRE-flight path so validate_input / validate_deck_spec catch it before generation, with next_tool_call=repair_slide{split_at_row} (the fix is already computed). title: Set isError / ok:false on failed or refused DeckSpec renders (template not found, action:refuse diagnostics)
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: closure-audit-1, mcp-surface (finding refs m.0, c1.1).

WHAT
The recommended fast-path tools return CallToolResult WITHOUT IsError for every domain failure. Observed on the wire (out_errs2/): template not found -> {"isError" absent, structuredContent:{ok:false,success:false,error:"template not found: midnight-blu; available templates: [...]"}}; unparseable spec (slides as object) -> isError absent, error "render_deck_spec: spec could not be parsed"; unknown chart type -> isError absent, error "invalid slide specification: slide 1: shape_grid: nested sub-grid at row 0 col 0: diagram in grid cell 204: svggen render failed: svggen: unknown diagram type \"barchart\""; validate_deck_spec with an unknown kind -> isError absent, ok:false. Argument-level failures on the SAME tools DO set isError (INPUT.MISSING_PARAMETER, INPUT.INVALID_PARAMETER), so isError is inconsistent within one tool and across the server: generate_presentation / validate_input / score_deck / render_* all set isError=true for the equivalent TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND. An agent (or a harness) that branches on isError — the only protocol-level failure signal — will treat a deck that was never written as done, then call render_deck_thumbnails on a stale/missing path.

ALSO REPORTED (closure-audit-1: "render_deck_spec / semantic render report ok:true and score 85 while emitting an action:refuse error diagnostic"): Closure audit spillover from go-slide-creator-j02x/htwq. The same modern-template deck that renders unusably returns, over MCP, `isError: null`, `ok: true`, `quality_summary.score: 85`, `pptx_path` set — with `diagnostics[] = [{code: text_overflow, severity: error, action: refuse}]` buried in the payload. The CLI behaves the same (`semantic render … ; echo $?` -> 0) even though --output-validation defaults to strict. An agent keying on ok/isError/score (which the server instructions tell it to use as the precondition) ships a broken slide; only reading every diagnostic's severity saves it.

WHERE
cmd/json2pptx/mcp_semantic.go: semanticSuccessOrInternal(), semanticRenderToMCP(), buildSemanticRenderFailure(); internal/api/mcp_result.go: MCPSuccessResult (only builder that omits IsError), MCPDiagnosticsError (sets it). Tools: render_deck_spec, validate_deck_spec (+ compile_deck_spec, explain_deck_spec in --tools all).
[closure-audit-1] cmd/json2pptx/mcp_semantic.go (render_deck_spec result assembly), internal/api/mcp_result.go MCPSuccessResult, semantic render CLI exit path; docs/AGENT_DIAGNOSTICS.md

HOW
Add api.MCPResultFor(ctx, data, ok bool) (or MCPFailureResult) that sets IsError=true when the payload's ok/success is false, and route the semantic handlers through it: in semanticSuccessOrInternal, inspect the built result's ok/success field and use MCPDiagnosticsError-style IsError. Keep the rich structuredContent exactly as-is (diagnostics + explanation_summary are valuable on failure) — only the IsError flag changes. Do the same for validate_deck_spec when ok=false has error-severity findings.

Alternative/extra HOW from closure-audit-1: Make any diagnostic with severity=error / action=refuse force ok:false (and isError or a blocking_reasons entry) and drop the heuristic score to 0 for the affected slide; keep the pptx path so the agent can still inspect, but label it `publishable:false, blocking_reasons:["render_refuse"]`. CLI should exit non-zero under --output-validation=strict.

VERIFY
go test ./cmd/json2pptx -run 'TestSemantic.*Error|TestRenderDeckSpecFailure'; on the wire: `render_deck_spec {spec:{meta:{title:"T",template:"midnight-blu"},slides:[{kind:"title",title:"x"}]}}` must return isError=true; a parity test asserting every tool whose structuredContent has ok=false or success=false also has IsError=true.
[closure-audit-1] Run the MCP call in /Users/seb/projects/json2pptx/.claude/review-evidence/r2/closure-audit-1/mcp/modern_fallback_mcp.json's repro: response must have ok:false (or blocking_reasons containing the refuse finding). `/Users/seb/projects/json2pptx/.claude/review-evidence/r2/j2p semantic render --spec sem/stress.yaml --template modern-template …; echo $?` must be non-zero.

title: Measured title-fit check must run without explicit layout_id (slide_type and DeckSpec paths fall back to 60-char heuristic)
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: closure-audit-2, dogfood-a (finding refs c2.4, a.1).

WHAT
CLOSURE AUDIT of go-slide-creator-vjwn (closed: 'One measured title check shared by validate/quality/fit report'). It only runs when the slide carries layout_id. With layout_id:'content' on modern-template a 105-char title yields the measured message in all three surfaces ('only fits its title placeholder at 60% of the template 45pt size; shorten to <= 74 chars', score 85). The SAME title with slide_type:'content' (no layout_id) yields the legacy heuristic 'title too long (105 chars, max 60)', score 70, and the fit report stays silent — and so does the DeckSpec path: render_deck_spec on an executive_summary slide with that title returns quality_summary issues:['title too long (105 chars, max 60)'] while validate_deck_spec reports no issues. Since DeckSpec is now the recommended agent path, the fix effectively does not apply where it matters.

ALSO REPORTED (dogfood-a: "DeckSpec (fast path) loses measured title-fit checks: 195-char title passes validate_deck_spec + render_deck_spec with no finding"): Same 195-char title, two paths. Raw path (validate_input) returns measured warnings: INPUT.title_wraps 'title (195 chars) only fits its title placeholder at 60% of the template 44pt size; shorten to <= 103' plus INPUT.max_length. Recommended DeckSpec path: validate_deck_spec returns ZERO findings (ok:true), render_deck_spec diagnostics are empty, and the only trace is the legacy character heuristic inside quality_summary ('title too long (195 chars, max 60)') while the deck still scores 90/100. Root cause: the per-kind compilers emit SlideInput with SlideType only and no LayoutID (e.g. CompileExecutiveSummary), and layoutForSlideResolved returns nil for an empty LayoutID, so both measureTitleInPlaceholder and collectTitleFitFindings skip the slide. This partially regresses go-slide-creator-vjwn/6cjs ('unify title length checks on actual box fit'): the unified measured check is bypassed on the path get_started recommends.

WHERE
cmd/json2pptx/title_measure.go:179 layoutForSlideResolved (returns nil when slide.LayoutID == ""), titlePlaceholderFor:195, collectTitleFitFindings:211; cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go:1812-1830 (fallback to maxTitleLen)
[dogfood-a] cmd/json2pptx/title_measure.go:179-205 layoutForSlideResolved/titlePlaceholderFor; cmd/json2pptx/fit_findings_collect.go:932 findLayoutForSlide (returns nil when LayoutID==""); cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go:1774 maxTitleLen=60 fallback; internal/semantic/slides/content.go:14 CompileExecutiveSummary (no LayoutID); cmd/json2pptx/semantic_cmd.go:577

HOW
Resolve the layout the generator would actually pick (the same auto-selection that produces resolved_layout_id, e.g. slideLayout4 here) before measuring, instead of bailing out on empty LayoutID; thread that resolved layout into computeQualityScoreWithLayouts and collectTitleFitFindings. Drop the 60-char fallback once the measured path always resolves.

Alternative/extra HOW from dogfood-a: Resolve the layout the generator will actually pick when LayoutID is empty (slide_type -> canonical layout id, the same resolution generate uses) inside layoutForSlideResolved, or have each semantic compiler set the canonical LayoutID it intends (title/content/blank-title/section/closing). Then drop the 60-char fallback to info-only. Add a semantic-path regression test asserting a 195-char title produces title_wraps at severity warning from validate_deck_spec.

VERIFY

title: Reconcile content-sized pattern heights with SLIDE_UNDERUSED: patterns fill 21-32% yet the finding blames an internal cap
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: gallery, quality-signal (finding refs g.3, q.7).

WHAT
After the content-sizing change (go-slide-creator-7km8) the pattern band no longer stretches, but nothing grows it either, so a normal consulting slide is a thin strip floating in the middle of the slide. Measured shape extents on forest-green.real (slide height 540pt, content zone ~142-502pt): kpi-3up 234.7-409.7pt (32% of the slide, 49% of the zone), process-flow 254-390pt (25%), timeline-horizontal 266-379pt (21%), stylish-panels 250-394pt (27%), before-after 252-392pt (26%) - versus stat-hero 67% and exec-summary 60% which do fill. Visually this is the most common realistic-content defect in the sweep (sheets/real.02.kpi-3up.png, real.06.kpi-inline.png, rev.forest-green.6.png). INPUT.SLIDE_UNDERUSED fires for some of them (process-flow, timeline-horizontal, stylish-panels, before-after, kpi-inline) but not for kpi-2up..6up (49% area vs the 45% threshold), and its fix hint reads 'remove bounds / max_height_pct caps, add a supporting zone, or merge with another slide' - the agent set no bounds and no max_height_pct; the cap is inside the pattern, so the hint cannot be acted on.

ALSO REPORTED (quality-signal: "SLIDE_UNDERUSED (45%) penalises round-1's content-sized pattern heights; fires on all three good decks"): SLIDE_UNDERUSED fires when the ink bounding box covers <45% of the safe content area. It fired on every one of my three deliberately well-crafted decks — G1 slide 6 (phase-roadmap, 43%), G2 slide 5 (before-after, 29%) and slide 6 (phase-roadmap, 42%), G3 slides 4 and 6 (43%) — all of which look correct in the renders. These are exactly the slides that round-1 bead go-slide-creator-7km8 ('Content-sized pattern heights: stop stretching cards/steps to full content area') deliberately made shorter. The finding now tells the agent to undo that fix ('remove bounds / max_height_pct caps'), and its fix kind is unexecutable anyway. Simultaneously the check is suppressed entirely when a body placeholder has content (fit_findings_geometry.go:290 hasBodyPlaceholderContent), so B03 — five slides each carrying one 1-word bullet ('Grow', 'Big', 'Good') — emits nothing and scores 100. title: Porter's five-forces connectors strike through Suppliers/Buyers boxes (wrong connection-site indices)
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18 (source: orch). Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b.

WHAT
Rendered porters_five_forces on midnight-blue: the two horizontal connectors start at the FAR side of the Suppliers and Buyers boxes and run straight through the box text into Rivalry (vertical connectors are fine). Root cause: connectorPairs in porters_shapes.go assumes rect connection site 1=right, 3=left; OOXML rect sites are 0=top, 1=left, 2=bottom, 3=right (corrected for shapegrid in commit 13e4292 / bead 2szb, but this caller was never updated). Also visible on the same slide: factor bullets render a stray orange '*' marker and the italic intensity line ('Medium (50%)') is overprinted by the connector.

WHERE
internal/generator/porters_shapes.go: connectorPairs (~line 442) {porterSupplier,porterRivalry,1,3} and {porterBuyer,porterRivalry,3,1}; generatePorterConnectorXML; bullet marker in generatePorterForceBoxXML. Reference fix: commit 13e4292 (internal/pptx connector sites).

HOW
Swap the horizontal pairs to supplier fromSite=3 (right) -> rivalry toSite=1 (left) and buyer fromSite=1 (left) -> rivalry toSite=3 (right); prefer named constants shared with the shapegrid connector code (siteTop/Left/Bottom/Right) over literals so the two cannot drift again. Replace the '*' text bullet with a real a:buChar bullet (or '•') in the box text color. Add a unit test asserting stCxn/endCxn idx per pair and that connector endpoints lie on facing edges.

VERIFY
Generate .claude/review-evidence/r2/orch/porter.json on midnight-blue and warm-coral, render, LOOK: horizontal arrows span only the gap between boxes, arrowhead touching Rivalry's left/right edge; no line crosses any box text. go test ./internal/generator/ -run Porter.

EVIDENCE
- .claude/review-evidence/r2/orch/porter.json
- .claude/review-evidence/r2/orch/porter-1.png (before)

Skill/docs sync (CLAUDE.md policy): any agent-visible change updates skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md (+ docs/FIT_FINDINGS.md / docs/PATTERNS.md / docs/INPUT_FORMAT.md / docs/SCHEMA_CHANGELOG.md as applicable) in the same commit.
Gates: golangci-lint run ./... && go test ./... -short -race (plus `cd svggen && golangci-lint run ./... && go test ./...` if svggen touched); go test -run TemplatePatternMatrix ./cmd/json2pptx/... if patterns/shapegrid/generator touched.
Visual evidence: build ./cmd/json2pptx, generate on midnight-blue AND warm-coral (-templates-dir templates), rasterize (pptx2jpg, or soffice -env:UserInstallation=<private> --headless --convert-to pdf + pdftoppm -r 90 -png), LOOK at before/after PNGs and cite their paths in the close reason.
close_reason: Fixed in 5845215. internal/generator/porters_shapes.go connectorPairs now resolves every site through pptx.ConnectionSiteIndex(pptx.GeomRoundRect, side) with named sides instead of literals, so this caller cannot drift from the shapegrid connector code again (the same literals were corrected there in 13e4292 / bead 2szb). Root cause confirmed: OOXML lists rect sites counter-clockwise from the top (0=top, 1=left, 2=bottom, 3=right), so the old {supplier,rivalry,1,3} and {buyer,rivalry,3,1} attached to the FAR side of each box. Verified in generated midnight-blue XML: 'Porter Supplier Power site 3 -> Porter Competitive Rivalry site 1' and 'Porter Buyer Power site 1 -> Porter Competitive Rivalry site 3' (previously 1->3 and 3->1); vertical pairs unchanged at 2->0 and 0->2. The overprinted italic intensity line was a consequence of the line crossing the box and is resolved by the correct attachment. Stray '*' marker: the factor bullets emitted <a:buChar char="•"/> with NO <a:buFont>, so the glyph resolved in the theme font and renderers substituted (the reported orange '*'). Added pptx.DefaultBulletChar / pptx.DefaultBulletFont (the values pptx.BulletOptions already defaulted to, now shared rather than duplicated) and the Porter bullets name the font — verified the XML now carries <a:buFont typeface="Arial"/> alongside every <a:buChar char="•"/>. Tests: TestPorterConnectorSites (asserts stCxn/endCxn idx per pair against pptx.ConnectionSiteIndex, resolving shape ids to names so the assertion reads as 'which side of which box'), TestPorterFactorBulletsDeclareBuFont (every buChar has a matching buFont and both use the shared constants). title: CI: make Arial fallback metrics deterministic across hosts
description: The root text-fit suite and svggen golden suites fail on Ubuntu because fontconfig silently aliases Arial to DejaVu Sans, changing reported fallback identity and SVG geometry. title: SVG HTTP timeline icon URLs permit server-side requests to private targets
description:
Baseline c9a5793. svggen/icon_loader.go:118-140 uses unrestricted http.Client.Get; svggen/timeline.go:1711-1713 accepts activity icon from user data and lines 1164-1185 load it. Default unauthenticated SVG server exposes this through POST /render. Closed rl3l hardened internal/resource, not this separate loader. Parent checked source; independent oracle-backed reviewer executed a loopback canary.

## Steps to Reproduce
POST /render with {"type":"timeline","data":{"activities":[{"name":"probe","start":"2024-01-01","end":"2024-12-31","icon":"http://127.0.0.1:<canary-port>"}]}}. Server returns 200 and loopback canary receives one GET even when its response is not an image. Invalid image decoding does not prevent request side effects. Cloud metadata, redirects and local-file disclosure were not runtime-tested.
acceptance_criteria: Enforce an explicit icon-source policy at the HTTP boundary. Reject private/loopback/link-local URL targets and redirects/DNS resolutions to them, or disable remote icons for HTTP. Preserve explicitly trusted CLI behavior if required. Add real local canary tests proving denied requests never connect; include redirect and DNS-rebinding-safe dialing policies and local icon-path boundaries.
close_reason: Implemented the reported defect with regression coverage; affected targeted package tests pass.

title: split_slide repeat_headers=false drops continuation table data
description:
Baseline c9a5793. cmd/json2pptx/split_slide.go:88-100 clears continuation headers; internal/generator/table.go:61-69 rejects headerless tables; internal/generator/media.go:294-305 downgrades this into skipped table media. This affects raw split_slide, separately from semantic content-preservation work fh57.6.

## Steps to Reproduce
Generate midnight-blue slideLayout2/body table with headers=[Metric], rows=[[RowAlpha],[RowBravo],[RowCharlie]], split by table.rows, group_size=1, repeat_headers=false, strict-fit off. Independent reviewer observed exit 0 and three slides, two warnings that table must have at least one header. ZIP XML text: slide1=[Metric,RowAlpha], slide2=[], slide3=[]. Parent confirmed conflicting contracts in source.
acceptance_criteria: Separate column definitions from header visibility, or reject unsupported repeat_headers=false before generation. Every input row must appear exactly once on its intended output page; test false and true modes, remainder pages and content diagnostics. Never return successful generation after silently dropping continuation rows.
close_reason: Implemented the reported defect with regression coverage; affected targeted package tests pass.

title: Failed generation deletes a pre-existing output deck
description:
Baseline c9a5793. internal/generator/slides.go:239-243 unconditionally removes req.OutputPath when generateSinglePass fails, although that invocation writes to a temporary file before publication. An invalid request can destroy a previously generated deck. Oracle review and independent child runtime reproduction confirmed this; parent verified local source.

## Steps to Reproduce
Write KEEP ME into existing.pptx. Call generator.Generate with that OutputPath, midnight-blue template and layout not-a-layout. Generation returns layout-not-found and os.Stat(existing.pptx) returns not-exist. The previous artifact should remain intact.
acceptance_criteria: On all pre-publication failures preserve existing destination bytes. Clean up only invocation-owned temporary files. Test invalid layout, template-open error and cancellation with existing sentinel output, plus successful replacement and no leftover temp files.
close_reason: Implemented the reported defect with regression coverage; affected targeted package tests pass.

title: Predictable generation temporary path follows symlinks and clobbers files
description:
Baseline c9a5793. internal/generator/contexts.go:211-215 sets tmpPath=outputPath+".tmp"; internal/generator/singlepass.go:108-129 opens it with os.Create. A process/user able to plant a symlink in the output directory can redirect truncation to any target writable by the generator. This is conditional local filesystem exposure, not proven remote traversal. Shared same-destination temp also risks concurrent interference, not yet reproduced.

## Steps to Reproduce
In a disposable output directory, write KEEP ME to a victim and symlink deck.pptx.tmp to it. Generate a valid midnight-blue slideLayout2 deck to deck.pptx. Independent oracle-review worker observed successful generation and victim replaced by 16384 bytes of PPTX. Parent checked local source.
acceptance_criteria: Use an exclusively created unique temporary file in the destination directory, retain ownership through cleanup, and atomically publish. Test planted legacy-name symlink remains untouched and parallel same-destination invocations never share/corrupt temporary files. Specify final-writer semantics.
close_reason: Implemented the reported defect with regression coverage; affected targeted package tests pass.

title: Placeholder table emits duplicate per-slide OOXML shape ID 4

title: Gate template portability with adversarial rendered regression fixtures
description:
Context: docs/SLIDE_QUALITY_REDESIGN.md; reviewed baseline 2c219bf. Scope is user-provided PPTX templates with seven canonical layouts, not arbitrary template reconstruction.

What
Build a reproducible content-by-template matrix covering bundled templates and independent seven-layout fixtures, including cases bundled templates do not exercise. Gate content/geometry deterministically and visually inspect/render representative outputs; do not use byte-identical screenshots as the sole oracle.

Where
tests/quality, internal/template fixtures, tests/quality/run.sh, CI workflows, examples/semantic/qbr.yaml

How
Include 4:3/16:9/ultrawide, reordered/nonnumeric role bindings, multiple masters, inherited styles, dark fills, foreground logos, font substitutions and sparse/dense/long/multilingual content. Pin renderer/font environment for golden jobs, use tolerant geometry/image comparisons and save contact sheets/failure artifacts. Keep unsupported malformed cases explicit. Require documented human review for baseline updates.

Boundary
Implement this deliverable and its tests together; reuse existing metadata, source maps, rendering and quality infrastructure. Do not implement unrelated epic work. Preserve backwards compatibility or explicitly document a migration.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce QBR wrong-layout defect and off-slide chrome on altered dimensions before fixes, pass after fixes. All matrix decks preserve facts and have no off-slide/forbidden overlap; rendered review detects planted tiny text, clipping and unreadable contrast. Run required CI job with renderer absent to confirm failure, local optional job to confirm explicit skip. Record which renderer was actually tested; PowerPoint/LibreOffice differences stay disclosed.
close_reason: Added adversarial portability matrix policy, required rendered CI job with renderer provenance/pixel hashes, explicit optional skip, aspect/template feature coverage, and fail-closed tests.

title: Generate executable source-grounded repairs with meaning safeguards
description:
Context: docs/SLIDE_QUALITY_REDESIGN.md; reviewed baseline 2c219bf. Scope is user-provided PPTX templates with seven canonical layouts, not arbitrary template reconstruction.

What

Where

How
Each proposal carries target stable ID/path, preconditions/revision, typed parameters, expected improvement and semantic impact. Unsupported targets return an actionable no-op diagnostic, never pretend success. Prefer geometry/recomposition/splitting before text edits; meaning-changing edits require review. Validate, regenerate and reinspect after application; retain best version and cap/reject oscillating or degrading changes.

Boundary
Implement this deliverable and its tests together; reuse existing metadata, source maps, rendering and quality infrastructure. Do not implement unrelated epic work. Preserve backwards compatibility or explicitly document a migration.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end tests for reduce_cell_text cell_path/max_chars, reshape_grid pattern-array values, swap_layout layout_id and replace_color from/to. Test stale revision, wrong target, unsupported repair, repeated proposals and harmful truncation of a negated claim. Assert proposed applicable repairs run successfully and semantic facts survive. Run visualqa, semantic and CLI tests.
close_reason: Implemented revision-bound targeted executable repairs, typed parameters, duplicate suppression, stale/wrong-target rejection, semantic truncation safeguards, and end-to-end tests; CLI/semantic/visualqa suites pass.

title: Make all-slide rendered inspection an available completion step
description:
Context: docs/SLIDE_QUALITY_REDESIGN.md; reviewed baseline 2c219bf. Scope is user-provided PPTX templates with seven canonical layouts, not arbitrary template reconstruction.

What
Connect generated deck pixels and contact sheet to host-agent or configured vision inspection, inspecting every slide plus cross-deck consistency. Do not require a specific vendor/API key or silently upgrade a heuristic fallback to visual review.

Where
cmd/pptx2jpg, cmd/json2pptx/mcp_visual_qa.go, internal/visualqa, preview/inspection tools and quality completion protocol

How
Expose current-revision thumbnails/contact sheet with actual semantic roles and findings that identify slide/object, category, severity, evidence and next action. Support host/manual recorded review and configured provider adapters using one contract. Keep content fidelity, readability, hierarchy, clipping, contrast and template fidelity separate. Include advisory design defects in final review status; bounded iterations must end with truthful unresolved findings. No automatic external paid calls without configured consent.

Boundary

title: semantic: add fail-fast payload-shape/usable-content validation layer shared by validate, explain, and compile
description:
## Summary
The semantic compiler's recurring rot is covert leniency: parsers/builders preserve malformed payloads, validation checks shallow presence/counts, normalize advertises ideal visuals, and compile later drops/degrades content. The desired policy is fail-fast: return actionable findings to the using agent as early as possible, instead of shipping empty/degraded slides behind .

## Proposed design
1. Decode root generically first and validate container shapes: root object, meta object, slides present array, each slide object.
2. Add a small per-kind payload contract table (not a full rewrite): required-one-of fields, expected JSON shapes, usable-content extractors, pattern feasibility caps.
3. Treat content-bearing required fields that extract to zero usable content as blocking errors. Type/shape mismatches should be errors under strict and at least warnings under warn; content-dropping cases should block even in warn.
4. Make Normalize/Explain consult the same feasibility checks as Compile so it never advertises a pattern compile will not emit.
5. Validate  payloads as raw slides before compile/render and map findings back to semantic paths.
6. Centralize strictness/output-validation enum parsing so CLI and MCP reject typos/wrong types instead of defaulting.

## Acceptance criteria
- Existing semantic-parser beads for silent type drops, raw escape hatch parity, meta unknown keys, duplicate empty-kind findings, weak placeholder false positives, and the new fail-fast gaps are covered by regression tests.
-  is a trustworthy precondition: a spec with  does not compile to blank/incomplete slides due to malformed payload shape.
- Strict mode blocks all advisories that imply compile degradation or content loss; warn mode still returns explicit findings early enough for an agent to repair.
- Explain/compile pattern parity remains true for degraded/over-cap inputs.
close_reason: Verified: fail-fast semantic validation layer fully implemented via 12 closed children. Container-shape decode (eklv), per-kind kindFieldShapes contract + validateFieldShapes (88g8), requireUsableContent zero-content blocking, shared feasibility caps for explain/compile parity (hadk/wzd4), preflightRawPatterns raw-slide validation before render mapped to semantic paths, and centralized strictness/output-validation enum parsing (jlk5/td00). Build/vet/test/lint green on both modules.

title: semantic: raw_json2pptx object with invalid raw slide validates and compiles to empty content instead of failing fast
description:
## Summary
A  payload that is an object but not a valid raw json2pptx slide passes semantic validate and compile. Unknown raw fields are discarded during decode, yielding a raw slide with  and no layout/slide_type — a broken escape-hatch slide that is not caught until later surfaces.

## Reproduction

 -> ok/no issues.  -> one slide: .

## Expected
Fail fast at : raw_json2pptx must be a valid raw SlideInput with at least a layout/slide_type and valid content/shape/pattern fields. Unknown raw fields should not be silently dropped inside the escape hatch.

## Root cause
 only checks  is non-empty.  marshals and unmarshals into ;  drops unknown fields by default.  preflights only pattern validity, not raw slide structural validity.

## Suggested fix
Validate the raw escape hatch as raw json2pptx input during semantic validation/compile. At minimum decode with unknown-field checking for raw slide payloads and require a renderable slide shape. Map diagnostics back to  paths.

Regression test + SKILL.md/SEMANTIC_COMPILER.md docs updated.

title: semantic: blank list entries satisfy required fields/counts, then compile to slides with missing body content
description:
## Summary
Required array fields count raw entries, not usable content. A process slide with three blank string steps validates with  because  is a non-empty array of length 3, but compile drops all blank steps and emits a title-only slide plus takeaway.

## Reproduction

 -> ok/no issues.  -> content slide containing only the title; all steps disappeared.

## Expected
Fail fast: required content-bearing lists must contain enough usable/nonblank items after extraction. For process this means 3-8 usable steps for a process-flow visual, and zero usable steps must be a blocking error.

## Root cause
 returns true for any non-empty list;  returns raw length. The compiler helpers (, , roadmap/comparison extractors) trim/drop blank entries, so validation and compile disagree about whether content exists.

## Suggested fix
Introduce per-kind usable-content validation: count renderable entries after the same trimming/extraction rules compile uses. Treat required fields that extract to zero usable content as errors, not warnings. Apply to process, roadmap, comparison, executive_summary, kpi_snapshot, chart_insight, and closing bullets.
close_reason: Implemented: required content-bearing lists (process steps, roadmap phases, kpi cells, comparison columns) are now validated by usable post-extraction count, not raw length. A required list whose entries are all blank/labelless now emits a blocking SEMANTIC_REQUIRED (always error) instead of passing and compiling to a title-only slide; density advisories also count usable entries so validate/compile agree. Mirrored the compiler's exact extractors via new exported slides.Usable*Count helpers. Added regression tests + synced docs/AGENT_DIAGNOSTICS.md.

title: semantic: chart_insight with chart+takeaway passes validation but compile drops the chart
description:
## Summary
A  slide can satisfy validation with a valid  and , but compile emits only title/takeaway and silently drops the chart. This is especially damaging because the slide kind's primary payload is the chart.

## Reproduction

## Expected
Fail fast unless there is a usable / payload, or treat  as the insight source during compile. In either case, a valid chart should not disappear behind a green validate gate.

## Root cause

## Suggested fix
Make  fail-fast require one of  or non-empty  (or update compile to use takeaway as a single insight). Add a regression asserting chart+takeaway alone cannot validate cleanly unless compile preserves the chart.
