- id="Section Number" type=body  FontSize=9600 (96pt)  Y=572,408    H=3,417,887  MaxChars=173 (decorative number)

Auto-numbering logic at cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go:692-705 scans content for PlaceholderID == "body" and, if absent, appends a ContentInput with PlaceholderID="body" carrying the formatted section number (e.g. "01"). On modern-template that injects "01" into the small 14pt tagline slot at the bottom of the slide, leaving the 96pt decorative "Section Number" frame at the top empty. Visual result: the prominent number area is blank; the small tagline shows a giant looking number.

Root-cause fix has two parts:
1. Engine: when a section-divider layout has both a "body" placeholder AND a section_number alias placeholder, route the auto-injected section number to the section_number alias ("Section Number" / "section_number" / "section_no" / "large_number") instead of "body". Use generator.IsSectionNumberAlias and the existing alias resolver (internal/generator/placeholder_resolver.go:325 resolveSectionNumber).
2. Template: decide whether modern-template's Section Divider should also keep a tagline "body" slot. If yes, document it. If not, remove the duplicate body placeholder so layouts agree across templates.
acceptance_criteria: Auto-numbered section divider slide on modern-template renders "01" in the 96pt Section Number frame, not in the 14pt body tagline slot. A test verifies that, given a layout with both "body" and a section_number alias, the auto-numbering injection targets the alias.
notes: Agent-native review: fix must route all section-divider text by placeholder role, not only auto-number injection. The section_number alias gets decorative section-number handling; optional body/tagline placeholders use normal text handling with caps/autofit so taglines are not boosted as section titles.
close_reason: Engine: auto-assigned section numbers now route to a layout's section_number placeholder (via canonical Role / alias ID / 'Section Number' name) before virtual-ID mapping, falling back to body only when no number frame exists. New injectSectionNumber/layoutHasSectionNumberPlaceholder/contentTargetsSectionSlot helpers + unit and end-to-end regression tests. modern-template's tagline body slot kept intentionally; documented section-divider auto-numbering + optional tagline contract in docs/TEMPLATE_SPEC.md.

title: estimateMaxChars ignores placeholder FontSize, so "Section Number" reports 146-297 char capacity instead of ~2
description:
Direct root cause of the user's reported "2-digit max placeholder gets stuffed with text" defect. internal/template/layouts.go:246-272 (estimateMaxChars) uses HARD-CODED charWidthEMU=91440 (~10 chars/inch) and lineHeightEMU=274320 — assumes a body font around 18pt. The placeholder's actual FontSize (already extracted into PlaceholderInfo.FontSize) is never consulted.

Measured impact on the decorative "Section Number" placeholder (rendered at 96-208pt):
- abstract: FontSize=13600 (136pt), MaxChars reported=146 (true capacity ~3)
- blue-corporate: FontSize=20800 (208pt), MaxChars=297
- business-template: FontSize=20800 (208pt), MaxChars=288
- forest-green / midnight-blue / warm-coral: FontSize=13600 (136pt), MaxChars=173
- modern-template: FontSize=9600 (96pt), MaxChars=173
- modern-yellow: FontSize=20800 (208pt), MaxChars=185
- modern: FontSize=13600 (136pt), MaxChars=201

Cascading consequences:
1. Agents reading template metadata see "this placeholder fits 200 characters" and fill it with text.
2. cmd/json2pptx/validate_template.go:378 (checkSectionNumberNaming) gates on MaxChars<5, which is therefore never true — the validator never warns even for misnamed decorative number frames.
3. cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go:1819 lint that warns on "section divider body misused as text" only fires when targeting "body" placeholder ID, not section_number aliases.

Fix: scale charWidthEMU by FontSize (e.g. charWidthEMU = round(91440 * FontSize/1800)) when FontSize > 0; clamp result. Re-run all template metadata fixtures and assert Section Number maxChars is in single digits.
acceptance_criteria: estimateMaxChars takes FontSize into account. For every shipped template, the "Section Number" placeholder reports MaxChars <= 5. checkSectionNumberNaming's font-size gate is removed or kept as a redundant guard. Existing tests for body/title maxChars still pass.
notes: Agent-native review: false max_chars corrupts planning context. Acceptance must cover all call sites, not just estimator math: ParseLayouts and synthetic layout generation must resolve FontSize before MaxChars, emitted metadata should include font_size_pt evidence, and corpus tests should prove section_number MaxChars <= 5 for parsed and synthesized layouts.
close_reason: Implemented: estimateMaxChars now scales char width and line height by the resolved placeholder FontSize (hundredths-of-a-point, 18pt baseline). Reordered extractPlaceholders so font is resolved before capacity estimate; synthesis passes gp.Style.FontSize. Corrected base glyph-advance constant to a self-consistent 0.5em so all shipped templates' Section Number placeholders report MaxChars<=5 (modern-template 96pt frame went 173->4). Added TestSectionNumberMaxCharsCorpus over all templates + font-scaling unit cases. checkSectionNumberNaming font-size gate kept as redundant guard.

title: fit/preflight validator uses different safe-area logic than generation, so layout-derived overlaps slip through
description: Validation gap revealed by the visual-QA overlap defects (go-slide-creator-3a29, -40to). cmd/json2pptx/fit_findings_collect.go (around lines 428-468, 482-527, 553-604) computes grid origins from body placeholders and resolves shape_grid bounds via shapegrid.DefaultBounds() or input.Bounds — it does NOT call the same resolveVirtualLayout / ContentZone helper used by generation in cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go and cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go. Consequence: preflight cannot detect the exact class of title/body overlap caused by template-specific chrome geometry; failures only show up after LibreOffice rendering. Fix: extract zone/bounds resolution into one helper consumed by both the generator and preflight, then re-run fit findings against that resolved geometry.
acceptance_criteria: A single layout-aware ContentZone/Bounds helper is shared between generation and fit/preflight. Adding a synthetic deck whose grid intrudes into the title triggers a preflight finding instead of only being caught visually.
notes: Agent-native review: promote this to the shared geometry contract for generation, preflight, preview, score, wireframe, and examine-template. Extract one layout-aware ResolveContentZone/Bounds helper under internal code; j15r and ihmo are concrete regression cases. Agents cannot trust preflight or plan shape_grid slides until this helper is shared.
close_reason: Extracted shared layout-aware geometry helper (resolveGridGeometry + resolveGridBounds in shape_grid.go) now consumed by generation (json_mode.go), preflight (fit_findings_collect.go), and preview (mcp_preview.go). Preflight resolves shape_grid cells with the same zone-clamp/override-bounds geometry generation renders, including virtual-layout slides that previously had no structural checks. Added DetectTitleCollision detector + title_collision finding code so a grid intruding into the title band is caught at preflight (e.g. flipped-geometry layouts) instead of only after LibreOffice render. Docs (FIT_FINDINGS.md, skills FINDINGS.md) updated.

title: internal/testrand hardcodes emoji codepoints in multiple stress corpora
description:
Root cause for go-slide-creator-6wnl. Hardcoded emoji currently shipped:
- internal/testrand/visual_deck.go:532-535 (panel_layout demo icons 📊 👥 🎯 📈)
- internal/testrand/visual_deck.go:653 (edge unicode bullet '📊 Revenue 📈 Growth 🎯 Target ✅ Achieved')
- internal/testrand/generator.go:215 (edge-case corpus '🚀 📊 💡 🎯 ✅ ❌' fed to maybeEdge() which injects into titles/bullets/footer/header/table)
- internal/testrand/svg_stress.go:735 (edge label '🚀📊💡')
These decks now violate the no-emoji policy enforced by cmd/json2pptx/no_emoji.go, so json2pptx generate fails on every deck testrand produces. Fix: replace hardcoded emoji with bundled icon names (panel_layout supports svg icons) or plain text labels, and drop emoji entries from edge-case corpora.
acceptance_criteria: rg --pcre2 '\p{Emoji_Presentation}' internal/testrand returns no matches in production code (tests may keep emoji to assert detection). bin/testrand visual produces decks that pass json2pptx generate without no_emoji violations on every template.
close_reason: Replaced hardcoded emoji in internal/testrand production code: panel_layout demo icons (📊👥🎯📈) → bundled icon names (chart-bar/users/target/trending-up); edge unicode bullet, edge-case corpus, and svg-stress edge label → non-emoji symbol/currency strings. Verified rg \p{Emoji_Presentation} matches only the test file, and testrand visual decks pass json2pptx generate with no no_emoji violations on all 4 templates.

title: extractFontSizeFromShape ignores RunProperties.FontSize attribute, underestimating title font size
description: New root cause contributing to title overflow / overlap severity. internal/generator/slides.go:610 declares runPropertiesXML.FontSize as an explicit XML attribute (sz). But internal/generator/text_helpers.go:177-204 (extractFontSizeFromShape) only inspects RunProperties.Inner via parseSzAttr — it never reads the parsed FontSize attribute. Consequence: when the template stores sz as an attribute on rPr (the common case), extractFontSizeFromShape returns 0, callers in internal/generator/text_population.go:192-199 and internal/generator/text_autofit.go:208-245 fall back to defaults (~20pt), wrap/truncation/autofit decisions are made against a font far smaller than the rendered title, and overflow is not detected. Fix: check run.RunProperties.FontSize before parsing Inner; preserve run-level FontSize when cloning template run properties.
acceptance_criteria: extractFontSizeFromShape returns the real font size for templates that store sz as an rPr attribute. Unit test with both attribute-form and inner-form sz returns identical results. Title wrap/autofit decisions reflect actual rendered size.
notes: Agent-native review: acceptance must include preservation as well as extraction. cloneRunProperties and createFormattedRuns must retain RunProperties.FontSize, and XML round-trip tests should assert populated title/subtitle runs keep rPr sz when the template stored font size as an attribute.
close_reason: Implemented: extractFontSizeFromShape now reads the parsed RunProperties.FontSize (sz) attribute before scanning inner XML, so templates that store sz as an rPr attribute report the real title font size for wrap/autofit/truncation. cloneRunProperties and createFormattedRuns now preserve run-level FontSize, and the guards in extractTemplateTextStyle/extractBulletTemplateStyles no longer drop attr-only runs. Added unit tests for attr-form extraction, attr/inner equivalence, and round-trip preservation through setTextParagraph.

title: resolveVirtualLayout priority-3 branch returns Bounds without ContentZone, so ClampBoundsToZone is skipped
description: Root cause contributing to grid/title overlap on templates that fall to the body/content fallback. cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go:84-100 (priority-3 branch) returns a virtualLayoutResult with only Bounds populated and Zone unset. cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go:209-223 only clamps explicit input.Bounds against the ContentZone when zone != nil, and DefaultBoundsFromZone is also bypassed. So on templates without blank/blank-title layouts, shape_grid resolution falls back to DefaultBounds(slideWidth, slideHeight) — generic full-slide defaults — with no title/footer protection. Fix: always populate ContentZone in the body/content fallback (derive TitleBottom/FooterTop/HMargin from the layout's title and footer placeholders), OR call BoundsFromTitleAndFooter consistently.
acceptance_criteria: resolveVirtualLayout always returns a non-nil Zone whenever it returns a result; clamp paths apply on every shape_grid slide. Unit test for a body/content-only layout shows ContentZone populated.
close_reason: Implemented: priority-3 (body/content fallback) branch of resolveVirtualLayout now always populates a ContentZone derived from the layout's title/footer placeholders (TitleBottom from title or content top, FooterTop from first utility placeholder or min bottom margin, horizontal extent from the content placeholder). Guarantees a non-nil Zone whenever a result is returned, so ClampBoundsToZone/DefaultBoundsFromZone chrome protection runs on every shape_grid slide instead of falling back to generic full-slide DefaultBounds. Added 3 regression tests (title+footer-derived zone, body-only fallback, explicit-footer).

title: resolveVirtualLayout ignores slide's explicit layout_id when computing shape_grid ContentZone
description: Root cause for go-slide-creator-3a29 slide 7 (grid covers title) and contributor to go-slide-creator-40to. cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go:940-955 always calls resolveVirtualLayout(layouts, ...) for any slide containing a shape_grid, with NO knowledge of slide.LayoutID. resolveVirtualLayout (cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go:50-103) then prefers (1) blank-with-title, (2) blank-title, (3) any body/content layout — so a slide with an explicit content layout can still get its title/footer bounds derived from an unrelated blank layout. Title height, footer top and side margins end up wrong, and shape_grid bounds intrude into title chrome. Fix: when slide.LayoutID is set, derive ContentZone from THAT layout's placeholders first; use virtual fallback only when no concrete layout is set.
acceptance_criteria: A shape_grid slide with an explicit layout_id derives its ContentZone (title bottom, footer top, side margins) from that layout. Unit test covers a slide whose layout is not the blank/blank-title pick. modern-yellow slide 7 grid no longer crosses the title baseline.
close_reason: Implemented: shape_grid ContentZone now derived from the slide's concrete (explicit/auto-selected) layout via new contentZoneFromLayout/findLayoutByID/titleOnlyContentZone helpers; virtual blank/blank-title resolution is used only for blank/virtual slides or as fallback when the concrete layout lacks title/body/footer geometry. Added unit tests.

title: Title-slide path bypasses truncation/autofit/font-cap, root-causing title+subtitle overlap
description: Root cause for go-slide-creator-3a29 slide 0 (modern-yellow title/subtitle overlap). On title slides both the title placeholder AND the subtitle are routed to generator.ContentTitleSlideTitle via isLikelySubtitle(): cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go:1131-1133 (typed path) and :1582-1584 (raw JSON path). That handler is internal/generator/text_population.go setTitleSlideTitle() (~line 238-282), which explicitly skips font capping, max-line truncation, replaceSpAutoFitWithNorm, and smart autofit so the template ctrTitle styling is preserved. Subtitles therefore inherit a giant 40-60pt font with no fit protection and overlap the title. Fix direction: only route the actual ctrTitle through ContentTitleSlideTitle; route the subtitle through normal text handling, OR apply at least wrap-aware truncation + autofit fallback inside setTitleSlideTitle for subtitle role.
acceptance_criteria: Title-slide subtitles no longer use ContentTitleSlideTitle, OR setTitleSlideTitle gains truncation+autofit for non-ctrTitle placeholders. Visual QA for modern-yellow slide 0 shows title and subtitle in distinct non-overlapping bands.
notes: Agent-native review: subtitle routing must land with rPr sz preservation from go-slide-creator-waic; otherwise textfit can measure one font size and render another. Add regression coverage for title-slide title and subtitle occupying distinct non-overlapping bands while preserving template run size attributes.
close_reason: Implemented: setTitleSlideTitle now applies non-destructive normAutofit overflow protection to both the title/ctrTitle and subtitle roles, plus wrap-aware truncation (maxSubtitleLines=3) for the short non-title subtitle band. Title-slide titles/subtitles no longer overflow their bands and overlap each other; large template fonts and centered alignment are preserved (normAutofit stays 100% when content fits, scales down only on overflow). Run-level sz preserved so the autofit pass measures the rendered size (waic). Added TestSetTitleSlideTitle_OverflowProtection regression coverage.

title: modern-yellow template has severe title and content overlap in visual QA deck
description: The all-template visual QA driver renders modern-yellow mechanically, but the output is visually unusable on multiple slides. Evidence: output/visual-qa/modern-yellow/generated-slide-0.jpg has the title and subtitle overlapping; output/visual-qa/modern-yellow/generated-slide-7.jpg has the enormous title hidden behind shape_grid cards; the contact sheet at output/visual-qa/modern-yellow/contact-sheet.jpg shows the same issue across other slides. Template-check passes, so this is a visual/layout defect not caught by conformance.

notes: Agent-native review: treat this as final visual verification for modern-yellow, not a separate implementation root. Implementation should come through subtitle/textfit, explicit-layout ContentZone, body fallback ContentZone, shape_grid z-order, compact section-divider metadata, and template tagging fixes; this bead closes when the visual QA deck renders cleanly after those blockers land.

title: testrand visual deck violates no-emoji policy and blocks all-template freestyle runner

title: Epic: extensive template testing matrix
description:
Today's automated template coverage is shallow: template-check (structural) + a handful of cross-template tests (shape_grid, table_style_resolver, pattern_resolve, style_extractor, corpus_headless). There is no comprehensive matrix that confirms every template renders every pattern and survives real-world content stress.

This epic groups the atomic test-coverage tickets that together produce a per-template green/red dashboard before any template (programmatic or designer) ships.

title: [security] MCP render_slide_image/render_deck_thumbnails/read_presentation lack pptx_path traversal validation
description: Three MCP tools accept pptx_path directly from LLM agents with zero path traversal checks: render_slide_image (mcp.go:1889), render_deck_thumbnails (mcp.go:1940), read_presentation (mcp_read.go:32). All call os.Stat(pptxPath) unchecked. The HTTP download handler uses ^[0-9a-f]{32}\.pptx$ regex — MCP has no equivalent. Add ValidateFilePath() shared helper and apply before os.Stat in all three handlers.

title: [security] Pattern POST handlers missing Content-Type and body size validation

title: Add MCP/CLI output-validation policy surfaces for corrupt-PPTX prevention
description:
Why:
Once a unified output-validation suite exists, the product still needs an agent-facing way to use it consistently. Today generation usually succeeds even when output validation would have warned, and there is no MCP tool dedicated to validating an already-generated presentation package.

Current facts confirmed in code:
- `generate_presentation` already has a strong structured-diagnostics boundary for input-side failures
- generation-time OOXML validation is currently warning-only and optional
- `json2pptx validate-output` exists for files, but there is no equivalent MCP-first output-validation surface

Scope:
- add an MCP tool such as `validate_presentation_output` (or the accepted equivalent name) for validating a generated PPTX/package through the unified suite
- add staged generation policy controls such as `output_validation=off|warn|strict` for MCP/CLI generation surfaces
- in strict mode, fail generation with the normal diagnostics envelope instead of returning success for a corrupt package

Non-goals:
- do not make strict blocking the default in this issue
- do not redefine the validation rules themselves here; this issue consumes the suite and provenance work

References:
- `cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go`
- `cmd/json2pptx/validate_output.go`
- `internal/api/mcp_result.go`
- `internal/diagnostics/diagnostic.go`
acceptance_criteria:
- an MCP-facing output-validation tool exists over the unified suite
- generation surfaces support staged output-validation policy values such as off, warn, and strict
- strict mode returns the standard diagnostics envelope rather than a success payload for corrupt output
- rollout remains additive: warn/off continue to support non-blocking adoption until the validator precision is proven
close_reason: Implemented: validate_presentation_output MCP tool, output_validation policy (off/warn/strict) for MCP generate_presentation and CLI generate, schema version bumped to 4.6.0

title: Add source provenance to output-validation findings for agent repair
description:
Why:
Output-validation findings are only useful to agents if they can be traced back to a source-side repair boundary when that mapping is deterministic. Without provenance, the agent only learns that a PPTX part is broken, not whether it should call `repair_slide`, fix a template, or report a generator bug.

Current facts confirmed in code:
- `repair_slide` already operates on source JSON and slide indices
- `slidepath` already provides stable JSON-path conventions for source-side targeting
- the proposed output-validation suite can identify PPTX parts and slide XML files, but that alone is not enough for agent repair

Scope:
- define provenance fields for output-validation findings, including PPTX part, slide index, source path when deterministic, repair scope, validator phase, and blocking flag
- map findings back to source JSON and existing repair semantics when the engine can do so reliably
- explicitly classify unmappable findings as template- or generator-scoped instead of fabricating source paths

Non-goals:
- do not add new validation rules here
- do not turn every output-validation finding into an auto-fix

References:
- `cmd/json2pptx/mcp_repair.go`
- `internal/slidepath/slidepath.go`
- `internal/diagnostics/diagnostic.go`
- `internal/pptx/validator.go`
- `internal/pptx/ooxml_validate.go`
acceptance_criteria:
- output-validation findings include structured provenance fields for phase, validator, PPTX part, and repair scope
- findings with deterministic source mapping include slide index and source path suitable for agent follow-up
- unmappable findings are explicitly classified as template- or generator-scoped
- tests cover one source-mappable OOXML finding and one package-level unmappable finding
close_reason: Added structured provenance fields (phase, validator, slide_index, source_path, scope) to output-validation Finding struct with deterministic source mapping for slide-level findings and generator/template classification for unmappable ones

title: Unify structural and OOXML PPTX validation into one output-validation suite
description:
Why:
Corrupt-PPTX prevention is currently fragmented across two different validators and two different command surfaces. Structural/package checks live in `internal/pptx.Validator` and `cmd/validatepptx`, while slide-content OOXML checks live in `internal/pptx.OOXMLValidator` and `json2pptx validate-output`. The generator path only uses the OOXML checks as optional warning strings.

Current facts confirmed in code:
- `internal/pptx/validator.go` checks required parts, dangling relationships, and malformed package XML
- `internal/pptx/ooxml_validate.go` checks invalid colors, duplicate shape IDs, invalid table grid cardinality, and zero extents
- `cmd/validatepptx/main.go` and `cmd/json2pptx/validate_output.go` expose different subsets of that functionality today

Scope:
- build one shared output-validation suite/report builder that can run structural and OOXML validators together
- classify rules as blocking vs warning with stable code families such as `OPC_*` and `OOXML_*`
- make both CLI validation entry points consume the same underlying engine and report shape

Non-goals:
- do not introduce generation-time blocking policy in this issue
- do not expand the validator corpus beyond the existing and immediately adjacent corruption rules unless needed to unify the suite

References:
- `internal/pptx/validator.go`
- `internal/pptx/ooxml_validate.go`
- `cmd/validatepptx/main.go`
- `cmd/json2pptx/validate_output.go`
acceptance_criteria:
- one shared output-validation engine/report exists for structural and OOXML checks
- rules are classified as blocking or warning with stable machine-readable code families
- `validatepptx` and `json2pptx validate-output` use the same underlying engine/report shape
- tests cover representative structural and OOXML failures through the shared suite
close_reason: Implemented unified OutputValidator with Finding/Report types, OPC_/OOXML_ code families, blocking/warning severity. Both CLI entry points now use the same engine.

title: Emit structured findings for diagram, icon, and image shape_grid cells
description:
Why:
The exact hybrid path we want agents to use is under-diagnosed at render time. Structural fit checks and visual findings already work well for text/table-heavy paths, but diagram/icon/image grid cells do not yet get equivalent structured findings when the engine actually renders them. That leaves agents blind when a grid-embedded visual is illegible or poorly placed.

Current facts confirmed in code:
- `fit_findings_collect.go` primarily reasons about shape/table cells and uses coarse defaults for diagram cells
- `cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go` already emits narrow-cell warnings for grid diagrams, but they are warning strings rather than first-class structured findings
- grid-cell diagram rendering is real and theme-aware, so the lack of findings is a contract gap rather than a missing feature gap

Scope:
- emit structured generation/render-time findings for `shape_grid` diagram, icon, and image cells where the engine can detect real issues
- include stable JSON path targeting for grid-cell content

title: Harmonize structured visual diagnostics across svggen and json2pptx
description:
Why:
Visual validation and render failures are expressed through multiple incompatible envelopes today. `json2pptx` already uses `diagnostics.Diagnostic` and `patterns.ValidationError/FitFinding`, while `svggen-mcp` translates svggen validation into its own `finding` shape. That fragmentation makes it harder for agents to recover consistently across placeholder diagrams, native-shape diagrams, and SVG/grid flows.

Current facts confirmed in code:
- `internal/diagnostics/diagnostic.go` defines the transport-neutral `Diagnostic` envelope used by MCP surfaces in `json2pptx`
- `internal/patterns/fit_finding.go` already supports `Fix` and `NextToolCall`
- `svggen/cmd/svggen-mcp/main.go` converts svggen validation errors into a separate local finding structure
- `svggen/core/validation.go` and `internal/patterns/errors.go` use different code/path conventions today

Scope:
- define one harmonized visual-diagnostics contract across svggen and json2pptx surfaces
- standardize top-level fields and semantics for code, path, severity, fix, next tool call, and details/context
- document or encode the mapping from svggen validation errors into the agent-facing contract used by json2pptx

Non-goals:
- do not promise repair coverage for every finding in this issue
- do not expand output-validation policy here; this is about the visual authoring contract

References:
- `internal/diagnostics/diagnostic.go`
- `internal/patterns/fit_finding.go`
- `internal/patterns/errors.go`
- `svggen/core/validation.go`
- `svggen/cmd/svggen-mcp/main.go`
acceptance_criteria:
- svggen-originated validation failures and json2pptx-originated visual failures can be surfaced through one documented machine-readable contract
- path, severity, fix, and next-tool-call semantics are consistent across placeholder, grid, native-shape, and SVG validation paths
- tests lock at least one svggen validation error and one json2pptx visual finding to the shared contract
- no new surface requires prose parsing to determine the next agent action

title: Expose placement-aware visual capability metadata for diagrams and grid cells
description:
Why:
Agents currently cannot discover the real authoring/render surface from one canonical source. `svggen/capabilities.go` exposes type-level limits, but the actual render-path truth leaks from `internal/generator/media.go` and grid-cell SVG support leaks from `cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go`. This makes the public contract incomplete and encourages brittle inference.

Current facts confirmed in code:
- `svggen/capabilities.go` publishes limits and status, but not placement/render-path truth
- `internal/generator/media.go` intercepts several placeholder-based diagram types into native OOXML grouped shapes before SVG rendering
- `cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go` renders grid-cell diagrams through the SVG/native-SVG insert path
- the same diagram family can therefore have different render paths depending on placement

Scope:
- add a canonical static visual-capability registry or extend the existing diagram capability registry so it can describe placement-aware render truth
- include additive machine-readable fields such as supported placements, placement-specific render pipeline, grid-cell support, authoring surface, and fallback behavior
- make `get_diagram_capabilities` and other agent-facing capability surfaces read from that single source of truth

Non-goals:
- do not mix runtime environment state into this issue; that belongs with `go-slide-creator-1etj.2`
- do not change `recommend_visual` output in this issue
- do not do docs-only cleanup here; existing children already cover that

References:
- `svggen/capabilities.go`
- `internal/generator/media.go`
- `cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go`
- `cmd/json2pptx/mcp_capabilities.go`
acceptance_criteria:
- a single canonical static capability source exists for diagram/grid render truth
- capability data is placement-aware and does not collapse behavior into a single flat native/svg field
- `get_diagram_capabilities` exposes additive fields for supported placement and render pipeline without breaking existing fields
- tests cover at least one native-intercept placeholder diagram, one SVG-first diagram, and one diagram embeddable in `shape_grid`

DiagramCapability now exposes placements, grid_cell_support, and authoring_surface fields. get_diagram_capabilities MCP tool enriches capabilities from the single source of truth. Full test coverage for native-intercept, SVG-only, and grid-cell scenarios.

title: Adopt placement-aware visual capability contract and staged output-validation gate
description:
Why:
The current agent-facing visual contract is split across `svggen/capabilities.go`, `internal/generator/media.go`, `cmd/json2pptx/skill_info.go`, `cmd/json2pptx/mcp_capabilities.go`, `internal/patterns/recommend_visual.go`, and multiple skills/docs. That creates two classes of risk:
- agents learn incomplete or incorrect rules about when to use placeholder diagrams, native-shape diagrams, raw `shape_grid`, or SVG-in-grid composition
- corrupt-PPTX prevention is treated as an afterthought because structural validation, OOXML validation, and agent-facing repair hints are not composed into one staged boundary

Decision:
Adopt a placement-aware visual capability contract and a staged output-validation architecture.

The agreed design boundaries are:
- static visual capability truth is separate from runtime environment state; do not fold this into the existing runtime-capabilities issue
- render truth is placement-aware, not a single flat `render_mode`; the same diagram family can be native OOXML in placeholder flow and SVG/native-SVG in grid-cell flow
- discovery/doc drift remains handled by the existing `go-slide-creator-1etj.4` and `go-slide-creator-1etj.7` children rather than creating a second overlapping docs umbrella
- findings come before repair: first harmonize diagnostics and emit structured findings for grid/native/SVG paths, then add deterministic repair mappings where justified
- output validation is staged: first unify structural and OOXML validation and classify blocking vs warning rules, then add MCP/CLI policy surfaces and only later make strict blocking the default if the validator corpus proves precise enough

Recommended sequencing:
1. placement-aware capability metadata
2. existing discovery/docs children consume that truth
3. `recommend_visual` consumes capability truth additively
4. diagnostics contract harmonization across svggen/json2pptx
5. render-time findings parity for diagram/icon/image grid cells
6. deterministic agent-action mapping for non-text grid findings
7. unified PPTX structural+OOXML output-validation suite
8. source provenance for output-validation findings
9. MCP/CLI validation-policy surfaces (`validate_presentation_output`, `output_validation=off|warn|strict`)

What should not be combined:
- static capability metadata with runtime capability exposure
- `recommend_visual` contract changes with docs-only cleanup
- findings parity with repair automation
- validation-suite consolidation with blocking-policy rollout
- stylish-panels feature work with general capability hardening beyond consuming the shared capability truth
acceptance_criteria:
- the decision records that render truth is placement-aware rather than a single flat native/svg field
- the decision records that docs/discovery work should stay in existing child beads `go-slide-creator-1etj.4` and `go-slide-creator-1etj.7`
- the decision records that output validation rolls out in stages: suite first, policy second
- the decision records that findings and repair are separate implementation tracks
close_reason: Decision recorded; implementation sequencing moved into child issue boundaries and dependencies

title: Advertise the full grid visual surface to agents, including diagram cells
description:
Why:
The product surface supports more grid/visual combinations than the machine-readable discovery surfaces admit. One concrete example: `shape_grid` already supports diagram cells, but `skill-info supported_types.grid_cell_types` omits `diagram`, which teaches agents an incomplete capability map.

Confirmed gaps:
- `cmd/json2pptx/skill_info.go buildSupportedTypes` currently lists grid cell types as `shape`, `table`, `icon`, `image` even though `jsonschema.GridCellInput` and `shape_grid` resolution also support `diagram`
- the server does not yet expose one complete machine-readable grid visual vocabulary that an agent can trust without reading source
- this incompleteness pushes agents toward shell archaeology and brittle guesswork instead of capability discovery

Scope:
- expose `diagram` as a supported grid cell type anywhere machine-readable grid capability metadata are returned
- ensure the relevant discovery surfaces (`skill-info`, `list_templates`, `get_capabilities`, or the post-consolidation equivalent) advertise the grid cell vocabulary consistently
- add or update tests that lock the advertised grid cell vocabulary
- if `go-slide-creator-1etj.9` lands first, consume that shared capability truth instead of inventing a second list here

Non-goals:
- do not do the docs/skills decision ladder here; that belongs to `go-slide-creator-1etj.4`
- do not redesign the capability model here; that belongs to `go-slide-creator-1etj.9`

Agent-native rationale:
This is a capability-discovery issue, not just a docs issue. The server should advertise every meaningful grid visual primitive that an agent can choose among when composing a slide.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- `supported_types.grid_cell_types` includes `diagram` where appropriate
- machine-readable discovery surfaces expose a consistent grid cell vocabulary
- tests cover the advertised grid cell vocabulary
- agents no longer have to infer diagram-in-grid support by reading source code
acceptance_criteria:

- tests cover the advertised grid cell vocabulary

title: Align skill/docs/MCP prose with the live agent contract
description:
Why:
The agent-facing prose surfaces have drifted apart. The skill, template guide, input-format docs, and some MCP descriptions still mix legacy and canonical guidance in ways that cause avoidable agent mistakes. This is not just documentation polish; it is a contract bug because agents are being taught contradictory authoring rules.

Specific drift confirmed during investigation:
- `skills/template-deck/TEMPLATE_GUIDE.md` still teaches legacy value examples in canonical-layout sections
- `docs/INPUT_FORMAT.md` still opens with `slideLayoutN` examples even though canonical layout IDs are the preferred authoring surface
- `cmd/json2pptx/mcp_input_schema.go` prose says `field_scope` while the emitted schema actually uses `x-field-scope`
- `skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md` currently treats `features.template_settings` as the write gate, but the real runtime gate lives in `JSON2PPTX_ALLOW_SETTINGS_WRITE` and should be checked via runtime capability state
- the docs under-explain the semantic difference between `blank` (title-only, shape-grid-oriented) and `content` (body-capable)
- `recommend_pattern` is over-emphasized where `recommend_visual` should be the first decision aid when the agent is unsure whether it needs a placeholder layout, named pattern, diagram, compose envelope, or raw `shape_grid`

Scope:
- this is the single docs/prose sink for the epic: update `skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md`, `skills/template-deck/TEMPLATE_GUIDE.md`, `docs/INPUT_FORMAT.md`, and the relevant MCP tool descriptions/examples after the underlying machine-readable surfaces settle
- standardize on typed content fields in examples, `x-field-scope` wording, canonical layout IDs, runtime capability checks, and the post-consolidation visual decision ladder
- if stylish-panels lands through its implementation/pattern beads, document it here as a reusable option rather than an undocumented one-off

Non-goals:
- do not change machine-readable JSON contracts in this issue except for minimal description strings needed to keep prose truthful
- do not duplicate metadata/discovery work owned by `go-slide-creator-1etj.7`

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- the major agent-facing docs all agree on typed content fields, `x-field-scope` wording, canonical layout IDs, and runtime capability gating
- examples no longer push agents toward raw `slideLayoutN` IDs or display-name guessing
- the `blank` vs `content` distinction is explicit
- the docs tell agents when to start with `recommend_visual` instead of jumping straight to `recommend_pattern`
- stylish-panels is mentioned here only if its implementation/pattern surfaces have actually landed
acceptance_criteria:
- the major agent-facing docs all agree on typed content fields, x-field-scope wording, canonical layout IDs, and runtime capability gating
- examples no longer push agents toward raw slideLayoutN IDs or display-name guessing

title: Make template discovery stable for agents: canonical aliases and quiet skill-info
description:
Why:
The current discovery surface still nudges agents toward unstable template-instance details. skill-info/list_templates surface raw slideLayoutN IDs and synthesized layout IDs without an explicit stable alias map, so agents try to memorize or infer raw IDs such as slideLayout5 or display names such as One Content. Separately, skill-info can emit synthesis/info logs to stderr during template analysis, which breaks naive machine parsing when callers merge stderr into stdout.

Observed problems:
- cmd/json2pptx/skill_info.go exposes layout_summaries with raw IDs but no canonical_layout_ids map
- synthesized layouts such as Blank + Title can appear as raw slideLayoutN handles even though agents should author against canonical IDs
- agents inspecting pwc-template had to reverse-engineer which raw layout corresponded to body-capable content
- machine-oriented CLI discovery commands should prefer JSON-only stdout and suppress non-essential info logging

Scope:
- Add an explicit canonical-to-concrete layout map per template in skill-info/list_templates output
- Keep raw layout summaries for human debugging, but clearly support authoring against canonical aliases first
- Suppress non-essential info logging for skill-info so normal stdout remains machine-readable JSON
- Update any related tests and compact/full-mode examples

Suggested output shape:
- canonical_layout_ids: {title: ..., content: ..., blank: ..., section: ..., closing: ...} for any aliases the template can satisfy
- optional notes in docs clarifying that raw slideLayoutN IDs are template-instance details, not the preferred authoring contract
acceptance_criteria:
- skill-info/list_templates include an explicit canonical layout alias map per template
- agents can discover the correct concrete layout for title/content/blank/etc. without reverse-engineering raw IDs
- skill-info stdout is clean JSON during normal machine-readable use
- tests cover the new discovery field and the quiet output behavior where practical
close_reason: Added canonical_layout_ids map to skill-info/list_templates output per template, suppressed slog info/warn during skill-info for clean machine-readable stdout, added ResolveAllCanonicalLayouts function with tests, updated SKILL.md

title: Expose runtime capability state in get_capabilities
description:
Why:
Agents currently have to learn several environment-dependent constraints by failing first. get_capabilities advertises static support flags such as features.template_settings=true, but it does not say whether settings writes are enabled in this server process, whether render dependencies are actually installed, or what runtime directories are active. This is a direct agent-native gap: the server exposes what it can do in theory, not what it can do right now.

Current gaps confirmed in code:
- cmd/json2pptx/mcp_settings.go gates template-setting writes on JSON2PPTX_ALLOW_SETTINGS_WRITE=1
- cmd/json2pptx/mcp_capabilities.go currently exposes only static features, so an agent cannot distinguish supported from enabled
- internal/render/render.go has CheckDependencies(), but render_slide_image/render_deck_thumbnails availability is not surfaced in capabilities
- the live templates_dir/output_dir used by the MCP server are not returned to callers

Scope:
- Extend get_capabilities with runtime state alongside the existing static features section
- Include at minimum: settings_write_enabled, render dependency availability with missing commands, active templates_dir, active output_dir, and a schema fingerprint/digest that can change without a semver bump
- Keep the static feature flags; runtime should complement them rather than replacing them
- Update the CLI capabilities subcommand and output schema to stay in sync

Architecture rationale from investigation:
This is the smallest high-value context-injection improvement because it lets agents decide whether they can write template settings, call render tools, or trust cached schema assumptions without probing by error.
acceptance_criteria:
- get_capabilities returns a machine-readable runtime section with settings_write_enabled, render dependency availability, templates_dir, output_dir, and schema fingerprint/digest
- outputSchemaGetCapabilities and the CLI capabilities command are updated to match
- tests cover both static support flags and runtime gating behavior
- skill/docs can point agents to runtime capability checks instead of failure-first probing
close_reason: Implemented: added runtime section to get_capabilities with settings_write_enabled, render dependency status, templates_dir, output_dir, and schema_fingerprint

title: Normalize canonical layout_id handling across validate, preview, and generate
description:
Why:
Explicit canonical layout IDs such as title, content, section, blank, and closing are not handled consistently across the agent-facing entrypoints. CLI JSON generation normalizes explicit layout IDs after template analysis, but dry-run and validation check raw values against concrete template IDs, and preview/generate MCP paths do not all share the same normalization path. Agents can therefore get different answers from preview, validate, and generate for the same deck.

Concrete failure mode:
- On pwc-template, blank resolves to a synthesized Blank + Title layout that only has a title placeholder
- Agents needing a body-capable layout for an image or chart try to infer a raw slideLayoutN or display-name mapping instead of using a stable canonical alias
- Preview, validation, and generation do not consistently agree on whether a canonical inline layout_id should be accepted and what concrete layout it resolves to

Scope:
- Add one shared layout-ID normalization helper for explicit slide.layout_id values
- Reuse it in CLI generate JSON mode, CLI dry-run/validate, MCP validate_input, preview_presentation_plan, and generate_presentation
- Preserve passthrough behavior for already-concrete slideLayoutN IDs and generated layout IDs
- Keep validation errors anchored to /slides/N/layout_id with useful did_you_mean suggestions when nothing resolves

Implementation hints:
- internal/layout/canonical.go already contains the canonical resolution rules
- dry_run.go validateSlidesAgainstTemplate currently validates raw slideInput.LayoutID against analysis.Layouts
- mcp_preview.go resolveSlideLayout currently copies explicit inline layout IDs through without canonical normalization
- mcp.go handleGenerate/handleValidate should share the same helper rather than each path inventing resolution logic
acceptance_criteria:
- canonical layout IDs resolve the same way in CLI generate, CLI dry-run, CLI validate, MCP validate_input, preview_presentation_plan, and generate_presentation
- preview output reports the concrete resolved layout when the input used a canonical alias
- regression tests cover at least title, content, and blank against template-tagged layouts
- agents no longer need to guess display names such as One Content or raw synthesized slideLayoutN IDs
close_reason: Added shared resolveCanonicalLayoutIDs helper and called it from all 4 entry points: CLI generate, CLI dry-run, MCP validate_input, and MCP preview_presentation_plan. Added regression tests.

title: Add JSON CLI partial-flag compatibility for generate and validate
description:
Why:
External agent callers already pass -partial to json2pptx generate and validate. The commands currently reject it as an unknown flag, which breaks Office Companion and other headless agent workflows before generation or validation even begins.

Reproduction:
- Office Companion invokes json2pptx generate with -partial in crates/oc-core/src/tools/pptx/json_integration.rs line 103
- Office Companion invokes json2pptx validate with -partial in the same file around line 217
- cmd/json2pptx/generate.go and cmd/json2pptx/validate.go do not define -partial today
- Because the commands use flag.ContinueOnError, the failure happens at argv parsing time instead of producing a structured headless result

Scope:
- Add CLI-level -partial support to generate and validate
- Wire real partial behavior where feasible; if generate cannot fully recover every slide path immediately, at minimum preserve compatibility without unknown-flag failure and document the exact behavior
- Ensure headless/json-output mode still yields machine-consumable output when partial mode is used
- Add regression tests covering the CLI flag contract

Notes from investigation:
- internal/pipeline/pipeline.go already has Partial support in ConvertRequest and ConvertSlidesPartial
- the current JSON generation path bypasses that pipeline, so this issue must explicitly decide whether to bridge into the shared pipeline or implement equivalent per-slide tolerance in the JSON mode path
acceptance_criteria:
- json2pptx generate -partial no longer fails with unknown flag
- json2pptx validate -partial no longer fails with unknown flag
- documented behavior explains what partial means for each command
- automated tests cover the accepted flag on both commands and the chosen behavior in headless mode
close_reason: Added -partial flag to generate and validate commands. Generate skips failing slides instead of aborting; validate accepts the flag for CLI compatibility.

title: Harden agent-facing json2pptx contract and discovery surface
description:
Why: Agents using the json2pptx MCP/CLI surface are still failing on avoidable contract and discovery gaps. Current pain points include the missing CLI partial flag contract, drift between schema/capabilities/skill docs, weak runtime capability disclosure, layout-selection ambiguity in skill-info/template guidance, and missing first-class stylish-panels guidance/pattern support.

What needs to happen:
- expose and test the CLI partial contract where Office Companion expects it
- tighten live MCP discovery so runtime gates and environment-dependent capabilities are machine-readable
- remove contract drift across SKILL.md, TEMPLATE_GUIDE.md, MCP tool descriptions, and input schema guidance
- improve template/layout guidance so agents choose body-capable layouts correctly
- add stylish-panels support as an agent-discoverable visual option and strengthen pattern/grid guidance so agents use the full surface intentionally

Acceptance:
- MCP/CLI/skill contract is internally consistent for the touched surfaces
- agent-facing discovery exposes runtime constraints instead of requiring failure-first learning
- deck skill and template guide steer agents toward the correct tool and layout choices
- stylish-panels is represented in the product surface with tests/docs

2026-05-07 triage split this umbrella into atomic child beads. This parent should track the overall agent-UX hardening effort only; implementation work should happen on the child issues.

title: Make the HTTP API explicit about its current legacy boundary
description:
The HTTP surface currently presents itself as richer and more modern than the implementation really is. The key problem is POST /api/v1/convert: agent-facing docs and OpenAPI imply support for modern deck constructs, but the handler still deserializes the legacy APISlide or APIContent model. Rich markers such as shape_grid, pattern-driven content, and typed chart or diagram payloads are therefore misleading, ignored, or unsupported in ways an agent cannot predict safely.

Scope this task to honesty and explicitness on the HTTP surface, not full parity. The main goal is to stop the HTTP API from pretending to be a peer of the MCP surface until it actually is. Favor explicit rejection of unsupported rich-deck markers, a capabilities endpoint or equivalent machine-readable boundary, and aligned docs. Do not include template-settings normalization or rendering parity work here.

This task should also absorb the relevant P4 preview-boundary notes from TODOS.md where they intersect with HTTP surface clarity.
acceptance_criteria:
- HTTP requests that use unsupported rich-deck markers fail explicitly instead of being silently accepted or partially ignored.
- The HTTP surface exposes a machine-readable statement of what it actually supports today, such as a capabilities endpoint.
- OpenAPI and README examples for HTTP match the real request and response contract.
- MCP or CLI-only features are labeled as such until parity exists.
close_reason: Implemented HTTP API legacy boundary: DisallowUnknownFields rejects unsupported fields (shape_grid, pattern, etc.) with UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE error code; added GET /api/v1/capabilities endpoint; fixed OpenAPI spec and README to match reality

title: Bring shape_grid diagram cells to parity and expose all supported grid shapes
description:
The audit confirmed that shape_grid already supports richer cell kinds than the agent-facing docs consistently advertise. In particular, diagram cells are implemented in runtime but under-discoverable across MCP help, docs, and examples. The agent-facing behavior also drifts from placeholder diagrams: grid-cell diagrams do not receive theme colors, narrow-placeholder style warnings skip grid cells, and fit_report coverage for grid diagrams is incomplete or absent.

That includes diagram cells, truthful documentation, examples, and fit diagnostics. This task should absorb the relevant P1 and P3 items from TODOS.md.

title: Make MCP and CLI discovery contracts authoritative
description:
Agent trust is currently undermined by discovery and schema drift on the canonical agent-facing surfaces. Concrete mismatches found in the audit include: mcpToolCatalog omits plan_deck and recommend_visual even though they are registered; get_capabilities advertises stale or incomplete output fields such as features.fit_report and omits vocabularies and error_codes; list_patterns schema says flat array while runtime returns grouped categories; and CLI discovery/search affordances do not cleanly mirror the MCP shape and pattern catalog surface.

title: Harmonize agent-facing surfaces across MCP, CLI, and HTTP
description:
Agent-facing behavior has drifted across the MCP server, CLI commands, and HTTP API. The main failure mode is unpredictability: discovery metadata is not always truthful, some surfaces advertise features they do not actually execute, and shape_grid or template-settings behaviors differ by entry point.

This epic tracks a bounded harmonization pass optimized for agent trust. The immediate direction is to make MCP and CLI the canonical truthful surface, make HTTP explicit about its current legacy boundary, and normalize shared runtime semantics so the same input yields the same behavior regardless of entry point.

Related existing work that should not be duplicated: go-slide-creator-6f1d, go-slide-creator-g12p, go-slide-creator-lbwj, go-slide-creator-287a.

title: Add get_input_schema MCP tool returning authoritative PresentationInput JSON Schema
description:
Agents currently have no way to introspect the full JSON Schema for PresentationInput. Field scopes (deck/slide/text/shape) are source-grep-only: design_mode is deck-level (cmd/json2pptx/json_schema.go:38), contrast_check is slide-level (:219), inset_top/left/right/bottom is text-level, geometry is shape-level. An agent that has called get_capabilities, list_templates, and list_patterns still cannot answer 'where do I put design_mode' without grepping Go source or reading docs (which drift).

title: Emit sparse_layout warning during expand_pattern when density < threshold
description:
The expand_pattern MCP tool always returns grid occupancy (filled_pct, bounds_pct) but NEVER emits warnings when average cell density is below a pattern-specific threshold. An agent calling expand_pattern for process-flow with 3 short steps receives a healthy-looking grid with no warnings, only to discover comically tall blocks after generation. Pre-generation density awareness would let the agent adjust bounds or swap to a compact variant before generating.

SCOPE:
1. Add SparseThresholdPct int field to PatternTaxonomy (internal/patterns/pattern.go:67-85) with default 20
2. Compute average cell DensityPct from cell_budgets in expand_pattern handler (cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:1500-1510)
3. Compare against pat.Taxonomy().SparseThresholdPct
4. Emit capacity_warning when below threshold with:
   - message explaining sparse layout risk
   - suggested bounds_override or max_height_pct
   - NextToolCall for re-expanding with recommended params
5. Special-case single-row patterns (process-flow, kpi-Nup) with threshold 15% since their vertical sprawl is worse

ROOT CAUSE: session-history.md:75-82 — process-flow expanded to full_content_area with 3% text density and no pre-flight warning. Agent discovered this only after generation.

ACCEPTANCE:
- expand_pattern for process-flow with 3 short steps emits capacity_warning
- Warning includes suggested max_height_pct (e.g. 35%)
- Warning includes NextToolCall for re-expansion with suggested params
- No false positives for patterns with normal-density content
acceptance_criteria:
1. expand_pattern emits sparse warnings for low-density patterns
2. Warnings include actionable suggestions
3. Warnings include NextToolCall

title: SKILL.md + docs/PATTERNS.md: add Cell Accent Variety section (cell_accent_mode usage and anti-patterns)
description:
## Why

cell_accent_mode is invisible to agents until SKILL.md teaches when to use it. Without skill guidance, the default uniform mode persists and the new override stays unused. docs/PATTERNS.md must describe the contract for pattern authors so new grid-shaped patterns embed the shared overrides correctly.

## What

1. skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md — add a section (after Text Capacity Awareness):

   §Y. Cell Accent Variety
   - Why visual hierarchy matters: monotone slides reduce perceived quality
   - The three modes (uniform, alternate, progressive) — when each fits
     • uniform: timelines, process flows, sequential steps (consistency aids comprehension)
     • alternate: paired comparisons, two-tier hierarchies
     • progressive: 4+ peer cells where differentiation matters (feature lists, benefit grids)
   - Interaction with accent_strategy (section-keyed shifts the base; mode walks from the base)
   - Anti-patterns expressed generically:
     • All cells same accent across many cells -> use progressive
     • Mixing alternate AND section-keyed without testing -> verify with analyze_deck_rhythm
   - Pre-emit checklist (Phase 3) gets an item: "patterns with 4+ peer cells use cell_accent_mode unless visual consistency is intentional"
   - Reference the analyze_deck_rhythm within_slide_accent_variety recommendation as the validation loop

2. docs/PATTERNS.md — add to the authoring contract:
   - Grid-shaped patterns embed the shared GridOverrides (or whatever the implemented struct is named) and call ResolveCellAccent in their cell-emission loop
   - Non-grid-shaped patterns (single-cell, axis-bound matrices, fixed-progression patterns) document why they don't expose cell_accent_mode
   - Test guidance: every grid-shaped pattern has a table-driven test exercising all three modes against multiple base accents

## Acceptance criteria

- §Y in SKILL.md with named subsections and the three-mode decision rule
- Pre-emit checklist updated
- Anti-patterns expressed without naming specific decks/templates/patterns
- docs/PATTERNS.md authoring contract section updated; references the helper function name (once chosen by implementation)
- Skill explicitly states which patterns currently support cell_accent_mode by category (grid-shaped) — does NOT enumerate specific pattern names that could go stale; instead links to the auto-derived list (skill-info / patterns show)

## Dependencies

Blocked by: cell_accent_mode bead (go-slide-creator-agv9) and analyze_rhythm extensions bead (go-slide-creator-8ych) for the recommendation reference. Should land in the same change set as agv9.

## Why

Once expand_pattern returns cell_budgets and Density.Status, agents need explicit, codified guidance on how to use them. Without a skill section, agents will ignore the new fields or interpret density bands inconsistently across decks. docs/PATTERNS.md is the authoring contract and must describe the engine's capacity model so contributors writing new patterns build them correctly.

## What

1. skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md — add a new section between "Workflow" and "Pattern Library":

   §X. Text Capacity Awareness
   - Core principle: every cell has a measurable capacity; agent content should target 60-110% of it
   - Workflow integration:
     • Phase 1 PLAN: pick patterns based on content volume (rough estimate)
     • Phase 2 VARY: call expand_pattern, read cell_budgets, adjust before render
     • Phase 3 RENDER: pre-emit checklist now includes "every cell at 60-110% density"
     • Phase 4 REPAIR: read cell_overflow / cell_underfilled findings, act on fix.kind
   - How to read cell_budgets[] from expand_pattern (field-by-field)
   - Density band semantics: underfilled (<60%, info), optimal (60-110%), overflow (>110%, warning/error)
   - Decision rules:
     • Underfilled -> add detail OR pick a smaller grid configuration
     • Overflow -> trim content OR pick a larger grid / different pattern
   - bounds_assumption field: how to interpret budgets when calling expand_pattern standalone vs in compose context
   - No specific patterns/templates/decks named — examples use synthetic 2x2/3x2 references and template-agnostic phrasing

2. docs/PATTERNS.md — add a "Cell Capacity Contract" subsection under the authoring guide:
   - Patterns must keep Expand() pure (values -> ShapeGridInput); capacity is derived externally by internal/textcapacity
   - Cells with multiple paragraphs at different sizes: budget targets the body paragraph
   - Font precedence rule (paragraph > shape > pattern override > pattern default > theme)
   - Determinism guarantee: textcapacity uses embedded metrics so budgets are stable cross-platform
   - How to test pattern-with-capacity: parameterize over grid configurations and assert density bands

## Acceptance criteria

- New §X in SKILL.md with named subsections; existing Workflow §s reference it
- Pre-emit checklist (§ Phase 3 RENDER) updated with the density check item
- Decision rules for underfilled / overflow exist as numbered steps the agent can follow
- docs/PATTERNS.md has a "Cell Capacity Contract" section (~40-80 lines)
- Zero specific decks / templates / patterns hardcoded as examples — generic configurations only
- Skill section closes by linking back to the relevant MCP tools (expand_pattern, validate_input, repair_slide)

## Dependencies

Blocked by: cell_budgets in expand_pattern bead (go-slide-creator-n0sk) so the documented response shape exists. Should land in the same change set.
close_reason: Added Text Capacity Awareness section to SKILL.md (density bands, workflow integration, decision rules, bounds_assumption, related tools) and Cell Capacity Contract section to docs/PATTERNS.md (expand purity, font precedence, determinism, testing guidance)

title: Policy: code, skill (skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md), and docs/ stay synchronized in every change
description:
## Why

skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md is the agent-facing contract for this engine; docs/ (FIT_FINDINGS.md, PATTERNS.md, STYLE_DEFAULTS.md, INPUT_FORMAT.md) is the contributor-facing contract. When code changes an agent-visible surface (response shape, finding code, override field, template metadata, severity band, recommendation message) without updating SKILL.md and the relevant docs, agents stay blind to the new capability and contributors propagate stale assumptions.

Both the skill and the docs live IN this repo. They are not external. Drift here is a project bug, not a downstream concern.

## What

Document and enforce the rule: any change that touches an agent-facing surface ships skill + docs updates in the same PR.

1. Update CLAUDE.md (root + json2pptx/CLAUDE.md) with a "Skill / Docs Sync" section under "Before Committing":
   - List the surfaces that count as agent-facing (CLI/MCP response shapes, fit-report finding codes and severities, JSON-schema overrides, template metadata, generate/validate/show/expand command outputs)
   - State that any change to those surfaces requires:
     a) Update skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md in the matching section
     b) Update the relevant docs/ file (FIT_FINDINGS.md for finding codes; PATTERNS.md for pattern overrides; STYLE_DEFAULTS.md for defaults; INPUT_FORMAT.md for JSON schema)
     c) PR description must reference the skill section(s) and doc section(s) updated
   - State the rule symmetrically: changes to SKILL.md or docs/ that describe non-existent code MUST add the corresponding code in the same PR (or be reverted)

2. Add a CI check (separate bead, see linked) that fails the build when:
   - A diff touches cmd/json2pptx/*_response struct shapes, internal/pipeline finding emission, or pattern OverridesSchema
   - AND skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md and the matching docs/ file are unchanged in the same diff
   - The check is heuristic and overridable with a commit-trailer 'Skill-Sync-Exempt: <reason>' for cases where no agent-visible behavior changed

3. Add a CI / pre-commit doctor that scans SKILL.md for finding codes and verifies each appears in internal/pipeline (or fit-report) emission sites — catches stale skill text claiming codes that don't exist

## Acceptance criteria

- CLAUDE.md sync policy section landed (root and project-level)
- A separate bead exists for the CI heuristic check (file it under labels skill-sync,ci)
- A separate bead exists for the SKILL.md <-> code finding-code reconciliation doctor
- This bead's notes reference the heuristic-check and doctor beads once filed

## Out of scope

The actual content updates for the text-capacity work — those are separate paired skill/docs beads (filed alongside this one).
close_reason: Policy moved directly into json2pptx/CLAUDE.md per user instruction; tracking via the document, not as an open issue. CI heuristic check (go-slide-creator-8p46) and reconciliation doctor (go-slide-creator-s6va) remain open as enforcement mechanisms.

title: Add cell_accent_mode to shared overrides for grid-shaped patterns
description:
## Why

Multi-cell patterns currently call ctx.ResolveAccent(...) once and apply that single accent to every cell. Decks that use only one pattern type (or rotate accents only at the slide level via accent_strategy) end up monotonous: 4-6 cells per slide all in accent1.

Templates expose 6 accents (accent1-6) plus neutral fills; agents have no mechanism to ask for variety within a slide. Adding cell_accent_mode unlocks all of that without changing the slide-level accent rotation.

## What

Extend the shared overrides struct (internal/patterns/overrides.go:13 TextOverrides — or a new GridOverrides struct embedding TextOverrides) with:

```go
CellAccentMode string `json:"cell_accent_mode,omitempty"` // uniform | alternate | progressive
```

Modes:
- uniform (default): every cell gets the resolved base accent — current behavior, fully backwards compatible
- alternate: cells alternate base, base+1 wrapping at accent6 (e.g., accent1, accent2, accent1, accent2, ...)
- progressive: cells progress base, base+1, base+2, ... wrapping at accent6

Helper: ResolveCellAccent(base string, idx int, mode string) string in internal/patterns/, called by every grid-shaped pattern's Expand() inside the cell-emission loop.

DROP the 'semantic' mode the source TODO mentions — there is no formal positive/negative/neutral role table on accents in this codebase, so it would be undefined behavior. File a separate bead later if semantic roles get a real definition.

## Patterns to update

Grid-shaped patterns (embed the new field): card-grid, kpi-Nup family (2up..6up), process-flow, icon-row, comparison-2col, arch-stack, before-after where applicable. Verify each one's Expand() actually emits multiple cells with fills.

Patterns that should NOT embed the field: pull-quote, stat-hero, matrix-2x2 (the four quadrants have axis semantics already), bmc-canvas (built-in progression — verify in code before promising this; if not built-in, file a separate bead).

## Schema / backwards compatibility

OverridesSchema currently uses WithAdditionalProperties(false). Adding the field is additive; existing JSON without cell_accent_mode behaves as uniform. Validation must reject unknown values (only the three enum values accepted).

If any pattern's Version() is asserted in tests as a fixed value, bump appropriately.

## Interaction with accent_strategy

accent_strategy: section-keyed already shifts the base accent per section. cell_accent_mode operates on top of the resolved base. Document explicitly: cell_accent_mode walks accents starting from the post-strategy base. Add a unit test covering both together.

## Acceptance criteria

- All listed grid-shaped patterns accept cell_accent_mode in overrides
- 'uniform' is the default, current behavior preserved
- 'alternate' and 'progressive' produce the expected accent indexes for any cell count and any base accent
- Schema rejects unknown values with a clear error message
- Tests are parameterized over patterns and base accents — no specific deck or template referenced
close_reason: Implemented cell_accent_mode (uniform/alternate/progressive) for all grid-shaped patterns: card-grid, kpi-Nup, process-flow, icon-row, comparison-2col, arch-stack, before-after. Added ResolveCellAccent helper, schema validation, and comprehensive tests.

title: runPatternsExpand must use template-aware LayoutBounds, not hardcoded defaults
description:
## Why

cmd/json2pptx/patterns_cmd.go:308 runPatternsExpand currently builds LayoutBounds with hardcoded EMU values (X:457200, Y:457200, Width:8229600, Height:4229100). Any cell-budget number derived from this will be wrong for templates whose content area differs (different slide dimensions, different chrome, different default layout placement).

Once cell_budgets ship in the expand_pattern response, agents will treat them as authoritative. Hardcoded bounds make those numbers lie for any non-default template.

## What

- Add a -template flag (or -templates-dir + -template-id pair) to the pattern expand CLI subcommand
- Resolve content-area bounds from the chosen template's slide master / layout (reuse the existing template-loading code path used by the generate subcommand)
- The MCP path (cmd/json2pptx/pattern_resolve.go) already flows real bounds through — verify and document
- When -template is omitted, fall back to today's default but emit a "bounds_source": "default_fallback" field in the response so agents can detect the case

## Acceptance criteria

- Calling expand for any bundled template produces cell_budgets that match what fit-report would compute for the same expanded shape_grid in the same template
- Cross-template tests: same pattern + same content + different templates -> different budgets
- bounds_source field in response distinguishes template-aware vs fallback resolution
- No specific template / deck / pattern combination hardcoded in tests; iterate over templates/ and patterns programmatically
close_reason: Implemented template-aware LayoutBounds for patterns expand: added -template/-templates-dir flags to CLI, reused resolveExpandContext in both CLI and MCP handlers, added bounds_source field to response, wrote cross-template tests.

title: Expose cell_budgets and density in expand_pattern response (CLI and MCP)
description:
## Why

After a pattern expands to a shape_grid, agents have no pre-generation visibility into how much text physically fits in each cell. They write content blind, then discover overflow only when the deck renders. The post-Expand() shape_grid has fully-resolved bounds; capacity is computable deterministically — agents just need it surfaced.

Critical: budgets must be computed AFTER Expand() against the resulting ShapeGridInput, NOT inside each pattern's Expand. This way authored shape_grids that bypass patterns participate identically, and patterns stay pure (values -> ShapeGridInput).

## What

Extend the response of both runPatternsExpand (CLI, cmd/json2pptx/patterns_cmd.go:308) and the MCP expand_pattern handler with a new field:

```json
{
  "shape_grid": { ... existing ... },
  "cell_budgets": [
    {"cell_index": 0, "row": 0, "col": 0, "max_chars": 95, "actual_chars": 42, "density_pct": 44, "status": "underfilled", "font_size_pt": 12.0},
    ...
  ]
}
```

Implementation: call internal/textcapacity.ForResolvedGrid on the expanded grid using the slide's actual content area bounds (theme + layout). Emit one Density entry per cell.

Also emit density_warnings (informational, derived) when any cell is underfilled or overflow:

```json
"density_warnings": [
  {"cell_index": 2, "field": "body", "actual": 142, "budget": 95, "status": "overflow"}
]
```

## Compose-envelope handling

When compose nests this pattern inside another, the slide's content area is sliced. expand_pattern called standalone (no compose context) returns budgets relative to the full content area — which is an upper bound. Document this in the response: include a "bounds_assumption": "full_content_area" field, or accept an optional input bounds override. The compose handler is responsible for re-running capacity post-resolution if it wants accurate numbers; the standalone CLI/MCP call documents its assumption.

## Backwards compatibility

The new fields are additive. Pattern Version() bump is not required for expand_pattern response shape changes (no schema validation on the response side).

## Acceptance criteria

- runPatternsExpand emits cell_budgets[] and density_warnings[] for any pattern that produces a shape_grid
- MCP expand_pattern handler emits the same fields
- Numbers are deterministic across macOS / Linux CI (relies on textcapacity guarantees)
- Status reflects density bands: underfilled <60%, optimal 60..110%, overflow >110%
- Zero hardcoded references to specific patterns / templates / decks in tests — all pattern-template combinations exercised via table-driven tests
- Response includes bounds_assumption field documenting whether the budgets reflect full-slide or compose-sliced bounds

## Dependencies

Blocked by textcapacity package bead. Closely related to (but not blocked by) the LayoutBounds template-aware fix bead.
close_reason: Implemented cell_budgets and density_warnings in both CLI expand and MCP expand_pattern responses. Uses textcapacity.ForResolvedGrid on the expanded grid with layout bounds from ExpandContext. Includes bounds_assumption field. Table-driven tests cover all patterns × contexts.

title: Add internal/textcapacity package as single source of truth for cell/placeholder budgets
description:
## Why

Three estimators currently coexist with conflicting assumptions:
- internal/template/layouts.go:248 estimateMaxChars — font-blind, single 0.4 fudge factor, assumes ~10cpi
- internal/shapegrid/grid.go:486-525 estimateCellTextHeightEMU / textHeightEMU — font-aware (1.4 line height) but only height
- internal/textfit/measure.go:37 MeasureRun — the only true font-aware multi-line oracle, already used by fit-report at cmd/json2pptx/fit_report.go:335

Adding a fourth in each pattern's Expand() (as the source TODO suggests) compounds the rot. Any agent-facing signal (expand_pattern budgets, fit-report findings, repair_slide truncation, list_templates hints, analyze_rhythm aggregates) must agree numerically; that requires one oracle.

## What

New package internal/textcapacity/ with two entry points:

```go
type Budget struct {
    MaxChars  int     // body-paragraph ceiling at resolved font size
    MaxLines  int
    FontPt    float64
    WidthEMU  int64   // from shapegrid ResolvedCell.CellBounds
    HeightEMU int64
}

type Density struct {
    Budget
    ActualChars int
    DensityPct  int    // round(actual / max * 100); 0 if no content
    Status      Status // underfilled <60, optimal 60..110, overflow >110
}

func ForResolvedGrid(grid *jsonschema.ShapeGridInput, ctx Context) ([]Density, error)
func ForPlaceholder(ph types.PlaceholderInfo, text string) Density
```

Internals:
- Run shapegrid.Resolve() to get authoritative CellBounds for every cell; wrap textfit.MeasureRun for the body-paragraph capacity (binary-search n such that n chars at this font fit, OR derive from MeasureRun.Lines/Fits semantics — use whichever is already idiomatic in the codebase).
- Font precedence per cell: paragraph.size > shape.text.size > pattern override (HeaderSize/BodySize) > pattern default > theme/layout default. Document the precedence in package doc.
- For cells with multiple paragraphs at different sizes, budget the body paragraph (the longest by JSON-schema maxLength). Aggregate header+body counts in ActualChars.
- Use post-markdown-conversion length (pptx.ConvertMarkdownEmphasis output) so '**bold**' doesn't inflate counts.

## Determinism / cross-platform

The project already documents font-metric drift between macOS dev and Linux CI (see CLAUDE.md and t.Logf vs t.Errorf patterns). Budgets emitted to agents must NOT jitter by platform. Either:
- Use an embedded deterministic metrics table (e.g., Liberation Sans) for budget computation regardless of host font, OR
- Round to nearest 5 chars and document ±10% drift in package doc.

Pick the embedded-table approach. Tests can then assert exact numbers cross-platform.

## Acceptance criteria

- New package internal/textcapacity/ with Budget, Density, Status, ForResolvedGrid, ForPlaceholder, Context types
- Unit tests cover: 2x2 / 3x2 / 3x3 grids at 12pt body, 16pt header — body budgets monotonically decrease as cells shrink
- Unit tests cover: same grid at multiple font sizes — budget shrinks as font grows
- Unit tests pass identically on macOS and Linux CI (deterministic metrics)
- Package doc states font-precedence rule and the post-markdown rule
- Zero callers wired in this bead — wiring is separate beads (fit-report refactor, expand_pattern, etc.)
close_reason: Implemented internal/textcapacity package with Budget, Density, Status types, ForPlaceholder, ForResolvedGrid entry points. Uses embedded Liberation Sans for deterministic cross-platform budgets. Comprehensive tests covering monotonic decrease with cell size/font size, grid sizes, markdown stripping, density status thresholds, and determinism.

title: Validate-time wrong-pattern diagnostic with swap_pattern Fix
description:
**Source**: 2026-05-05 audit, R2#7. PREREQUISITE for xvyv.

**Why agents struggle**: When an agent passes 9 cells to card-grid, validator hard-errors with a string-embedded hint (cardgrid.go:194-205). When 7 cells, no hint at all. KPI similarly only hints across 3<->4. There is no general 'you sent shape X, pattern Y wants shape Z, but pattern W matches X exactly' cross-recommendation. A search for wrong_pattern/content_shape_mismatch returns zero hits. Agents who pick wrong (the most common cold-start LLM failure) get a bare validation error and re-call recommend_pattern from scratch — a round-trip cost that pushes them toward card-grid (loose constraints, always works).

**Fix**:
1. Define ErrCodeWrongPattern in internal/diagnostics/codes.go.
2. On validation count/shape failure, run a reverse-recommender: 'which patterns in the registry accept this exact (item_count, has_metrics, columns, has_long_body) shape?'
3. Attach Fix.Kind=swap_pattern with params.suggested=[{from, to, field_mapping}].
4. This unblocks repair_slide swap_pattern (xvyv).

**Acceptance**: 9-cell card-grid validation returns Fix=swap_pattern{to:'bmc-canvas',mapping:...}. 7-cell card-grid suggests 'no exact match — reduce to 6 (2x3) or expand to 9 (3x3)'.
close_reason: Implemented wrong_pattern diagnostic with swap_pattern fix: added ErrCodeWrongPattern error code, SuggestSwap reverse-recommender, ErrWrongPatternFor constructor. Card-grid and KPI validators now emit structured swap suggestions when content shape matches a different pattern. Added item constraints to bmc-canvas rule. 6 regression tests.

title: recommend_pattern: accept recent_patterns[] + prefer_variety, return confidence/disambiguation
description:
**Source**: 2026-05-05 audit, R1#3 + R1#9. The pair to deck-rhythm.

**Why agents struggle**: mcpRecommendPatternTool (cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:819-831) accepts only intent + content_hints. There is no avoid_patterns, no previous_pattern, no slide_index. The scorer in recommend.go:348-406 has no penalty hook — even if the agent KNOWS it overused card-grid, it cannot tell the recommender 'rank cards lower.' Returns 0.5-1.0 scores with no confidence band, so an agent confidently picks the top result without knowing the recommender was nearly indifferent.

**Fix**:
