1. Add fields to recommend_pattern: recent_patterns: []string, prefer_variety: bool, slide_index: int.
2. Apply decay penalty per recent occurrence in the scorer.
3. Return confidence_band: high|medium|low, near_miss[] with what would tip scoring, disambiguating_questions[] like ['how many items?', 'do you have a chart?'].
4. Returning a 'diversity bonus' candidate (a strong unused pattern) when prefer_variety is set.

**Acceptance**: Given recent_patterns=['card-grid','card-grid','card-grid'], 'overview of categories' must NOT return card-grid as top suggestion.
close_reason: Implemented: recommend_pattern now accepts recent_patterns[], prefer_variety, slide_index. Applies cumulative 0.15/occurrence decay penalty, returns confidence_band (high/medium/low), near_misses with would_tip_if, disambiguating_questions, and injects diversity bonus candidate.

title: analyze_deck_rhythm MCP tool — surface pattern runs, density CV, accent dominance
description:
**Source**: 2026-05-05 audit, R1#2 + R1#10 + R2#5. Companion to j8rr.

**Why agents struggle**: At slide N, the agent literally cannot answer 'have I used card-grid 3 times in a row?' Every MCP tool is per-slide or per-deck-as-input; there is no deck-level state surface (cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go has no analyze_deck_rhythm). structural_smells.go only inspects single ShapeGridInputs. score_deck returns aggregates but no per-slide pattern fingerprint and no n-gram statistics. The system is slide-local, but quality is deck-global.

**Fix**: New MCP tool analyze_deck_rhythm(presentation) returning:
- per_slide: [{slide_index, pattern, density_class (low|med|high), accent_role, dominant_visual}]
- aggregates: {pattern_runs:[(name,start,len)], longest_run, repetition_index, accent_balance:{accent1:0.7,...}, density_cv}
- recommendations: e.g. 'slide 5: break a card-grid run; recommended_break_pattern=stat-hero|pull-quote|timeline-horizontal'

**Acceptance**:
- Run on the pre-P1-4 ADV deck flags 10x card-grid as longest_run=10 with insert recommendations at indices 3, 6.
- Surfaces in score_deck as new composition_score axis (separate from correctness).
- Feeds into recommend_pattern via slide_index + presentation_so_far context.
close_reason: Implemented analyze_deck_rhythm MCP tool with per-slide fingerprints, pattern run detection, density CV, accent balance, recommendations, and composition score. Added CLI subcommand, output schema, contract test coverage, and unit tests.

title: Deck-level accent rotation strategy (one-week visual win)
description:
**Source**: 2026-05-05 3-reviewer audit, finding R2#2.

**Why agents struggle**: Every pattern hardcodes accent1 via internal/patterns/overrides.go:25-35 ResolveAccent. A grep across internal/patterns/*.go for accent[2-6] returns zero non-test hits. Templates ship 6 accent slots; we use 1. Result: even with varied patterns, slides look chromatically identical across a deck. This is the highest-leverage SMALL change.

**Fix**: Add Presentation.AccentStrategy enum: 'primary' (today, default), 'rotate' (round-robin per slide), 'section-keyed' (one accent per section). At expand time, compute effective accent from strategy + slide index + section header. Default unset patterns to the rotated accent rather than literal accent1.

**Acceptance**:
- Re-render examples/full-showcase.json with strategy='rotate' produces visually distinct slides without JSON edits beyond top-level field.
- recommend_pattern previews honor the active strategy.
- Existing decks with explicit accent values are unchanged.

**Estimated**: <300 LOC. Senior debate consensus: ship this in week 1.
close_reason: Implemented deck-level accent_strategy field (primary/rotate/section-keyed) with round-robin accent1-6 rotation via ExpandContext. All 18 pattern Expand methods updated to use ctx.ResolveAccent. Enum validation, schema fingerprint bump (3.3.0), changelog, and tests included.

title: P1-33: `render_deck_thumbnails` re-converts PPTX on every call — no cache
description:
**Labels:** `performance`, `P1`, `feedback-loop`

**Summary**
`internal/render/render.go:163-212` re-invokes LibreOffice headless + ImageMagick end-to-end every call, with no cache keyed on pptx mtime/hash. In a repair loop agents pay 5-10s per verification. `mu sync.Mutex` serializes across concurrent sessions, compounding the cost.

**Fix**
Hash PPTX bytes → cache dir under `os.TempDir()`; return cached PNGs on hash match. Expose `force: true` for byte-identical-but-intentionally-re-rendered cases.

**Acceptance**
- Second call to `render_deck_thumbnails` with unchanged PPTX returns in <100ms.
- Changing one byte of the PPTX invalidates the cache.
close_reason: Implemented content-hash-based render cache. Cached PNGs keyed by SHA-256(pptx)+density in os.TempDir(). Second call with unchanged PPTX skips LibreOffice/ImageMagick entirely. Added force parameter to bypass cache.

title: P1-32: svggen charts lack target/trend lines, annotations, data-label formatting, dual-axis
description:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `P1`, `charts`, `svggen`

**Summary**
`svggen/charts.go` `ChartSeries` carries only `Values`, `Labels`, `Color`. `legend.go` supports positioning. Missing:
- Target/reference lines (horizontal dashed "Target: 95%")
- Trend lines (linear regression overlay)
- Annotations (callout arrow pointing to an outlier + label)
- Data label units / format strings (`$1.2M`, `24%`, `+3.2pp`)
- Axis-break / truncation indicator (zig-zag when y-axis starts at 80 not 0)
- Dual-axis (volume bars + conversion-rate line)
- Color-blind-safe palette flag

Real consulting charts always have a target, source note, and at least one annotation.

**Fix**
Add `annotations`, `data_labels.format`, `axis.y.truncated`, `palette: colorblind-safe`, and `dual_axis` chart type to the envelope:
```json
"annotations": [
  {"kind": "reference_line", "axis": "y", "value": 95, "label": "Target", "style": "dashed"},
  {"kind": "trendline", "series": "Revenue", "method": "linear"},
  {"kind": "callout", "x": 4, "y": 120, "text": "Launch of product X"}
],
"data_labels": {"format": "${value:,.1f}M", "show_on": "last|all|peaks"}
```

**Acceptance**
- Revenue-plus-target bar chart renders dashed target line with label and a callout on the quarter that missed.
- Colorblind palette usable via a single flag; documented in `docs/CHARTS.md`.
close_reason: Implemented: annotations (reference_line, trendline, callout), data_labels (format, show_on), and colorblind-safe palette for svggen charts

title: P1-31: Tables cannot do conditional formatting, totals rows, highlight columns, banded headers
description:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `P1`, `tables`, `design`

**Summary**
`internal/jsonschema/table.go` exposes only `Striped` (boolean zebra). Professional tables need: highlight column (tinted recommended option), totals row (bold + top border), negative-red / positive-green conditional cell fill, grouped column headers (merged sub-headers), column data types (right-align numbers, left-align text, auto-format currency/percent). Without these, comparison and financial tables look like spreadsheet screenshots.

**Fix**
Extend `TableStyle` and `CellStyle`:
- `TableStyle.HighlightColumn int` — 1-indexed; applies `accent3-tint3` fill
- `TableStyle.TotalsRow bool` — last row: bold, top border `dk1` 1pt
- `TableStyle.ColumnTypes []string` — `text|number|currency|percent|delta`; drives alignment + number formatting + optional red/green on `delta`
- `TableStyle.HeaderBands [][]int` — merge ranges for grouped headers
- `CellStyle.Conditional` — `{rule: positive|negative|threshold, threshold: float, fill: scheme}`

**Acceptance**
- Vendor-comparison matrix with "Recommended" column tinted, capability scores color-coded, and weighted-total bold row at bottom renders from a minimal JSON spec.
close_reason: Implemented: highlight_column, totals_row, column_types (with delta red/green), and per-cell conditional formatting for tables

title: P1-30: Missing consulting staples — pyramid, swimlane, process-flow, before/after, roadmap-phased, arch-stack
description:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `P1`, `patterns`, `design`

**Summary**
Current pattern list covers KPIs, cards, timelines, BMC, and a 2x2 matrix. Six shapes appear in nearly every consulting / strategy deck but cannot be expressed:
- **Pyramid / Hierarchy** — 3-5 stacked trapezoids
- **Process flow with decision diamonds** — rectangles + diamonds + arrows, left-to-right
- **Swimlane** — horizontal bands per actor/function, shapes placed per lane/step
- **Before / After** — two-column with explicit "From → To" chevron
- **Phased roadmap** — quarters across, workstreams down, pills per phase (distinct from `timeline-horizontal` which is a single-row event list)
- **Architecture stack** — labeled tiers (presentation/logic/data) + cross-cutting side rails

`svggen/org_chart.go` is closest to a structural diagram but has no pattern wrapper.

**Fix**
Ship `pyramid`, `process-flow`, `swimlane`, `before-after`, `roadmap-phased`, `arch-stack`. Each 80-150 LOC, reusing shape primitives. Prioritize `before-after` and `pyramid` — highest-frequency missing patterns.

**Acceptance**
- Each new pattern has an example deck in `examples/` and passes visual QC.
- `recommend_pattern` suggests them for matching content shapes.
close_reason: Implemented all 6 consulting patterns: pyramid, before-after, process-flow, swimlane, roadmap-phased, arch-stack. Added recommendation rules and aliases.

title: P1-29: Missing "emphasis" patterns — no stat-hero or pull-quote slide types
description:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `P1`, `patterns`, `design`

**Summary**
Consulting decks punctuate dense slides with single-idea emphasis slides: a 160pt number with one line of context, or a pull-quote with attribution. These create the visual rhythm that makes a 25-slide deck feel paced. Current pattern registry (`cardgrid`, `kpi-3up`, `kpi-4up`, `matrix-2x2`, `bmc-canvas`, `icon-row`, `comparison-2col`, `timeline-horizontal`) has no single-hero-idea layout. `kpi-Nup` are plural by design — cannot produce "$2.4B TAM" full-bleed.

**Fix**
Two new patterns:
- `stat-hero` — one oversized number (80-200pt) + label + optional one-line subtext + optional source footer. Fields: `value`, `unit`, `label`, `context`, `accent`, `source`.
- `pull-quote` — italic serif quote block (60-80pt) + attribution row + optional left accent rule. Fields: `quote`, `attribution`, `role`, `accent_side`.

Both implement the standard pattern contract (LayoutBounds occupancy, density variants, contrast autofix).

**Acceptance**
- Executive summary deck can render `$2.4B — addressable AI consulting market by FY27` as a stat-hero.
- Pattern registry documents both in `docs/PATTERNS.md`.
close_reason: Implemented stat-hero and pull-quote patterns with full validation, expansion, schemas, tests, golden files, recommendation rules, and aliases

title: P1-28: No OOXML pre-flight validator — P0-1 class bugs can recur
description:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `P1`, `ooxml`, `ci`

**Summary**
P0-1 (scheme name written into `srgbClr`) landed in shipped code and reached users before the visual-QC review caught it. `cmd/validatepptx/` exists but doesn't run on every generation and doesn't cover the full OOXML-compliance bar. There's no systematic "does this file open cleanly in PowerPoint" check.

**Fix**
Add a post-generate hook that unzips the PPTX and runs schema-targeted validators:
- `<a:srgbClr val="...">` matches `^[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$`
- `<a:schemeClr val="...">` is in `{bg1,bg2,tx1,tx2,accent1..6,lt1,lt2,dk1,dk2,hlink,folHlink}`
- Every `<p:sp>` has unique `cNvPr@id` per slide
- Chart XML cat+val rows equal length
- Table rows/cols match `<a:tblGrid>`
- No zero-width/height shapes unless intentional

Expose as `validate_output: true` option on `generate_presentation` and as CLI `json2pptx validate-output <file.pptx>`. Run in CI on every example deck; fail build on any violation.

**Acceptance**
- Regression test for P0-1 (scheme-name-in-srgbClr) fails without the fix.
- CI catches any new OOXML violation introduced by generator changes.
close_reason: Implemented OOXML pre-flight validator: validates srgbClr hex format, schemeClr vocabulary, unique shape IDs per slide, table grid/cell consistency, and zero-extent shapes. Exposed as validate-output CLI subcommand and ValidateOutput option on GenerationRequest. Includes P0-1 regression test.

title: P1-27: No "constrained" design mode — agents can pick any color/font/size
description:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `P1`, `design-system`

**Summary**
JSON accepts `theme_override`, raw `shape_grid` with arbitrary `fill`/`color`/`text.size`. Contrast is auto-fixed only for layout-background text; shape-grid text is warn-only (per CLAUDE.md). Prior art (Gamma, Pitch, Marp) restrict author degrees of freedom — geometry and typography are theme-owned. json2pptx lets agents break brand by accident. Result: "every slide is a different orange" and inconsistent typography across a deck.

**Fix**
Introduce a `design_mode: "constrained" | "free"` deck flag (default `constrained`). In `constrained`:
- Reject raw hex in `fill`/`color`; require scheme names (`accent1`, `lt2`, `dk1`).
- Reject absolute font sizes on body text; require named sizes (`title`, `heading`, `body`, `caption`) that resolve via template.
- Emit a `design_mode_violation` fit-finding when the deck attempts to break out.
Power users set `free` to unlock raw controls.

**Acceptance**
- Default-mode deck with a raw hex fill is rejected with a fix suggesting the nearest scheme color.
- `free` mode preserves current behavior.
- The constrained palette produces visually consistent decks across 20+ slides.
close_reason: Implemented design_mode field (constrained/free) with validation rejecting raw hex colors and absolute font sizes in constrained mode, emitting design_mode_violation diagnostics with fix suggestions

title: P1-26: No declarative output schema on MCP tools
description:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `P1`, `api-contract`, `mcp`

**Summary**
Every tool declares inputs (`WithString`/`WithObject`) but none declares an `outputSchema` (`cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:151-205`). Response shapes are prose-described in tool descriptions. MCP spec best practice: declare `outputSchema` so clients validate structured responses deterministically; use `structuredContent` alongside text. Without output schemas, agents must prose-parse ad-hoc JSON; self-correction loops (repair_slide, fit-report) are fragile.

**Fix**
Add `WithOutputSchema(...)` to each tool. Critical for `generate_presentation`, `expand_pattern`, `score_deck`, `repair_slide`, `validate_input`, `preview_presentation_plan`. Publish JSON Schemas under `internal/jsonschema/` and reuse for response validation in tests.

**Acceptance**
- Every MCP tool declares an output schema.
- MCP clients can validate tool responses without prose-parsing the description.
- Response struct drift is caught by schema-conformance tests.
close_reason: Implemented: added WithRawOutputSchema to all 23 MCP tools with hand-crafted JSON Schemas in mcp_output_schemas.go, plus schema-conformance tests

title: P1-25: MCP error codes are a free-form string namespace with no taxonomy
description:
**Labels:** `bug`, `P1`, `api-contract`, `error-taxonomy`, `mcp`

**Summary**
Error codes passed to `api.MCPSimpleError` / `MCPDiagnosticsError` are inline string literals sprinkled across handlers with no central definition: `MISSING_PARAMETER`, `INVALID_JSON`, `TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND`, `STRICT_FIT`, `UNKNOWN_PATTERN`, `INTERNAL`, `unknown_enum` (lowercase — inconsistent), plus Pattern-layer codes using different casing (`ErrCodeUnknownLayoutID`, `legacy_authoring_form`, `style_collision`). No enum, no const block, no code → semantics doc. Agents catching `TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND` from one tool cannot write a single handler for the same semantic from another tool.

**Fix**
Create `internal/diagnostics/codes.go` defining every code as a typed const, grouped by family (`INPUT_*`, `TEMPLATE_*`, `RESOURCE_*`, `RENDER_*`, `INTERNAL_*`), all SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE. Reject new code string literals in code review. Publish the list via `get_capabilities.error_codes`.

**Acceptance**
- Test asserts every error code emitted by `MCPSimpleError`/`MCPDiagnosticsError` belongs to the declared enum.
- All codes are SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE (linter catches regressions).
close_reason: Implemented: Created internal/diagnostics/codes.go with typed Code constants grouped by family (INPUT_*, TEMPLATE_*, RESOURCE_*, RENDER_*, SETTINGS_*, INTERNAL), all SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE. Fixed 3 inconsistent lowercase codes (unknown_enum, ambiguous_input, validation_failed). Added error_codes field to get_capabilities response. Added tests enforcing the taxonomy (all codes SCREAMING_SNAKE, unique, and no undeclared string literals in handlers).

title: P1-24: `validate_input` and `generate_presentation` return incompatible diagnostic shapes
description:
**Labels:** `bug`, `P1`, `api-contract`, `error-taxonomy`, `mcp`

**Summary**
For the same failure, the response shape depends on which tool the agent called. `generate_presentation` returns `CallToolResult{IsError:true, StructuredContent: mcpErrorEnvelope{Diagnostics, Summary}}`. `validate_input` returns a success envelope `dryRunOutput{Valid, Diagnostics, Errors []string, Warnings []string, FitFindings}` — `IsError` is false even on validation failures, and the same error text is duplicated in both `Diagnostics` (structured) and `Errors` (free text, `mcp.go:721-736`). The CLI `validate` returns yet a third shape (`validate.go:122-132`). A repair loop that calls validate → generate cannot parse errors uniformly.

**Fix**
Standardize on one envelope: every tool returns `StructuredContent: {ok: bool, diagnostics: [], warnings: [], data: ...}`. Drop the string-only `Errors`/`Warnings` arrays in `dryRunOutput` and `validateResult` — redundant with Diagnostics and encourage free-text parsing. Make `IsError` reflect `any(diag.Severity == error)` uniformly. Update `validate_input` so a failing presentation returns `IsError:true`.

**Acceptance**
- Agent can write a single diagnostic-handler function that works for validate_input, generate_presentation, and CLI `validate -format=json`.
- All three surfaces emit identical `{code, path, severity, fix}` shapes for the same input.
close_reason: Unified validate_input error shape: IsError=true with diagnostics envelope on failure (same as generate_presentation); dropped redundant Errors/Warnings backfill from MCP path; added diagnostics[] to CLI validate -json output

title: P1-23: `get_capabilities` advertises booleans, hiding Fix.Kind / finding code / placeholder alias vocabularies
description:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `P1`, `api-contract`, `discoverability`, `mcp`

**Summary**
`capabilitiesFeatures` (`cmd/json2pptx/mcp_capabilities.go:29-36`) exposes only `fit_report: bool`, `named_patterns: bool`, etc. Everything agents need to plan a repair loop — Fix.Kind vocabulary, fit-finding codes, placeholder aliases, accepted enum values for `transition`/`build`/`background.fit` — is invisible. `repair_slide` supported kinds are only documented in a free-text tool description at `cmd/json2pptx/mcp_repair.go:50-57`. An agent cannot enumerate them programmatically; unsupported kinds silently return `{applied: false, message: "kind_not_supported"}` indistinguishable from a valid kind that had nothing to fix.

**Fix**
Extend `capabilitiesFeatures` to publish `repair_fix_kinds: []string`, `fit_finding_codes: []string`, `placeholder_aliases: map[string][]string`, `content_types: []string`, `slide_transitions: []string`, `chart_types: []string`, `pattern_variants: map[pattern][]variant`. Emit these from the same Go sources that implement them (the `applyRepairFix` switch, finding-code constants) so they stay in sync.

**Acceptance**
- `get_capabilities` response contains enumerated vocabularies for every categorical parameter.
- Adding a new Fix.Kind to `applyRepairFix` automatically appears in capabilities (test asserts this).
- Agent can detect "this server doesn't support `swap_pattern` yet" before attempting the call.
close_reason: Extended get_capabilities with vocabularies section exposing repair_fix_kinds, fit_finding_codes, content_types, slide_transitions, chart_types, diagram_types, placeholder_aliases, pattern_names, and pattern_aliases. Added AST-based sync test ensuring new repair fix kinds auto-appear.

title: P1-22: Layout synthesis events are invisible to agents
description:
**Labels:** `bug`, `P1`, `feedback-loop`, `any-action-auditable`

**Summary**
When `SynthesizeIfNeeded` (`internal/template/synthesis.go:29,151,258`) fabricates `Blank + Title` or `Two Content` layouts (triggered by pwc-template among others), decisions emit `slog.Info` only — no finding is added to the generator response. The slide uses an unbranded layout but `generate_presentation` returns success with no warning. Agents believe they got the user's template; visually they got a mongrel. P1-16 mentions this in passing but scopes the fix to one template. The broader bug: the synthesis event itself never reaches the agent.

**Fix**
New fit finding: `code: layout_synthesized`, `severity: warning`, `action: review`, `fix.params: {layout_id, capability, base_layout_id}`. Emit one per synthesized layout. Surface through `result.FitFindings`. Then reconsider whether synthesis should exist at all (see P1-16).

**Acceptance**
- Generating against a template missing `slideLayout5` emits `layout_synthesized` in the response.
- The finding includes which base layout was adapted so the agent can judge visual impact.
close_reason: Implemented: SynthesizeIfNeeded now returns []patterns.FitFinding with code layout_synthesized for each synthesized layout, surfaced in MCP and CLI responses

title: P1-21: `score_deck` scores input JSON, not the produced PPTX
description:
**Labels:** `bug`, `P1`, `feedback-loop`, `mcp`, `agent-ergonomics`

**Summary**
The tool description promises "Use this after `generate_presentation` to get structured visual feedback" but the handler at `cmd/json2pptx/score_deck.go:93-100` only re-runs `collectFitFindings` on the input JSON. It never opens the output PPTX. Any render-time autofix, layout synthesis, contrast swap, or text trim that only materializes during generation is invisible to `score_deck`. Two calls with the same input always yield the same score — the "after generate" contract is a lie, and agents waste round-trips thinking they've re-verified.

**Fix**
Accept `pptx_path` parameter and run the deterministic checker against the produced file (reparse layouts from the output, not the input). Alternative: fold the tool into `generate_presentation`'s response as a `score` block derived from `result.FitFindings + result.ContrastSwaps + post-render occupancy`.

**Acceptance**
- `score_deck(pptx_path=...)` returns different findings than `score_deck(presentation=...)` when generation-time autofix kicked in.
- The score reflects actual rendered state, including pagination, autofit shrink, and contrast swaps.
close_reason: score_deck now runs full generation pipeline to capture render-time findings (contrast swaps, autofit, clamping) instead of only static analysis on input JSON

title: P1-20: No read-back tool — agents can't introspect what `generate_presentation` actually produced
description:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `P1`, `round-trip`, `mcp`, `feedback-loop`

**Summary**
The server accepts deck JSON and emits a `.pptx`, but there is no MCP tool or CLI subcommand that reads a `.pptx` back into deck JSON. Once a PPTX is written — and the engine has applied layout synthesis, normalized placeholder names, auto-mapped virtual placeholders, injected footers, applied contrast auto-fixes (`result.ContrastSwaps` at `cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:437`), and `normAutofit`-shrunk text — the agent's only option is `render_slide_image` (base64 PNG). It cannot answer "what text ended up on slide 3?", "which placeholder received the body?", "was text silently trimmed?", or "will a re-run produce the same bytes?". Breaks idempotency verification and repair-loop convergence.

**Fix**
Add a `read_presentation` MCP tool (and CLI `json2pptx read <file.pptx>`) that returns best-effort deck JSON reconstruction plus the materialized resolution: layouts used, placeholder_id remappings, contrast swaps, synthesis manifest, footer applied. Alternative: have `generate_presentation` echo `resolved_presentation` in its response alongside `output_path` so the agent sees the canonical deck it really rendered.

**Acceptance**
- `read_presentation` returns `{slides: [{index, layout_id, placeholders: [{id, text, bounds}], shapes, tables, charts}]}` — entirely deterministic, no LibreOffice dependency.
- Round-trip test: deck JSON → generate → read → diff against input, assert only documented transformations (auto-fix, pagination).
close_reason: Implemented read_presentation MCP tool and CLI read subcommand for best-effort PPTX content extraction

title: P1-16: pwc-template missing layouts — agents target slideLayout5-8 but only 1-4 exist
description:
**Labels:** `bug`, `P1`, `templates`

**Summary**
`pwc-template.pptx` has only 4 layouts (Title, Section Header, One Content, Closing). Agents routinely request `slideLayout5` for "Blank + Title" and `slideLayout6`-8 for two-column variants because that's what built-in templates advertise. The generator currently **synthesizes** these missing layouts at runtime (confirmed in logs: `INFO template missing layout capabilities, synthesizing missing="[two-column blank-title]"`), but:
- Synthesized layouts don't follow pwc brand typography (no Georgia title, no orange accents).
- The synthesis is invisible to validation/pattern selection.
- Agents can't preview what they'll get.

**Fix**
Add native layouts to `pwc-template.pptx` matching built-in conventions:
- `slideLayout5` — "Blank + Title" — title bar top, empty content area below
- `slideLayout6` — "Two Content" — title + 50/50 two-column body
- (Optional) `slideLayout7` — "Two Column (60/40)"
- (Optional) `slideLayout8` — "Two Column (40/60)"

Each must inherit PwC brand (Georgia + accent1 orange accents in title, Arial body). Use forest-green / midnight-blue as structural templates; restyle to pwc theme.

Also consider: should the **runtime synthesis** code exist at all? It hides template deficiencies. Two options:
- (a) Keep it but emit a warning finding `code: synthesized_layout, severity: warning, action: review` so the agent sees it.
- (b) Remove it; require templates to declare all layouts they support.

Option (a) is pragmatic (compatibility), option (b) is cleaner long-term.

**Location**
- `~/.json2pptx/templates/pwc-template.pptx` — needs layouts added
- `internal/template/` — grep for `synthesiz` to find runtime-synthesis code

**Acceptance**
- `pwc-template.pptx` advertises ≥6 layouts.
- Generating a card-grid slide with `layout_id: "slideLayout5"` on pwc-template uses the native layout, not a synthesized one (no synthesis log line).
- Either the synthesis code emits a fit-finding when it fires, or it's removed.
close_reason: Added pwc-template to mktemplate with Georgia/Arial/orange-accent branding and all 7 standard layouts (including native blank-title). Regenerated all bundled templates with the new blank-title layout. Synthesis code already emitted fit findings for layout_synthesized.

title: P1-15: `section_number` placeholder resolver alias + naming convention
description:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `P1`, `placeholders`, `templates`

**Summary**
Every template ships a large-font upper-right placeholder on its Section Divider / Section Header layout, semantically intended for a section number. In every template it's labeled `<p:ph type="body" idx="1"/>` with no semantic distinction from a regular body slot. Agents can't target it cleanly: asking for `body` works but lies about intent, asking for `subtitle` silently drops (P0-2). Layouts with both a "real body" and a section-number slot (if any are added) can't be disambiguated at all.

**Fix**
Three coordinated changes:

1. **Template convention:** the section-number placeholder shape must have `<p:cNvPr name="Section Number">` (PascalCase, with space). Applied to `pwc-template.pptx` slideLayout2. Pending for built-ins (see P2-17).

2. **Resolver alias:** `internal/generator/placeholder_resolver.go` treats `section_number`, `section_no`, and `large_number` as aliases that resolve in this order:
   - Shape whose `cNvPr name` equals `"Section Number"` (case-insensitive)
   - `body idx=1` on a layout whose name contains "Section" (case-insensitive)
   - Fallback: `body idx=1`

3. **Generator handling:** when resolving a placeholder via a `section_number` alias (or a shape named `"Section Number"`), skip the 24pt body cap (see P0-5) and pass `maxFontSizeHPt=0` so layout typography is preserved.

**Acceptance**
- Content `{"placeholder_id": "section_number", "text_value": "02"}` on pwc-template Section Header renders 208pt orange "02" in upper-right.
- Same content on a built-in forest-green Section Divider renders at that template's declared size (96pt today, possibly larger after P2-17).
- `skill-info` output advertises `section_number` as a supported placeholder_id on layouts that have a `"Section Number"` shape.
close_reason: Implemented section_number placeholder resolver alias with 3-level priority chain (shape name → body idx=1 on section layout → body idx=1 fallback), ContentSectionTitle treatment to skip font cap, pwc-template Section Divider shape rename, normalizer preservation, and skill-info advertisement

title: P1-7: `timeline-horizontal` needs `chevron` and `gantt` styles
description:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `P1`, `patterns`, `design`

**Summary**
Current `timeline-horizontal` renders as disconnected dot-and-label pairs on a flat line — no sense of progression or phase. User explicitly requested chevron or Gantt variants.

**Fix**
Add `style` field to `timeline-horizontal`:
- `dots` (current, default)
- `chevron` — connected right-pointing arrow shapes per stop; label inside chevron, date below
- `gantt` — horizontal bars with start/end anchored to `date`; optional `end_date` field on stop; label left of bar

Consider splitting Gantt into a separate `timeline-gantt` pattern since it needs different value schema (ranges, not points).

**Acceptance**
- ADV AI roadmap slide (6 stops from 30 Apr → 30 Sep) renders as connected chevrons with accent-color gradient across the chain.
- Gantt variant tested with at least one range-style value set.
close_reason: Implemented chevron and gantt styles for timeline-horizontal pattern with gradient fills, end_date support, and full test coverage

title: P1-6: card-grid has no visual variety — monotone orange bars
description:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `P1`, `patterns`, `design`

**Summary**
Every `card-grid` slide looks identical: orange header bar + body text. Over a 19-slide deck this is visually monotonous even when correctly rendered.

**Fix**
Add optional `visual_variant` field on `card-grid`:
- `numbered-badge` — extract `"1. "`, `"2. "` prefixes from `header` into a large circled badge
- `accent-stripe` — left-edge vertical stripe in `accent1` instead of top bar
- `icon-card` — cell accepts optional `icon` slot
- `tinted` — alternating `lt1` / `lt2` card backgrounds

**Acceptance**
- Three consecutive card-grid slides in a deck can look visually distinct by varying `visual_variant`.
- Each variant passes contrast check without auto-fix.
close_reason: Implemented: Added 5 visual variants (filled, accent-stripe, numbered-badge, icon-card, tinted) via overrides.style field on card-grid pattern

title: P1-5: Body text auto-scale floor too low (6pt illegible)
description:
**Labels:** `bug`, `P1`, `patterns`, `typography`

**Summary**
Visual QC found multiple slides with body text at 6-8pt — unreadable at normal viewing distance. The auto-fit shrink path will go as low as 6pt to avoid overflow before triggering a fit-finding.

**Fix**
- Raise auto-fit floor to 10pt.
- When text cannot fit at 10pt, emit `fit_overflow` with `fix.kind: split_at_row` or `reduce_text` — do not shrink below the floor.
- Above the floor, patterns should scale body text proportionally to cell height (not inversely to text length).

**Acceptance**
- No body text on any slide renders below 10pt.
- `strict_fit: strict` correctly refuses slides that would require < 10pt.
close_reason: Enforced absolute 10pt minimum font size floor in textfit.Calculate() and text_autofit overflow fallback. No body text will render below 10pt regardless of MinFontScalePct overrides. Overflow emits fit_overflow finding with split_at_row fix kind.

title: P1-4: Patterns ignore `LayoutBounds` — slides render with 50-80% wasted whitespace
description:
**Labels:** `bug`, `P1`, `patterns`, `rendering`

**Summary**
Every named pattern emits rows with `Height: 0`. The shape-grid engine (`internal/shapegrid/grid.go:58-78`) interprets all-zero-height grids as "shrink `Bounds.CY` to measured content height." Result: a 3-card grid on a 7-inch-tall slide collapses to a 1-inch strip at the top, leaving the rest of the slide empty. Visual-QC rejected every slide of a 19-slide deck with this pattern.

The `ExpandContext.LayoutBounds` field exists (`internal/patterns/pattern.go:61-67`) but no pattern consumes it.

**Location**
- `internal/shapegrid/grid.go:58-78` — shrink-to-content path
- `internal/patterns/cardgrid.go:240-243` — emits `Height: 0` rows
- `internal/patterns/timelinehorizontal.go:212-221` — same
- `internal/patterns/pattern.go:61-67` — unused `LayoutBounds`

**Fix**
1. Patterns compute `LayoutBounds.height / rows` and assign it to each row (or use a `row_ratio` default).
2. OR: shape-grid engine, when all heights are zero AND `LayoutBounds` is provided, distributes available height evenly instead of shrinking.

Option 2 is safer (one change, no pattern-by-pattern edits) but hides the implicit contract. Option 1 is explicit. Recommend Option 2 as short-term fix + Option 1 refactor across patterns as follow-up.

**Acceptance**
- Rendered `card-grid` with 3 cells on `slideLayout5` fills ≥ 70% of the content area.
- New fit-finding (see P2-10) no longer fires on any slide in the ADV deck.
close_reason: Added FillHeight flag to Grid; pattern-expanded grids now fill layout area instead of shrinking to content

title: feature: resolve_theme MCP tool — return resolved colors and fonts for a template
description:
Agent picks 'accent1' thinking blue, gets coral on warm-coral template. Today the agent has no way to verify what semantic color names resolve to without generating and rendering. Pure read-only tool returning the theme inline.

## Tool surface

`resolve_theme(template_name, color_names?: [string], font_names?: [string]) → {\
  template: string,\
  colors: {accent1: '#1F4E79', accent2: '#...', lt1: '...', lt2: '...', dk1: '...', dk2: '...', hyperlink: '...', followed_hyperlink: '...'},\
  fonts: {major: {latin, ea, cs}, minor: {latin, ea, cs}},\
  resolved_for: [string]   // echoes which names the agent asked about\
}`

If color_names/font_names are omitted, return the full theme. If provided, return only the requested names plus mark unknown ones in an 'unknown' array with did_you_mean.

## Why it changes outcomes

- Cold-start: agent can preview the palette before authoring shape colors and avoid mid-deck color clashes.
- Pairs naturally with 4eau preview_presentation_plan — agent can ask 'show me what slide 3 will look like AND what accent1 resolves to' in two cheap calls.
- Closes the small but persistent class of bugs where authored hex colors fight the template theme.

## Implementation pointers

- internal/template/ already loads themes during validate-template. Surface the parsed theme object via a new function GetResolvedTheme(templatePath) (\*ResolvedTheme, error).
- internal/generator/text_contrast.go already does color resolution — likely already has the helpers needed.
- Tiny new MCP handler.
- Cache: theme is invariant per template binary; cache by templates_dir + template_name + mtime.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All 4 bundled templates return distinct, non-empty palettes.
- [ ] Unknown color name returns structured error with did_you_mean (use the same ClosestMatch helper that fmsh wired up).
- [ ] Tool description in MCP and skill-info entry (coordinate with tfvv).
- [ ] Tests: golden palette per template; theme parsing roundtrip.

Effort: tiny. The data is already loaded internally; this just exposes it.

Found by: agent-native-reviewer + codex-rescue follow-up audit 2026-05-01.
close_reason: Implemented resolve_theme MCP tool: returns resolved theme colors/fonts for any template, with filtered queries, did_you_mean for unknown color names, and color_roles. Tests cover all 4 templates, distinct palettes, filtered queries, unknown colors, and error cases.

title: feature: expose internal/visualqa as MCP score_deck tool with deterministic-rule subset
description:
internal/visualqa/agent.go already runs visual-quality findings internally but is not callable via MCP. Per memory ('Visual QA: Haiku agents produce ~60% false positives on layout issues'), the haiku-based output is unreliable — but the **rule-based** subset (alignment, density on rendered output, contrast post-render, footer collision actually-rendered) is deterministic. Split deterministic from heuristic, expose the deterministic layer as an MCP tool.

## Tool surface

`score_deck(deck_or_path, mode?: 'deterministic' | 'with_heuristics' = 'deterministic') → {\
  overall_score: int 0-100,\
  per_slide: [{index, score, findings: [{code, severity, message, fix: {kind, params}}]}],\
  summary: {top_codes: [...], slide_count, problem_slides_count},\
  mode_used: string\
}`

## Why it changes outcomes

After render-to-image (companion bead, see depends-on) the agent can SEE its output. score_deck gives the agent **structured** visual feedback so it can iterate without burning vision tokens on every check. Combined with fit-findings (text-domain) and render-to-image (vision-domain), the agent has three independent feedback channels.

## Pre-requisite: classify visualqa checks

Before exposing, audit internal/visualqa/agent.go and prompts.go to classify each check:
- **Deterministic** (geometry math, theme color resolution, computed contrast against rendered fill): always exposed.
- **Heuristic** (Haiku vision flagging 'top clipping', 'title cut off' — 60% FP per memory): gated behind mode='with_heuristics' with explicit confidence-low warning in output.

Findings the haiku layer flagged but proved false in the 472-slide sweep should be retired or downgraded to informational.

## Implementation pointers

- Refactor internal/visualqa/ into deterministic/ and heuristic/ subpackages.
- New cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go handler handleScoreDeck.
- Reuse FitFinding {kind, params} envelope for output (consistent with to8a epic decisions).
- Score formula: 100 - sum(severity_weights * findings_per_slide); document in skill-info.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Deterministic mode emits zero false positives across the 14 example decks × 4 templates baseline (per memory, this is the same eval surface used for the FP measurement).
- [ ] Heuristic mode is opt-in only; default returns deterministic-only.
- [ ] FitFinding envelope reused, so agents reading score_deck output use the same parsing path as fit-report.
- [ ] Tests: deterministic checks have golden-output tests against known-good and known-bad decks.

Depends on: render-to-image bead (some deterministic checks need rasterized output for accurate measurement, especially contrast-on-render and post-autofit overflow).

Found by: agent-native-reviewer + codex-rescue follow-up audit 2026-05-01.
close_reason: Implemented score_deck MCP tool with deterministic scoring: created internal/visualqa/deterministic/ subpackage with ScoreFromFindings scorer, added score_deck MCP tool handler that reuses existing fit-findings pipeline, registered tool in MCP server. Score formula: 100 - sum(severity_weights × findings_per_slide). Tests pass, lint clean.

title: feature: render-to-image MCP tool — close the agent visual-feedback loop
description:
Today agents are visually blind: they generate JSON, get text fit-findings, and ship without ever seeing what the deck looks like. The cmd/json2pptx/pptx2jpg/ binary already does PPTX → JPG conversion via LibreOffice + ImageMagick. Wrap it as an MCP tool so coding agents with vision can self-evaluate.

## Tool surface

`render_slide_image(deck_or_path, slide_index, density?: int = 100) → {png_base64, width, height, density_used}`

`render_deck_thumbnails(deck_or_path, density?: int = 50, max_slides?: int = 50) → {slides: [{index, png_base64, width, height}], truncated: bool}`

Both accept either an inline deck object (post-arsr) or a path to a generated .pptx.

## Why it changes outcomes

Loop today: JSON → fit-report → guess if it looks ok → ship → human catches visual issues.
Loop after: JSON → render → see → fix.

This is the single largest blind spot no parity/contract bead can address. It also unlocks higher-quality visualqa rule checks that need the actual rasterized output (alignment, contrast on rendered text, footer-bar overlap on the actual canvas).

## Implementation pointers

- Existing: cmd/pptx2jpg/main.go does the PPTX→JPG conversion. Refactor the core into internal/render/ as a callable function (RenderSlideToPNG / RenderDeckToPNGs).
- New MCP tool registration in cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go alongside existing handlers.
- Streaming: thumbnails default to density=50 (small PNGs), single-slide default to density=100. Cap base64 payload per slide at ~200KB; if exceeded return a path reference instead of inline (mode controlled by tool param: 'inline' | 'path').
- Concurrency: LibreOffice headless is single-threaded per process; serialize slide rendering via a mutex or per-call temp dir.
- Caching: keyed by sha256(deck_json + density). Honor the existing storage retention policy (internal/config StorageConfig).

## Risks

- LibreOffice startup is slow (~3-5s cold). Mitigation: keep one warm process per MCP server; fall back to cold start if it dies.
- Token cost of base64 PNGs is real. Default to thumbnails for full-deck, full-DPI for single-slide. Document in tool description.
- Image generation can fail in headless container envs. Surface specific errors (Code:'libreoffice_unavailable', 'imagemagick_unavailable') with Fix.Kind:'install_dependency'.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] render_slide_image returns a valid base64 PNG that decodes to the requested dimensions for at least 3 example decks across 2 templates.
- [ ] render_deck_thumbnails on a 50-slide deck returns under 30s on a warm server.
- [ ] Tool descriptions in MCP advertise density tradeoffs and base64 cost.
- [ ] skill-info enumerates the new tools (coordinate with tfvv).
- [ ] Failure mode for missing LibreOffice surfaces structured error, not raw stderr.
- [ ] Tests: golden image hash comparison on at least 2 templates.

Found by: agent-native-reviewer + codex-rescue follow-up audit 2026-05-01. Highest impact item neither parity audit covered.
close_reason: Implemented render_slide_image and render_deck_thumbnails MCP tools with internal/render package

title: feature: MCP preview_presentation_plan tool — return fully resolved generation plan without rendering
description:
Validation today stops at template checks + optional fit-report sampling (cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:656-665), but generation performs additional resolution work: auto-layout selection from content mix, virtual placeholder remapping, pattern expansion, shape-grid virtual layout resolution (cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go:530-566, 596-643, 1701-1799). An agent cannot ask 'what layout/body slot/bounds will you actually use?' without paying a full generation round-trip and parsing the resulting PPTX.

This forces trial-and-error on every non-trivial deck. Codex audit identified this as the single most impactful gap — the bold suggestion.

## Tool surface

`preview_presentation_plan(presentation, template_name) → {\
  resolved_slides: [{\
    layout_id, layout_id_source: 'inline'|'auto'|'fallback',\
    placeholders: [{name, resolved_id, resolved_geometry: {x,y,w,h}}],\
    expanded_patterns: [{name, cells_after_expansion}],\
    shape_grid_resolution: {virtual_layout_used, geometry},\
    applied_defaults: {table_style, cell_style},\
    pre_generation_findings: [...]\
  }],\
  warnings: [...],\
  errors: [...]\
}`

## Implementation pointers

The codebase already has the pieces in:
- cmd/json2pptx/dry_run.go:244-421 (validateSlidesAgainstTemplate)
- cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go:530-643 (convertPresentationSlides)
- cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go:1701-1799 (autoMapPlaceholders, virtual layout)
- cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go:1500-1555 (slide_type inference)

Lift these into a new function pipeline.ResolvePlan(input, templateLayouts) that returns the resolved plan struct and is shared by both `generate_presentation` (which then renders) and the new `preview_presentation_plan` (which stops at the plan).

This bead also closes the round-trip identified in al8r (validate fit_report parity) at a structural level — once preview returns the plan, validate can call collectFitFindings against the resolved plan instead of the raw input, and structural fit findings naturally come along.

## Why this is worth it

Currently the agent loop is: validate → generate → parse PPTX → fix → repeat. With this, the loop becomes: preview → fix → generate-once. Codex justification: 'Anything smaller keeps the current multi-tool, multi-round-trip loop intact.'

Found by: codex-rescue audit 2026-05-01 (THE bold suggestion). Top-4 friction in the rank order. Companion to al8r and rs8y.
close_reason: Implemented: preview_presentation_plan MCP tool that resolves the full generation plan (layout selection, placeholder mapping, pattern expansion, shape_grid virtual layout) without rendering a PPTX. Includes fit_findings by default.

title: bug: discovery surface is split and partially stale (skill-info vs list_templates vs README's nonexistent list-templates)
description:
CLI advertises `skill-info` as the metadata entrypoint (cmd/json2pptx/main.go:73-95). examples/README.md describes a nonexistent `json2pptx list-templates` command (examples/README.md:73-77). MCP discovery is split across `list_templates`, `get_data_format_hints`, `get_chart_capabilities`, and `get_diagram_capabilities` (mcp.go:189-212, 535-581) — but `skill-info` already bundles all four (cmd/json2pptx/skill_info.go:22-31, 118-130, 214-228).

Agents end up calling 3-4 tools to assemble what one already returns, and follow stale README guidance into commands that don't exist.

## Implementation direction

- Define skill-info as THE canonical discovery surface; the four MCP tools become thin facades over the same underlying data.
- Either remove or alias the README's `list-templates` (likely add as alias for `skill-info templates` if backward compat is desired).
- Add cross-references: each of the four narrow MCP tools should mention skill-info in its description as the bundled alternative.
- Sweep examples/README.md for other stale CLI references.
- Coordinates with we1y (closed) MCP-tool-description doc work.

Found by: codex-rescue audit 2026-05-01. Top-3 friction.
close_reason: Fixed: examples/README.md referenced nonexistent list-templates CLI command (now points to skill-info --mode list). Added cross-references in get_data_format_hints, get_chart_capabilities, and get_diagram_capabilities MCP tool descriptions pointing to list_templates as the canonical bundled discovery tool.

title: bug: two JSON dialects coexist with no canonical authoring form
description:
examples/basic-deck.json uses typed fields (text_value) and canonical placeholder IDs (title/body) — examples/basic-deck.json:6-17, 29-38. examples/README.md still teaches legacy `value` fields and raw template names like 'Title 1' and 'Content Placeholder 2' — examples/README.md:45-67, 83-90. Parser explicitly accepts both forms (cmd/json2pptx/json_schema.go:141-167).

Consequence: agents seeing the contract for the first time guess wrong about half the time, and golden examples disagree about which form is preferred. The legacy form interacts badly with auto-layout selection because raw template names skip the placeholder-ID portability layer.

## Implementation direction

- Pick one canonical form: `text_value`-typed fields with portable placeholder IDs (title, subtitle, body, body_2). This is what basic-deck.json and skill-info already advertise.
- Demote legacy `value` + raw 'Title 1' usage to a single 'Compatibility' appendix in examples/README.md with a clear 'do not use for new decks' banner.
- skill-info `get_data_format_hints` should emit a deprecation note for legacy form so agents see it inline.
- Sweep all examples/*.json that still use legacy form and update — or carve them into examples/legacy/ to make the split structural.
- Validate emits informational finding when legacy form is detected: Code:'legacy_authoring_form', Fix:{Kind:'rewrite_field', Params:{from:'value', to:'text_value'}}.

Found by: codex-rescue audit 2026-05-01. Top-2 friction.
close_reason: Implemented: canonical form enforcement — README updated to show typed fields and portable placeholder IDs, legacy form compatibility appendix added, validation emits legacy_authoring_form finding with rewrite_field fix, skill-info deprecations field added

title: feature: MCP tools should accept structured object parameters, not JSON-as-escaped-string
description:
Today MCP `generate_presentation` takes `json_input` as a string (cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:139-186), `validate_input` does the same, and pattern tools require `values`, `overrides`, and `cell_overrides` as separate JSON strings (mcp.go:214-229, 709-751). Every authoring step requires double-serialization. Quoting failures are common, partial-input reuse across calls is awkward, and many MCP clients have to wrap+unwrap.

## Implementation direction

- Add object-typed siblings on each affected tool: `presentation` (object) alongside `json_input` (string), `values_object` alongside `values`, etc.
- If both forms are passed, error with patterns.ValidationError{Code:'ambiguous_input', Fix:{Kind:'use_one_of', Params:{allowed:['presentation','json_input']}}}.
- Keep string forms working for one minor version (compatibility), then deprecate via skill-info.
- Tool descriptions in MCP must declare the new shape — wire into we1y-class doc updates.

Found by: codex-rescue audit 2026-05-01 (independent review). Top-1 friction in the agent-UX rank order.
close_reason: Implemented object-typed parameter siblings for all MCP tools that accept JSON-as-string: generate_presentation, validate_input, score_deck get presentation object param; validate_pattern and expand_pattern get values_object, overrides_object, cell_overrides_object, callout_object. Ambiguous input (both forms) returns structured error with ambiguous_input code and use_one_of fix.

title: feature: per-template settings file with gated MCP write tools (table_styles + cell_styles V1)
description:
Persistent per-template settings store so agents can register named custom styles once and reference them by name from deck JSON, instead of repeating the full defaults block in every deck.

## Storage

Sibling YAML next to each .pptx: templates/<name>.settings.yaml. One file per template — discoverable, version-controllable, atomic write via temp-file + rename, path-traversal contained (writes only land in templates/<known-template-name>.settings.yaml).

## Schema (V1 — table_styles + cell_styles only)

```yaml
template: midnight-blue
table_styles:
  our-brand-table:
    style_id: '{2D5ABB26-...}'   # or @template-default
    use_table_style: true
    header_row: true
    banded_rows: false
cell_styles:
  callout-card:
    fill: { color: accent1, alpha: 0.15 }
    border: { color: accent1, weight: 1.5 }
    text_align: center
```

## Resolution order at generation time (most-specific wins)

1. Inline `style` on table/shape
2. Deck-level `defaults.table_style` / `defaults.cell_style`
3. Named lookup — JSON references `style: 'our-brand-table'` → resolved from settings file
4. Template-default sentinel `@template-default`

## MCP tools

- `list_template_settings(template_name) → {table_styles, cell_styles}`
- `register_template_setting(template_name, kind, name, definition) → {written, path}` — idempotent
- `delete_template_setting(template_name, kind, name) → {removed}`

## Write authority — GATED

Writes default OFF. Opt-in via env `JSON2PPTX_ALLOW_SETTINGS_WRITE=1` (and/or CLI flag `-allow-settings-write` for the MCP server). When disabled, register/delete return error code `settings_write_disabled` with a Fix.Kind:'enable_flag' pointing at the env var. Read (`list_template_settings`) is always allowed. Rationale: in multi-tenant deployments a malicious or buggy agent could otherwise persist garbage settings affecting all later decks across all sessions.

## Validation on register

`register_template_setting` MUST validate the proposed setting before persisting:
- For table_styles: run the same style_id resolver work as eq3k bead — reject unknown GUIDs with patterns.ValidationError{Code:'unknown_table_style_id', Fix:{Kind:'use_one_of', Params:{available, did_you_mean}}}.
- For cell_styles: validate fill.color resolves through theme color resolver.

This means eq3k (style_id LookupTableStyleID) is a soft prerequisite — the resolver should land first or be co-implemented.

## Out of scope for V1 (file as follow-ups, do NOT bundle)

- Custom layouts (would require template binary editing — separate domain)
- Color palette / theme overrides
- Per-template pattern definitions
- Font overrides
- User-scoped settings at `~/.json2pptx/` — only template-dir scope in V1

## Implementation pointers

- New package: internal/templatesettings/ with Load(templateDir, templateName), Save(...), Delete(...).
- Integrate resolution into cmd/json2pptx/defaults.go applyDefaults pipeline as a new layer between deck defaults and template-default sentinel.
- MCP tool registration in cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go alongside existing list_templates / get_data_format_hints.
- Tests must cover: gated-off rejection, validation rejection of bad style_id, atomic write under concurrent registers, named-lookup resolution at all 4 priority levels.

Found by: agent-native-reviewer + codex-rescue audits 2026-05-01. User-confirmed scope: gated write, table+cell only.
close_reason: Implemented: per-template settings YAML sidecar files with list/register/delete MCP tools, write-gating via JSON2PPTX_ALLOW_SETTINGS_WRITE=1, style_id and cell fill color validation, named style resolution in generation pipeline (priority 3), and named_style field on grid cells

title: Harden visual QA output contract with schema validation and repair
description:
## Why
The current visual QA system asks the model for a JSON array but then trusts any parseable array of objects. That means enum drift, empty fields, or hallucinated categories can pass through as if they were valid findings. For agent workflows this is fail-open behavior: the model can be wrong in a structured-looking way and the system will still treat it as success.

## Scope
- Tighten the prompt contract for system and per-slide prompts.
- Make parseFindings schema-aware.
- Reject unknown severities/categories and empty description/location values.
- Add one bounded repair pass that echoes validation failures back to the model.
- Surface structured INVALID_MODEL_OUTPUT diagnostics when repair still fails.

## Implementation Notes
- Keep the list of valid severities and categories centralized in code, not only in prompt text.
- Consider carrying parser violations on SlideResult in a machine-readable field rather than plain Error text alone.
- Preserve raw output in truncated/debug form to help investigate recurring model drift.
- Ensure report aggregation does not silently ignore unknown severities anymore.

## Candidate Files
- internal/visualqa/prompts.go
- internal/visualqa/agent.go
- internal/visualqa/types.go
- internal/visualqa/agent_test.go

## References
- internal/visualqa/prompts.go:3-121
- internal/visualqa/agent.go:72-165
- internal/visualqa/agent.go:209-248
- internal/visualqa/types.go:1-77
design: Tighten the visual QA loop from prompt-only discipline to enforced contract validation. The parser should fail closed on malformed-but-parseable model output, optionally perform one repair pass using validation feedback, and record structured invalid-model-output diagnostics instead of silently accepting drift.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Visual QA findings are validated for allowed severity/category values and required non-empty fields. 2. Invalid-but-parseable model output is rejected rather than silently accepted. 3. One bounded repair/retry path exists for malformed model output, with tests. 4. When output is still invalid, the result contains structured invalid-model-output diagnostics plus truncated raw output for debugging. 5. Prompt/tests are updated with explicit contract examples.

title: Adopt structured diagnostics in MCP generate and validate
description:
## Why
The main MCP tools are the highest-value agent entrypoints, but they still use plain mcp.NewToolResultError strings for most user-fixable failures. Agents have to special-case tool-level text parsing here even though validate_pattern already proves the server can return structured diagnostics.

## Scope
- Apply the shared diagnostic model from go-slide-creator-6gzn to generate_presentation and validate_input.
- Standardize expected caller-fixable failures such as:
  - invalid JSON
  - missing required fields
  - enum validation failures
  - strict-fit failures
  - template resolution / template analysis failures when user-actionable
  - invalid slide specification / placeholder / layout validation failures
- Preserve compatibility for existing MCP clients.

## Implementation Notes
- Reuse the D10-style structured approach from cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go pattern validation instead of inventing a second MCP contract.
- Prefer additive rollout: preserve plain-text fallback and current error semantics while attaching machine-readable diagnostics.
- Keep a hard line between user-fixable diagnostics and true internal/runtime failures.
- Use existing structured sources where available:
  - patterns.ValidationError / splitValidationErrors
  - generator.GenerationResult.ValidationErrors
  - existing validate_input dryRunOutput fields

## Candidate Files
- cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go
- internal/api/mcp_encode.go
- cmd/json2pptx/mcp_parity_test.go
- cmd/json2pptx/mcp_patterns_test.go

## References
- cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:233-367
- cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:560-640
- cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:711-959
- internal/api/mcp_encode.go:11-48
design: Roll out the shared diagnostic model to caller-fixable MCP failures while preserving MCP transport semantics. Expected input/template/validation failures should become machine-readable without regressing existing clients that rely on IsError or text fallbacks. Internal/runtime faults should remain operational errors, not validation payloads.
acceptance_criteria: 1. generate_presentation and validate_input emit one consistent machine-readable diagnostic shape for caller-fixable failures. 2. Backward compatibility is preserved via text fallback and current MCP error-channel expectations. 3. Semantic validation errors, enum failures, template resolution failures, and invalid slide specification failures are covered by tests. 4. Internal marshal/runtime failures remain operational errors.

title: Agent diagnostics core for machine-readable server feedback
description:
## Why
Agent-facing surfaces in this repo currently expose multiple incompatible failure shapes. MCP generate/validate mostly return plain tool-error strings, HTTP has a stable outer error envelope but weak inner diagnostics, and pattern validation already has richer structured data. Before changing any public handler behavior, we need one internal diagnostic contract that can represent user-fixable issues consistently across transports.

## Scope
- Define a transport-neutral diagnostic type for expected caller-fixable failures.
- Include machine fields for code, message, path or field, and optional fix/details/severity.
- Add helpers that convert existing structured errors into the shared model.
- Keep this issue focused on shared types and helpers, not endpoint rollout.

## Implementation Notes
- Likely home: internal/api/errors or a sibling package dedicated to diagnostics.
- Promote existing structures where possible:
  - internal/patterns/errors.go ValidationError / FixSuggestion
  - internal/generator/slides.go GenerationResult.ValidationErrors
- Preserve raw cause text in details rather than flattening everything.
- Avoid transport-specific fields like HTTP status or MCP IsError in the core model.

## Candidate Files
- internal/api/errors/errors.go or new sibling package
- cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go (helper extraction only if needed)
- internal/patterns/errors.go
- internal/generator/slides.go

## References
- cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:233-367
- cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:560-640
- cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:711-959
- internal/api/errors/errors.go:11-21
- internal/patterns/errors.go:125-180
- internal/generator/slides.go:133-144
design: Create a transport-neutral diagnostic model reused by MCP and HTTP. Reuse existing structured sources like patterns.ValidationError and generator.ValidationErrors instead of inventing parallel ad hoc structs. Do not change transport semantics in this issue; establish types and conversion helpers first.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A shared diagnostic type exists with code/message/path-or-field and optional fix/details/severity. 2. Conversion helpers cover at least patterns.ValidationError plus one non-pattern validation source. 3. Unit tests cover joined-error splitting and JSON serialization stability. 4. No public HTTP or MCP contract changes are required to complete this issue.
close_reason: Implemented transport-neutral Diagnostic type with code/message/path/severity/fix/details fields. Added converters from patterns.ValidationError, FitFinding, joined errors, and plain warnings. Unit tests cover all converters, joined-error splitting, JSON serialization stability, and helper functions.

title: Fail fast in agent-facing tools with typed input diagnostics
description:
Context
Agent-facing MCP entrypoints still accept or surface several contract problems as plain strings or soft warnings. `handleGenerate` and `handleValidate` unmarshal request JSON directly, unknown keys are collected as strings after parse time, and many early exits return free-form error text. Pattern validation is only partially structured: `validate_pattern` returns structured errors from `pat.Validate(...)`, but parse/unmarshal failures still fall back to string errors.

Problem
Agents do not get consistent, actionable feedback when input is malformed. Typos, unknown keys, trailing junk, enum mistakes, and invalid nested payloads should fail at the boundary with path/code/fix metadata instead of letting execution continue or returning ad hoc text.

Scope
Use the shared diagnostic contract to make MCP tools fail fast on input-contract violations and return typed diagnostics for both request-shape and domain validation failures. Preserve compatibility where necessary, but optimize the MCP agent path for strictness and actionable feedback.
design:
Implementation notes
- Reject malformed JSON decisively, including trailing data where applicable.
- Promote unknown-key and enum diagnostics into typed MCP errors for agent-facing tools instead of string warnings.
- Convert parse/validation failures into shared diagnostics with `path`, `code`, `message`, and `fix` fields.
- Normalize pattern argument failures so `values`, `overrides`, `cell_overrides`, and `callout` all use the same structured shape.

Key references
- `cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:233-327`
- `cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:559-633`
- `cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:851-959`
- `cmd/json2pptx/unknown_keys.go:116-118`
- `cmd/json2pptx/unknown_keys_check.go`
- `cmd/json2pptx/enum_validation.go`
acceptance_criteria:
- `generate_presentation`, `validate_input`, `validate_pattern`, and `expand_pattern` return typed diagnostics for malformed or invalid input instead of free-form error strings.
- Unknown keys and invalid enum values are machine-identifiable with stable codes and paths.
- Representative tests cover malformed JSON, unknown key, unknown enum, invalid cell override key, and unsupported callout cases.
- Generation does not proceed when boundary validation has already proven the request contract is wrong.
notes:
Consensus from the debate
Be strict by default on agent-facing MCP tools. If a compatibility escape hatch is needed later, add it explicitly rather than keeping the default ambiguous.
close_reason: Implemented typed diagnostics for all agent-facing MCP tools: generate_presentation, validate_input, validate_pattern, expand_pattern, show_pattern, and list_templates. All error paths now return structured diagnostics with code/path/message/fix instead of plain text. Added strictUnmarshalJSON to reject trailing data. Promoted unknown-key warnings to errors on the MCP agent path. Added 14 regression tests.

title: Introduce shared agent diagnostics and MCP result helpers
description:
Context
The repo already has rich structured validation primitives in `internal/patterns/errors.go` and `internal/patterns/fit_finding.go`, but MCP responses still collapse most results into JSON text blobs or free-form error strings. `internal/api/mcp_encode.go` only marshals bytes, and `cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go` mixes `api.MarshalMCPResponse(...)` on success with many `mcp.NewToolResultError(...)` calls on failure.

Problem
Agents cannot rely on transport-native structure today. Successful tool calls require reparsing text JSON, and failed tool calls lose path/code/fix metadata entirely. That blocks consistent machine interpretation and makes follow-up tool use brittle.

Scope
Add a shared diagnostic/result contract that can be reused across MCP, HTTP, and visual QA, then add MCP helpers that emit both fallback text and `StructuredContent`, while preserving `IsError=true` for failing tool calls. Keep the abstraction minimal: shared diagnostic primitives plus transport helpers, not a large generic framework.
design:
Implementation notes
- Add a shared diagnostic type with at least: `severity`, `code`, `message`, `path`, `fix`, `source`, and optional metadata.
- Add MCP helpers that return `*mcp.CallToolResult` with `StructuredContent` populated and JSON text fallback preserved for backward compatibility.
- Support structured error results with `IsError=true` instead of `mcp.NewToolResultError(...)` string-only payloads.
- Keep the new primitives decoupled from any one endpoint so convert/patterns/visual QA can reuse them later.

Key references
- `internal/api/mcp_encode.go:11-25`
- `cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:233-408`
- `cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:559-642`
- `internal/patterns/errors.go:1-120`
- `internal/patterns/fit_finding.go:1-34`
acceptance_criteria:
- There is one shared diagnostic/result package or module with documented fields and JSON tags.
- MCP helpers emit structured content on success and error while preserving text fallback.
- At least one representative failing MCP tool result sets `IsError=true` and still carries machine-readable JSON or structured content.
- Unit tests cover success and error helpers, including fallback text and structured content presence.
notes:
Why this first
Downstream work should build on one canonical contract instead of inventing slightly different envelopes in each subsystem.
close_reason: Added MCP result helpers (MCPSuccessResult, MCPDiagnosticsError, MCPSimpleError) in internal/api/mcp_result.go. These bridge the existing diagnostics package to mcp-go CallToolResult with StructuredContent + text fallback. Converted handleGenerate success path to emit StructuredContent and enum validation errors to use structured diagnostics with IsError=true. Unit tests cover success, error, fix round-trip, and summary.

title: agent-native: align HTTP convert/pattern diagnostics with MCP repair hints
description:
Problem
The HTTP API exposes the same core capabilities as MCP for conversion and pattern operations, but its failure payloads are materially less usable by agents. `internal/api/patterns.go:75-167` returns raw `err.Error()` strings for pattern validation/expand, even though MCP already has `splitValidationErrors(...)` and fix-aware payloads in `cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:711-959`. `internal/api/convert.go:184-248` also collapses JSON parse failures into `INVALID_REQUEST` + "Failed to parse request body" instead of a syntax-aware machine-readable diagnostic.

Why this matters
The pattern spec explicitly requires validate parity across CLI/MCP/HTTP and a structured error shape (`docs/PATTERN_LIBRARY_SPEC.md:49-50`), but the HTTP endpoints currently drift from that contract. Agents using HTTP cannot reliably determine which field failed, whether a fix exists, or whether the error is a bad request vs bad JSON.

Scope
- Reuse the same typed validation/diagnostic structs across HTTP pattern validation and expansion.
- Improve `POST /api/v1/convert` parse/validation failures so JSON syntax problems use the correct code and include actionable location data when available.
- Normalize ad hoc `details map[string]any` usage into a documented, predictable structure for agent-visible validation failures.

Out of scope
- Reworking successful HTTP response bodies for convert/download/template listing.
- Hiding internal server errors beyond what is already intentionally opaque.
design: Build on the shared diagnostic work instead of forking a second schema. Preserve the existing top-level HTTP error envelope where practical, but make the contents typed instead of stuffing heterogeneous data into `details`. Avoid leaking internal stack traces or implementation-specific generator errors to clients.

title: agent-native: preserve structured MCP diagnostics without breaking failure semantics
description:
Problem
Several agent-facing MCP handlers still collapse domain failures into plain `mcp.NewToolResultError(...)` strings, which makes them hard for models to interpret and impossible to repair against deterministically. The strongest examples are `generate_presentation` in `cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:233-405`, `validate_input` request parsing in `cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:559-643`, and the pattern discovery/expand paths in `cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:811-1033`.

Why this matters
The repo already has richer machine-readable diagnostics in some places: `validate_pattern` returns structured `{ok, errors[]}` entries with field/code/fix data (`cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:711-959`), and the CLI/JSON output types already expose `validation_errors`, `fit_findings`, and `quality` (`cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go:113-150`). The current MCP failure paths fall back to opaque strings instead of preserving those structures.

Scope
- Introduce a shared MCP result helper that can emit machine-readable JSON for recoverable/domain failures while preserving MCP failure semantics (`isError=true` or equivalent).
- Cover the reviewed MCP handlers first: `generate_presentation`, `validate_input`, `show_pattern`, `expand_pattern`, and the capability/data-hint helpers where response formatting is inconsistent.
- Keep success payloads backward-compatible at the root shape; do not wrap every successful response in a new envelope.

Out of scope
- Reworking unrelated CLI output formats.
- Adding new agent workflows or orchestration logic.
design: Use a shared helper rather than open-coding JSON/text/error decisions in each handler. Prefer additive shapes that reuse existing structs (`patterns.ValidationError`, fit findings, quality output) over inventing a brand-new agent protocol. Avoid a blanket `ok/data/error` wrapper for all success responses because that would create unnecessary client churn.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Recoverable/domain failures from the reviewed MCP tools return JSON that includes a stable error code, message, and structured fields such as `field`, `path`, or `fix` when available.
2. MCP clients still observe tool failure semantics on those failures instead of silently treating them as success.
3. `handleGetChartCapabilities`, `handleGetDiagramCapabilities`, and similar helpers use the same response marshalling path as other MCP success responses.
4. Tests cover at least: invalid JSON, missing template, unknown pattern, invalid pattern values, and generation refusal/strict-fit failure.
notes: Key evidence: `internal/api/mcp_encode.go:11-25` already centralizes response marshalling but only for success payloads; `cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:535-556` bypasses it for capability helpers; `docs/PATTERN_LIBRARY_SPEC.md:49-50` promises parity + structured errors that the current generate/show/expand paths do not fully deliver.
close_reason: Migrated all MCP handlers to use shared api.MCPSuccessResult() for success (adds StructuredContent) and api.MCPSimpleError() for errors (adds structured diagnostics with IsError=true). Covers generate, validate, list_templates, show/expand/validate/list patterns, capability helpers, list_icons, and table_density_guide. Added 18 tests verifying StructuredContent on success and error paths.

title: bug: fontcache nil collapses FitResult to 'fits perfectly' — fail-fast at boot
description:
internal/textfit/textfit.go:120-124 and measure.go:42-48 treat a nil fontcache.Get() as FitResult{} / {Fits:true}. Any downstream fit-check on that font silently reports 'fits' even when nothing was measured. This is a boot-time invariant violation, not a feedback gap — the correct fix is log.Fatal at cmd/json2pptx/main.go init if fontcache fails to initialize, not an agent-visible hint mid-slide.

## Scope
- Validate fontcache initialization at process start (main.go init + api/mcp entry points)
- Panic or log.Fatal with actionable message if required fonts fail to resolve
- In textfit, change the nil path to return (FitResult{}, error) so callers can distinguish 'unknown' from 'fits'

## Why P1
Hides a whole class of font-misconfiguration bugs — decks look fine in dev, break in prod. Consensus from advocate/devil's-advocate debate on 2026-04-24: DA argued this is mis-categorized as an agent-feedback issue; advocate agreed in synthesis.

## Acceptance
- Process fails fast on missing fontcache at startup in all three entry points (CLI generate, API server, MCP server)
- textfit.MeasureRun returns error on nil-cache rather than silently succeeding
- Test: start binary with stripped fontcache → non-zero exit with clear message
