title: Detect placeholder overflow with three-condition autofit-aware gate
description:
Agents currently cannot tell if body text overran frame; rendering is the only signal. Three-condition gate prevents false-positive spam on templates relying on PowerPoint normAutofit.

## What changes
- New internal/generator/placeholder_overflow.go (~180 LOC)
- Walk placeholder shapes post-textfit measurement
- Emit ONLY when ALL THREE conditions hold:
  1. measured_h / frame_h > 1.15 (not any overshoot)
  2. placeholder autofit is 'none' OR template bodyPr has neither normAutofit nor spAutoFit
  3. Required lines at minimum autofit font size > frame-allocated lines
- Uses read-only measurement from internal/textfit
- Does NOT modify internal/pipeline/overflow.go (body-only contract preserved)
- Walker in internal/generator/, NOT internal/textfit/ (textfit stays measurement-only)

## Acceptance
- Unit test: overshoot 10% -> no finding (below 1.15)
- Unit test: overshoot 20% + normAutofit present -> no finding (autofit handles)
- Unit test: overshoot 20% + autofit none + lines-at-min fits -> no finding
- Unit test: all three conditions hit -> finding emitted
- Code: 'placeholder_overflow'; action 'shrink_or_split'

## Risk
Three-condition logic drifts from autofit engine. Mitigation: share minFontSizeEMU constant; test uses same fixture as autofit tests.

## Depends on
Bead: Introduce fitFinding type embedding patterns.ValidationError
close_reason: Implemented three-condition placeholder overflow detector in internal/generator/placeholder_overflow.go. Added MeasureHeight to textfit for 100%-scale height measurement. Added ErrCodePlaceholderOverflow to patterns. Six test cases cover all acceptance criteria (below threshold, normAutofit present, fits-at-min, all conditions hit, empty input, spAutoFit).

title: Detect slide-bounds overflow for JSON-authored shapes (center threshold)
description:
Off-slide content is silent data loss; agents need detection without rendering. Center-based threshold eliminates the 1-EMU rounding false-positive class while preserving warn-mode parity.

## What changes
- New internal/generator/bounds_check.go (~90 LOC)
- Walk JSON-authored shapes only. Skip shapes inherited from layout master.
- Skip shapes tagged role: background or role: decor
- Emit FitFinding when shape CENTER falls outside slide rect (not any corner — 1 EMU past edge is rounding)
- Runs at warn AND strict. Not gated by autofit.
- Slide dims from template.ParseSlideDimensions

## Acceptance
- Unit test: shape with corner 1 EMU off-edge but center inside -> no finding
- Unit test: shape with center outside slide rect -> finding emitted at warn
- Unit test: role: decor shape fully off-slide -> skipped
- Code: 'slide_bounds_overflow'; action 'refuse' (strict) or 'shrink_or_split' (warn)

## Risk
Role tags not universally applied. Mitigation: document convention; default (no role) = treated as content = checked.

## Depends on
Bead: Introduce fitFinding type embedding patterns.ValidationError
close_reason: Implemented bounds_check.go with center-based slide-bounds overflow detection. Added ErrCodeSlideBoundsOverflow error code, DetectSlideBoundsOverflow function, and 8 unit tests covering: corner-off-center-inside (no false positive), center-outside, role=decor/background skip, normal in-bounds, vertical overflow, no-role=content, and zero-dimension guard.

title: Detect footer collisions on shape_grid + layout-declared footers only
description:
Agents need programmatic signal when authored shapes intrude into footer reserved area; today only visual QA catches it. Scoped to avoid false positives on decorative layout placeholders.

## What changes
- New internal/generator/footer_collision.go (~120 LOC)
- Walk shape_grid JSON-authored shapes per slide
- Only fire when slide's resolved layout DECLARES a footer placeholder (check via internal/template layout inspection). Never fire on heuristic fallback in generator/footer.go.
- Never fire for placeholders inherited from layout master
- Emit FitFinding when authored shape bbox intersects footer rect
- Tri-state via existing strict_fit param: strict -> refuse + finding; warn -> emit finding only; off -> skip

## Acceptance
- Unit test: layout with declared footer + intruding shape_grid cell -> finding at warn, refusal at strict
- Unit test: same intrusion on layout WITHOUT declared footer -> no finding
- Unit test: placeholder inherited from master (not JSON-authored) -> no finding
- Code: 'footer_collision'; action 'refuse' (strict) or 'review' (warn)

## Risk
Misidentifying layout-inherited placeholders as JSON-authored. Mitigation: source tracking exists in slide_preparation; test both paths explicitly.

## Depends on
Bead: Introduce fitFinding type embedding patterns.ValidationError
close_reason: Implemented DetectFooterCollision detector with tri-state strict_fit (off/warn/strict), layout-declared-footer gate, decorative role exclusion, and full test coverage

title: Add single MCP response encoder with env-gated compact mode
description:
Route all 8 MCP marshal sites through one helper so compact mode is a one-line flip; avoid per-call drift. ~45% payload reduction with zero schema-break risk.

## What changes
- New internal/api/mcp_encode.go (~40 LOC). Export MarshalMCPResponse(v any) ([]byte, error)
- When MCP_COMPACT_RESPONSES=1, use json.Marshal (no indent) and respect struct omitempty on SCALARS ONLY (arrays/maps keep []/{})
- Audit 8 call sites in cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go, swap to helper
- Full keys, no renaming (research consensus)

## Acceptance
- All 8 sites use the helper (grep assertion in test)
- With env unset: output byte-identical to pre-change (golden test)
- With env set: size reduction >=35% on examples/basic-deck.json round-trip
- Empty arrays still serialize as []

## Risk
Accidentally dropping omitempty on a slice breaks schema. Mitigation: lint rule + golden test comparing key sets before/after on fixture responses.
close_reason: Implemented: single MarshalMCPResponse helper in internal/api/mcp_encode.go; all 8 MCP marshal sites in mcp.go now use it; MCP_COMPACT_RESPONSES=1 enables no-indent mode; full test coverage

title: Introduce fitFinding type embedding patterns.ValidationError
description:
Unify fit-signal shape across footer, bounds, and placeholder overflow without polluting the generic validation envelope. Embedding (Go composition) gives unification without leaking fit-domain fields into the shared type.

## What changes
- New file internal/patterns/fit_finding.go (~60 LOC). Exports:
  - type FitFinding struct { patterns.ValidationError; Action string; Measured *Extent; Allowed *Extent; OverflowRatio float64 }
  - type Extent struct { WidthEMU, HeightEMU int64 }
  - func ActionRank(action string) int  ('refuse' > 'shrink_or_split' > 'review' > 'info')
- No changes to ValidationError itself.

## Acceptance
- FitFinding marshals with all ValidationError fields at top level (embedding flattens)
- ActionRank unit-tested with 4 actions + unknown fallback
- No changes to ValidationError

## Risk
JSON field collision between embedded and outer struct. Mitigation: go vet catches; explicit test asserting marshaled key set.
close_reason: Implemented FitFinding type embedding patterns.ValidationError with Extent, ActionRank, and full test coverage

title: Introduce TableStyleResolver interface and @template-default sentinel
description:
Allow JSON authors to opt into the template's declared table style without a flag-day default swap. Keeps the hardcoded engine-default GUID as the fallback forever.

## What changes
- internal/generator/table_style_resolver.go (new, ~40 lines):
  type TableStyleResolver interface { ResolveTableStyleID(authored string) string }
- internal/template/template.go (+~20 lines): *Template implements ResolveTableStyleID
  - authored == '@template-default' -> first declared GUID from index if present, else engine-default
  - authored starts with '{' and is in index -> return as-is
  - authored non-empty but unresolvable -> return verbatim, let downstream validation warn
  - empty -> engine-default
- Table generation call site (~5 lines): route style_id through the resolver

## Acceptance
- Existing decks with no style_id: identical PPTX bytes (golden test)
- Existing decks with explicit style_id GUID: identical output
- New style_id '@template-default' with declared styles: resolves to first declared GUID
- '@template-default' without declared styles: resolves to engine-default (graceful degradation)
- Resolver interface has exactly one method; table code depends on interface, not *Template

## Risk
First-declared ordering within a single template is deterministic (same file, same parse). Test asserts stable pick across 100 parses.

## Depends on
TBL-01 (style index)
close_reason: Implemented TableStyleResolver interface in generator package, ResolveTableStyleID on template.Reader with @template-default sentinel support, threaded resolver through PopulateTableInShape, comprehensive tests for all resolution paths including stability across 100 parses

title: json2pptx validate --fit-report=path NDJSON: per-cell measurement using patterns.ValidationError envelope
description:
Wire MeasureRun (go-slide-creator-dx8k) into the validate subcommand to produce a per-cell fit report that the agent can consume to self-correct. Reuse existing patterns.ValidationError envelope (go-slide-creator-a3s3) — DO NOT design a new envelope.

## What it does
`json2pptx validate input.json --fit-report=path.json` walks every:
- table cell (in content layouts AND inside shape_grid cells)
- shape_grid shape-cell containing text

…and calls MeasureRun(cell.text, cell.font, cell.width_emu, max_lines_for_row_height). Emits one NDJSON line per problematic cell using the existing ValidationError shape:

```json
{"code": "fit_overflow",
 "path": "slides[3].content[0].rows[6][4]",
 "message": "text needs 3 lines @ 10pt; cell allows 2",
 "fix": {"kind": "split_at_row", "row": 8},
 "binding_dimension": "height",
 "required_pt": 11.5,
 "allocated_pt": 10,
 "wrap_lines": 3,
 "action": "unfittable"}
```

## Stable error codes (enumerate in internal/patterns/errors.go)
- ErrCodeFitOverflow — text exceeds cell width × maxLines
- ErrCodeDensityExceeded — table rows*cols beyond TDR ceiling at given font (mechanical TDR check, no rendering)
- ErrCodeStackedTables — sibling tables in shape_grid with row_gap < 4pt
- ErrCodeDividerTooThin — divider shape height < 4% slide
- ErrCodeHexFillNonBrand — same code as the dry_run warning (go-slide-creator-55z5)

## fix.kind enum
- split_at_row | shrink_text | drop_column | use_semantic_color | increase_cell_height | reduce_text

## Output channels
- stderr (default human-readable summary table)
- --fit-report=PATH writes NDJSON
- --fit-report=- writes NDJSON to stdout
- Warning-only: validate exits 0 even with unfittable cells. Errors come via --strict-fit on generate (separate bead).

## Why this is the agent-recovery primitive
The reviewer + agent-native review identified that the agent needs THREE primitives to self-heal: (1) measurement [MeasureRun], (2) reshape [split_slide], (3) introspection of binding constraint. This bead delivers (1) + (3) — agent gets cell coordinate, binding dimension, and structured fix kind, so it can re-author without guessing.

## Acceptance criteria
- New flag --fit-report=PATH on validate subcommand
- Walks all tables (placeholder + shape_grid embedded) and all shape-cells with text
- Output uses patterns.ValidationError envelope (NOT a new shape)
- Stable error codes added to internal/patterns/errors.go
- fix.kind structured (not free-text); existing ValidationError.Fix promoted to {kind, params} retroactively (closes the 'free-text fix' debt — devil's advocate cleared this folding into B2)
- NDJSON: one line per finding, no array wrapping
- Unit tests: empty deck → empty report; deck with overflow → expected codes + paths
- Documentation in docs/ for the report schema
design: Consensus: B2 + B9 fold together. Don't design a new envelope; reuse a3s3's. Promoting Fix to {kind, params} is a small retroactive change since the field is internal. Both engineers agreed measurement-only, refusal lives in the strict-fit bead.
notes:
Files involved:
- cmd/json2pptx/validate.go:98-204 (existing structural validate)
- internal/patterns/errors.go:9-18 (existing error code enum to extend)
- internal/patterns/errors.go:50-78 (ValidationError + Fix free-text — promote to structured)
- internal/jsonschema/table.go (table schema — visit cells)
- internal/shapegrid/grid.go (shape-grid cells)
close_reason: Implemented --fit-report flag on validate subcommand. Promoted ValidationError.Fix from string to structured FixSuggestion{Kind, Params}. Added fit-report error codes (fit_overflow, density_exceeded, stacked_tables, divider_too_thin). Walker measures all table cells (content + shape_grid embedded) and shape text using MeasureRun. Outputs NDJSON with structured fix kinds. Comprehensive tests cover empty deck, no overflow, table overflow, density exceeded, shape grid text, embedded tables, NDJSON output, and text extraction.

title: Hex-fill warning in dry_run.go validateShapeFillColor (additive, no behavior change)
description:
cmd/json2pptx/dry_run.go:443-462 (validateShapeFillColor) accepts both #RRGGBB hex and scheme names without flagging hex usage. Skill Rule 12 says 'prefer semantic over hex' but the binary doesn't enforce it. This was a root cause of the PwC field report (mixed accent1 + #65686B on the same slide).

## Scope
- Emit a warning (slog.Warn or via existing dry-run report channel) when validateShapeFillColor encounters a hex value that is NOT in the brand-color allowlist (define a small allowlist constant — black, white, transparent — for things that are deliberately raw).
- Warning level only. NO refusal. NO behavior change to generation.
- Surface in dry-run JSON output as a structured warning entry (using the existing patterns.ValidationError envelope from go-slide-creator-a3s3 — code: 'hex_fill_non_brand', path: JSON-pointer, fix: 'use accent1/accent2/lt2/dk1 instead').

## Why P1, why now
Cheapest possible win. ~10-line change. Gives us telemetry on how often agent-authored decks use raw hex BEFORE we decide if/how to ban it harder. Both engineers agreed: ship this with the MeasureRun PR.

## Acceptance criteria
- validateShapeFillColor emits a warning for non-allowlist hex values
- Warning appears in dry-run --json output as a patterns.ValidationError-shaped entry
- New unit test: hex value triggers warning; semantic name does not; allowlisted hex (#000000, #FFFFFF) does not
- Existing tests still pass; no generation behavior change
notes:
Files:
- cmd/json2pptx/dry_run.go:443-462 (validateShapeFillColor — current state accepts hex silently)
- internal/patterns/errors.go:50-66 (ValidationError envelope from go-slide-creator-a3s3 — reuse this)
close_reason: Implemented hex-fill warning: validateShapeFillColor now emits structured patterns.ValidationError (code: hex_fill_non_brand) for non-allowlisted hex colors. Allowlist covers #000/#fff variants. Warning appears in dry-run JSON output as validation_warnings array. Unit tests cover scheme names, allowlisted hex, non-allowlisted hex, and empty values.

title: Extract pure MeasureRun(text, fontPt, widthEMU) primitive in internal/textfit
description:
The reviewer + research showed: textfit measurement is built (internal/textfit/textfit.go) but the useful primitive (per-run wrap with width budget) is private (wrapText, lines 271-307). Public surface is whole-paragraph Calculate() and binary-search MaxFontForWidth() — neither matches the per-cell measurement needed by tables and shape-grid cells.

## Scope
Add a new pure function in internal/textfit/:

```go
type RunMeasurement struct {
    Lines        int     // wrap line count at given width
    RequiredEMU  int64   // height EMU to render those lines at fontPt
    OverflowChars int    // chars that can't fit in (widthEMU × maxLines), 0 if fits
    Fits         bool    // shorthand: OverflowChars == 0
}

// MeasureRun measures text rendered at fontPt within widthEMU using the
// resolved font metrics. Pure function — no I/O, no mutation. Safe to call
// from any goroutine.
func MeasureRun(text string, fontName string, fontPt float64, widthEMU int64, maxLines int) RunMeasurement
```

Internally: factor the existing private wrapText helper into the new public function; existing Calculate() and MaxFontForWidth() refactored to call MeasureRun where useful, but their public signatures unchanged.

## Why this first
Every downstream item (--fit-report, schema density caps, structural smells, strict-fit, eval harness) depends on this primitive. Both engineers in debate ranked it P0/P1.

## Non-goals
- Do NOT change any existing rendering behavior. This is a pure refactor + public API addition.
- Do NOT call MeasureRun from table.go or shapegrid yet — those are separate beads.

## Acceptance criteria
- New exported MeasureRun in internal/textfit/textfit.go (or new measure.go file)
- Unit tests covering: short text fits 1 line; text > width wraps to N lines; text > maxLines reports OverflowChars > 0; multibyte (Japanese) text; empty string
- Existing Calculate() and MaxFontForWidth() still pass their golden tests bit-for-bit
- Pure: no slog, no os, no global state mutation
- Reviewer-verified: textfit.go:271-307 wrapText helper is now removed (or unexported via MeasureRun)
design: Per the reviewer: 'Extracting MeasureRun is closer to a small refactor than a one-line export.' Both senior engineers agreed this is P0/P1 and blocks B2/B5/B7/B8.
notes:
Files:
- internal/textfit/textfit.go:90 (Calculate — existing)
- internal/textfit/textfit.go:216 (MaxFontForWidth — existing reusable building block reviewer didn't credit)
- internal/textfit/textfit.go:271-307 (wrapText — currently private)
close_reason: Implemented MeasureRun in internal/textfit/measure.go with RunMeasurement struct. 11 unit tests covering: short text fits, wrapping, overflow beyond maxLines, multibyte CJK, empty string, zero width/font, unlimited/negative maxLines, height growth, purity. Existing Calculate/MaxFontForWidth tests pass unchanged. wrapText remains unexported, accessed publicly via MeasureRun.

title: Skill PR: Inline TDR Rule 20 + 'Two-tables-one-grid' + 'Hex-fill mix' anti-patterns + multiline cell counting
description:
External reviewer + AI engineer research showed the agent had the Table Density Reference (TDR) in skill but violated it because: (a) TDR was offloaded to 'json2pptx tables guide' subcommand (passive/optional/never executed), (b) ~8k tokens of context drift between skill load and table authoring, (c) rule-as-reference vs rule-as-imperative-checkpoint.

Fix the skill (no Go changes) by inlining the rules at end of Stage 2 — last things the model sees before generation.

## Changes to skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md

1. **New Rule 20 — TDR enforced inline:** MUST split if rows > 7 || cols > 6 || font_size < 9. Cross-link from existing line 149-151 'tables guide' pointer back to this rule.

2. **New Anti-pattern 'Two-tables-one-grid':** sibling tables in shape_grid with row_gap < 4pt or divider shape height < 4% of slide. Show good/bad JSON examples.

3. **New Anti-pattern 'Hex-fill mix':** any slide containing both `accent1`/`lt2`/`dk1` semantic fills AND non-brand `#RRGGBB` fills. Currently Rule 12 is permissive ('Prefer ... over hex'). Tighten to: hex allowed ONLY for brand-color allowlist; mixed-on-same-slide is forbidden.

4. **Multiline cell counting:** explicit rule that a table cell containing \n or comma-list with ≥3 items counts as N rows where N = max(line_count, comma_items+1). Apply this BEFORE the rows>7 check.

5. **Final pre-emit checklist (recency reorder):** end Stage 2 with: '(1) every table rows × cols ≤ TDR ceiling; (2) every fill is semantic except brand-color allowlist; (3) no sibling shapes with computed gap < 4pt.'

6. **Refusal phrasings:** teach exact wording, e.g. 'This table needs N rows; per Rule 20 I cannot fit 7×6 — emitting split_slide.' Models reliably parrot taught refusals.

## Why ship without binary changes first
Devil's advocate position (lean): A1+A5 alone get ~60% of the win at ~5% of the cost. Run for 1-2 weeks, gather post-skill telemetry from existing slog warnings and dry-run reports, THEN decide the binary scope. Skill is reversible in 5 minutes if it overfires.

## Acceptance criteria
- skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md updated with Rule 20, two new anti-patterns, multiline counting rule, recency-reordered final checklist
- Existing line 149-151 'tables guide' pointer updated to cross-link Rule 20
- Existing Rule 12 (color preference) tightened to ban mixed-hex-and-semantic
- A 'good vs bad' JSON example exists for each new anti-pattern
- No Go changes
design: Decision: file as ONE bead (not 5), because skill edits compose and need a coherent rewrite. Folding A6/A7/A8 (refusal phrasings, recency reorder, mid-gen self-check) here — they are skill polish, not separate mechanisms.

- skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md:120 — Rule 12 (hex-soft, needs tightening)
- skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md:137 — Rule 17 is unrelated footer trap; new TDR rule must be Rule 20
- skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md:149-151 — current 'tables guide' pointer that needs cross-link

Already-done prereqs: go-slide-creator-itiw (TDR moved to 'json2pptx tables guide' CLI).

title: EPIC: Agent-native textfit + density validation (post-PwC field report)
description:
Post-production review of an agent-authored deck (PwC, 2026-04-22) surfaced four root causes that the current binary+skill stack does not catch:

1. Slide B violated Table Density Reference: 7×5 rows × font 7pt vs the 10-11pt / 6-col ceiling. Agent had the rule (in skill) and broke it.
2. Stacked tables with 2%-height divider shapes — unnamed anti-pattern. Each table loses ~40% of vertical budget to its sibling.
3. Multiline \n cells + 40+ char prose cells in cols 4-5 cannot be measured by the agent — only the binary can do per-column glyph advance.
4. Inconsistent divider fills (#65686B hex vs accent1 semantic) on the same slide — skill mandates semantic but doesn't enforce.

External reviewer + 3-agent research pass (repo-research-analyst, agent-native-reviewer, ai-engineer) + senior Go engineer debate (advocate / devil's advocate) reached consensus on a phased rollout.

This epic tracks the rollout. See child issues for the 14 individual deliverables across 4 PRs.

## Phasing
- PR1 (P1, 1-2 days): skill rules — TDR/anti-pattern/multiline/hex (1 bead)
- PR2 (P1, 1 week): MeasureRun extraction + fit-report NDJSON + hex warning (3 beads, additive only — no behavior change)
- PR3 (P2, 1-2 weeks): graduated --strict-fit + layered table refusal + structural smells + MCP parity (4 beads)
- PR4 (P2, 1 week): split_slide envelope + minimal eval harness (2 beads)
- PR5 (P3, deferred): shapegrid migration + pattern density caps + fix loop + measure_text MCP (4 beads)
notes: Sources: external reviewer feedback received 2026-04-23; closed beads go-slide-creator-2g0s, itiw, uaa, a3s3 are prerequisites already shipped.
close_reason: All 13 child beads completed across PRs 1-4. Only kdc1 (shapegrid heuristic migration) remains deferred as P3 per design, gated on eval harness baseline + 2 weeks telemetry. Epic deliverables shipped.

title: Envelope-level callout for opt-in patterns (card-grid, comparison-2col)
description:
Add full-width callout band below pattern content for the two user-requested patterns. Envelope-level PatternInput.Callout field; opt-in via CalloutSupport interface so non-uniform patterns (matrix-2x2, bmc-canvas, timeline-horizontal) can reject cleanly.

Scope (subtasks):
- Add PatternCallout DTO {text, emphasis?, accent?} in internal/patterns/pattern.go
- Add PatternInput.Callout *PatternCallout field in cmd/json2pptx/pattern_resolve.go
- Add CalloutSupport interface { SupportsCallout() bool }
- card-grid and comparison-2col implement CalloutSupport -> return true
- Post-expand decorator in expandPattern appends full-width row (ColSpan = len(grid.Columns), AutoHeight)
- Callout cells are NOT addressable via cell_overrides (explicit in docs)
- Shared schema fragment composed into patterns show output beside overrides/cell_overrides
- skill-info surfaces supports_callout: bool per pattern
- Update SKILL.md with ~45-token paragraph documenting callout
- Add decision D18 to docs/PATTERN_LIBRARY_SPEC.md

Why:
Currently PatternInput is XOR with shape_grid (spec D1). Agents who want 'cards + summary takeaway underneath' have no legitimate path: either abandon the pattern and hand-roll ~600 tokens of shape_grid, or push the callout into a body placeholder that most blank layouts don't have. This blocks the most common 'cards + key takeaway' composition.

Design decisions (from debate):
- Callout is envelope-level (not per-pattern values field) -> one doc site, shared schema
- Opt-in via interface (not blanket decorator) -> non-uniform patterns can refuse
- text is plain string (no nested shape_grid, no bullets) -> preserves D15 discipline
- No positioning knobs in v1 -> YAGNI; add later if needed

How to verify:

- comparison-2col with callout renders correctly
- matrix-2x2 with callout returns clear error: 'matrix-2x2 does not support callout'
- cell_overrides indices unchanged from pre-callout values

title: Wire pattern resolution into pipeline + fix computeQualityScore for non-content slides
description:
Why: Patterns are inert without a pipeline hook that expands slide.Pattern into slide.ShapeGrid before downstream rendering. This bead adds the hook AND fixes a pre-existing bug surfaced during design review (D17): computeQualityScore treats slides with no Content as empty, even when they have a shape_grid (or now, a pattern) that fully renders the slide.

What:
1. Create cmd/json2pptx/pattern_resolve.go with a helper expandPattern(p *PatternInput, ctx ExpandContext) (*ShapeGridInput, []Warning, error) that uses the registry from internal/patterns to look up by name, unmarshal Values/Overrides/CellOverrides into the typed structs the pattern provides, validate, and expand.
2. Hook it into cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go convertPresentationToSlideSpecs (around lines 561-596), AFTER JSON unmarshal, BEFORE resolveShapeGrid. Add XOR enforcement: slide.Pattern != nil && slide.ShapeGrid != nil returns a hard error. After successful expand, set slide.ShapeGrid = expanded and let the existing path run unchanged.
3. Fix computeQualityScore in cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go (around lines 1106-1107 and 1130-1140): a slide with non-nil Pattern OR non-nil ShapeGrid must NOT be scored as empty when Content is empty. Add a regression test.
4. End-to-end test using kpi-3up: build a minimal PresentationInput with one pattern slide, run through convertPresentationToSlideSpecs, assert resulting SlideSpec has the expected RawShapeXML/IconInserts/ImageInserts populated.

See /Users/ahrens/projects/json2pptx/docs/PATTERN_LIBRARY_SPEC.md (full design context, decisions D1-D17, integration point file:line refs).

title: Hand-authored JSON Schema scaffolding for patterns
description:
Why: D13 establishes that pattern discovery surfaces use hand-authored JSON Schemas (not reflection-generated) as the authoritative external contract. Before implementing concrete patterns, we need a typed Go helper to declare these schemas concisely so per-pattern code stays readable.

What: Add internal/patterns/schema.go with a Schema type and helpers for declaring object/array/string/number/enum constraints in a fluent style. Should serialize to valid JSON Schema draft 2020-12 via json.Marshal. No external runtime JSON Schema validator dependency — this is a *declaration and serialization* layer only; per-pattern Validate() in code remains authoritative.

Suggested helpers (sketch, refine in implementation):
  ObjectSchema(props map[string]*Schema, required []string) *Schema
  ArraySchema(items *Schema, minItems, maxItems int) *Schema
  StringSchema(maxLen int) *Schema
  NumberSchema(min, max float64) *Schema
  EnumSchema(values ...string) *Schema

See /Users/ahrens/projects/json2pptx/docs/PATTERN_LIBRARY_SPEC.md (full design context, decisions D1-D17, integration point file:line refs).

Out of scope: implementing any concrete pattern's schema (those happen in beads 4, 5, 13-18); reflection-from-Go-structs (D13 explicitly rejects this for the external contract).
design:
Decision D13 (spec §2): Hand-authored JSON Schemas per pattern are the authoritative external contract for agent-facing discovery. Runtime enforcement remains Go validation; semantic invariants ("exactly 3 cells", "no overlapping spans") live in code and may exceed what the schema expresses. Reflection-based generation, if used at all, is internal scaffolding only — never presented to clients as the contract.

Implication: Schema is for discovery surfaces (skill-info, MCP show_pattern, HTTP GET /patterns/{name}). Validation routes through Pattern.Validate, not through Schema.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] internal/patterns/schema.go compiles
- [ ] Helper constructors for object/array/string/number/enum at minimum
- [ ] Schema marshals to valid JSON Schema draft 2020-12
- [ ] Test: a sample schema (object with required string + array of strings) round-trips through json.Marshal/Unmarshal and matches a hand-written expected JSON
- [ ] No new runtime dependencies on JSON Schema validators
- [ ] golangci-lint run ./... clean

close_reason: Implemented Schema type in internal/patterns/schema.go with constructors (ObjectSchema, ArraySchema, StringSchema, NumberSchema, IntegerSchema, EnumSchema, BooleanSchema) and fluent modifiers (WithDescription, WithDefault, WithDefs, WithAdditionalProperties, AsRoot). Marshals to valid JSON Schema draft 2020-12. 10 tests covering round-trip, all type constructors, defaults, constraints, and omit-empty behavior.

title: Color: emit <a:schemeClr> for semantic color names instead of hardcoded hex
description:
When JSON input uses semantic names (`accent1`-`accent6`, `lt1`/`lt2`, `dk1`/`dk2`, `bg1`/`bg2`, `tx1`/`tx2`, `hlink`, `folHlink`), json2pptx resolves them to hex and emits `<a:srgbClr val="RRGGBB"/>`. The output PPTX has no `<a:schemeClr>` references, so colors do NOT adapt when the template's theme changes.

This is the highest-impact color fix — it affects every shape, text run, border, and cell fill in the deck.

## Current vs expected XML

Current (accent1 fill):
```xml
<a:solidFill><a:srgbClr val="FD5108"/></a:solidFill>
```

Expected:
```xml
<a:solidFill><a:schemeClr val="accent1"/></a:solidFill>
```

## Good news: shape_grid already does this correctly

`internal/shapegrid/shape.go:98-147` — `ResolveFillInput()` already checks `schemeColorNames` map and emits `pptx.SchemeFill()` for semantic names. The XML emission layer (`internal/pptx/fill.go:132-177`) properly writes `<a:schemeClr>`. Tests at `internal/shapegrid/shape_test.go:276-287` prove this path works.

The problem is **other code paths** that resolve semantic names to hex too early.

## Emission points needing update

Per research, the following hardcode hex (or are missing scheme support):

1. `internal/template/synthesis.go:639` — bullet color (`<a:buClr><a:srgbClr val="%s"/>`)
2. `internal/template/synthesis.go:688` — font color in defRPr
3. `internal/pptx/fill.go:202-208` — pattern fill foreground/background (srgbClr only)
4. `internal/generator/table.go:667` — header cell fill (currently uses hardcoded scheme via `mapToSchemeColor`, partially OK)
5. `internal/generator/table.go:673,685,728` — table border colors (hardcoded `tx1`)

## Acceptance criteria

- Every input that names a semantic color produces `<a:schemeClr val="..."/>` in output
- Every input that supplies a hex literal continues to produce `<a:srgbClr val="..."/>`
- The boundary between "semantic name" and "hex" is preserved through the entire pipeline (no early hex resolution)
- Color helper: introduce a `ParseColorSpec(string) (Fill, error)` that returns SchemeFill for semantic names, SolidFill for hex — use it everywhere
- Golden XML tests updated to expect schemeClr where appropriate

## Architectural change required

Currently the codebase has multiple parallel color-input parsers. Consolidate into one helper that all parsers use:

```go
// Returns SchemeFill for semantic names, SolidFill for hex
func ResolveColorInput(s string) Fill
```

Apply at:
- shapegrid (already correct — verify)
- table styles (header_background, border colors)
- text run colors
- bullet colors
- template synthesis

## Risk

- Test goldens in `internal/generator/testdata/golden/` may hardcode hex for theme colors and need bulk updates
- If the template's theme is malformed, schemeClr references could render unexpectedly — verify default theme fallback
- Contrast checking (`internal/generator/text_contrast.go:65-101` `resolveSchemeColorToHex`) still needs hex internally for ratio calculations — that path can stay; only XML emission changes

## Coordination

This is a foundation for Issue 8 (lumMod/lumOff) — both rely on preserving semantic name through to XML emission. Recommend rolling them out together.
close_reason: Implemented: Added pptx.ResolveColorString/IsSchemeColor helpers. Fixed synthesis.go to emit schemeClr for scheme color names in bullet and font colors. Fixed style_extractor.go and font_resolver.go to preserve scheme names instead of resolving to hex. Updated mapToSchemeColor to accept all OOXML scheme names. Added scheme color support to pattern fill fg/bg. Consolidated duplicate schemeColorNames maps to single canonical source in pptx package.

title: Table: only emit header cell <a:solidFill> when header_background is explicitly set
description:
Every header cell receives an explicit `<a:solidFill><a:schemeClr val="accent1"/></a:solidFill>` in its `<a:tcPr>`, even when `header_background` is not specified in the JSON. This overrides the table style's `firstRow > tcStyle > fill` and prevents Brand Table 3's firstRow appearance (bg1 lumMod=95000 light gray with accent1 text) from taking effect.

## Root cause

`internal/types/table.go:43` sets `DefaultTableStyle.HeaderBackground = "accent1"`, so when JSON omits the field it still resolves to accent1 inside `generateCellProperties`. The XML emission at `internal/generator/table.go:664-668` then writes the solidFill unconditionally.

## Acceptance criteria

- When the JSON style object omits `header_background`, no `<a:solidFill>` is emitted on header cells (just `<a:tcPr/>`)
- When `header_background` is explicitly set to a scheme name (`accent1`-`accent6`) or hex, current behavior is preserved
- When `header_background: "none"`, no fill emitted (current behavior already supports this)
- Distinguish "user set accent1 explicitly" from "default fell through to accent1"

## Where to change

- `cmd/json2pptx/json_schema.go:273-277` — `TableStyleInput.HeaderBackground` is a plain string; we lose the "was-it-set" signal. Change to `*string` pointer or add a separate sentinel.
- `internal/types/table.go:43` — drop the `"accent1"` default OR keep default but change `generateCellProperties` to distinguish.
- `internal/generator/table.go:654-678` — `generateCellProperties()` only emits solidFill when header_background was explicitly set.
- Update tests: `TestGenerateTableXML_HeaderStyling` at `internal/generator/table_test.go:82`.

## Coordination

Pair with the "skip tblBorders" fix — both are required to allow template table styles to render correctly.
close_reason: Changed TableStyleInput.HeaderBackground to *string pointer to distinguish 'not set' from 'explicitly set'. Removed accent1 default from DefaultTableStyle. When header_background is omitted in JSON, no solidFill is emitted on header cells, allowing the table style's firstRow appearance to take effect.

title: Table: skip <a:tblBorders> emission when borders=none
description:
Tables generated by json2pptx always emit <a:tblBorders> XML, which overrides the template table style border definitions. When `borders: "none"` is specified, json2pptx writes explicit noFill entries for all 6 border positions, suppressing the table style's `wholeTbl > tcBdr` definitions (e.g. Brand Table 3's bg2-colored 12700-width insideH lines).

This blocks template-styled tables from rendering correctly.

## Acceptance criteria

- When `borders: "none"`, do NOT emit `<a:tblBorders>` at all
- When borders is omitted (and a table style is being used), do NOT emit `<a:tblBorders>`
- When `borders: "horizontal"` or `borders: "all"`, retain current behavior
- Add golden test verifying the absence of tblBorders for none/omitted cases

## Where to change

- `internal/generator/table.go:726-764` — `generateTableLevelBorders(borderStyle string)` currently always returns a `<a:tblBorders>` block. Change so the `"none"` case returns empty string.
- `internal/generator/table.go:186` — `GenerateTableXML()` calls the function; ensure empty result is handled.
- Tests: `internal/generator/table_test.go:123` (`TestGenerateTableXML_NoBorders`) and `:1286` (`TestGenerateTableLevelBorders`) need updating to expect no tblBorders element.

## XML expected (borders=none)

```xml
<a:tblPr firstRow="1" bandRow="1"/>
```

(no tblBorders child)
close_reason: generateTableLevelBorders now returns empty string for borders=none; caller skips tblBorders when borders omitted with a table style. Tests updated.

title: Integrate PPTX structural validator into generator test suite
description:
## Test gap: No OOXML validation in generator tests (HIGH severity)

Generator integration tests open output PPTX as ZIP and count slides, but do NOT validate:
- presentation.xml slide ID list matches actual slide files
- [Content_Types].xml has overrides for all slides and notes
- presentation.xml.rels references match slide filenames
- slide relationship files contain correct media references

The project already has cmd/validatepptx that performs structural validation, but it is NOT integrated into the test suite.

## Fix
Call the PPTX validator as a test helper after generation in generator_test.go, or add assertions verifying relationship graph consistency. This would catch OOXML structural bugs before they reach users.

title: P1: Icon overlay not centered when shape has empty text content
description:
## Description
When a shape_grid cell has a shape with an icon overlay and empty text (content: ""), the icon renders at the top of the cell instead of being vertically centered. This happens because the hasText check treats any non-null JSON text object as "has text", even when the text content is empty.

## Visual Evidence
Slides 2, 3, 8, 24 on all templates: orange icon squares sit at the top of each row instead of being vertically centered with the adjacent text content.

## Root Cause
internal/shapegrid/grid.go:155:
```go
hasText := cell.Shape != nil && len(cell.Shape.Text) > 0 && string(cell.Shape.Text) != "null"
```

When JSON has `"text": {"content": "", "size": 13}`, the Text field is a non-empty json.RawMessage (it's a valid JSON object). So `len(cell.Shape.Text) > 0` is true and `hasText = true`.

This triggers `resolveIconPosition()` (line 574-587) to return "top" instead of "center", because it thinks there's text that the icon needs to avoid.

## Fix
Check for empty text content, not just presence of the text field:

```go
// internal/shapegrid/grid.go:155
hasText := cell.Shape != nil && hasNonEmptyText(cell.Shape.Text)
```

Add helper:
```go
func hasNonEmptyText(text json.RawMessage) bool {
    if len(text) == 0 || string(text) == "null" {
        return false
    }
    // If it's a string, check if non-empty
    var s string
    if json.Unmarshal(text, &s) == nil {
        return strings.TrimSpace(s) != ""
    }
    // If it's an object, check the "content" field
    var obj struct{ Content string `json:"content"` }
    if json.Unmarshal(text, &obj) == nil {
        return strings.TrimSpace(obj.Content) != ""
    }
    return true
}
```

## Also fix the JSON
The sovereign-ai-strategy.json icon cells have unnecessary empty text objects:
```json
"text": {"content": "", "size": 13}
```
These should be removed — a shape with just an icon doesn't need a text field at all.

## Files to Modify
- internal/shapegrid/grid.go:155 — fix hasText check to inspect content, not just presence
- examples/sovereign-ai-strategy.json — remove empty text objects from icon-only cells

## Verification
1. Generate sovereign-ai-strategy with PwC template
2. Check slides 2, 3 — icons must be vertically centered in their cells
3. Run go test ./internal/shapegrid/ -count=1
close_reason: Fixed hasText check to inspect actual text content rather than just field presence. Added hasNonEmptyText helper that checks string/object content. Removed empty text objects from icon-only cells in sovereign-ai-strategy.json.

title: P1: Footer Y position must be derived from template footer placeholders, fallback 5.5mm from bottom
description:
## Description
The footer vertical position must be determined by scanning all slides/layouts/masters in the template for any existing footer placeholder (type:dt, type:ftr, type:sldNum). If any footer placeholder is found anywhere in the template, use its Y position. If NO footer placeholder exists in any template slide/layout/master, default to 5.5mm above the bottom border.

## Current Behavior
`internal/generator/footer.go:307-345` (`resolveFooterPositions()`) reads footer positions from the **slide master** only. If the master has no footer placeholders, it falls back to hardcoded defaults:
```go
// footer.go:24-37
"type:dt":     Y: 6492875  (94.7% of 6858000)
"type:ftr":    Y: 6492875
"type:sldNum": Y: 6492875
```

These defaults were tuned for PwC and may not match other templates.

## Required Behavior
1. **Scan all template sources for footer positions** in priority order:
   a. Slide master footer placeholders (current behavior)
   b. Slide layout footer placeholders (not currently checked)
   c. If found in ANY source, use the highest-priority match
2. **If no footer placeholder found anywhere**: use fallback Y = slideHeight - 5.5mm - footerHeight
   - 5.5mm = 198000 EMU (1mm = 36000 EMU)
   - Default footer height: 365125 EMU (~0.4 inches)
   - So fallback Y = slideHeight - 198000 - 365125

## Implementation

### Step 1: Extend getFooterPositionsForLayout() to also check layout XML
Location: `internal/generator/singlepass.go:469-553`

Currently reads master only. Add a second step: if master has no footer placeholders, parse the layout XML itself for footer shapes.

### Step 2: Update resolveFooterPositions() fallback
Location: `internal/generator/footer.go:307-345`

When `len(positions) == 0` (no master footer positions), instead of using `defaultFooterPositions`, compute Y from 5.5mm rule:
```go
const defaultFooterMarginMM float64 = 5.5
const emuPerMM int64 = 36000
footerMarginEMU := int64(defaultFooterMarginMM) * emuPerMM  // 198000
defaultCY := int64(365125) // standard footer height
fallbackY := slideHeight - footerMarginEMU - defaultCY
```

### Step 3: Update FooterTopEdge() 
Location: `internal/generator/footer.go:295-305`

This function is used by ContentZone to determine where content must stop. Update to use the same 5.5mm logic when no template footer position is known.

## Files to Modify
- `internal/generator/footer.go:22-37` — update default Y calculation to use 5.5mm rule
- `internal/generator/footer.go:295-305` — `FooterTopEdge()`: use 5.5mm fallback
- `internal/generator/footer.go:307-345` — `resolveFooterPositions()`: update fallback logic
- `internal/generator/singlepass.go:469-553` — `getFooterPositionsForLayout()`: also check layout XML for footer placeholders

## Verification
1. Generate with PwC template — footer position should match master's sldNum Y (6501384)
2. Generate with a template that has NO footer placeholders — verify footer is 5.5mm from bottom
3. Verify ContentZone (shape_grid bounds) correctly accounts for the new footer position
close_reason: Implemented: Footer Y position derived from template footer placeholders (master then layout), with 5.5mm-from-bottom fallback when no footer placeholder exists

title: P1: Modern template title slide — title overlaps subtitle text
description:
## Description
On the modern-template, the title slide (slide 1) has the large title text ("THE STRATEGIC IMPERATIVE OF SOVEREIGN AI") overlapping with the subtitle/date text. The title renders in large uppercase font and collides with the smaller subtitle positioned in the same area.

## Root Cause
The modern-template's title layout (slideLayout1 in modern, but mapped as Title Slide) has an unusual placeholder arrangement where the **subtitle is positioned ABOVE the title**:

```
slideLayout1 (modern "Title Slide"):
  ctrTitle: x=1930708 y=2801929 cx=8686801 cy=2565902  (center of slide, ~41% from top, 2.8" tall)
  subTitle:  x=1346090 y=1726269 cx=3024899 cy=547908   (upper-left, ~25% from top, 0.6" tall)
```

The subtitle placeholder (y=1726269, ~25% down) sits above the title (y=2801929, ~41% down). The title is 2565902 EMU tall (2.8 inches) — a massive centered placeholder. When long title text is placed here, it expands and overlaps with the subtitle above.

This is a **template design issue**: the modern-template title slide is designed for a large centered title with a small label above it. Our generator places subtitle text (with date/prepared-for metadata) into the subTitle placeholder, which collides when the ctrTitle text is long.

## Fix Options

### Option A: Template fix (preferred)
Modify `templates/modern-template.pptx` to adjust the title slide layout:
- Move subTitle below ctrTitle (y > ctrTitle.y + ctrTitle.cy)
- Or reduce ctrTitle height to leave room above for subTitle
- Or swap the positions to match PwC's convention (title top, subtitle below)

### Option B: Generator-side autofit
In `internal/generator/text_autofit.go`, when populating a ctrTitle placeholder, check if the rendered text would exceed the placeholder bounds and scale the font size down. This is complex and doesn't address the positional overlap.

### Option C: Content-aware placement
In `internal/generator/text_population.go`, when the title slide layout has subtitle above title (detected by comparing Y positions), swap the content: put the shorter text in the upper placeholder and the main title in the lower one.

## Files to Modify
- `templates/modern-template.pptx` — adjust title slide layout placeholder positions (Option A)
- OR `internal/generator/text_population.go` — add subtitle/title position detection (Option C)

## Affected Templates
- modern-template: severe overlap on title slide (slide 1)
- Other templates: OK (subtitle is below title)

## Depends On
- o19j (ContentZone) — general title/content overlap framework

## Verification
1. Generate sovereign-ai-strategy with modern-template
2. Convert slide 1 to image
3. Verify title and subtitle do not overlap
close_reason: Fixed by adjusting modern-template slideLayout1: moved ctrTitle up (y=1500000, cy=1800000) and subTitle below title (y=3500000, cx=8686801, cy=800000). Subtitle is now below title with 200K EMU gap, matching other templates' convention.

title: Icon overlay resolveIconPosition defaults to 'top' too aggressively — icons not centered
description:
Icons in accent boxes are vertically top-aligned instead of centered. The auto-detection in resolveIconPosition (grid.go:572-581) defaults to 'top' for any cell where CX <= 2*CY. This threshold is too aggressive — cells with 1.5:1 aspect ratio get 'top' positioning.

For standalone icon cells (no text), icons should be centered. For icon+text cells, the 'top' position pins the icon at shapeBounds.Y + 3pt gap, which looks wrong on accent boxes that have no text below.

FIX:
1. Lower threshold to CX > 1.2*CY for 'left' mode
2. For cells with no text content and an icon, default to 'center' instead of 'top'
3. In the 'top' case (grid.go:621-630), center the icon within its allocated zone instead of pinning to absolute top:
   Y: shapeBounds.Y + (iconZoneH-size)/2

KEY FILES:
- internal/shapegrid/grid.go:572-581 (resolveIconPosition — lower threshold)
- internal/shapegrid/grid.go:620-629 (top position — center within zone)
close_reason: Fixed: lowered left-mode threshold to 1.2x, no-text cells default to center, top-mode centers icon within zone

title: Two-column layout blank on Modern and Warm Coral — synthesis + normalization failure
description:
Same JSON renders two-column slides correctly on PwC but produces blank content on Modern and Warm Coral templates.

ROOT CAUSE 1: findBestContentLayoutIndex (synthesis.go:262-295) returns -1 when the content layout's body placeholder has zero bounds (inherits from master but not resolved). Synthesis silently returns without creating two-column layouts.

ROOT CAUSE 2: Synthesized layouts are NEVER normalized by normalizeTemplateLayouts (singlepass.go:146-172) because the normalizer only iterates template ZIP files, not syntheticFiles. Synthesized placeholders keep their raw 'slot1'/'slot2' names and lack type='body', causing resolver edge cases.

FIX:
1. In findBestContentLayoutIndex, fall back to master-resolved bounds when layout bounds are zero
2. In normalizeTemplateLayouts (singlepass.go), also normalize ctx.syntheticFiles entries
3. Add integration test: verify synthesized two-column produces non-empty content across 3+ templates

KEY FILES:
- internal/template/synthesis.go:262-295 (findBestContentLayoutIndex — zero bounds fallback)
- internal/generator/singlepass.go:146-172 (normalizeTemplateLayouts — add syntheticFiles)
- internal/template/synthesis.go:723 (hardcoded slideMaster1.xml ref — see separate bead)
close_reason: Fixed: (1) findBestContentLayoutIndex now falls back to first content layout when all body placeholders have zero-area bounds, (2) synthesizeTwoColumn uses title-derived fallback content area when bounds are zero, (3) normalizeTemplateLayouts now normalizes synthesized layout files in syntheticFiles

title: Route SVG images through native embedding (asvg:svgBlip) instead of raster-only
description:
When ImageSpec.Path points to an SVG file in a shape_grid cell, it currently goes through the raster mediaRel pipeline. It should be routed through the nativeSVGInsert pipeline instead, giving SVG-quality rendering.

This is the minimal change that enables custom SVG support via the existing ImageSpec pathway — users can immediately use custom SVGs by specifying them as images:
  {image: {path: './diagrams/custom-flow.svg'}}

DETECTION: IsSVGFile() already exists in internal/generator/svg.go. Use it to detect SVG paths in the shape_grid image resolution code.

EMBEDDING: Same as icons — asvg:svgBlip with 1x1 transparent PNG fallback.

KEY FILES:
- internal/generator/singlepass.go:356-377 (image registration — detect SVG and route to nativeSVGInsert instead of mediaRel)
- internal/generator/media.go (processImageContent already has SVG detection, adapt for shape_grid images)
close_reason: Implemented: SVG images in shape_grid ImageInserts are now detected via IsSVGFile() and routed through nativeSVGInsert (asvg:svgBlip) with transparent PNG fallback, instead of the raster mediaRel pipeline.

title: Support custom SVG icons from file paths (icon.path field)
description:
Add a 'path' field to IconSpec/IconInput so users can specify custom SVG icons from any file path, in addition to bundled icon names.

JSON SCHEMA:
  {icon: {name: 'shield'}}           // bundled (existing)
  {icon: {path: './icons/custom.svg'}} // custom file (NEW)

VALIDATION: Exactly one of 'name' or 'path' must be set. Error if both or neither.

RESOLUTION:
- Relative paths resolved against the directory containing the JSON input file (not CWD)
- filepath.FromSlash() for cross-platform (Windows backslash → forward slash)
- filepath.Clean() + filepath.Abs() for canonicalization
- filepath.EvalSymlinks() for symlink-aware security
- Reuse existing utils.ValidatePath() for traversal checking

FILL OVERRIDE: Only supported for bundled icons (Tabler structure with stroke/fill=currentColor). Custom SVGs skip fill rewrite — document this limitation. Users must pre-color their SVGs.

VIEWBOX HANDLING: Custom SVGs may have arbitrary viewBox dimensions (not 24x24 like Tabler). The FitContain sizing should use the SVG's actual aspect ratio, not assume 1:1.

EMBEDDING: Custom SVGs flow through the same nativeSVGInsert pathway as bundled icons — asvg:svgBlip with 1x1 transparent PNG fallback.

KEY FILES:
- cmd/json2pptx/json_schema.go (IconInput — add Path field, validation)
- internal/shapegrid/types.go (IconSpec — add Path field)
- cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go:resolveIconSVG() — branch on Name vs Path
- icons/lookup.go (no changes — stays bundled-only)
- internal/utils/path.go (add EvalSymlinks to ValidatePath)
close_reason: Implemented: Added icon.path field for custom SVG icons from file paths. Validation enforces exactly one of name/path. Relative paths resolve against JSON input directory. EvalSymlinks + ValidatePath for security. Custom SVGs skip fill rewrite. Tests added.

title: Closing slide subtitle not visible in PowerPoint — empty placeholder overlapping
description:
On slide 25 (closing slide with slideLayout5/ctrTitle layout), the user reports seeing an empty placeholder covering the subtitle content in PowerPoint. The subtitle text IS present in the XML but may be hidden by an overlapping empty placeholder shape from the layout.

LibreOffice renders it correctly, but PowerPoint may handle placeholder inheritance differently — an empty inherited placeholder could be covering the populated subtitle.

FIX: After populating slide content, remove any placeholder shapes that have no text content. This is the same issue as go-slide-creator-asve (empty placeholder cleanup) but specifically manifests on the closing slide.

KEY FILES:
- internal/generator/output.go (post-population cleanup)
- Check if slideLayout5 has extra placeholders that inherit into the slide
close_reason: Added removeEmptyPlaceholders cleanup step in writeSingleSlide that strips any placeholder shape with no text content (excluding footer types). This prevents layout-inherited empty placeholders from overlapping populated content in PowerPoint.

title: Content items need font_size override for placeholder text sizing
description:
JSON content items targeting template placeholders (title, subtitle, body) cannot override the font size. The template's placeholder style determines the size.

NEEDED: A font_size field on content items that overrides the template's default:
  {placeholder_id: 'title', type: 'text', text_value: 'Thank You', font_size: 72}

This is critical for closing slides where 'Thank You' needs to be much larger (72pt) than the template's default ctrTitle size (~36pt).

IMPLEMENTATION: In internal/generator/text_population.go where placeholder text runs are created, if the content item has a font_size field, set the rPr sz attribute to override the template default.

KEY FILES:
- cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go (ContentItem struct — add FontSize field)
- internal/generator/text_population.go (populateShapeText — apply font size override)
close_reason: Added font_size field to ContentItem, JSONContentItem, and ContentInput. Font size (in points) is applied as sz attribute on run properties and overrides lstStyle inherited sizes.

title: Bullet text uses literal '• ' character instead of proper OOXML buChar formatting
description:
Shape_grid text cells with bullet content render '• ' as a literal Unicode character in the text run, not as a proper OOXML bullet paragraph. This means:

1. PowerPoint does not recognize them as bullet points
2. No hanging indent — text wraps flush left instead of indented past the bullet
3. Cannot be reformatted using PowerPoint's bullet tools
4. No marL/indent spacing for proper bullet hierarchy

CURRENT OUTPUT:
<a:p><a:pPr algn='l'/><a:r><a:rPr sz='1600'/><a:t>• 78% of EU Government Data...</a:t></a:r></a:p>

EXPECTED OUTPUT:
<a:p><a:pPr algn='l' marL='342900' indent='-342900'><a:buChar char='•'/></a:pPr><a:r><a:rPr sz='1600'/><a:t>78% of EU Government Data...</a:t></a:r></a:p>

The bead go-slide-creator-y1n added bullet detection to buildTextBody via shared pptx.ParseBulletText, but it appears the detection is stripping the prefix without adding the buChar/marL/indent formatting, OR the JSON text still has literal '• ' from our earlier JSON fix that prepended them.

TWO-PART FIX:
1. CODE: Ensure pptx.ParseBulletText returns proper bullet paragraphs with buChar, marL=342900, indent=-342900 (matching the corrected PPTX reference). Verify in internal/pptx/text.go or internal/shapegrid/shape.go:buildTextBody.

2. JSON: The '• ' prefixes in the JSON text content should be detected and converted. If the code now handles '- ' prefix for bullets, change all '• ' to '- ' in the JSON, OR ensure '• ' is also detected.

KEY FILES:
- internal/pptx/text.go (ParseBulletText — must emit buChar + marL + indent)
- internal/shapegrid/shape.go:buildTextBody (bullet paragraph construction)
- examples/sovereign-ai-strategy.json (text content with bullet prefixes)
close_reason: Added Unicode bullet prefix (• ) detection to ParseBulletText alongside existing dash prefix (- ) detection. Bullet paragraphs now get proper OOXML buChar, marL, and indent formatting. Added regression test.

title: Footer slide numbers show wrong values — not using auto-updating field or correct sequence
description:
Multiple slides show incorrect slide numbers in the footer. Haiku QA agents report slides 10-25 showing '1' or '2' instead of the actual slide number. This is caused by either:

1. The slide number being hardcoded from a wrong source (not the actual slide position in the deck)
2. The slide number not using the OOXML auto-updating <a:fld type='slidenum'> mechanism

This is a sub-issue of the broader footer overhaul but is specifically about the NUMBER being wrong, not just the formatting.

FIX: Use <a:fld> with type='slidenum' instead of hardcoded text. This makes PowerPoint auto-compute the correct number based on slide position.

XML for auto-updating slide number:
<a:p><a:fld id='{GUID}' type='slidenum'><a:rPr lang='en-US' sz='1050'/><a:t>‹#›</a:t></a:fld></a:p>

KEY FILES:

title: Icon overlay not centered in accent shape — offset varies by column layout
description:
When a shape_grid cell has a shape+icon overlay, the icon pic is not centered within the accent shape. The offset direction and magnitude vary:

MEASUREMENTS:
- Slide 2 (columns=[10,90]): icon center is 227076 EMU (6.3mm) to the RIGHT of shape center
- Slide 20 (columns=[15,85]): icon center is 372364 EMU (10.3mm) to the LEFT of shape center  
- Slide 24 (columns=[10,90]): icons shifted LEFT of shape center

The icon should be centered horizontally and vertically within the accent rectangle.

ROOT CAUSE: The icon position is calculated from the cell bounds after FitContain, but the shape bounds were changed by the c2b2 fix to use full cell width (FitStretch). The icon positioning still uses the old FitContain cell bounds rather than the actual rendered shape bounds.

Expected: icon_x = shape_x + (shape_cx - icon_cx) / 2
Actual: icon_x is calculated from the original cell bounds before the shape/icon split

FIX: In the icon overlay positioning code (internal/shapegrid/grid.go or cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go), after determining the shape bounds (full cell) and icon bounds (contained square), center the icon within the shape bounds:
  icon_x = shape_bounds.X + (shape_bounds.CX - icon_cx) / 2
  icon_y = shape_bounds.Y + (shape_bounds.CY - icon_cy) / 2

KEY FILES:
- internal/shapegrid/grid.go:166-170 (CellKindShape with icon overlay — icon bounds calculation)
- cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go (icon insert position assignment)
close_reason: Centered icon overlay within shape bounds using (shape_cx - icon_cx)/2 for both X and Y offsets instead of left-aligning with padding

title: Shape+icon overlay: icon fills entire cell height — needs size cap or scale param
description:
When a shape_grid cell has both a shape (full-width colored bar) and an icon overlay, the icon is sized to fill the entire cell height via FitContain. On header-bar cells (wide and short), this makes the icon dominate the bar, overlapping the text and making it unreadable.

EXAMPLE: Slide 4 header bars are 99x29mm. Icons render at 29x29mm (full height), covering most of the bar width and hiding the text behind them.

CORRECTED PPTX REFERENCE: Icons in header bars should be ~15x15mm (roughly 50-60% of bar height), positioned on the left side with text flowing to the right.

FIX OPTIONS:
1. Add a max_size field to IconSpec (in points) that caps the icon dimensions
2. When a cell has both Shape and Icon (overlay mode), auto-cap icon to 60% of min(cx,cy) and position it on the left with padding
3. Add a scale field (0.0-1.0) to IconSpec for proportional sizing

KEY FILES:
- internal/shapegrid/types.go:84-87 (IconSpec — add Size/Scale field)
- internal/shapegrid/grid.go:166-170 (CellKindShape with icon overlay — apply size cap)
- cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go (icon bounds calculation for overlay mode)
close_reason: Added Scale field to IconSpec and iconOverlayBounds function. Icon overlays on shapes now default to 60% of min(cx,cy), positioned left-aligned with padding. Custom scale (0.0-1.0) supported via IconSpec.Scale.

title: Pervasive text-too-small across shape_grid slides (9-11pt in dense layouts)
description:
Multiple visual QA reviewers rated text readability 2-3/5 across many slides. The JSON specifies font sizes of 10-13pt for shape_grid cells, but at presentation distance these are too small. Affects slides 2-4, 6, 9, 11, 12, 13, 17, 18, 19, 20.

The root cause is twofold:
1. JSON authors (including AI generators) set conservative font sizes to avoid overflow, since shape_grid has no autofit
2. The shape_grid renderer faithfully renders the specified size with no minimum floor

This is coupled with the autofit issue (separate bead). Once autofit is added, the JSON can specify larger sizes (14-16pt) and let PowerPoint shrink to fit. Without autofit, setting larger sizes causes text to overflow and get clipped.

INTERIM FIX (JSON): Increase all shape_grid text sizes in sovereign-ai-strategy.json to minimum 13pt for body text, 16pt for header/label text.

CODE FIX: Add a configurable minimum font size to shape_grid rendering. In internal/shapegrid/shape.go:buildTextBody, enforce sz >= 1200 (12pt) as a floor. Combined with normAutofit, this gives PowerPoint room to scale down from 12pt but never below 8pt (the autofit floor).

KEY FILES:
- internal/shapegrid/shape.go:buildTextBody (add font size floor)
- examples/sovereign-ai-strategy.json (increase sizes)
close_reason: Added 12pt minimum font size floor in shape_grid renderer (both buildTextBody functions). Updated sovereign-ai-strategy.json to bump all sizes below 13pt to 13pt.

This is a recurring issue with the two-column layout path. The JSON uses layout slideLayout8 (Two Column 40/60) with content items targeting 'body' and 'body_2'. The placeholder_resolver resolves 'body_2' via semantic fallback to 'slot1' (logged: 'placeholder resolved via fallback requested=body_2 resolved_to=slot1'). This fallback may be mapping to the wrong physical shape, or the resolved shape may not exist in the synthesized layout.

INVESTIGATION:
1. Check if slideLayout8 (synthesized Two Column 40/60) actually has two body placeholders with correct names
2. Check if the fallback 'slot1' maps to the RIGHT column or accidentally to the same shape as 'body'
3. The log line 'placeholder resolved via fallback' suggests the direct resolution failed

- internal/generator/placeholder_resolver.go — verify semantic fallback for 'body_2' on synthesized two-column layouts
- internal/template/synthesis.go — ensure synthesized two-column layouts create distinguishable placeholder IDs for left and right columns
- cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go — validate that both body and body_2 resolve to DIFFERENT physical shapes

This may also be a JSON issue: the example may need to use the correct placeholder_id for the synthesized layout.

title: Shape_grid text has no autofit — text overflows silently
description:
shape_grid's buildTextBody (shapegrid/shape.go:267) creates TextBody with no AutoFit field, defaulting to 'no autofit' in OOXML. Text that exceeds the cell bounds simply overflows and gets clipped at render time with no warning.

Visible on multiple slides: slide 9 (2x2 matrix — text cramped), slide 11 (strategic pathways — text dense), slide 12 (hybrid model — unreadable), slide 22 (left column overflow).

The template placeholder path (text_population.go) has elaborate autofit with font capping, text truncation, and wrapping enforcement built over years. shape_grid has NONE of these defenses.

FIX: Add normAutofit to shape_grid text bodies:
1. In internal/shapegrid/shape.go:267, set AutoFit: 'normAutofit' on the TextBody. This tells PowerPoint to shrink text to fit the cell bounds.
2. Add a minimum font size floor (e.g., 800 = 8pt) to prevent text from becoming microscopic.
3. Optionally add overflow detection: estimate text height from content lines × font size, compare to cell height, and emit WARN log if overflow is likely.

KEY FILES:
- internal/shapegrid/shape.go:267 (buildTextBody — add AutoFit)
- internal/pptx/text.go (TextBody struct — verify AutoFit field exists)
close_reason: Added normAutofit to both buildTextBody functions in shapegrid/shape.go so PowerPoint auto-shrinks text to fit cell bounds

title: Shape_grid text cells lack bullet support — '- ' prefix not rendered as bullets
description:
shape_grid text rendering (shapegrid/shape.go:buildTextBody at lines 240-254) treats all lines as plain paragraphs. It does NOT detect '- ' prefixed lines as bullets and does NOT add bullet markers, MarginL, or Indent. Visible on slide 12 (Hybrid Partnership Model) where bullet points are missing.

Contrast with panel_shapes.go:396-432 (panelBulletsParagraphs) which explicitly checks for '- ' prefix and adds panelBulletMarginLeft, panelBulletIndent, and pptx.BulletDef. Also contrast with text_population.go:250-333 (setBulletParagraphs) which has elaborate bullet level detection.

This is part of a broader architectural issue: THREE independent text rendering pipelines exist (text_population.go, panel_shapes.go, shapegrid/shape.go) with different capabilities. shape_grid is the newest and lacks bullet support entirely.

FIX: In internal/shapegrid/shape.go:240-254 (buildTextBody), detect '- ' prefixed lines and emit pptx.Paragraph with:
- Bullet: &pptx.BulletDef{Type: 'char', Char: '•'} 
- MarginL: 228600 (matching panelBulletMarginLeft)
- Indent: -228600 (matching panelBulletIndent)
- Strip the '- ' prefix from the text content

Also detect numbered prefixes like '1. ', '2. ' etc. for numbered lists.

KEY FILES:
- internal/shapegrid/shape.go:240-254 (buildTextBody — add bullet detection)
- internal/generator/panel_shapes.go:396-432 (reference implementation)
close_reason: Added bullet detection in buildTextBody: '- ' lines render as bullet points, 'N. ' lines render as numbered bullets with proper MarginL/Indent/BulletDef. Added regression tests.

title: Shape_grid row heights don't match between columns — stacked boxes misaligned
description:
In shape_grid layouts with asymmetric columns (e.g., narrow icon col + wide text col), the stacked boxes in column 2 have heights that don't visually align with column 1 boxes. Visible on slides 2, 3, 4, 6 of the sovereign-ai-strategy deck.

ROOT CAUSE (from developer debate): resolveRowHeights() in internal/shapegrid/grid.go:271-327 uses text-content-based height estimation (estimateRowHeightPct at line 332) which counts newlines. Cells with different text lengths in different columns get different height estimates. Additionally:

1. Integer truncation accumulates across rows (int64 conversion at line 81)
2. When row_span is used, the spanning cell height = sum of spanned rows + gaps, but individual cells in other columns each have independently calculated heights
3. Gap calculations (rowGapEMU * numRows-1) add their own truncation error

FIX APPROACH:
1. When all cells in a row have the same row_span (or no span), force equal row heights across columns — the tallest cell determines the row height for ALL columns.
2. Add rounding correction: distribute truncation remainder across rows to ensure total height exactly matches available space.
3. For rows where one column has stacked cells and another has a spanning cell, constrain the stacked cells to sum exactly to the spanning cell height.

KEY FILES:
- internal/shapegrid/grid.go:74-84 (height calculation)
- internal/shapegrid/grid.go:271-327 (resolveRowHeights)
- internal/shapegrid/grid.go:332 (estimateRowHeightPct)
close_reason: Implemented distributeEMU() with largest-remainder rounding to eliminate integer truncation drift in row heights and column widths. Total allocated EMUs now exactly match available space.

title: Icons render as solid colored squares in LibreOffice — SVG not displayed
description:
FIXED: Icons were rendering as solid colored squares because of a z-order bug in output.go.

ROOT CAUSE: In internal/generator/output.go, insertNativeSVGPics() was called BEFORE insertRawShapes(). Since OOXML renders shapes later in spTree on top of earlier ones, the orange accent rectangles (from shape_grid) were painted directly over the icon pics, completely hiding them. Both had identical position and size.

FIX: Moved the insertNativeSVGPics() call to AFTER insertRawShapes() so icon pics appear later in spTree and render on top of the accent rectangles.

The SVG content and embedding structure were correct all along — this was purely a z-order (insertion order) issue.
close_reason: Fixed: swapped SVG pic insertion order in output.go to render icons on top of shape_grid rects

title: Shape_grid gap between icon column and text column too large (1.2cm vs 0.5cm)
description:
In shape_grid layouts with a narrow icon/accent column (col1) and wide text column (col2), the horizontal gap between them is too large — approximately 458,419 EMU (1.2cm) when it should be about 192,000 EMU (0.5cm).

MEASUREMENTS from sovereign-ai-strategy.pptx:

- User-fixed (slide 25): icon rect right edge at x=1,465,966; text rect starts at x=1,658,319 → gap=192,353 EMU

The user-fixed version has the text rectangle wider (cx=10,136,015) and closer to the icon column, which makes the content area feel more integrated and less sparse.

FIX LOCATION: The gap calculation in shape_grid rendering. The JSON specifies gap:4 (4% of slide width). For a 2-column layout where column 1 is 10% and column 2 is 90%, the 4% gap between them is too generous. Consider reducing the inter-column gap or making it proportional to the narrower column width rather than the full slide width. Check internal/generator/ where shape_grid column positions are calculated from the bounds/gap/columns spec.
close_reason: Cap column gap to 15% of narrowest column pre-gap width for asymmetric layouts. Prevents oversized gaps between narrow icon columns and wide text columns.

title: Shape_grid text cells use anchorCtr=1 causing horizontal centering instead of left-align
description:
In shape_grid text cells, the bodyPr element has anchorCtr='1' which centers the TEXT BLOCK horizontally within the shape. Even though pPr has algn='l' (left-aligned text within the block), the entire block floats to center, making text appear 'all over the place' (user's words) instead of flush-left.

AFFECTED SLIDES: All shape_grid slides with text cells — slides 2, 3, 20, 24 in sovereign-ai-strategy.pptx.

GENERATED XML (bad):
<a:bodyPr wrap='square' lIns='127000' tIns='76200' rIns='101600' bIns='76200' anchor='ctr' anchorCtr='1'/>
Result: text block centered in shape → text appears to float/shift based on line length

USER-FIXED XML (good):
<a:bodyPr rtlCol='0' anchor='ctr'/>
Result: text block starts from left → flush-left appearance, no anchorCtr

The visual effect is especially bad with multi-line cells where the first line (bold title like 'Weeks 1-2:...') is longer than the second line (detail text) — the block centers on the longer line making the shorter line look indented randomly.

FIX: Remove anchorCtr='1' from bodyPr in shape_grid text cells. In internal/pptx/text.go, the TextBody struct likely has an AnchorCenter bool — ensure shape_grid cells set this to false. Keep anchor='ctr' for vertical centering only.
close_reason: Removed anchorCtr=true from shape_grid text cells. Both buildTextBody and buildParagraphsTextBody were incorrectly tying anchorCtr to vertical alignment (vAlign=='ctr'), causing text blocks to be horizontally centered. Set AnchorCtr to false so text stays flush-left.

FIX LOCATION: Look in internal/generator/ where shape_grid cells get their text body populated — likely in panel_shapes.go or wherever shape_grid text runs get their rPr sz attribute. The font size should be at minimum 1400 (14pt) for body text in shape_grid cells, scaling up to 1600 when cell height allows. Consider the text_autofit.go system for dynamic sizing.
