title: Icon fill color override may break SVG rendering — needs verification
description:
## Problem
In the icons-and-svg-grid-test, slide 2 (Icon Gallery) has 12 icon cells ALL with explicit fill color overrides. Every single one is invisible in the rendered PDF. Meanwhile slide 7 (Categories) has 15 icons WITHOUT fill overrides and they all render perfectly.

This strongly suggests that the `applyIconFill()` function breaks SVG rendering.

## How applyIconFill Works
```go
func applyIconFill(svgData []byte, fill string) []byte {
    s := string(svgData)
    idx := strings.Index(s, "<svg")
    closeIdx := strings.Index(s[idx:], ">")
    insertPos := idx + closeIdx
    return []byte(s[:insertPos] + fmt.Sprintf(` fill="%s"`, fill) + s[insertPos:])
}
```

This injects `fill="#FF0000"` into the root `<svg>` tag. But:
1. Many SVGs use `stroke` not `fill` for outline icons — adding fill may not change color
2. The injected fill may conflict with internal `fill="none"` or `fill="currentColor"` attributes
3. LibreOffice may have issues with SVGs that have conflicting fill specifications

## Fix Options
1. Instead of injecting fill on root `<svg>`, replace all `stroke="..."` attributes in path elements
2. Use a proper SVG color replacement that handles both fill and stroke
3. Test in PowerPoint to verify if this is a rendering issue or a data issue

## Related
go-slide-creator-3ix (verify icon fill color override)
close_reason: Verified: not reproducible. applyIconFill works correctly — all 12 icons on slide 2 (with fill overrides) render visibly with correct colors in LibreOffice PDF export. The fix in go-slide-creator-3ix already resolved the duplicate attribute issue.

title: Icons not visible in LibreOffice PDF export (slide 2 blank, slides 4/6 missing icons)
description:
## Problem
Icons inserted via shape_grid icon cells are NOT visible in LibreOffice PDF export on multiple slides:
- Slide 2 (Icon Gallery): Completely BLANK — 12 icon cells with fill color overrides show nothing
- Slide 4 (Process Flow): Icons in header row INVISIBLE — only 3 small text labels ("Discover", "Plan", "Execute") visible at bottom, no icons
- Slide 3 (Outline vs Filled): Only 5 of 8 icons visible, 3 cells blank
- Slide 7 (Icon Categories): 15 icons visible and rendering correctly — this slide WORKS
- Slide 8 (Feature Comparison): Icon cells in body rows all invisible — only text labels show

## What DOES Work
- Slide 3: Some outline/filled icons render (heart, star, bookmark, bell visible)
- Slide 7 (Categories): All 15 icons render correctly at large size — pie chart, download, check, briefcase, thumbs-up, bar chart, upload, x, book, thumbs-down, trend-up, share, alert, certificate, heart

## Pattern
Icons seem to render when they're in simple grids with large cells but fail in:
1. Cells with fill color overrides — slide 2 has fill overrides on every icon, all blank
2. Mixed icon+shape grids where icons are in specific rows
3. Small cells or cells where the icon bounds may be too small

## Root Cause Candidates
1. **Fill color override breaks SVG rendering** — `applyIconFill()` injects a fill attribute into the root SVG tag. This may conflict with the SVG's own styling, or LibreOffice may not render SVGs with injected fill attributes.
2. **Icon cell bounds too small** — when icons are in small cells within complex grids, the EMU bounds may be below a minimum threshold for SVG rendering.
3. **LibreOffice SVG rendering limitation** — some SVG features may not export to PDF correctly.

## Verification Needed
Open the PPTX in actual PowerPoint to determine if this is a LibreOffice export issue or a genuine PPTX generation bug.

## Affected Files
- `cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go:303-313` — icon insert generation
- `cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go:461-477` — applyIconFill
- `internal/generator/slides.go` — icon embedding into PPTX
close_reason: Fixed applyIconFill creating duplicate fill attributes (invalid XML). Now properly replaces stroke=currentColor for outline icons and fill=currentColor for filled icons, keeping fill=none intact on outline icons.

title: SVG/icon aspect ratio not preserved when scaling in shape_grid cells
description:
## Problem
Icons and SVG images inserted into shape_grid cells are scaled to fill the cell bounds without preserving aspect ratio. This distorts icons and diagrams, making circles into ovals and squares into rectangles.

Observed in:
- icons-and-svg-grid-test.pptx: icons appear stretched
- gear-process-chain.pptx: gear shapes distorted

## Expected Behavior
When inserting SVG icons or raster images into a cell, the system should:
1. Determine the native aspect ratio of the SVG/image
2. Scale to fit within the cell bounds using the SHORTEST dimension (contain mode)
3. Center the scaled content within the cell
4. Never stretch or squash content

## Algorithm
```
cellW, cellH = cell bounds
imgW, imgH = native image/SVG dimensions

scaleW = cellW / imgW
scaleH = cellH / imgH
scale = min(scaleW, scaleH)  // use longest edge to constrain

finalW = imgW * scale
finalH = imgH * scale
offsetX = (cellW - finalW) / 2  // center horizontally
offsetY = (cellH - finalH) / 2  // center vertically
```

## Affected Files
- `internal/generator/slides.go` — icon/image insertion
- `internal/pptx/svg.go` — SVG embedding
- `cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go` — icon insert bounds computation

## Note
The FitMode "contain" in shape_grid already does this for shapes (types.go:29-30), but it only applies to ShapeSpec, not to IconSpec or ImageSpec. The same logic needs to be applied to icon/image insertion.
close_reason: Icons and images in shape_grid cells now default to contain fit mode, preserving aspect ratio and centering within the cell. Shapes and tables retain the default stretch behavior.

title: PwC template: contrast fixer replaces white text on accent1 (orange) with dark #272727
description:
## Problem
When using pwc-template, the contrast fixer replaces #FFFFFF (white) text on accent1 (PwC orange #E55300) with dark #272727. This produces dark text on orange backgrounds — readable but ugly and off-brand. PwC's brand uses white text on their orange accent.

8 contrast fixes applied on shape-grid-panels-pwc.pptx (all white-on-accent1).

Log: "replacing low-contrast sRGB color original=#FFFFFF contrast_ratio=3.30 replacement=#272727"

White on PwC orange has 3.30:1 contrast — fails WCAG AA normal (4.5:1) but passes AA large text (3.0:1). Since these are all bold headers at 18pt, the large text threshold should apply.

## Additional PwC Template Issues
The generated PwC slides also show that the header text on the orange accent1 bar now reads as dark grey on orange instead of white on orange, which is visually terrible.

## Related
go-slide-creator-2s0 (contrast fixer over-correction — same root cause, different template)
close_reason: Lowered contrast fixer threshold from WCAGAANormal (4.5:1) to WCAGAALarge (3.0:1) for both scheme and sRGB color enforcement. Presentation text is almost always large text (18pt+), so the large text threshold is appropriate. White on PwC orange (3.77:1) now passes and is no longer replaced with dark grey.

title: Auto-height grey panels too short on slides 2-4: text barely fits, massive whitespace below
description:
## Problem
Slides 2 (Strategic Pillars), 3 (Service Offerings), 4 (Market Segments) on shape-grid-panels.pptx: the grey content panels (auto_height=true) are sized to minimum text height, resulting in:
1. Panels are very short (~15-20% of available grid height)
2. Massive whitespace below the panels (~60% of slide is empty)
3. Visually unbalanced: the blue header bar takes 18% but the content row is barely taller

The same issue appears on BOTH midnight-blue and pwc-template.

## Root Cause
`auto_height: true` estimates height from text content and sizes to fit. For short text (2-3 lines at 10-11pt), this produces tiny panels. The algorithm lacks a MINIMUM HEIGHT constraint.

## Expected Behavior
When auto_height is used, there should be a minimum row height (e.g., 40-50% of remaining grid space) so panels don't look like thin slivers. The content should fill the available space vertically, not shrink-wrap to text.

## Proposed Fix Options
1. Add `min_height` parameter to row: `{"auto_height": true, "min_height": 50}` (percentage)
2. Change auto_height algorithm: use max(estimated_text_height, equal_share_of_remaining) instead of just estimated_text_height
3. Fall back to equal-split when auto_height produces rows shorter than 30% of remaining space

## Affected Files
- `internal/shapegrid/grid.go` — resolveRowHeights, auto-height calculation
- `internal/shapegrid/autoheight.go` (if separate)

## Visual Evidence
Slides 2-4 of shape-grid-panels on both midnight-blue and pwc-template: grey panels are thin strips with ~60% empty space below.
close_reason: Auto-height rows now get at least an equal share of remaining space after fixed rows. resolveRowHeights uses max(text_estimate, equal_share) so panels fill available space instead of shrink-wrapping to short text.

title: Slide 5 (Implementation Roadmap): text not left-aligned, inconsistent margins
description:
## Problem
Slide 5 (Implementation Roadmap) on shape-grid-panels.pptx: the description text in the grey panels is CENTER-ALIGNED both horizontally and appears vertically centered. This creates two visual issues:

1. **Text is not flush-left** — The description text ("Discovery & Assessment\nConduct stakeholder interviews...") appears centered within the panel rather than left-aligned. This makes it look unprofessional for body text.

2. **Left margin inconsistent with top/bottom margins** — The text needs equal padding from all edges. Currently `inset_left: 10` but the text appears to float in the center of the panel.

## Root Cause
The JSON uses `"align": "l"` (left) and `"vertical_align": "ctr"` (center). However, `inset_left: 10` (10pt) is applied. The visual center-alignment appearance may be because:
- The text wraps and the paragraph alignment appears centered in the wide panel
- OR `vertical_align: "ctr"` is correct but `align: "l"` is not being respected visually

Looking at the PDF rendering: the text on midnight-blue IS left-aligned but with an `inset_left: 10` offset. On PwC template, the text is also left-aligned but the horizontal centering of the overall text block within the shape makes it LOOK center-aligned because the shape is so wide.

## Fix
Change the JSON example to use consistent flush-left layout:
- `"align": "l"` — keep
- `"vertical_align": "t"` — change from "ctr" to "t" (top-align)
- `"inset_left": 10, "inset_top": 8, "inset_bottom": 8, "inset_right": 10` — equal margins

This is primarily a JSON content fix, not a code bug. But the vertical centering in a thin auto-height row creates the appearance of inconsistent spacing.

## Visual Evidence
Slide 5 on both templates: text floats in center of grey panels rather than being flush-left with consistent margins from all edges.
close_reason: Fixed: changed vertical_align from ctr to t and added consistent insets (top:8, bottom:8, right:10) on all 5 Implementation Roadmap rows in shape-grid-panels.json

title: Connector lines route through homePlate shapes instead of spanning gap between them
description:
## Problem
Connector arrows between homePlate shapes (phase timeline) appear as horizontal lines slicing THROUGH the shapes rather than connecting at the edges in the gap space between cells.

## Visual Evidence
Slide 5 (Connector Lines) of visual-maturity-stress-test.pptx: cyan arrow lines pierce through Phase 1-4 homePlate shapes at vertical center.

## Root Cause
`pptx.RouteBetween()` calculates connector bounds based on shape centers and edge assumptions that don't account for:
1. homePlate geometry has a pointed TIP on the right side extending beyond the rectangular bounds
2. Connection site indices for homePlate point to the tip, not the flat edge
3. Connector bounds overlap with shape bounds instead of spanning only the gap

## Recommended Fix (from senior Go developer debate)
**Phase 1 (immediate):**
- In `RouteBetween()`, compute startEdgeX/endEdgeX at actual shape edges, not centers
- For homePlate, add tip offset (~15-20% of shape width beyond X+CX)
- Set connector bounds to span the gap: X = rightEdgeOfShapeN, CX = gapWidth

**Phase 2 (robust):**
- Build a ConnectionSiteResolver mapping geometry type → actual connection site coordinates
- Use OOXML preset geometry definitions for each shape type
- Eliminate geometry-specific hacks

## Affected Files
- `internal/pptx/cxngen.go` — RouteBetween function
- `internal/shapegrid/grid.go:180` — where RouteBetween is called
close_reason: Fixed: RouteBetween now accounts for pointed geometries (homePlate, chevron, arrows) by adding tip offsets to connector endpoints. Grid resolver passes actual shape Bounds and Geometry instead of CellBounds.

title: Contrast fixer over-corrects: silently replaces user-specified colored text (gold, grey) with near-black
description:
## Problem
The automatic WCAG contrast fixer silently replaces deliberately-chosen brand/accent text colors with near-black or other dark shades, destroying design intent. Tested across ALL 4 templates.

## Cross-Template Test Results (4 slides x 4 templates)

### Contrast Fix Counts
| Template | Fixes Applied | Severity |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| midnight-blue | 16 | High — gold→near-black, white→dark on accent fills |
| forest-green | 20 | Worst — gold on accent2 (orange) becomes olive #4B4000 |
| warm-coral | 16 | High — gold→#1D1800, white→#181818 on warm fills |
| modern-template | 25 | **CATASTROPHIC** — accent fills are LIGHT/PASTEL, so nearly ALL text gets darkened |

### Visual Evidence Per Template

**midnight-blue:** Gold text on accent1 (dark blue) replaced with near-black #0A0900. White text on accent2 (red) replaced with #464646. Gold on accent1 IS readable (3.16:1) but fails strict 4.5:1.

**forest-green:** Gold on accent2 (ORANGE) has contrast 1.63:1 — legitimately bad. BUT the fixer replaces it with olive #4B4000 which is also ugly. White on accent2 (orange) at 2.29:1 also gets darkened. The orange accent makes MANY light colors fail.

**warm-coral:** Similar to midnight-blue. Gold→#1D1800, white→#181818 on warm accent fills. Red on black (#CC0000) at 3.57:1 gets shifted to #D73838.

**modern-template:** **WORST CASE.** Accent colors are LIGHT PASTELS (pink, lavender, mint). Every single white/light text color fails against these light backgrounds. All 25 text runs get contrast-fixed. The KPI cards become unreadable — large numbers in grey on pastel is terrible. The fixer turns the entire deck into dark-text-on-light, destroying the intended white-on-color KPI card design.

## Root Cause Analysis
1. **The fixer applies 4.5:1 (WCAG AA normal) threshold universally** — doesn't distinguish large text (3.0:1 threshold per WCAG)
2. **It doesn't track user intent** — all colors treated as auto-generated
3. **It replaces silently** — no way for JSON authors to opt out
4. **It doesn't account for template variation** — same JSON works great on midnight-blue but gets mangled on modern-template because accent colors resolve differently

## The Modern Template Problem (CRITICAL)
Modern-template has light/pastel accent colors. When the JSON says `"fill": "accent1"` with white text, the author expects a dark accent fill. But modern-template's accent1 is light pink. The contrast fixer sees white on light pink (ratio ~1.4:1) and darkens the text to grey #606060.

This is a **template portability problem**: JSON designed for dark-accent templates breaks on light-accent templates, AND the contrast fixer makes it worse by mangling the colors instead of flagging the real issue.

## Recommended Fix (from senior Go developer debate)
### Option A: Large text threshold (minimum fix)
- Apply 3.0:1 threshold for text >=18pt or >=14pt bold (WCAG AA large text)
- Apply 4.5:1 for smaller text
- Would fix KPI cards (28pt bold) and headers (16pt bold) but not 9-10pt body text

### Option B: Never replace user-specified colors (preferred)
- Track color source: explicit user JSON vs defaults
- For user-specified colors: LOG WARNING but don't replace
- For auto-generated/default colors: apply threshold + replace
- Add `"skip_contrast_fix": true` per-shape escape hatch

### Option C: Template-aware contrast (best but most complex)
- Resolve scheme colors to actual RGB BEFORE contrast check
- If accent1 resolves to a light pastel, warn that white text won't work
- Suggest alternative text colors instead of auto-replacing

## Files
- `internal/generator/text_contrast.go` — fixSrgbColorsForContrast, fixSchemeColorsForContrast
- `internal/generator/slides.go` — where contrast fix is called in the pipeline
close_reason: Changed enforceShapeGridContrast to warn-only mode: user-specified text colors in shape_grid cells are now preserved instead of being silently replaced. Low-contrast colors are logged as warnings but never modified. Template-inherited colors in enforceTextContrastInSlide remain auto-fixed.

title: Add text-over-image overlay layout pattern (Bain slides 5/25)
description:

title: No image support in shape_grid cells — cannot achieve consulting-quality slides
description:
## Problem
The shape_grid system has no image support. CellKind only supports Shape, Table, and Icon. The Bain reference deck relies heavily on full-bleed photography, image backgrounds, and photo-text hybrids.

## What's Missing
- No ImageSpec type in grid cells
- No background image support for slides or individual cells
- No image fit modes (cover, contain, stretch, focal point)
- Cannot create any Bain slide pattern that uses photography

## Bain Reference Slides Requiring Images
- Slide 1: Full-bleed cover photo with text overlay
- Slide 4: Half-text, half-lighthouse dramatic photo
- Slide 5/25: Numbered list over dramatic background photo with dark overlay
- Slide 8: Split comparison + side-by-side photos
- Slide 14: Full-width image strip (5 photos with labels overlaid)
- Slide 15: Building photo as background with timeline overlay

## Proposed Solution
1. Add `ImageSpec` to Cell struct: `{path: string, fit: "cover"|"contain"|"stretch", alt_text: string}`
2. Add `CellKindImage` to CellKind enum
3. Handle image generation in resolveShapeGrid (register image in PPTX media)
4. Add slide-level `background.image` field for full-bleed backgrounds

## Impact
Without image support, the tool cannot replicate ~60% of Bain's visual language. This is the biggest capability gap for achieving consulting-quality output.
close_reason: VERIFIED: CellKindImage, ImageSpec, overlay, and text-on-image all implemented in types.go and shape_grid.go.

title: Text not rendering in shape_grid examples (other than basic-deck)
description:
## Problem
User reports that text is not visible/rendering in shape_grid example slides, other than the basic-deck examples. The JSON definitions clearly include text content, but it may not be reaching the PPTX output in all cases.

## Observed Behavior
- basic-deck examples render text correctly
- shape-grid-panels, consulting-layouts, business-model-canvas slides may have missing text
- Need to verify: is text present in OOXML XML but not displayed? Or is it missing entirely?

## Possible Root Causes
1. Text rendering works for standard placeholder-based slides but fails for shape_grid injected shapes
2. The `buildTextBody()` function in `internal/shapegrid/shape.go:176` may not be generating valid txBody XML for all shape types
3. Font resolution (`+mn-lt` theme minor font) may not resolve correctly in injected shapes
4. Text body anchor/wrap settings may cause text to overflow or be positioned outside visible area

## Investigation Steps
1. Open generated PPTX, inspect XML for shape_grid shapes — is `<p:txBody>` present with content?
2. Check if text is present but invisible (e.g., white text on white background, or zero-size font)
3. Verify text rendering works for all geometry types used in examples (roundRect, rect, chevron, homePlate)

## Affected Files
- `internal/shapegrid/shape.go` — GenerateShapeXML, buildTextBody
- `internal/pptx/spgen.go` — GenerateShape, txBody generation
- `cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go` — resolveShapeGrid pipeline
close_reason: Fixed: TextBody.WriteTo() was emitting <a:txBody> (DrawingML namespace) instead of <p:txBody> (PresentationML namespace) inside p:sp shape elements. This caused PowerPoint/LibreOffice to ignore text content in shape_grid shapes. The namespace fixer couldn't correct it because it only matches unprefixed <txBody>, not already-prefixed <a:txBody>.

title: Add virtual layout resolver orchestrating grid on blank+title
description:
Create the virtual layout resolution flow that takes a grid spec and produces a positioned slide using blank+title as base.

## Flow
1. Caller specifies slide with shape_grid (and optionally slide_type: "blank" or "virtual")
2. Resolver selects base layout:
   a. Find layout tagged "blank" with title placeholder
   b. Fallback: find layout tagged "blank-title" (synthesized)
   c. Fallback: use "One Content" layout, body placeholder bounds become grid bounds
3. Compute grid bounds:
   a. Blank+Title: shapegrid.BoundsFromTitleAndFooter(title, footer, 9pt)
   b. One Content: shapegrid.BoundsFromPlaceholder(bodyPlaceholder.Bounds)
4. Call shapegrid.Resolve(grid, bounds, alloc) → []ResolvedCell
5. Dispatch ResolvedCell by Kind to XML generators
6. Set SlideSpec.LayoutID = selected base layout, SlideSpec.RawShapeXML = generated fragments

## Location
- Resolution logic in cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go (replaces current resolveShapeGrid call at line 480)
- Bounds computation uses shapegrid.BoundsFrom* helpers
- Layout selection queries TemplateAnalysis.Layouts for tags

## Key constraint
Grid bounds MUST be derived from actual placeholder metadata, not hardcoded:
- Different templates have different title heights, footer positions, content areas
- The 9pt gap (114300 EMU) between title/footer and grid area is the standard

## Verification
- JSON fixture with shape_grid on blank slide → correct bounds from template
- JSON fixture with shape_grid on content slide → bounds match body placeholder
- Different templates produce different grid bounds
- go test with integration fixtures
close_reason: Implemented virtual layout resolver: resolveVirtualLayout selects blank/blank-title/content layout and computes grid bounds from placeholder metadata. Integrated into convertPresentationSlides for slides with shape_grid and no/blank/virtual layout. Added overrideBounds parameter to resolveShapeGrid. 8 new tests covering all resolution paths.

title: Synthesize blank+title layout when template lacks one
description:
Extend internal/template/synthesis.go to guarantee every template has a blank+title layout for virtual layouts.

## Changes to internal/template/synthesis.go
- Add "blank-title" to requiredCapabilities check
- In SynthesizeIfNeeded: if no layout tagged "blank" exists with a title placeholder:
  1. Find best content layout via findBestContentLayoutIndex
  2. Generate new layout XML with ONLY the title placeholder (no body)
  3. Add Footer and Slide Number placeholders from the base layout
  4. Register as synthetic layout with tag "blank-title" (or "blank" + "virtual-base")
  5. Add to analysis.Synthesis.SyntheticFiles

## Layout XML generation
- Use existing GenerateLayoutXMLBytes pattern
- appendTitlePlaceholder from base layout
- Do NOT append body/content placeholders
- Keep footer and slide number placeholders

## Grid bounds derivation
When using synthesized blank+title as virtual layout base:
- Grid x/w = title placeholder x/w
- Grid top = title bottom + 9pt gap (114300 EMU)
- Grid bottom = footer top - 9pt gap
- These bounds are computed by shapegrid.BoundsFromTitleAndFooter()

## Verification
- Template without blank layout → synthesis produces one
- Template with existing blank+title layout → no synthesis needed
- Synthesized layout appears in TemplateAnalysis.Layouts with correct tags
- go test ./internal/template/ must pass

title: Extract shape grid to internal/shapegrid/ package
description:
Move shape grid domain logic from cmd/json2pptx/ to a new internal/shapegrid/ package. This is a prerequisite for virtual layouts and unblocks the HTTP API from using grids.

## New package: internal/shapegrid/

### types.go
- Grid, Row, Cell structs (internal representations, NOT JSON DTOs)
- CellKind typed string constants: CellKindShape, CellKindTable (extensible for future CellKindChart, CellKindImage)

### grid.go

- Move resolveColumns, equalSplit, resolveRowHeights, pctToEMU from cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go
- Resolve returns ResolvedCell structs (geometry + kind), NOT raw XML
- Import only internal/pptx for RectEmu and ShapeIDAllocator

title: [Epic] Native OOXML shape generation for slide layouts
description:
# Native OOXML Shape Generation

## Goal
Add native PowerPoint shape generation to internal/pptx/ so slide layouts can use arranged shapes (chevrons, boxes, arrows, rounded rects, etc.) that are editable in PowerPoint and inherit theme colors/fonts.

## Why Native Shapes (not SVG)
- **Editability**: Users can click and modify text/shapes in PowerPoint
- **Theme inheritance**: schemeClr values respect template themes
- **Font inheritance**: Omitting typeface lets template font apply
- **Auto-fit**: normAutofit lets PowerPoint shrink text to fit
- **Professional layouts**: Chevron processes, timeline arrows, comparison columns, matrix grids

## Architecture Decisions
- **Build from scratch** — unioffice is commercial, gooxml is AGPL, neither has shape creation API anyway
- **bytes.Buffer XML generation** — matches existing patterns in picgen.go, panel_shapes.go. NOT encoding/xml (broken namespace handling since 2013)
- **Extend internal/pptx/** — not a new package. Uses existing InsertIntoSpTree, ShapeIDAllocator, Relationships infrastructure
- **Composable types** — Fill, Line, TextBody, ShapeOptions structs with MarshalXML(buf) methods. NOT a full framework, just enough to avoid 45-line fmt.Sprintf calls
- **Don't parse presetShapeDefinitions.xml** — PowerPoint renders presets natively from the prst="" attribute. No path data needed for generation.
- **Hybrid with svggen** — Native shapes for editable layout elements. SVG for complex diagrams (charts, fishbone, Gantt, etc.). Generator decides per-diagram.

## Phased Shape Coverage

### Phase 1: Layout Essentials (~20 shapes)
rect, roundRect, round1Rect, round2SameRect, ellipse, triangle, diamond, 
parallelogram, trapezoid, hexagon, octagon, chevron, homePlate, pentagon,
plus, rightArrow, leftArrow, upArrow, downArrow, donut

### Phase 2: Connectors + Flowchart (~20 shapes)
straightConnector1, bentConnector2-5, curvedConnector2-5,
flowChartProcess, flowChartDecision, flowChartTerminator, flowChartDocument,
flowChartInputOutput, flowChartPredefinedProcess, flowChartConnector

### Phase 3: Callouts, Stars, Misc (~20 shapes)
wedgeRectCallout, wedgeRoundRectCallout, cloudCallout,
star4, star5, star6, ribbon, ribbon2, cloud, heart,
leftRightArrow, upDownArrow, curvedRightArrow, notchedRightArrow

### Phase 4+: Remaining shapes as needed
Complete the remaining ~127 shapes driven by actual usage.

## OOXML Reference
- 187 preset shapes defined in ECMA-376 ST_ShapeType (ISO/IEC 29500)
- Shapes use prst="" attribute in <a:prstGeom>
- Adjustment handles in <a:avLst> with values in 1/60000th units
- Units: 1 inch = 914400 EMU, 1 pt = 12700 EMU
- Angles: 60000ths of a degree (90° = 5400000)
- Connectors use <p:cxnSp> with <a:stCxn>/<a:endCxn> for connected endpoints
- Groups use <p:grpSp> with child coordinate space
close_reason: Phases 1-3 complete: 60+ preset geometries defined, spgen/cxngen/grpgen/fill/line/text/transform/effects all implemented in internal/pptx/, all tests pass. Phase 4 (remaining 127 shapes) tracked separately as go-slide-creator-6mj (P4 backlog).

title: Define public API surface and freeze stable types

## Task

## Problem
Moving from internal/ to a public module freezes the API. Types with any in public structs (e.g., StyleSpec.Palette is typed as any) must be cleaned up BEFORE going public.

## Types to Review

- RequestEnvelope, OutputSpec, StyleSpec, ThemeColorInput
- SVGDocument, RenderResult, BuilderRenderResult
- Diagram, DiagramWithBuilder, MultiFormatRenderer interfaces
- Registry, NewRegistry(), DefaultRegistry()
- Render(), RenderMultiFormat(), Types(), Register(), Alias()
- Color, ParseColor(), MustParseColor(), EnsureContrast(), WCAGAANormal, WCAGAALarge
- SVGBuilder, NewSVGBuilder() (needed for custom diagram authors)
- StyleGuide, Palette, Typography, Spacing, Strokes
- RenderCache, NewRenderCache(), CacheConfig
- Decoder, DecodeJSON(), DecodeYAML(), ValidationError

### Review for cleanup before making public
- StyleSpec.Palette typed as any — should be string | []string or a proper type
- Any other any-typed fields in public structs
- Functions that accept/return tdewolff/canvas types (leaks transitive dependency)
- SVGBuilder fields that expose canvas.Canvas/canvas.Context

### Should remain internal
- Helper functions used only by diagram implementations
- Internal layout algorithms (unless useful for custom diagrams)
- Font cache internals

## Acceptance Criteria

- No any-typed fields in public structs
- No tdewolff/canvas types in public API signatures
- go doc ./svggen/ produces clean, usable documentation

title: [Epic] Extract svggen into standalone Go module with CLI/API/MCP surfaces
description:
# SVG Generation Library Extraction

## Goal
Extract internal/svggen (~75K lines, 30+ diagram types) from the go-slide-creator monorepo into a standalone Go module that can be consumed as a library, CLI tool, HTTP API server, or MCP server.

## Agreed Architecture (Advocate/Devil's Advocate Consensus)

### Phase 1: Go Workspace (same repo)
Use go.work to create a module boundary within the monorepo. This gives API enforcement without operational overhead.

### Phase 2: Separate repo (when external consumers exist)
Full extraction to github.com/ahrens/svggen with its own CI, releases, and versioning.

## Key Decisions
- **Raster mutex**: Export via public raster package so monorepo consumers share the same mutex
- **init() registration**: Provide core/ sub-package for selective diagram registration + root package with auto-registration
- **Fonts**: Embed Liberation Sans in the library (fonts/ as public package, SIL OFL licensed)
- **workerpool**: Replace with golang.org/x/sync/errgroup
- **api/errors**: Define local error codes in server/httpserver/
- **MCP server**: Wrap HTTP API initially, standalone binary later if needed

## Module Structure
```
svggen/
  go.mod
  *.go (core library files)
  internal/ (fontcache, raster, safeyaml)
  fonts/ (embedded TTFs)
  core/ (types + registry without init())
  server/httpserver/ (HTTP API)
  server/mcpserver/ (MCP server)
  cmd/svggen/ (CLI)
  cmd/svggen-server/ (HTTP server binary)
  cmd/svggen-mcp/ (MCP server binary)
```

## Risk Mitigations
- Go workspace avoids version coordination tax in Phase 1
- Golden tests stay co-located until Phase 2
- Single CI pipeline until Phase 2
- core/ sub-package enables tree-shaking for minimal binaries
close_reason: Extraction complete: svggen module exists at svggen/ with go.mod, go.work configured, all code imports from github.com/ahrens/svggen, CLI/server/MCP binaries in cmd/, core/ sub-package for selective registration, fonts/ embedded, all tests pass

title: Tests for radial-hub: count sweep 4–8 across all templates incl. p-style, spoke rendering, split cells, MCP intents
description:
Parent epic: go-slide-creator-jk8j7 (circular / loop layout family). Label: circular-layouts-20261006.

## What / where
Same wall as cycle-ring: cmd/json2pptx/radial_hub_matrix_test.go (N 4..8 × all templates incl. p-style), budget test, post-expand fit-report test, budget probe, schema_maxima pins, accent restraint, preview parity, compose 50/60 + nested cell with the hub still round and `labels: legend` engaging; LibreOffice-gated render asserting a spoke's accent pixels exist midway between hub and satellite. MCP intents: "hub and spoke", "ecosystem around the platform", "capabilities around the core", "stakeholder map" rank radial-hub first; "today vs future" still ranks state-shift-hub.

## Verify
Green with `-short -race`; renders N=4 and N=8 on abstract and p-style attached.

## Family contract (applies to every bead in epic circular-layouts-20261006)

Native OOXML first: every shape is a preset-geometry `<p:sp>` emitted through the shape grid (internal/shapegrid). No SVG unless a geometry is provably impossible natively (none of the family needs it: `blockArc`, `circularArrow`, `pie`, `arc`, `donut`, `ellipse`, `chevron`, `homePlate`, `triangle`, `line` are all in internal/pptx/preset.go and shape cells already take `rotation`, `flip_h` and `adjustments` — internal/jsonschema/shapegrid.go:224-235, written at internal/shapegrid/shape.go:80-102).

Template parity, exactly like every other pattern:
- Colours are scheme names only (`accent1`, `dk2`, `lt2`...), never hex. Default accent = `ctx.DefaultAccent()`; tints via `ctx.ResolveSurface` / `neutralFillJSON` / `surfaceFillJSON`; ink on any fill chosen by measurement (internal/patterns/fill_contrast.go), so warm-coral / business-template / blue-corporate pick their own primary fill (docs/PATTERNS.md "Restrained accent defaults").
- Restrained accent: at most ONE solid-accent block >= 0.5in by default (the `highlight` item); structural segments / nodes take a neutral tint; `cell_accent_mode` (uniform | alternate | progressive) via `TextOverrides` + `ValidateCellAccentMode` + `ResolveCellAccent`. cmd/json2pptx/accent_restraint_gallery_test.go must pass without adding the pattern to `accentIsTheMessage`.
- Fonts: text sized at >= 12pt (`shapegrid.EffectiveTextSizePt`), rows sized from `writtenFitHeightPt` with `ctx.themeFonts()`, `MeasureFonts` stamped (expansion does this); `TestPatternExemplarsStoreNoAutofitShrink` and cmd/json2pptx/pattern_autofit_font_sweep_test.go must pass.
- Gaps wrapped in `ctx.Gap()`; filled shapes carry `noLine` (internal/patterns no_outline_test.go).
- Renders on ALL 10 templates including the local gitignored templates/p-style.pptx (abstract has the smallest body, 687x294pt; p-style 899x360pt) with zero refuse-class findings: cmd/json2pptx/template_pattern_matrix_test.go (non-short) is the gate.
- Works alone on a slide AND in split layouts: a horizontal `compose` segment of 50% and 60% width, a vertical segment, and a nested `shape_grid` cell `pattern` (see the split-layout bead). Circles must stay circles there (`fit: "contain"` on the ring cell, lattice edges recomputed from the actual cell).

Render recipe on this Mac (no pptx2jpg): `soffice --headless --convert-to pdf --outdir <dir> <pptx>` then `pdftoppm -r 80 -png <pdf> <prefix>`; private LO profile if soffice hangs (memory: libreoffice-macos-restore-modal-hang). Judge the actual render, including p-style, not green tests alone (memory: layouts-must-not-look-like-ai-html, native-slide-output-standard).

Angles: OOXML preset angles are in 60000ths of a degree, 0 = 3 o'clock, positive = clockwise. `blockArc` adj1 = start angle, adj2 = end angle, adj3 = ring thickness as a fraction of the short side (1/100000); `circularArrow` adj1 = shaft thickness, adj2 = arrowhead end angle, adj3 = start angle, adj4 = arrowhead sweep, adj5 = head width — confirm against ECMA-376 presetShapeDefinitions.xml and pin the chosen values with the golden.

Docs are part of the deliverable, same commit (CLAUDE.md "Skill, Docs, and Code Sync" policy is mandatory): a pattern bead is not done until it has (1) its CLAUDE.md "Named Patterns" table row (TestPatternDocumentationMatchesRegistry), (2) its skills/generate-deck/PATTERNS.md copy-budget paragraph (per item count; no static index — TestAgentPatternGuideUsesLiveCatalog), (3) its docs/PATTERNS.md selection-table row and peer-fill category entry plus any new authoring-contract section, (4) a docs/SCHEMA_CHANGELOG.md entry under the family's SchemaVersion, (5) a docs/wiki/visual-vocabulary.md entry (when to use it, when not, the sibling to prefer) and, where it has a split recipe, a docs/wiki/split-and-complex-layouts.md recipe whose YAML block validates (internal/semantic tests validate wiki YAML blocks), (6) internal/semantic/reach.go entry, (7) recommend.go rules. Anything agent-visible (new override key, new finding, new values field) also lands in skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md or its guide files, within the 100 KiB bundle budget (TestGenerateDeckSkillBudgets — memory: skill-and-tools-list-byte-budgets; trim elsewhere if needed).

Before closing any code bead: `make lint`, `go test ./internal/patterns/... -count=1`, `go test ./cmd/json2pptx -run 'TestPatternDocumentationMatchesRegistry|TestEveryPatternDeclaresMotif|TestPatternReachCoversTheRegistry|TestSchemaMaximaStayReadable|TestRecommendVisualEveryPatternIsAuthorable|TestPatternSmoke_AllPatterns|TestAccentRestraintGallery' -count=1`, then `go test ./... -short -race` (CI shape; see memory ci-differs-from-local-test-run). Any new file in internal/patterns stales templates/previews manifests — run `make template-previews` ONCE at the end of the family (see the docs/previews bead), not per pattern.

title: pattern radial-hub: central idea with 4–8 spokes to labelled satellites (hub-and-spoke, no sequence)
description:
Parent epic: go-slide-creator-jk8j7 (circular / loop layout family). Label: circular-layouts-20261006.

## Why
'Everything relates to the centre' (operating-model hub, platform + capabilities, stakeholder map, ecosystem) is drawn today with state-shift-hub (which forces a today/future semantic and 3–4 pairs) or a card-grid. SmartArt 'Basic Radial' / 'Diverging Radial'. Non-sequential: no numbers, no arrows.

## Values (typed struct in internal/patterns/radial_hub.go, hand-authored Schema() <= 6000 bytes with $defs — TestPatternSchemaCompression)
`center {label (<= 24), sublabel (<= 32, optional)}` required; `spokes []{label (<= 26), description (<= 60, optional), icon?}` 4..8; `highlight int` optional.

## Layout (native, via shape-grid `layers` + the lattice; see ring_common.go)
Ring square cell with layers: hub `ellipse` (diameter 0.34·side, solid accent — the one solid block — hub label 14–16pt bold measured ink + sublabel 12pt), N spoke layers = thin `rect` (2pt) layers rotated to each item angle spanning hub edge → satellite edge (frame = the rotated line's bounding box; verify LibreOffice rotation of a thin rect reads as a line, else use a `line` preset layer), N satellite `ellipse` layers on the ring (diameter 0.16·side, neutral tint, icon via the icon slot or the first letter), labels outside via the shared lattice rows; `overrides.labels: inside` for N <= 6 puts the label into a larger satellite (0.24·side, <= 14 chars). Start angle −90 so item 1 sits at 12 o'clock when N is even? No: use the cycle-ring start (segment begins at 12 o'clock) so for N=4 satellites sit at the diagonals and labels have room; N=6 → one at top and bottom (band labels).

## Overrides
`labels` outside (default) | inside | legend; `spokes` lines (default) | none; `highlight`; `cell_accent_mode` (satellites).
Standard: `TextOverrides` embedded; `cell_accent_mode` uniform|alternate|progressive (ValidateCellAccentMode / ResolveCellAccent); `rejectUnusedTextOverrides` + `textOverridesSchemaWithout` for any published key the pattern cannot act on; `highlight` is the only solid accent block by default.

## Capacity / budgets
N=4–6: label 26 / description 60; N=7–8: 22 / 40; inside label 14. `BudgetConfigurations()` for 4 and 8.
Rows sized from `writtenFitHeightPt(..., ctx.themeFonts())`; every text at >= 12pt; `PostExpandWarnings` emits `BODY_TOO_LONG`-class warnings naming the item when a label or description cannot hold at the floor on the current template (the same message shape as team-bios / driver-tree).

## Registration + discovery (same commit)
- `init() { Default().Register(&radialhub{}) }`; `Name()`, `Description()`, contrastive `UseWhen()` (must contain prefer/instead/unless/not/rather — pattern_test.go:426), non-empty `NotWhen()` naming siblings: cycle-ring / cycle-nodes (ordered loop), state-shift-hub (today/future pairs), icon-row / card-grid (peers without a centre), driver-tree (hierarchy); `Version()`; `Taxonomy()` (Category diagram, NarrativeRole, DensityClass, AccentWeight, SparseThresholdPct, DataVisual false); `CellsHint()`; `ExemplarValues()` with realistic consulting content (no "Step 1" placeholders — exemplar_realism_test.go) that stores no autofit shrink on every template incl. p-style.
- internal/patterns/motif.go: `"radial-hub": {base: MotifDiagram}` (+ overrideStyles entries for any style that changes the look).
- internal/patterns/recommend.go: >= 2 `rule` entries (keywords, itemMin/itemMax, rationale) so TestRecommendVisual_AllRegisteredPatternsReachable passes and recommend_visual ranks it for the intents listed below; internal/patterns/recommend_visual_forms.go `visualNameAliases` entry `named_pattern:radial-hub`; an eval case in internal/patterns/testdata/recommend_visual_eval.json.
- internal/semantic/reach.go entry (`""` until the `cycle` DeckSpec kind bead maps it; that bead flips it).
- cmd/json2pptx/schema_maxima_test.go: pins in BOTH `schemaMaximaShrinkPt` and `pStyleSchemaMaximaShrinkPt`.
- Smoke slide in examples/patterns-smoke.json + regenerated cmd/json2pptx/testdata/json/patterns_smoke.golden.json (TestPatternSmoke_AllPatterns); dedicated examples/radial-hub.json deck (min count, max count, one split-layout slide) that passes every examples/*.json corpus test (examples_validate_test, strict_fit_substance_test, verdict_parity_corpus_test, contrast_parity_corpus_test, sibling_size_written_test, corpus_headless_test — run the integration-tagged ones locally, memory corpus-headless-integration-tag).
- Goldens: internal/patterns/testdata/radial-hub/default.golden.json and sizemetric.golden.json (UPDATE_GOLDEN=1).
- Docs: CLAUDE.md Named Patterns row; skills/generate-deck/PATTERNS.md per-count copy budget paragraph; docs/PATTERNS.md selection-table row + peer-fill category + any new contract; docs/SCHEMA_CHANGELOG.md entry; docs/wiki/visual-vocabulary.md entry (use / avoid / sibling to prefer); examples/README.md line.

## Tests (own file internal/patterns/radial_hub_test.go; the companion test bead adds the cross-template and split-layout walls)
Metadata, SchemaIsValidJSON, Validate (happy path for every count in range; wrong count with sibling hint; missing required; max length exceeded with one multi-byte value inside the budget — runeLen not len; invalid cell_override keys), ExpandLayout (geometry per layer: segment adj values, badge frames, label sides, no overlapping lattice rectangles for every N), ExpandStyling (DefaultAccent, accent override, cell_accent_mode ×3 against accent1 and accent3, highlight = one solid fill, measured ink), PostExpandWarnings, Golden, RecommendIntents.
- `TestRadialHubSpokesTouchBothEnds`: each spoke's bounding frame endpoints are within 1pt of the hub and satellite circumferences.
- `TestRadialHubHubIsTheOnlySolidAccent`.
- `TestRadialHubNoOverlapForEveryCount`.

## Verify
- `go test ./internal/patterns -run TestRadialHub -count=1` and the registry-wide tests listed in the family contract green; `make lint` green.
- `json2pptx generate -json examples/radial-hub.json -template <t> -templates-dir templates -output /tmp/radial-hub/<t>` for all 10 templates incl. p-style: zero refusals; render abstract + p-style + midnight-blue via soffice→pdf→pdftoppm and look: circles are circles, labels never touch the ring, the highlighted item is the only solid accent, text >= 12pt, nothing crosses the title or footer chrome.
- `json2pptx preview-patterns -templates-dir templates -output assets/pattern-previews -pattern radial-hub` renders on every template (TestPatternPreviewIsTheGeneratedSlide).

title: Thumbnail identity: a slide on a master's second layout has one key on every template, so a cached image of another template is returned
description: render.VisibleSlideKeys follows master to layout relationships. A layout first reached through its master is digested inside a cycle (the way back to the master is cut to its part name) and that partial digest is memoised, so a slide using that layout gets a key without master or theme content. Repro: render validateRevisionSpec (title, 2 kpi, closing) on midnight-blue and on forest-green with different output_filename; VisibleSlideKeys of slide 4 (closing, slideLayout5) is equal in both files although slideMaster1.xml and theme1.xml differ. stabilizeSlidePNGs stores images by that key, so render_deck_thumbnails can hand back the midnight-blue image for the forest-green slide. Found while fixing go-slide-creator-o477e, which needs the key to be right; fixed on that branch in internal/render/slide_identity.go (master to layout relationships are not followed; a digest computed inside a cycle is not memoised) with a case in TestVisibleSlideKeys. close_reason: Fixed by 93e57ced with go-slide-creator-o477e: VisibleSlideKeys no longer memoises the layout digest inside the master/layout cycle, so a slide key includes its master and theme; case added to TestVisibleSlideKeys. CI run 37328021336 green.

title: A labelled image placeholder bypasses readiness findings in the copy-ready image_case example
description:
## Reproduction
Current source 9a6816674a471cf3fd9362fb6274665a0686fa3d / schema 4.164.0. Fetch list_slide_kinds(kinds=["image_case"], fields=["example"]). Render its example on midnight-blue. The example supplies image_label:"Photo of the cutover room" but no image/photo/screenshot. render_deck_spec returns ok:true, deterministic_ready:true and no diagnostics. Its rendered left half is a dashed rectangle reading Image placeholder / Photo of the cutover room. The case-study caption describes a photo that is absent.

## Root cause
internal/semantic/kind_examples.go:142-146 deliberately substitutes image_label for an image. internal/semantic/validate.go:967-973 suppresses SEMANTIC_IMAGE_MISSING when image_label/placeholder is nonempty. The weak-content scan sees only the input strings; the literal Image placeholder is generated later by internal/patterns/image_text_split.go:451. TestImageCaseWithoutImageWarns explicitly asserts that labelled placeholders receive no missing-image diagnostic (kinds_g9b_test.go:54-56). Thus an intentional draft placeholder is indistinguishable from a final image in the readiness summary, contrary to the MCP initialization rule never to ship placeholder content.

## Scope and severity
P2: the manual visual review step still works and is an effective last defense. The audit submitted changes_requested with a P1 missing_content finding; the server correctly kept publishable:false. This is NOT a claim that render alone publishes the deck. Preserve deliberate placeholders for wireframes/drafts, but carry their incomplete status to the agent and publication gate. A labelled empty picture should not erase the signal that the picture remains to be supplied.

## Evidence and prior work
Call 50 generates the example without findings; call 77 renders the visible placeholder; call 97 records the visual rejection. Durable evidence: tests/quality/results/mcp-quality-audit-20261005/ (image-case-placeholder.jpeg, compact transcript, exact input). Related closed zj4yq fixed the raw-path wording and made labelled placeholders deliberate. Closed 327g6 promised detection of every product-emitted placeholder. This residual is the generated placeholder bypass, not a duplicate of the old Add an image (values.image.path) text defect.
acceptance_criteria: Labelled missing images may render as drafts, but return an explicit field-addressable incomplete-asset/placeholder finding and cannot be marked ready for delivery until supplied or the slide is intentionally changed to a text-only kind. Missing-image signalling must survive an image_label, its alias, and custom label text. Copy-ready examples should disclose the needed asset in the MCP response. Add an end-to-end MCP regression covering example -> render -> thumbnails -> readiness, plus an actual-image control and a deliberate draft/wireframe control.
notes: Implemented in ce09f057. Reviewed and pruned redundant strictness/alias combinations and duplicate image embedding checks; retained real PPTX totals styling, all-kind schema validation, readiness controls, and thumbnail/review publication regression. All 2400 CLI tests executed with race coverage in four CI shards; only the skill bundle size check failed and passed after prose compression. Remaining root packages executed with race coverage; two obsolete schema assertions were removed/replaced, and the entire semantic package passed on rerun. Focused final race regressions, svggen race suite, pinned lint, build, formatting, and skill sync passed. Combined root coverage 83.1%. No images or audit-history commits included; preview manifests change only diagnostic-source provenance. Serial CLI timeout/documentation follow-up remains go-slide-creator-vs5gp.
close_reason: Implemented, reviewed for necessary test coverage, and validated; both regressions fixed.

title: CI coverage threshold step can never fail: grep total matches two lines
description: In .github/workflows/ci.yml job test, step Check coverage threshold reads COVERAGE with: go tool cover -func=coverage.out | grep total | awk print-third-field. The merged profile has a function with total in its name, so COVERAGE is two lines (CI run 37222013440 printed: Total coverage: 100.0 then 83.1% meets threshold 70%). The bc comparison then prints two lines and the bash arithmetic test is a syntax error, which is false, so the step passes whatever the coverage is. Reproduction: feed the step a summary with one function line containing total at 100.0% and total: at 60.0%; observed: syntax error in expression, step continues and prints meets threshold; expected: exit 1 below 70. Fix: read only the line whose first field is total: and fail when the value is not a number. Found by m1-citime.
close_reason: Fixed and merged to main in schema 4.164.0 (2026-10-04); verified by the owning agent; lint, short suite, non-short internal and svggen tests and the integration corpus job green on the merged tree.

title: render-slide-from-json fails with INTERNAL on a repeat call; cached MCP render answers in a different shape
description: Input: json2pptx render-slide-from-json slide.json --template midnight-blue --out a.png --format json, run twice with the same slide (slide = slides[1] of examples/basic-deck.json). title: Type step and canvas scale are held back or wrong where the stand-in font measure differs from the template face
description: Two symptoms of one cause. (a) go-slide-creator-ttpae: on business-template several levels do not scale because the conservative Liberation Sans stand-in says the text would lose its line (swimlane step text, kpi-5up/6up values, contact-directory initials). Acceptance: the fit decision for stepping/scaling uses the template face metrics where available (internal/textfit), and no pattern relies on a stored fontScale to make text fit; an exemplar sweep finds no sibling shapes rendered at different sizes (SIBLING_SIZE_MISMATCH) on the 9 shipped templates + p-style.

title: No repeatable check that the agent journey stays good
description:
## Journey stage
review

## What happened to the agent
This review used five first-time-user agents against the live MCP server and CLI. Their enjoyment scores were 6-7 of 10
and the same classes of friction appeared in every journey, but nothing in the repository measures them, so they will
regress unnoticed.

- tests/quality/results/agent-journey-20261003/harness/ (bridge and brief used)

The journeys are a tracked evaluation with metrics over time.

Root cause was not investigated in code unless stated; the journey agents saw only the product's own output.
acceptance_criteria:

Deterministic journey metrics are asserted in tests: onboarding bytes, calls and round-trips to a first clean render for a
fixed spec, validate/render parity, and that every emitted patch clears its finding.

title: Renders leave sidecars and hundreds of megabytes of temp files behind
description:
## Journey stage
delivery

## What happened to the agent
The machine holds 2,465 `json2pptx-lo-*` temp directories (617 MB) and 311 MB of layout previews; an undocumented
`<deck>.pptx.authoring.json` sidecar is written next to every deck and is left behind for renders that failed (no pptx).

## Evidence

- This session: t-*.pptx.authoring.json files without a pptx after refused renders.

## Expected
Temp directories are removed when a command ends, caches are bounded, and sidecars are documented and consistent.

Root cause was not investigated in code unless stated; the journey agents saw only the product's own output.
acceptance_criteria:

The authoring sidecar is documented, can be turned off, and is not written for a failed render.

title: Generic autofit diagnostics misclassify KPI captions as body text
description:
## Description
A valid 10.08pt KPI caption blocks deterministic readiness because the generic OOXML autofit scan labels the entire mixed stat box as body text. Role-aware validation accepts the same revision. This is a diagnostic consistency defect, not a demonstrated visual readability failure.

## Steps to Reproduce
Render quantitative/deckspec-v4-modern.json under .claude/review-evidence/2026-10-03-consulting/. In render-v4-modern.json result.structuredContent.diagnostics[1], slide_index 7, raw_path /slides/7/rendered_shapes/206 emits TEXT_BELOW_READABLE_MIN warning: body text renders at 10.1pt below 12pt. Generation succeeds but deterministic_ready=false and slide 8 scores 80. suspect-geometry.json shows shape 206 containing 17% and FY26 EBIT margin, caption 14pt times stored autofit 72% = 10.08pt. Durable inputs/evidence: tests/quality/results/consulting-benchmark-20261003/.

## Actual Behavior
internal/generator/autofit_readability.go:104 unconditionally uses TextRoleBody in the generic XML scan. Role-aware grid validation uses caption semantics. internal/tokens/typography.go:18 explicitly classifies KPI labels as captions, with a 10pt presentation floor. The final revision has no role-aware validation readability violation.

## Expected Behavior
Generic generated-text diagnostics preserve or recover paragraph roles and agree with the documented role floors. Do not report a compliant caption as failing body text.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The reproduced 10.08pt KPI caption does not emit a false body-floor finding or prevent deterministic readiness.
- Captions genuinely below 10pt and body paragraphs below 12pt still trigger their correct findings in present mode.
- Test mixed KPI figure/caption boxes with stored autofit, and preserve stricter presentation-scale requirements where applicable.
- Validate and render agree on role and threshold; inspect slide 8 without enlarging the caption merely to evade a wrong role.

title: Plan spatial regions and preserve mixed-content requirements within a slide
description:
## Problem

plan_deck plans one kind/pattern per whole slide, so explicit requests for different visual types in named regions never become a region structure the authoring agent can fill. The tool's slots are narrative slide slots, not spatial content slots.

## Steps to Reproduce

Reproducible inputs, outputs, and screenshots are preserved in tests/quality/results/layout-composition-20261002/. The report maps this finding to the exact evidence.

## Actual Behavior and Evidence

- MCP plan_deck(format=deckspec, slide_budget=3, template=modern-yellow) was given a title, a middle slide with left65% revenue chart / top-right32% gross margin KPI / bottom-right launch timeline, and a closing ask. It returned title/decision/next_steps; no spatial layout was represented. The gross-margin KPI and final revenue point were unplaced_facts, while other revenue facts were assigned to closing.
- The matching raw_json2pptx compose control renders a legible one-slide chart+KPI+timeline using the existing engine. See mixed-control-args.json and mixed-control.png in the final evidence bundle.
- internal/deckplan/deckplan.go Slide has a single RecommendedPattern and attach skeleton code calls SkeletonForPattern once. internal/deckplan/deckspec_plan.go BuildDeckSpecPlan maps each narrative slot to one kind; neither result model carries a region tree.

## Root Cause

Planning operates at whole-slide narrative granularity only. Region relationships, type assignments and spatial size constraints are absent from the planning result model, even though raw compose can execute them.

## Expected Behavior

- Provide an explicit way to represent and retain same-slide spatial requirements, including region roles, visual types and hierarchy; avoid promising unrestricted natural-language understanding.
- The chart-left plus KPI/timeline-right request produces a fillable composition draft with every required visual mapped to a region, using the existing raw_json2pptx/compose path or a typed semantic region surface.
- Preserve all required facts and report any unsupported region requirement explicitly rather than converting it into an unrelated closing fact.
- Exercise both default DeckSpec planning and raw planning, validate the generated draft after filling values, and inspect the final mixed-region slide.

## Scope and Prior Work

title: Keep exhibit callouts attached to source-image points through crop and layout changes
description:
## Problem

A product demo or operational case study uses one screenshot/photo as evidence. Two numbered callouts should identify a delayed queue and its status badge. The same exhibit must render on templates with different content regions and picture aspect ratios.

## Steps to Reproduce

Reproducible inputs, outputs, and screenshots are preserved in tests/quality/results/layout-composition-20261002/. The report maps this finding to the exact evidence.

## Actual Behavior and Evidence

Image-text-split pairs image and narrative but does not bind each statement to a location in the image. Existing overlay endpoints are slide percentages or named points on the grid-cell rectangle; no source-image coordinates or image crop transform is available to their resolver. A marker placed at one global percentage must be recomputed when frame/crop changes.

## Root Cause

See renderer and authoring pointers below.

- internal/jsonschema/shapegrid.go:147 (GridImageInput has no annotations/region coordinates)
- internal/jsonschema/shapegrid.go:261 (OverlayPointInput only X/Y and AnchorCell)
- internal/jsonschema/shapegrid.go:269 (named anchor points only)
- cmd/json2pptx/overlays.go:300 (resolveOverlayPoint uses cell rectangle or slide percentages)
- internal/generator/grid_image_crop.go:13 (raster image cover crop calculated independently)
- internal/generator/image_placement.go:28 (native image placement transform)

## Expected Behavior

- Specify an image target point in intrinsic pixels or normalized source-image coordinates and a native callout label.
- Resolve its endpoint with the same contain/cover/native-placement transform used for the actual picture; leaders remain attached after changing frame aspect/template.
- Report an off-crop target instead of silently pointing at another visible region; preserve the supplied image and callout wording.
- Demonstrate a product screenshot with two labelled targets in wide and square frames, with readable native labels and leaders avoiding the labels.
- Reuse the current overlay mechanism rather than adding a generic new split or editorial pattern.

## Existing Alternative

For a fixed artifact, manually compute final image position and crop, author slide-percentage arrow endpoints, and inspect every slide. Or bake callouts into an SVG/bitmap before embedding. Both create a valid static exhibit; the first becomes stale on layout/crop changes, and the second scales callout text with the picture rather than preserving the current native readability floor.

## Geometry Evidence

A 1600x900 screenshot cover-filled into a square exposes source horizontal interval [0.21875,0.78125]. A target at source x=0.25 lands at cell x≈0.05556 rather than x=0.25. The existing named cell anchors cannot express this relation and slide-percent points do not update with the frame.

title: Make the bundled sales-pitch example a credible, actionable presentation exemplar
description:
## Problem
The shipped examples/semantic/sales_pitch.yaml compiles but its seven-slide warm-coral output is not a top-quality example for agents to imitate. The rendered market-spend chart in billions inherits Acme customer benchmark, 2025 (n=42 deployments), with no visible statement that the market figures are illustrative and no actual/forecast distinction for 2026. The partnership decision exceeds its own visual label budget, falls back to plain bullets, and repeats the pilot recommendation. The final slide says ready to start when you are without an actionable next step, accountable role or timing.

## Evidence
All seven slides were rendered and visually inspected via MCP. validate_deck_spec reports decision option 2 label 66 characters >60, INPUT.SEMANTIC_PATTERN_DEGRADED on slides[5].options. render_deck_spec gives score99/deterministic_ready=true; the all-slide visual review records changes_requested. See tests/quality/results/output-quality-20261002/report.json and sales-market-source.png, sales-decision-fallback.png, sales-closing.png.

## Root Cause and Scope
This is example authoring, not renderer fabrication: the broad default source, market values, long option text and vague closing are authored in examples/semantic/sales_pitch.yaml. internal/semantic/slides/decision.go deliberately falls back when labels exceed decisionLabelMax=60. Retain that guard; make the canonical example fit it, using concise labels plus details. The existing closed ixfrr only removed an unsupported section subtitle; the open QBR chronology bead z99un covers a different example.

## Requested Change
Clearly disclose illustrative data and distinguish market assumptions/projections from the customer benchmark. Give the alternatives concise labels with useful supporting detail so the comparison and recommendation render visually. End with a concrete pilot decision/next action, role and timing (clearly illustrative rather than invented real commitments). Inspect the full revised deck, not only its schema validity.
acceptance_criteria: Rendered sales_pitch shows appropriate evidence/projection disclosure, retains its visual decision treatment without SEMANTIC_PATTERN_DEGRADED, and closes with a concrete pilot action/owner/timing; review every slide and record before/after evidence.
close_reason: sales_pitch.yaml discloses illustrative data and forecasts, decision labels fit the visual pattern, closes on next_steps with owners and timing; fixture test added.

title: Negative bar labels overlap category names because the lower plot edge has no label clearance
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
Render the tracked output-quality-20261002 report's modern-yellow or p-style spec via MCP. Slide 4 is chart_insight/bar_chart with categories North, West, South, East and values [9,4,0,-2]. Render and inspect the full slide at density 100.

## Actual Behavior
The negative value −2 crowds/overlaps East even though both labels are short and the chart is sparse. The same geometry fails on two templates. MCP reports diagram.text_overlap at 55% (info) and still gives deterministic_ready=true / score 98. In modern-yellow's embedded SVG, East baseline y=332.6362 with font 19.2px, and −2 baseline y=319.6724 with font 16px, at identical x=683.3782: only 12.9638px separates baselines. The rendered PNG confirms the collision.

## Expected Behavior
Negative values, category labels and the zero baseline remain clearly separated without requiring the agent to shorten a four-letter category or suppress data labels.

## Root Cause
svggen/charts.go builds the scale from yMin and withBarTopHeadroom(yMax); only positive maxima receive explicit label clearance. drawLabelledAxes places categories below plotArea.Y+plotArea.H. svggen/series.go drawValueLabel puts negative values below the bar endpoint using TextBaselineTop. A minimum exactly on the domain boundary consumes the same bottom band as the categories. Reserve measured lower clearance or position the negative annotation safely; use consistent geometry in the axes and direct-label paths.

## Evidence and Scope
Report and PNG negative-bar-label.png: tests/quality/results/output-quality-20261002/. Source verified in embedded image3.svg in both PPTX files. Related closed go-slide-creator-xv1k only added positive top headroom; go-slide-creator-s1uvj.29 concerns stacked domains, not this non-stacked label collision. Existing headroom tests pass.

## Validation
Include mixed-sign and all-negative series with minima exactly on nice tick boundaries, short and long category labels, and before/after rendered slides in both templates.
acceptance_criteria: The [9,4,0,-2] chart has a clear gap between −2 and East on both templates, with no text_overlap finding; test lower-edge clearance for mixed-sign and all-negative data while preserving the zero baseline and positive-label clearance.
close_reason: svggen default label precision keeps small distinct values (up to 4 decimals, nonzero never prints zero); bar scale reserves measured lower clearance for negative labels.

title: DeckSpec planner misses explicit Compare A with B requests and recommends a single-stat slide
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Real MCP plan_deck(format=deckspec, slide_budget=12) brief: Compare internal support (€0.8m per year) with outsourcing (€0.5m per year) on cost and launch speed. Recommend internal support to retain customer relationships.

The explicit recommendation and its rationale are absent from all slots[].facts and unplaced_facts=[]. Spare budget exists, so this is not budget pruning.
Root: internal/deckplan/deckspec_plan.go cueOptions accepts enumerated options, options evaluated against criteria, or build/buy wording but not compare X with Y. facts.go factOption similarly omits compare/compared; extractBriefFacts excludes recommendation clauses without a number, acronym, proper noun, or recognized option token before classifyFact can route them. The numeric comparison is then classified as one metric. This frustrates the advertised brief-sensitive storyline path.
Related closed khzni and gvbw8, but this exact ordinary comparison syntax remains broken. Evidence comparison-plan.json and decimal-plan.json in .claude/review-evidence/2026-10-02.

Include positive Compare/compare with/compared to tests and negative benchmark cases (revenue compared with plan) so benchmark facts remain metrics.

title: Shipped QBR example mixes Q2 review, completed Q4 results and ARR versus revenue measures
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

The recommended semantic authoring example examples/semantic/qbr.yaml renders cleanly and scores 99, but its evidence is internally inconsistent. Cover is Q2 FY26 / path to H2; summary says Q2 revenue grew 18% QoQ. The chart presents completed Q1–Q4 FY26 quarterly revenue [34,40,44,48], calls the Q4 launch already landed, then claims continued acceleration into H2. The chart Q2/Q1 growth is 17.65% (consistent with 18%), but future Q3/Q4 values are never marked forecast. Slide 3 calls $48M Annual recurring revenue; the chart labels the same 48 as quarterly revenue ($M) without distinguishing measures. A Q2 board deck cannot establish Q4 actuals and then discuss the coming H2 in the same fiscal year without explaining chronology.
Root: authored content in examples/semantic/qbr.yaml and the examples' semantic correctness coverage, not chart math or slide layout. Agents are explicitly encouraged to copy examples, so these labels can seed polished but misleading decks. Do not attempt a generic deterministic prose truth detector as the fix.
Evidence: qbr-validate.json no issues; qbr-score.json overall 99, gate true; rendered slide 1 and 4, OOXML text. Existing closed zvu7c corrected duplicate callouts, not period/measure consistency.
acceptance_criteria: Choose a coherent as-of date and period: use historical quarters through Q2, or label Q3/Q4 forecast explicitly, or convert the whole deck to a year-end review. Distinguish ARR from period revenue. Check every title, source, KPI label, chart and closing deadline against that same chronology, and add a focused fixture-content check for the chosen labels.
close_reason: qbr.yaml is now a coherent Q2 FY26 review with actuals through Q2 and ARR distinct from quarterly revenue; chronology fixture test added.

title: Pattern text sizing measures Calibri with Carlito while the writer's autofit measures Liberation Sans
description: Found while fixing the phase-roadmap corpus regression (2026-10-02, commit eaf8df2b). Pattern row sizing (textBlockHeightPt / theme-font model) now measures the theme body font Calibri with the embedded metric clone Carlito (svggen/fontcache metric_clones.go), but the writer's autofit (internal/pptx/autofit.go AutofitScaleFor / AutofitFitsFor, autofitFontName) always measures with Liberation Sans. Carlito is narrower, so text the pattern thinks fits in N lines needs N+1 by the writer: the writer stores an autofit shrink. phase-roadmap got a written-fit backstop (writtenNeedOrOverflowPt), but ~19 other model-only textBlockHeightPt call sites remain exposed on Calibri templates (modern, business-template, forest-green, midnight-blue...): their text can be written slightly shrunk above 12pt (or refused below it). Expected: one measurement font for sizing and writing — either the writer resolves the same font as the model (Carlito for Calibri) or the model uses the writer's font — with the remaining model-only call sites backstopped by the written fit; add a sweep test asserting no stored autofit shrink for in-budget exemplars on Calibri templates.

title: bullet_groups spacing does not group: gap after a header can exceed the gap before it
description:

Gestalt proximity is the whole point of bullet groups. Also the sub-bullets take the master's level-2 indent (forest-green marL 768096 = 60pt, abstract 54pt) under a flush-left header, wasting a sixth of the column. Expected: header spcBef >= 1.5x the bullet pitch, header spcAft ~2-4pt, first sub-bullet spcBef 0, and a capped sub-bullet indent (~18-24pt from the header's left edge) independent of the master's deep level-2 margin.

title: Pattern/grid zone starts at the title bottom, not the body placeholder: content-sized rows float mid-slide (SLIDE_UNDERU
description:
fallbackContentZone sets ContentZone.TitleBottom from the title placeholder (cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go:150-165) and DefaultBoundsFromZone adds a fixed 9pt gap (shapegrid/bounds.go:32-35, shape_grid.go:681/711), ignoring where the layout's body placeholder actually begins. Content-sized patterns (card-grid, kpi-Nup, quote-cluster... via contentSizedRow MaxHeight, patterns/content_fit_text.go:98-128) then get a non-stretch VAlign (shapegrid/grid.go:730-740) and are centred in that zone. Two visible consequences: (1) native and pattern slides in the same deck start their content at different heights — on p-style native body text starts at y=185px (out-p-style/slide-02.png) while comparison-2col starts at y=90px, hard against the title (out-p-style/slide-14.png); (2) a 3-card row sits as an island in the vertical middle with ~200px of white above it and the title orphaned at the top (out-p-style/slide-12.png, out-p-style/slide-13.png, out-abstract/slide-12.png, out-abstract/slide-13.png, out-forest-green/slide-12.png, out-modern-template/slide-12.png). Consulting layouts hang content from the title with a consistent title-to-content gap across every slide. Expected: zone top = the layout's body/content placeholder top when one exists (or title bottom + the template's own title-to-body gap), and content-sized blocks top-anchored (or centred only when they fill > ~60% of the zone).

Merged findings from other review areas:
- [visual-semantic] roadmap, timeline, framework and team defaults float a thin band mid-slide (SLIDE_UNDERUSED on 4 kinds): Rendering the kind examples with default geometry leaves large dead zones above and below the content on roadmap (phase-roadmap with no milestones: 3 header boxes + a line + one caption each), timeline, framework (SWOT grid at 28-38% of its allocated height: 'sparse_layout' on slide 13) and team (three grey tiles + 3 lines). The render gate reports SLIDE_UNDERUSED on slides 17, 18, 21, 28 on every template (27-29% of the safe area) and sparse_layout for SWOT; p-style additionally 23/24. Evidence: abstract/slide-18.png (roadmap: 100px gap above, 150px below), abstract/slide-19.png, modern-yellow/slide-14.png (SWOT centred in the middle third), abstract/slide-21.png (team), midnight-blue/slide-18.png. The top margin also varies by kind on p-style: process/comparison/decision/architecture start ~35px under the title while SWOT/roadmap/timeline start 100-180px lower (p-style/slide-10.png vs p-style/slide-14.png). The agent did nothing wrong; the defaults waste the slide and feel inconsistent slide to slide.

ACCEPTANCE:
On a deck mixing native bullets and card-grid/kpi-3up/comparison-2col slides, the first content pixel row on pattern slides is within 6pt of the native body placeholder top for abstract, p-style, forest-green and modern-template; a content-sized row shorter than 60% of the zone is anchored at the zone top (VAlignTop) by default with an override to centre. Golden fixtures and SKILL.md note the rule.
Default geometry for roadmap/timeline/framework/team is top-anchored under the title with content-sized height (or fills >=35% of the safe area via capped growth), so the kind examples render without SLIDE_UNDERUSED/sparse_layout on abstract, midnight-blue and p-style; content-top offset is consistent (within ~10pt) across kinds on blank-title.

title: No per-slide text-density ceiling: 6+ bullets and 80 words per placeholder pass every gate
description:
Principle: slides fail the glance test above roughly 5-6 bullets / ~75 words, and on-screen text that duplicates narration hurts comprehension (6x6 rule, https://ethos3.com/6-reasons-the-6x6-rule-works/; '75 words' / 'max 5 bullets' thresholds, https://veeso.ai/blog/presentation-slide-density-guide; Mayer/Sweller redundancy effect, https://www.speakwithpersuasion.com/lot-of-text-on-slides/; Reynolds signal-to-noise, https://www.garrreynolds.com/design-tips). Repo: the only ceilings are per PLACEHOLDER — `maxBodyWords = 80` and `maxHeadlineWords = 12` (cmd/json2pptx/fit_findings_content_lint.go:18-27) — and a bullets>8 deduction that exists only in the input-only quality score (json_mode.go:2049-2202), not in score_deck or validate_deck_spec; DeckSpec kinds accept 'one to six insights' (DECKSPEC.md chart insight row) and `comparison` up to ten rows per column with no density finding. Evidence: topic-titles.yaml chart_insight with 6 two-line insights validated `ok: true`; a two-column slide may legally carry 2x80 words. `SEMANTIC_DENSITY` exists but is advisory and keyed to visual budgets, not words. Why it matters: text walls are the most common agent failure after topic titles, and today nothing deterministic says 'too many words on this slide'.

ACCEPTANCE:
A slide-level finding (e.g. `SLIDE_TEXT_DENSE`, review) fires when total body words > ~75 (configurable per `viewing_mode`: ~60 live, ~110 report), bullets > 6, or a bullet wraps beyond 2 lines at its rendered size, with a `split_slide`/`shorten` fix; it is included in score_deck weighting and documented in docs/FIT_FINDINGS.md and SKILL.md; kinds' item_schema maxItems for insights/points align with the ceiling.

title: analyze_deck_rhythm ignores narrative structure and nudges toward MORE accent; ignores pattern AccentWeight
description:
The tool is sold as the pre-generation monotony/accent check (SKILL.md, RAW_PATH.md:131-142, WORKFLOW.md Phase 2) but internal/rhythm/rhythm.go:460-513 only produces three recommendation types: runs >=3 of one family, >=5-cell slides with one accent, and >30% underfilled cells. It never reports a missing executive summary, missing next-steps/closer, absence of section dividers or agenda on long decks, slides without takeaway/source, or a bullets-heavy deck below the run threshold: the 9-slide mixed.json deck (5 topic-titled bullet slides, no sources, 'Thank you' close) gets composition_score 90 and recs []. accent_balance is {} for both the bullets deck and the compiled QBR DeckSpec because accents are only read from raw shape_grid cell fills (cmd/json2pptx/mcp_analyze_rhythm.go:115-128), so on the default DeckSpec/pattern path the 'accent imbalance' metric is never measured and accent_dominance can never fire. For the all-bullets deck the break suggestions are stat-hero, comparison-2col, timeline-horizontal (breakPreferences default, rhythm.go:591-593) regardless of what the slides say — timeline-horizontal for a margin-analysis bullet slide is exactly the decorative use RULES.md:178 forbids.

Merged findings from other review areas:
- [visual-patterns] analyze_deck_rhythm nudges agents toward MORE accent and ignores pattern AccentWeight: internal/rhythm/rhythm.go:482-495 emits, for every slide with >=5 cells and a single accent, the recommendation 'slide N has K cells but only 1 accent — add cell_accent_mode: progressive to the pattern overrides for visual hierarchy'. That fires on card-grid, kpi-5up/6up, roadmap-phased, framework-grid, bmc-canvas etc. — i.e. exactly the slides that are already restrained — and pushes agents to rotate accents across cells, the opposite of the one-emphasis-per-slide standard. Meanwhile the taxonomy AccentWeight ("strong" on 10 patterns, e.g. hero-detail herodetail.go:42, process-grid-2row, kpi-inline) is exposed in list_patterns (cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:1975, skill_info.go:195) but is never consumed: computeAccentBalance (:372) only counts which accent role is used, SKILL.md has no accent-weight guidance (grep -i accent skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md only hits chart highlight notes), and no rule flags a run of strong-accent slides or a slide whose cells are mostly solid accent (see roadmap-phased/process-flow findings). Expected: drop or invert the single-accent rule (recommend progressive accents only when the slide expresses ordered/graded data), add an accent-heaviness check (share of cells with solid accent fill, consecutive AccentWeight=strong slides) and document the AccentWeight field in SKILL.md.

ACCEPTANCE:
analyze_deck_rhythm emits recommendations for: no executive_summary/exec-summary in a deck >= 6 slides; closing without next-steps; >= 10 content slides with no section/agenda; evidence slides lacking takeaway or source; >= 3 bullets-only slides anywhere in the deck. accent_balance is computed for pattern slides from the pattern's resolved accent (accent_strategy + cell_accent_mode). Break suggestions for native-content runs are derived from the slide's content (numbers -> kpi/stat, options -> comparison, dates -> timeline) and never propose timeline-horizontal without date-like content.
analyze_deck_rhythm no longer recommends cell_accent_mode: progressive for slides whose cells are neutral-filled; it emits a recommendation when a slide has >=N solid-accent cells or when >=3 consecutive slides use AccentWeight=strong patterns; SKILL.md explains AccentWeight and the per-deck budget for strong patterns. Unit tests cover both the removed and the new rule.
