title: Pie/donut defaults: ceiling never fires for pie_chart, unsorted slices, legend + labels double-encode, highlight ignored
description:
Principle: pies are acceptable only for a coarse part-to-whole view with few slices, sorted descending from 12 o'clock, directly labelled with no legend, small slices grouped into 'Other'; otherwise use a bar (Knaflic 'What is a pie chart', https://www.storytellingwithdata.com/blog/2020/5/14/what-is-a-pie-chart; Zelazny component comparison; McKinsey: pies have 'a very narrow but legitimate role', https://umbrex.com/resources/the-busy-consultants-guide-to-quantitative-charts/pie-and-doughnut-type-charts/). Repo: (1) the slice ceiling in cmd/json2pptx/fit_findings_substance.go:710-714 switches on `"pie", "donut", "doughnut"` but the authored type is `pie_chart` / `donut_chart` (RULES.md rule 9 mandates the `_chart` underscore form), so `chartMaxSliceCategories = 7` is never applied and an 8-slice pie falls through to the generic 12-category ceiling — confirmed: `validate -fit-report` on scratchpad/review/best-practices-research/charts/deck.json reported no CHART_OVERLOADED for the 8-slice pie; (2) slices are drawn in input order (svggen/charts.go:3077-3086), no 'Other' bucketing, capabilities allow 200 categories (svggen/capabilities.go:141); (3) the default draws BOTH a right-hand legend (charts.go:2905) and outside percent labels (charts.go:2790-2798), so category names and values are split across two places. Evidence: charts/slide-2.png — 8 colours, legend plus percent labels, no 'use a bar' hint. Why it matters: pies are the chart agents reach for most often for 'share' messages; the defaults produce the exact clutter every dataviz authority warns against.

Merged findings from other review areas:
- [charts-diagrams] Pie/donut always draw a legend plus value-only outside labels; small-slice labels collide and `highlight` is ignored: svggen/chart_diagrams.go:294-297 forces the legend on every pie/donut ('ALWAYS show legend'), and svggen/charts.go:3008-3010 prints outside labels as the value only, so each slice is double-encoded (colour swatch in a legend to the right + a bare percentage outside) and the pie is pushed left with dead space on the right (.../charts-diagrams/out/charts-deck-midnight-blue/slide-07.png, slide-08.png; warm-coral slide-07.png; p-style slide-07.png). On the 7-slice donut the 2% and 1% labels overprint as '2%1%' (.../out/charts-deck-midnight-blue/slide-08.png and .../out/charts-deck-abstract/slide-08.png) because the 2 degree sweep floor in the LabelStrategy shows them without a collision pass. The slide message 'Our company leads with 35% share' cannot be expressed: `highlight` is only wired for single-series bar (svggen/charts.go:52-57, :1152-1160), so the pie paints five categorical hues including red/green on midnight-blue and a solid black slice on p-style. Expected (consulting standard): direct 'Name 35%' labels with leader lines and no legend when <= ~6 slices, grey slices with accent only on the highlighted slice, tiny slices merged into 'Other' or their labels suppressed/stacked to avoid overlap. Why it matters: pies are the most common agent-chosen chart for shares and these defaults produce a cluttered, unfocused chart on every template.

ACCEPTANCE:
`chartCategoryCeiling` matches `pie_chart`/`donut_chart` (and the bare forms) so >7 slices draw CHART_OVERLOADED with a 'use bar_chart' fix hint; pie/donut default to descending order from 12 o'clock with an optional `group_small_below_pct` (default ~3%) 'Other' bucket; when slices <= 6 the legend is suppressed and labels carry 'Name  NN%'; recommend_visual demotes pie below bar when more than 5 categories or when the top two slices are within 10% of each other; unit tests for each.
1) Pie/donut with <= 6 slices default to combined name+value outside labels (or inside for large slices) and no legend; legend only when forced via style.show_legend or above the slice cap; 2) adjacent outside labels are collision-resolved (stacked/leadered) so no two labels overlap in the 40/25/15/12/5/2/1 case; 3) `highlight` on pie/donut paints the named slices accent1 and the rest neutral, documented in SKILL.md/RULES.md; 4) capabilities LabelStrategy text updated.

title: Line charts cannot highlight one series; multi-series lines render as spaghetti + legend
description:
Principle: emphasise the one series the message is about and push the rest to grey context (Knaflic preattentive attributes; 'draw the series you care about in strong colour and push everything else into light grey', https://andymcdonaldgeo.substack.com/p/when-a-line-chart-becomes-spaghetti; Tufte: colour as a data tool). The engine already does this for bars (`defaultHighlight` + `BarNeutralInk = 0.38`, svggen/bar_highlight.go:17,153-171) but `Highlight` is only read in the bar path (svggen/charts.go:1152-1160); nothing in the line/area path greys non-focus series, markers are drawn on every point, and above 4 series the chart falls back to a bottom legend (charts.go:268-284). Evidence: scratchpad/review/best-practices-research/charts/slide-3.png — title 'EMEA is the only region still growing after Q3', five saturated lines of equal weight, markers everywhere, legend at the bottom; EMEA is not visually distinguished. QUALITY.md §4 tells the agent to 'highlight the one bar, row or cell the title is about' but gives it no lever for lines. Why it matters: multi-series trend charts are the second most common evidence slide; without emphasis they fail the 3-second glance test.

ACCEPTANCE:
`data.highlight` (indices or series names) is honoured by line/area/grouped-bar: highlighted series in accent1 (2pt), others dk1 at ~38% (1pt, no markers), highlighted series labelled at line end; default picks the series named in the slide title/takeaway when exactly one matches, else no highlight; markers off by default when points*series > ~12; recommend_visual suggests 'highlight' in its chart candidate `next_tool_call`; documented in SKILL.md/RULES.md.

title: Emphasis quota (stat-hero/pull-quote every ~5 slides) pushes agents to add filler slides
description:
Three surfaces mandate decorative 'emphasis' slides independent of the message: (1) ensureEmphasis (internal/deckplan/deckplan.go:1182-1237) rewrites every ~5th planned slide to stat-hero or pull-quote with seed 'Standout metric or memorable takeaway' — make_deck's QBR produced a pull-quote slide titled 'Standout metric or memorable takeaway' quoting Alan Kay (makedeck/slide-7.png) and a stat-hero '$2.4B Addressable AI consulting market' on a churn slide (slide-4.png); (2) score_deck's composition axis emits missing_emphasis for any deck of >=10 slides without stat-hero/pull-quote (cmd/json2pptx/mcp_score_deck.go:552-568) — it fired on the well-formed 10-slide QBR DeckSpec (score_qbr.json) whose every slide carries a sourced chart/KPI/decision; (3) WORKFLOW.md:94 'Insert a narrative-break pattern (stat-hero, pull-quote) every ~5 slides' and the plan_deck description ('an emphasis slide ... about every ~5 slides'). This contradicts QUALITY.md:80 ('Do not choose a visual because it looks varied; a card grid of topics proves nothing') and consulting practice, where a pull quote with no evidence role is clutter. An agent obeying the tools adds a quote slide to a QBR to clear the warning.

ACCEPTANCE:
ensureEmphasis only promotes a slide to stat-hero when the brief routed a single headline number to it, and never inserts pull-quote without a quoted fact; missing_emphasis is removed from score_deck composition diagnostics (or restricted to decks whose evidence slides are all dense tables/grids); WORKFLOW.md and the plan_deck description drop the 'every ~5 slides' rule in favour of 'a stat or quote slide only when the message is a single number or a stakeholder voice'.

title: abstract: One Content title placeholder sits 0.5in right and ~1in lower than Two Content / Blank + Title, so titles jump
description:

A consulting deck keeps the title on one fixed baseline across all content-family layouts.

title: DATA_WITHOUT_SOURCE is info-only and absent from validate_deck_spec; no default source
description:
Principle: 'Every data point has a source' with the source line bottom-left on every data slide (Deckary consulting slide standards, https://deckary.com/blog/consulting-slide-standards; Slideworks: 'Each slide should have a slide number and a source in the bottom section', https://slideworks.io/resources/how-mckinsey-consultants-make-presentations). Repo: QUALITY.md §5 says 'Source every number' and the engine has a good 9pt source zone (internal/generator/source_note.go), but `DATA_WITHOUT_SOURCE` has action `info` (cmd/json2pptx/fit_findings_source.go:39-70; finding_meta.go:465-479), scoring 0 points and excluded from the gate; on the default DeckSpec path `json2pptx semantic validate` on scratchpad/review/best-practices-research/topic-titles.yaml (kpi_snapshot + chart_insight with no `source`) returned `ok: true` with no source finding at all — it surfaced only later in `score`. There is no deck-level `meta.source`/`sources` default (internal/semantic/spec.go has only `meta.date` and `meta.chrome`), so a 12-slide deck from one data set needs the same string typed 10 times, and omissions are silent. Evidence: score output for topic-titles shows DATA_WITHOUT_SOURCE as `severity: info` on slides 3 and 4 while the gate passed. Why it matters: an unsourced data slide is the first thing a senior reviewer rejects; the skill says so, the engine whispers.

ACCEPTANCE:
DATA_WITHOUT_SOURCE is emitted by validate_deck_spec (mapped to `slides[N].source`) and weighted as `review` on chart/table/KPI/stat slides in score_deck; `meta.source` (DeckSpec) / top-level `source` (raw) provides a default applied to every data slide lacking its own; 'Illustrative' remains an accepted value; SKILL.md, DECKSPEC.md and docs/FIT_FINDINGS.md updated.

title: Gantt sorts swimlanes alphabetically, truncates the lane header ("Disco...") and stacks milestones as rows above the lan
description:
Input groups Discovery -> Build -> Test (chronological, as authored) render as Build, Discovery, Test because svggen/gantt.go:433-437 `sort.SliceStable` orders rows by swimlane string before `collectSwimlanes` (gantt.go:533-544) records 'order of appearance'. title: exec-summary column split: DECKSPEC.md's 90-char lead budget vs ~42-char lead column; string points leave the support co
description:
DECKSPEC.md:74 tells agents 'Each lead is at most 90 characters and support at most 200' for executive_summary. A 4-point summary with leads of 43/45/65/69 chars and one-sentence supports renders fine (two-line bold leads, scratchpad/review/agent-guidance/qbr_midnight-blue/slide-02.png) but every render reports four warning BODY_TOO_LONG 'exec-summary points[i].lead is 43 characters; 4 points hold about 42 lead characters each with this bottom line' and blocks deterministic_ready with 'quality gate: 4 substantive review finding(s) remain' (qbr_midnight-blue/render.json, same on p-style and warm-coral). The documented budget is more than double the enforced one, so a compliant agent is blocked on its first render and told to shorten conclusions to ~42 characters — shorter than most action-title clauses. The rendered layout also gives the bold conclusion column ~30% of the width and the one-line support ~55%, so the leads wrap while the supports sit in white space (slide-02.png; same on p-style slide-02.png); the pattern was sized for short leads/long supports while the guidance (QUALITY.md 'bold lead-in statements, each with one supporting sentence') asks for the opposite.

Merged findings from other review areas:
- [visual-semantic] executive_summary with plain-string points keeps an empty support column and wraps short leads: qbr.yaml (the shipped semantic example) authors executive_summary points as plain strings. execSummaryPoints accepts that (internal/semantic/slides/content.go:170-180) and the pattern still lays out number / lead / support columns, so the lead sits in the fixed ~30% lead column while the support column (60% of the width) is blank on every row; 'Revenue grew 18% QoQ, ahead of plan.' wraps to two lines next to 600px of white space. Evidence: abstract/slide-29.png, modern-yellow/slide-29.png, midnight-blue/slide-29.png, warm-coral/slide-29.png. Combined with content-sized rows the slide is four short bold fragments spread down the left third.

ACCEPTANCE:
DECKSPEC.md and list_slide_kinds publish the real per-count lead/support budgets (with and without bottom_line) and the pattern's BODY_TOO_LONG for exec-summary is not classified as a gate-blocking substantive review when the text fits on two lines; exec-summary gives the lead column >= 45% width (or wraps supports first). The review QBR spec renders deterministic_ready=true with no BODY_TOO_LONG.
When no point carries support, the lead cell spans the lead+support columns (or the compiler emits a single-column variant); rendered QBR exec summary shows each lead on one line across the full width. Pattern test covers the all-leads case.

title: Multi-series charts rotate through raw template accents (alert red/green) and fall back to solid black series
description:
Series colours come from `distinctSeriesPalette` (svggen/series_colors.go:56-98): the template accents in declared order, with `p.TextSecondary` / `p.TextPrimary` as the first fallbacks when neighbouring accents are too close (lines 80-85). On midnight-blue a 3-series grouped bar is blue / red / yellow and the stacked bar's second series is red (.../charts-diagrams/out/charts-deck-midnight-blue/slide-03.png, slide-04.png); on p-style (accents FD5108, FE7C39, FFAA72, A1A8B3, ..., dk1/dk2 = 000000) the third region is painted solid black (.../out/charts-deck-p-style/slide-03.png) and the pie gets a black slice (p-style slide-07.png); on abstract the same chart is brown / blue / orange. The funnel already avoids this ('Stages take a single-hue ramp of accent1 ... so no stage is painted in the template's alert red', capabilities.go:208) but bar/line/pie/stacked/treemap do not. Consulting standard: series ordered accent1 -> tonal ramp of accent1 (or accent1 + neutral greys) with red reserved for negatives; never text ink as a data colour. Why it matters: red/green series carry unintended meaning ('EMEA is bad'), and black bars on p-style look like a rendering fault.

ACCEPTANCE:
1) Default multi-series palette for bar/grouped/stacked/line/area/pie/donut/treemap is a tonal ramp of accent1 plus neutral greys (or the template's declared data_palette when present), not raw accent rotation; 2) TextPrimary/TextSecondary are never chosen as a series fill; 3) a per-template test asserts no series colour has ΔE < 25 to the template's dk1 and that colours with a 'negative' semantic role are not assigned to positive-only series; 4) SKILL.md/RULES.md explain how to request categorical colours when semantically needed.

title: RULES.md tells agents charts accept `subtitle` and `footnote`; the validator rejects both as unknown fields
description:
skills/generate-deck/RULES.md:227-229 ('Charts: Subtitle vs Footnote — Charts accept both `subtitle` and `footnote` fields ... `footnote` for source attribution rendered at the chart bottom'). internal/types/chart.go:16-58 (ChartValue) has no Subtitle or Footnote field and the input schema is closed, so `json2pptx validate` on a chart_value carrying them reports `unknown field "footnote"` and `unknown field "subtitle" (did you mean "title"?)` (probe: .../charts-diagrams/probe.json, slide 1) and the generator drops them. svggen itself supports Subtitle/Footnote on the RequestEnvelope (chart_render.go:366 forwards `spec.Subtitle` for diagrams; CartesianLayout takes data.Subtitle/data.Footnote), so the renderer is ready and only the chart_value surface is missing. There is also no chart-level `source` treatment on the raw chart path, whereas the pattern path has `values.source` (QUALITY.md:51-55 requires a source line on every data slide). Why it matters: agents follow the rule, lose the source attribution silently, and the chart ships without the required source line.

ACCEPTANCE:
1) ChartValue accepts `subtitle` and `footnote` (or `source`) and forwards them to svggen so they render under the chart title / at the chart bottom; 2) validate no longer warns for them; 3) RULES.md matches the real field names and placement; 4) an example in examples/charts.json uses `footnote`; 5) test asserts the footnote text appears in the SVG.

title: body_and_lead hardcodes 16pt lead / 12pt bullets regardless of template, density and space
description:
setBodyAndLeadParagraphs forces FontSize "1600" on the lead and "1200" on every bullet (internal/generator/text_population.go:697-722; deckinput.go:493-494 documents the same). It is the only body content type that bypasses BodySizeForDensity (body_typography.go:21-33; shouldNormalizeBodyTypography text_population.go:... excludes ContentBodyAndLead) so a 4-bullet slide renders a 16pt sentence over 12pt footnote-sized bullets and leaves ~60% of the body placeholder empty, while the plain-bullets slide next to it runs 18-20pt. On p-style the hardcoded 12pt also inherits the master's lvl3 lnSpc 125% + spcBef (tpl/p-style master lvl3) so 12pt lines sit on a 27px (2.0x) pitch. PNG evidence: out-abstract/slide-07.png, out-p-style/slide-07.png, out-forest-green/slide-07.png, out-modern-template/slide-07.png (compare body size with slide-02.png on each). Expected: lead and bullets sized from the same density policy as bullets (e.g. bullets at the density target, lead one or two scale steps above, both capped by measured fit), so the thesis/evidence hierarchy stays but the text fills the slide at readable size.

ACCEPTANCE:
body_and_lead with <= 6 bullets renders bullets at >= 14pt (the density target, within BodySizePolicy) and the lead one step above (>= 16pt bold), on all shipped templates; the lead/bullet ratio is preserved under autofit; a test asserts no hardcoded 1200/1600 when the placeholder has room; docs/INPUT_FORMAT.md and SKILL.md updated.

title: Unify the left edge: grid cell inset (14pt) vs placeholder inset vs takeaway band — pattern text and callouts never alig
description:

Consulting decks keep one left alignment line for title, body and exhibits. Expected: either shift grid bounds left by (cell inset - placeholder inset) when the first column has no fill/outline on its left edge, or expose the optical left edge to patterns so unfilled first-column text (numerals, labels, rules) starts at the placeholder text edge.

Merged findings from other review areas:
- [visual-semantic] Takeaway band left edge does not align with pattern content or pattern callouts: The generator's takeaway/source bands take their left edge from the chrome frame (internal/template/chrome_frame.go:102-115: contentSpan(layout) else 3.75% margin) while shape-grid patterns size against their own content area, so on abstract the takeaway bar sits at x~118px when every pattern (KPI cards, stat, table, pattern callouts) starts at x~73-78px; on midnight-blue 113 vs 108; the source line sits at yet another x. A test compares the first-column text x against the title placeholder x + lIns.

title: Contrast fixer strips brand accent from hero numbers on warm-accent templates (p-style, warm-coral)
description:
The contrast pass chooses a text body's threshold from its SMALLEST run (internal/generator/text_contrast.go:414-421 smallestTextPt) and only whitelists accents that clear 4.5:1 (text_contrast.go:212-219), so an accent that passes WCAG large-text 3:1 is swapped out even on 40-100pt display numbers. On p-style (accent1 #FD5108, 3.3:1 on white) every KPI value, the stat hero, 'Key Insights' headers, team initials and callout text go black (render log: contrast_predicted '#FD5108 -> #000000' on slides 5, 6, 12, 14, 18, 20, 22, 30); on warm-coral (#E64A19, 3.9:1) they go dark brown. Evidence: p-style/slide-05.png and slide-30.png (black KPI values), p-style/slide-06.png (black $2.4B hero), warm-coral/slide-06.png, warm-coral/slide-07.png (Key Insights header dark while the bar is accent). The deck loses its accent exactly where consulting slides put it: the big number. Also the auto-fix on the p-style section slide only reaches 3.0 (log: '#FD5108 -> #F34E08 ratio 2.8 -> 3.0'), so the fixer accepts 3:1 there but not for the 60pt hero.

ACCEPTANCE:
Runs >=18pt (or >=14pt bold) keep an accent that clears 3:1; mixed-size bodies are evaluated per run (or split) so an 11pt label is fixed while the 40pt value keeps the accent; when a fix is needed for large text prefer the minimal darken (lerp) of the accent over dk1. Rendered p-style and warm-coral kpi_snapshot/stat examples show accent-coloured values; existing go-slide-creator-9ux4 small-text behaviour unchanged.

description:

description:

title: Stacked-bar segment labels: fixed 8pt, mixed precisions, bypass ValueFormatter, no stack totals
description:
Principle: one notation per chart (IBCS UNIFY/CHECK: consistent number formats and scaling, https://www.ibcs.com/standards/); readable labels (the repo's own 10pt caption floor, internal/tokens/typography.go:49-84); stacked columns normally show the total above each stack. Repo: svggen/charts.go:1248 sizes segment labels as `math.Max(7, math.Min(8, style.Typography.SizeCaption))`, which always yields 8pt because SizeCaption >= 10 — below the floor every other label obeys; labels use a hardcoded `%.0f`/`%.1f` (charts.go:1245-1299) and bypass the shared ValueFmt/`value_format`, so one stack shows '12' next to '5.0' and '3.0'; there is no stack-total label, no `normalize: percent` (100%-stacked) mode and no 'Other' bucketing. Evidence: scratchpad/review/best-practices-research/charts/slide-5.png — segment labels '12', '5.0', '3.0' in the same column, tiny text, totals absent. Why it matters: stacked bars are the standard 'composition over time' visual; mixed decimals and 8pt labels read as sloppy at projection size and contradict the engine's readability guarantees.

Merged findings from other review areas:
- [charts-diagrams] Stacked bar segment labels mix precisions in one chart ("8.1" next to "10") and no stack totals are shown: svggen/charts.go:1283 formats stacked segment labels with the rule 'integers if >= 10, one decimal if < 10', bypassing the chart-wide ValueFormatter that value_format.go:170-215 explicitly introduced so that one chart never prints two number formats. Result: Subscription reads 8.1 / 9.6 / 10 / 12 for values 8.1 / 9.6 / 10.4 / 12.2 while the sibling segments read 2.4, 2.0, 3.1 (.../charts-diagrams/out/charts-deck-midnight-blue/slide-04.png, .../out/charts-deck-warm-coral/slide-04.png). The segment labels are also hard-coded to 7-8pt (charts.go:1248 `math.Max(7, math.Min(8, ...))`), and there is no total above each stack even though a stacked bar's primary message is usually the total. Expected: segment labels go through `config.ValueFmt` like every other label, totals drawn above each bar (ValueFmt-formatted) by default when ShowValues is on, and segment labels inherit the type-scale small size rather than a 7pt constant. Why it matters: inconsistent precision looks like a data error to a finance audience, and a mix chart without totals forces mental arithmetic.

ACCEPTANCE:
Stacked segment labels use the chart's shared value formatter (same decimals/thousands/compact rules as axis ticks), are >= 10pt or suppressed when the segment is too small, and a total label is drawn above each stack by default (`show_totals` to disable); `normalize: "percent"` renders a 100%-stacked variant; a svggen test asserts no label below the caption floor and uniform decimals within a chart.
1) Stacked bar segment labels use the resolved ValueFormatter (same precision as the axis/data labels; 10.4 renders as 10.4 when 8.1 renders as 8.1); 2) stack totals are drawn above each positive stack when values are shown, suppressed via data_labels:false; 3) segment label font comes from Typography.SizeSmall (>= 10pt floor) not a 7-8pt constant; 4) unit test on [8.1, 9.6, 10.4, 12.2] asserts uniform decimals.

Expected: neutral-tinted steps with dk1 text (accent reserved for the decision diamond or a highlighted step), connectors in the same accent/dk2 used elsewhere, and a height derived from the written fit (like value-chain) instead of a fixed 45% band.

Merged findings from other review areas:
- [visual-semantic] process kind with bare labels renders four giant solid-accent boxes and an empty lower half: The built-in process example (steps: Qualify / Discover / Propose / Close) compiles to process-flow; processFlowSparse caps it at processFlowSparseHeightPct=50 (internal/semantic/slides/visual.go:366-385) but the result is still four ~155-180px tall full-saturation accent blocks each holding one 9-11pt word, with the bottom 50% of the slide blank and the takeaway floating at the bottom. process-flow-compact (height-capped ~35%, built for short labels) is never selected by ProcessPattern (visual.go:531-551). Not flagged by SPARSE_FILL because each box is <10% of the slide. Four saturated accent slabs for four words is the opposite of restrained accent use.

ACCEPTANCE:
Default process-flow render uses at most one solid-accent shape per slide (decision or highlighted step); connector colour matches the accent used by before-after/value-chain; step height is content-sized with a cap at or below ~30% of the content area so a 4-step exemplar no longer produces >150px blocks at 80dpi. process-flow-compact is visibly shorter than process-flow for the same payload.
A 3-6 step process with labels averaging <40 chars and no descriptions compiles to a compact flow (box height <= ~2.5x the label size, or process-flow-compact / numbered-step-strip stacked-box) and the rendered slide covers >=35% of the safe area or is top-anchored under the title; rendered boxes are not solid accent fills unless the deck's accent strategy asks for it.

title: MCPResultFor loses isError on modern protocol without text fallback
description: MCPSuccessResult omits Content on negotiated 2025-06-18; MCPResultFor only checks firstTextContent, so a top-level ok:false or success:false producer payload is returned with IsError=false. Derive the protocol-level failure flag from the payload independently of Content, and cover modern and legacy protocols.
close_reason: Modern MCP results now include a <=1 KB actionable text synopsis beside full structuredContent; legacy/always modes retain full compact JSON; images remain one native block each. Producer IsError derives from the original payload independent of Content. Full short and race suites, focused final race tests, lint, and build passed.

title: matrix-2x2 allows 60-character horizontal axis title that renders below 12pt
description: The documented matrix-2x2 x_axis_label budget is 60 characters, but a valid 60-character unbroken wide label (60 W glyphs) rendered on the modern template stores a:normAutofit fontScale=72000 on a 14pt run (effective 10.08pt), below the 12pt present-mode floor. Repro: jq sets x_axis_label to W*60 in /tmp/json2pptx-matrix-axis-repro.json and generates /tmp/json2pptx-matrix-axis-v6/matrix-axis-wide-title.pptx. Discovered while fixing go-slide-creator-ix9qu. Calibrate the horizontal-axis budget or layout using measured text fit, update raw/DeckSpec discovery and docs, and add a regression for wide unbroken copy across local template corpus.
acceptance_criteria: A valid horizontal axis title at its advertised limit remains at or above the 12pt floor across shipped templates and local p-style, or the documented/validated limit is lowered with a measured regression test.
close_reason: Horizontal matrix axis cap calibrated to 16 wide characters across all local templates, including ignored p-style; full-stack budget probe fixture now tracks schema maxima. Full short suite, lint, build, and golden-output check passed.

title: matrix-2x2 horizontal axis title is occluded by its arrow
description: The matrix-2x2 horizontal axis title is rendered directly over the blue shaft. In the one-slide repro /tmp/json2pptx-matrix-axis-v2/matrix-axis-repro.pptx.png, Effort is nearly unreadable between Low effort and High effort. Repro uses the midnight-blue template and ordinary 11-character axis-end labels. The title and arrow are separate shapes in the nested x-axis grid; give the title a clear text zone or interrupt/offset the shaft, preserving axis direction and quadrant bounds. Add a rendered regression check. This was discovered while verifying go-slide-creator-x5pbi and is distinct from label-size findings.
acceptance_criteria: A rendered matrix-2x2 with a nonempty x_axis_label clearly shows that title without arrow overlap on bundled templates and local p-style; regression coverage detects the overlap.
notes: Fixed horizontal axis by placing the title and text-free rightArrow in adjacent nested cells, and raising axis row from 12% to 16% so the title stays >=12pt even in modern. Rendered examples: /tmp/json2pptx-matrix-axis-v5/matrix-axis-repro.pptx.png and /tmp/json2pptx-matrix-axis-v5/matrix-axis-pstyle.pptx.png (side-by-side layout), /tmp/json2pptx-matrix-axis-v6/matrix-axis-modern.pptx.png (modern, taller row). New TestMatrixAxisTitleClearsArrow inspects final PPTX geometry and effective font size across AllTestTemplateNames including ignored local p-style. Full short suite, lint, build, schema maxima pass; determinism hashes unchanged. Separate long-title budget bug filed as go-slide-creator-eg96u. Mac LibreOffice remains intermittently stalled; Quick Look provided visual proof.
close_reason: Horizontal title and right-pointing arrow now occupy non-overlapping cells; final PPTX geometry and >=12pt effective title size verified across all local templates, with Quick Look visual checks, full short suite, lint, build, and schema-maxima gate passing.

title: Dark authored taxonomy fills retain dark text with insufficient contrast
description: Native SWOT, PESTEL, BMC and nine-box allow explicit RGB or semantic accent fills; their header/body text is fixed to dk1. A dark authored fill such as #102030 therefore makes labels unreadable after correct RGB serialization. Choose text color against the effective fill while preserving authored fill exactly; add contrast regression cases for light/dark hex and theme schemes.
close_reason: Authored RGB taxonomy/semantic-accent panels now select exact black or white text and bullets by contrast; all four framework paths, generator suite, lint, build, and golden-hash check pass.

title: Porter-force native boxes use HSL brightening on theme accents
description: porters_shapes.go porterBoxFill uses lumMod/lumOff on accent-linked boxes; saturated template accents can appear neon. Use RGB tint for lightened accent boxes and update the associated text-contrast color model and tests.
close_reason: Porter-force scored fills now use RGB tint and intensity-text contrast uses the same effective color; saturated-accent regression, generator suite, lint, and golden-hash check pass.

title: Heatmap native cells use HSL accent brightening and contrast model
description: heatmap_shapes.go derives sequential cell fills with lumMod/lumOff; saturated theme accents can drift to neon. Replace with RGB tint while updating heatmap value text contrast calculations to use the exact new rendered fill; add theme-saturation and contrast tests.
close_reason: Heatmap native fills use RGB tint and value-text contrast computes the same effective fill; saturated-accent tests, generator suite, lint, and golden-hash check pass.

title: Process-flow status panels use HSL brightening that can turn accents neon
description: process_flow_shapes.go status fill paths use lumMod=20000/lumOff=80000 on accent1/2/3/6, causing saturated template accents to render fluorescent. Replace with RGB tint and add regression coverage for each status.
close_reason: All process-flow step types now use shared RGB tint with full-accent outlines; generator suite, lint, and golden-hash check pass.

title: Authored hex colors in native taxonomy diagrams serialize as invalid schemeClr
description: authoredTaxonomyColors stores #RRGGBB in taxonomyTint.scheme; SWOT, PESTEL, nine-box and BMC call pptx.SchemeFill on it, emitting invalid <a:schemeClr val="#RRGGBB">. Preserve exact authored hex as <a:srgbClr>, including bullets, while retaining theme-linked tint for scheme colors. Add generator regression tests for authored hex colors.
close_reason: Explicit hex and semantic-accent RGB colors now serialize as srgbClr in taxonomy/native diagrams and bullets; regression coverage passes.

This flattens the title/body hierarchy; adjust the authored layout so title > body and verify rendered slide and corpus gate. Discovered while implementing go-slide-creator-ss8ch.

title: Contrast fixer skips scheme text colors with OOXML luminance modifiers
description: On blue-corporate slideLayout3, a title uses <a:schemeClr val="bg1"><a:lumMod val="95000"/></a:schemeClr> on an author-set white background. Contrast preflight predicts a white/light-text repair, but generate records no swap and leaves the modified light text. fixSchemeColorsForContrast only matches simple schemeClr and ignores child modifiers. Resolve actual modified foreground and apply a readable replacement; cover with a regression and template parity case.
close_reason: Contrast renderer now skips empty template text and resolves modified scheme foregrounds; focused regressions, full serial Go suite, and lint pass.

title: Colorless layout text style masks master color during inherited contrast repair
description: A layout placeholder may declare lvl1pPr/defRPr size but no solidFill, while its master txStyles supplies the actual text color. inheritedTextStyleFragment returns the colorless layout fragment and never falls back to the master, so enforceInheritedTextContrast finds no color and leaves same-color text unreadable on an author-set background. Reproduced by TestAuthoredBackgroundPlaceholderContrastMatchesGeneration: abstract, modern, modern-template, modern-yellow, p-style predict a swap but generate records none. Fix color inheritance per property while retaining layout size/weight, and add a regression using actual layout/master fragments.
close_reason: Fixed in cce3b9aa: when a layout placeholder declares size/weight but no color, inherited contrast repair now resolves the master txStyles color and records its provenance while retaining the layout threshold. New regression covers the repair and absent-master fallback; full go test ./... and lint pass.

title: contrast_autofixed findings advertise unusable replace_color fixes for generated text
description: contrastSwapsToFindings emits replace_color for every render-time text swap, including inherited placeholder runs and grouped shape-grid output. repair_slide defaults to fill and source JSON may have no authored text color or only pattern values. Give a target=text repair only when the source has a precise editable authored color/path; otherwise provide informational metadata without an executable fix. Add convergence tests across raw grid, grouped grid, and template-inherited text.
notes:
Render-time contrast findings now offer target=text replace_color only when /shape_grid/shapes/I maps one-to-one to a simple authored raw cell and its resolved authored foreground matches the actual swap; grouped, inherited, generated/pattern, and ambiguous connector cases remain informational with source in message. Added end-to-end convergence and negative-path tests; focused tests/lint pass. Full suites, race, and CI pending.
Added actual RunPresentation integration proving a rendered /shape_grid/shapes/1 swap maps to authored cell 1 (including scheme lt1), plus synthetic convergence and negative cases. Full command/patterns suites, focused race, and lint pass; CI pending.
close_reason: Only exactly mapped authored raw shape-grid text gets executable target=text repair; all ambiguous/inherited/generated swaps remain informational. Rendered integration, full local suites, race, lint, and CI/Docker/CodeQL passed.

Profile per-test duration and overlapping fixture/setup work, remove only redundant checks or share immutable setup safely, and preserve cross-template coverage including local ignored p-style. Verify before/after duration and all CI gates.
notes: Local full cmd/json2pptx short race suite now passes in 548.896s under a 10-minute timeout after parallelizing template probes and bounding schema workers. Focused race cases: schema 34.838s vs 115.69s prior CI; strict-fit corpus 10.080s vs 52.10s; template skill-info 8.357s vs 32.35s. Awaiting CI/Docker on commits 4f352ccf and 228bb8f7 before closure.
close_reason: Focused race hotspots were parallelized/bounded; full local cmd/json2pptx short race suite passed in 548.896s under 10m, and CI/Docker/Push runs for both speed commits passed.

title: card_fill can erase recommended soft-card highlight
description: Card-grid soft-card supports cells[].recommended and generic overrides.card_fill. expandCell applies card_fill after expandSoftCard, so setting both repaints the selected accent card and can leave its contrast-selected ink against the wrong fill. Define and enforce precedence or a validation error; add a pattern test for the combination and preserve readable selection.
close_reason: p-style soft cards now use a subtle accent tint when no template surface is supplied; recommended cards keep accent fill despite card_fill. Rendered p-style QA confirms visible panel/contrast; commit 43ce4396 passed full CI and Docker.

description: A rendered decision two-card slide using the local p-style template shows an unselected soft-card with a white surface on a white slide, so only the selected accent-filled card reads as a panel. The current soft-card fill resolves subtle to white. Make the unselected card visibly but very lightly tinted (neutral grey or derived from the accent) while preserving readable text and template identity. Verify with a rendered p-style two-card slide and pattern tests; do not commit the gitignored template.
close_reason: p-style soft cards now use a subtle accent tint when no template surface is supplied; recommended cards keep accent fill despite card_fill. Rendered p-style QA confirms visible panel/contrast; commit 43ce4396 passed full CI and Docker.

title: Composite grid children shift cell budget mapping
description: computeCellBudgets iterates authored grid.Rows cells but indexes textcapacity.ForResolvedGrid(result) by a sequential cellIdx. shapegrid.Resolve emits two ResolvedCells (text and diagram) for one composite source cell, so the second child is mistaken for the next authored cell and subsequent budgets/warnings shift. Use ResolvedCell.RowIdx/ColIdx (and merge composite children intentionally) to map capacity back to authored coordinates; add a mixed composite/plain grid regression test.
close_reason: Mapped composite and spanning resolved cells to authored coordinates in aa63d2b0; full local tests/build/lint and CI, Docker, CodeQL all passed.

title: Semantic source map cannot resolve nested JSON Pointer finding paths
description: internal/semantic/sourcemap.go parentPath only walks dotted/bracket syntax. New finding paths are JSON Pointers; an exact /slides/0/content/1 alias works, but /slides/0/content/1/bullets_value does not ascend to that alias and ResolveSemantic reports no mapping. Add JSON Pointer parent traversal and slide-index extraction without regressing legacy dotted paths.
acceptance_criteria: A source map entry at /slides/0/content/1 resolves nested pointer findings beneath it; unmatched /slides/N paths still recover N; dotted/bracket lookup remains unchanged. Cover escaped pointer segments.

Sites include fit_findings_duplicate_title.go, fit_findings_content_lint.go, fit_findings_collect.go, chrome_collision.go, title_measure.go, and grid_rhythm.go. This prevents replace_field/JSON Patch round-tripping. Preserve legacy by-name repair_slide selectors but emit authored numeric-index JSON Pointers for diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: Audit every fit-finding producer in cmd/json2pptx that uses slidepath.Content; emitted findings resolve against their authored deck via JSON Pointer tests, including duplicate-title, content-lint, chrome, title, and rhythm cases. Do not alter repair_slide selector matching.

Authored content is an array, so these are repair_slide selectors but not JSON Pointers usable by replace_field or JSON Patch. Carry the authored content index into render-time findings (or resolve the placeholder ID to an actual array index), update PATH_GRAMMAR.md's pseudo content/by-name examples, and test each emitted render finding path against the authored deck with a JSON Pointer resolver.
close_reason: Closed

title: Constrain pptx2jpg command runner fallback to approved executables
description: golangci-lint reports gosec G702 at cmd/pptx2jpg/main.go:74: RealCommandRunner.Run falls through to exec.Command(name, args...) for names outside the LibreOffice and rasterizer allowlists. Determine intended arbitrary-command use by tests/callers, then constrain the production fallback or document/suppress with an evidence-backed boundary; ensure lint passes and guard tests cover rejection.
close_reason: Unsupported command-runner fallback removed in d4bb85ab; focused tests, local lint, and all CI workflows green.

title: Disambiguate recommend_visual required_layout from semantic required_layouts
description: Investigation corrected the original premise: semantic meta.required_layouts intentionally accepts only canonical layout IDs because the compiler assigns each requirement as a concrete layout to one compatible narrative slide. recommend_visual.template_support.required_layout is a feasibility label and may be a derivable capability such as full-image or grid base. Copying that label into meta.required_layouts yields a confusing unknown-layout error. Keep semantic validation narrow; make the two contracts explicit in agent guidance/tool descriptions and test that capability names remain rejected as semantic canonical requirements.
close_reason: Recommendation required_layout versus semantic required_layouts guidance and schema 4.118.0 shipped in 8ead5c20; all CI green.

title: Stabilize pptx2jpg subprocess timeout tests under parallel load
description: The full root suite failed in TestRealCommandRunnerLibreOfficeTimeoutKillsWorker: fake soffice did not start a worker. The fake script had only a 100ms timeout to launch a shell, fork sleep, and write its PID; a focused ten-run retry passed, suggesting scheduler contention during parallel full-suite/build/lint verification. The rasterizer timeout test uses the same 100ms window. Make these tests robust under normal parallel CI load while preserving assertions that the runner returns DeadlineExceeded and kills an actually started child. Verify with repeated focused tests and the full root suite.
close_reason: Raised fake subprocess timeout startup allowance to one second while retaining DeadlineExceeded and real worker-cleanup assertions. Focused repeated tests, focused race tests, and full root suite pass. Pushed in e1e61cc7.

title: Re-resolving an edited slide can retain a stale asymmetric column split
description: resolveCanonicalLayoutIDs stores ColumnLeftPercent internally when an asymmetric canonical layout_id is resolved, but does not clear it if a later patch/edit changes layout_id to another canonical role. Reusing the SlideInput then sends the stale 65/35 split to generator, which may derive columns on the wrong layout or fail on One Content. Clear the split when a new canonical alias supersedes it while preserving it for the already-resolved concrete ID; add a regression sequence test.
close_reason: Repeated canonical resolution clears stale derived splits after layout edits; sequence regression test passes.

Normalize these tracked files mechanically, verify the diff has no semantic changes, and keep the format gate green. Avoid touching user worktrees and unrelated untracked files.
close_reason: Formatted all 60 previously unformatted tracked Go files; exact comparison proves each changed Go file apart from the separately tracked timeout test equals gofmt of HEAD. make fmt-check, full tests, builds, and lint pass. Pushed in e1e61cc7.

title: fmt-check scans untracked nested worktrees and reports unrelated Go files

A local make fmt-check emitted hundreds of unrelated paths, including .claude/worktrees/agent-af27..., so the gate depends on external working directories rather than the repository. Scope formatting validation to tracked project Go files or explicitly exclude nested worktrees; test the command with an untracked nested worktree fixture.
close_reason: Scoped fmt and fmt-check to Git-tracked plus non-ignored untracked Go files; the ignored nested worktree is excluded, a deliberately unformatted new Go file is caught, and make fmt-check passes. Pushed in e1e61cc7.

title: pptxread collapses body and body_2 placeholders to the same ID
description: internal/pptxread/read.go:placeholderID always returns body when p:ph type=body, ignoring the shape's canonical name and idx. Reading a generated Two Content slide returns two placeholders both ID=body, so consumers cannot distinguish left/right or round-trip body_2 content. Preserve canonical shape names (body_2, body_3) or use idx while retaining a single body as body; add a read-back test on a real two-column PPTX.
close_reason: PPTX read-back retains canonical body_2/body_N names and preview-to-generated round-trip tests pass.

title: Preview template metadata is not normalized before placeholder lookup
description: loadPreviewTemplate parses and synthesizes layouts but does not call template.NormalizeLayoutFiles on analysis.Layouts before populating layoutByID. resolveSlidePlaceholders compares content placeholder IDs (canonical body/body_2) to raw layout PlaceholderInfo.ID, so templates with Content Placeholder names can report missing geometry/remapping in preview even though generation normalizes those layout shapes. Normalize preview metadata before mapping and add a real-template parity test.
close_reason: Preview template metadata is normalized before placeholder mapping; real unnormalized template test passes.

title: Preview and preflight use native 50/50 bounds for derived asymmetric layouts
description: When layout_id is two-column-wide-narrow or two-column-narrow-wide, resolution now retains a 65/35 or 35/65 split and generation resizes slide body transforms, but preview_presentation_plan resolveSlidePlaceholders and collectFitFindings still read unmodified template LayoutMetadata by resolved ID. Preview placeholder bounds, wireframe overlay placement, and preflight width/fit findings can contradict the generated slide. Derive the same per-slide metadata geometry after chrome reservation for preview/validation, or explicitly report accurate derived bounds; test both variants and a side-art template (modern-yellow) against final PPTX geometry.
close_reason: Preview and preflight now use per-slide derived bounds after chrome reservation; preview-to-generated PPTX parity and per-slide fit budget tests pass.

title: matrix_2x2 silently skips malformed quadrant entries
description: Matrix2x2Diagram.Validate only checks non-nil Data; parseQuadrantItemLists skips non-object quadrants and ignores non-array items without a finding. A request with malformed quadrant entries can render an empty matrix despite authored data. Validate these entry shapes or emit an actionable structured finding before rendering.
close_reason: Reject malformed matrix_2x2 quadrant arrays, entries, items, and item labels with field-specific validation errors; direct rendering now validates too; full suites, lint, and builds pass.

title: svggen get_capabilities omits diagram finding codes
description: buildSvggenVocabularies advertises only a subset of emitted chart.* findings and omits all diagram.* findings (including items_dropped, text_overlap, org_chart_depth_pruned, and quadrant_position_defaulted). Its vocabulary test rejects any diagram.* code. Include every emitted finding code in finding_codes and test parity so agents can discover the diagnostics they may receive.
close_reason: Matrix quadrants now default missing/invalid positions by index with a structured finding; titles and items survive; QA example corrected; svggen capability discovery includes all emitted codes; root/svggen tests, lint, builds, and generated QA deck verified

title: matrix_2x2 silently drops items with invalid quadrant positions
description: parseQuadrantItemLists skips a quadrant when its position string is unrecognized, dropping every item without a structured finding. Validate explicit positions (including underscore aliases) and report a specific actionable finding; preserve items through a deterministic index fallback or refuse rather than silently omit them.
close_reason: Matrix quadrants now default missing/invalid positions by index with a structured finding; titles and items survive; QA example corrected; svggen capability discovery includes all emitted codes; root/svggen tests, lint, builds, and generated QA deck verified

title: Tinted card-grid paper cards blend into the slide background

All shipped template metadata maps paper to lt1, the page background, and the paper card has no outline, so every second tinted card disappears. Use a subtle outline for paper cards while preserving card_fill/border overrides, and add a regression for template metadata paper:lt1.

Remove the dedicated execution or exclude them from the later test pass while retaining the post-test git diff/status drift check and clear failure signal. Count the effective merged footer configuration in structural checks and add a chrome-only regression.

description: cmd/pptx2jpg/main.go RealCommandRunner.Run uses exec.Command(...).Run without a deadline or process group. A wedged LibreOffice launcher can block indefinitely, and terminating pptx2jpg can leave a soffice worker behind. Reuse the scoped LibreOffice guard from internal/render without breaking the mock CommandRunner interface; bound the conversion and test parent death/timeout with fake executables. Do not signal unrelated user LibreOffice processes.
acceptance_criteria: pptx2jpg conversion has a bounded deadline; cancelling the CLI leaves no owned soffice worker; unrelated LibreOffice state remains untouched; mocked runner tests and integration tests pass.
close_reason: Guarded LibreOffice subprocess groups and bounded pptx2jpg conversion; macOS/Linux tests and corrective CI, Docker, CodeQL all passed at c814478c

title: Local make vulncheck can scan with a different Go toolchain than CI
description: Makefile vulncheck installs govulncheck@latest using the host Go toolchain and runs that binary, so developers with newer Go may scan a different standard library than the go.mod/CI baseline. The latest scanner may also require Go 1.26 while the repo supports patched 1.25. Align local scanner version and toolchain with the root go.mod declaration, scan both modules, and verify local make vulncheck reports the same clean result as CI.
acceptance_criteria: make vulncheck uses the pinned compatible scanner and the Go version declared by root go.mod for root and svggen scans, and exits nonzero on scanner failure.
close_reason: make vulncheck derives pinned Go1.25.14 from root go.mod, checks svggen baseline parity, and runs pinned govulncheck v1.7.0 on both modules; target passes.

acceptance_criteria: Root and svggen resolve jsonparser >=v1.1.2, tests pass, and GO-2026-4514 is absent from govulncheck package findings.
close_reason: Both graphs use jsonparser v1.1.2; GO-2026-4514 absent from govulncheck output and tests pass.
