title: CI lint action download fails on runner TLS self-signed certificate
description: On pushed SHA e29b2701, GitHub Actions CI run 35917291991 lint job 107372032248 failed before linting. golangci/golangci-lint-action@v9 attempted to download pinned v2.8.0 binary from GitHub releases twice and Node rejected the TLS chain with self-signed certificate (20:38:40 and 20:38:53 UTC). Local golangci-lint run ./... passes; earlier SHA CI lint passed. Determine whether this is transient runner infrastructure; rerun failed job after run completes, and if recurring use a repository-controlled install path or CA configuration without disabling TLS verification. Verify CI lint reaches and passes actual analysis.
acceptance_criteria: CI lint job installs the pinned linter securely and reaches the lint step; latest main SHA CI completes green (or persistent external runner problem is documented with reproducible evidence).
close_reason: Transient golangci-lint installer TLS failure on CI run 35917291991 attempt 1; reran failed job and attempt 2 completed success. Local lint also passes.

title: Default auto_repair gate can pass decks that score_deck rejects on composition, accent overload, or problem-slide share
description: score_deck EvaluateQualityGate applies min_composition_score=65, allow_accent_overload=false, and max_problem_slides_pct=40 in addition to min_score/P0/P1/takeaway. auto_repair evaluateAutoRepairGate applies only the latter four, yet tool docs say default gate_passed and score_deck quality_gate.passed agree. A composition-55 monotony deck can therefore converge under auto_repair defaults and fail score_deck with the same deck/score. Align the contracts or explicitly separate a loop-stop flag from ship-quality verdict; add a behavioral parity regression for a composition-only failure and test the other extra criteria.
acceptance_criteria: A default auto_repair gate cannot report pass for an unchanged deck that fails score_deck only on composition, accent overload, or problem-slide share; response/docs distinguish any intentionally relaxed loop gate.
close_reason: auto_repair now computes composition and delegates gate evaluation to score_deck criteria, retaining fixed accent/composition/problem-share blockers with configurable numeric thresholds; added criterion-parity and rendered monotony tests; full tests, build, lint pass.

title: Text contrast pass skips layouts inheriting a master-only background
description: slide_preparation.go obtains bgHex only from extractLayoutBackgroundColor(layoutData) when the slide has no authored background. If the layout has no p:bg but its master has one, bgHex is empty and both explicit and inherited text contrast correction are skipped. effectiveGridSlideBackgroundHex already falls back to master, demonstrating the missing branch. Add master fallback and render/preflight parity tests.
acceptance_criteria: A slide layout without p:bg but with a solid master p:bg evaluates text against the visible master background, including color transforms, and emits/avoids contrast findings appropriately.
close_reason: Text contrast now falls back from a layout without p:bg to its master background through the shared inherited-background resolver; regression tests and full suite pass.

title: Constrained chart_value.style.background bypasses raw-hex color validation
description: checkContentItem in cmd/json2pptx/design_mode.go validates chart_value.style.colors but omits chart_value.style.background, unlike diagram_value and shape_grid diagrams. A constrained deck can set a raw hex chart background even though the design-mode contract and chart style hints say raw hex requires free mode.
acceptance_criteria: Constrained chart_value.style.background rejects raw hex with a design_mode_violation at the exact field path; scheme names remain valid; free mode permits raw hex; tests cover all three.
close_reason: Constrained chart_value.style.background now rejects raw hex at its exact field path; constrained scheme and free hex cases covered.

title: Chart style.colors silently ignores series colors after sixth entry
description: diagramSpecToSVGGen caps synthesized accent slots at six and does not forward style.colors[6:] to DataPalette, despite its comment. On a seven-series chart the seventh authored color is discarded without a finding, and validation cannot predict the palette. Define and implement an explicit >6-series color policy with render/preview parity and regression coverage.
acceptance_criteria: A chart with seven or more authored series colors either renders every specified color in series order or reports an actionable finding for each unsupported entry; render and dry-run agree.
close_reason: Explicit style.colors now retains series colors beyond six via svggen ExtraAccents; render and dry-run retain order, unresolved seventh entries produce CUSTOM_COLOR_DROPPED, and both module test/lint/build suites pass.

title: Bar and line vertical x-label pivots diverge on identical canvas
description: With the same dense nominal categories and canvas, the bar x-axis rotated-label pivot is 15.6px above the line chart pivot. The existing parity test did not exercise the 90-degree branch; nominal-label changes exposed divergent bottom-margin/plot-area calculations.
acceptance_criteria: Bar and line chart x-axis label pivot Y agrees within 1px at 90-degree rotation for identical canvas/data; regression test passes without suppressing label rendering.
close_reason: Nominal categories no longer thin; crowded/ellipsized axes emit actionable findings, dry-render and fit-report tests pass; bar/line vertical pivot geometry aligned and rendered repro verified.

title: Waterfall labels+values normalization silently truncates mismatched arrays
description: svggen/waterfall.go normalizeWaterfallData sets n=min(len(labels),len(values)) and discards surplus labels or values without a diagnostic before Validate/Render. A chart with three labels and two values ships with its final bar missing. Validate equal nonzero lengths and report a precise error; add public svggen.Render regression tests.
close_reason: waterfall labels+values shorthand now rejects empty/mismatched arrays and nonnumeric values without normalizing/truncating them; public render regression covers both mismatch directions and valid full bridge

title: title_wraps validation fix proposes shorten_title params that repair_slide refuses
description: A real validate_input response for a 113-character, 15-word title emits INPUT.title_wraps with remediation.primary.params {kind:shorten_title,max_chars:90}. After propose_repairs correctly adapts the FindingEnvelope and emits a repair_slide tool_call, repair_slide returns Applied:false semantic_review_required: it says the trim would cut 15 words to 7. The guidance is not directly replayable. Investigate max_chars/max_length parameter mismatch and align fit suggestion with repair_slide's semantic-loss guard; add a validate→propose→repair regression that proves an applicable safe suggestion, or emit advisory when no safe automatic trim exists. Discovered while implementing go-slide-creator-e9w6a.
close_reason: Closed

title: Waterfall points accept missing or non-numeric values as zero
description: svggen/waterfall.go WaterfallDiagram.Validate checks only that points is a nonempty array, while parseWaterfallData silently leaves Value=0 when value is missing or a string. A typed waterfall with a malformed point can render a mathematically wrong bridge without a diagnostic. Validate each point label/value/type and reject invalid values before rendering; add public-path tests.
close_reason: waterfall validation and direct rendering now reject malformed point labels, missing/non-numeric/nonfinite values, and invalid types; public render regressions and valid numeric variants covered

title: Short-mode test suite invokes real LibreOffice for coverage-only and visual integration cases
description: go test ./cmd/json2pptx -short hangs locally in TestHandleRenderSlideImageFromJSON_DensityClampParsing because it invokes headless LibreOffice solely for density-branch coverage and accepts render failure. Generator visual tests such as TestTemplateDefaultWithoutDefinitionRendersFilledHeader and image-zorder also have no testing.Short guard. Split logic tests from visual integration when practical; skip actual conversion cases in -short while preserving full/CI integration coverage. Audit all direct render.DependencyStatus-gated tests for short-mode consistency.
acceptance_criteria: go test ./cmd/json2pptx -short and relevant generator short-mode tests do not invoke real LibreOffice when it is installed; full tests retain their rendering assertions and branch parsing remains covered by deterministic tests.
close_reason: Replaced duplicate fake-PPTX density branch tests with one deterministic shared parser test; split visual-QA degraded and real-render paths; made true LibreOffice integration tests short-aware. go test ./... -short -count=1 passes locally with p-style present and no headless soffice spawned.

title: Cancelling render tests can orphan headless LibreOffice subprocess groups
description: On local macOS, terminating go test while render tests are in headless LibreOffice left four test-owned soffice processes alive for >24 minutes (PIDs 42194/42195/42342/42343). The conversion helper already uses a 90s timeout and process-group kill on context cancellation, but parent-process termination does not trigger that callback. Investigate a scoped test/process lifecycle guard that cleans test-owned conversion groups when the test process exits, without touching pre-existing user LibreOffice processes.
acceptance_criteria: Cancelling or timing out a local render test run leaves no test-owned LibreOffice descendants; user LibreOffice state is untouched.
notes: Reproduced locally: go test ./cmd/json2pptx -short -count=1 reached render-from-json single-slide headless conversion and stalled for >44s. Explicitly stopped own go test PID 49725 and test-owned soffice PIDs 42194/42195/42342/42343/50246/50247; verified only pre-existing user soffice PID 15291 remained. Focused handle tests, internal/semantic suite, build, and lint pass.
close_reason: Guarded LibreOffice subprocess groups and bounded pptx2jpg conversion; macOS/Linux tests and corrective CI, Docker, CodeQL all passed at c814478c

title: Gantt progress outside 0–100 is not validated or clamped before drawing
description: svggen/gantt.go accepts task progress as float64 and drawTaskBar computes barWidth * progress/100 without bounds checking. Progress >100 paints beyond the task bar; negative values silently show the no-progress state. Validate or clamp the value at the render boundary and add 0/100/out-of-range tests. Discovered while fixing go-slide-creator-wm380.
acceptance_criteria: Gantt progress 0 and 100 have defined visual endpoints; out-of-range input cannot draw outside the task bar and has a clear validation or diagnostic outcome.
close_reason: Fixed semantic template color plumbing, Gantt completed/remaining encoding, progress range validation and draw clamping; focused, svggen suite, goldens, lint, and build pass.

title: Local LibreOffice conversion stalls across templates despite isolated profiles
description: Local macOS LibreOffice conversion stalls across templates, including the ignored p-style fixture and shipped modern-template, even with isolated user profiles. The corpus test now has a 60-second per-conversion timeout, Unix process-group cleanup, an actionable case/source/profile diagnostic, and aborts the remaining cases; CI passes. The underlying local LibreOffice environment remains unusable for headless round-trips. Diagnose/recover it without terminating the pre-existing user LibreOffice app or altering unsaved documents without approval. Keep p-style.pptx gitignored and in local corpus discovery.
acceptance_criteria: Local headless round-trips for a shipped template and p-style complete successfully, or the environmental limitation is identified and documented with an approved recovery; no user LibreOffice state is lost.
notes:
Sequential isolated probe also timed out after 30s converting templates/p-style.pptx directly to PDF with a unique LibreOffice profile. ZIP integrity passes. This points to a source-template/LibreOffice compatibility issue, not merely a generated deck or concurrent test contention.
Correction to earlier inference: direct conversion of shipped modern-template.pptx also timed out after 20s, and an isolated generated basic-deck × modern-template round-trip timed out after 40s. Thus the current failure is broader local LibreOffice conversion, not proven p-style source incompatibility. Add bounded subprocess timeout and diagnostics; keep p-style in local template corpus.
Implemented 60s per-conversion deadline, Unix process-group kill, and abort of the remaining corpus cases after the first timeout. Local end-to-end probe timed out at 60.05s with case/source/profile diagnostic and no orphaned test-owned soffice process. The existing user LibreOffice process (PID 15291) remains untouched; underlying local conversion stall is still unexplained, so retain this Bead until that is diagnosed or accepted as environment-specific.
2026-09-23 full local go test ./... remained in headless LibreOffice after >2m: TestDryRunEndToEnd qualitybench conversion and TestTemplateDefaultWithoutDefinitionRendersFilledHeader conversion both stalled in distinct isolated profiles while pre-existing user soffice PID 15291 was running. Stopped only the test-owned go test process; did not touch user LibreOffice. svggen full suite, targeted generator/template tests, build, vet, lint pass. CI verification pending push.
2026-09-23: A short-mode cmd/json2pptx suite also hung in headless LO; prior cancelled full suite left four test-owned soffice processes for >24 minutes. Separate atomic test-process cleanup Bead filed; user soffice PID 15291 untouched.
close_reason: Current local headless round-trips succeeded with isolated, 45-second-bounded LibreOffice profiles: direct p-style source -> 1-page PDF and modern-template source -> 4-page PDF; generated p-style option-matrix deck -> PDF/pixel render; generated modern-template section deck -> PDF. No existing LibreOffice session was terminated or modified. Earlier stall was intermittent; timeout/process-group diagnostics remain in place.

title: Alpha shape-grid fills composite over lt1 instead of the actual slide background
description: internal/generator/text_contrast.go applyShapeFillModifiers composites alpha fills against theme lt1 even when a slide/background scrim or layout/master uses another color. The preflight effectiveShapeFillColor similarly uses lt1. A 50% accent fill over a dark authored slide can therefore receive a false or missed contrast fix. Resolve the underlying effective canvas in both generate and validate and add parity tests.
close_reason: Closed

title: Contrast preflight must re-resolve layout background under theme_override
description: The new LayoutMetadata.BackgroundHex is resolved from the original template theme. A deck theme_override can recolor a scheme-based layout/master background, so validate would compare transparent grid text against stale hex while generate reads the overridden theme. Store the mapped background scheme source in metadata and resolve it against the effective theme at preflight; retain literal sRGB backgrounds unchanged.
close_reason: Closed

title: Update FIT_FINDINGS contrast_predicted docs to size-aware thresholds and transparent cells
description: docs/FIT_FINDINGS.md still says contrast_predicted always checks WCAG AA Large 3:1 even though the engine now uses 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 only for large text. It also omits transparent shape-grid cells resolved against slide/layout/master backgrounds. Align documentation and skill findings catalog with current behavior.
close_reason: Closed

title: Contrast preflight ignores slide contrast_check:false for shape-grid cells
description: collectContrastPreflightFindings skips opted-out placeholder background pairs but still scans shape_grid cells and emits contrast_predicted even though generate bypasses enforceShapeGridContrast for the slide. Make the opt-out apply to both paths and assert validate/generate parity.
close_reason: Closed

title: Contrast pass skips text in transparent shape-grid cells
description: internal/generator/text_contrast.go extractShapeFillHex returns empty for noFill/transparent shapes, so contrast on the inherited slide/background is never evaluated. This is separately visible from the abstract chart-palette bug. Resolve the effective background for transparent cells and add generate/validate parity tests across light and dark slide backgrounds.
close_reason: Closed

title: Rework abstract template accent1 so it is visible on its light canvas
description: Abstract theme accent1 #E9E6DF is only 1.25:1 on lt1 #FFFFFF. The engine will warn and avoid it in automatic chart palettes, but the source template still has an inherently near-background first accent. Recolor the template or intentionally document a dark-surface-only role; then remove its conformance allow-list entry and rebaseline affected outputs.
close_reason: Recolored abstract accent1 to #8E8172 (3.8:1 on white), preserved all other PPTX entries, removed conformance exception, updated color-role/chart regressions and layout preview; template-check, examination gate, full tests, and lint pass.

title: timeline-horizontal chevron date row height ignores 12pt renderer floor
description: expandChevron defaults date_size to 9pt and computes dateRowH from that authored size, but shapegrid.ResolveTextInput raises explicit text below 12pt to 12pt. Thus the date row MaxHeight/MinHeight is about 3.6pt too short even for one line, and date labels can clip despite passing the character budget. Align row sizing and date-capacity warnings with effective font size; verify emitted OOXML and fit findings across template geometry.
close_reason: Closed

title: timeline-horizontal chevron derives unreadable body font sizes from label_size
description: In internal/patterns/timelinehorizontal.go, expandChevron passes labelSize to buildChevronTextContent, which sets body text to labelSize-2 and ignores the declared body_size override. Schema allows label_size as low as 6pt, so the body can render at 4pt with no readability finding. Add a readable floor, honor body_size consistently, and cover both chevron and fit-report behavior.
close_reason: Closed

title: Ignored scratch PPTX in templates directory contaminates embedded corpus and tests
description: An ignored local templates/p-style.pptx exists in the workspace. templates/embed.go uses //go:embed *.pptx, so go build embeds ignored local files; DiscoverBuiltinTemplates also glob-scans them and TestBuiltinTemplateCoverage fails as if they were shipped. Fix shipped-template selection so ignored/untracked scratch PPTX cannot alter builds or corpus tests, while still failing when a genuinely tracked new template lacks a coverage classification. Preserve the local file; do not delete it.
close_reason: Implemented picture z-order and native SVG layering with XML and rendered-pixel regression tests; isolated shipped templates from ignored local PPTX and updated corpus tests. Full go test, lint, and build pass.

title: Determinism corpus uses midnight-blue layout IDs against other templates
description: TestDeterministicCorpus rewrites only the template name in examples/basic-deck.json, leaving slideLayout2/content placeholder IDs from midnight-blue. On modern-template slideLayout2 is Section Divider; after removing its invalid extra body placeholder, rendering fails because body and section-number map to the same placeholder. Make the cross-template fixture use each template’s canonical layout/placeholder mapping or supply a template-specific fixture. Preserve byte-stability assertions and update only the reviewed modern-template golden hash.
close_reason: Changed basic-deck example to portable canonical layout IDs; all four determinism corpus cases pass with only modern-template golden updated after its intentional repair.

title: Preflight must report missing SVG raster converter for grid-cell charts
description: Grid-cell chart/diagram generation now requires rsvg-convert or resvg to produce a text-preserving PNG fallback. generate_presentation fails when both are absent, but validate_input / dry-run still renders only SVG and can report valid. This creates a validate/generate parity gap and does not tell the agent to install a converter until generation. Distinct from the raster quality fix in mn0ll.
acceptance_criteria: With neither converter available, validate_input and CLI dry-run return a clear blocking dependency diagnostic for a grid-cell diagram; generation fails with the same actionable message. With either converter available, both validate and generate succeed. Regression pins both dependency states without relying on host PATH.
close_reason: Preflight and CLI dry-run now block grid-cell diagrams when both raster converters are absent, with the same actionable message as generation; deterministic dependency-state tests and full quality gates pass.

title: UNKNOWN_LAYOUT_ID repair suggestion is non-executable for raw unknown IDs
description: validateSlidesAgainstTemplate emits fix.kind=use_one_of with only available/did_you_mean for a raw unknown layout_id. AttachNextToolCalls forwards it to repair_slide, but applyUseOneOf requires params.path and params.value, so the suggested repair fails rather than converging. The canonical-alias branch is being corrected in go-slide-creator-jrev1; audit raw layout IDs and no-close-match cases independently so every offered tool call is executable or advisory.
acceptance_criteria: For raw unknown layout IDs, a close-match repair_slide suggestion changes layout_id and passes validation; when no safe choice exists, no non-executable repair_slide call is offered. Regression covers both cases.
close_reason: Raw unknown layout IDs now offer executable use_one_of repairs only for close matches; no-match diagnostics omit repair calls. Regression applies suggested fix and revalidates. Full tests, lint, and build pass.

title: Complete blue-corporate master footer placeholders and retire chrome warning allow-list
description: The blue-corporate master declares ftr and sldNum but no dt. go-slide-creator-qzn3u makes generated chrome render via a synthetic anchor and template-check warn, but the shipped PPTX remains incomplete and now needs a conformance allow-list entry. Add an authored dt placeholder to the master with non-overlapping geometry and retire that allow-list entry once the bundled template passes with zero warnings. Preserve layout IDs and existing brand/chrome appearance.
acceptance_criteria: blue-corporate template-check has zero warnings; conformance allow-list entry removed; generated confidentiality/date and page number still render without overlap; template portability tests pass.
close_reason: Added native dt placeholder with unused idx 20 and non-overlapping geometry; preserved generated left alignment and page number; removed final conformance exception. Template-check zero WARN, examination gate, full Go tests, lint, and archive asset comparison pass.

title: Periodic temp-cleaner test races timer under full-suite load
description: In full go test ./... -count=1, internal/generator TestTempFileCleanerPeriodicCleanup failed after sleeping exactly 100ms for a 50ms ticker. The test uses a fixed shared /tmp filename and wall-clock sleep, so load/scheduling or concurrent runs can leave the file present. Targeted -count=20 passed. Make the test isolated and synchronize/poll with a bounded deadline instead of relying on two timer intervals.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated full-suite and targeted runs pass without timing-dependent false negatives; temp artifacts are isolated per test; test still proves periodic cleanup happened.
close_reason: Closed

title: Uncapped raw shape_grid is mislabeled pattern in SLIDE_UNDERUSED
description: checkSlideUnderused maps authorCappedBand(false) to band_capped_by:pattern and pattern-specific prose. A raw shape_grid without bounds has no pattern and no author cap, so the finding claims its height was content-derived by a pattern and suggests choosing a denser pattern. Add an explicit uncapped/non-pattern source with accurate threshold and remediation, including schema/docs/tests.
acceptance_criteria: Raw shape_grid without a restrictive cap reports a truthful source and actionable non-pattern advice; pattern-owned and genuinely author-capped branches remain intact; full-area bounds are covered by nf8ad.
close_reason: Full-area explicit bounds and uncapped raw grids now report band_capped_by:none with 22% threshold and non-cap advice; restrictive authored bounds remain author, content-sized patterns remain pattern. Focused and full tests, lint, build pass.

title: Full-height grid bounds falsely trigger author-cap SLIDE_UNDERUSED advice
description: authorCappedBand treats any non-nil Pattern.Bounds or raw ShapeGrid.Bounds as a restrictive author cap, even when bounds.height is 100% (and width 100%). A sparse full-height grid can then get the 45% author-cap threshold and advice to raise/remove a cap that cannot be raised; removing it may shrink rather than improve coverage. Distinguish a genuine restrictive bound from a full-area explicit bound and test pattern and raw-grid cases.
acceptance_criteria: A full-height/full-width explicit bound does not produce non-convergent raise-cap advice; genuinely restrictive author bounds still use the author-cap branch; focused tests cover both surfaces.
close_reason: Full-area explicit bounds and uncapped raw grids now report band_capped_by:none with 22% threshold and non-cap advice; restrictive authored bounds remain author, content-sized patterns remain pattern. Focused and full tests, lint, build pass.

title: patterns CLI positional name can disagree with embedded PatternInput.name
description: parsePatternInputFile preserves a name embedded in the JSON file even when the CLI positional pattern name differs. patterns validate historically checks the positional pattern, while patterns expand passes the embedded name to expandPattern, so the two commands can inspect/render different patterns for the same invocation. Define one authority (prefer explicit positional name) and reject or normalize conflicts consistently in validate and expand.
acceptance_criteria: Both patterns validate and patterns expand resolve the same named pattern when a full PatternInput file contains a conflicting name; regression tests cover the conflict and error contract.
close_reason: CLI validate now runs shared expansion/fit analysis, emits standard findings envelope with field paths and non-zero fit failures; positional pattern name consistently wins in validate and expand. Targeted and full package tests, repository-wide tests, lint and build pass.

title: patterns validate CLI misses content-fit failures that MCP validate_pattern catches
description: The CLI runPatternsValidate path validates schema/values/callout but never expands or checks PostExpandWarnings, density, or cell budgets. A card-grid 4x3 with 105-character bodies passes CLI validation while MCP validate_pattern now reports FIT.BODY_TOO_LONG. Align the CLI checker with the shared pattern expansion/fit pass and define a consistent JSON diagnostic contract.
acceptance_criteria: CLI patterns validate rejects the same card-grid overflow as MCP validate_pattern; tests cover fit failure and ordinary valid values; JSON result exposes actionable finding paths.
close_reason: CLI validate now runs shared expansion/fit analysis, emits standard findings envelope with field paths and non-zero fit failures; positional pattern name consistently wins in validate and expand. Targeted and full package tests, repository-wide tests, lint and build pass.

title: BODY_TOO_LONG description conflates word-count and pattern character budgets
description: internal/patterns/finding_meta.go describes BODY_TOO_LONG only as a body exceeding 80 words, but card-grid and other pattern PostExpandWarnings emit BODY_TOO_LONG for geometry-specific character budgets (e.g. 4x3 card body >60 characters). Agents following describe_finding receive the wrong remediation target. Clarify or split the finding semantics so describe_finding matches both emitters; test the documented thresholds against representative pattern warnings.
close_reason: describe_finding now distinguishes 80-word content lint from geometry-specific pattern budgets; 80/81-word and 60/61-character boundaries tested. Full CI, Docker and CodeQL passed for commit 10ff2e4e (run 35846938073).

title: Right-axis titles overlap wide tick labels
description: Axis.drawTitle uses axisTitleOffset (tick-label height) for AxisPositionRight, so wide right-side tick labels can collide with the rotated title. Mirror the measured visible-label width behavior of the left-axis fix, while checking right margin/viewBox constraints and adding a targeted geometry regression.
close_reason: Right title now uses measured visible tick-label width; dedicated rendered-SVG geometry regression, full svggen race suite, lint, and root build pass.

title: nine_box_talent docs wrongly say numeric 1-3 ratings are ignored
description: docs/diagrams/nine_box_talent.md says numeric performance/potential ratings are ignored and collapse into Core Employee, but normalizeNineBoxLevel supports numeric 1-3 and regression coverage cites go-slide-creator-pc2a. Update the canonical guide and any agent-facing copies to match the implemented input contract.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical and agent-facing nine_box_talent documentation consistently describe accepted string and numeric rating forms; examples and tests remain aligned.
close_reason: Corrected canonical and agent-facing nine-box docs for string and numeric 1-3 ratings; existing numeric tests and MCP tests pass.

title: Pie/donut value_format is accepted but bypassed by slice labels
description: WHAT: pie_chart and donut_chart accept style.value_format under the shared chart schema, but PieChart.Draw formats slice labels directly through LabelFormat (default %.0f%%) and never resolves or uses ChartConfig.ValueFmt. Donut RenderWithBuilder does not even copy req.Style.ValueFormat into its config. Currency, compact, prefix/suffix and decimals therefore render differently from the documented one-format-per-chart contract, while generic value-format findings can describe defaults that the slice labels did not apply. WHERE: svggen/chart_diagrams.go PieChartDiagram/DonutChartDiagram RenderWithBuilder; svggen/charts.go PieChart.Draw around pctStr/LabelFormat. FIX: define the intended pie/donut contract explicitly (share percentages versus raw values), route supported value formatting through the shared formatter, reject or diagnose incompatible styles, and keep pie/donut behavior consistent. VERIFY: render-level table tests for percent decimals, prefix/suffix or explicit rejection, donut parity, and findings that match visible SVG output.
acceptance_criteria: Pie and donut no longer silently accept an ignored value_format; documented behavior, rendered labels, and findings agree; regression tests cover both chart types.
close_reason: Pie/donut slice labels now honor explicit value_format: percent formats calculated shares, other styles format raw values; findings, docs, and render-level parity tests agree.

title: Substance detectors misclassify `layout_id: "section"` dividers as content slides once resolveCanonicalLayoutIDs has rewritten the id
description:
Why: SLIDE_NEARLY_EMPTY "slide N carries 1 word(s) … add the substance" (fix add_items) fires on a section divider that carries a Section Number item; an agent that obeys it adds body copy to a divider. Seen on the real host-agent deck slide 4.
Root cause: dry_run.go:321 resolveCanonicalLayoutIDs() rewrites slides[i].LayoutID "section" -> "slideLayoutN" BEFORE collectFitFindings; fit_findings_substance.go slideCarriesArgument() -> inferSlideType() (json_mode.go:2245) only recognises the literal "section" string. Same hole affects MISSING_TITLE and monotony detectors.
Repro: deck with {layout_id:"section", title, "Section Number":"01"} -> `validate --json --fit-report` emits INPUT.SLIDE_NEARLY_EMPTY at /slides/1.
Fix: slideCarriesArgument consults the resolved layout's tags (section-header) via the `layouts` already passed in (or placeholderrole.IsSectionNumberAlias on content); add a regression test. Evidence: .claude/review-evidence/r3/orchestrator-ledger.md O1.
close_reason: inferSlideType now recognizes resolved section layout metadata, and substance/monotony checks receive the same layouts. A regression covers a title-less numbered section divider and confirms a true sparse content slide is still flagged; full short suite and lint pass.

title: contrast_predicted (validate) disagrees with contrast_autofixed (generate): 9 predicted vs 4 actual swaps, different replacement colours, white_text_safe ignored
description:
Why: an agent pre-fixes colours that the renderer would have kept (white 28pt KPI value predicted -> #000000 on #D4463A; render correctly keeps white) and trusts wrong replacements (#D4463A -> #BD3F34 predicted; render swaps to #1B2A4A). On the real host-agent deck: validate --verbose-fit predicts 9 swaps, generate --json-output-report performs 4; 5 predictions never happen, 1 replacement differs, 1 swap (#43A047 -> #337936 sibling propagation) unpredicted. Template-portability reviewer reproduced the disagreement on 6/9 templates.
Root cause: internal/generator/preflight_contrast.go:50 claims parity with text_contrast.go:690 (threshold from smallestTextPt + bold), but the pair builder in cmd/json2pptx/fit_findings_collect.go:1504 passes a different TextPt/Bold (TextPt 0 => 4.5:1) and never applies the sibling-cell propagation or white_text_safe (text_contrast.go:255) that the renderer applies.
Fix: build preflight pairs from the resolved run sizes the renderer uses (smallest run in the cell txBody, bold flag, white_text_safe, sibling propagation) — ideally by calling the same function on the compiled shape XML; parity test asserting predicted set == autofixed set for every examples/*.json across the 9 templates. Evidence: .claude/review-evidence/r3/orchestrator-ledger.md O2; .claude/review-evidence/r3/quality-signals/report.md F5; .claude/review-evidence/r3/template-portability/report.md F-11.

title: BUG: DeckSpec schema must reject an empty flat slides array
description:
Location: internal/semantic/schema.go Schema root slides property and schema tests.

Problem: runtime validation requires at least one flat slide, but the published JSON Schema declares slides as an array without minItems. A schema-aware MCP client therefore accepts {slides: []} even though validate_deck_spec and semantic validate reject it. The structured sections branch already enforces minItems:1, so the two authoring forms disagree at the schema boundary.

Change: add minItems:1 to the top-level slides schema and ensure the constraint survives both the full nested validate_deck_spec schema and the outline schemas used by other semantic tools.

Verification: schema unit tests assert minItems:1 in Schema, CompactSchemaAt, and OutlineInlineSchema; MCP tool schema test checks validate_deck_spec and one outline tool; runtime empty-slide validation remains unchanged.

title: BUG: detect arbitrarily long numeric section labels as sequence mismatches
description:
Location: cmd/json2pptx/fit_findings_substance.go collectSectionNumberSequenceFindings.

Problem: numeric section labels are parsed with strconv.Atoi. Labels longer than the platform integer range return an error and are skipped, so an authored all-digit label can evade SECTION_NUMBER_SEQUENCE_MISMATCH even though it is plainly not the expected sequence.

Change: compare normalized decimal strings instead of machine integers: validate digits, trim leading zeroes with zero normalization, and compare against the current section index. Preserve accepted variants such as 1 and 01 for section one and the existing expected two-digit repair value.

Verification: table-driven tests for 1, 01, mismatched 02, all-zero values, and a hundred-digit label. Assert huge numeric labels receive the normal mismatch finding and repair payload.
acceptance_criteria: Every all-digit label is compared without overflow; equivalent zero-padded expected values pass; huge and incorrect values yield the existing structured mismatch finding.
close_reason: Numeric section labels now compare normalized decimal strings without machine integer overflow; huge/all-zero regression cases added.

title: Semantic quality: diagnose missing evidence visuals and narrow visual-family breadth
description:
## What
Add semantic diagnostics for evidence and visual-family breadth so research and market-analysis decks cannot appear complete while relying almost entirely on bullets and decorative boxes.

The failed agentic-AI deck had seven slides but only two text layouts, KPI rectangles, and a strategy-house. It contained no chart, image, timeline, or data-bearing visual. Existing rhythm checks catch consecutive identical families, but they do not ask whether the deck uses an appropriate evidence visual for its archetype.

## Where
- internal/semantic/rhythm.go and DeckIR visual-family metadata
- internal/semantic/archetypes.go / archetype definitions
- semantic validate, explain, render quality summaries
- internal/diagnostics codes and descriptions
- skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md, FINDINGS.md, docs/SCHEMA_CHANGELOG.md

## How
Define conservative archetype-level expectations rather than a universal image quota. For example, `market_analysis` should contain at least one data-bearing evidence slide (`chart_insight`, `table`, `kpi_snapshot`, or sourced stat) and should not consist solely of structural/text/comparison slides. Longer decks should expose their distinct visual-family count and evidence-family count in explain/quality output.

Emit advisory diagnostics such as `SEMANTIC_EVIDENCE_VISUAL_MISSING` and `SEMANTIC_VISUAL_FAMILY_NARROW` with suggested compatible slide kinds. Keep exceptions explicit for short decks and decks whose archetype does not imply external evidence. Do not require decorative stock imagery.

## Verification
- A 7-slide market-analysis spec containing only title, bullets, comparison, section, and closing emits an evidence-visual warning.
- Adding a sourced chart or KPI slide clears the evidence warning.
- A varied 10-slide market-analysis deck reports its family counts and passes.
- A 3-slide status note and a strategy proposal with appropriate non-chart evidence do not false-positive.
- Explain, validate, render, and MCP/CLI responses carry identical diagnostic codes and semantic paths.
- Add calibration cases for at least three archetypes and document why each passes or warns.
- Run `go test ./internal/semantic/... ./cmd/json2pptx/...` and `golangci-lint run ./...`.
acceptance_criteria: Archetype-aware semantic validation warns when a market-analysis deck has no data-bearing evidence visual or materially narrow visual-family breadth; short/non-evidence decks avoid false positives; explain/validate/render expose consistent counts and diagnostics with calibration tests.
notes: Distinct from closed go-slide-creator-xx9i: xx9i gates consecutive-pattern composition. This bead adds archetype-aware evidence-family and deck-level visual-family breadth diagnostics.
close_reason: Implemented the specified schema, compiler, validation, rendering, MCP/CLI, documentation, and skill changes. Verified with go test ./..., go build ./..., golangci-lint (0 issues), skill canonical check, bead lint, all-seven-layout semantic render, template-missing coverage unit test, and midnight-blue/warm-coral JPG inspection for divider numbers and blank-canvas strategy-house headline clearance.

title: Preflight fit and readability detectors ignore deck rhythm grid
description:
WHAT

Several preflight detectors still call resolveGridGeometry without a rhythm grid: collectStructuralFindings (fit_findings_collect.go), shape-grid text fit (fit_report.go), and readability findings (readability_findings.go). On a deck with an explicit rhythm grid, those detectors measure different cell rectangles from generation and can miss or invent overflow, collision, and readability findings.

FIX
Carry the resolved deck rhythm grid through the shared preflight geometry contract and use the same takeaway-aware zone as generation in all detectors. Add a regression where a narrow rhythm frame changes a text-fit finding and assert preflight/generation coordinates agree.

Standalone pattern expansion now uses template LayoutBounds, matching generation; compose/pattern preflight and preview reuse the shared valid-grid resolver. Regression demonstrates a 1000-word cell fits the template area but overflows the tighter rhythm area and predicts 3.6pt versus 7.2pt readability. Corrected schema-maxima pins for newly visible process-flow (9.1pt) and timeline-horizontal (5.5pt) debt; updated existing go-slide-creator-tp23k to cover 33 remaining patterns. title: Preview ignores deck rhythm grid when expanding and placing shapes
description:
WHAT

Generate calls patternExpansionGeometry with rhythmGrid and overrides the content zone before pattern expansion and rendering. A deck with an explicit grid can therefore preview one set of cell positions/heights and generate another.

The existing three-surface preview/generate parity test now runs both template-default and configured-rhythm cases and compares selected layout, every cell rectangle, and generated shape XML; all six cases pass. title: Compose content-sized leaves use full-slide bounds instead of segment bounds
description:
WHAT
expandCompose in cmd/json2pptx/compose.go expands every leaf pattern with the same slide-level ExpandContext before resolving segment size_pct and merging the grids. A content-sized leaf (for example kpi-3up) therefore computes font fit, card height, and column width against the whole slide content rectangle even when the merged segment receives only a fraction of that rectangle. Supplying the correct slide LayoutBounds in go-slide-creator-byr2b fixes the top-level box but cannot make each segment size to its own allocated box.

REPRO
Compose a kpi-3up leaf in a 50% horizontal segment or a short vertical segment and compare its expansion decisions with the cell rectangle it renders into. Nested compose has the same issue because inner envelopes receive the outer context unchanged.

FIX
Resolve segment allocation before leaf expansion where sizes are explicit. For smart_compose, define an iterative or conservative sizing contract that avoids circular density calculation. Give each leaf and nested compose its allocated LayoutBounds, and test rendered fit across horizontal, vertical, and nested cases.
notes: Compose now probes each segment once for row/column structure and smart density, computes its allocated rectangle including merged grid gaps, and expands each leaf/nested compose again with that LayoutBounds. Fixed smart shares derive from content-only probe to avoid a sizing/density cycle. Regression covers explicit and smart vertical KPI row sizes (139pt full to 91pt/101pt), horizontal KPI value font (36pt full to 26pt), and nested compose inheritance. Full go test ./... passed, golangci-lint 0 issues, go build ./... passed. Rendered and visually inspected 3 compose slides each on midnight-blue and warm-coral. title: Preview auto-layout can differ from generated pattern and compose slides

WHAT

Generate binds pattern/compose/shape_grid slides to the canonical blank-title canvas before heuristic scoring in json_mode.go:convertSinglePresentationSlide. The preview's resolved layout and content rectangle can therefore differ from the generated slide. Supplying LayoutBounds to preview pattern expansion does not solve this upstream mismatch.

REPRO

FIX
Make preview use the same composition layout selection rule and geometry as generation. Add an end-to-end parity regression for automatic pattern and compose slides, including layout ID and resolved cell bounds.

It preserves auto placeholder mapping before assigning the resolved layout ID to geometry expansion. title: Generate path expands patterns without LayoutBounds, so content-sized patterns size against the wrong box
description:
Root cause found while closing go-slide-creator-4uxi (2026-09-20).

WHAT
All three patterns.ExpandContext constructions on the generate path (cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go, for compose, pattern, and nested cell patterns) set Metadata/SlideWidth/SlideHeight/AccentStrategy/SlideIndex/SectionIndex/Theme but NOT LayoutBounds. expandContentSize() therefore falls through to shapegrid.DefaultBounds(slideWidth, slideHeight), so every pattern that sizes itself with contentAreaPt()/expandContentSize() measures against the full-slide default instead of the template content zone the renderer actually lays the grid into.

MEASURED (kpi-3up, midnight-blue, 16:9):
  without LayoutBounds: contentH = 388.8pt -> row max_height 175.0pt (45.0% of 388.8)
  with    LayoutBounds: contentH = 308.1pt -> row max_height 139.0pt (45.1% of 308.1)
The renderer frame is 3913340 EMU = 308.1pt, so the emitted 175pt is 56.8% of it. That is exactly the 57% closure-audit-1 reported as c1.11, and it is not a KPI bug: the pattern applies its fraction correctly to the box it was handed.

BLAST RADIUS
Every content-sized pattern, not just kpi-Nup: anything calling contentAreaPt / expandContentSize for cap rows, column widths, or label-fit decisions (kpi-Nup, process-flow, icon-row, value-chain, horizontal-bar-with-callouts, waterfall-bridge, ...). Each is sizing against a box ~26% taller than the real one on midnight-blue.

WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-LINE FIX
The zone depends on the resolved layout, and for a pattern slide with no layout_id the layout is chosen by resolveVirtualLayout -- which needsVirtualLayout() gates on slide.ShapeGrid != nil, i.e. AFTER expansion. So supplying LayoutBounds means resolving geometry before expansion (or a two-pass resolve), which reorders convertSinglePresentationSlide.

EXPECT CHURN: this changes the size of every pattern block at generation. Budget for golden_hashes.json rebaseline on all four templates, the TemplatePatternMatrix, and a visual sweep of the pattern gallery on at least midnight-blue and warm-coral.

WHERE
cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go (the three ExpandContext literals), cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go (needsVirtualLayout / resolveGridGeometry ordering).

VERIFY
Expand kpi-3up on midnight-blue through the generate path and assert the emitted row max_height is 0.45 * the SAME content height the renderer uses (308.1pt -> 139pt), and that preflight and generate agree on the zone.
notes: Resolved grid geometry before expansion and passed LayoutBounds to pattern, compose, and nested cell expansion. Nested patterns now size against their inset cell rectangles. Aligned compose and pattern fit preflight and preview expansion with layout-aware bounds, including canonical layout aliases. Regression covers midnight-blue generate/preflight KPI parity, a 3913340-EMU rhythm frame yielding a 139pt KPI row, compose preflight/generate shape equality, and nested KPI sizing. Full go test ./... passed; post-alias cmd/json2pptx short suite passed; TemplatePatternMatrix passed; golangci-lint 0 issues; go build ./... passed. Three separate follow-ups filed for preview auto-layout (iy892), compose segment bounds (burq4), and explicit pattern bounds (a2ldx). Golden hashes remained unchanged. Visually inspected 3 pattern slides each on midnight-blue and warm-coral; no clipping or overlap seen.

title: value-chain does not measure its step labels, so 10-step chains render mid-word breaks
description:
WHAT
examples/value-chain.json slide 4 (10-step closed-loop chain) renders "Manufactur / ing", "intermediat / e inputs" and "Decommissi / oning end- / of-life" — the bundled showcase deck ships the defect. Found while measuring go-slide-creator-rxkt (rendered /tmp/vc/s-4.png, soffice -> pdftoppm).

The deterministic detector already reports it as an advisory TEXT_EXCEEDS_SHAPE (ratio 1.35 for "Manufacturing", 1.55 for "Decommissioning"), but advisory is all it can be: the same detector fires at 1.15 on examples/process-grid-2row.json, which renders correctly, so the estimate cannot be trusted to block.

WHERE
internal/patterns/value_chain.go — the step-label sizing. Compare internal/patterns/numbered_step_strip.go fitChevronLabels, which measures each label against the shape's text width, surrenders notch depth, shrinks to a 12pt floor and then reports what still does not fit via PostExpandWarnings. That measured warning is now blocking (go-slide-creator-rxkt), so a value-chain that did the same would fail the gate on a deck that genuinely breaks.

HOW
Give value-chain the same treatment: measure the widest word of each step label against the step column width at the authored size, shrink to a readable floor, and emit TEXT_EXCEEDS_SHAPE from PostExpandWarnings for the labels that still cannot fit. Then shorten the labels in examples/value-chain.json (or drop it to fewer steps) so the bundled deck is clean.

VERIFY
Render examples/value-chain.json: no mid-word break on any slide. j2p score --json examples/value-chain.json passes the gate. A 10-step chain with genuinely long labels emits the blocking TEXT_EXCEEDS_SHAPE.
close_reason:
Fixed in 95779aa1 (+ 3a545936 restoring the example file compact formatting).

CHANGE: new fitValueChainLabels in internal/patterns/valuechain.go measures every step label against its own column width (equalColumnWidthPt over the content area, minus 2x defaultShapeInsetLRPt), shrinks ONE shared size until each fits on a single line, and returns the labels that still cannot. Expand uses the fitted size; PostExpandWarnings emits TEXT_EXCEEDS_SHAPE for the unfit ones, which is blocking since go-slide-creator-rxkt, so a deck that will break mid-word now fails the quality gate. The existing highlight-contrast warning still stacks alongside it.

THE FLOOR IS THE RENDERER FLOOR — the whole lesson of this bead. My first cut used 9pt. The expansion duly emitted size 9, and the rendered PPTX came back with sz="1200" and the same "Manufactur / ing" break: internal/shapegrid raises any authored size below shapegrid.MinTextSizePt (12pt) back to 12. A fit that promises a size the renderer will not honour is not a fit. valueChainMinLabelPt now REFERENCES shapegrid.MinTextSizePt rather than repeating a number, and a test asserts the two stay equal. (That is also why numbered-step-strip chevronMinLabelPt is 12.)

With the floor right the pattern names exactly the two labels the render breaks: "Manufacturing, Distribution" at 10 steps.

VERIFY:
- examples/value-chain.json slide 4 shortened (Manufacturing->Make, Distribution->Deliver, and two descriptions whose long words broke). Rendered soffice->pdftoppm at /tmp/vc5/s-4.png: every one of the ten labels on a single line, every description wrapping at word boundaries, no mid-word break anywhere.
- j2p score --json examples/value-chain.json --template midnight-blue: gate passes. Before the label edit the same command failed the gate with "1 P1 (shrink_or_split)" naming the two labels — i.e. the new check catches the defect that was actually shipping.

TESTS: internal/patterns/valuechain_test.go — six short labels leave 12pt alone; the floor equals the renderer floor (guards the exact mistake above); ten steps report Manufacturing and Distribution as unfit and do NOT report the ones that fit; the warning carries the blocking code prefix and stacks with the highlight warning; short labels say nothing.

DOCS: docs/PATTERNS.md gained a "Fitting a label to its shape" section stating the contract (measure the width the shape leaves, shrink one shared size, floor at the RENDERER floor, report the rest as TEXT_EXCEEDS_SHAPE) for the next pattern that paints text into a shape it sized itself; docs/SCHEMA_CHANGELOG.md.

GATES: make lint (pinned v2.8.0) 0 issues both modules; go test ./... green both modules.

title: Native panel_layout bodies are ~80% empty; stat_cards content is top-anchored
description:
Split out of go-slide-creator-rkq0 (closed in 63c66fe5, which fixed the picture-frame half: the svggen coordinate-scale collapse, the natural-aspect override for org_chart/gantt/timeline, and the native process_flow step height).

WHAT (reproduced 2026-09-20, midnight-blue, rendered and looked at):
A native diagram_value of type panel_layout with three panels draws a header band and a body rectangle per panel, and the body rectangle fills the whole remaining placeholder height with the text anchored to the top. A one-sentence body leaves roughly 80% of each bordered box empty — a visible outline around nothing. Evidence: /tmp/plr/s-1.png.
stat_cards has the same class of problem per the round-2 charts-diagrams review (content top-anchored with a blank lower half); a first attempt to reproduce it used the wrong data key and rendered an empty slide, so the data shape needs establishing first.

WHERE
internal/generator/panel_shapes.go: generatePanelGroupXML (bands from panelColumnsBands(totalHeight, hasIcons), body box gets all remaining height), generatePanelBodyXML (Anchor "t"). generateStatCardsGroupXML for the stat_cards half.

HOW
Measure each panel body at the panel width with internal/textfit (the generator already uses it for tables), take the max across the row so the panels keep a shared baseline, size the body band to that plus insets, and centre the whole group vertically within the placeholder bounds. This is the native-shape equivalent of what internal/patterns does with contentCardHeightPt + GridVerticalAlignDefault. Do NOT simply switch the body anchor to centre: the box itself is the wrong size, and centring the text inside an oversized outline still reads as an empty box.

VERIFY
Regenerate a 3-panel panel_layout and a 3-card stat_cards on midnight-blue AND warm-coral: each body box hugs its text (< 30% unused area per box, the target docs/PATTERNS.md already states for cards) and the group sits at the vertical centre of the placeholder. Cite the before/after PNG paths.

Gates: golangci-lint run ./... both modules; go test ./... both modules; go test -run TemplatePatternMatrix ./cmd/json2pptx/...
close_reason:
Fixed in c6583de9. Native panel_layout bodies and stat_cards are now sized to the text in them and centred in the placeholder.

REPRO (before): /tmp/panels.json on midnight-blue, rendered soffice->pdftoppm. /tmp/plr/s-1.png shows three body rectangles each ~260px tall holding one line of ~15px text — a bordered outline around ~85% empty space. /tmp/plr/s-2.png shows three stat cards ~330px tall for a hero + caption; the text was already Anchor ctr (so "top-anchored" in the report was really "card far taller than its content"), and the card itself was the wrong size.

CHANGE (new internal/generator/panel_content_fit.go):
- panelBodyBoxHeight measures a panel body at the panel width with internal/textfit, using the same paragraphs panelBulletsParagraphs produces so the measurement sees the renderer own line breaks. measureWidthEMU adds back the 7.2pt side margins textfit subtracts, because the body box declares its own insets.
- panelColumnsLayout keeps the icon / header / gap bands at their existing sizes (fixed furniture) and sizes only the body band, to the tallest body in the row so the panels keep a shared baseline. Returns the y-offset that centres the group.
- statCardsLayout / statCardBoxHeight do the same for the grid, measuring hero (32pt), caption (12pt) and delta (11pt) at their own sizes plus insets and any icon band.
- generatePanelGroupXML / generateStatCardsGroupXML take the theme body font (ctx.themeFontName) and apply the offset; panelGroupBounds narrows the group rect to what it draws; panelIconRects applies the same offset so icons stay on their cards.
- Only ever shrinks: content needing the full height keeps it with offset 0. Every measured block carries half a line of slack (panelBodySlackFrac) so a substituted face cannot clip the last line.

VERIFY (rendered and looked at, both templates):
- midnight-blue after: /tmp/plr2/s-1.png (3 panels, boxes hug 1-2 lines, group centred), /tmp/plr2/s-2.png (3 stat cards hugging hero+caption, grid centred).
- warm-coral after: /tmp/plr3/s-3.png (dense: 5-bullet panel, 2-bullet panel, 3-line prose panel — box sized to the tallest, nothing clipped) and /tmp/plr3/s-4.png (4 stat cards with delta lines, all three lines present, grid centred).
- Machine check, new internal/generator/panel_content_fit_test.go: TestPanelColumnsBodyHugsText and TestStatCardsHugContent assert <= 30% unused area (the docs/PATTERNS.md card target); TestPanelColumnsGroupIsCentred and the stat-card half assert equal slack above and below; TestPanelColumnsDenseBodyKeepsFullBand asserts dense content keeps the full band at offset 0; TestPanelBodyBoxHeightGrowsWithText / TestStatCardBoxHeightCountsEveryLine assert the measurement responds to content; TestMeasureWidthEMUCompensatesInsets pins the inset compensation.

Golden internal/generator/testdata/golden/panel_columns_4.xml regenerated (group 4197500 -> 1747500 tall, y 2129246 -> 3354260).

title: plan_deck pads a long deck with repeated roles, which is what forces repeated patterns
description:
WHAT
go-slide-creator-8fq4 capped how often one pattern FAMILY may appear in a plan (twice), and the cap holds at a 10-slide budget. At 20 it cannot always: the planner allocates four comparison slots and three framework slots from a three-sentence brief, and the comparison role has only a handful of candidate patterns, so two or three slides end up with the same one whatever the cap says. The residual is now reported in rhythm_check.repeated_families rather than hidden, but the reporting is a workaround for the real cause.

THE REAL CAUSE
Role allocation scales the slot counts with the slide budget rather than with what the brief can actually support. A brief with one comparison ("build vs buy") produces four comparison slots at budget 20. Pattern selection is then asked to make four different-looking slides out of one idea, which no cap can do.

HOW (sketch)
Cap each narrative role by the evidence the brief carries for it — the fact extractor already classifies quantity and named-entity clauses — and let the leftover budget go to roles that can absorb it (evidence, emphasis) or simply return a shorter plan than the budget with a note saying why. A plan that says "this brief supports 12 slides, not 20" is more useful than 20 slides of which 6 repeat.

VERIFY
For each brief in internal/deckplan.metricBriefs at budget 20, rhythm_check.repeated_families is empty, OR the plan returns fewer slides than the budget with a stated reason. internal/deckplan.TestPlanCapsPatternRepeats already asserts the 10-slide case and tolerates the reported 20-slide case; tighten it when this lands.
close_reason:
Fixed in 748af67f. Role allocation is now bounded by what can fill each role, and the variety cap can actually enforce itself.

CAUSE CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT (baseline in a HEAD worktree, budget 20, the four internal/deckplan.metricBriefs):
  board QBR   roles=map[comparison:3 emphasis:4 evidence:8 framework:3] repeats=[before-after x4 comparison-2col x3]
  quarterly   comparison:3 ... repeats=[before-after x4 process-flow x3]
  migration   comparison:3 ... repeats=[before-after x4 kpi x4]
  unit econs  comparison:3 ... repeats=[before-after x4 kpi x4 process-flow x3]

CHANGES
1. internal/deckplan/role_capacity.go (new): roleFamilyCapacity (comparison = the closed comparisonFamily, everything else = distinct families in the registry whose taxonomy covers the role), roleBriefCapacity (comparison = the number of brief CLAUSES carrying a comparison cue, so "compare build vs buy" is one comparison, not three cues; a brief with none still gets the arc single decision moment), and applyRoleCapacity, which trims over-capacity roles, moves the surplus to evidence/framework/emphasis, and returns a note when the surplus fits nowhere.
2. distributeRoles takes the registry and brief and returns (roles, note); proportionalRoleCounts split out to keep gocognit under the ceiling. A plan whose surplus cannot be placed comes back SHORTER than the budget, ending on the closing slide.
3. New Result.BudgetNote (JSON budget_note), omitted on a full-length plan.
4. findRepeatReplacement searched only 12 recommender candidates; a 20-slide plan has already spent a dozen families by then, so it returned "" and the repeat stood. It now searches len(reg.List()) candidates and appends taxonomyFallbackCandidates for the role.
5. That wider search immediately broke go-slide-creator-xmpb invariant by putting horizontal-bar-with-callouts in a comparison slot (caught by TestBuildDeckPlan_StructuralSlidesComparisonAndEmphasisCap/long). Replacements for a comparison slot are now confined to comparisonFamily.
6. Because a comparison slot cannot move, capPatternRepeats now counts role-locked slots FIRST (alongside must_include) so an ordinary slide earlier in the deck gives the family up instead of spending it. Without this, board QBR still showed before-after x3.

VERIFY (the bead condition, met on the first branch — no plan needed shortening):
  board QBR / quarterly / migration / unit econs, budgets 10 AND 20: repeated_families = [] and budget_note = "".
  Wider sweep, 9 briefs (the 4 metric briefs plus series-b, transformation, annual, short, qbr) x every budget 3..30 = 252 plans: zero plans with a repeated family and no explanation; zero plans whose slide count differs from the budget without a note.
  Comparison slots dropped from 3 to 1 for a one-comparison brief at budget 20.

TESTS: internal/deckplan/role_capacity_test.go — comparisonClauseCount counts ideas not cues; roleCapacity bounds comparison by both the family size and the brief while leaving evidence unbounded; applyRoleCapacity moves the surplus without losing slots, and shortens with a note naming "4 fewer slide" / "comparison 5→1" when nothing can absorb it; distributeRoles keeps opening/closing; comparison slots stay inside their family across all four metric briefs. TestPlanCapsPatternRepeats tightened as the bead asked: a full-length plan may not repeat at all, and a repeat is only tolerated alongside a budget_note. title: Shape-scaled text budgets for the remaining 33 over-budget patterns
description:
WHAT
cmd/json2pptx.TestSchemaMaximaStayReadable (go-slide-creator-0g6p) measures, for every registered pattern, the smallest size its own schema maximum renders at, across all four bundled templates. 33 of 43 patterns permit schema-legal content that lands below the 12pt readable floor. card-grid has the fix: the cap stays (it is right for the smallest shape) and PostExpandWarnings names the budget for the shape the author actually chose. The other 32 still have only TEXT_BELOW_READABLE_MIN, which says the text will shrink but not how much is affordable.

THE MEASURED TABLE (smallest predicted size at schema maxima, worst first; corrected in go-slide-creator-7eib to take the WORST template rather than the best)
card-grid 2.4 (FIXED), bmc-canvas 3.8, driver-tree 4.1, comparison-2col 4.2, roadmap-phased 5.0, team-bios 5.5, swimlane 5.5, numbered-step-strip 5.8, kpi-inline 5.8, horizontal-bar-with-callouts 6.0, agenda-with-images 6.0, before-after-compact 6.0, phase-roadmap 6.2, timeline-horizontal 6.2, stylish-panels 6.4, hero-detail 6.7, table-highlight 6.7, quote-cluster 6.7, dual-org-ladder 7.0, exec-summary 7.2, waterfall-bridge 7.2, stat-hero 7.4, scqa-summary 7.4, agenda 7.8, value-chain 8.2, strategy-house 8.2, arch-stack 8.6, journey-maturity-model 9.1, process-flow-compact 9.1, pyramid 9.2, chart-insights-split 9.4, matrix-2x2 10.1, pull-quote 17.3.
Clean at their maxima: before-after, icon-row, image-text-split, kpi-2up..kpi-6up, process-flow, process-grid-2row.

HOW
Per pattern, the same three steps card-grid took:
1. Probe the readable budget at each shape: build the payload at that shape, run collectReadabilityFindings against a real template, step the length down until it is clean. (card-grid's probe is in the go-slide-creator-0g6p commit history.)
2. Add a measured budget function and emit BODY_TOO_LONG from PostExpandWarnings naming the shape and the number the author has to hit.
3. Put the table in the field's schema description, and RAISE the pin in schemaMaximaShrinkPt (the gate fails when a pin improves without following, so an improvement has to be recorded).

TWO THINGS TO INVESTIGATE FIRST
- bmc-canvas's probe has a cliff that does not look physical: 1-3 bullets per cell are readable at the full 200 characters, 4-6 collapse to ~10, and 7+ fit nothing. Nine cells of very different heights share one budget; find the binding cell before writing the table.
- pull-quote at 17.3pt is flagged against a DISPLAY role floor, not the 12pt one. A 500-character quote renders perfectly well (looked at it), so check the role floor before treating it as a defect.

VERIFY
TestSchemaMaximaStayReadable's pins move UP, each with its measured probe; no pattern's maxLength is lowered where the small-shape budget is genuinely that size.
notes:
2026-09-20 geometry correction: standalone collectReadabilityFindings now expands patterns against the real template content rectangle (go-slide-creator-vrckb), matching generation. TestSchemaMaximaStayReadable remeasures process-flow at 9.1pt rather than clean/0 and timeline-horizontal at 5.5pt rather than 6.2pt; pins updated to record the newly visible debt. Include process-flow in the shape-scaled budget work and use 5.5pt as timeline baseline. These are measurement corrections, not new authoring limits.
2026-09-21 completion audit: all 32 remaining patterns were investigated in child Beads. Shape-aware BODY_TOO_LONG guidance was added for binding cases; pull-quote was reclassified as prose and arch-stack measured clean at all schema maxima. Existing schema-maxima shrink pins remain measurements of intentionally retained worst-case legal payloads, so the original instruction to raise those pins conflicts with preserving sparse maxima; authored content now gets specific fit-report budgets instead. Full short suite, lint, and build passed after final production change; arch-stack opt-in probe passed all four templates.
close_reason: All child calibrations closed. Binding pattern copy now receives measured, actionable fit-report budgets; pull-quote uses the correct prose floor and arch-stack stays readable at maximum content. Schema maxima were retained for sparse layouts, so the original shrink pins remain measurements of worst-case legal payloads.

title: Porter's five forces prints an invented "Medium (50%)" when no intensity was given
description:
WHAT
internal/generator/porters_shapes.go:porterForceFromMap defaults intensity to 0.5 when the payload does not carry one, and the renderer then prints "Medium (50%)" under every force label. The author never said that. A five-forces chart where all five read "Medium (50%)" looks like an assessment and is actually a default.

EVIDENCE
Rendered a five-forces slide from a payload with factors and no intensities (midnight-blue): all five boxes show "Medium (50%)" and all five take the accent3 tint, so the colour coding — the whole point of the intensity — says nothing.

HOW
porterForceData needs an "unset" intensity distinct from 0.5: a *float64, or a hasIntensity bool. When unset:
- draw the force in a neutral fill rather than the medium tint, and
- omit the intensity line entirely rather than printing a number nobody supplied.
When SOME forces carry an intensity and others do not, that is worth a finding of its own (a partially scored chart is misread as a fully scored one).

NOTE
go-slide-creator-anzx's DeckSpec `framework` kind passes an author-stated intensity through (including "high"/"medium"/"low" as words) and deliberately does NOT invent one, so the fix here is the renderer's alone.

VERIFY
A five-forces payload with no intensities renders with no intensity labels and a neutral fill; one with intensities is unchanged; a mixed payload emits the new finding.
close_reason:
Fixed (efae7b0e).

THE FIX
porterForceData.intensity is now *float64, so "the author did not score this" is distinct from 0.5 rather than equal to it. An unscored force is drawn on the template's neutral surface (lt2) with NO intensity line at all; a scored one is unchanged. The encoding that round-trips forces through the panel value field ("type:intensity") encodes an unstated intensity as an empty field, so "nobody scored this" survives the trip instead of becoming 0.5 on the other side.

THE FINDING I DID NOT ADD
The bead (mine) proposed a finding for a PARTIALLY scored chart. After the fix it is unnecessary and I left it out: the render itself now says it. Two neutral boxes with no intensity line beside three coloured ones with labels is unmistakable on the slide — better than a finding that says the same thing in a different surface. Verified by rendering a 3-of-5 payload and looking at it.

TWO THINGS THIS TURNED UP
1. pptx.LumMod(0) writes a 0% luminance, which renders BLACK — it is not "no modifier". The first render of the fix was five black boxes with invisible text. The neutral fill now omits the modifiers entirely (porterBoxFill), and the test asserts no zero lumMod is emitted. The unscored box's outline also moves to dk2: lt2 on white is not an edge.
2. Measuring the fixed render turned up a second contrast defect on the same slide, pre-existing: the intensity line was painted in the box's OWN scheme colour on the box's own tint of that colour. Measured on midnight-blue: 3.28, 2.62 and 1.55 for high / low / medium — all below AA, the last by a factor of three. porterIntensityTextColor now picks lt1 or dk2 against the fill a reader actually sees, the same way heatmapValueColor does (go-slide-creator-vdvs). Measured after: 5.63, 7.08, 10.11. Without theme colours there is nothing to measure and the historical colour stands.

EVIDENCE
Rendered two slides on midnight-blue through the new DeckSpec framework kind — one with no intensities at all, one with three of five scored — converted via soffice+pdftoppm and looked at both, and sampled the pixel ratios quoted above. Tests: TestPorterUnscoredForceAssertsNothing (no "Medium", no "50%", neutral scheme, no zero lumMod, and a scored force keeps "High (85%)") and TestPorterIntensityTextIsPickedByMeasurement (the text colour is never the fill's own, and falls back to the historical colour with no theme).

DOCS
docs/diagrams/porters_five_forces.md's field table said "default 0.5 if omitted" — now says what omitting it actually does. svggen's capability OverflowBehavior for the type says it too, so an agent budgeting against the capability sees it.

GATES
golangci-lint 0 issues in both modules; go test ./... passes in both; build clean.

title: Detect pattern/content mismatch: a timeline of KPIs, a 2x2 of dates
description:
WHAT
The engine has no signal for a pattern that does not match its content. The calibration corpus's B07_wrong_pattern draws Q3 KPIs ($48M / 118% / 41d) as a timeline-horizontal and an implementation timeline (January, April, August, December) as a matrix-2x2. Every slide is structurally sound — correct field counts, no overflow — so no geometric check sees it, and a human graded the deck 30/100.

It used to fail the gate, but only as a side effect of pattern_overcrowded firing on every conforming timeline and 2x2 (fixed in go-slide-creator-wrsb / 34b095ff). Catching one bad deck by accident is not a signal, so B07 is now a documented staticPathMisses entry.

HOW (sketch)
A content-shape check per pattern, emitted as a review-severity finding with a swap_pattern fix:
- timeline-horizontal whose stop LABELS are all numeric / currency / percentage while its DATES are words -> the author has the axes inverted, or wants kpi-Nup.
- matrix-2x2 whose four quadrant headers are all dates or months -> wants timeline-horizontal or phase-roadmap.
- process-flow / pyramid with one item per step and no verbs -> probably a list.
recommend_visual already ranks patterns for a stated intent; the same scoring, run backwards over an authored slide, is most of this.

VERIFY
B07_wrong_pattern fails the gate again, for the right reason (a named mismatch finding, not an overcrowding one), and no bundled example deck or the G* calibration decks gain a false mismatch finding. Then remove B07 from staticPathMisses in cmd/json2pptx/calibration_test.go.
close_reason:
Implemented in c9da8ab2. New PATTERN_CONTENT_MISMATCH finding.

WHAT IT CATCHES (cmd/json2pptx/fit_findings_pattern_match.go, read off the authored slides[].pattern.values at preflight, review severity, swap_pattern fix with {from, to}):
1. timeline-horizontal whose 3+ stops ALL carry a measurement label ($48M, 118%, 41d) and NO stop date is a period -> axes inverted; swap to kpi-Nup sized to the stop count.
2. matrix-2x2 whose four quadrant headers ALL name points in time -> swap to phase-roadmap.
3. process-flow / process-flow-compact / pyramid whose 3+ items are ALL short (<=3-word) labels carrying a figure ("EMEA $12M") -> swap to kpi-Nup.

NOT FIRING IS THE HARD PART (the previous signal, pattern_overcrowded, fired on every conforming timeline and 2x2 — go-slide-creator-wrsb). Every rule demands EVERY item match, and the two classifiers refuse the ambiguous cases:
- a bare number is a period, not a measure: "2026" / "3" are legitimate timeline stops (pinned in TestPeriodAndMeasureLabels);
- a timeline of metrics against REAL periods ($12M at Q1) is a trend and is correct;
- one named stop among measurements, or one non-date quadrant among three dates, clears the rule;
- a step that mentions a figure in prose ("Collect the first $1M in deposits") is still a step — only short label-plus-figure items count;
- fewer than 3 items is too few to judge.

VERIFY (bead condition):
- B07_wrong_pattern now emits 3 mismatch findings (slides 3, 4 and 5: the timeline of KPIs, the 2x2 of months, the process-flow of regional revenues), scores 55 and FAILS the quality gate — for the named mismatch, not an overcrowding one. Removed from staticPathMisses in cmd/json2pptx/calibration_test.go and added to TestCalibrationDefectClassesAreDetected so the specific code is pinned.
- Swept all 19 bundled example decks and all 16 calibration decks: the ONLY deck that reports a mismatch is B07. Pinned as TestPatternMismatchQuietOnBundledDecks so a future loosening of the rules shows up as a named false positive rather than a score drift.
- No G* deck gained a finding (they pass the gate; TestCalibrationRanking asserts good decks are never blocked).
- Spearman against the blind human grades: 0.800 -> 0.782, well above the 0.70 floor.

TESTS: cmd/json2pptx/fit_findings_pattern_match_test.go — TestPatternMismatchFires (all four shapes, asserting code, review action, swap_pattern from/to and the /slides/N/pattern path), TestPatternMismatchStaysQuiet (10 conforming cases including the near-misses above), TestPatternMismatchQuietOnBundledDecks, TestPeriodAndMeasureLabels (the classifiers, including that a bare number is neither).

DOCS: new code registered in internal/patterns/errors.go + finding_meta.go (so describe-finding covers it), docs/FIT_FINDINGS.md full section with the rule table and the deliberate non-firing cases, skills/generate-deck/FINDINGS.md row, docs/SCHEMA_CHANGELOG.md.
