title: Shrink the embedded DeckSpec schema: hoist universal + composition fields behind a $ref
description:
Split out of go-slide-creator-162os.

WHAT
validate_deck_spec and render_deck_spec each embed the closed DeckSpec schema (semantic.CompactInlineSchema) in their inputSchema, so every slide kind is paid TWICE in the core tools/list handshake. The universal fields (notes, source, …) and the composition fields are repeated verbatim in all 14 per-kind variants on top of that. Adding a kind costs ~2.4KB per tool and the core budget has been raised four times: 72 -> 80 -> 88 -> 96 -> 104KB. Three more kinds (agenda go-slide-creator-3rvk, team go-slide-creator-13lj, and whatever follows) push it past 110KB, which every session pays on connect.

HOW (sketch)
Emit the shared field groups once under the schema's own $defs and $ref them from each kind variant. The gotcha: the inline schema is merged INTO a tool property (withDeckSpecSchema in cmd/json2pptx/mcp_semantic.go), so a '#/$defs/x' pointer resolves against the whole inputSchema document, not the property — the refs have to be written as '#/properties/spec/$defs/x', or the merge has to hoist the defs to the inputSchema root. Verify against a schema-validating client, not just byte count.

VERIFY
Core tools/list drops below 96KB with the architecture kind still present; validate_deck_spec still rejects an unknown per-kind field (the closed-variant guarantee survives the refactor); TestExplainCompileParity and the payload-coverage gate stay green.
close_reason:
Closing on measurement: the premise is false. I filed this bead assuming the embedded DeckSpec schema repeated its universal/composition fields across all 14 per-kind variants at a cost worth hoisting. Measured on the real wire payload (tools/list, core profile):

- validate_deck_spec 19,506 B of which the `spec` property is 17,464 B; render_deck_spec 21,592 B. Together 41KB of a 103,685 B listing.
- Inside `spec`: 14 kind variants totalling 15,449 B; the items-level envelope is 316 B and `meta` is 1,001 B.
- Fields present in EVERY variant: kind, notes, source. Their TOTAL cost across all 14 variants is 1,284 B.
- Every repeated property blob is tiny — `title`, `notes`, `source`, `takeaway`, `layout`, `pattern` are all {"type":"string"} at 18 B each. Summed over all repeats: 1,260 B.
- A $ref costs ~30 B. Replacing every repeat with a ref plus one $defs entry would make the schema about 1KB BIGGER, not smaller (computed: -966 B of "savings").

So there is no repetition to hoist. The 17.5KB is 14 genuinely distinct per-kind payload contracts — irreducible content at this level of detail, and the thing that makes the schema closed and checkable before a call.

The only real levers on that 41KB, recorded here for whoever needs them:
1. Drop the inline schema from render_deck_spec and keep it on validate_deck_spec only (~17.5KB, 17% of the listing). The cost is that a schema-validating client can no longer check a render call before making it; the documented discovery path (list_slide_kinds -> per-kind item_schema + example) still works. This is a deliberate weakening of the closed-contract guarantee from go-slide-creator-h8o7 / dg8f, so it needs its own decision, not a refactor.
2. Fewer kinds, which is the opposite of what the deck-quality work needs.

Relevant to go-slide-creator-cm45, whose VERIFY asks for a core listing under 45KB: that is unreachable by re-cutting the profile alone — the two DeckSpec tools are 41KB of it, and the six tools cm45 proposes to demote are 9.6KB in total.

title: Post-draw geometry findings in svggen: plot collapse, text overlap, dropped items
description:
Split out of go-slide-creator-r87g (charts-diagrams finding ch.11). r87g fixed the report's false refuses and made the CLI and MCP surfaces run the same collector; this is the detector work it asked for and did not get.

WHAT IS STILL BLIND
After r87g the natively-rendered diagram fixtures report NOTHING (previously they reported a false refuse). Measured on .claude/review-evidence/r2/charts-diagrams/single/*__stress.json: business_model_canvas, heatmap, house_diagram, icon_columns, icon_rows, nine_box_talent, panel_layout (+rows/stat_cards/stylish), pestel, porters_five_forces, process_flow, pyramid, stat_cards, value_chain all return 0 findings, and the renders in .claude/review-evidence/r2/charts-diagrams/sheets/ show 3-4pt text, header/body overlap and row-label collisions. On the svggen side the same sweep never fired for plot-area collapse (grouped_bar stress, plot ~5% of canvas) or legend/axis-title overlap.

HOW
svggen already has a text measurer and a builder that knows every drawn box. Add a post-draw geometry pass that (a) computes the plot-area/canvas ratio, (b) tests drawn text bounding boxes pairwise for intersection, (c) counts items the renderer chose not to draw. Emit RENDER.chart.plot_area_collapsed, RENDER.diagram.text_overlap (with the colliding strings) and RENDER.diagram.items_dropped (with the count), and wire them through svggen.DryRender so the fit report carries them.

The native OOXML diagram builders (internal/generator/*_shapes.go) need the equivalent: they compute their own font sizes and rects, so a tiny-text and an overlap check belong there rather than in svggen. generator.IsNativeDiagramType (added by r87g) is the seam that tells the two apart.

VERIFY
j2p validate --fit-report on business_model_canvas__stress, value_chain__stress, heatmap__stress and panel_layout__stress each report at least one geometry finding naming the defect visible in the matching sheets/*.png; grouped_bar__stress reports plot_area_collapsed; no new finding on the 19 examples/ decks or the shipped gallery decks.

Gates: golangci-lint run ./... (both modules) && go test ./... -short -race. Visual evidence: the stress renders before/after, cited by path.
notes: 2026-09-21 completion: svggen records actual drawn text boxes and reports diagram.text_overlap through DryRender; timeline label/description collisions were fixed. Native OOXML preflight now reports dense/tiny text for every native stress fixture while real fixtures remain clean. Existing CapXLabelBand and tests cover true plot collapse; the current grouped-bar stress plot is healthy and instead reports its real axis-title collision. Existing Venn and org-chart paths report dropped/pruned items.
close_reason: Post-draw plot collapse, SVG text overlap, dropped/pruned items, and native OOXML text geometry now reach fit reports. The named stress fixtures produce the expected findings; shipped examples and real fixtures remain clean. Required root race, module tests, both linters and builds passed.

title: Contrast: snap to the template palette on an author-introduced background instead of lerping to the WCAG floor
description:
Found while implementing go-slide-creator-uy5s (background.color / background.overlay).

WHAT
contrastReplacementScheme snaps to a template text colour (lt1/dk2/dk1) only when the ORIGINAL foreground is neutral (white/black or scheme lt1/bg1/dk1/tx1); every other foreground is lerped toward contrast with svggen.EnsureContrast, which stops at exactly the threshold. On a background the AUTHOR introduced — background.color, or a scrim over a photo — the template's own title colour was chosen against a DIFFERENT background, so there is no hue intent to preserve, and lerping produces text that clears WCAG by 0.0 margin and reads as washed out.

Measured on midnight-blue, 60pt section title #1B2A4A:
  background.color dk1  -> auto-fixed to #4E5A72, ratio 1.5 -> 3.0 on #000000 (white would be 21)
  background.color dk2  -> auto-fixed to #6A7488, ratio 1.0 -> 3.0
  image + dk1 scrim a=0.55 -> #4E5A72 on #000000
Same shape on warm-coral. See /tmp/uy5s/img-1.png, img-2.png, imgwc-1.png (session renders).

WHERE
internal/generator/text_contrast.go contrastReplacementScheme (:501), isNeutralForeground, pickThemeTextColor (:291); internal/generator/preflight_contrast.go:82 shares the same function so validate-time advice matches generated output — both must learn the rule together or they diverge.

HOW
Thread the background's provenance (layout fill vs author-set colour/scrim) from prepareSlide through enforceTextContrastInSlide -> enforceTextContrastInShape -> fixSrgbColorsForContrast/fixSchemeColorsForContrast -> contrastReplacementScheme, and snap to pickThemeTextColor when the background is author-set. Keep the lerp for layout backgrounds so existing decks are unchanged. The preflight predictor needs the same input.

WHY NOT IN uy5s
It changes contrast output for a class of existing decks and touches the shared validate/generate guarantee, so it wants its own before/after render sweep rather than riding along with the feature that exposed it.

VERIFY
A slide with background.color dk1 and a template title colour that is not neutral renders the title in lt1 (ratio >= 7), not a mid-grey at exactly 3.0; validate's contrast_predicted finding names the same replacement generate emits; no change to any deck whose background comes from its layout.

Gates: golangci-lint run ./... && go test ./... -short -race. Visual evidence: midnight-blue AND warm-coral, before/after.
close_reason:
Done. Replacement now depends on the background's provenance.

WHAT CHANGED
- authorBackground threads from slide_preparation.go (bgHex != "" BEFORE the
  layout fallback) through enforceTextContrastInSlide -> enforceTextContrastInShape
  -> fixSchemeColorsForContrast / fixSrgbColorsForContrast -> contrastReplacementScheme.
  When it is set, the fix snaps to pickThemeTextColor (lt1 -> dk2 -> dk1 -> tonal
  shade) instead of lerping to the WCAG floor.
- ContrastPreflightPair.AuthorBackground gives validate the same rule.
- cmd/json2pptx: authorBackgroundContrastPairs() pairs each populated placeholder's
  inherited FontColor with the slide's own background, so validate predicts the case
  at all. generator.EffectiveSlideBackgroundHex is exported so preflight resolves the
  background through exactly the renderer's rule (scrim included).
- shape_grid cells pass false explicitly: the author chose fill and text together.

MEASURED (before-binary from a stash of the three files)
  midnight-blue /slides/0  #1B2A4A -> #4E5A72 on #000000 (1.5 -> 3.0)   BEFORE
  midnight-blue /slides/0  #1B2A4A -> #FFFFFF on #000000 (1.5 -> 21.0)  AFTER
  midnight-blue /slides/1  #2E5090 -> #5874A7 on #1B2A4A (1.8 -> 3.0)   BEFORE
  midnight-blue /slides/1  #2E5090 -> #FFFFFF on #1B2A4A (1.8 -> 14.2)  AFTER
  warm-coral    /slides/0  #3E2723 -> #685552 on #000000 (1.5 -> 3.0)   BEFORE
  warm-coral    /slides/0  #3E2723 -> #FFFFFF on #000000 (1.5 -> 21.0)  AFTER
  slide 3 (layout background, no author background): no finding in either build.

VISUAL EVIDENCE (soffice -> pdftoppm, 60dpi, both templates)
  /tmp/s7wmh/s-before-midnight-blue-1.png  grey-blue title, near-invisible on black
  /tmp/s7wmh/s-after-midnight-blue-1.png   white title
  /tmp/s7wmh/s-before-warm-coral-1.png     muddy brown-grey title on black
  /tmp/s7wmh/s-after-warm-coral-1.png      white title

VERIFY, point by point
1. "renders the title in lt1 (ratio >= 7), not a mid-grey at exactly 3.0" -- yes,
   #FFFFFF at 21.0 on both templates.
2. "validate's contrast_predicted names the same replacement generate emits" -- yes:
   validate reports #1B2A4A -> #FFFFFF (on #000000, 1.5 -> 21.0), source
   slide_background, replacement_mode flip; generate reports the identical swap.
   GAP: a layout that leaves its placeholder colour to the master's txStyles
   (midnight-blue slideLayout4) has no FontColor in PlaceholderInfo, so slide 2 of
   the probe deck is still generate-only. Filed as a follow-up rather than widened
   here -- closing it means resolving master txStyles through clrMapOvr in the
   template parser, which moves FontColor for every caller.
3. "no change to any deck whose background comes from its layout" -- yes. Scanned all
   19 examples/: zero new findings. TestDeterministicCorpus unchanged on all four
   templates (no golden rebaseline needed).

TESTS
- internal/generator/author_background_contrast_test.go: snap on author background
  (ratio >= 7, lt1), lerp preserved on a layout background (lands within 0.5 of the
  4.5 floor), shape_grid cell keeps its lerp, preflight/render agreement.
- cmd/json2pptx/contrast_author_background_test.go: the prediction exists and names
  #FFFFFF with source slide_background; none for a layout background; none under

DOCS SYNC

title: Chart axis ticks and data labels use different number formats; no agent-facing style.value_format
description:
Split out of go-slide-creator-66qb (charts-diagrams half), which fixed the data
labels but not the axis.

WHAT
Within one chart the axis and the data labels are formatted by different code
with different rules. On a bar chart of [1240, 865, 413] the axis prints
"1000 / 1200 / 1400" while the data labels now print "1,240 / 865 / 413"; on
larger ranges the axis uses compact notation ("1.2M", "800K") while the labels
print grouped digits. Pie prints percentages only; gauge prints the raw value
plus a free-text unit that collides with its label.

There is also no single agent-facing knob. `data.data_labels.format` reaches the
LABELS (and carries units, e.g. "€%.1fM"), but nothing reaches the ticks, so an
EUR deck cannot get "€1.2m" on both.

HOW (from the original bead's charts-diagrams reporter)
Add style.value_format {style: plain|compact|percent|currency, decimals,
prefix, suffix, thousands_sep} and apply it uniformly to axis ticks, data
labels and in-mark labels, defaulting to today's behaviour for both. The label
side already has autoValueFormat / formatValueGrouped in svggen/value_format.go
to build on; the tick side is svggen/scales.go FormatCompact /
LinearScale.TickFormat.

VERIFY
A deck with style.value_format {style:"compact", prefix:"€"} renders "€1.2m" on
BOTH the axis and the data labels of
.claude/review-evidence/r2/charts-diagrams/single/bar__real.json. Document it in
data-format-hints and SKILL.md.
close_reason:
Implemented in 40fca17.

WHAT LANDED
- svggen: ValueFormatSpec {style: plain|compact|percent|currency, decimals, prefix, suffix, thousands_sep} on core.StyleSpec; one ValueFormatter per chart (svggen/value_format.go) built from the chart's own values and used by BOTH the axis ticks and every label site (bar/line series, funnel, gauge, treemap, waterfall).

title: [bug] Text inherited from a layout's lstStyle is never contrast-checked: white bullets on a white section layout stay invisible
description:
Found while fixing go-slide-creator-hln7 (chrome contrast on modern-template).

WHAT
examples/basic-deck.json on modern-template, slide 2 ("Agenda", slideLayout2 —
the Section Divider): the five bullets render white on a white background and
are completely invisible. The title on the same slide is fine.

WHY the existing contrast pass misses it
enforceTextContrastInSlide walks the SLIDE's shapes and rewrites scheme colors
it finds in the slide's own lstStyle / run properties. These bullets carry no
color in the slide XML at all — `unzip -p out.pptx ppt/slides/slide2.xml` shows
exactly one color on the whole slide. The text color is inherited from the
layout's placeholder lstStyle, which the pass never reads, so there is nothing
for it to rewrite and no finding is emitted. Contrast enforcement is
structurally blind to inherited color.

REPRO
  json2pptx generate -json examples/basic-deck.json -template modern-template \
    -templates-dir templates -output /tmp/x
  soffice -env:UserInstallation=file:///tmp/p --headless --convert-to pdf \
    --outdir /tmp/x /tmp/x/basic-deck.pptx
  magick -density 110 /tmp/x/basic-deck.pdf /tmp/x/s-%d.png   # look at s-1.png

WHERE
internal/generator/text_contrast.go enforceTextContrastInSlide /
enforceTextContrastInShape (slide-local colors only);
internal/generator/slide_preparation.go:140 is the only caller.

HOW (sketch)
Resolve the effective text color for a placeholder the way the renderer does:
slide run -> slide lstStyle -> LAYOUT placeholder lstStyle -> master txStyles ->
theme, applying the layout's color map override at each step (the override
resolution landed in go-slide-creator-hln7: parseLayoutColorMapOverride /
resolveSchemeColorMapped). When the resolved color fails WCAG AA against the
resolved background, write an explicit color onto the slide run rather than
leaving it inherited, and record a contrast_autofixed swap as usual.

Note this is partly layout misuse — basic-deck's agenda slide lands on a Section
Divider — but the engine should not emit invisible text whatever layout is
chosen, and today it emits no finding either.

VERIFY
basic-deck on modern-template: slide 2's bullets legible (>= 4.5:1 against the
rendered background) and a contrast_autofixed finding at the bullets' path. No
byte change to decks on midnight-blue / warm-coral / forest-green, which have no
color map override.
close_reason:
Implemented in 53f0561.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by inspecting the generated XML): modern-template's slideLayout2 carries a clrMapOvr inverting the slots (tx1→lt1, bg1→dk1). Its background is <a:schemeClr val="tx1"/> → lt1 → #FFFFFF. Its body placeholder declares NO colour, so the text falls through to the master's bodyStyle (<a:schemeClr val="tx1"/>) → through the same override → #FFFFFF. White on white. The slide XML contained exactly one colour (the title's bg1), so enforceTextContrastInSlide had nothing to rewrite and emitted no finding.

WHAT LANDED (internal/generator/inherited_text_contrast.go)
- enforceInheritedTextContrast: for every placeholder shape that states no colour anywhere, resolve the inherited colour the way the renderer does — layout's matching placeholder lstStyle → master txStyles (titleStyle/bodyStyle/otherStyle by ph type) — mapped through the layout's clrMapOvr via the existing resolveSchemeColorMapped, and checked against the background the slide actually shows (effectiveSlideBackgroundHex already handles a slide's own background).
- Failing text gets an explicit <a:solidFill><a:srgbClr/> on each RUN (not the shape lstStyle: a lvl1pPr colour styles only outline level 0, so a second-level bullet would stay invisible), plus one contrast_autofixed swap per shape.
- Two new fix.params.source values: layout-lstStyle, master-txStyles.
- masterXMLForLayout + a per-master XML cache on TitleFitContext.

VERIFY
- basic-deck on modern-template: slides 2, 3 and 5 now carry #2C3932 (the template's dk2) on their bullets; finding 'auto-fixed low-contrast text: #FFFFFF → #2C3932 (on #FFFFFF, ratio 1.0 → 12.1)' at /slides/1, /slides/2, /slides/4. Rendered before/after at 70dpi: bullets go from invisible to legible (evidence /tmp/ucmgr/s-before-2.png vs s-after-2.png).
- Byte-identical output on midnight-blue, warm-coral and forest-green (sha256 of the generated .pptx compared before/after with a binary built from the pre-change tree); only modern-template changes. Exactly the bead's no-regression clause.

TESTS (internal/generator/inherited_text_contrast_test.go)
TestInheritedTextContrast_WhiteOnWhite (the repro, incl. one swap per shape not per run, ratio before ~1.0 / after ≥4.5, source=master-txStyles, and the runs actually carrying the recorded colour), _ReadableIsLeftAlone (no swap AND no XML rewritten — the byte-identity guarantee), _LayoutStyleWins (layout lstStyle beats master, source=layout-lstStyle), _SkipsStatedColors (run-stated and lstStyle-stated colours stay the other pass's job), _NonPlaceholdersAndEmptyText, _HostilePaletteStillReads, TestInheritedTextThreshold (4.5 vs 3.0 by size/bold), TestPlaceholderMatches (7 cases: idx wins over type, ctrTitle≡title, indexed layout vs unindexed slide).

NOT FIXED (and the bead says so): basic-deck's agenda content landing on a Section Divider is layout misuse — the title and the bullets still overlap on that slide. This bead's contract was 'the engine should not emit invisible text whatever layout is chosen', which it no longer does.

- Cells are grouped by (resolved original text colour, contrast threshold). A scheme-spelled colour joins the group of the hex it RESOLVES to, which is how the reported deck spells the same colour two ways.
- A group only forms when its fills are one visual family: pairwise contrast <= 3:1 (maxFillSpread). title: Renders cannot be cancelled and report no progress; a cancelled 120-slide render runs to completion
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: mcp-surface (finding refs m.16).

WHAT
Sent notifications/cancelled for an in-flight render_deck_thumbnails of a 120-slide deck 1.0s after dispatch; the server replied 3.7s later with the full 3,069,812-byte result (120 images) — the cancellation was ignored and the payload was still delivered. Thread the tool-call ctx (mcp-go cancels it on notifications/cancelled) into every render helper — runBounded already takes ctx, so the gap is the handlers dropping it — and make the mutex acquisition ctx-aware so a queued call aborts instead of waiting. When _meta.progressToken is present, emit notifications/progress from the thumbnail loop (progress = slides converted, total = slide count) via server.SendNotificationToClient.

description:

Split the flag: `deterministic_ready` (gate passed on complete evidence + author-supplied content) and `visually_approved`. title: Pattern field maxLength budgets are 3-20x the rendered cell capacity, so schema-legal content renders at 4-8pt
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: gallery (finding refs g.15).

WHAT
Every value in the MAX deck respects the patterns' own JSON-schema maxLength limits, yet the expander reports 300-2100% of cell capacity: bmc-canvas cell 0 max_chars=224 vs actual 2023 (903%; the schema allows 10 bullets x 200 chars per block), hero-detail 1429%, stylish-panels 1352% (8 bullets x 200 chars), card-grid 886% (300-char body), strategy-house 666%, comparison-2col 510% (10 rows x 200 chars), swimlane/roadmap-phased 543%. WHERE
per-pattern schemas in internal/patterns/*.go (StringSchema/ArraySchema maxima), text_budget_guide in the same files, docs/PATTERNS.md (cell capacity contract)

close_reason:
Done (ae41c6cf), with the bead's HOW deliberately not followed. The finding is real; the proposed fix would have made things worse.

WHAT I MEASURED
Built, for every registered pattern, the largest payload its OWN schema permits (walking the pattern's JSON Schema: strings at maxLength, arrays at maxItems, plus the cross-field rules the schema cannot express — icons take one source, card-grid's cells match columns x rows, and so on) and ran it through the same readability prediction the fit report gives an agent, on all four bundled templates. 33 of 43 patterns permit schema-legal content that renders below the 12pt floor: card-grid 2.6pt, bmc-canvas 3.8, driver-tree 4.3, comparison-2col 4.8, down through matrix-2x2 at 10.1. Ten are clean at their maxima. The full table is in go-slide-creator-tp23k.

WHY NOT THE PROPOSED FIX
The bead says: "Set per-field maxLength from the measured per-cell budget". I probed card-grid at every shape and the budget is not one number — it is the shape's:
  1x1, 2x1, 2x2 -> 300 chars   3x2 -> 220   4x2 -> 160   3x3 -> 100   4x3 -> 60   5x3 -> 40   4x4 -> 20   5x5 -> nothing fits.
The schema's 300 is CORRECT for a 2x1 and catastrophic for a 5x5. Lowering it to fit the dense case would reject decks that render perfectly well today in order to warn about ones that do not — a strictly worse trade, and a breaking schema change made on top of it. The bead's own parenthesis ("where a range is legitimate, shrink the per-item maxLength as the item count grows") is not expressible in JSON Schema at all.

WHAT LANDED INSTEAD
1. The measurement is a permanent gate: cmd/json2pptx.TestSchemaMaximaStayReadable, with the result pinned per pattern. It fails when a number gets WORSE (a maxLength grows past what its cell holds, or a new pattern ships without being measured) AND when one IMPROVES without the pin following, so ground a fix wins cannot be given back.
2. card-grid carries the shape-scaled budget: the cap stays, its schema description carries the measured table, and PostExpandWarnings emits BODY_TOO_LONG naming the number for the shape the author chose — "cells[0].body is 300 characters; a 4x3 grid holds about 60 per card". TEXT_BELOW_READABLE_MIN already said the text would shrink; it never said how much was affordable, which is what an agent needs to fix it in one pass.
3. docs/PATTERNS.md gains the authoring rule ("A field's maxLength is the budget of the pattern's SMALLEST shape") beside the two existing measurement rules.

ONE CLAIM IN THE BEAD THAT IS NO LONGER TRUE
"An agent that trusts the schema produces unreadable slides, and (see finding 1) nothing warns it." The fit report now warns precisely: on a 4x3 card-grid at schema maxima it names every cell and the size it will render at (6.7pt). Verified on a real deck through the real pipeline, not through the harness.

A CORRECTION TO MY OWN FIRST MEASUREMENT
My first harness measured density against a grid resolved with no layout bounds and reported pull-quote at 383% of capacity. I rendered a 500-character pull-quote before acting on it: it is perfectly readable, and the real fit report reports nothing. The harness was measuring against a smaller box than the renderer uses. It was rewritten to go through collectReadabilityFindings with the real template layouts, which is why the numbers above are the ones an agent actually sees. Worth stating because the bead's own figures (bmc-canvas 903%, hero-detail 1429%) came from a density sweep and may carry the same inflation — the readable-size numbers are the ones to work from.

FOLLOW-UP
go-slide-creator-tp23k: the remaining 32 patterns, with the measured table, the three-step recipe card-grid used, and two things to check first (bmc-canvas's non-physical 3->4 bullet cliff, and pull-quote being flagged against a display-role floor rather than the 12pt one).

golangci-lint 0 issues in both modules; go test ./... passes in both; TemplatePatternMatrix passes; build clean.

WHAT CHANGED (internal/patterns/pullquote.go)
The quote and its attribution were consecutive paragraphs in ONE cell. They are
now two rows of the pattern's grid:
  row 0  quote, bottom-anchored, bottom inset = the gap (0.6em of the quote size,
         clamped to 10-28pt), MaxHeight = measured quote height + gap, capped at
         80% of the content area
  row 1  attribution, top-anchored, Min=MaxHeight = its measured height
Separate text bodies, so the quote's autofit cannot reach the attribution:
attrSize is floored at 11pt (pullQuoteAttrMinPt) and no longer rides the quote's
fontScale. Both rows are content-sized, so the block is centred and the rule
stops where the text does.

The accent rule is now a COLUMN with row_span 2 rather than a per-cell accent
bar. Two bars would be pulled apart by the row gap, and a row_gap of 0 is
indistinguishable from "unset" in the resolver (it falls back to the 8pt
default), so a zero gap was not expressible. accent_side none/right behave as
before; the attribution row lists only its own cell because the resolver skips
the column the row-span occupies.

autofit is a bare <a:normAutofit/> — no fontScale — while the quote's body
carries fontScale="78000". So the attribution renders at a true 14pt, >= 11pt,
independent of the quote's shrink. Before, both sat in one body under one
fontScale.

Done (6650b5e3).

WHAT LANDED
internal/semantic/slides/decision.go (new; CompileDecision moved out of content.go): 3-6 options compile to numbered-step-strip in its stacked-box style, and exactly 2 options that each carry a detail compile to a two-card card-grid. The recommendation goes into the PATTERN'S CALLOUT BAND beneath the options — PatternInput.Callout, which both patterns support — so the ask is the last thing on the slide before the takeaway, in the accent band. The slide's own takeaway is untouched and sits below it.

WHY NOT EXACTLY THE BEAD'S SHAPE
The bead proposed card-grid {columns:1, rows:N, style:'numbered-badge'}. I used numbered-step-strip for the 3-6 case instead, for one reason worth stating: card-grid REQUIRES a body on every cell, so `options: ["Hold coverage", "Fund the pod", "Offshore"]` — bare labels, the commonest way an author writes options — could not reach it and would still have got bullets, which is the complaint. numbered-step-strip needs only a label and takes the detail when there is one, so bare labels get the visual too. card-grid is kept for the 2-option case, where the strip's own 3-step minimum rules it out.

description:

Fixed (48292f0d).

ONE CAUSE UNDER ALL THREE SYMPTOMS
The bead reads as three defects (bars invisible, value labels piled on the y-axis, footnote clipped). Measuring the SVG showed one: EVERY bar was drawn at x=57.4 with the same 45.2pt width. AdaptXLabels ellipsizes long category labels IN PLACE and returns them as XLabelLayout.Categories; the waterfall builds its CategoricalScale from those, then looks each bar's position up by the ORIGINAL p.Label. Every lookup missed, CategoricalScale.Scale returns its range minimum on a miss, and all fourteen bars landed in the first slot — taking their value labels with them and pushing the footnote out of the canvas.

THE FIX
XLabelLayout.Categories is now the identity a caller's scale is keyed by and stays untouched; the ellipsized text goes to DisplayLabels, which the axis config was ALREADY using to print (it just never received anything on the truncation path). The label band's measurement now reads the display text too, so an ellipsized chart still earns the smaller bottom margin its shorter labels deserve rather than reserving space for the full ones.

Separately: a non-zero step now draws at least 2pt tall. The -0.8 and +2.5 steps on a 3,000-unit axis were a fraction of a pixel, so a real step was invisible even once it was in the right place. The value label beside it carries the number.

The bead's HOW proposes computing the domain from the cumulative walk and applying broken-axis zoom. calculateDomain ALREADY walks the running totals (and the render proves it: the axis spans -1,000 to 2,000, which is the walk's range, not the deltas'). No domain change was needed. The footnote needed no clamp either — it is drawn across the full canvas width and was only pushed out by the pile-up.

THE BAR CHART ESCAPED THIS
charts.go keeps a display copy (displayData.Categories = categories) and looks up by the same truncated strings it built the scale from, so it was internally consistent. I checked before claiming otherwise: a narrow bar chart with the same labels draws its bars correctly both before and after. It gets a guard anyway, since the invariant is now shared, and I verified its axis still prints ellipsized labels after the change.

title: Table conditional formatting rejects a string threshold and fails the whole deck parse
description:

title: Funnel chart collapses to an unreadable spike and paints stages with the categorical accent rotation (red = MQL)
description:

Done (8de567ee). DeckSpec kind `framework` takes SWOT, Porter's five forces and the Business Model Canvas.

DESIGN
One kind, not three. `framework` names which (swot / porters_five_forces / bmc, with the spellings an author reaches for — five_forces, "business model canvas", "Porter's Five Forces", SWOT — resolving to them), and `sections` carries the parts by their own names. That is one documented payload field instead of eighteen, which matters: each documented field costs tool-listing bytes, and the three frameworks have disjoint part names.

ROUTING
- bmc -> the bmc-canvas PATTERN, with each cell's canonical heading supplied by the compiler, so the canvas reads as the canvas whatever the author called its boxes.
- swot and porters_five_forces -> the native OOXML DIAGRAM of that name. This is the first DeckSpec kind to reach a diagram rather than a pattern (the epic's "0 of 21 diagrams").
- The diagram lands on a `diagram` slide, not blank-title: blank-title has no body placeholder, and the first render dropped the diagram on the floor with "placeholder_id \"body\" does not exist in layout slideLayout7". Caught by looking at the render.
- Explain/compile parity holds: FrameworkPattern reports bmc-canvas only for a complete BMC and "" for the two diagrams, so the plan advertises a layout only where compile emits no pattern.

DEGRADE
Every part is required. A SWOT missing its threats is not a SWOT, so an incomplete framework degrades to bullets grouped under each part's heading and SEMANTIC_DENSITY names the missing parts ("framework is missing opportunities, threats; the visual draws every part or none of it"). A framework this kind does NOT draw — a PESTEL, say — keeps every section the payload carries, under headings made from its own keys, rather than collapsing to a title-only slide. That last case was a silent drop in the first draft; the test caught it.

INTENSITY
A five-forces payload may state a force's intensity as 0.0-1.0 or as the word an author writes ("high"/"medium"/"low"). An intensity they did NOT state is left out entirely rather than invented.

FOLLOW-UP FILED
The renderer defaults an absent intensity to 0.5 and prints "Medium (50%)" under every force, so an unscored five-forces chart looks like an assessment and is actually a default; all five boxes also take the same accent3 tint, so the colour coding says nothing. Bead filed with the rendered evidence.

EVIDENCE
Rendered a 4-slide spec (SWOT, five forces, the full 9-cell BMC, and a half-SWOT degrade) on midnight-blue and warm-coral, converted via soffice+pdftoppm, and looked at every slide. SWOT draws four tinted quadrants with the bullets in place; the five forces draw the centre-and-four-arrows layout with each force's factors; the BMC draws all nine cells with the canonical headings and the template's own styling; the degrade reads "Strengths — ...; Weaknesses — ..." with nothing lost.

GATES
golangci-lint 0 issues in both modules; go test ./... passes in both; build clean. Core tools/list is 94839 of the 102400-byte budget.

title: patterns expand output cannot be fed back into generate: every authored size is a design_mode_violation in constrained mode
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: gallery (finding refs g.11).

WHAT

THE MECHANISM
jsonschema.ShapeGridInput gains `source`, stamped by expandPattern as "pattern:<name>" — inside the shared expander, so every consumer gets it: the MCP expand_pattern / expand_patterns tools, the CLI `patterns expand`, and the internal generate path alike. checkShapeGrid skips the absolute-font-size finding for a grid whose source names a REGISTERED pattern.

(c) "document that expansion is preview-only" keeps a documented workflow broken and tells the agent to live with it. THE FIX
Pointed steps (type chevron and type arrow) now:

2. inset their text by the notch depth + 3pt on BOTH sides, so the label sits in the chevron body;

1. I first borrowed the notch depth from numbered-step-strip's chevronStripGeometry, as the bead suggests. That was 16pt short: the strip sizes its chevrons from its own aspect cap (81pt tall at four steps) while process-flow's row is 136pt, and the notch is adj x the SHORTER side. It is computed from process-flow's own cell size now, and the helper is shared with the row-height calculation so the two cannot drift.
2. With a CORRECT inset the label was left 110pt of a 198pt shape and even "Board sign-off" broke mid-word. The cause is the same arithmetic: a tall chevron has a deep notch. A row of pointed steps is now capped at half its step width (the same aspect rule numbered-step-strip uses), which takes the label from 110pt to 132pt of the 198pt shape.

A 31-character German compound still breaks mid-word in a four-step row — no inset can help a word wider than the shape. That is the readability/density signal's business, not the geometry's.

title: scatter and bubble label every single point, producing an unreadable mush at realistic densities
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: charts-diagrams (finding refs ch.10).

WHAT
With 6 series × 9 points (a normal account-level scatter) every point label is drawn, producing solid overlapping text across the whole plot; the same happens for bubble with 36 bubbles. capabilities describe the strategy as 'point labels with smart alignment; font reduced for overlaps' and 'labels clamped to viewBox; no truncation' — in practice there is no collision resolution and no thinning. Scatter emits RENDER.chart.scatter_label_skipped plus FIT.findings_truncated; bubble emits nothing at all.

WHERE
svggen/charts.go ScatterChart/BubbleChart label drawing; svggen/direct_label_collision.go (the collision pass that exists for line direct labels is not applied here)

HOW
Reuse the direct-label collision pass: sort labels by value, place greedily, skip on collision, and stop labelling entirely above ~15 visible points unless `style.show_values` is set; count skipped labels in the existing scatter_label_skipped finding and add the same finding for bubble.

VERIFY

Visual evidence: build ./cmd/json2pptx, generate on midnight-blue AND warm-coral (-templates-dir templates), rasterize with pptx2jpg (or soffice -env:UserInstallation=<private> --headless --convert-to pdf + pdftoppm -r 90 -png), LOOK at before/after PNGs and cite their paths in the close reason.
close_reason:
Fixed (6e9aca5d).

ROOT CAUSE, WHICH IS NOT QUITE WHAT THE BEAD SAYS
The bead says "there is no collision resolution and no thinning". There IS: scatter tries four positions around each point and skips a label that fits none. The defect is that the whole label pass ran INSIDE the per-series loop, so the placed-label set was reset for every series — collisions were resolved within a series and ignored across them. That is why six series of nine points produced a wall of overlapping text while each series looked internally tidy. The density adaptation was broken the same way: it counted one series' points (9), never the chart's (54), so the font and length reductions never fired at the density that needed them.

THE FIX
The pass is hoisted out of the loop: labels are collected across every series and placed once, with one shared collision set. Above 15 labelled points nothing is labelled — past that the labels cover the plot they describe — and style.show_values still forces them for a caller who wants them anyway.

FINDINGS
- Over the threshold: ONE warning naming the count ("54 point labels dropped — above 15 the labels cover the plot they describe; label the points that matter, or set show_values to force all of them"), fix kind reduce_items.
- Under it, a genuine collision: ONE info finding with a count, fix kind increase_canvas (a collision is a room problem; the existing test pins that kind and it is still right). It used to be one finding PER skipped label, which the finding cap then truncated — the agent was told neither how many were lost nor, after truncation, that any were.
- bubble_chart is a ScatterChart with VariableSize, so it now reports identically. The bead notes it "emits nothing at all"; that is fixed by the same code.

EVIDENCE
Rendered three cases and looked at each: the bead's 6x9 scatter (before: 54 labels in a solid field of overlapping text; after: a readable point cloud with the series legend and one finding), a 4x9 bubble chart (36 bubbles, same), and a 12-point scatter (under the threshold: every label placed, none overlapping, which also shows the shared collision set working).

CAPABILITY TEXT
The bead's other complaint is that capabilities advertise "point labels with smart alignment; font reduced for overlaps" and "labels clamped to viewBox; no truncation" while neither saved the case. Both scatter's and bubble's label_strategy and density_behavior now state the 15-point threshold, what happens past it, and the escape hatch. docs/diagrams/scatter_chart.md and bubble_chart.md say the same on the labels field.

GATES
golangci-lint 0 issues in both modules; go test ./... passes in both; build clean.

close_reason:
Shipped in 93803417.

REPRODUCED FIRST (midnight-blue and warm-coral, 6 steps, labels Attract/Qualification/Proposal/Negotiate/Onboarding/Expansion): "02 Qualific / ation", "03 Propos / al", "04 Negotia / te", "05 Onboar / ding", "06 Expansi / on" — exactly as reported.
  before: /tmp/e97v-before-midnight-blue.png, /tmp/e97v-before-warm-coral.png
  after:  /tmp/e97v-after-midnight-blue.png,  /tmp/e97v-after-warm-coral.png
Both after-renders: every label on one line, on both templates. Looked at all four.

ROOT CAUSE was three compounding measurement errors, not one:
1. chevronStripGeometry took stepW = contentWidth / count. The pattern sets Gap: 0, but a zero gap reads as "unset" in the grid DTO (cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go resolves 0 -> shapegrid default 8pt), so each chevron is 8pt narrower than its share. Assumed 138pt, rendered 131.3pt. Fixed: stepW = (contentW - 8pt*(n-1))/n, which now matches the emitted a:ext cx (1667934 EMU = 131.33pt) exactly.
2. The renderer lays text inside the chevron shape own text rectangle, which is ALREADY pulled in past the point and the notch; the lIns/rIns the pattern emits stack on top. Budgeting one inset per side said a 13pt "Qualification" fitted in 84pt; the label really had about 51pt, which is why "Proposal" (8 chars) fitted and "Negotiate" (9) did not. The width model subtracts the notch TWICE and that matches the render.
3. textfit measures on whatever font this machine has (Liberation Sans substitutes for the template font) while the renderer uses its own. Labels are required to fit inside 90% of the computed width; the last few points are not knowledge we have.

THE FIX (internal/patterns/numbered_step_strip.go):
- fitChevronLabels searches notch depth from chevronAdj (30000) down to chevronMinAdj (12000) in 3000 steps and takes the FIRST depth at which every label fits one line. Cheapest remedy first: a blunter arrow still reads as an arrow.
- Past the shallowest notch the label shrinks via fitSingleLineSize, floored at chevronMinLabelPt = 12.0 (= shapegrid.MinTextSizePt; below that the readability policy is the signal).
- PostExpandWarnings emits BODY_TOO_LONG naming the offending labels, the step count and the size when even the floor wraps. (Reach caveat: expandPatternsForFit drops PostExpandWarnings, so it surfaces in MCP preview but not yet in validate/generate fit reports — that is go-slide-creator-wn4v, unchanged by this commit.)

VERIFIED BEHAVIOUR (emitted XML): 3 steps adj=30000 sz=1300; 4 steps adj=30000 sz=1300; 6 steps with long labels adj=15000 sz=1300 (the notch pays, the type does not). Short labels keep the full arrow because the search starts at 30000 and stops at the first depth that fits.

TESTS: TestNumberedStepStrip_Chevron_LongLabelsGiveUpNotchDepth (short keeps 30000/13pt; long shallows the notch but keeps 13pt and every label measures one line), _ShrinksToTheReadableFloor (six 15-20 char labels -> adj floor + size below 13 but never below 12), _WarnsWhenEvenTheFloorWraps (code prefix, label names, stacked-box exempt), TestChevronStripGeometry_SubtractsTheColumnGap (stepW narrower than the column share, equal to the gap-corrected width).

SIDE EFFECT CAUGHT BY A GATE: TestSchemaMaximaStayReadable reports numbered-step-strip schema maxima now render at 7.0pt rather than 5.8pt — an improvement; the pin was raised to hold the ground.

DOCS/SYNC: docs/PATTERNS.md gains the three measurement traps and the give-up-notch-before-type rule under the pointed-shape section; SKILL.md numbered-step-strip entry states the one-line label contract, the 12pt floor and the BODY_TOO_LONG signal.

title: Each embedded chart SVG carries ~1.1 MB of base64 Calibri font faces; an 11-slide deck ships 4.4 MB of media and a 128px PNG fallback
description:

WHAT
Unzipping the final 2.1 MB deck: ppt/media holds 4 SVGs of 1.10-1.11 MB each (4.4 MB total) and 4 PNGs of ~1.5 KB. svggen/builder.go Render (font embedding around the @font-face injection); internal/generator/contexts.go:343 iconFallbackPNGSizePx=128 and singlepass.go:388 pngData: iconFallbackPNG(...).

HOW
Subset the embedded font to the glyphs actually drawn (or drop embedding when the family resolves locally and rely on the font-family fallback chain that fixSVGFontFamilyFallbacks already adds), and deduplicate: embed each face once per deck rather than per chart. Separately, raster the PNG fallback for CHART/diagram SVGs at the placed size (>=1000px on the long edge), not the 128px icon size.

VERIFY

close_reason:
Fixed in f76a1478. Embedded chart/diagram fonts are subsetted to the glyphs actually drawn.

REPRO: examples/charts.json generated at HEAD~1 produced a 3,420,281-byte pptx whose ppt/media held six SVGs of 1,103,827-1,107,665 bytes each. Each SVG was ~5.2 KB of drawing plus two @font-face blocks carrying 547,616 and 552,608 base64 characters — full unsubsetted Calibri regular and bold, re-embedded per chart.

CAUSE: svggen/builder.go Render called svg.New(&buf, w, h, nil). nil means canvas svg.DefaultOptions, which is EmbedFonts:true, SubsetFonts:FALSE.

CHANGE: a named svgRenderOptions var (EmbedFonts true, SubsetFonts true, SizeUnits mm, Lossless) documenting the one field we differ from the library defaults in.

RESULT: charts.pptx 3,420,281 -> 380,045 bytes (89% smaller); each chart SVG 1.10 MB -> 18-20 KB. All 19 bundled example decks together: 14 MB -> 2.5 MB. Both VERIFY numbers met (each chart SVG < 50 KB, package < 400 KB).

RENDER PARITY: this needed a renderer that honours an embedded @font-face. rsvg-convert does NOT — stripping the font block from a subsetted SVG produced a byte-identical raster (AE 0), so its identical before/after output proved nothing, and LibreOffice is the same story (it also has the PNG fallback to fall back on). Verified in Chrome headless instead, rasterising the packaged SVG bytes before and after: charts image1/image11 and diagrams image1/3/5/7/9. RMSE 0.4-2.3%, every label present and in the same position; the residual is glyph-edge antialiasing from the subset dropping hinting tables. Looked at the two worst pairs side by side (funnel chart, radar chart) — visually identical.

PNG FALLBACK HALF: already correct, the report conflated two paths. iconFallbackPNGSizePx=128 (internal/generator/contexts.go) is used only for shape_grid ICON SVGs; a chart or diagram carries renderResult.PNG, svggens own raster at the placed size — measured 1875x775 on every chart PNG in this deck, well over the 1000px floor. No change needed.

DEDUPLICATION: not pursued and not needed. OOXML media parts are independent files with no shared CSS, so "embed each face once per deck" would mean a cross-part font resource the SVG spec gives no way to reference. With subsetting each face costs a few KB per chart, which is under the per-chart budget by an order of magnitude.

title: No-emoji policy rejects check/cross/star and (R)(TM), breaking competitor matrices
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: capability-gaps (finding refs cap.17).

WHAT
IsEmoji() treats U+2600-27BF wholesale as emoji, so a feature-comparison table using ✓ (U+2713) and ✗ (U+2717) is rejected with 16 blocking errors — the single most common encoding for a competitor matrix. ★/☆/☑/☐/♦ are rejected too, and so are © ® ™ (explicitly listed), which means a deck cannot write 'Acme®' or 'Windows™'. Meanwhile √ × ● ○ ◐ ■ ▲ → ① pass. The error message tells the agent to use a bundled SVG icon — impossible inside a table cell, which accepts only strings. The workaround an agent is forced into (√ / ×) looks wrong to a consultant.

WHERE
internal/policy/emoji/emoji.go:30-67 IsEmoji, the validator entry point in the same package, docs/… no-emoji rule in skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md 'Icon Names'

HOW
Narrow the block ranges: allowlist the monochrome dingbats/symbols that render in ordinary text fonts — U+2713/2714 (check), U+2717/2718 (ballot X), U+2605/2606 (star), U+2610/2611 (ballot box), U+00A9/00AE/2122 (©®™) — and keep rejecting the pictographic ranges (U+1F300+, regional indicators, ZWJ sequences, variation selectors, U+26xx weather/emoji faces). Add a test table covering the allowed/blocked codepoints, and state the allowed symbol set in SKILL.md so the agent does not fall back to √.

VERIFY
j2p validate capability-gaps/b5/deck_checkmarks_rejected.json → VALID; a deck containing 🚀 or 1F600 still fails; the rendered competitor matrix shows ✓/✗.

WHAT CHANGED
internal/policy/emoji/emoji.go: TypographicSymbols is an explicit allowlist
checked first in IsEmoji, and AllowedSymbols() exposes it in codepoint order for

©/®/™ special case is gone, since those are in the allowlist now.

Permitted: ✓ (2713) ✔ (2714) ✗ (2717) ✘ (2718) ★ (2605) ☆ (2606) ☐ (2610)
☑ (2611) ☒ (2612) © (00A9) ® (00AE) ™ (2122).

   after:  VALID — Slides: 12 | Diagrams: 3 | Tables: 1
2. "a deck containing 🚀 or 1F600 still fails" — both still refused, each with

3. "the rendered competitor matrix shows ✓/✗" — generated and rasterised:
   /tmp/l38d/matrix-07.png shows the SSO / pricing / on-prem / SOC2 matrix with

DECISIONS WORTH FLAGGING
- ☒ (2612) is allowed alongside ☐/☑ — the bead named the pair, but the trio is

close_reason:
Shipped in 6e35b136.

REPRODUCED (midnight-blue, 3 series ending 43/44/44 — the exact case in the audit): /tmp/lntx-before.png is a 200dpi crop showing "Real-time platform", "Hybrid streaming layer" and "Batch reporting pipeline" printed on top of each other at the right edge, unreadable. AFTER /tmp/lntx-after.png: three stacked labels with leader lines, all three legible. Looked at both.

WHY IT WAS ONLY BARS: fallBackFromCollidingDirectLabels + barDirectLabelsCollide guard the bar path; the line path (drawLineDirectSeriesLabels) drew each series name at its own endpoint y with no awareness of the others.

WHAT SHIPPED (svggen/charts.go):
- lineEndLabels collects each series rightmost drawable point (the per-scale x resolution moved into lineLabelPointX, so CategoricalScale / LinearScale / TimeScale are handled in one place instead of inline in the draw loop).
- stackLineEndLabels sorts by y and runs a downward pass (each baseline at least lineLabelLineHeight = 1.45 label heights below the one above) and an upward pass (if the stack overran the plot bottom, push it back up). Labels that already clear each other are left exactly where they were — verified by a test.
- A label that moved more than 1.5pt gets a leader line back to its own endpoint at 45% alpha, so the reader can still tell which series it names.
- When len(labels) * lineH exceeds the plot height the function returns false and the caller draws a LEGEND instead, emitting chart.overflow_suppressed at info severity. The bar fallback is silent; this one says why.

Done (1e64d114). DeckSpec kind `image_case` compiles onto the existing image-text-split pattern.

WHAT LANDED
- internal/semantic/slides/imagecase.go — CompileImageCase, imageCaseFrom (image / bullets / metrics / side resolution), ImageCasePattern, ImageCaseOverBudget, UsableImageCaseNarrative, compileImageCaseFallback.
- Registered in all seven places; tests in imagecase_test.go (pattern path, three picture forms, the side override, half-metric dropping, five degrade reasons, fallback completeness, aliases).
- Docs same commit: SKILL.md kind row, SEMANTIC_COMPILER.md list + table + prose, SCHEMA_CHANGELOG.
- internal/semantic/validate.go gains shapeStringOrObject, because `image` is legitimately a path string OR a {path, alt} object and the shape contract had no way to say so.

THREE JUDGEMENTS
1. A metric needs both its figure and its words. {value: "41"} with no label, or a label with no value, is half a claim and is dropped rather than rendered as a blank cell.
2. A picture with nothing said about it is a plain image slide, not a case study. The kind refuses it with "has a picture but nothing said about it; give it a body or at least one bullet" — which is the same thing the pattern's own validator says.
3. No placeholder label is invented for a missing picture. The first render filled the placeholder box with the caption, which then appeared TWICE — once inside the box and once in the italic line directly beneath it. Caught by looking at the render; the pattern's own "Image placeholder" text is what belongs there.

DEGRADE
Past the column's budgets (body ≤300, eyebrow ≤30, heading ≤80, ≤5 bullets ≤140 each, ≤3 metrics with value ≤10 / label ≤40, caption ≤120) it compiles to a content slide: eyebrow + heading + story as text, and the bullets, the metrics ("2 — clearers migrated") and an "Image: <caption>" line as bullets. The picture cannot come to a text slide, so the caption stands in for it rather than the slide pretending there was never an image. With both text and bullets it becomes a two-column slide so neither buries the other.

ONE THING I DID NOT FIX
With no picture the pattern's placeholder reads "Image placeholder / Add an image (values.image.path)". For a DeckSpec author the field is `image`, not `values.image.path` — the hint names the pattern's own path. It is the pattern's placeholder text, correct in its own context, and changing it would change every hand-authored image-text-split slide too. Left alone deliberately rather than papered over with an invented label.

EVIDENCE
Rendered a 3-slide spec (full case study with three metrics and a caption; a picture on the right with a placeholder label; a 315-character story that degrades) on midnight-blue and warm-coral, converted via soffice+pdftoppm, and looked at every slide. The split renders the eyebrow, heading, body, bullets and the three-metric strip with the caption beneath the picture; image_side: right moves the picture; the degrade keeps every word. Validation reports exactly one finding: "image case body is 315 characters; the column holds 300".

golangci-lint 0 issues in both modules; go test ./... passes in both; build clean. Core tools/list is 95871 of the 102400-byte budget.

close_reason:
Shipped in 63c66fe5. The VERIFY passes; one part of the WHAT is split out as go-slide-creator-5smrk (see the end).

MEASURED BEFORE/AFTER (org_chart on midnight-blue, 11.5in x 4.75in body placeholder):
  BEFORE: picture frame 6.85in x 4.76in — 60% of the placeholder width, chart cramped into the middle with leaf labels overlapping their boxes. /tmp/rkq0-orgchart-before.png
  AFTER:  11.5in x 4.75in — 100% of both, labels clean. /tmp/rkq0-orgchart-after.png
  VERIFY asked for >= 85% width and >= 60% height. Same for gantt and timeline (both 11.5 x 4.75 now).
  process_flow: steps 0.5in -> 1.0in, still centred. /tmp/rkq0-processflow-before.png, /tmp/rkq0-processflow-after.png. Looked at all four.

TWO CAUSES, and the first was WORSE than the report and previously unknown:

1. A COORDINATE-SCALE COLLAPSE. svggen renders in millimetres and then rewrites every coordinate to pixels. The rewriter splits the document at the LAST <style>/<defs> so it never touches base64 font data — but injectTabularNumsStyle put a <style> at the HEAD of the document BEFORE that split ran. On any diagram the canvas emits with no trailing font block (i.e. any diagram that draws no text), the split landed at byte ~146 and the WHOLE drawing stayed in millimetres under a pixel viewBox: it rendered at 26.5% of its own canvas, in the corner of the frame. Measured on a text-free org chart: background path spanned 292 of a 1104-wide viewBox; after the fix 1104. The injection now runs after the pixel scaling. This is why the very first repro render looked far emptier than the bead described.

2. THE NATURAL ASPECT. org_chart, gantt and timeline declare natural dimensions via RenderWithHelperDimensions and "contain" fitted that aspect inside the caller box. A natural aspect is a DEFAULT for a caller that gives no dimensions, not a constraint on one that does — charts have worked that way all along (getSourceAspectRatio returns the container ratio for every chart type, documented as "contain is effectively a no-op"). applyFitModeWithSource now returns the container when req.Output.Width and Height are both set. These diagrams lay out FROM the canvas they are handed (DefaultOrgChartConfig sizes nodes from width/height), so this is a relayout, not a stretch. An explicit aspect_ratio on the request still wins over both.

CONSEQUENCE I FOLLOWED THROUGH: diagram_aspect_conflict is retired. It existed solely to predict letterboxing from the natural aspect for these three types, and that letterboxing no longer happens — a prediction that contradicts the renderer is worse than none. Removed: CheckDiagramAspectConflictFinding, its threshold, its three call sites, ErrCodeDiagramAspectConflict + sentinel, the finding_meta entry, and seven tests. svggen.NaturalAspect stays (it still describes what a dimension-less caller gets) with its doc rewritten to say so; the diagram_aspect_mismatch meta entry lost its stale cross-reference.

3. NATIVE process_flow: pfStepDimensions used pfMinStepHeight (0.5in) regardless of the placeholder. pfStepHeight(bounds) scales with the available height (bounds.Height/4), floored at the minimum and capped at twice it. The cap is deliberate: a flow reads as a strip, and a 3in-tall box on a 4.75in canvas would be worse than a short one — the pattern world caps process-flow at 35% of content height for the same reason.

TESTS: svggen TestRenderScalesADiagramWithNoTextRuns (renders a rectangle-only diagram and asserts the drawing spans its viewBox — the exact shape that regressed), TestSplitSVGContentAndStyleIgnoresALeadingStyle (documents the sharp edge), TestExplicitOutputBoxWinsOverTheNaturalAspect (box wins; no box keeps the natural aspect; explicit aspect_ratio still wins); generator TestPFStepHeightScalesWithTheSpace (four zones plus the cap). svggen/testdata/golden/org_chart_basic.svg regenerated (633 -> 800 height: the golden now uses the box it asked for).

SPLIT OUT, NOT DROPPED: the WHAT also named panel_layout bodies (~70-80% empty) and stat_cards (top-anchored). Those are native panel builders with their own geometry, not the picture-frame path this changes, and fixing them means measuring text in internal/generator and re-banding the group. Reproduced panel_layout (/tmp/plr/s-1.png) and filed go-slide-creator-5smrk with the reproduction, the WHERE, the approach and a VERIFY. The bead VERIFY named org_chart and process_flow only, and both pass.

description:

WHAT

An agent copying seeds into slide content ships that text.

WHERE
internal/deckplan/facts.go (fact extraction / sentence split), cmd/json2pptx/mcp_plan_deck.go seed assembly

HOW
Strip leading list markers ('-', '*', '•', '1.') and trailing punctuation before seeding; never join two facts into one seed with ';' (one fact per seed, extra facts to unplaced_facts); balance brackets by dropping an unterminated '(' clause.

VERIFY
plan_deck with the bulleted brief in /Users/seb/projects/json2pptx/.claude/review-evidence/r2/closure-audit-1/mcp/batch3b.log and slide_budget 4: no seed or unplaced_fact starts with '-', none contains ';', and every seed has balanced parentheses.

close_reason:
Shipped in 6cd83749.

REPRODUCED FIRST with a bulleted brief at --slides 4:
  BEFORE seeds: "- 1,250 customers; - Gross margin 78.2% — Key data point or supporting detail" and "- ARR reached €12.5m (up 31% — Detailed evidence or case study"; unplaced_facts all carried "- " prefixes.
  AFTER seeds: "1,250 customers. Gross margin 78.2% — Key data point or supporting detail" and "ARR reached €12.5m (up 31%) — Detailed evidence or case study"; unplaced_facts = ["14 enterprise logos", "Net revenue retention 118%", "Sales cycle down to 41 days", "EU expansion is on track", "Churn 4% in the SMB segment"].
  Programmatic check over every seed and unplaced fact: none starts with a marker, none contains ";", every one has balanced parentheses. VIOLATIONS: [].

THREE DEFECTS, NOT ONE — the reported string was the product of all three:
1. The clause trim was strings.Trim(raw, " \\t\\"()[]"), which stripped the CLOSING bracket off "ARR reached €12.5m (up 31%)". That is where the unterminated parenthesis came from — not from the split, as the bead assumed. Brackets are no longer trimmed.
2. List markers were never stripped. factListMarker removes "-", "*", "•", "▪", "·", "1.", "2)" from the head of a clause.
3. The seed join used "; " — the exact character the clause splitter cuts on, so two facts read as one malformed clause. Facts are separate sentences in the seed now ("A. B — role hint"); facts[] remains the structured surface, so nothing is lost and nothing is forced into unplaced_facts.

PLUS balanceFactBrackets as a backstop: a clause still open at its end is cut back to the last point where every bracket was closed. That covers both a split landing inside a bracket AND the 100-char cap cutting one, which the bead did not separate.

OPENING SEED: it quoted the brief raw — newlines and "- " markers included, so an agent copying "Title and context: …\\n- ARR reached…" shipped the markup too. normalizeBriefForSeed flattens it to one line of prose with markers dropped, and truncateSeed closes a bracket the ellipsis lands inside.

BONUS BUG FOUND: TruncateBrief documented "at most maxLen runes" but sliced BYTES (s[:maxLen-3]). It under-measured any non-ASCII brief and could split a multi-byte character in half — "ARR reached €12.5m" is an ordinary brief. It counts runes now and trims a trailing space rather than emitting " ...". Two stale test assertions updated: the length check (a cut after a space legitimately yields 19 of 20) and the "; " seed prefix.

DELIBERATE SCOPE DECISION: a first draft made the splitter bracket-aware so "(up 31%; ahead of plan)" survived whole. That contradicts the bead VERIFY (no seed contains ";") and it is the wrong rule: a semicolon IS a clause boundary wherever it appears, and a fact that keeps one reads as two facts spliced. The splitter is unchanged; such a parenthetical is cut at the semicolon and the half-open remainder dropped, giving "ARR reached €12.5m". Losing "ahead of plan" from a HINT beats shipping "(up 31%".

ONE HONEST CAVEAT on the literal VERIFY: the opening seed quotes the brief verbatim (normalised), so if the AUTHOR writes a semicolon it appears there. No fact and no fact-derived seed contains one. Rewriting the author-s own prose would be worse than quoting it.

TESTS (internal/deckplan/facts_test.go): TestExtractBriefFacts_BulletedBrief (markers, semicolons, balanced brackets across a five-bullet brief with -, *, •, "1." and "2)" markers), TestBalanceFactBrackets (five cases including a fully-open clause). deckplan_test.go TestTruncateBrief gains a rune-budget case with € and a utf8.ValidString check.

DOCS/SYNC: SKILL.md plan_deck paragraph now states the seeds are cleaned for copy-paste — markers dropped, half-open parentheticals dropped, two facts as two sentences and never spliced with a semicolon.

JUDGEMENT: A milestone carrying an end_date spans a period rather than marking a point, and the pattern REJECTS an end_date in any style but gantt. So a payload with any range compiles with style: gantt rather than dropping the end dates. The fallback renders a range as "Jan 2025–Mar 2025".

WHAT LANDED — THE BLOCKER (34b095ff)
The kind's example could not validate clean, and it was not the example's fault. Three measurement bugs made a three-stop timeline emit six findings, none of them true:
1. internal/shapegrid estimateCellTextHeightEMU unmarshalled cell text into {content,size} only. Rows sized to their own text reported a phantom overflow; a genuinely tall stack reported none. Now reads paragraphs — an 8-paragraph cell in a 30pt row measures 113pt where it used to measure 27.
2. internal/textcapacity defaultInsetPt was 7.2 — the OOXML LEFT/RIGHT inset — applied vertically. Every cell was budgeted 14.4pt of vertical inset where the renderer takes 7.2 (internal/pptx.autofitDefaultInsetPt = 3.6/side), so a 28pt cell holding one 14pt line was predicted to shrink to 80% and the readability check reported text below the floor. 3. patternRecommendedMax counts grid cells, but timeline-horizontal's entry was 6 — the pattern's own STOP maximum, in the wrong unit. Its dots layout emits three cells per stop, so every conforming timeline, down to three stops, was "overcrowded". Now 21 (7 stops x 3 cells), with the unit documented in FIT_FINDINGS.md.
Also aligned the estimator's line-height and padding (1.4 and 12pt) with the ones the patterns size rows with and the renderer lays out with (1.2 and 7.2pt). Regression tests for all three.

title: Reject chart series whose values length != categories length (and string values) at validate time
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: charts-diagrams, closure-audit-1, mcp-surface (finding refs c1.9, ch.12, m.11).

WHAT
Edge case beyond go-slide-creator-dg8f. `chart.data = {categories:[Q1,Q2,Q3,Q4], series:[{name:Rev, values:[10]}]}` passes validate_deck_spec with 'no issues' and renders a chart with one bar and three silently empty categories (ok:true, zero diagnostics). The dg8f work added a good hint for a malformed data *shape*, but a length mismatch — the most common hand-authoring slip — produces a confidently wrong chart.

ALSO REPORTED (charts-diagrams: "series[].values / categories length mismatch is accepted silently and renders a missing bar"): SKILL.md rule 8 says 'series[i].values length equals len(categories)', but nothing enforces it: `{categories:[A,B,C], series:[{values:[1,2]}]}` generates a chart with an empty third slot and `j2p validate --fit-report` reports only the unrelated takeaway_missing. This is the single most likely agent data bug (truncated arrays after an edit) and it ships silently. Nulls inside values are likewise coerced to 0 without a word.

ALSO REPORTED (mcp-surface: "Validate DeckSpec chart payloads: length mismatches and string values pass validate and render broken"): In the inlined spec schema and in list_slide_kinds' item_schema, chart.data is typed only as {"type":"object"} and chart.type as a free string. Consequences measured end-to-end: (a) categories ['a','b','c'] with series values [1] -> validate_deck_spec ok=true, no findings; render success=true, score 100, and the rendered chart shows one bar over three ticks (out_chart/m.jpg left). (b) values ['1','two'] -> validate ok=true, render success=true score 100, slide renders an empty plot with a format-error label. (c) chart.type 'barchart' -> validate ok=true with NO finding, then render fails with an internal message (see the separate finding). Only the fully empty data map is caught (SEMANTIC_DENSITY). So the one deterministic gate the agent is told to run before rendering cannot see the most common chart mistakes.

WHERE
internal/semantic (chart validation, same place SEMANTIC_DENSITY for chart.data is raised), svggen chart data normalisation
[charts-diagrams] svggen/validation.go (per-type schema validation — it already produces excellent messages for missing/unknown fields), internal/types/chart.go UnmarshalJSON
[mcp-surface] cmd/json2pptx/mcp_input_schema.go / internal/semantic (per-kind item_schema construction for chart_insight), internal/semantic validation rules (SEMANTIC_DENSITY chart checks), svggen chart data conversion.

HOW
Emit a warning (error under --strict) when len(values) != len(categories) for any series, with path slides[i].chart.data.series[j].values and fix.params {categories_len, values_len}; document the code in docs/FIT_FINDINGS.md and SKILL.md's chart_insight row.

Alternative/extra HOW from charts-diagrams: Add a cross-field check in the chart schema validator: len(series[i].values) must equal len(categories) for bar/grouped_bar/stacked_bar/line/area/stacked_area/radar; error with the same style as the existing messages ('series "X" has 2 values but 3 categories'). Reject nulls (or coerce with an explicit INPUT.chart_value_coerced warning).

Alternative/extra HOW from mcp-surface: Type the chart payload in the per-kind schema: data as oneOf[{categories:[string], series:[{name:string, values:[number]}]}, {categories:[string], values:[number]}] with additionalProperties:false, and chart.type as an enum sourced from the svggen registry (same list get_chart_capabilities returns) so the schema itself rejects 'barchart'. Add semantic validations emitting errors (not warnings): CHART_SERIES_LENGTH_MISMATCH (len(values) != len(categories), with the two lengths in evidence), CHART_VALUE_NOT_NUMERIC (path slides[i].chart.data.series[j].values[k]), CHART_TYPE_UNKNOWN with did_you_mean + allowed list.

title: score_candidates cannot discriminate candidates (excellent 100, near-empty 95, lorem 90; funnel == bar == 85)
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: dogfood-b, quality-signal (finding refs b.13, q.20).

WHAT
Tried the advertised use case: choose between three renderings of the pipeline slide (funnel, funnel with show_percentage, the same data as a bar chart). All three returned slide_score 100, rhythm_penalty 15, score 85, rank by input order, findings []. The bar chart is objectively far more legible than the funnel (whose lower stages are 3px slivers -- see the funnel finding), but the tool has no signal for that, because its inputs are fit findings + pattern-run rhythm only. An agent that trusts it will keep the worse chart. Its description ('Use this to choose between alternative slides (e.g., different patterns, different shape grids, different content shapes)') oversells what it can decide.

ALSO REPORTED (quality-signal: "score_candidates cannot discriminate: excellent 100, near-empty 95, lorem-overflow 90 for one slot"): score_candidates is the tool for choosing between alternative slides. I gave it three candidates for slot 2 of the G1 deck: (a) the real kpi_snapshot slide, (b) a slide whose only content is one bullet 'TBD', (c) a slide with a 68-word title and nine 40-word lorem bullets. Scores: 100 / 95 / 90. A 5-point penalty for an empty slide and 10 for an unreadable one is inside the noise of the tool's own findings, so an agent ranking candidates learns almost nothing — and the empty candidate is scored *better* than the dense one, which is the wrong direction for a consulting deck.

WHERE
cmd/json2pptx/score_candidates.go:222 (collectFitFindings + rhythm penalty only).
[quality-signal] cmd/json2pptx/score_candidates.go (slide_score = 100 - severity weights; rhythm_penalty)

HOW
Either (a) add chart-legibility signals to the deterministic score -- minimum rendered label size, minimum segment/bar extent as a fraction of the plot, label-collision count, occupancy of the plot area -- most of which the geometry findings added in round 1 (go-slide-creator-t5gw) already compute; or (b) honestly narrow the description to 'ranks candidates by text-fit and pattern rhythm only; it cannot judge chart legibility' and add a ties note when all candidates score equal.

Alternative/extra HOW from quality-signal: Score candidates on the same enriched criteria as the deck gate once content findings exist (weak content, emptiness, title presence), and widen the scale — e.g. report a 0-100 with explicit sub-axes {fit, density, content, rhythm} so ties break on something meaningful. At minimum, an empty candidate must score below a dense one.

VERIFY
score_candidates on {funnel, bar} for 12400/3100/890/212 ranks the bar chart strictly higher, with a finding naming the sub-minimum funnel segment width.
[quality-signal] score_candidates with the three candidates in quality-signal/calibration.md → real slide > 90, near-empty < 60, lorem-overflow < 50.

Fixed in bccf607d.

MEASURED BEFORE (quality-signal trio, G2 deck slot 1): real 95, near-empty 70, lorem 55. Already better than the 100/95/90 the bead recorded — the content findings added since (WEAK_CONTENT, SLIDE_NEARLY_EMPTY, TITLE_OVERFLOW, BODY_TOO_LONG) do most of that work — but still too flat, and near-empty outranked lorem only by accident of which findings happened to fire.

REPRODUCED AND VERIFIED BY RENDER (looked at all four PNGs):
  BEFORE /tmp/tee7-before.png (built from 2af6dc43, midnight-blue, 3 items): cards fill the whole content zone — an oversized rocket icon at the top, "Launch the platform" near the bottom, and a band of empty accent fill between them. Exactly the reported defect.

title: SVG HTTP method routing blocks configured CORS preflight requests
description:
Baseline c9a5793. svggen/server/httpserver/server.go:166-198 registers only method-specific GET/POST routes and wraps individual handlers with CORS; middleware.go:165-184 has OPTIONS handling that the mux never reaches. Parent inspected source; independent oracle-backed worker used actual Server.ServeHTTP through httptest.

## Steps to Reproduce
Set Security.AllowedOrigins=["https://review.example"]. OPTIONS /render with Origin=https://review.example, Access-Control-Request-Method=POST and Access-Control-Request-Headers=content-type,x-api-key returns 405 Method Not Allowed with no Access-Control-Allow-Origin, rather than expected 204. Configured browser JSON/API-key clients cannot make their intended request. Browser itself was not run.
acceptance_criteria: Run CORS around the mux or explicitly register preflight routes. Handler-level tests cover /render and /render/batch, allowed and disallowed origins, auth-enabled preflight without credentials, supported headers, and actual POST auth enforcement.

## Steps to Reproduce
Call NewRateLimiter(limit,time.Hour).Allow("review-client") 150 times within one window. Observed allowed counts: limit100=100, limit128=128, limit129=150. CLI --rate-limit-enabled --rate-limit-requests 129 --rate-limit-window 1h exposes the ineffective limiter.
acceptance_criteria: Size tracking capacity to the supported limit or explicitly reject unsupported configurations. Test limits 100,128,129 and larger with window expiry and exact boundary rejection; configured positive limits must never silently disable enforcement.
close_reason: Implemented the reported defect with regression coverage; affected targeted package tests pass.

title: CI rewrites svggen golden baselines before checking regressions
description:
Review baseline c9a5793. .github/workflows/ci.yml:148-152 runs go test -run TestGolden -update before the normal svggen test step. svggen/golden_test.go:168-180 writes current output into the expected SVG and returns without comparison under -update; the next step therefore compares the implementation against output generated from the same implementation. A deterministic layout/content regression is automatically blessed on every PR. Structural quality tests still run, but they cannot replace the golden regression check. This is separate from the tests/quality envelope/budget failure tracked by fh57.1 and from the proposed template portability matrix in fh57.13.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Make a deterministic chart geometry or label change that differs from a committed golden SVG but passes structural checks.
2. Run the svggen-test job commands in order: go test -run TestGolden -update, then go test ./... -short -v -race.
3. The first command overwrites the expected SVG from the changed implementation, so the second no longer detects the regression.
Verified by inspecting the CI command sequence and GoldenTest update/compare branches; no workflow was triggered.
acceptance_criteria: CI must compare against reviewed committed baselines without invoking -update. Pin or normalize the rendering/font environment, or maintain explicit platform baselines for unavoidable variation. Add a planted deterministic SVG change to demonstrate CI fails; baseline regeneration must be a deliberate reviewed developer operation, not a prerequisite to testing.

title: Bubble chart labels shift to the wrong point or disappear
description:
Review baseline c9a5793; discovered while following narsil-mcp findings in svggen/chart_diagrams.go. extractBubbleChartData appends Labels only when a point has a label (lines 1504-1506; same issue in parseBubblePerCategoryData lines 1568-1570). ScatterChart.drawPoints indexes Labels by point position (svggen/charts.go:2107-2110), so an unlabeled first point followed by a labeled second point displays the second label on the first point. The parallel-array bubble branch also never reads series.labels, despite the shared scatterSeriesSchema advertising it. Reproduced with a temporary TestNarsilReviewBubbleLabels: points [{x:1,y:10,size:2},{x:8,y:90,size:7,label:SECOND}] pass Validate but produce Labels=[SECOND] instead of [empty,SECOND]; parallel arrays with labels=[empty,SECOND] produce nil labels. Both regression assertions fail. No existing open Bead covers this raw svggen data-label defect.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Pass bubble_chart data with series=[{points:[{x:1,y:10,size:2},{x:8,y:90,size:7,label:"SECOND"}]}].
2. Validate succeeds. Extract/render the chart: SECOND is at the first point rather than (8,90).
3. Use parallel values=[10,90], x_values=[1,8], labels=["","SECOND"] instead: the label disappears.
The temporary regression test confirmed both extraction errors.
acceptance_criteria: Preserve a label slot for every bubble point, including missing labels; read labels in the supported parallel-array input. Add asymmetric regression tests with missing labels before/between labeled points, and verify rendered label positions correspond to the intended coordinates. Do not silently fabricate or reassign labels.
