title: Measure end-to-end agent slide quality against a human-rated baseline
description:
Context: docs/SLIDE_QUALITY_REDESIGN.md; reviewed baseline 2c219bf. Scope is user-provided PPTX templates with seven canonical layouts, not arbitrary template reconstruction.

What
Test the user's actual claim with fresh agents producing decks from briefs, not only pre-authored JSON fixtures. Compare current baseline to redesigned workflow with a frozen rubric and held-out templates. Determine whether the workflow improves useful visual output instead of merely passing more validators.

Where
tests/quality/prompts, tests/quality/README.md, new benchmark runner/report alongside existing quality harness

How
Use at least 12 briefs spanning KPI, comparison, process, narrative and charts, at least 3 template families including an unseen seven-layout template, and two repeated runs per configuration. Record model/version, prompts, tool calls, artifacts, cost and iterations. Blind paired ratings by two reviewers on readability, hierarchy, template fidelity, factual completeness and overall usability; report disagreements and failures. Pre-register target >=80% usable without manual slide editing, zero lost critical facts, and clear paired improvement; treat target as proposed product bar, not a proven guarantee.

Boundary
Implement this deliverable and its tests together; reuse existing metadata, source maps, rendering and quality infrastructure. Do not implement unrelated epic work. Preserve backwards compatibility or explicitly document a migration.
acceptance_criteria: Runner must actually invoke the configured agent and capture tools/artifacts; static fixture replay is labeled separately. Publish per-run evidence and aggregate uncertainty rather than only average score. Release decision requires achieved target and no critical content/template defects; otherwise narrow advertised capability or iterate. No unapproved paid/provider runs in default CI.
close_reason: Added fresh-agent benchmark runner for 12 briefs x 3 template families x 2 repeats/configuration, per-run tool/artifact/cost evidence, blind two-reviewer ratings, Wilson uncertainty, and honest release bar; default CI makes no provider calls.

title: Windows template install path uses Unix dotfile instead of AppData
description:
**Source:** Office Companion integration tests, 2026-06-01, against main `1134c1e5`.
**Affects:** `install.ps1`, `cmd/json2pptx/template_resolve.go`. Windows only.

## Problem

On a fresh Windows install, templates are placed in a Unix-style dotfile dir (`%USERPROFILE%\.json2pptx\templates\`) instead of the conventional `%LOCALAPPDATA%\json2pptx\templates\`. Apps should not create dotfile dirs in the user profile root.

The Go resolver (`cmd/json2pptx/template_resolve.go`) only checks `~/.json2pptx/templates/` (via `os.UserHomeDir()`) as priority #3 and has no `%LOCALAPPDATA%` path, so installer and resolver agree on the wrong location. OC's Rust resolver (`tools/json2pptx.rs:default_templates_dirs()`) already searches `{data_local_dir}/json2pptx/templates/` as #2 — correct but empty because the installer never writes there.

| Component | Path |
|-----------|------|
| install.ps1 (templates dest) | `%USERPROFILE%\.json2pptx\templates\` |
| install.ps1 (MCP --templates-dir) | `%USERPROFILE%\.json2pptx\templates\` |
| Go resolver (#3) | `os.UserHomeDir()/.json2pptx/templates/` = same |
| OC Rust resolver (#1 default) | `home_dir()/.json2pptx/templates/` = same |
| OC Rust resolver (#2 default) | `data_local_dir()/json2pptx/templates/` = **correct but empty** |

## Suggested fix

**1. install.ps1** — `$TemplatesDst = Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA "json2pptx\templates"`; update MCP `$TemplatesPath` to match (with `-replace '\\','/'`).

**2. cmd/json2pptx/template_resolve.go** — before the home-dir fallback, add a Windows branch:

```go
if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
    if localAppData := os.Getenv("LOCALAPPDATA"); localAppData != "" {
        winDir := filepath.Join(localAppData, "json2pptx", "templates")
        if dirExists(winDir) {
            return winDir, false
        }
    }
}
```

**3. install.sh** — no change (dotfiles are conventional on Unix).

## Migration

Existing users at `%USERPROFILE%\.json2pptx\templates\` keep working — the home-dir check stays as fallback; LOCALAPPDATA is just preferred on Windows. A future release could log a deprecation warning when templates are found only via the dotfile path on Windows.
close_reason: Implemented: install.ps1 writes templates to %LOCALAPPDATA%\json2pptx\templates (dest + MCP --templates-dir + help/summary text); template_resolve.go adds localAppDataTemplatesDir() helper, preferred over ~/.json2pptx dotfile on Windows in both resolveTemplatesDir and resolveTemplatePath; home-dir fallback retained for existing installs. Regression tests added.

title: KPI delta/trend field silently dropped during compilation
description:
**Source:** Office Companion integration tests (oc-cli pptx_semantic_* tools), 2026-06-01, against main `1134c1e5`.
**OC-side bead:** `kuse-cowork-jaily` (closed, deferred to maintainer)

## Symptom

KPI `delta`/`trend`/`change`/`sub` fields are silently dropped during compilation — content loss with no warning or fit finding.

### Repro

Semantic spec slide:

```yaml
slides:
  - kind: kpi_snapshot
    title: "Key Performance Indicators"
    kpis:
      - label: "Revenue"
        value: "$50M"
        delta: "+5%"
      - label: "NRR"
        value: "127%"
        delta: "+3%"
      - label: "Churn"
        value: "2.1%"
        delta: "-0.4%"
```

Compile with `json2pptx semantic compile --spec ... --include-compiled-json`. The compiled JSON shows `kpi-4up` with only `{big: "$50M", small: "Revenue"}` — delta values vanish.

## Root cause

`KPICell` (`internal/patterns/kpi_common.go:22-26`) has only three fields:

```go
type KPICell struct {
    Big   string   `json:"big"`
    Small string   `json:"small"`
    Icon  *IconRef `json:"icon,omitempty"`
}
```

`UnmarshalJSON` aliases `value`/`number`→Big and `label`/`caption`→Small but has NO field for `delta`/`trend`/`change`/`sub`. `json.Unmarshal` drops unknown fields silently; no diagnostic emitted.

## Suggested fix

**Option A — render support (recommended):** add `Sub string json:"sub,omitempty"` to KPICell; in UnmarshalJSON capture `firstNonEmpty(obj.Sub, obj.Delta, obj.Trend, obj.Change)`; render Sub as a small (green/red) annotation below/beside Big in kpi-Nup. Shared `KPICell` means the fix propagates to all kpi-Nup variants (kpi-3up, kpi-4up, kpi-inline, kpi-parametric).

**Option B — warn only (minimum viable):** detect when delta/trend/sub keys are present in raw JSON but unconsumed, emit a fit finding pointing at the `trending-up`/`trending-down` icon workaround.

## Agent-facing sync note

If Option A lands, a new KPICell field (`sub`) is a JSON-schema addition to a pattern shape → update `skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md` and `docs/PATTERNS.md`. If Option B, a new fit finding code → update `docs/FIT_FINDINGS.md` + SKILL.md.
close_reason: Implemented Option A: added KPICell.Sub field (aliases delta/trend/change) rendered as a small annotation in kpi-Nup/kpi-inline; fixed the actual semantic-compile drop point in internal/semantic/slides/kpi.go (kpiCell + kpiCells + bullet fallback). Updated SKILL.md, docs/PATTERNS.md. Added regression tests in patterns + semantic/slides; e2e verified sub reaches compiled JSON.

title: semantic: MCP strict enum wrong-type silently defaults to warn
description:
## Summary
Semantic MCP tools should fail fast on malformed arguments, but `strict` values with the wrong JSON type are treated as omitted and silently default to `warn`. Example: `{"strict": true}` should be an `INVALID_PARAMETER`, not a warning-mode validation.

## Reproduction
Call any semantic MCP tool such as `validate_deck_spec` with:
```json
{
  "spec": {"meta": {"title": "Deck"}, "slides": [{"kind": "title", "title": "Hi"}]},
  "strict": true
}
```
Static path: `semanticStrictArg` calls `request.RequireString("strict")`; any error is treated as missing and returns `StrictnessWarn`.

## Expected
Fail fast with structured `INVALID_PARAMETER` at `strict`, expected type `string`, allowed values `off|warn|strict`.

## Root cause
`cmd/json2pptx/mcp_semantic.go:semanticStrictArg` conflates wrong-type errors with absence/empty string. The same pattern appears in optional `template` reads where wrong type is silently ignored.

## Suggested fix
Inspect raw arguments to distinguish absent from present-wrong-type, or add a shared enum/string helper for MCP args. Use it for `strict`, `output_validation`, and other semantic MCP enum/string parameters.
close_reason: Implemented: semantic MCP tools now fail fast on wrong-typed optional args. Added shared semanticOptionalString/semanticOptionalBool helpers that distinguish absent from present-but-wrong-type, rewired strict/template/output_validation/include_compiled_json across validate/compile/render handlers to return INVALID_PARAMETER instead of silently defaulting. Regression test TestSemanticMCP_WrongTypedEnumArgs added.

title: semantic: CLI render --output-validation accepts typos instead of failing fast
description:
## Summary
`json2pptx semantic render --output-validation` accepts arbitrary strings. A typo like `--output-validation stric` is passed into the render runner instead of rejected at argument parsing. For a valid deck this command exits 0 and renders a PPTX, so the caller may believe strict output validation was applied when it was not.

## Reproduction
```yaml
meta:
  title: One
  template: modern
slides:
  - kind: title
    title: One
```
Run:
```bash
json2pptx semantic render --spec one.yaml --output out.pptx --output-validation stric
```
Actual: command succeeds and writes `out.pptx`.

## Expected
Fail fast with an invalid flag/parameter error: output-validation must be one of `off`, `warn`, or `strict`.

## Root cause
`cmd/json2pptx/semantic_cmd.go:runSemanticRender` parses `outputValidation` as a string and passes it directly to `RunPresentation`. MCP `render_deck_spec` does validate the enum, so CLI/MCP behavior diverges. In the runner, only exact `strict` blocks on validation findings; typo values are not strict.

## Suggested fix
Add a shared parser for output-validation (`off|warn|strict`) and use it in semantic CLI and MCP wrappers. Add a CLI regression test for `--output-validation stric` returning non-zero before rendering.
close_reason: Implemented: semantic render CLI now rejects --output-validation typos via new parseOutputValidation(off|warn|strict) helper, failing fast before any spec read or render — matching generate and MCP render_deck_spec. Added regression test asserting 'stric' errors and writes no pptx.

title: semantic: comparison over 10 balanced rows validates cleanly but compile falls back and explain over-promises comparison-2col
description:
## Summary
A  slide with exactly two balanced columns and 11 rows validates with no findings, but compile falls back to a generic content bullet slide because  caps at 10 rows. The explain/normalize plan still advertises the ideal comparison visual.

## Reproduction

title: skill(generate-deck): SKILL.md omits the entire semantic deck-spec MCP surface (validate/compile/render/explain_deck_spec, list_deck_archetypes, list_slide_kinds)
description:
## Summary
The semantic DeckSpec authoring path is a full agent-facing MCP surface — 6 tools registered in `cmd/json2pptx/mcp_semantic.go`:
`validate_deck_spec`, `compile_deck_spec`, `render_deck_spec`, `explain_deck_spec`, `list_deck_archetypes`, `list_slide_kinds` — plus the `json2pptx semantic {validate,compile,render,explain,schema}` CLI. **None of it is mentioned in `skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md`** (or its sub-files TOOLS/WORKFLOW/FINDINGS/RULES/PATTERNS). The only `docs/` coverage is the contributor-facing `docs/SEMANTIC_COMPILER.md` and `examples/semantic/`.

## Why this matters
Per the repo's skill-sync policy (CLAUDE.md): agent-facing CLI/MCP surfaces require SKILL.md coverage. An agent reading the skill never learns that a compact, validated, archetype-aware authoring surface exists — it only sees the raw PresentationInput + pattern path. The compact DeckSpec is precisely the surface a planning agent would prefer (kind-tagged slides → auto pattern/rhythm planning).

## Expected
Add a SKILL.md (or TOOLS.md) section documenting:
- When to use the semantic surface vs. raw `generate_presentation`.
- The 6 MCP tools and their envelope shapes (`validate_deck_spec` first-check, `compile_deck_spec` → raw PresentationInput, `render_deck_spec` → pptx, `explain_deck_spec` planning/rhythm, the two discovery tools).
- The DeckSpec shape: `meta{title,subtitle,archetype,template,...}` + `slides[]` with the 11 kinds (title, section, executive_summary, kpi_snapshot, chart_insight, comparison, process, roadmap, decision, closing, raw_json2pptx), required payload fields per kind, and strictness (`off|warn|strict`).

## Note
Several engine bugs in the semantic parser were just filed (see label `semantic-parser`). Documenting the surface should follow/accompany hardening it, so the skill does not advertise behaviors that are mid-fix (e.g. silent type-drops).

title: semantic: raw_json2pptx with non-object slide passes validate but crashes compile (parity gap, leaks deckinput.SlideInput, escapes envelope)
description:
## Summary
A `raw_json2pptx` slide whose `slide` payload is not an object passes `semantic validate` (`ok:true, no issues`) but then **fails `semantic compile`** with an opaque Go error that leaks `deckinput.SlideInput` and is returned **outside the finding envelope** (the printed envelope still says `ok:true`).

## Reproduction
```json
{"meta":{"title":"X"},"slides":[{"kind":"raw_json2pptx","slide":"i am a string not an object"}]}
```
`json2pptx semantic validate` → `ok:true, no issues`.
`json2pptx semantic compile` → stdout envelope `ok:true`, then stderr:
```
Error: semantic compile: slide 0 (raw_json2pptx): decode raw slide payload: json: cannot unmarshal string into Go value of type deckinput.SlideInput
```

## Expected
1. **Parity**: `validate` should reject a non-object `raw_json2pptx.slide` with a hard SEMANTIC_* finding, so the documented "spec that passes semantic validation always compiles" contract holds.
2. **Envelope consistency**: compile-stage failures should be represented as a structured finding (with the `slides[i].slide` path), not a bare Go error string leaking internal types.

## Root cause
- `internal/semantic/validate.go`: required-field check only verifies `slide` is non-empty (a non-empty string passes); no object-type check for the raw escape hatch.
- `internal/semantic/slides/raw.go` `CompileRaw`: marshals then `json.Unmarshal`s into `deckinput.SlideInput`; a scalar payload errors with the leaked type name. The error propagates via `Compile` as a plain `error`, and `cmd/json2pptx/semantic_cmd.go` (runSemanticCompile, ~L247) prints `result.Diagnostics` (empty here) then returns the bare error.

## Suggested fix
- In `validateSlide` for `KindRawJSON2pptx`, require `body["slide"]` to be a `map[string]any`; emit a hard `CodeSemanticRequired`/`CodeSemanticInvalidShape` finding otherwise.
- In `CompileRaw`, wrap the decode failure in a friendlier message (no internal type leak); ideally surface it as a diagnostic on `result.Diagnostics` so the envelope reflects it.
- Add a parity regression test asserting validate-rejects ⇔ compile-rejects for this input.
close_reason: Verified validate already rejects non-object raw_json2pptx.slide via validateRawEscapeHatch and compile blocks at the gate (structured envelope, no leaked type). Added TestRawNonObjectValidateCompileParity asserting validate-rejects ⇔ compile-rejects + envelope consistency, hardened CompileRaw decode error to not leak deckinput.SlideInput, and added TestCompileRaw_NonObjectPayload.

title: semantic: non-object slide element yields opaque INVALID_JSON leaking internal type rawDeck, with no slide path
description:
## Summary
A slide list element that is not a JSON object (string, number, array, null) aborts the whole parse with an opaque decoder error that **leaks the internal Go type name `rawDeck`** and carries **no `where.slide` path** — directly contradicting the documented design intent in `yaml.go`.

## Reproduction
```json
{"meta":{"title":"X"},"slides":["this is not a slide object", 42]}
```
Run: `json2pptx semantic validate --spec spec.json`

## Actual
```
code: INPUT.INVALID_JSON
message: json: cannot unmarshal string into Go struct field rawDeck.slides of type map[string]interface {}
```
No slide index, leaks `rawDeck` / `map[string]interface {}`.

## Expected
A path-scoped finding such as `slides[0]: slide must be an object (got string)` — matching the stated design goal. The comment at `internal/semantic/yaml.go` rawDeck declaration says: *"Slides are decoded as generic maps so that an unknown or malformed slide kind surfaces as a path-scoped semantic diagnostic rather than an opaque decoder error."* That goal is only met for a malformed *kind*, not a malformed slide *element*.

## Root cause
`internal/semantic/yaml.go`: `rawDeck.Slides []map[string]any`. A non-object element fails struct decode before per-slide handling runs.

## Suggested fix
Decode `Slides []json.RawMessage` (or `[]any`), then in `buildDeckSpec` loop per element: if it is not an object, emit a `slides[i]`-scoped `CodeInvalidSlide` diagnostic ("slide must be an object, got <type>") and continue, so other slides still validate. Never surface raw Go type names.
close_reason: Implemented: decode rawDeck.Slides as []any so a non-object slide element emits a path-scoped CodeInvalidSlide finding (slides[i]: slide must be an object, got <type>) instead of an opaque decoder error leaking rawDeck/map[string]interface{}; other slides still validate. Added regression tests.

title: semantic: unknown/typo'd keys inside meta are silently dropped, contradicting DeckMeta additionalProperties:false
description:
## Summary
Unknown keys at the **top level** get a helpful "did you mean" diagnostic, but unknown keys inside `meta` are silently ignored. This contradicts the published schema — `json2pptx semantic schema` declares `DeckMeta.additionalProperties:false` — and gives no hint when a meta key is misspelled.

## Reproduction
```json
{"meta":{"tilte":"Typo Title","archetpe":"qbr"},"slides":[{"kind":"title","title":"Hi"}]}
```
Run: `json2pptx semantic validate --spec spec.json`

## Actual
Only `meta.title is required` (because `tilte` was dropped and real `title` is absent). The typos `tilte`/`archetpe` are never reported.

## Expected
Per the schema's `additionalProperties:false`, unknown meta keys should each emit a SEMANTIC_UNKNOWN_FIELD finding with a "did you mean `title`?" / "did you mean `archetype`?" suggestion — mirroring `checkUnknownTopLevel`.

## Root cause
`internal/semantic/yaml.go`: `checkUnknownTopLevel` only inspects the root map. `meta` is decoded by struct unmarshal (no `DisallowUnknownFields`), so unknown meta keys disappear. The schema in `internal/semantic/schema.go` sets `additionalProperties:false` for DeckMeta → drift between advertised schema and parser behavior.

## Suggested fix
Add `checkUnknownMeta(top["meta"], &ds)` reusing the existing `editDistance`/suggestion machinery against the known DeckMeta json keys (`title,subtitle,archetype,template,audience,author,date`). Reuse the `topLevelMigrations`-style table for common aliases.

title: semantic render skips raw generate asset resolution despite raw_json2pptx
description:
[P2] Raw generate resolves URLs and local assets before generation, but semantic render assumes compiled decks have no asset references and skips that path. Because raw_json2pptx passes raw slide payloads through, a semantic deck can still contain image/asset references that need the same guarded resolution.

Impact: the raw escape hatch can behave differently under 'semantic render' than the same raw JSON under 'generate', especially for relative image paths or URLs.
design:
## Suggested fix
- Either forbid asset/URL references in raw_json2pptx with clear diagnostics, OR run the same guarded resolution hook using the semantic spec directory as the base.
- Add tests for relative image paths in raw_json2pptx under semantic render.
acceptance_criteria:
- raw_json2pptx asset/URL refs under semantic render are resolved (base = spec dir) or rejected with a clear diagnostic
- test covers relative image path in raw_json2pptx under semantic render
- behavior matches 'generate' for the same raw JSON
close_reason: Implemented: semantic render now runs the same guarded URL download + relative-asset resolution as generate for raw_json2pptx escape-hatch slides, resolving relative paths against the spec dir (base = spec dir) and rejecting unreachable/missing assets with the same URL_FETCH_FAILED/IMAGE_PATH diagnostics. Added regression tests for the resolve and reject cases; documented the parity in docs/SEMANTIC_COMPILER.md.

title: semantic compile succeeds with raw pattern JSON that later fails render
description:
[P2] A valid semantic kpi_snapshot can compile successfully but fail at render/output-validation time because the lowered raw kpi-2up pattern rejects long KPI values such as 'CHF 142.3M'.

The compiler appears to select KPI patterns mainly by metric count, while render-time raw pattern constraints enforce text length and density later.

Impact: agents treat validate/compile as a renderability signal, then hit late render failures after the semantic spec already looked valid. Repair diagnostics arrive too late in the flow.
design:
## Suggested fix
- Add a post-compile raw validation/preflight stage before PPTX generation.
- Map raw pattern/schema failures back to semantic paths with recommended edits.
- Where possible, choose fallback patterns or transform long values before emitting known-invalid raw JSON.
- Add regression tests for KPI length/density failures (e.g. 'CHF 142.3M' in kpi-2up).
acceptance_criteria:
- post-compile raw preflight runs before PPTX generation
- raw pattern failures map back to semantic spec paths with recommended edits
- long KPI value (e.g. CHF 142.3M) selects a fallback or fails at validate/compile, not at render
- regression test covers KPI length/density failure

title: Reject shape-grid gaps that exceed grid bounds to avoid negative extents
description:
Problem: Shape-grid resolution subtracts total row/column gaps from bounds without guarding against negative available width/height. Negative totals can flow into DrawingML extents.

Where: internal/shapegrid/grid.go Resolve available width/height calculation around lines 31-44; distributeEMU around lines 578-635; internal/pptx/transform.go emits extents around lines 22-36.

Impact/repro: A small shape_grid bounds with many columns and large col_gap/row_gap can produce negative CX/CY values and XML like <a:ext cx="-...">, which is invalid DrawingML geometry or renders invisible shapes.

Implementation: In Validate or Resolve, reject grids where totalColGap >= grid.Bounds.CX or totalRowGap >= grid.Bounds.CY, with a clear diagnostic. Also make distributeEMU defensively reject/handle negative totals so invalid geometry cannot be emitted even if validation is bypassed.
acceptance_criteria:
- Invalid gap/bounds combinations return a validation/render error instead of negative extents.
- Valid existing grids continue to resolve as before.
- Add tests for excessive col_gap and row_gap.
close_reason: Implemented: guard in shapegrid.Resolve rejects grids whose total col/row gap meets-or-exceeds the grid bounds (returns an error instead of negative DrawingML extents); distributeEMU defensively returns zero-width entries for non-positive totals. Added regression tests for excessive col_gap/row_gap, a within-bounds positive case, and the distributeEMU clamp.

title: Make table rendering avoid mutating caller-owned TableSpec rows
description:
Problem: GenerateTableXML truncates overflowing rows by assigning back to table.Rows, mutating the caller-owned model during rendering.

Where: internal/generator/table.go GenerateTableXML truncation block around lines 151-179.

Impact/repro: Call GenerateTableXML(table, smallBounds) where rows overflow; table.Rows is shortened and a summary row is inserted. Reusing the same TableSpec for a later larger render, validation pass, or diagnostics silently loses original rows.

Implementation: Treat rendering as pure over the input spec. Work on a local rows slice/copy for truncation and derived row counts. Do not assign to table.Rows or mutate caller-owned cell slices unless explicitly documented and safe.
acceptance_criteria:
- GenerateTableXML leaves input TableSpec.Rows unchanged after overflow truncation.
- Rendered XML still includes the truncation summary row when needed.
- Add a test that calls GenerateTableXML and verifies the original TableSpec is unchanged.
close_reason: Implemented: GenerateTableXML now renders purely over input spec; overflow truncation builds a fresh renderRows slice instead of reassigning/mutating caller-owned table.Rows and its backing array. Added regression test TestGenerateTableXML_DoesNotMutateCallerRowsOnTruncation.

title: Sanitize XML 1.0 illegal control characters in raw OOXML text paths
description:
Problem: Some XML escape helpers handle &, <, >, quotes, etc. but do not strip or reject XML 1.0 illegal control characters such as U+0000..U+0008, U+000B, U+000C, and U+000E..U+001F. JSON can legally carry these as escaped strings.

Where: internal/pptx/text.go escape/text emission around lines 206-232; internal/generator/table.go table cell XML escaping around lines 1016-1035. internal/generator/notes.go already strips these via xmlEscapeString, showing inconsistent behavior.

Impact/repro: A shape-grid/table/footer/source/takeaway text value containing `` can produce non-well-formed XML inside the PPTX, causing Office repair dialogs or open failures.

Implementation: Centralize XML text sanitization in a shared helper, preferably in internal/pptx or a nearby XML utility. Strip or reject illegal XML 1.0 runes before writing raw OOXML fragments. Apply it consistently to pptx text and table text paths without double-escaping valid content.
acceptance_criteria:
- Text containing illegal XML 1.0 controls cannot produce malformed slide/table XML.
- Valid Unicode text, newlines/tabs where allowed, and XML metacharacters still render correctly.
- Add regression tests for  in table cells and generated shape text.
close_reason: Implemented: centralized XML 1.0 illegal control-char stripping via pptx.IsIllegalXMLChar; applied to pptx a:t text, attr values, table cells, and notes; added regression tests

title: Honor template bullet capacities above default pagination threshold
description:
Problem: effectiveMaxBullets claims to return the highest MaxBullets across text-capable layouts, but only returns best when it is lower than DefaultMaxBullets. Capacities above 8 are ignored.

Where: internal/pagination/pagination.go effectiveMaxBullets around lines 259-278.

Impact/repro: With a layout whose Capacity.MaxBullets is 12 and a slide with 9 bullets, PaginateWithLayouts still paginates into continuation slides at the default threshold of 8. This creates unnecessary slides and can break intended layout rhythm.

Implementation: Return best whenever best > 0. Only fall back to DefaultMaxBullets when no text-capable layout has capacity info. If a hard cap is intentional, document and test it explicitly instead of contradicting the comment.
acceptance_criteria:
- effectiveMaxBullets returns capacities greater than DefaultMaxBullets.
- Existing lower-than-default capacity behavior is preserved.
- Add unit tests for no capacity, lower capacity, equal capacity, and higher capacity cases.
close_reason: Implemented: effectiveMaxBullets now returns the highest layout capacity whenever positive (not just when below DefaultMaxBullets), honoring template capacities above 8. Updated/added unit tests for no-capacity, lower, equal, and higher capacity cases.

title: Use configured file retention for HTTP download expires_at
description:
Problem: The API response for file downloads hardcodes expires_at to now + 1 hour, while the output cleaner deletes files according to cfg.Storage.FileRetention.

Where: internal/api/convert.go sendFileResponse around lines 333-352; cmd/json2pptx/serve.go starts OutputCleaner with cfg.Storage.FileRetention around lines 128-134; internal/config/config.go storage file_retention around lines 61-67.

Impact/repro: If file_retention is 5m, clients receive a URL claiming validity for an hour but it may 404 after cleanup. If retention is longer than an hour, clients are told links expire too early.

Implementation: Add file retention to api.ServerConfig and ConvertService, pass cfg.Storage.FileRetention from runServe, and compute expires_at from that configured retention. Ensure zero/invalid duration preserves sensible existing default semantics.
acceptance_criteria:
- expires_at matches the same retention duration used by OutputCleaner.
- Existing default behavior remains one hour if default retention is one hour.
- Add a test that configures a short retention and verifies response expiry delta.
close_reason: Implemented: expires_at now derived from configured Storage.FileRetention via ServerConfig.FileRetention -> ConvertService.SetFileRetention, with DefaultFileRetention (1h) fallback for zero/invalid; added regression test for short/long/zero retention

title: Reject trailing tokens after HTTP convert JSON request body
description:
Problem: The HTTP convert handler decodes one JSON value and never checks for EOF, so bodies with trailing garbage or multiple JSON documents can be accepted.

Where: internal/api/convert.go parseAndValidateRequest around lines 183-210.

Impact/repro: A request body like `{"template":"x","slides":[...]} {"unexpected":true}` can be accepted as if only the first object existed. This hides malformed client requests and weakens strict validation.

Implementation: After decoder.Decode(&req) succeeds, call decoder.Decode(&struct{}{}) and require io.EOF. Any non-EOF result should return INVALID_JSON/400 using the existing JSON parse error response pattern. Keep MaxBytesReader and DisallowUnknownFields behavior intact.
acceptance_criteria:
- Single valid JSON object is accepted.
- Valid object followed by whitespace is accepted.
- Valid object followed by another JSON value or trailing junk returns HTTP 400.
- Add focused API tests for trailing object and trailing junk.
close_reason: Implemented: HTTP convert handler now rejects trailing tokens after the JSON body (requires io.EOF after decode); trailing object/junk returns INVALID_JSON/400, trailing whitespace still accepted. Added focused API tests.

title: Reject invalid HTTP API slide types during request validation
description:
Problem: The HTTP API casts APISlide.Type directly to types.SlideType without validating it. Unknown slide types can flow into layout selection and generate unexpected slides instead of returning a client error.

Where: internal/api/convert.go apiSlidesToPresentation around lines 451-479; internal/types/presentation.go SlideType constants/helpers around lines 57-82; parseAndValidateRequest in internal/api/convert.go is the right validation seam.

Impact/repro: POST /api/v1/convert with a slide containing `"type":"contnet"` may proceed to generate a deck instead of returning INVALID_SLIDE_TYPE/400. Layout selector default behavior can treat unknown types as broadly suitable.

Implementation: In parseAndValidateRequest, validate every non-empty slide.type with types.IsValidSlideType. Empty type should preserve current default-to-content behavior. On invalid value, return HTTP 400 with the invalid field/value and types.SupportedSlideTypes() in details.
acceptance_criteria:
- Empty slide.type still defaults to content.
- Unknown non-empty slide.type returns HTTP 400 before generation.
- Error response includes supported slide types.
- Add API tests for valid, empty, and invalid type values.
close_reason: Implemented: validate non-empty slide.type in parseAndValidateRequest via types.IsValidSlideType; empty defaults to content, unknown returns 400 INVALID_SLIDE_TYPE with field and SupportedSlideTypes() in details; added API tests

title: MCP: Add guarded path-based template inspection parity
description:
Location: cmd/json2pptx/mcp_examine_template.go:35; cmd/json2pptx/mcp_examine_template.go:60; cmd/json2pptx/examine_template.go:71; cmd/json2pptx/examine_template.go:101; cmd/json2pptx/cli_command_classification.go:97

Problem: CLI examine-template accepts any local PPTX path and can emit inspection artifacts. MCP examine_template only accepts template_name resolved through configured template lookup, while validate-template and template-check are CLI-only. MCP-only agents cannot validate or inspect a newly supplied template file until it has been installed/registered in the server template directory.

Root cause: Template authoring/inspection parity is split between path-based CLI commands and name-based MCP tools without a safe import/path inspection primitive.

Impact: Agents working through MCP cannot complete template authoring or validation loops for local template files, despite the CLI being able to do so.

Implementation notes: Add a guarded template_path form to examine_template or introduce a separate import/examine_template_file primitive with path validation against allowed roots/base_dir. Keep name-based registered-template inspection as the default. Surface validate-template/template-check limitations and the path workflow in get_capabilities.
acceptance_criteria: MCP agents can inspect a local PPTX template path within allowed roots or receive a clear forbidden-path diagnostic; existing template_name behavior remains; validate-template/template-check parity or documented MCP workaround is exposed in get_capabilities; tests cover registered-template inspection, allowed path inspection, and rejected unsafe paths.
close_reason: Implemented: examine_template MCP tool now accepts a guarded template_path (resolved against base_dir, containment-checked via utils.ValidatePath) alongside template_name; forbidden/missing/wrong-ext/ambiguous cases return clear structured diagnostics; examine_template added to capabilities base_dir list; validate-template/template-check CLIOnlyReasons updated to document the path workflow + remaining conformance limitation; SchemaVersion 4.55.0 + changelog + TOOLS.md; tests cover registered, allowed-path, forbidden, traversal, not-found, wrong-ext, ambiguous, and parity.

title: AGENT: Add resumable per-pass state for auto_repair and make_deck
description:
Location: cmd/json2pptx/mcp_auto_repair.go:1; cmd/json2pptx/mcp_auto_repair.go:44; cmd/json2pptx/mcp_make_deck.go:1; cmd/json2pptx/mcp_idempotency.go:93

Problem: auto_repair and make_deck hide multi-step loops behind one long-running call and return trace only after completion. Idempotency deduplicates retries but does not provide checkpoint/resume semantics or per-pass partial progress.

Root cause: Workflow facades are implemented as synchronous server-side loops without a durable or caller-visible loop state model.

Impact: Agents cannot inspect, stop, resume, or correct a long repair workflow mid-flight. If rendering or vision stalls/fails late, useful intermediate artifacts and findings are not exposed as a resumable state.

Implementation notes: After truthful artifact/evidence status exists, introduce sessionized loop state or next_state snapshots after each deterministic/visual repair pass. Include current artifact path, presentation JSON, findings, attempted fixes, pass index, gate state, and safe resume token. Do not implement before idempotency and evidence-status fixes land.
acceptance_criteria: auto_repair/make_deck can return or persist per-pass state including artifact path, presentation JSON, findings, attempted fixes, gate state, and next action; agents can resume from a checkpoint without repeating completed passes; partial/degraded completion is explicit; tests cover resume after deterministic pass and after visual QA/render failure.
close_reason: Implemented resumable per-pass state for auto_repair and make_deck: new mcp_loop_state.go adds a per-process TTL'd loopSessionStore + loopCheckpoint + caller-visible next_state {completion, resumable, resume_token, next_action, passes_run, next_pass, max_passes, artifact_path, remaining_findings}. runAutoRepairLoop now takes a tool name + optional resume state, seeds start pass/trace from the checkpoint (continuous global pass numbering, no completed pass repeats), tracks stall, classifies completion (converged/converged_degraded/max_passes_exhausted/no_progress/render_incomplete), and snapshots the post-repair deck. Both facades accept resume_token (RESUME_TOKEN_NOT_FOUND/MISMATCH errors; deck/trace/provenance inherited, gate+max_passes overridable, presentation/outline ignored; make_deck preserves plan; deck deep-copied so re-resume is deterministic). presentation/outline relaxed from schema-required (handler still enforces fresh-run). Output schemas advertise next_state (required); SKILL.md + SCHEMA_CHANGELOG (4.56.0) + SchemaVersion updated. Tests: store round-trip/expiry/nil, completion classifier, resume-after-deterministic-pass, resume-after-render-failure checkpoint, deterministic re-resume, token errors, make_deck plan preservation.

title: LAYOUT: Separate canonical blank and blank-title layout IDs

title: FIT: Unify contrast preflight and render replacement evidence
description:
Location: internal/generator/preflight_contrast.go:69; internal/generator/text_contrast.go:518; svggen/style.go contrast helpers

Problem: contrast preflight predicts replacements through svggen.EnsureContrast, while render-time text contrast enforcement has additional neutral-color flipping logic. The same white-on-light-accent case can be predicted as muddy grey in validation but rendered as black.

Root cause: validation and generation use different contrast replacement algorithms/evidence, and neither reports which algorithm/palette mode produced the suggested color.

Impact: Agents can see validate-time advice that does not match generated output, causing unnecessary JSON edits or confusion during QA.

Implementation notes: Either share the replacement algorithm or make the finding evidence explicit enough to explain the difference. Preserve template/theme palette context and do not break defensive render-time contrast fixes.
acceptance_criteria: Preflight and render-time contrast findings agree on replacement color for the same resolved foreground/background/template context, or findings explicitly disclose algorithm/palette mode when they differ; tests cover white-on-light accent and normal dark-on-light cases; render-time defensive contrast behavior remains intact.
close_reason: Implemented: extracted shared contrastReplacement() algorithm used by both render-time contrast pass (fixSrgb/fixSchemeColorsForContrast) and the preflight predictor (DetectContrastPreflight), so contrast_predicted now matches the contrast_autofixed swap (white-on-light-accent flips to dk1, not muddy gray). Added replacement_mode (flip|lerp) to finding evidence; regression tests assert preflight==render for flip and lerp cases; updated FINDINGS.md, FIT_FINDINGS.md, finding_meta.go.

title: FIT: Preserve contrast finding paths for render-time text swaps
description:
Location: internal/generator/text_contrast.go:518; cmd/json2pptx/fit_findings_collect.go:967; internal/generator/preflight_contrast.go:35

Problem: render-time contrast enforcement records generator.ContrastSwap values with colors/ratios, but not slide/path/source location. contrastSwapsToFindings then emits contrast_autofixed findings without enough location for agents to map the issue back to the source cell/text.

Root cause: ContrastSwap does not carry JSON path or slide context through the renderer, and the finding adapter cannot reconstruct it after generation.

Impact: Even when the renderer fixes a contrast issue, the diagnostic is hard to repair or audit because it lacks the owning slide/cell/text path.

Implementation notes: Thread slide index/path/source context into contrast swap recording for shape_grid cells and other render-time text surfaces. Keep this separate from changing the contrast replacement algorithm.
acceptance_criteria: contrast_autofixed findings include slide index and source JSON/path for shape_grid text swaps at minimum; existing color/ratio evidence is preserved; tests cover a shape_grid white-on-light fill swap and assert path points to the cell/text; no unrelated contrast behavior changes are required.
close_reason: Implemented: thread slide index/path/source into ContrastSwap records. enforceShapeGridContrast and enforceTextContrastInSlide now stamp swaps (via annotateContrastSwaps) with 0-based slide index, a JSON pointer (/slides/N/shape_grid/shapes/M for grid cells, /slides/N for layout/run text), and a source label (shape_grid/lstStyle/run). contrastSwapsToFindings surfaces path on the finding and source in fix.params; color/ratio evidence preserved. Added regression tests + synced FIT_FINDINGS.md, PATH_GRAMMAR.md, FINDINGS.md, finding_meta.go.

title: QA: Expand built-in template coverage via discovery helper
description:
Location: cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid_cross_template_test.go:12; cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid_cross_template_test.go:44; cmd/json2pptx/pattern_resolve_test.go:279; internal/template/style_extractor_test.go:375; templates/

Problem: several cross-template tests hard-code only forest-green, midnight-blue, modern-template, and warm-coral even though templates/ contains additional built-ins such as abstract, blue-corporate, business-template, modern, and modern-yellow.

Root cause: template coverage was manually curated and did not grow with designer-owned built-in templates.

Impact: shape grids, callouts, style extraction, pattern resolution, and table-style paths can regress on built-ins that are shipped but not exercised by these tests.

Implementation notes: Add a bounded discovery helper over templates/*.pptx with explicit inclusion/exclusion rules and CI cost guard. Do not blindly make every expensive test run over every template if runtime/flakiness grows; start with corpus/smoke tests and tracked skips only.
acceptance_criteria: Cross-template tests use a shared built-in template discovery helper or documented corpus list; all shipped templates are either covered by relevant smoke tests or explicitly skipped with a bead/reference explaining why; CI runtime remains acceptable; tests fail when a new built-in template is added without classification/coverage decision.
close_reason: Implemented: shared built-in template discovery helper (internal/testutil/templates.go) with explicit TierCore/TierSmoke classification, scratch-file exclusion (~$, dot, underscore), and a coverage guard (TestBuiltinTemplateCoverage) that fails when a shipped templates/*.pptx lacks a classification or vice versa. Cross-template matrices (shape_grid, callout) now source the core corpus from CoreTemplateNames(); the table-style load/smoke test now exercises all 9 built-ins via AllBuiltinTemplateNames(). Expensive matrices stay bounded to the 4 core templates per the cost guard.

title: QA: Fix lexicographic slide image ordering in template visual QA script
description:
Location: scripts/test_template_visual_qa.sh:40; scripts/test_template_visual_qa.sh:176; cmd/pptx2jpg/main.go:105; internal/render/render.go:31

Problem: pptx2jpg emits unpadded zero-based filenames such as generated-slide-0.jpg and generated-slide-10.jpg. The template visual QA script sorts image paths lexicographically and then labels them as 1-indexed slides. Decks with 10+ slides can attach screenshots to the wrong source slide in reports.

Root cause: a script-level sort/label assumption did not account for unpadded numeric filenames. The internal render package has numeric sorting helpers, but this shell workflow still needs its own fix or padded output.

Impact: QA reports for template-qa-deck can misdiagnose slides after slide 9, causing agents to fix the wrong JSON slide or miss the actual visual defect.

Implementation notes: Audit all remaining slide PNG/JPG sort sites before changing output names. Prefer numeric/version sort in scripts unless changing pptx2jpg filenames is intentionally backward-compatible. Correct comments around zero-based vs one-based slide labels.
acceptance_criteria: Template visual QA reports preserve numeric slide order for 10+ slides; slide labels map generated-slide-0 to slide 1, generated-slide-10 to slide 11, etc.; tests or a shellcheck-style fixture cover unpadded filenames; audit confirms no other lexicographic slide-image report paths remain or files follow-up beads.
close_reason: Implemented: template visual QA script now uses 'sort -V' (matching e2e_visual_test.sh) over unpadded ImageMagick filenames so 10+ slide decks map screenshots to the correct source slide; pptx2jpg listing sorted numerically via new sortSlideJPGs/slideIndexFromName helpers with regression tests; corrected script header comment (generated-slide-N, 0-indexed). Audit: audit_palette.go uses pdftoppm (zero-padded) so its lexicographic sort is correct; no other unpadded slide-image sort sites remain.

title: WF: Mark preview-wireframe output as structural-only
description:
Location: cmd/json2pptx/mcp_wireframe.go:1; cmd/json2pptx/mcp_wireframe.go:49; cmd/json2pptx/mcp_output_schemas.go:833; skills/generate-deck/TOOLS.md:72; skills/generate-deck/WORKFLOW.md:125

Problem: preview_slide_wireframe is a LibreOffice-free structural geometry preview, not rendered visual QA. Docs mention this, but the response lacks a machine-readable contract field that prevents agents from treating wireframe PNGs as proof of rendered text flow, icon/text collisions, SVG label readability, or visual polish.

Root cause: the tool contract relies on prose descriptions rather than a response field describing inspection kind and limitations.

Impact: A workflow can substitute wireframe inspection for rendered pixel inspection and miss PowerPoint text wrapping, icon overlay insets, template font metrics, SVG readability, or image fidelity.

Implementation notes: Add a response field such as contract: structural_only or inspection_kind: wireframe_structural, plus limitations/not_text_flow_safe. Update output schema and skill docs so render-only/wireframe-only is not equivalent to visual QA.
acceptance_criteria: preview_slide_wireframe responses include a machine-readable structural-only contract/inspection_kind and limitation flags; output schema tests assert the fields; docs distinguish wireframe, rendered image generation, and rendered visual inspection; no visual-QA categories or quality verdicts are emitted by wireframe preview.
notes: Follow-up from 2026-05-22 agent-native review: skills/generate-deck/TOOLS.md can be read as treating inspect_slide_images OR render_slide_image/render_deck_thumbnails as equivalent repair-phase checks. While this bead already covers wireframe limitations, include docs language that rendered image creation alone is not visual inspection; rendered pixels must be inspected by an agent/tool before they count as visual QA evidence.
close_reason: Implemented: preview_slide_wireframe now stamps a machine-readable structural-only contract on every response (inspection_kind=wireframe_structural, contract=structural_only, not_text_flow_safe=true, limitations[]); output schema marks these required with pinned enums; added handler + schema regression tests asserting the fields and the absence of visual-QA verdicts; updated TOOLS.md (catalogue entry + REPAIR phase wording that rendering alone is not inspection) and WORKFLOW.md (three-way wireframe/render/inspect distinction).

title: VQA: Report requested versus actual quality mode
description:
Location: cmd/json2pptx/mcp_visual_qa.go:50; cmd/json2pptx/mcp_visual_qa.go:127; cmd/json2pptx/mcp_visual_qa.go:229; cmd/json2pptx/mcp_auto_repair.go:380; cmd/json2pptx/mcp_output_schemas.go:1103

Problem: quality_mode can say deterministic+visual_qa whenever visual QA was requested, even when render tools are unavailable and inspection_mode is skipped. The response has some truth fields, but the top-level label is request-derived and easy for agents to misread.

Root cause: requested capability and actual inspection backend are conflated in the response contract.

Impact: Agents and users can overestimate QA rigor, believing rendered/vision inspection happened when the pipeline only ran deterministic checks or skipped visual QA.

Implementation notes: Preserve backward compatibility for existing fields. Add explicit requested_quality_mode/actual_quality_mode or a quality object with requested, actual, inspection_mode, and fallback_reasons. Do not rename existing fields without aliases.
acceptance_criteria: Responses clearly expose both requested and actual quality mode; render-unavailable visual QA requests show actual deterministic/skipped state and fallback reason; malformed present visual_qa arguments fail fast with INVALID_PARAMETER instead of silently disabling the requested mode; absent visual_qa keeps the deterministic default; existing clients relying on quality_mode still receive a compatible value or documented alias; tests cover requested visual QA with render available, heuristic fallback, render unavailable skip, and malformed visual_qa input.
notes: Follow-up from 2026-05-22 agent-native/reliability review: REL-007 found extractVisualQAConfig silently disables visual QA when the present visual_qa object cannot be marshaled/unmarshaled. Treat this as part of requested-vs-actual quality reporting: absent visual_qa may default to deterministic, but malformed present visual_qa must be a corrective argument error so agents do not unknowingly lose pixel/vision inspection.
close_reason: Implemented requested-vs-actual quality reporting: added always-present quality{requested,actual,inspection_mode,fallback_reasons} object to auto_repair/make_deck (buildQualityReport), made quality_mode an alias of quality.actual so a requested-but-skipped visual phase reports deterministic instead of overstating rigor; extractVisualQAConfig now fails fast with INVALID_PARAMETER on present-but-malformed visual_qa instead of silently disabling (REL-007), absent/null keeps deterministic default. Updated output schemas (both required), capabilities hint, SKILL.md, SCHEMA_CHANGELOG (4.57.0), schema-fingerprint comment. Added tests for vision/heuristic/skipped quality mapping, malformed fail-fast, and absent default.

title: SVG: Distinguish authored and effective aspect evidence for grid diagrams
description:
Location: cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go:729; internal/generator/media.go:680; cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go:987

Problem: current diagram aspect findings can conflate authored/cell aspect with effective rendered aspect. After render-time dimension injection, a diagram may render without letterboxing while findings still compare against fallback 800x600 dimensions. Conversely, using only effective dimensions could hide authoring mistakes when fit modes letterbox or scale the visual.

Root cause: aspect diagnostics lack explicit evidence for original cell bounds, fit-adjusted bounds, authored dimensions, and effective render dimensions.

Impact: agents may chase false aspect findings or miss cases where authored dimensions intentionally fight the cell.

Implementation notes: Keep this separate from dimension resolver implementation if possible. Add evidence fields/details rather than simply replacing one ratio with another. Make the finding message distinguish authored mismatch from actual rendered mismatch.
acceptance_criteria: diagram_aspect_mismatch findings include enough evidence to see cell aspect, fit-adjusted/render bounds, authored dimensions, and effective render dimensions; unset dimensions that render at cell aspect do not emit stale fallback mismatch; tests cover unset, both-set mismatch, and fit mode cases.
close_reason: Implemented: diagram_aspect_mismatch finding now carries authored/effective/cell(pre-fit)/render(post-fit) aspect evidence + fit_adjusted, distinguishing authoring mistakes from fit-driven render mismatches. Signature takes cellBounds+renderBounds; trigger compares authored vs post-fit frame; unset/partial dims still nil. Updated docs (FIT_FINDINGS.md, FINDINGS.md, finding_meta.go) and tests (unset, both-set, fit-mode cases).

title: SVG: Propagate template body font into placeholder diagrams and dry-render
description:
Location: cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go:517; cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go:982; internal/generator/media.go:1096; internal/generator/slides.go:47; cmd/json2pptx/fit_findings_chart_dryrender.go:76

Problem: shape-grid diagram cells receive GridDiagramContext.FontFamily and inject the template body font when diagram style omits font_family. Placeholder/slide-level diagram rendering injects theme colors and data palette but not the active template body font. Dry-render findings likewise do not consistently receive the same font context.

Root cause: template font context is threaded only through GridDiagramContext, while GenerationRequest/renderDiagramSpecFull lacks an equivalent body-font field or shared style resolver.

Impact: Templates with distinct typography can still render placeholder diagrams with svggen defaults, so the fix for diagram-cell fonts is incomplete at deck level. Dry-render label findings may also be measured under a different font than real rendering.

Implementation notes: Thread template body font through placeholder diagram render and chart dry-render paths using the same diagram style resolver as shape-grid diagrams. Only set it when the diagram spec does not explicitly provide style.font_family.
acceptance_criteria: Placeholder diagrams inherit the active template body font when style.font_family is unset; explicit diagram font_family still wins; dry-render uses the same font context as render; tests generate/inspect equivalent placeholder diagrams across two templates with distinct body fonts and assert emitted SVG font-family differs appropriately.
close_reason: Implemented: thread template body font into placeholder/slide-level diagram render (resolveDiagramWithMetadata via ctx.themeFontName), shape-grid diagram cells (new GridDiagramContext.FontFamily, populated in json_mode/mcp/per-slide contexts), and chart/diagram dry-render (collectChartDryRenderFindings -> dryRenderSpecToFindings now sets req.Style.FontFamily). Font is injected only when style.font_family is unset; explicit diagram font_family still wins. Added regression tests in internal/generator (placeholder path) and cmd/json2pptx (shape-grid path) asserting emitted SVG font-family differs across two distinct body fonts and that explicit font wins.

title: Improve template QA stress JSON grid slides
description: Revise the template QA stress JSON after visual inspection: make the grid layouts more complex/full-page and replace weak pattern slides that only cover half-page or render nonsensical top-down triangle geometry.
close_reason: Reworked template QA JSON after wireframe visual inspection; slides 8-10 now use full-page native shape grids with embedded svggen diagrams and inline SVG icons; all bundled templates generate under strict output validation.

title: Stress test installed deck skill across all templates
description: Install the in-repo Claude Code skills and run a generation/validation stress test using every bundled PPTX template.
close_reason: Installed skills and generated strict-validation stress decks for all bundled templates; raster pass blocked by missing LibreOffice.

title: Add --json-output-report as a non-breaking alias for --json-output
description:
Source: magarida-test.md S-2 (Note/Suggestion).

Problem: The --json-output flag on the generate command
(cmd/json2pptx/generate.go L20) outputs a structured result report (success,
warnings, quality score), not the PPTX itself. The name could imply 'output
the result as JSON' vs 'output a report in JSON format'.

Note: a direct rename is a breaking change for existing scripts/integrations,
so we add a non-breaking alias and deprecate the old name.

Debate:
- Advocate: Add --json-output-report as the clear name, keep --json-output as
  a deprecated alias, and update docs to prefer the new spelling.
- Devil's Advocate: Two names for one flag add long-term surface area.
- Resolution: Add the alias and mark the old flag deprecated in help text
  for now. Deleting the old name can be a later breaking-change decision.
design:
Use one backing variable with two flag registrations.
If both flags are set, allow identical values and reject differing values.
Update README examples and runGenerate usage text in the same change.
acceptance_criteria:
- generate accepts both --json-output and --json-output-report, writing the same manifest/report file.
- Help text and README examples prefer --json-output-report; conflicting values produce a clear error.
- Verification: go test ./cmd/json2pptx -run 'TestGenerateJSONOutputFlagAliases|TestGenerate_JSONOutputManifest' -count=1
close_reason: Implemented: added --json-output-report as the preferred name for generate's JSON result report, kept --json-output as a deprecated alias backed by the same destination. Conflicting values across the two flags produce a clear error. Updated help text, README flags table/examples, and SKILL.md to prefer the new spelling; added TestGenerateJSONOutputFlagAliases.

title: Add an install-method decision table to README
description:
Source: magarida-test.md D-6 (Severity: Low).

Problem: README.md L130-177 shows make install, install.sh, and install.ps1
as parallel install paths. There's also scripts/install-dist.sh for
distribution archives. It's unclear which method a new user should use and
when.

Debate:
- Advocate: Add a simple decision table: source checkout vs release archive,
  Unix vs Windows, full install vs binary-only.
- Devil's Advocate: Installation docs can become overly verbose fast.
- Resolution: Add one short decision matrix and mark a default
  recommendation per environment. Keep all methods, but explain when each
  exists.
design:
Edit README.md; optionally add one clarifying sentence in the script headers if needed.
Suggested table columns: 'You have', 'Recommended command', 'What it does'.
Do not rewrite the installer scripts in this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- README install section tells users which install path is recommended for source checkouts vs prebuilt release archives.
- The distinction between install.sh and scripts/install-dist.sh (and Windows equivalents) is explicit.
- Verification: go test ./cmd/json2pptx -run TestReadmeListsAllMCPTools -count=1
close_reason: Implemented: Added 'Which method should I use?' decision table to README install section covering source checkout vs prebuilt archive across Unix/Windows/Docker, with an explicit note distinguishing the source-checkout install.sh (builds from source) from scripts/install-dist.sh staged into release archives as install.sh (installs prebuilt binary, no toolchain).

title: Make template docs canonical and link to them from AGENTS/CLAUDE
description:
Source: magarida-test.md D-2 (Severity: Medium).

Problem: Template structure, placeholder IDs, layout requirements, and
content types are partially duplicated across:
  skills/template-deck/TEMPLATE_GUIDE.md (~560 lines) — agent-facing
  docs/TEMPLATE_SPEC.md (~187 lines) — contributor-facing
  AGENTS.md L27-48 — shape grid typography hierarchy
  CLAUDE.md L142-175 — named patterns table

A contributor looking for template requirements finds conflicting levels of
detail across files.

Debate:
- Advocate: Declare canonical docs by audience. Replace duplicated prose
  elsewhere with links.
- Devil's Advocate: Some duplication in CLAUDE.md is intentional for agent
  convenience.
- Resolution: Keep short summary pointers where needed, but move substantive
  template rules out of secondary docs.
design:
Trim CLAUDE.md template prose down to a short 'see these docs' section.
Keep skills/template-deck/TEMPLATE_GUIDE.md and docs/TEMPLATE_SPEC.md as the substantive sources.
If helpful, add a tiny 'Which template doc should I read?' note in README.md or CONTRIBUTING.md.
acceptance_criteria:
- One canonical doc is named for template usage and one for template authoring/validation.
- Secondary docs (at least CLAUDE.md, optionally AGENTS.md) link to those canonical docs instead of restating detailed template rules.
- Verification: go test ./... -count=1
close_reason: Implemented: declared skills/template-deck/TEMPLATE_GUIDE.md canonical for template usage and docs/TEMPLATE_SPEC.md canonical for authoring/validation, with cross-link headers in each. CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md now link to the canonical docs instead of restating template rules; added a 'Which template doc?' note and a TEMPLATE_GUIDE.md docs-index entry to README.

title: Collapse SLIDE_FORMAT.md into a redirect to docs/INPUT_FORMAT.md
description:
Source: magarida-test.md D-1 (Severity: High — repeat info, confusion).

Problem: SLIDE_FORMAT.md (3.9 KB) and docs/INPUT_FORMAT.md (11.7 KB) both
describe the JSON input model: top-level structure, slide objects, and all
content types. README.md again repeats this in the JSON Input Format section.

Maintaining two near-duplicate tutorials increases drift risk for a
user-facing contract that already has a canonical schema source.

Debate:
- Advocate: Reduce SLIDE_FORMAT.md to a short redirect/quick pointer to
  docs/INPUT_FORMAT.md and the live schema. One canonical tutorial is enough.
- Devil's Advocate: The short quickstart is useful for readers who do not
  want the longer doc. Removing it entirely may reduce approachability.
- Resolution: Keep SLIDE_FORMAT.md as a tiny stub, not a second tutorial.
  Point at docs/INPUT_FORMAT.md and get_input_schema.
design:
Edit SLIDE_FORMAT.md, README.md, and any obvious inbound links (docs/INPUT_FORMAT.md, tests/integration docs if needed).
Preserve the get_input_schema reference so the doc still passes the schema-doctor expectation.
Do not add new input-format content in this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- SLIDE_FORMAT.md becomes a short redirect-style page rather than a second tutorial.
- Links that currently point at SLIDE_FORMAT.md are updated where a canonical tutorial link is more appropriate.
- Verification: go test ./cmd/json2pptx -run TestSchemaDocsDoctor -count=1
close_reason: Implemented: collapsed SLIDE_FORMAT.md into a short redirect stub pointing at docs/INPUT_FORMAT.md and get_input_schema; repointed inbound links in README.md, docs/INPUT_FORMAT.md, tests/integration/README.md, and code comments in enums.go/skill_info.go. TestSchemaDocsDoctor passes.

title: Add a neutral alias for the testrand toolbox
description:
Source: magarida-test.md I-5 (Severity: Low).

Problem: cmd/testrand/main.go presents testrand as a random E2E generator,
but subcommands visual, validate, and qa are systematic utilities, not random
generation. Only generate and svg-stress are randomized. The current name
undersells a multi-purpose test toolbox and makes non-random functionality
harder to discover.

Debate:
- Advocate: Introduce a neutral alias such as testkit while keeping testrand
  as a compatibility name. Fixes discoverability without breaking scripts.
- Devil's Advocate: Even a soft rename adds docs/build churn and two names
  to support.
- Resolution: Add a preferred alias but keep testrand working unchanged.
  Update help text and docs to describe the tool as a test toolbox.
design:
Build the same ./cmd/testrand package under a second output name; no new command package is required.
Use filepath.Base(os.Args[0]) if you want usage text to reflect the invoked binary name.
Update scripts/docs to prefer the alias gradually; do not remove testrand.
acceptance_criteria:
- A neutral alias binary is buildable from the existing cmd/testrand package without changing subcommand behavior.
- Docs/help present the tool as a broader test toolbox and keep testrand as a compatibility name.
- Verification: go build -o /tmp/testkit ./cmd/testrand && /tmp/testkit help >/dev/null
close_reason: Implemented: added testkit as a neutral alias binary built from cmd/testrand (Makefile MAIN_CMDS); usage text now reflects the invoked binary name via filepath.Base(os.Args[0]) and reframes the tool as a test toolbox while keeping testrand as a compatibility name. Updated README + added regression test.

title: Route e2e visual rendering through pptx2jpg
description:
Source: magarida-test.md I-4 (Severity: Medium — consistency).

Problem: Three PPTX-to-image paths exist today:
  cmd/pptx2jpg/main.go             LibreOffice -> PDF -> convert -> JPG
  scripts/e2e_visual_test.sh       LibreOffice -> PDF -> pdftoppm (or convert)
  cmd/json2pptx/render_cmd.go      LibreOffice -> PDF -> magick -> PNG

scripts/test_template_visual_qa.sh already standardizes on pptx2jpg, but
e2e_visual_test.sh maintains its own conversion implementation. That drift
makes dependency troubleshooting and image-output differences harder to
reason about — and may yield divergent visual-QA results.

Debate:
- Advocate: Make scripts/e2e_visual_test.sh call pptx2jpg instead of
  hand-rolling LibreOffice + pdftoppm. Immediately removes one divergent
  path with minimal code risk.
- Devil's Advocate: pptx2jpg and json2pptx render still differ internally,
  so this does not fully standardize the stack.
- Resolution: Standardize the script first because it is the smallest correct
  change with immediate payoff. Deeper library-level unification can wait.
design:
Edit scripts/e2e_visual_test.sh; reuse the same pptx2jpg build/invocation pattern as scripts/test_template_visual_qa.sh.
If downstream tooling depends on <template>-slide-<n>.jpg, rename emitted files after conversion or adjust the temporary PPTX basename.
Do not change internal/render in this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- scripts/e2e_visual_test.sh no longer shells out to pdftoppm directly for slide conversion.
- The script preserves its existing report/input contract, including stable per-slide image naming.
- Verification: go test ./cmd/pptx2jpg -count=1 && TEST_MODE=random ./scripts/e2e_visual_test.sh
close_reason: Implemented: scripts/e2e_visual_test.sh now routes PPTX->JPG through cmd/pptx2jpg (built in Step 1) instead of hand-rolling LibreOffice + pdftoppm/convert. Preserves report contract (generated.pptx/generated.pdf) and stable per-slide naming by renaming pptx2jpg's generated-slide-<n>.jpg to <template>-slide-<n>.jpg (0-indexed). go test ./cmd/pptx2jpg passes; script verified to build+invoke pptx2jpg correctly (conversion itself needs LibreOffice+ImageMagick, absent on this box).

title: Peel MCP server bootstrap out of mcp.go
description:
Source: magarida-test.md I-2 — second atom.

Problem: cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go is 2614 lines and currently mixes server
bootstrap (runMCP, hooks, registration), config plumbing, tool constructors,
and large handlers. The package already shows a better pattern with separate
files such as mcp_preview.go, mcp_repair.go, and mcp_make_deck.go.

A first split that isolates server/bootstrap concerns is low-risk and makes
later handler extractions easier.

Debate:
- Advocate: Move mcpConfig, runMCP, and registerMCPTools into dedicated
  files so mcp.go stops being the default dumping ground. Safest first cut
  because it touches orchestration, not business logic.
- Devil's Advocate: A small bootstrap split may barely reduce the file and
  could feel cosmetic.
- Resolution: Start with bootstrap/registry extraction because it is
  cohesive and behavior-stable. Do not try to split all handlers in one bead.
design:
Create mcp_server.go / mcp_registry.go in cmd/json2pptx.
Move mcpConfig, runMCP, registration, and nearby non-domain helpers such as bootstrap hooks there.
Leave large handlers in place for now; preserve existing function names to minimize churn.
acceptance_criteria:
- MCP server bootstrap, registration, and config wiring no longer live in cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go.
- Tool registration order and runtime behavior are unchanged.
- Verification: go test ./cmd/json2pptx -count=1
close_reason: Implemented: extracted mcpConfig/resolvePresentationURLs/runMCP into mcp_server.go and registerMCPTools into mcp_registry.go; mcp.go no longer holds server bootstrap, config wiring, or tool registration. Registration order and runtime behavior preserved verbatim. Updated two tests that parsed mcp.go by name (catalog test -> mcp_registry.go, compact-responses drift test -> mcp_server.go).

title: Extract rhythm analysis into internal/rhythm
description:
Source: magarida-test.md I-1 — atomized.

Problem: cmd/json2pptx/analyze_rhythm.go (~655 lines) mixes MCP tool schema,
response DTOs, slide fingerprinting, run detection, accent-balance logic, and
recommendations. score_deck.go also calls analyzeDeckRhythm, so the logic is
already reused indirectly inside package main.

Pulling the analysis engine into internal/rhythm would reduce hidden coupling
and make future scoring/refinement work easier.

Debate:
- Advocate: Extract the pure analysis engine and its result types, then have
  both analyze-rhythm and score call the same internal/rhythm package. One
  source of truth for composition analysis.
- Devil's Advocate: The current code works directly on SlideInput, so a
  package split may require an adapter layer or duplicate input structs.
- Resolution: Add a minimal package-local input model in internal/rhythm and
  a thin adapter from SlideInput in cmd/json2pptx. Keeps the package boundary
  explicit without moving the entire JSON schema first.
design:
Create internal/rhythm with Analyze([]Slide) *Result.
Model only the fields the analyzer actually needs: slide type, pattern name, content kinds, grid cells, accent hints.

title: Extract deck-planning core into internal/deckplan

- Devil's Advocate: Template-support annotation currently lives near MCP

title: Document Beads as opt-in local workflow state
description:
Source: magarida-test.md B-2 (Severity: Low) — split into 2 atomic beads.

Problem: The repo root contains .beads/ (with .beads-credential-key, .gitignore)
plus local Beads state, while AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md both assume 'bd prime' is
already usable. README.md has no Beads setup note, so new contributors cannot
tell whether .beads/ is committed state, optional local state, or something
they must initialize themselves.

That ambiguity causes onboarding churn and encourages accidental assumptions
about local issue-tracker data.

Evidence (verified 2026-05-21):
  .beads/ exists locally but is gitignored
  bd list returns 'No issues found' on a fresh checkout
  AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md both contain BEGIN BEADS INTEGRATION blocks
  No setup pointer in README.md

Debate:
- Advocate: Add one short contributor-facing section that says Beads is
  optional local workflow state, explains when to run it, and points at the
  setup command. Resolves ambiguity without touching runtime state.
- Devil's Advocate: If the team actually wants shared Beads state in-repo,
  documenting it as optional could cement the wrong policy.
- Resolution: Document the current lowest-risk behavior: Beads is opt-in local
  workflow state unless explicitly required by a task. Do not try to version
  the live .beads/ database in this bead.
design:
Add a small 'Beads workflow (optional)' section to CONTRIBUTING.md; optionally add a one-line pointer from README.md.
Reference .beads/README.md as background, but make the tracked contributor doc the canonical onboarding source.
Keep this bead docs-only; do not change .beads/ contents or git-tracking policy.
acceptance_criteria:
- README or CONTRIBUTING clearly states whether Beads is required for normal build/test work and how a contributor opts in.
- The docs explain that .beads/ contains local workflow state and should not be assumed present in every clone.
- Verification: go test ./... -count=1
close_reason: Implemented: added 'Beads Workflow (Optional)' section to CONTRIBUTING.md stating Beads is opt-in local workflow state (not required to build/test, .beads/ is gitignored and absent in fresh clones, how to opt in) and a one-line pointer note from README.md Contributing section; references .beads/README.md as background

title: Migrate HTTP serve-mode error responses to FindingEnvelope
description:
Surface migration split from go-slide-creator-b15n. Depends on go-slide-creator-xqmd.

CHANGE: internal/api/errors/errors.go Response {success, error{code,message,details}} is written by ~36 handler sites (convert.go, templates.go, patterns.go, download.go, server.go) via apierrors.Write. Pattern-validation already flattens diagnostics into details.validation_errors (patterns.go writePatternValidationError). DESIGN DECISION: unify on FindingEnvelope. Either replace Response with the envelope (big blast radius across all handlers + tests) or carry a findings[] envelope for diagnostic-bearing endpoints (convert validation, pattern validation) while keeping the simple error shape for transport errors (415/413/504). Recommend the latter to bound scope.

LOCKSTEP TESTS: internal/api/contract_test.go, errors/errors_test.go, convert_test.go, patterns_test.go, templates_test.go, download_test.go, server_test.go.

ACCEPTANCE: diagnostic-bearing HTTP endpoints emit a FindingEnvelope; transport-only errors documented; tests + lint pass.
close_reason: Implemented: HTTP serve-mode pattern validation (POST /api/v1/patterns/{name}/validate and /expand) now emits diagnostics.FindingEnvelope as the response body (subcommand validate_pattern/expand_pattern, pattern name carried on each finding's evidence.pattern) instead of the legacy apierrors.Response with details.validation_errors. Transport/request errors (convert, JSON-parse, 404/415/413/504/500) keep the simple Response shape per the bounded-scope design recommendation. Lockstep tests migrated: contract_test.go, patterns_test.go. Docs synced: AGENT_DIAGNOSTICS.md, docs/api/openapi.yaml (added FindingEnvelope+Finding schemas, removed unemitted PATTERN_VALIDATION_FAILED from ErrorDetail enum), docs/api/README.md. SKILL.md unaffected (documents MCP/CLI, not HTTP serve mode).

comments.author: platon2001
comments.text: DESIGN DECISION (bounded scope per task recommendation): The only HTTP serve-mode endpoint that produces structured []diagnostics.Diagnostic today is pattern validation (writePatternValidationError, shared by POST /patterns/{name}/validate and /expand). Migrating that path to emit a diagnostics.FindingEnvelope as the response body. All other HTTP errors — convert request/content validation, JSON parse, unsupported-field, and transport errors (404/415/413/504/500) — keep the simple apierrors.Response {success,error{code,message,details}} shape and are documented as transport/request errors. Rationale: (1) convert builds ad-hoc typed errors, not diagnostics; converting it would either split /convert into two shapes (confusing) or rewrite the 32KB convert_test.go (the big blast radius the task says to avoid); (2) keeping each surface internally consistent (pattern=envelope, convert=Response) is cleaner than per-error-code shape switching. Lockstep tests touched: contract_test.go, patterns_test.go. Docs synced: AGENT_DIAGNOSTICS.md, docs/api/openapi.yaml, docs/api/README.md. SKILL.md unaffected (it documents MCP/CLI, not HTTP serve mode).
