title: Finish canonical-taxonomy adoption in cmd heuristics + extract placeholder-role aliases to a shared low-level package
description:
Follow-up to go-slide-creator-a3jh, which landed the canonical classifier (template.ClassifyLayoutCanonical / ClassifyPlaceholderRole / DerivableLayouts), persisted types.LayoutMetadata.CanonicalType + types.PlaceholderInfo.Role in ParseLayouts, and adopted EffectiveCanonicalType in cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go resolveVirtualLayout.

Remaining from a3jh deliverable 5 + NOTES:
1. Migrate cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go applyChromeSkip from raw layout.Tags ("title-slide"/"closing") to canonical type. NOTE the behavior divergence: a section-divider title-only layout currently carries the structural "title-slide" tag and is skipped today, but classifies canonically as Section Divider. Decide intended chrome-skip semantics for section dividers before migrating, and keep tag-based matching for caller-supplied arbitrary skip tags.
2. Audit other heuristic/tag selection sites (layout/, pipeline/, recommend_visual) and route them through types.CanonicalLayoutType where 1:1 equivalent.
3. Extract the placeholder-role alias sets (section_number aliases in internal/generator.placeholder_resolver.go and the eyebrow/subtitle/chrome hints duplicated in internal/template/canonical.go) into a lower-level internal package shared by both, so internal/template never depends on internal/generator (per a3jh NOTES). Currently the 3-entry section_number alias set is duplicated in canonical.go.

Acceptance: applyChromeSkip + audited sites use the canonical taxonomy; alias sets live in one shared package; all gates green.
close_reason:
Finished canonical-taxonomy adoption in cmd heuristics + extracted placeholder-role aliases to a shared leaf package.

(1) applyChromeSkip (cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go) migrated from raw layout.Tags to template.EffectiveCanonicalType for the two well-known skip names: 'title'->CanonicalLayoutTitleSlide, 'closing'->CanonicalLayoutClosing. DECISION on the section-divider divergence: a title-only Section Divider carries the structural 'title-slide' tag and used to be skipped, but classifies canonically as Section Divider and is now KEPT in the numbered body flow by default — which matches the already-documented SKILL.md contract ('auto-suppressed on title and closing slides', default skip [title,closing]). So this fixes drift rather than introducing it. Arbitrary caller-supplied skip values still match structural layout.Tags, so ['section-header'] can opt section dividers back out. Regression test added (chrome_skip_test.go).

(2) Audit of other tag/heuristic selection sites: internal/layout/heuristic.go (~15 fine-grained tags: title-hidden, title-at-bottom, quote, statement, big-number, agenda, timeline-capable, icon-grid, content, two-column, comparison, full-image, blank, thank-you, ...) and internal/layout/canonical.go (canonicalNames require/exclude/nameHint alias resolution) are intentionally NOT 1:1 with the coarse 7-type taxonomy and operate on tag-only inputs (CanonicalType unpopulated in tests/synthesized paths) — routing them through types.CanonicalLayoutType would change scoring and break the heuristic suite. internal/pipeline and recommend_visual do no layout-tag selection. Conclusion recorded in a doc-comment in internal/layout/canonical.go. applyChromeSkip was the one clean 1:1 site.

(3) Extracted the section_number alias set + eyebrow/subtitle/date/page-number/footer name hints + the section-number font threshold into new stdlib-only leaf package internal/placeholderrole, shared by internal/generator (resolver) and internal/template (canonical classifier). Removes the duplicated 3-entry alias map and keeps internal/template free of any internal/generator dependency. generator.IsSectionNumberAlias retained as a thin re-export for existing cmd/test callers. SKILL.md page_numbers.skip note clarified.

Gates: go build/vet ./... clean; affected packages (placeholderrole, template, layout, generator, cmd/json2pptx) tests pass; svggen tests pass; new files lint clean; only pre-existing failures remain (TestSVGFixtures_Sizes uj0j; lint debt rn7d/ks40, none in changed files).

title: Return structured manifests for CLI commands that write files
description: Several CLI file-write modes succeed only through logs or stderr, which is weak for agents. Standardize JSON success manifests for commands such as preview-wireframe --out, preview-icon --out-svg/--out-png, preview-patterns, and generate without requiring agents to scrape logs.

Human-friendly stdout/stderr remains available but is not the only machine-readable result.
close_reason: Implemented: shared WriteManifest type (path/kind/bytes/sha256 + warnings) and --manifest flag for preview-wireframe, preview-icon, preview-patterns; generate already returns this via --json-output (output_path/content_hash/warnings). title: Make render thumbnail and slide image artifacts collision-free
description: render_slide_image and render_deck_thumbnails can expose temp paths such as /tmp/json2pptx-slide-0.png or /tmp/json2pptx-thumb-0.png that later renders can overwrite. Agents using those paths for visual QA need stable artifact identity. Store large render outputs under content-addressed or deck-scoped paths and return hashes/manifests.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated concurrent or sequential render_slide_image/render_deck_thumbnails calls for different decks never return the same mutable path unless content hash is identical. Responses include artifact path, content hash, source deck identity or input hash, slide index, and expiration/cleanup semantics. Tests cover two decks rendering the same slide index without path collision.
close_reason: Implemented: content-addressed render artifacts. Large render_slide_image/render_deck_thumbnails/render_slide_image_from_json(+overlay) outputs now write to <render-cache>/artifacts/slide-<sha256>.png instead of index-keyed /tmp paths, so two decks at the same slide index never collide and a path is reused only when bytes are identical. SlideImage gains content_hash, source_hash, and cleanup fields; output schemas + TOOLS.md + SCHEMA_CHANGELOG updated; SchemaVersion bumped 4.41.0->4.42.0. Added 4 render-pkg regression tests incl. two-decks-same-index collision test.

It avoids assigning impossible layouts/patterns where a supported alternative exists, and tests prove plan_deck and recommend_visual agree for the same template constraints.
close_reason: Implemented: plan_deck accepts optional template context and reuses the shared generator.TemplateSupportContext helper (the same one recommend_visual uses) to annotate each planned slide and alternative with template_support {status, reasons[], required_layout}; recommended patterns the template cannot host are swapped for supported alternatives; result echoes the vetted template. title: Add pure apply_deck_patch MCP primitive
description: Agents need a primitive way to add, remove, move, duplicate, or replace deck JSON sections after scoring and inspection without invoking a repair workflow. Add apply_deck_patch or patch_deck as a pure MCP transform that accepts full deck JSON plus a limited JSON Pointer/RFC6902-style op list and returns patched JSON plus validation/preflight findings. Do not add persistent workspace CRUD in this bead.
acceptance_criteria: MCP apply_deck_patch supports bounded operations for slide insert, remove, replace, move, duplicate, and field replace. It validates paths, rejects unsafe or schema-breaking patches with structured findings, returns patched_deck without writing files by default, and exposes schemas/capabilities/tool classification. Tests cover pruning, reordering, duplicating, and replacing a slide before regenerate.
close_reason: Implemented: apply_deck_patch pure MCP transform primitive — bounded ops (insert/remove/replace/move/duplicate slide + RFC6901 field replace), atomic with structured rejection findings, returns patched_deck + FindingEnvelope without writing files; registered in catalog/constructors/tool_list with output schema; SchemaVersion 4.46.0 + fingerprint bumped; SKILL/TOOLS/changelog synced; tests cover prune/reorder/duplicate/replace + regenerate + atomic/schema-break rejection

title: Add reverse CLI-to-MCP parity gate for agent-facing commands

title: checkSectionNumberNaming validator never fires because its MaxChars<5 gate relies on the broken estimate
description:
cmd/json2pptx/validate_template.go:378 (checkSectionNumberNaming) is supposed to warn when a section-header layout has a body-typed placeholder that looks like a decorative number frame but is misnamed. Its trigger requires ALL of:
  - PlaceholderType == body
  - MaxChars < 5
  - FontSize > 4000 (>40pt)
  - Y in upper third
  - name != "Section Number"

Because estimateMaxChars is FontSize-oblivious (see sister bead on layouts.go:246-272), every actually-decorative section-number placeholder reports MaxChars in the 140-300 range — never < 5. So the MaxChars gate fails first and the validator is silently a no-op.

This means a template author can ship a new template whose decorative number placeholder is named e.g. "TextBox 7" instead of "Section Number", and the engine will treat it as body text and fill it with section-title prose. The validator we wrote precisely to catch this case never fires. It is the inverse of the user's complaint: today agents stuff text into Section Number frames; tomorrow they could overwrite an unnamed decorative frame because the validator failed to flag it.

Fix: after estimateMaxChars is fixed to be FontSize-aware, this validator will start working. As an immediate safety net, also detect the inverse pattern: body placeholder where FontSize > minFontSize AND Y is in upper third AND name is not "Section Number" — without requiring MaxChars<5 — and emit a warning. Add a unit test using a synthetic layout to confirm the validator now triggers.
acceptance_criteria: Either after fixing FontSize-aware estimateMaxChars the existing heuristic triggers on a synthetic misnamed decorative number layout, OR the heuristic is loosened to not require MaxChars<5. Unit test added that constructs a section-header layout with a misnamed body placeholder at 100pt in the top third and asserts a warning is produced.
close_reason: Loosened checkSectionNumberNaming: dropped the MaxChars<5 gate so the validator fires on misnamed decorative section-number frames regardless of width. Trigger is now section-header layout + body type + FontSize>40pt + upper-third + name != 'Section Number'. Added acceptance test (100pt misnamed frame) and wide-banner safety-net test; updated below-thresholds test to drop the now-invalid large-MaxChars no-warning case. Verified bundled templates still emit no false positives.

title: modern-yellow Section Divider geometry is title-at-bottom but title and body placeholder roles are flipped relative to size
description:
modern-yellow.pptx Section Divider layout (tags: content, title-at-bottom, section-header) has:
- "Section Number" type=body  FontSize=20800 (208pt)  Y=814,389    H=2,614,612 → top of slide, very large
- "Title 4"        type=title FontSize=4800  (48pt)   Y=4,433,888  H=1,516,062 → bottom of slide, small

The layout intends a giant number at the top with a small section title below. But:
1. The title slot at the bottom only has H=1,516,062 EMU (~1.6"), so any multi-line section title overflows.
2. The agent-facing metadata still reports the title placeholder normally, and the user sees "title-at-bottom" tag only via metadata.tags, with no semantic hint that the title's character capacity is small. estimateMaxChars reports 275 chars for the title, but visually only ~30 chars fit.
3. The bottom-of-slide title placement combined with modern-yellow's other overlap issues (see go-slide-creator-3a29) means the title is the most truncation-prone area.

Root-cause fix:
1. Tighten modern-yellow's title placeholder bounds (or accept smaller text capacity in metadata) so MaxChars reflects what visually fits at the rendered FontSize once item P1 (FontSize-aware estimateMaxChars) is fixed.
2. Add a layout tag like "compact-title" or a metadata hint surfacing that the title slot is small, so agents can plan accordingly.
3. Document the title-at-bottom convention in docs/INPUT_FORMAT.md so JSON authors know the title and decorative number visual order is reversed.
acceptance_criteria: On modern-yellow Section Divider, the title placeholder's MaxChars (after FontSize-aware estimate) reflects realistic single-line capacity; documented as title-at-bottom; planning heuristics avoid sending long section titles to this layout, or the layout is updated to give the title slot more room.
notes: Agent-native review: this depends on canonical roles and font-aware capacity. The fix should surface compact title/title-at-bottom semantics in template metadata so plan_deck, recommend_visual, preflight, and examine-template can avoid placing long section titles into a visually small title slot.
close_reason: Implemented: modern-yellow Section Divider compact-title hint. Dependencies (a3jh role classifier, sjzb font-aware estimateMaxChars) already fixed the misleading capacity (title now reports max_chars=30, Section Number=1). Added a 'compact-title' structural layout tag in internal/template/classifier.go that fires when a title-at-bottom layout's visible title slot only fits a short single-line title (max_chars < 35) — fires on exactly modern-yellow's Section Divider across the whole corpus, zero false positives. Documented the title-at-bottom convention in docs/INPUT_FORMAT.md and the new tag in skills/template-deck/TEMPLATE_GUIDE.md + skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md. Added unit + corpus regression tests.

title: Title placeholder IDs are not harmonized across templates (title vs Title 1 vs Title 4 vs Title 123)
description:
Per-template audit of title placeholder shape names (validate-template -json -verbose across templates/):
- abstract.pptx: mixes "title" and "Title 1"
- blue-corporate.pptx: mixes "Title 1" and "Title 123" (stray copy-paste name)
- business-template.pptx: "Title 1" only
- forest-green.pptx, midnight-blue.pptx, modern-template.pptx, warm-coral.pptx: "title" only
- modern-yellow.pptx: mixes "title" and "Title 4"
- modern.pptx: "Title 1" only

Consequence: JSON authors and agents cannot rely on a single placeholder_id for the title slot. A deck written for forest-green ("title") silently fails to populate the title on blue-corporate ("Title 1"). isTitlePlaceholderID() (cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go:2121) papers over some cases by accepting both, but agents reading template metadata see different IDs per template and produce inconsistent output. Also, "Title 123" is a stray PowerPoint default name that escaped into a shipped template.

Root-cause fix: run internal/template.NormalizePlaceholderNames over every shipped template so all title-typed placeholders normalize to the canonical "title" ID; commit the normalized PPTX files. Add a test that asserts every layout's title placeholder is named exactly "title" (case-sensitive) on disk.
acceptance_criteria: Every template in templates/ has all title-typed placeholders renamed to the canonical "title". "Title 1", "Title 4", "Title 123" do not appear. A unit test loads each template, parses layouts, and fails if any title placeholder name != "title".
notes: Agent-native review: scope this to on-disk template hygiene, validate-template, examine-template, and CI artifacts. Runtime normalization can paper over names, but agent-facing template evidence and future CI gates should see canonical title placeholder IDs on disk.
close_reason: Normalized title placeholders to canonical 'title' on disk across all shipped templates (abstract, blue-corporate, business-template, modern-yellow, modern via NormalizeLayoutBytes; forest-green/midnight-blue/modern-template/warm-coral already canonical). Removed stray 'Title 1'/'Title 4'/'Title 123' names. Embedded ppt/media assets preserved byte-for-byte. Added regression test TestTitlePlaceholdersAreCanonicalOnDisk asserting every layout's title placeholder is named exactly 'title' on disk.

title: Makefile dist-linux duplicates the non-recursive skill-copy bug from install-skill
description: Same root pattern as go-slide-creator-w5kw, in a second location. Makefile install-skill (lines 169-177) uses 'cp "$$skill_dir"* DEST/' which skips nested directories like skills/generate-deck/examples. The dist-linux target (Makefile ~lines 256-260) repeats the exact same shallow cp pattern when staging skills into dist/, so released tarballs ship with the same missing nested skill assets even after install-skill is patched. Fix both call sites together — replace with 'cp -R "$$skill_dir".' / DEST/' or rsync — and add a check that asserts skills/generate-deck/examples/ exists in the staged dist.

title: No-emoji policy lives in package main (cmd/json2pptx), preventing reuse by testrand and other producers
description: Architectural root cause for repeated emoji-in-corpus regressions (latest instance: go-slide-creator-6wnl). cmd/json2pptx/no_emoji.go defines ValidateNoEmojiInText / containsEmoji in package main, so internal/testrand and any future generator cannot import the same predicate to sanitize their output. Result: producers and validator drift, and policy violations are only caught at generate-time. Fix: move emoji detection (and the policy spec) into an importable internal package (e.g. internal/policy/emoji), keep cmd/json2pptx as a thin caller, and have internal/testrand sanitize its corpora through the same function so producers stay consistent with the enforcer by construction.
acceptance_criteria: ValidateNoEmojiInText / containsEmoji live in an internal package importable by both cmd/json2pptx and internal/testrand. testrand corpus generation routes string literals through the shared sanitizer (or unit test asserts the corpus passes the validator).
close_reason: Implemented: moved no-emoji policy (predicate, sanitizer, validator) into importable internal/policy/emoji package. cmd/json2pptx now a thin caller (call sites + diagnostics adapter only); internal/testrand routes its edge corpus through emoji.Sanitize in maybeEdge and adds regression tests asserting both the random and visual decks pass emoji.ValidateNoEmojiInText, so producers stay consistent with the enforcer by construction.

title: shape_grid raw shapes always inserted at end of spTree, rendering on top of title placeholders
description: Amplifier root cause for go-slide-creator-3a29 (slide 7) and go-slide-creator-40to. internal/generator/output.go:738-752 inserts shape_grid raw XML via insertRawShapes(), which calls pptx.InsertIntoSpTree with InsertAtEnd. internal/pptx/sptree.go:29-35 documents that InsertAtEnd means visually on top. Consequence: even minor geometry intrusion into title space becomes a full visual cover-up because cards/charts paint over the title rather than being clipped behind it. Fix direction: default raw shape_grid insertion to InsertAtStart (under placeholders) — or introduce explicit z-order bands (background-grid, mid, overlay) and place grids in the background band. Native SVG icon pics that should sit on top of grid cells already insert later as a separate step (output.go:756+), so they remain on top.
acceptance_criteria: shape_grid raw shapes render behind native title/body placeholders by default. Existing tests for icon-on-grid stacking still pass. Visual diff shows grids no longer cover titles even when bounds are slightly off.
close_reason: Implemented: insertRawShapes now uses pptx.InsertAtStart so shape_grid raw shapes render behind native title/body placeholders instead of on top. Native SVG icon pics still insert later (InsertAtEnd) so they remain on top of grid cells. Added regression tests TestInsertRawShapes_BehindPlaceholders and TestInsertRawShapes_IconsRemainOnTop.

title: e2e visual runner exits before reporting generation failures
description: scripts/e2e_visual_test.sh uses set -e and captures json2pptx generate output in a command-substitution assignment. When generation fails, bash exits immediately from that assignment before GEN_STATUS is checked, so the script does not print the captured json2pptx error, update inspection_report.json, continue to later templates, or run its CREATE_BEADS_ISSUES failure path. This happened on the abstract template when the generated deck hit the no_emoji policy.
acceptance_criteria: Generation failures are captured and reported with the underlying stderr/stdout; the script records a per-template failure, continues to remaining templates, writes the combined report, and honors CREATE_BEADS_ISSUES when enabled.
close_reason: Implemented: made the json2pptx generate output capture in scripts/e2e_visual_test.sh tolerant of failure under 'set -e'. Replaced the bare GEN_OUTPUT=$(...) command-substitution assignment (which exited the script immediately on a non-zero generate) with 'GEN_STATUS=0; GEN_OUTPUT=$(...) || GEN_STATUS=$?', so generation failures now print the captured stderr/stdout, record a per-template failure result, continue to remaining templates, and run the CREATE_BEADS_ISSUES path. GEN_STATUS reset prevents a stale non-zero from a prior failed template leaking into a later success.

title: Approximate non-text shape_grid visual issues in validate_input preflight
description:
Why:
Agents benefit from catching visual problems before generation, but non-text grid-cell preflight is currently much weaker than the real render-time path. After the diagnostics contract and render-time findings are stable, the repo needs a separate decision about which non-text grid issues can be approximated reliably in `validate_input` without teaching agents false confidence.

Current facts confirmed in code:
- `cmd/json2pptx/fit_findings_collect.go` still estimates non-text grid cells with coarse defaults
- the debate concluded that render-time findings and static preflight should be separate implementation tracks
- some issues are only knowable during actual rendering, while others may be safe to approximate early

Scope:
- evaluate which diagram/icon/image grid-cell issues can be approximated reliably in `validate_input` and related preflight surfaces
- extend preflight only for the safe subset, reusing the harmonized finding codes/paths where possible
- clearly distinguish heuristic/preflight findings from render-time findings when confidence differs

Non-goals:
- do not block on full parity with generation-time findings
- do not invent repair semantics here; this issue is only about preflight detection quality

References:
- `cmd/json2pptx/fit_findings_collect.go`
- `cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go`
- `internal/patterns/fit_finding.go`
- `internal/diagnostics/diagnostic.go`

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- `validate_input` can emit harmonized findings for the safe subset of non-text grid issues that are approximable before rendering
- preflight findings reuse the shared path/code semantics where practical
- the implementation documents or encodes which classes remain render-time-only
- tests cover at least one approximated non-text grid finding and one intentionally render-time-only case

title: Map non-text grid visual findings to deterministic agent actions
description:
Why:
Actionable error messages require more than detection. Once non-text grid findings exist, the agent needs deterministic next actions where safe, while leaving ambiguous cases in review-only mode. Today that mapping is uneven across fit findings, visual QA categories, and svggen validation.

Current facts confirmed in code:
- `patterns.FitFinding` and `diagnostics.Diagnostic` can already carry `Fix` and `NextToolCall`
- `cmd/json2pptx/mcp_repair.go` already supports generic fix kinds such as `reshape_grid`, `swap_layout`, `replace_value`, and `use_semantic_color`
- `internal/visualqa/repair_map.go` already maps some visual categories to candidate fixes, but not around a unified non-text-grid findings contract

Scope:
- define which non-text visual findings can safely map to deterministic agent actions
- attach `Fix` and `NextToolCall` for those cases using existing generic repair kinds where possible
- leave unsupported or ambiguous findings in explicit review-only mode instead of inventing speculative fixes

Non-goals:
- do not invent broad media-specific mutation verbs unless existing repair kinds cannot express the action
- do not promise full auto-repair parity for every diagram/image/icon case

References:
- `internal/patterns/fit_finding.go`
- `internal/diagnostics/diagnostic.go`
- `cmd/json2pptx/mcp_repair.go`
- `internal/visualqa/repair_map.go`
acceptance_criteria:
- non-text visual findings that have deterministic source-side remediations carry `Fix` and `NextToolCall`
- existing repair kinds are reused wherever possible before adding new ones
- unsupported cases are explicitly marked review-only rather than pretending to be auto-fixable
- tests cover at least one grid-diagram action mapping and one case intentionally left without auto-fix semantics
close_reason: Mapped non-text grid visual findings to deterministic agent actions: diagram_clamped → swap_layout, grid_diagram_narrow → reshape_grid (already had Fix, now verified NextToolCall attachment), diagram_render_failed → explicit review-only Fix. Added IsReviewOnly() and ReviewOnlyCategories for image_quality/aspect_ratio/border_style. Updated SKILL.md, FIT_FINDINGS.md, and skill sync doctor.

title: Add placement and host-strategy guidance to recommend_visual from capability truth
description:
Why:
`recommend_visual` can rank charts, diagrams, patterns, and layouts, but it cannot tell an agent where a winning candidate should live or how that candidate should be authored safely. Without capability-backed placement advice, agents still guess when to use placeholder content, native-shape diagrams, or SVG-in-grid composition.

Current facts confirmed in code:
- `internal/patterns/recommend_visual.go` currently returns a flat candidate contract: category, name, score, rationale, confidence band
- `cmd/json2pptx/mcp_output_schemas.go` locks that narrow shape into the public MCP surface
- the debate concluded that render metadata must come from a placement-aware capability source, not a hard-coded second truth table inside the recommender

Scope:
- extend `recommend_visual` additively so candidates can reference capability truth and placement advice
- expose fields such as capability reference, preferred placement, host strategy, grid embeddability, or equivalent additive guidance that helps the agent choose the right authoring path
- keep ranking logic focused on routing; do not turn the recommender into a renderer-internals dump

Non-goals:
- do not redesign the ranking heuristics wholesale
- do not publish a misleading single `native=true` style field

title: Normalize shared runtime and template-settings semantics across entry points
description:
Even where surfaces expose similar features, the runtime semantics differ in ways that surprise agents. The audit found drift in named template-settings resolution, embedded-template sidecar handling, template discovery and search policy, output filename and retention semantics, asset resolution, and possible dead or inconsistent cache settings. A concrete example is that MCP resolves named template settings before generate and validate, while CLI generate or preview and HTTP follow different paths; another is that embedded-template settings can fall back into the current working directory when no settings directory is available.

Scope this task to shared runtime normalization under the hood. The goal is that equivalent inputs and template references behave the same way regardless of whether the call arrived through MCP, CLI, or HTTP. Keep discovery-schema fixes, HTTP contract honesty, and shape-grid rendering parity out of scope for this issue.

This is the implementation track that sets up a later internal deck or discovery layer without forcing that larger refactor into the immediate harmonization pass.
acceptance_criteria:
- Named template-settings resolution follows one shared code path across MCP, CLI, and HTTP where the feature is supported.
- Embedded-template settings no longer fall back to writing or reading from ambiguous current-working-directory locations.
- Output path, retention, and cleanup behavior are documented and consistent by surface.
- Tests cover at least one cross-surface template-settings scenario and one output-lifecycle scenario.
close_reason: Extracted resolveInputNamedSettingsForDir as shared standalone function; wired into CLI generate and dry-run paths; fixed embedded template CWD fallback; added cross-surface tests

title: Make PatternTaxonomy.DensityClass drive generation behavior, not just metadata
description:
PatternTaxonomy includes DensityClass ("low", "medium", "high") in internal/patterns/pattern.go:67-85, but this field is NEVER read during pattern expansion or generation. It is purely decorative metadata consumed only by show_pattern and analyze_deck_rhythm. When a "medium" density pattern like process-flow receives very short content, the system does not adjust bounds or suggest compact mode. The taxonomy metadata reads well but does not drive behavior.

SCOPE:
1. Add density-aware expansion logic to ExpandContext:
   - If pattern.DensityClass="medium" but computed density <15%, emit sparse warning
   - If pattern.DensityClass="high" but computed density <30%, emit underfill warning
2. In expand_pattern handler (cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:1480-1510), compare actual cell budgets against pattern's DensityClass expectation
3. If divergence exceeds threshold, emit capacity_warning with suggestion to:
   - Use compact variant if available
   - Add max_height_pct override
   - Switch to a different pattern with matching density class
4. Update recommend.go to use DensityClass as a constraint when selecting patterns (prefer patterns whose DensityClass matches estimated content density)
5. Add tests for density-class-aware recommendation and expansion

ROOT CAUSE: The taxonomy system was designed for agent discovery but never wired into generation. Making it active would prevent the 'medium-density pattern with low-density content' mismatch that causes sparse layouts.

ACCEPTANCE:
- DensityClass is used during expand_pattern to validate density expectations
- RecommendVisual considers content density hints when scoring patterns
- Warnings emitted when density diverges from pattern's DensityClass
- Warnings include actionable suggestions (compact variant, bounds override, pattern swap)
- Tests cover all three density classes
acceptance_criteria:
1. DensityClass drives expansion warnings
2. RecommendVisual considers density
3. Divergence warnings are actionable
4. Test coverage for all density classes
notes: This makes the taxonomy metadata actually useful. Without it, DensityClass is just a label. With it, the system can self-correct when content doesn't match the pattern's intended density.
close_reason: Implemented density-class-aware expansion warnings and recommendation scoring

title: Add hero-detail pattern for big-stat + supporting bullets layout
description:
A common consulting slide layout is a large hero statistic at the top with 2-3 supporting detail bullets below.    - Row 2: N columns for detail cards (occupies ~60% height)

5. Register with taxonomy: DensityClass="low", Category="hero", NarrativeRole=["evidence"], PairsWith=["kpi-3up", "chart"]

title: Make compose envelope content-aware with density-based segment sizing
description:
The compose envelope merges multiple pattern grids vertically or horizontally via mergeVertical/mergeHorizontal (cmd/json2pptx/compose.go:125-179). It distributes heights by explicit SizePct or equal splits. It has NO content-aware balancing — a stat-hero (one big number, ~5% density) + kpi-3up (three metrics, ~40% density) with equal splits wastes space because the hero takes 50% height even though it only needs ~20%.

SCOPE:
1. After expanding each compose segment, compute computeGridOccupancy for each sub-grid (reuse mcp.go:1535-1598 logic)
2. Calculate content_height_emu / bounds_height_emu ratio for each segment
3. Use ratios to drive proportional sizing instead of equal splits when SizePct is not explicitly provided
4. Add SmartCompose flag to ComposeInput (default false for backward compatibility)
5. When SmartCompose=true, auto-balance segment heights based on actual content density
6. Ensure callout rows and connector rows are sized correctly in smart mode
7. Add test coverage for density-based balancing

ROOT CAUSE: The compose envelope is the agent's primary tool for combining patterns, but it cannot produce balanced slides because each pattern internally fills 100% of its allocated slice. Without smart sizing, the agent must manually tune SizePct.

ACCEPTANCE:
- stat-hero + kpi-3up compose produces balanced slide with hero taking ~25% and KPIs ~75%
- SmartCompose flag exists and defaults to false
- Equal splits still work when SmartCompose=false
- Explicit SizePct overrides smart sizing
- Tests cover at least 3 compose scenarios
acceptance_criteria:
1. SmartCompose flag added to ComposeInput
2. Density-based auto-balancing works
3. stat-hero+kpi-3up produces balanced slide
4. Backward compatibility preserved
5. Test coverage for compose scenarios
notes: This is a compose-level fix that mitigates the pattern rigidity issue at the composition layer. Even if individual patterns always fill their slice, smart compose can allocate slices proportionally.
close_reason: Implemented SmartCompose flag on ComposeInput with content-density-based segment sizing. When smart_compose=true and no explicit size_pct, segment heights are proportional to content cell count (e.g. stat-hero 1 cell → 25%, kpi-3up 3 cells → 75%). Backward compatible: defaults to false, explicit size_pct always overrides.

title: Add compact pattern variants: process-flow-compact, before-after-compact, kpi-inline
description:
Patterns like process-flow and before-after always expand to full_content_area (100% height) regardless of content length. When an agent has short content (3-6 steps, brief labels), the resulting blocks are comically tall with ~3-10% text density. The agent's only recourse is to abandon patterns entirely and hand-craft a shape_grid with custom bounds. This is a major abstraction leak.

SCOPE:
1. Add VariantSupport interface to internal/patterns/pattern.go with Variants() []PatternVariant and ExpandVariant()
2. Create internal/patterns/processflow_compact.go — process-flow variant with:
   - Same values schema as process-flow
   - Grid height capped at 30-40% of content area
   - Rest of slide available for callout/description
   - DensityClass: "low", TargetDensityPct: 0.25
3. Create internal/patterns/beforeafter_compact.go — before-after variant with:
   - Same values schema as before-after
   - Body row height capped at ~35% each
   - DensityClass: "low"
4. Create internal/patterns/kpi_inline.go — horizontal inline KPIs (not big cards):
   - Values: same as kpi-Nup but rendered as horizontal bar
   - Height: ~25% of content area
   - For decks where KPIs support a larger narrative, not hero slides
5. Register variants in default registry with aliases
6. Update recommend.go so short-content intents suggest compact variants

ROOT CAUSE: session-history.md:75-82, 87-92 — agent had to drop to raw shape_grid for both process-flow and before-after because full-height patterns produced sparse layouts.

ACCEPTANCE:
- process-flow-compact registered and expandable via expand_pattern
- before-after-compact registered and expandable
- kpi-inline registered and expandable
- All variants return reasonable density (>20%) with short content
- recommend.go suggests compact variants for low-density intents
- show_pattern for base patterns lists available variants
acceptance_criteria:

2. before-after-compact variant exists and works
3. kpi-inline variant exists and works
4. Short content produces >20% density in compact variants
5. Recommendation engine suggests compact variants appropriately

title: CI / pre-commit heuristic: fail when agent-facing surface changes without skill+docs updates
description:
## Why

The skill-code-docs sync policy bead establishes the rule; this bead enforces it mechanically. Without an automated check, the policy will erode the moment a contributor forgets — and the failure mode is silent agent regression, which is the worst kind.

## What

A CI step (and optional pre-commit hook) that runs on every PR / push:

1. Detect agent-facing surface changes by file/path heuristics:
   - cmd/json2pptx/*_cmd.go response struct shapes
   - cmd/json2pptx/skill_info.go output struct shapes
   - cmd/json2pptx/fit_report.go finding emission
   - internal/patterns/*Overrides struct fields and OverridesSchema
   - internal/types public types reachable from CLI/MCP responses

2. If any of those changed in the diff, require ONE of:
   - skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md was also modified, AND
   - docs/ relevant file (FIT_FINDINGS.md / PATTERNS.md / STYLE_DEFAULTS.md / INPUT_FORMAT.md) was also modified
   - OR a commit trailer 'Skill-Sync-Exempt: <reason>' is present, with reason >= 20 chars

3. Failure message must point to the policy bead and explain the rule succinctly.

4. False-positive escape hatch: the heuristic will sometimes flag pure refactors (e.g., field rename with no agent-visible change). Trailer-based exemption handles those; document the trailer in CLAUDE.md.

## Implementation notes

- Implement in .github/workflows/ci.yml as a small Go or shell tool, OR as a pre-commit hook script in scripts/
- Should run fast (file diff inspection only)
- Output specifies which files triggered the rule and which doc(s) it expected to be updated

## Acceptance criteria

- Check fails on a synthetic PR that adds a new finding code without touching SKILL.md / FIT_FINDINGS.md
- Check passes on a synthetic PR with both code and skill+docs updated
- Check passes on a synthetic PR with the Skill-Sync-Exempt trailer
- CLAUDE.md documents the exemption trailer format
- No specific patterns / templates / decks referenced

## Dependencies

Related to (does not block): the policy bead. File this once the policy bead is merged so CLAUDE.md exists to reference.
close_reason: Implemented: shell script check + CI job that fails when agent-facing surface changes lack SKILL.md/docs updates, with Skill-Sync-Exempt trailer escape hatch

title: Extend analyze_deck_rhythm with within-slide accent variety and density distribution
description:
## Why

cmd/json2pptx/analyze_rhythm.go tracks per-slide accent dominance (rhythmSlideInfo.AccentRole, accentBalance:62) and surfaces slide-level monotony. It is blind to two within-slide signals that drive perceived quality:
1. Whether a slide's cells use a single accent or several (visual hierarchy)
2. How many cells are underfilled / overflow across the deck (content-layout coupling)

Both signals are derivable from data the other beads will already produce; this bead surfaces them.

## What

Extend rhythmSlideInfo with:
- within_slide_accent_variety int — count of distinct accent slots used across the slide's shape_grid cells

Extend rhythmAggregates with:
- density_distribution: { underfilled_cells, optimal_cells, overflow_cells } — totals across the deck, computed by re-running textcapacity.ForResolvedGrid per slide and counting Status values

Extend rhythmRecommendation generation with two new rules:
- Slide has 5+ cells AND within_slide_accent_variety == 1 -> recommend cell_accent_mode: progressive
- Deck has >30% underfilled cells -> recommend adding detail or using smaller grids

Recommendations include slide_index and the specific suggested override (cell_accent_mode or layout swap).

## Acceptance criteria

- New fields populated for any deck input — pattern-expanded or authored shape_grids
- Recommendations are actionable (specify the slide and the override to apply)
- No specific deck or pattern referenced in tests; cover the rules with synthetic minimal inputs
- Performance: re-running textcapacity per slide must not noticeably regress analyze_deck_rhythm latency on decks of 20+ slides

## Dependencies

Blocked by textcapacity package bead. Compatible with cell_accent_mode bead landing in either order — recommendation messages can reference cell_accent_mode regardless of whether patterns implement it yet.
close_reason: Implemented: added within_slide_accent_variety to per-slide fingerprint, density_distribution to aggregates, and two new recommendation rules (accent variety for 5+ cell slides, underfilled cell ratio)

title: Add cell_underfilled finding code and density-band severity to fit-report
description:
## Why

Fit-report today emits cell_overflow when content exceeds capacity (cmd/json2pptx/fit_report.go:317 measureShapeText with Action:'refuse'). It has no signal for the inverse failure mode: cells that are visually empty because the agent used too small a slice of the available capacity. Half-empty grids and oversized containers around tiny content are a major perceived-quality problem.

Once textcapacity computes Density.Status, this is a one-finding addition next to the existing overflow detection.

## What

Add finding code 'cell_underfilled' alongside the existing 'cell_overflow' (or 'fit_overflow' — preserve whichever name fit-report currently uses). Severity bands by density_pct from textcapacity:

- info: 40-60% (underfilled — consider adding detail or smaller grid)
- warning: <40% (very underfilled) OR 110-130% (moderate overflow)
- error: >130% (severe overflow — emit even when strict_fit is 'warn')

Finding shape:

```json
{
  "path": "slides[i].shape_grid.rows[r].cells[c]",
  "code": "cell_underfilled",
  "severity": "info|warning",
  "message": "cell content is N chars (P% of capacity) — consider adding detail or smaller grid",
  "fix": {"kind": "add_detail_or_resize", "params": {"current_density_pct": P}}
}
```

The path format must mirror existing cell_overflow paths so downstream tools (and any repair_slide hooks) can target findings consistently.

## Acceptance criteria

- New finding code with severity bands as specified
- Walks all shape_grids (pattern-expanded and authored) via the same textcapacity.ForResolvedGrid call
- Strict_fit semantics:
  - 'strict' refuses generation on severity=error
  - 'warn' allows generation, includes findings in output
  - 'off' suppresses underfilled findings entirely (still emits overflow at warning+)
- Tests cover all three density bands (underfilled, optimal, overflow) using parameterized inputs — no specific deck/template referenced

## Dependencies

Blocked by fit-report textcapacity refactor bead.
close_reason: Implemented cell_underfilled finding code with density-band severity (info: 40-59%, warning: <40%, warning: 110-130%, error: >130%). Added ErrCodeCellUnderfilled constant, Severity field to fitFinding, density-band switch in walkShapeGrid, and parameterized tests covering all four bands plus optimal.

title: Refactor fit-report to consume internal/textcapacity (replace inline estimators)
description:
## Why

cmd/json2pptx/fit_report.go already walks shape_grid cells (walkShapeGrid at :239, measureShapeText at :317, MeasureRun call at :335) and emits cell-level fit_overflow findings — but it derives cell width/height inline via estimateCellWidthEMU at :402 and estimateCellHeightEMU at :429 with simplified row-flex semantics that diverge from internal/shapegrid.Resolve(). That divergence is invisible today but would compound the moment expand_pattern, repair_slide, or analyze_rhythm consume capacity numbers from a different code path.

Refactoring fit-report to call internal/textcapacity.ForResolvedGrid is the proof the abstraction is correct: if it doesn't simplify here, the package design is wrong and should be revisited before more callers land.

## What

- Replace the inline cell-bounds derivation (fit_report.go:402 estimateCellWidthEMU, :429 estimateCellHeightEMU) with a call to textcapacity.ForResolvedGrid which internally runs shapegrid.Resolve.
- measureShapeText becomes a thin shim: take []Density for the resolved grid, emit cell_overflow when Status == overflow, preserving existing finding shape (path, code, severity, message, fix.kind=reduce_text, fix.params.max_chars).
- All existing fit-report golden tests must pass unchanged (or be updated with explicit justification — divergence is expected in templates where the old simplified math was wrong).

## Acceptance criteria

- estimateCellWidthEMU and estimateCellHeightEMU deleted from fit_report.go
- walkShapeGrid + measureShapeText call textcapacity.ForResolvedGrid; no other capacity math remains in fit_report.go
- All existing tests in cmd/json2pptx/ pass; any golden updates documented in commit message
- Behavior parity verified across all bundled templates and shape_grid configurations in examples/

## Dependencies

Blocked by the textcapacity package bead.
close_reason: Refactored walkShapeGrid and checkShapeGridStructural to use shapegrid.Resolve + textcapacity.ForResolvedGrid. Deleted estimateCellWidthEMU, estimateCellHeightEMU, checkRowMaxHeightOverflow, measureShapeText, and extractShapeTextAndFont (dead code). All tests pass.

title: Chart data coercions emit structured diagnostics, not log warnings
description:
**Source**: 2026-05-05 codex audit, finding #4.

**Why agents struggle**: internal/types/chart.go:340-359 + 492-499 coerce non-numeric chart values to zero with only a log warning — fabricated zeroes can render a plausible-looking but semantically wrong chart. internal/types/chart.go:516-599 buildChartData repairs wrong shapes by inventing defaults (gauge gets min=0,max=100; scatter gets ordinal x; waterfall point types inferred from sign) rather than failing. svggen/registry.go:106-109 logs empty data and renders blank. cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go:1021-1082 — chart/diagram validation failures come back as plain warning strings, decode failures dropped entirely.

**Fix**: Replace log warnings with structured fit-findings (codes: chart_value_coerced, chart_shape_inferred, chart_data_empty). Action=review with next_tool_call to repair_slide for the agent to provide correct data. Keep coercion behavior for backward compatibility but always surface a finding.

**Acceptance**: Sending a column-chart with a string value returns a chart_value_coerced finding listing the row+column. Empty-data SVG render returns chart_data_empty as a refuse-action finding.

title: Enforce shapegrid.Validate on production render path
description:
**Source**: 2026-05-05 codex audit, finding #3.

**Why agents struggle**: cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go:182-239 resolveShapeGrid converts DTOs and emits XML directly. The structural validator at internal/shapegrid/validate.go:8-88 is NEVER invoked on the hot path. Grid overlap and span errors are only caught by tests or external callers. Agents need hard boundary failures BEFORE degraded XML is produced, not silent wrong output.

**Fix**: Call shapegrid.Validate in resolveShapeGrid before XML emission. On validation failure, return structured diagnostic with error code and Fix suggestion. Add regression test feeding overlapping grid spans through generate_presentation and asserting validation error rather than success-with-bad-XML.

**Acceptance**: A grid with overlapping cells fails generation with a clear error citing the offending cells. CI test demonstrates.
close_reason: Added shapegrid.Validate call in resolveShapeGrid before XML emission. Grids with overlapping cells or out-of-bounds spans now fail with a clear validation error. Added 2 regression tests.

title: card-grid de-incentivize: auto-suggest more specific pattern at validate
description:
**Source**: 2026-05-05 audit, R1#14.

**Why agents struggle**: cardgrid.go accepts 'Header | Body' shorthand (line 64-77), arbitrary rows*cols, and treats style as free-form. By contrast kpi-3up requires exactly 3 items with big/small fields, bmc-canvas requires 9 named blocks, pyramid 3-5 tiers. From an agent's token economy, card-grid is ALWAYS the path of least resistance: type less, validate easier, succeed faster. That economic gradient pushes agents toward homogeneity even before rhythm enters the picture.

**Fix**: Two complementary moves:
1. At validate time, when card-grid is chosen but a more specific pattern would fit (3 cells with numeric headers -> kpi-3up; 9 cells in 3x3 with named keys -> bmc-canvas), emit a pattern_substitution_suggested warning with Fix.Kind=swap_pattern.
2. Make kpi-3up's shorthand input cheaper: accept ['.2M | ARR', ...] tuple syntax to close the cost gap.

**Acceptance**: Generating a deck where every slide passes 3 kpi-shaped items to card-grid produces 3 substitution warnings. Adopting the suggestion converts to kpi-3up with no JSON expansion.
close_reason: Implemented KPI-shaped card-grid detection with swap_pattern warnings, and KPI cell shorthand syntax

title: split_pattern Fix kind: split overflowing patterns into 2 distinct slides
description:
**Source**: 2026-05-05 audit, R2#10. Sharpens 18p8.

**Why agents struggle**: When content overflows, internal/textfit/textfit.go:24-75 only shrinks (FitResult is shrink-only, minFontScalePct=60%). The fit action shrink_or_split is named for splitting but the only Fix.Kind emitted is split_at_row (tables only — structural_smells.go:230). For a 5x5 card-grid that overflows, no Fix.Kind=split_pattern exists. Agents learn 'overflow means less content per slide' rather than 'two visually distinct slides covering the same idea' — collapsing pacing variety.

**Fix**: For card-grid / iconrow / kpi-Nup / timeline-horizontal: when overflow predicted, emit Fix.Kind=split_pattern with params={first:N1, second:N2, title_part_2:'(continued)'}. repair_slide honors this. surface in score_deck.

**Acceptance**:
- 12-cell card-grid that overflows returns split_pattern{first:6,second:6,title_part_2:'(continued)'}.
- repair_slide applies it producing two slides with paired titles.

**Depends on**: x1t6 + r9t1 (repair must understand structural fixes).
