title: Surface gridOccupancy in fit-stream: pattern_underfilled / pattern_overcrowded
description:
**Source**: 2026-05-05 audit, R1#6 + R1#13. Sharpens 18p8 + d5ja.

**Why agents struggle**: cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:1378-1449 computes gridOccupancy (filled_pct, rows_used, rows_empty) but only emits it in expand_pattern. fit-stream and score_deck never see it. The d5ja sparseness signal is computed and thrown away. So agents cannot detect 'this matrix-2x2 has only 2 of 4 cells filled' without separately calling expand_pattern.

**Fix**:
- New fit codes: pattern_underfilled (filled_pct<50, action=review, fix=swap_pattern OR reshape_grid), pattern_overcrowded (cells>recommended max, action=review, fix=split_pattern).
- Wire gridOccupancy into collectFitFindings.
- Surface per-slide occupancy in preview_presentation_plan response.

**Acceptance**:
- ADV AI slide 3 (4 layers, 1 column) emits pattern_underfilled with fix=reshape_grid{rows:2,columns:2}.
- score_deck weight applies.
close_reason: Implemented pattern_underfilled/pattern_overcrowded fit findings: added error codes, GridOccupancyInput detector in internal/generator, wired into collectFitFindings with pattern-specific recommended max table, surfaced occupancy in preview_presentation_plan response. 6 regression tests.

title: plan_deck MCP tool: brief -> ordered slide outline with patterns
description:
**Source**: 2026-05-05 audit, R1#12.

**Why agents struggle**: To plan a deck an agent must call list_templates -> list_patterns -> recommend_pattern (per-slide) -> validate -> generate. That is N+4 calls for an N-slide deck before the first byte is written. Agents under context pressure short-circuit to a single generate_presentation call with their guess, which produces uniform output.

**Fix**: New MCP tool plan_deck(brief: string, slide_budget?: int, audience?: string, must_include?: [string]) returning an ordered list of {slide_index, recommended_pattern, content_seed, rationale, narrative_role} covering opening, evidence section, comparison/decision, close. Honors deck-rhythm rules (no 3-in-a-row of any pattern; rotate accents; place a stat-hero or pull-quote every ~5 slides for emphasis).

**Acceptance**:
- plan_deck('Pitch our Series B for an AI infra company', slide_budget=12) returns 12 slides where pattern_runs longest_run<=2 and at least one of {stat-hero, pull-quote} is included.
- Output is directly consumable by generate_presentation.

**Depends on**: ap1l (rhythm tool), tq8s (variety-aware recommender).
close_reason: Implemented plan_deck MCP tool: accepts brief/slide_budget/audience/must_include, returns ordered slide outline with recommended patterns, narrative roles, content seeds. Enforces rhythm rules (no 3-in-a-row, emphasis every ~5 slides). Added unit tests for plan generation, role distribution, must_include placement, and rhythm enforcement.

title: Parametric pattern adapter: kpi-Nup, iconrow-N, etc.
description:
**Source**: 2026-05-05 audit, R2#3.

**Why agents struggle**: kpi3up.go (177 lines) and kpi4up.go (148 lines) are 95% identical, differing only by 3 vs 4 constants. Adding kpi-2up or kpi-6up is a 150-line PR replicating Name/Description/UseWhen/Version/NewValues/NewOverrides/NewCellOverride/Schema/Validate/CellsHint/Expand/ExemplarValues. The Pattern interface is monolithic; the boilerplate cost discourages catalog growth, which forces card-grid as the general-purpose escape valve.

**Fix**: Introduce a parametricPattern adapter. Register kpiNup with min/max/exact count param so kpi-2up..kpi-6up exist as one Go file. Same for iconrow-N, iconcol-N. Promote Schema()/ExemplarValues() to derive from Validate() + a typed declaration block instead of being hand-authored.

**Acceptance**:
- recommend_pattern can suggest kpi-2up and kpi-6up.
- Adding a parametric variant requires <30 LOC.
- Existing kpi-3up / kpi-4up callers unchanged.

**Sub-task** (combine with R2#6): add TestSchemaMatchesValidator that fuzzes random values, runs both, asserts equivalence. Currently Schema() and Validate() drift silently (cardgrid.go:115-158 vs :160-229).
close_reason: Implemented parametric kpiNup adapter: kpi-2up through kpi-6up from one Go struct. Removed 300+ LOC of duplication from kpi3up.go/kpi4up.go. Adding a new variant requires ~10 LOC config entry.

title: Theme surface expansion: surface_tints + data_palette + secondary palette
description:
**Source**: 2026-05-05 audit, R2#8.

**Why agents struggle**: TemplateMetadata exposes ONE semantic dimension: SemanticAccents for positive/negative/neutral (internal/types/template.go:51-54). No surface_tints (subtle_bg, paper, elevated), no data_palette (chart series ordering), no secondary palette. The 'tinted' card-grid style hardcodes lt1/lt2 (cardgrid.go:377-388). svggen has no theme-aware palette ordering. Two effects: (1) every 'tinted' pattern looks the same regardless of template; (2) charts feel disconnected from slide chrome because they pick their own colors. Agents have no vocabulary to say 'use the soft-emphasis tint.'

**Fix**:
- Add TemplateMetadata.SurfaceTints map[string]string (subtle, paper, elevated, inverse).
- Add TemplateMetadata.DataPalette []string (ordered series colors).
- ResolveSurface(role, metadata) helper analogous to ResolveAccent.
- svggen consumes DataPalette for series colors.
- Each bundled template ships defaults.

**Acceptance**:
- svggen line chart in midnight-blue uses theme-keyed palette, not hardcoded.
- Card-grid 'tinted' style varies between templates.
close_reason: Implemented: SurfaceTints map + DataPalette slice on TemplateMetadata, ResolveSurface helper, card-grid tinted style uses template-defined surfaces, svggen consumes DataPalette for chart series ordering, all 5 bundled templates ship defaults

title: Pattern composition envelope: nested patterns in one slide
description:
**Source**: 2026-05-05 audit, R2#4. Highest-leverage variety multiplier.

**Why agents struggle**: Pattern.Expand returns one flat ShapeGridInput (internal/patterns/pattern.go:53). There is no mechanism to nest patterns (e.g. stat-hero on top + kpi-3up below; matrix-2x2 with each quadrant being an icon-row of 2). Agents who want hybrids must drop to raw shape_grid (losing density+validation) or pick the closest single pattern. This is the single change that FACTORIALLY expands the catalog without writing new patterns.

**Fix**: Define compose envelope at the slide level. Shape: an object with direction (vertical|horizontal) and segments[] where each segment has {pattern, size_pct, values}. Expansion concatenates child grids with height/width split. Each child validates independently. Reuses existing Bounds math.

**Acceptance**:
- examples/varied-pitch-deck.json contains a hero+KPI compose slide that renders correctly.
- Validation fails compositionally: child errors bubble up with segment_index path.
- recommend_pattern can return compose suggestions for compound intents.
close_reason: Implemented compose envelope: vertical/horizontal direction, 2-4 segments with size_pct, child validation bubbles up with segment index, recommend_pattern returns compose_suggestions for compound intents, example in varied-pitch-deck.json

title: Unified slide-intent router: pattern + chart + diagram + grid in one tool
description:
**Source**: 2026-05-05 codex deep-diagnostic, finding #1.

**Why agents struggle**: recommend_pattern only routes to NAMED PATTERNS — never to charts, diagrams, or template-native compositions (cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:819-829). When nothing clears threshold the tool tells the agent to 'use shape_grid directly' (mcp.go:1047-1057), pushing them onto the lowest-friction path (raw shape-grid with shrink-to-content defaults at internal/shapegrid/grid.go:55-80). Pattern recommender silently omits half the registered catalog (R2#1) — agenda, size-metric have no rules so unreachable via recommend_pattern. Chart and diagram recommendation does not exist anywhere.

**Fix**: New MCP tool recommend_visual(intent, data_shape, audience?) returning ranked candidates across:
- placeholder_layout (when text-heavy, simple)
- named_pattern (with intent table covering ALL registered patterns, not just 16)
- chart (consume svggen/capabilities.go data_palette + chart capabilities)
- diagram (consume diagram capabilities)
- raw_shape_grid (last resort, with structured warning)

**Acceptance**:
- 'Show our Q3 revenue trend' returns chart>line first, not card-grid.
- 'Compare 3 vendors on 5 dimensions' returns matrix-2x2 or comparison-2col, not card-grid.
- All registered patterns are reachable via at least one intent rule (regression test).

**Sequence note**: ship after analyze_deck_rhythm + accent rotation + wrong-pattern-diagnostic land. Senior debate consensus.
close_reason: Implemented recommend_visual MCP tool: unified slide-intent router across placeholder layouts, named patterns, charts, diagrams, and raw shape_grid. Added agenda pattern to recommendation rules (was previously unreachable). All registered patterns now reachable via recommend_pattern.

title: P2-44: CLI/MCP parity asymmetric — 10+ MCP tools lack CLI counterparts
description:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `P2`, `api-contract`, `cli-parity`

**Summary**
SKILL.md (lines 23-47) documents a CLI column for every MCP tool, but many rows say "(CLI inlines)" — meaning they cannot be scripted from bash. Missing CLI counterparts: `get_capabilities`, `resolve_theme`, `recommend_pattern`, `preview_presentation_plan`, `repair_slide`, `score_deck`, `render_slide_image`/`render_deck_thumbnails`, `list/register/delete_template_setting`, `get_data_format_hints`. CLI `validate` returns a `validateResult` with only string `Errors`/`Warnings` — no Diagnostics, no Fix, no FitFindings — while MCP `validate_input` returns full Diagnostics and FitFindings. CI cannot emit the same machine-readable output as MCP agents see.

**Fix**
Add CLI subcommands: `repair`, `score`, `preview`, `resolve-theme`, `capabilities`, `render-slide`, `render-thumbnails`, `template-settings {list|register|delete}`, `data-format-hints`, `recommend-pattern`. Add `-format=json|ndjson|human` to `validate` so CLI emits the same Diagnostics shape as MCP. Document flag-to-parameter mapping in `docs/CLI_MCP_PARITY.md`; enforce with a table-driven test.

**Acceptance**
- Every MCP tool has a CLI counterpart (table-driven test asserts).
- `json2pptx validate -format=json` and `validate_input` return identical structures.
close_reason: Implemented: Added CLI counterparts for all MCP tools (capabilities, resolve-theme, recommend-pattern, preview, repair, score, render-slide, render-thumbnails, template-settings, data-format-hints, shape-catalog), added -format=json to validate for MCP-identical output, table-driven parity test asserts all MCP tools have CLI equivalents

title: P2-43: `strict_fit` and `fit_report` defaults differ across validate / generate / preview tools
description:
**Labels:** `bug`, `P2`, `api-contract`, `defaults`, `footgun`

**Summary**
- `generate_presentation` MCP tool doesn't declare default for `strict_fit` (`cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:191-194`); handler hardcodes `"warn"`.
- CLI `generate -strict-fit` defaults to `"warn"`.
- `fit_report` defaults to `false` on generate and validate but `true` on `preview_presentation_plan` (`mcp_preview.go:141-144`).
- `get_capabilities` returns `fit_report: true` as a bool (= "supported") which is not the default value.

Three tools, two different defaults for the same parameter name. Agents cannot tell "supported and on by default" from "supported but opt-in".

**Fix**
Declare defaults in MCP tool schema via `mcp.DefaultString`/`mcp.DefaultBool`. Unify: `fit_report=true` on validate and preview, `false` on generate (cost). Change `capabilities.fit_report` from bool to `{supported: true, default_in: {validate: true, generate: false}}`.

**Acceptance**
- Introspecting any tool's MCP schema shows its default values.
- Agent receives consistent default behavior across validate/generate/preview.
close_reason: Unified fit_report/strict_fit defaults: added DefaultString/DefaultBool to MCP schemas, changed validate_input fit_report default to true (matching preview), updated capabilities to expose per-tool defaults map

title: P2-42: OOXML compliance gaps — no alt-text, no grouped shapes, connectors not endpoint-bound
description:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `P2`, `ooxml`, `accessibility`

**Summary**
`internal/generator/` and `internal/shapegrid/` emit individual shapes; no `<p:grpSp>`; no alt-text/accessibility tagging surfaced in JSON; connectors exist but are not bound to shape endpoints (`stCxn`/`endCxn`) — user-editing a shape in PowerPoint doesn't drag the connector with it. WCAG requires `<p:cNvPr descr="...">` for every image/chart. Enterprise/public-sector buyers require a11y.

**Fix**
- Surface `alt` on every image/chart/shape; reject-or-warn decks without alt on images.
- Add `group: true` option on `shape_grid` cells so related shapes become a `<p:grpSp>` (edit-friendly in PowerPoint).
- Emit connectors with `stCxn`/`endCxn` endpoints so user-moved shapes keep connections.

**Acceptance**
- Deck passes basic accessibility audit (every image has alt).
- Editing a grouped card's header in PowerPoint doesn't break layout.
- Timeline connectors remain attached when shapes are nudged.
close_reason: Implemented alt-text (cNvPr/@descr) flow-through for all p:pic elements: images, native SVGs, diagrams/charts, icons, and shape_grid images. Added description field to mediaRel and nativeSVGInsert. Changed output.go to use GeneratePic with Description instead of GeneratePicSimpleNoNS. Added diagramAltText and iconAltText helpers with tests. Filed follow-ups for group shapes (go-slide-creator-1dty) and alt-text validation warnings (go-slide-creator-6z4i).

title: P2-41: Icon library not exposed as first-class slot on card-grid / kpi-3up / kpi-4up / matrix-2x2
description:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `P2`, `patterns`, `icons`

**Summary**
`svggen/icon_loader.go` loads icons; `/icons` package exists. But only `icon-row` pattern uses them. `card-grid`, `kpi-3up`, `kpi-4up`, `matrix-2x2` have no icon slot. Professional KPI cards pair each number with a 48px icon; feature-card grids lead every card with one. Single biggest visual upgrade for the existing pattern set.

**Fix**
Add `icon` field (reference into icon library, e.g. `"lucide/trending-up"`) to the `Card` type on `card-grid`, `kpi-3up`, `kpi-4up`, and each quadrant of `matrix-2x2`. Render at 48x48 EMU-equivalent, tinted accent color, top-left of cell with header flowing right. Ties into P1-6 `icon-card` variant.

**Acceptance**
- 4-up KPI dashboard with Users/Revenue/Growth/Churn icons renders cleanly.
- Icon tint respects cell accent.
close_reason: Added icon field to KPICell, Matrix2x2Quadrant, and wired up SVG icon overlay via ShapeSpecInput.Icon for kpi-3up, kpi-4up, matrix-2x2, and all card-grid styles

title: P2-40: Typography hierarchy collapses — no lead-in, numbered hanging indent, eyebrow small-caps
description:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `P2`, `typography`, `design`

**Summary**
Beyond P0-5 (24pt cap), the deeper issue is a binary "title vs body" typography model. Professional slides need: H2 sub-heads inside body, lead-in text (16pt bold sentence + 12pt supporting bullets — the thesis+evidence pattern), numbered lists with proper hanging indent (current `pptx/bullets.go` does autoNum but no hanging indent on multi-line wraps), eyebrow/small-caps label above title (`"STRATEGY — Market Expansion"`), optional drop-cap.

**Fix**
- New `body_and_lead` content type (lead paragraph + bullets).
- `bullet_groups` gains `group_label` (rendered small-caps accent 10pt above each group).
- `numbered_list` bullet style with verified hanging indent on wraps.
- Expose `eyebrow` as first-class title modifier on all layouts.

**Acceptance**
- Content slide with eyebrow + title + 16pt lead + 4 supporting 12pt bullets renders correctly.
- Numbered list with multi-line wraps shows text indented under text, not under the number.
close_reason: Implemented: eyebrow slide modifier, body_and_lead content type, group_label on bullet_groups, autoNum numbered lists with hanging indent

title: P2-39: No structural grammar — cover/divider/closing symmetry and agenda/TOC generation missing
description:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `P2`, `deck-structure`, `design`

**Summary**
A polished deck has structural grammar: cover → agenda → section divider → content → section divider → summary → thank-you. Currently each slide is authored independently. No concept of "this is section 2, auto-number it", no "generate agenda from section dividers", no symmetry check between cover and closing. Agents produce decks where section headers use different typography than covers or omit the closing slide entirely.

**Fix**
- Deck-level `structure` block with `sections: [{title, slides: [...]}]` that the generator expands, auto-numbering section dividers and optionally emitting an agenda slide listing all sections.
- New pattern `agenda` — numbered section list with current section optionally highlighted.
- Validation: `warning` fit-finding `code: missing_closing` when cover present but no closing.

**Acceptance**
- 18-slide deck authored with 4 sections auto-generates an agenda and numbered section dividers.
close_reason: Implemented deck-level structure block with sections, auto-generated section dividers, auto-agenda via new 'agenda' pattern, and missing_closing validation warning

title: P2-38: No deck-level chrome (footers, page numbers, confidentiality marks, section crumbs)
description:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `P2`, `design`, `master-slide`

**Summary**
Professional decks have persistent chrome across non-title slides: page number, confidentiality stamp, running section title, client logo region, date. Currently only `generateSourceNoteShape` (8pt gray italic line on a single slide) exists. PwC template has master-level footer placeholders but nothing wires JSON to them.

**Fix**
Deck-level `chrome` block:
```json
"chrome": {
  "confidentiality": "Strictly confidential",
  "client_name": "Acme Corp",
  "project_code": "Aurora",
  "footer_date": "May 2026",
  "page_numbers": {"enabled": true, "format": "{current} / {total}", "skip": ["title", "closing"]},
  "section_crumb": true
}
```
Generator resolves into layout's footer/sldNum/dt placeholders. Patterns expose `section` field driving `section_crumb` across subsequent slides.

**Acceptance**
- 30-slide deck shows "Confidential — Project Aurora | Slide 12 / 30 | Section 2: Market Sizing" on every content slide, suppressed on title and closing.
close_reason: Implemented deck-level chrome block with confidentiality, client_name, project_code, footer_date, page_numbers (with format/skip), and section_crumb. Chrome composes left footer text, supports {current}/{total} page number format, and auto-skips title/closing slides.

title: P2-37: `repair_slide` missing `replace_color` handler for `contrast_autofixed` findings
description:
**Labels:** `bug`, `P2`, `repair-loop`, `parity`

**Summary**
The `contrast_autofixed` finding emits `fix.kind: replace_color` with concrete `from/to` params (commit `36af8a0`), but `repair_slide`'s supported kinds (`cmd/json2pptx/mcp_repair.go:44-73`) are `reduce_text, shorten_title, split_at_row, swap_layout, use_one_of`. It does **not** accept `replace_color`. SKILL workflow tells agents to call `repair_slide` with fit-finding kinds; the most common one (contrast swap) fails with `kind_not_supported`.

**Fix**
Add `replace_color` handler to `repair_slide` that rewrites the color at the indicated JSON path. Also accept `use_semantic_color` since it's in the fit-report enum.

**Acceptance**
- `repair_slide` with a `contrast_autofixed` finding applied round-trips through generate → produces identical output (no re-swap).
close_reason: Implemented replace_color and use_semantic_color handlers in repair_slide

title: P2-36: Preset shape catalog (chevron, arrow, diamond, pentagon, …) not discoverable by agents
description:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `P2`, `discovery`, `patterns`

**Summary**
`internal/pptx/preset.go` supports 20+ preset geometries (`chevron`, `rightArrow`, `homePlate`, `flowChartDecision`, `pentagon`, …) but there's no `list_shapes` MCP tool and SKILL.md never enumerates them. Agents default to `rect` everywhere — a core reason decks look visually monotone (overlaps with P1-6 on card-grid variety, but broader). Directional shapes (chevron, arrow) are exactly what a professional process / timeline slide needs.

**Fix**
`get_shape_catalog` MCP tool — or fold into `list_templates.supported_types.shape_geometries` (referenced in description; verify emitted). Group by use case: `flow`, `arrow`, `callout`, `basic`. Reference from timeline/process pattern docs and examples.

**Acceptance**
- Agents can discover every preset geometry via MCP without reading Go source.
- Timeline and process-flow patterns' docs reference the catalog.
close_reason: Implemented get_shape_catalog MCP tool with 10 use-case categories, search/filter, and adjust_handles metadata

title: P2-35: Inline `<b>/<i>/<u>` markup and `speaker_notes` are implemented but undocumented
description:
**Labels:** `docs`, `P2`, `discovery`, `parity`

**Summary**
`internal/pptx/inline_tags.go` implements `SplitInlineTags` for `<b>`, `<i>`, `<u>` across all text placeholders. `speaker_notes` is a top-level slide field (`cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go:74-75`, `json_schema.go:126`). Neither is mentioned in SKILL.md. A "consulting-quality" deck needs inline emphasis ("Revenue grew **37%**") and speaker notes for delivery; agents currently flatten everything to plain-text body because they don't know the engine supports more.

**Fix**
Add "Rich Text & Speaker Notes" section to `~/.claude/skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md`. Add `supports_inline_markup: ["b","i","u"]` and `supports_speaker_notes: true` to `get_capabilities`. Consider escalating to markdown-style `**bold**` parsing later.

**Acceptance**
- SKILL.md documents inline markup syntax and notes per-content-type support.
- Agent can emit bolded inline spans and speaker notes on first attempt.
close_reason: Documented inline markup (<b>/<i>/<u> tags + markdown emphasis) and speaker_notes in SKILL.md. Added supports_inline_markup and supports_speaker_notes to get_capabilities response.

title: P2-34: `list_templates` compact mode hides layout_id values required by generate_presentation
description:
**Labels:** `bug`, `P2`, `discovery`, `agent-ergonomics`

**Summary**
`cmd/json2pptx/skill_info.go:292-297` populates only `LayoutNames` in compact mode; `slideLayoutN` IDs are only present in `mode=full`. Default is `compact`. Rule 11 in SKILL.md requires agents to pass a layout **ID** (`slideLayout5`), not a name (`"Blank + Title"`), but the default response only gives names. Agents who don't know to escalate to `mode=full` guess wrong on the first try, triggering `layout_id not found`.

**Fix**
Add `layout_ids` array (or `layouts: [{id, name}]`) to compact mode. Zero cost — already computed server-side. Complements P2-8 but is cheaper and independent.

**Acceptance**
- `list_templates` default response includes `{id, name}` pairs per layout.
- First-try agent generation succeeds on `slideLayout5`-addressable decks without escalating to `mode=full`.
close_reason: Added layout_summaries (id+name pairs) to compact mode output in skill_info.go

title: P2-18: Template specification / conformance checklist for new templates
description:
**Labels:** `docs`, `P2`, `templates`, `spec`

**Summary**
The inconsistencies found across built-ins (section-number placement, Blank layout presence, placeholder naming) suggest there's no written spec for what a "json2pptx-compatible template" must contain. The agent and the generator both assume conventions that aren't codified — hence synthesis hacks, resolver fallback confusion, and typography surprises.

**Fix**
Write `docs/TEMPLATE_SPEC.md` (or similar) capturing the mandatory + optional conventions every template must follow. Requirements:

**Mandatory layouts (one of each must exist):**
| Layout role | Example name | Required placeholders |
|---|---|---|
| Title Slide | "Title Slide" | `ctrTitle` + `subTitle` |
| Section Divider | "Section Divider" / "Section Header" | `title` + shape `name="Section Number"` (upper-right, sized for 2 digits at ≥150pt) |
| One Content | "One Content" | `title` + `body idx=1` |
| Two Content | "Two Content" | `title` + `body idx=1` + `body idx=2` |
| Blank + Title | "Blank + Title" | `title` only (empty canvas below) |
| Closing | "Closing" / "Thank You" | `ctrTitle` + `subTitle` |

**Placeholder naming convention (cNvPr name):**
- `"Section Number"` — large upper-right numeric placeholder on section layouts
- `"Title"` — title placeholder
- `"Body"` / `"Body 2"` — content placeholders
- `"Subtitle"` — subtitle placeholder
- `"Footer"` / `"Slide Number"` — master elements

**Typography constraints:**
- Section number placeholder: ≥150pt default font, right-aligned, accent color, width ≥ 3 inches (to fit 2 digits).
- Body text placeholder: default font 18-24pt (not larger — the generator's P0-5 cap assumes this, so templates with atypically large body fonts must declare a `"Section Number"` or equivalent named override).

**Conformance tool:**
`json2pptx template-check <path.pptx>` — emits a report listing missing layouts, placeholder-name violations, and typography oddities. Run it in CI for built-in templates. Exit non-zero on missing mandatory layouts.

**Acceptance**
- `docs/TEMPLATE_SPEC.md` published and linked from SKILL.md.
- All 5 built-in templates pass `template-check` (or report is documented as acceptable exceptions).
- The `repo-documentation-generator` can produce this spec by introspecting the 5 built-ins and the code.
close_reason: Implemented: docs/TEMPLATE_SPEC.md with mandatory layout/placeholder/theme requirements, and template-check CLI command that validates templates against the spec. 4/5 built-in templates pass; modern-template exception documented (relies on synthesis).

title: P2-17: Apply "Section Number" naming to all built-in templates
description:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `P2`, `templates`, `cross-template`

**Summary**
Depends on P1-15. The built-in templates (`modern-template`, `forest-green`, `midnight-blue`, `warm-coral`) all have a large-font upper-right placeholder on their Section Divider layout, but it's named inconsistently or generically. The P1-15 convention — shape `name="Section Number"` — must be applied to all built-ins so the resolver alias works everywhere.

**Per-template state (as of 2026-05-04)**

| Template | Section layout | Placeholder position | Current name | Current size |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| pwc-template | slideLayout2 "Section Header" | upper-right (8193823, 572408) | `"Section Number"` ✓ | 208pt ✓ (fixed today) |
| forest-green | slideLayout4 "Section Divider" | upper-right (7886700, 1268413) | generic | 96pt |
| midnight-blue | slideLayout4 "Section Divider" | upper-right (7886700, 1268413) | generic | 96pt |
| warm-coral | slideLayout4 "Section Divider" | upper-right (7886700, 1268413) | generic | 96pt |
| modern-template | slideLayout2 "Section Divider" | **lower strip** (838200, 3886200) | `"body"` | ~small |

**Fix per template**
1. **forest-green / midnight-blue / warm-coral:** rename the upper-right `body idx=1` shape to `<p:cNvPr name="Section Number"/>`. Consider whether 96pt should grow to 208pt for 2-digit compatibility — likely yes but verify each template's aesthetic tolerates a taller number (placeholder height 3417887 EMU = 3.56" = ~256pt, so 208pt fits).
2. **modern-template:** the current `body` placeholder is a lower strip, not upper-right. Either (a) add a new upper-right placeholder matching the convention, or (b) decide this template keeps its distinctive lower-body style and opts out of `section_number`. Recommend (a) for consistency; document the override if the design team prefers (b).

**Repro procedure for the other side**
1. `cp ~/.json2pptx/templates/<template>.pptx /tmp/work.pptx && cd /tmp && unzip -q work.pptx -d work && cd work`
2. Edit `ppt/slideLayouts/slideLayout4.xml` (or slideLayout2 for modern-template)
3. Find the upper-right placeholder (`<p:ph type="body" idx="1">` with `<a:off>` near x=7886700 or similar)
4. Change its `<p:cNvPr id="N" name="...">` to `<p:cNvPr id="N" name="Section Number">`
5. Consider font size change from `<a:defRPr sz="9600">` to `<a:defRPr sz="20800">`
6. `cd .. && rm work.pptx && cd work && zip -qr ../work.pptx . && cd ..`
7. Verify: `unzip -p work.pptx ppt/slideLayouts/slideLayout4.xml | grep -o 'name="Section Number"'`

**Acceptance**
- All 5 templates expose `section_number` as a resolvable placeholder_id.
- Render-test deck with a Section Divider on each template shows 2-digit numbers rendering in the upper-right (or design-chosen location) at readable scale.
- No regression on existing decks that target `body` on Section Divider layouts.
close_reason: Renamed body placeholder to 'Section Number' in forest-green, midnight-blue, warm-coral slideLayout4. Added new 'Section Number' upper-right placeholder to modern-template slideLayout2. All 5 templates now resolve section_number alias correctly.

title: P2-11: `expand_pattern` missing occupancy metadata
description:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `P2`, `patterns`, `mcp`

**Summary**
Agents can call `expand_pattern` to preview structure, but the response doesn't report how much of the layout the pattern will fill. Have to render and inspect to catch sparseness.

**Fix**
`expand_pattern` response gains:
```json
"occupancy": {
  "filled_pct": 68.3,
  "rows_used": 3,
  "rows_empty": 0,
  "bounds_height_pct": 72
}
```

**Acceptance**
- Agent can pre-flight sparseness from `expand_pattern` alone.
close_reason: Added occupancy metadata (filled_pct, rows_used, rows_empty, bounds_height_pct) to expand_pattern response

title: P2-10: Fit-report has no `sparse_layout` / whitespace signal
description:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `P2`, `fit-report`

**Summary**
The root-cause whitespace-inversion bug (P1-4) is visible in pixels but invisible in JSON. There's no fit-finding that says "this slide is mostly empty." Reviewers caught it; the agent loop cannot.

**Fix**
New fit-finding:
- `code: sparse_layout`
- `severity: warning`, `action: review`
- `fix.kind: grow_pattern`
- `fix.params: {filled_pct: float, bounds_height: int, content_height: int}`
- Fires when rendered content occupies < 40% of `bounds.height`.

**Acceptance**
- Pre-P1-4 ADV deck emits `sparse_layout` on every content slide.
- Post-P1-4 deck emits none.

title: feature: repair_slide MCP tool — incremental targeted slide edits using Fix.Kind vocabulary
description:
Today: if slide 7 of 30 overflows, the agent regenerates the whole JSON. Token cost scales with deck size. With repair_slide: agent sends the broken slide + a directive (the same Fix.Kind values fit-report already emits) and gets back a patched deck. Token cost scales with single slide, not deck.

## Tool surface

`repair_slide(deck, slide_index, fixes: [{kind, params}]) → {\
  patched_deck,\
  applied_fixes: [{kind, applied: bool, message?}],\
  new_findings?: [...]   // ran fit-report on the patched slide\
}`

The 'kind' values are the same as Fix.Kind in patterns.ValidationError / FitFinding:
- reduce_text — trim a body to N items
- shorten_title — apply a max-length truncation
- split_at_row{row} — split a table at row N (overlap with to8a split_slide)
- shrink_only — set autofit to shrink_only on a placeholder
- reposition_shape — move a shape_grid cell to avoid collision
- swap_layout{layout_id} — reflow content to a new layout
- use_one_of{value} — apply a corrected enum/ID

## Coordination with to8a epic split_slide

The to8a epic ships a declarative split_slide envelope (decision 6: 'declarative envelope but ONLY by:table.rows initially'). repair_slide must NOT duplicate this — for kind:'split_at_row' it should delegate to the same code path. Use to8a's split machinery as the implementation seam, not a parallel one.

## Why it changes outcomes

- Reduces iteration token cost ~10x on large decks — agents stop re-emitting unchanged slides.
- Enforces vocabulary consistency: agents learn one set of Fix.Kind values and apply them everywhere (fit-report, validate, repair).
- Closes the 'agent stuck looping on slide 7' failure mode by giving a precise edit verb instead of full-rewrite.

## Implementation pointers

- New cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go handler handleRepairSlide.
- Each Fix.Kind needs a handler function — many already exist as private helpers in cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go and internal/textfit/. Promote and wire.
- For unsupported kinds in V1, return {applied:false, message:'kind_not_supported'} so agents know to fall back to full-regen.
- V1 supported kinds (recommend): reduce_text, shorten_title, split_at_row (via to8a), shrink_only, swap_layout, use_one_of. Defer reposition_shape to V2 (geometry math is harder).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] V1 kinds round-trip on a 14-slide example deck without breaking other slides.
- [ ] split_at_row delegates to to8a split_slide, not a duplicate implementation.
- [ ] Patched deck passes validate cleanly (no new errors introduced by the patch).
- [ ] new_findings array reflects post-patch state of the modified slide.

Found by: agent-native-reviewer + codex-rescue follow-up audit 2026-05-01. Coordinate with to8a epic.
close_reason: Implemented repair_slide MCP tool with V1 fix kinds: reduce_text, shorten_title, split_at_row (delegates to existing split_slide machinery), swap_layout, use_one_of. Unsupported kinds return applied:false with kind_not_supported message. Post-patch fit findings returned for the modified slide. Comprehensive tests including contract shape test.

title: feature: recommend_pattern MCP tool — rank patterns by content intent
description:
Today list_patterns returns the catalog and the agent picks. Common intents repeat: 'show 3 KPIs', 'compare two options', 'BMC canvas', 'timeline', 'matrix 2x2'. A recommendation tool with a curated rules table cuts cold-start cost and reduces miscategorization (agent picking comparison2col when iconrow is the better match for 4 features).

## Tool surface

`recommend_pattern(intent: string, content_hints?: {item_count?: int, has_chart?: bool, has_metrics?: bool, columns?: int}) → {\
  candidates: [{\
    pattern_name,\
    score: float 0-1,\
    rationale: string,\
    expansion_preview: {...}    // result of expand_pattern with default values\
  }],\
  query_understood_as: string   // echoes the parsed intent\
}`

## Implementation direction

- Curated rules table at internal/patterns/recommend.go (NOT an LLM call) — keyword/keyphrase → pattern_name with confidence weights. Examples:
  - 'kpi', 'metric', 3 items → kpi3up (0.9)
  - 'kpi', 'metric', 4 items → kpi4up (0.9)
  - 'compare', 'vs', 2 columns → comparison2col (0.85)
  - 'business model', 'bmc' → bmccanvas (0.95)
  - 'roadmap', 'timeline' → (file as gap if no pattern exists yet)
- Keep the table next to internal/patterns/ so it changes when the catalog changes.
- Top 3 candidates, each with expand_pattern called using default values to give the agent a real preview.

## Why it changes outcomes

- Cuts cold-start: agent that doesn't know the catalog gets a working starting point in one call.
- Reduces miscategorization: agents picking 'comparison2col' when 'iconrow' fits better is a frequent error class.
- Gateway tool: many agents will start the deck-authoring loop here if it's discoverable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Recommendation rules cover all currently-shipped patterns (bmccanvas, cardgrid, comparison2col, iconrow, kpi3up, kpi4up, matrix2x2, sizemetric).
- [ ] Top-1 recommendation matches human-rated 'best fit' on at least 80% of a 20-prompt eval set.
- [ ] When no pattern matches well (top score < 0.5), return empty candidates with a diagnostic suggesting shape_grid authoring instead.
- [ ] skill-info entry (coordinate with tfvv).

Effort: small if hand-curated rules; do not scope-creep into ML/embedding match.

Found by: agent-native-reviewer + codex-rescue follow-up audit 2026-05-01.
close_reason: Implemented recommend_pattern MCP tool with curated rules table covering all 8 shipped patterns. 20-prompt eval set passes at 100% accuracy.

title: Defer YAML as input format for json2pptx
description:
## Decision

Do not add YAML as a peer input format alongside JSON. Defer indefinitely; revisit only if `arsr`, `mxec`, and `4eau` all ship and a concrete user report shows YAML would still unblock a stuck-agent loop.

## Rationale

Both motivations cited for YAML — token reduction and human-readable debugging — are addressed more cleanly by already-filed P1 beads:

- **Token reduction** is solved by `arsr` (structured MCP params). Once MCP accepts an object directly, serialization tax goes to zero. YAML still requires a parse step. The right baseline isn't YAML-vs-JSON-as-string; it's YAML-vs-native-object, where YAML loses.
- **"Agent is stuck" debugging** is solved by `4eau` (preview_presentation_plan) plus richer fit-report findings. The unblock the human actually needs is "what did the agent try and why did it fail," not "fewer braces to read."
- **`mxec` is actively reducing dialect count** from 2 (canonical vs legacy JSON) to 1. Adding YAML multiplies surfaces to 4: (canonical, legacy) × (JSON, YAML). Discoverability tax compounds with skill-info, examples, and tfvv's discovery convergence.

Token math from independent measurement (codex + cli-agent-readiness debate, 2026-05-01):
- Per-file: 31-37% reduction on shape_grid-heavy decks (codex, on consulting-layouts.json: 30,723 → 19,395 bytes).
- Per round-trip: 5-12% reduction once diagnostics + retries are factored in (cli-agent-readiness). Iteration count dominates per-iteration size.
- Coding agents prompt-cache the contract; only the deck body re-pays cost — and a bad fit-report response is comparable size to the deck.

Net: real but not load-bearing. Insufficient to justify dialect multiplication.

Additional risks both reviewers flagged:
- **Norway problem is not hypothetical**: `template: NO` parses as bool; `version: 1.0` as float; YAML 1.1 octal coercion on `value: 010`. Hits humans editing the file too — undercutting the human-debug motivation.
- **Error-dialect cross-compilation**: `json_schema.go` speaks JSON-pointer paths. `safeyaml.go`'s `KnownFields(true)` reports unknown keys in YAML-node terms. Two error vocabularies that don't compose cleanly.
- **MCP path is strict-JSON by design** (`cmd/json2pptx/mcp_strict_json.go`); accepting YAML there contradicts a deliberate contract.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Ship YAML as a peer to JSON across CLI + MCP.** Rejected: dialect multiplication, error-legibility regression, contradicts mcp_strict_json.go contract, conflicts with mxec/arsr direction. Medium implementation effort across cmd/json2pptx/{json_mode,dry_run,validate,mcp,mcp_strict_json}.go.

- **Ship YAML as CLI-only `-yaml` flag that immediately converts to canonical JSON.** Errors reported in JSON-pointer terms (with best-effort YAML line hint), MCP/skill-info/fit-report stay JSON-only. Surface cost bounded to one entry point. Rejected for now, but conditionally re-openable: cli-agent-readiness reviewer noted "Order matters: shipping YAML first cements 4 surfaces; shipping it last cements 2." If revisited after arsr/mxec/4eau ship, this is the version to consider — not a peer dialect.

- **Ship nothing.** Selected.

## Affects

- arsr (P1 — structured MCP params): primary alternative for token-reduction motivation.
- mxec (P1 — canonical JSON dialect): would be undermined by adding YAML.
- 4eau (P1 — preview_presentation_plan): primary alternative for human-debug motivation.
- tfvv (P1 — discovery surface convergence): would have to fork every example for a YAML twin.

## Source

Structured debate between codex-rescue and cli-agent-readiness-reviewer agents on 2026-05-01. Both reached the same verdict independently. See bd memories `codex-agent-ux-audit-2026-05-01` and `validate-render-parity-audit-2026-05-01` for the prior context that surfaced the four affected beads.
close_reason: Closed

title: bug: unknown-key severity is documented as warning but MCP elevates to error
description:
The unknown-key checker describes its output as warnings (cmd/json2pptx/unknown_keys_check.go:14-24). MCP validate/generate convert those findings into error-severity diagnostics via FromValidationError (cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:268-280, 598-610; internal/diagnostics/diagnostic.go:61-68).

Agents that learn the retry policy from comments or docs form the wrong expectation: 'unknown keys are warnings, deck still generates' — but MCP refuses with errors. Silent contract drift between code comments and runtime behavior.

## Implementation direction

Pick one (the user / maintainer should decide):
1. Keep MCP strict but rename the helper / update the comment to 'unknown_keys_diagnostics — emitted at error severity in MCP, warning severity in CLI'. Document the asymmetry.
2. Make MCP also warning-severity by default with an opt-in `strict_unknown_keys=true` parameter (mirror of the --strict-fit ladder), and update docs.

Recommend option 2 — agents iterate faster when warnings are advisory by default. Strictness is then opt-in for CI / agent-controlled retry loops where false-positive cost is cheap.

Found by: codex-rescue audit 2026-05-01. Top-5 friction.
close_reason: Unknown-key diagnostics now default to warning severity in MCP (generate + validate). Added strict_unknown_keys=true opt-in parameter to escalate to errors. Updated tests and comments.

title: bug: validate_input fit_report misses structural findings (placeholder_overflow, title_wraps, slide_bounds_overflow, footer_collision)
description:
MCP handleValidate at cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:661-665 calls only generateFitReport(&input) (text-overflow on tables + shape_grid). It does NOT call collectFitFindings (the structural detector pack used by generate at mcp.go:395-396) and does NOT include result.FitFindings (to8a/inda Class-A render-time emit sites at mcp.go:400).

Consequence: agents using 'validate -fit-report' as a precheck for strict_fit=strict cannot see placeholder_overflow, title_wraps, slide_bounds_overflow, footer_collision, contrast_autofixed, table-row truncation, or diagram clamp findings. Generate then refuses, agent loops. Breaks the validate-as-strict-superset-of-generate-preflight invariant.

Implementation direction:
- mcp.go:661-665: replace generateFitReport(&input) with collectFitFindings(&input, templateLayouts, slideWidth, slideHeight). The function already exists in cmd/json2pptx/fit_findings_collect.go.
- Apply the same per-slide budget (8he8, closed).
- Render-time findings (result.FitFindings appended at mcp.go:400) are by definition unavailable without rendering. Two options: (a) document the gap explicitly, (b) lift Class-A emit sites that don't require XML serialization (autofit/text-fit predictions, table density, footer collision, bounds check) into a pipeline.PreflightFindings(input, analysis) callable from both surfaces. Recommend (a) for this bead and file (b) as a follow-up if needed.

Found by: agent-native-reviewer audit 2026-05-01. Depends on 8he8 (closed, per-slide budget).
close_reason: validate_input fit_report now uses collectFitFindings (text overflow + structural detectors) instead of just generateFitReport. Also changed dryRunOutput.FitFindings type to patterns.FitFinding for consistency with generate path.

title: Bring HTTP pattern errors to structured parity with MCP
description:
## Why
HTTP pattern endpoints already have a standardized outer error envelope, but they currently flatten semantic validation to err.Error() strings. That drops machine-usable path/code/fix information that already exists in MCP pattern validation and forces agents to scrape prose from HTTP responses.

## Scope
- Update POST /api/v1/patterns/{name}/validate.
- Update POST /api/v1/patterns/{name}/expand for pre-expansion validation failures.
- Preserve the current top-level HTTP error shape while adding structured diagnostics under details.
- Keep message strings human-readable for compatibility.

## Implementation Notes
- Reuse the shared diagnostic model from go-slide-creator-6gzn.
- Reuse or extract the existing splitValidationErrors / toPatternValidationError logic rather than duplicating behavior in HTTP.
- Include pattern name and affected field/path in machine-readable details.
- Do not leak MCP-specific wrappers into HTTP; only share the inner diagnostic representation.

## Candidate Files
- internal/api/patterns.go
- internal/api/errors/errors.go
- internal/api/patterns_test.go
- cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go (helper extraction if needed)

## References
- internal/api/patterns.go:75-167
- internal/api/errors/errors.go:11-21
- internal/api/errors/errors.go:61-78
- cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:711-959
design: Keep the existing HTTP error envelope intact but enrich error.details with structured issue entries derived from the shared diagnostic model. Reuse the same conversion helpers used by MCP pattern validation so HTTP and MCP expose equivalent remediation detail for the same domain failures.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Pattern validate and expand endpoints preserve the current HTTP error envelope. 2. error.details includes structured issue entries for semantic validation failures. 3. Joined validation errors are split into separate machine-readable items. 4. Tests cover parse failures, unsupported callout/cell overrides, and semantic validation parity with MCP.

title: Harden visual QA schema and teach explicit pass criteria
description:
Context
The visual QA path already asks the model for JSON, but the contract is still brittle. `internal/visualqa/prompts.go` only asks for a raw array of findings, and `internal/visualqa/agent.go` strips fences and unmarshals directly into a weak anonymous struct. There is no versioned schema, no local enum validation for category/severity beyond string assignment, and no repair strategy when the model drifts. The prompt also describes what to inspect, but it does not explicitly encode what a good result looks like in a reusable machine-readable way.

Problem
A single formatting wobble or category drift turns the entire QA result into `RawOutput` plus a parse error. Even when parsing succeeds, the model is not given enough explicit positive criteria to consistently distinguish acceptable output from merely non-broken output.

Scope
Move visual QA to a versioned, typed response object, validate it locally, and strengthen the prompt so the model understands both failure modes and pass criteria. Include a bounded repair path for malformed model output instead of silently degrading to opaque raw text.
design:
Implementation notes
- Replace the bare array contract with a small versioned object such as: `version`, `pass`, `summary`, `good_signals`, and `findings`.
- Add local validation for allowed severities, categories, required fields, and empty-response semantics.
- Add a repair path for malformed model output (for example one deterministic cleanup or retry pass) that still returns a structured parse diagnostic if recovery fails.
- Enrich slide-type prompts with explicit pass criteria and "looks good" guidance grounded in existing heuristics such as readability, footer clearance, hierarchy, and balance.

Key references
- `internal/visualqa/prompts.go:3-129`
- `internal/visualqa/agent.go:72-249`
- `internal/visualqa/types.go:1-76`
- `cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go:1157-1260`
acceptance_criteria:
- Visual QA responses use a documented, versioned schema instead of an untyped array contract.
- Parser code validates enum values and required fields before accepting findings.
- A malformed model response produces either a successful repaired parse or a structured parse diagnostic, not only an opaque raw string.
- Tests cover happy path JSON, fenced JSON, invalid enum/category, and malformed-response recovery failure.
notes:
Debate outcome
Keep the prompt improvements concrete and deterministic. The goal is not more prose from the model; it is a tighter contract plus clearer pass/fail criteria.

title: Add machine-readable diagnostics parity to HTTP convert and pattern endpoints
description:
Context
The HTTP API already has a standard error envelope, but it is much thinner than the repo's internal validation data. `internal/api/convert.go` and `internal/api/patterns.go` mostly emit `code + message + details`, while request decoding still allows silent unknown-field loss and success responses only expose warnings as raw strings. The server injects `X-Request-ID`, but the JSON payloads do not carry a request identifier or reusable diagnostic objects.

Problem
HTTP clients cannot reliably automate remediation because they do not receive the same typed feedback that the generator and pattern subsystems already know. They also cannot easily correlate a body-level failure with server logs.

Scope
Preserve the current HTTP API shapes where possible, but enrich both success and error payloads with machine-readable diagnostics and request correlation. Tighten decoding enough to stop silent contract drift without surprising existing consumers unnecessarily.
design:
Implementation notes
- Extend the shared HTTP error format with optional `request_id` and `diagnostics` fields while keeping existing `success/error` compatibility.
- For convert and pattern handlers, translate parse and validation failures into structured diagnostics with stable codes and JSON paths.
- Reject unknown fields or trailing junk in agent-relevant request bodies, or expose them as explicit diagnostics with a clear compatibility plan.
- Consider adding optional success-side `diagnostics` so warnings stop being string-only.

Key references
- `internal/api/errors/errors.go:9-84`
- `internal/api/convert.go:53-337`
- `internal/api/patterns.go:24-257`
- `internal/api/server.go:92-123`
acceptance_criteria:
- HTTP error payloads can include a request identifier and a structured diagnostics array without breaking existing top-level compatibility.
- Convert and pattern endpoints surface parse and validation failures with stable codes, paths, and fix hints where available.
- Tests cover at least one convert failure and one pattern failure end-to-end through the HTTP handlers.
- Warning-level feedback is no longer available only as unstructured strings on the HTTP path.
notes:
Debate outcome
Do not replace every HTTP success payload with a brand-new envelope in one shot. Enrich the existing shapes incrementally and document any strictness changes.

title: agent-native: add contract tests and docs for agent-visible response parity
description:
Problem
The repository documentation and skills already assume stronger agent-facing contracts than the implementation consistently provides. `docs/PATTERN_LIBRARY_SPEC.md:49-50` promises parity and structured errors, and `skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md:84-85` tells agents that validation and strict-fit findings are directly actionable. Without dedicated contract tests and doc updates, the code will keep drifting and agents will learn the wrong interface.

Scope
- Add regression tests that lock the intended response contracts across MCP, HTTP, and visual QA.
- Update the relevant docs/skills to match the actual response shapes after the implementation slices land.
- Document which fields are stable for machine consumption vs advisory/human-readable only.

Out of scope
- Re-implementing the diagnostic helpers themselves; this issue should consume the shared contracts from the dependent work.
design: Treat this as the final parity sweep after the contract work lands. Avoid duplicating long examples in multiple places; prefer one canonical response contract per surface and concise references elsewhere. Keep the tests focused on externally visible semantics, not internal helper names.
acceptance_criteria:
1. There are explicit regression tests for at least: MCP failure payload structure, HTTP pattern-validation parity, HTTP convert malformed-JSON diagnostics, and visual-QA invalid-model-output handling.
2. `docs/PATTERN_LIBRARY_SPEC.md`, `skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md`, and any other touched guidance accurately describe the shipped machine-readable contract.
3. The docs clearly distinguish stable machine fields from free-form explanatory text.
4. The issue links to or depends on the implementation slices that establish the contracts.
notes: This issue exists because the current docs are ahead of the code. It should not start until the shared MCP diagnostics, HTTP parity, and visual-QA contract issues have converged on the final shapes.
close_reason: Added contract regression tests for MCP error envelope, MCP generate/validate success, HTTP convert/pattern-validation error shapes, and visual QA Finding/Report/SchemaError shapes. Updated PATTERN_LIBRARY_SPEC.md D10 and SKILL.md to match actual diagnostics contract and distinguish stable vs advisory fields.

title: agent-native: harden visual QA output contract and teach the model what good looks like
description:
Problem
The visual QA agent asks for JSON, but its contract is still too loose for dependable automated use. The shared prompt in `internal/visualqa/prompts.go:3-129` lists defect categories and severities, yet it does not encode positive success criteria strongly enough for the model to anticipate what a well-formed slide should look like. The parser in `internal/visualqa/agent.go:209-248` accepts arbitrary category/severity strings without validation, so malformed or invented labels pass through until downstream consumers infer meaning from free text.

Why this matters
This code is supposed to help agents judge whether output looks acceptable, but today it is only robust when the model behaves perfectly. The repo already has stronger visual-quality guidance in `docs/VISUAL_CRITERIA.md` and `docs/REPAIR_LOOP.md`, and the current prompt does not fully leverage that material.

Scope
- Tighten the prompt contract so the model sees both failure modes and positive quality targets.
- Validate parsed findings against an allowed enum/schema and fail fast on malformed model output.
- Add a bounded repair path (for example, a single retry with schema-feedback) or return a structured parse error that callers can react to explicitly.

Out of scope
- Exposing visual QA as a new MCP/HTTP tool in this slice.
- Changing visual scoring methodology beyond what is needed for contract reliability.
design: Do not solve this only with prompt prose. Pair prompt improvements with parser validation so the model has guidance and the code enforces the contract. Keep the schema small and stable; avoid adding high-cardinality scoring rubrics that the parser cannot verify. Reuse the repo’s existing visual criteria language instead of inventing a second standard.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The system prompt and slide-type prompts explicitly encode allowed severities/categories and at least a concise notion of what acceptable output looks like, grounded in existing visual criteria docs.
2. `parseFindings` rejects unknown severities/categories or structurally invalid findings instead of silently accepting them.
3. The agent either performs one bounded retry on schema-invalid model output or returns a structured error that callers can distinguish from transport/API errors.
4. Tests cover invalid severity/category values, malformed JSON fences, and a no-issues response (`[]`).
notes: Key evidence: `internal/visualqa/prompts.go:7-26` specifies the expected JSON shape but not enforceable enums beyond prose; `internal/visualqa/agent.go:232-247` maps raw strings directly into findings; `docs/VISUAL_CRITERIA.md:5-31` and `skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md:82-90` already define clearer “good slide” expectations that the prompt can borrow.
close_reason: Hardened visual QA output contract: added allowed severity/category enums with ValidSeverity/ValidCategory validators, SchemaError type for distinguishable schema violations, positive quality targets in system prompt grounded in VISUAL_CRITERIA.md, and parseFindings now rejects unknown values. Tests cover invalid severity/category, malformed JSON, and empty array.

title: docs: MCP generate_presentation description missing pattern, defaults, strict_fit
description:
Agent-native audit 2026-04-24 (reviewer: agent-native-reviewer) found that cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:130-153 (mcpGenerateTool description) does not mention:

1. **slide.pattern** field (XOR with shape_grid) — primary-path pattern slot per PATTERN_LIBRARY_SPEC D1. Agents reading only the MCP tool description cannot discover named patterns.
2. **defaults** top-level block — {table_style, cell_style} swap-only, documented in docs/STYLE_DEFAULTS.md but absent from tool surface.
3. **strict_fit** enum — wired at mcp.go:158-161 but not described in the tool text; agents must guess it exists.
4. **split_slide** envelope — referenced in docs/REPAIR_LOOP.md but not in tool description.

Also mcpListTemplatesTool description (line 170) omits the full response shape: color_roles, table_styles, white_text_safe, data_format_hints_digest (commits 629a673, ce801d9).

## Fix
Extend tool descriptions to enumerate these fields. Keep compact — one line per major capability. Cross-reference STYLE_DEFAULTS.md and PATTERN_LIBRARY_SPEC.md.

## Acceptance
- mcpGenerateTool description mentions pattern, defaults, strict_fit, split_slide
- mcpListTemplatesTool description enumerates the response fields an agent needs
- Test: an agent running only MCP with tool descriptions (no docs access) can author a deck using pattern and defaults

## Why P2
Critical agent-native parity gap. Agent without doc access literally cannot discover these surfaces.
close_reason: Extended mcpGenerateTool description to document pattern (XOR with shape_grid), defaults block (table_style/cell_style), split_slide envelope, and strict_fit context. Extended mcpListTemplatesTool description to enumerate response shape: color_roles, table_styles, white_text_safe, data_format_hints_digest, chart/diagram capabilities.

title: docs: FIT_FINDINGS.md action taxonomy is stale vs code (refuse/shrink_or_split vs unfittable/warning)
description:
Narsil doc audit 2026-04-24 surfaced two action enums on the fit-report envelope:

- docs/FIT_FINDINGS.md:37-48 documents: refuse | shrink_or_split | review | info
- cmd/json2pptx/fit_report.go:19-29 (CLI NDJSON) emits: unfittable | warning
- cmd/json2pptx/fit_findings_collect.go:45-63 (MCP convertTextFitFinding) preserves Action='unfittable' from text-fit findings

patterns.ActionRank('unfittable') = -1 → MCP clients parsing sort-order will rank the most common text-overflow case as 'unknown severity'.

Exit-code rule (FIT_FINDINGS.md:226-232) also broken: doc says nonzero exit on action=='refuse'; validate.go:87 checks action=='unfittable'.

## Fix (pick one)
(a) Reconcile code to doc: rename CLI 'unfittable'→'refuse', 'warning'→'review' across fit_report.go and fit_findings_collect.go. Add 'unfittable' as alias mapping for one release. — cleaner long-term
(b) Reconcile doc to code: document both enums (CLI vs MCP) and add 'unfittable'/'warning' to ActionRank. — faster, ships mess forward

Recommend (a). Schema change; coordinate with to8a epic.

## Acceptance
- Single action vocabulary across CLI NDJSON and MCP envelope
- ActionRank covers all emitted values (no -1 cases)
- Exit-code check matches doc rule
- docs/REPAIR_LOOP.md references same vocabulary (currently uses CLI's 'unfittable'/'warning')
- Test: validate on each action case exits with documented code

## Why P2
Consumers misclassifying severity on the most common finding. Blocks any external tooling that parses fit-report.
close_reason: Reconciled action taxonomy: renamed 'unfittable'→'refuse' and 'warning'→'review' in CLI fit-report emitters, strict-mode checks, repair loop driver, and docs/REPAIR_LOOP.md. All actions now use single vocabulary matching docs/FIT_FINDINGS.md and ActionRank.

title: feature: theme_override.colors — warn on unknown scheme-color keys
description:
internal/types/template.go:186-192 (ApplyOverride) only writes when c.Name is already in the template's color list. Unrecognized keys (e.g., 'brand1', 'primary', 'Accent1' capitalized differently) are silently discarded. Not covered by additionalProperties:false because the Colors field deserializes to a typed map — the invalid keys deserialize fine and just get dropped at apply time.

## Fix
In ApplyOverride, collect unrecognized keys and return them to the caller (via fit-report warnings or a dedicated override-report). Emit:
ValidationError{Code:'unknown_scheme_color', Path:'theme_override.colors.Accent1', Fix:{Kind:'use_one_of', Params:{allowed:['accent1','accent2','dk1','lt1','lt2','dk2','hyperlink',...]}}}

## Acceptance
- Override keys that don't resolve → ValidationError surfaced in generate response warnings[] and MCP fit_findings
- Fix suggestion lists the 12 canonical theme color names
- Test: theme_override.colors with {'brand1': '#ff0000', 'Accent1': '#00ff00'} → 2 warnings, both with did_you_mean

## Why P2
Colors are the #1 thing agents try to tweak. Silent drops produce 'why won't it recolor?' loops. Narsil audit 2026-04-24 finding #18.
close_reason: ApplyOverride now returns warnings for unrecognized scheme-color keys. Warnings surface in pipeline ConvertResult.Warnings and MCP fit_findings. Added test for single and multiple unknown keys.

title: feature: JSON schema additionalProperties:false at entry points (strict unknown-key rejection)
description:
No entry point uses json.Decoder.DisallowUnknownFields or equivalent schema additionalProperties:false. Audit sites:
- cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go:175
- cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:215, 470
- cmd/json2pptx/dry_run.go:92
- internal/api/patterns.go:90, 128
- cmd/json2pptx/pattern_resolve.go:38, 47, 66

Typos like 'slide_tpye', 'accennt1', 'placeholderId' vs 'placeholder_id' are silently dropped — agent sees 'valid' and ships broken output.

## Approach (schema-first, per DA debate on 2026-04-24)
Add 'additionalProperties': false at each level of the JSON schema. Enforce at validate and generate. Graduated rollout via the schema version, NOT via a new strict_decode flag ladder (would conflict with --strict-fit ladder in to8a epic).

Graduation: ship 'warn' severity for one release with ValidationError{Code:'unknown_key', Path:'slides[0].slide_tpye', Fix:{Kind:'rename_field', Params:{from:'slide_tpye', to:'slide_type'}}}. Did-you-mean via stringdist over the schema's property list. Flip to 'error' in next release.

## Acceptance
- additionalProperties:false at each object level in cmd/json2pptx/json_schema.go
- Unknown-key → ValidationError with did_you_mean suggestion
- Suggestion uses stringdist (already in repo) over the schema's property set
- Test: each entry point accepts a deck with 'slide_tpye' typo → returns ValidationError, not a broken deck

## Why P2
Closes 4 findings (#15, #23, #26 from audit + adjacent). Most LLM regressions come from invented field names. Also removes the need for a second strict_decode flag ladder — single contract enforcement via schema.
close_reason: Implemented additionalProperties:false enforcement via unknown-key detection at all JSON input levels. Walks the full PresentationInput hierarchy (slides, content, shape_grid, tables, etc.) checking for unknown keys with did-you-mean suggestions via Levenshtein distance. Integrated as warnings at validate, MCP validate/generate, dry-run, and CLI generate entry points. 8 test cases cover typo detection, did-you-mean, nested levels, and clean input.

title: feature: JSON schema enum constraints for transition, transition_speed, build, background.fit
description:
cmd/json2pptx/json_schema.go:128-131,135-139 declares these fields as free-form strings. Unknown values (e.g., 'slide-left', 'snappy', 'stagger', 'contin') are accepted at validate but the generator emits no-op XML — the agent sees a PPTX without the requested effect and no diagnostic.

## Approach (schema-first, per devil's-advocate pushback on 2026-04-24)
Add 'enum': [...] constraints to the JSON schema. Validate against the same schema at all entry points. Do NOT add parallel enum-table validation in Go handler code per entry point — the schema is the single authoritative contract.

Enums to add:
- transition: fade, push, wipe, cover, uncover, cut, dissolve, none (source: internal/generator/transition.go:41-71 validTransitions)
- transition_speed: slow, med, fast
- background.fit: cover, stretch, tile
- build: enumerate accepted values from generator (currently only '' / default is honored — may need a PR to first expand, or schema reflects actual support)

## Envelope on failure
ValidationError{Code:'unknown_enum', Path:'slides[i].transition', Fix:{Kind:'use_one_of', Params:{allowed:['fade','push',...]}}}

## Acceptance
- All four fields enum-validated at validate and generate via shared schema
- Unknown enum → ValidationError with fix-suggestion listing allowed values
- No new CLI flag (do NOT create a second flag ladder parallel to --strict-fit)
- Test: each free-form field fuzzed with 5 bad values → all rejected with identical code across CLI/MCP/HTTP

## Why P2
Closes 3 findings (#17, #20, #21) from narsil audit with one schema-level change.
close_reason: Added enum validation for transition, transition_speed, build, and background.fit fields. Unknown values now produce ValidationError with code unknown_enum and use_one_of fix suggestion listing allowed values. Wired into all 4 entry points (validate, generate CLI, MCP generate, MCP validate, dry-run).

title: bug: validate/generate parity — pattern Callout support checked only after Expand
description:
cmd/json2pptx/pattern_resolve.go:85-89 validates CalloutSupport after Expand() succeeds. POST /patterns/:name/validate does not inspect Callout at all, so the validate endpoint says OK then expand rejects with CalloutUnsupported.

## Fix
Move the CalloutSupport check into Validate() (or mirror it in unmarshalPatternInputs). Emit ValidationError{Code:'callout_unsupported', Path:'pattern.callout', Fix:{Kind:'remove_field_or_switch_pattern', Params:{supports_callout_patterns:[...]}}}.

- Parity: validate and expand return the same error code/shape
- Fix suggests the set of patterns that DO support callout

Same class as fmsh (layout_id parity): breaks validate-as-precheck. Caught in narsil audit 2026-04-24.
close_reason: Implemented: moved callout support check before Expand, added check to CLI validate and MCP validate_pattern endpoints, added callout param to MCP tool, structured ValidationError with fix suggestion listing supported patterns

title: bug: validate/generate parity — layout_id not found is warn in validate, error in generate
description:
cmd/json2pptx/dry_run.go:262-267 emits a warning for unknown layout_id; the generator (internal/generator/stringdist.go:103-117 → singlepass/pipeline) hard-errors. MCP validate_input has the same warn-only behavior.

The result: 'json2pptx validate' returns valid:true with warnings, then 'json2pptx generate' fails. The agent cannot rely on validate as a precheck.

## Fix
Promote layout_id-not-found from warning to error across dry_run.go, validate_input MCP tool, and API /validate. Reuse layoutNotFoundError from stringdist.go so all surfaces emit the same patterns.ValidationError{Code:'unknown_layout_id', Path:'slides[i].layout_id', Fix:{Kind:'use_one_of', Params:{available:[...], did_you_mean:'...'}}}.

## Acceptance
- validate rejects unknown layout_id with same error code/shape as generate
- MCP validate_input and HTTP /validate both error on unknown layout_id
- did_you_mean suggestion included (stringdist already exists)
- Parity test: fuzz 20 typo layout_ids — all surfaces behave identically

## Why P2
validate is the agent's primary precheck. Broken parity wastes LLM turns. Caught in narsil audit 2026-04-24; consensus in adv/DA debate that this is a clear bug, not a design question.
close_reason: Promoted layout_id-not-found from warning to error in validate. Exported ClosestMatch/FormatAvailableIDs/LayoutNotFoundError from generator. Added ErrCodeUnknownLayoutID to patterns. Structured ValidationError with use_one_of fix and did_you_mean. Regression test covers typo, completely-wrong, and valid cases.

title: bug: MCP handle_generate swallows template-analysis errors; produces empty deck
description:
cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:258-277 — three nested 'err == nil' blocks silently discard OpenTemplate / ParseLayouts / ParseTheme failures. templateLayouts stays nil, generation proceeds with zero layouts, and the caller gets a near-empty PPTX with no diagnostic. The CLI/validate path at dry_run.go:137-142 already handles this correctly, so this is also a contract mismatch across surfaces.

## Fix
Wrap the chain and return mcp.NewToolResultError with the first-fail message. Mirror dry_run.go:137-142.

## Acceptance
- Broken/missing template file via MCP generate_presentation → tool result is error, not empty-deck success
- Test: POST generate_presentation with a template path that errors → response has .IsError=true + structured message
- Parity with CLI: same invalid template triggers the same error code on both surfaces

## Why P2
Silent empty-deck is among the worst failure modes for an LLM caller — nothing in the output indicates a problem. Caught in narsil audit 2026-04-24.
close_reason: Fixed: OpenTemplate/ParseLayouts errors now return mcp.NewToolResultError instead of being silently swallowed

title: Deck-local defaults block for table_style and cell_style (V1)
description:
Capture 95% of in-deck token-repetition savings without a new file, registry, or MCP surface.

## What changes
- Add optional top-level 'defaults' object to PresentationInput: { table_style: {...}, cell_style: {...} }
- New stage in cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go between json.Unmarshal and convertPresentationSlides that shallow-applies defaults onto each table block and shape-grid cell BEFORE struct validation
- Semantics: **swap-only** if a block sets an overriding field inline, that field wins; otherwise the defaults value is copied in. No deep merge. Matches internal/patterns/ precedent.
- Both 'table_style' and 'cell_style' supported (same code path; one kind key per block type)

## Acceptance
- Existing 14 examples/*.json parse and generate byte-identical output (defaults absent = current behavior)

- Cross-deck reuse (separate styles.json sidecar) — deferred to future bead
- MCP registry tools (list_styles, show_style) — deferred
- internal/stylelib/ package creation — deferred pending leaf-variant spike

## Risk
Low. Purely additive top-level field. Pre-struct application means zero churn in generator/ or jsonschema/.

## Anchors
- cmd/json2pptx/json_mode.go:267-339 — wiring hook
- internal/jsonschema/table.go:98-105 — shape to shallow-apply onto
- internal/jsonschema/shapegrid.go:53-123 — cell-style target

title: Minimal eval harness tests/quality/: 10 prompts, mechanical metrics, Haiku visual QA
description:
The reviewer asked: 'how do we MEASURE whether the proposal actually improves design quality?' Build the MINIMAL version (devil's advocate trim from 30→10 prompts, defer the gold-plating).

## Scope
Create tests/quality/ with:

### Golden prompt set (10 prompts to start, expand later)
- dense-table-16x6.txt (forces TDR violation if not split)
- comparison-matrix-5vendors.txt
- kpi-grid-9-tiles.txt
- narrative-strategy-15slide.txt
- two-tables-stacked.txt (forces structural smell)
- mixed-hex-and-semantic.txt (forces fill-mix smell)
- multiline-cells-table.txt (forces multiline-counting rule)
- pattern-card-grid-overflow.txt
- pattern-bmc-canvas-dense.txt
- (one more: any historical regression you've fixed; lock it in)

### Harness
- Bash/Go runner that takes each prompt, drives the skill via local Claude or MCP harness, captures generated JSON
- Runs json2pptx validate --fit-report=PATH on the JSON
- Computes mechanical metrics from the JSON:
  - TDR violation rate per slide (rows>7 || cols>6)
  - Hex-fill ratio (non-brand # fills / total fills)
  - Tiny-divider count (sibling pairs with computed gap < 3pt)
  - font_size < 9 count
  - Mixed semantic+hex slide count
- Computes render-time metrics from --fit-report:
  - unfittable rate per slide
  - shrink-invocation rate (proxy for 'agent asked too much')
- Runs the existing slide-visual-qa skill (Haiku-powered) on rendered images
- Outputs CSV: prompt, run_id, each metric, visual_qa_score

### Regression guard
- Run the harness against the 14 example decks in examples/
- Track delta vs prior baseline; any example whose visual QA drops >0.5 → flag for human review (NOT auto-fail)

### Anti-thrash (used by go-slide-creator-pending fix loop)
- Cap repair attempts at 2 per slide; after that, force split_slide

## Why P2 minimal (not P3)
Devil's advocate position: 'eval harness is multi-week.' Counter: 10 prompts + existing visual-qa skill is one week, not six. Without it, every other change in this epic is unguarded. 

Compromise: ship MINIMAL (10 prompts, mechanical metrics, existing visual-qa), defer the 30-prompt full set + custom dashboards.

## Acceptance criteria
- tests/quality/prompts/ with 10 .txt files
- tests/quality/run.sh (or go test) executes the harness
- CSV output with all metrics listed above
- README documents how to add a prompt
- Initial baseline committed; subsequent runs diff against baseline
- Existing examples/ validated as regression guard

title: split_slide declarative envelope (windowed-data only; NOT a general workflow primitive)
description:
The most contentious item in the debate. Devil's advocate concern: 'split_slide is workflow-in-engine — anti-pattern.' Advocate counter: 'pagination.go is the precedent; the agent already authoring N sibling slides has the duplicated-chrome failure mode the AI engineer flagged.'

CONSENSUS: ship as a DECLARATIVE envelope with explicit scope guards — windowed-data over a single source array, NOT a general loop construct. This is closer to the existing internal/pagination/pagination.go (which auto-paginates bullet overflow) than to a workflow runtime.

## JSON shape
```json
{ "type": "split_slide",
  "base": { "layout_id": "content", "title": "Vendor Matrix",
            "footer": {...},
            "table_value": { "rows": [...18 rows...] } },
  "split": { "by": "table.rows",
              "group_size": 6,
              "title_suffix": " ({page}/{total})",
              "repeat_headers": true } }
```

## Scope guards (reject at validate time)
- `split.by` enum: ONLY 'table.rows' for now (NOT shape_grid.cells, NOT content.bullets — those are separate beads if needed)
- Reject if base.table has merged header rows that would cross split boundaries
- Reject if base contains both a table and a chart/diagram (no semantics for splitting heterogeneous content)
- Reject if group_size <= 0 or > base.table.rows.length
- group_size > rows → emit ONE slide, no suffix (no error)
- {page}/{total} substitution happens at engine time; agent doesn't compute

## Engine behavior
- Walks split_slide nodes during pipeline expansion (similar to pattern expansion)
- Emits N regular slides with the data window applied
- Repeats table headers if repeat_headers: true
- Footer page numbers reflect post-split numbering
- Documents in docs/ that this is for windowed data only — agents authoring heterogeneous multi-slide narratives must write sibling slides

## Why P2 (and explicit scope)
Devil's advocate had a real point. Counter is that the existing pagination.go and slot_split.go set a precedent for declarative split — but neither handles tables. The fix isn't 'agent authors sibling slides' (which causes drift in title/footer/source/layout); it's 'engine handles ONE windowing primitive while staying out of general workflow.'

The narrow scope (only by: table.rows) is the agent-native compromise: the engine provides ergonomic chrome-replication for the ONE pattern that's painful to express, nothing more.

## Acceptance criteria
- New JSON type 'split_slide' in schema
- Validate-time rejection of all invalid combinations listed above
- Engine expands split_slide → N regular slides
- repeat_headers: true repeats first row on each output slide
- title_suffix substitution for {page}/{total}
- Footer page numbering correct post-split
- Examples: examples/split-slide-vendor-matrix.json (golden test)
- Documentation explicitly says 'windowed data only'
design: Both engineers agreed: keep narrow (only by: table.rows initially). Defer shape_grid.cells and content.bullets variants until requested.
notes:
Existing precedents reviewed:
- internal/pagination/pagination.go (auto-paginates bullets when frontmatter autopaginate set)
- internal/pipeline/slot_split.go:47 (maybeSplitSlide for slot-count overflow)

Neither handles tables — that's the gap split_slide closes.
close_reason: Implemented split_slide declarative envelope: custom UnmarshalJSON detects split_slide entries and expands inline to N regular slides by windowing table rows. Supports title_suffix with {page}/{total} substitution, repeat_headers, speaker_notes/source on first page only. Validates: by must be table.rows, group_size > 0, no table+chart mixing, no row_span crossing boundaries. 13 unit tests covering expansion, validation errors, edge cases, and full JSON round-trip. Example in examples/split-slide-vendor-matrix.json.

description:
Devil's advocate point that won the debate: do NOT extend internal/pipeline/overflow.go to detect structural smells. overflow.go:18-50 (estimateBodyOverflow) is a clean, narrow body-placeholder check returning bool. Conflating it with whole-slide structural linting (stacked tables, tiny dividers, hex+semantic mix) creates a god-function with mixed inputs/outputs/policy.

## Scope
Create a NEW file internal/pipeline/structural_smells.go (or internal/lint/structural.go) with a separate preflight that analyzes whole-slide structure and emits patterns.ValidationError warnings:

- **'Two-tables-one-grid'**: sibling tables in the same shape_grid where computed gap < 4pt or divider shape height < 4% of slide. Code: ErrCodeStackedTables.
- **'Tiny-divider stack'**: any sibling shape pair where computed gap < 3pt. Code: ErrCodeDividerTooThin.
- **'Hex-and-semantic mix'**: any slide containing BOTH non-allowlist hex fills AND semantic fills. Code: ErrCodeMixedFillScheme.

## Output
Same NDJSON envelope as --fit-report. Emitted by:
- json2pptx validate (warn-only)
- json2pptx generate --strict-fit=warn|strict (warn or refuse)

## Why P2 (after fit-report)
Builds on the same envelope and pipeline as --fit-report. Defer slightly so we can ship the cell-level signal first and see how often structural smells appear in real telemetry.

## Acceptance criteria
- New file internal/pipeline/structural_smells.go (or similar)
- DOES NOT modify overflow.go
- Three smell detectors with stable error codes
- Each detector has unit tests with positive and negative fixtures
- Detectors visit shape_grid AND content layouts (not just shape_grid)
- Documented schema for each smell in docs/
