title: Tests for concentric-rings: 3–5 layers across all templates incl. p-style, ladder fallback, split cells
description:
Parent epic: go-slide-creator-jk8j7 (circular / loop layout family). Label: circular-layouts-20261006.

## What / where
cmd/json2pptx/concentric_rings_matrix_test.go (M 3..5 × all templates incl. p-style: zero refusals, no shrink, >= 12pt), budget test, post-expand fit-report test, budget probe, schema_maxima pins, accent restraint, preview parity, compose 50% + nested cell (ladder engages, circles stay round). MCP intents: "onion model", "layers of influence", "core adjacent ecosystem", "nested layers" rank concentric-rings first.

## Verify
Green with `-short -race`; renders M=3 and M=5 on abstract and p-style attached.

## Family contract (applies to every bead in epic circular-layouts-20261006)

Native OOXML first: every shape is a preset-geometry `<p:sp>` emitted through the shape grid (internal/shapegrid). No SVG unless a geometry is provably impossible natively (none of the family needs it: `blockArc`, `circularArrow`, `pie`, `arc`, `donut`, `ellipse`, `chevron`, `homePlate`, `triangle`, `line` are all in internal/pptx/preset.go and shape cells already take `rotation`, `flip_h` and `adjustments` — internal/jsonschema/shapegrid.go:224-235, written at internal/shapegrid/shape.go:80-102).

Template parity, exactly like every other pattern:
- Colours are scheme names only (`accent1`, `dk2`, `lt2`...), never hex. Default accent = `ctx.DefaultAccent()`; tints via `ctx.ResolveSurface` / `neutralFillJSON` / `surfaceFillJSON`; ink on any fill chosen by measurement (internal/patterns/fill_contrast.go), so warm-coral / business-template / blue-corporate pick their own primary fill (docs/PATTERNS.md "Restrained accent defaults").
- Restrained accent: at most ONE solid-accent block >= 0.5in by default (the `highlight` item); structural segments / nodes take a neutral tint; `cell_accent_mode` (uniform | alternate | progressive) via `TextOverrides` + `ValidateCellAccentMode` + `ResolveCellAccent`. cmd/json2pptx/accent_restraint_gallery_test.go must pass without adding the pattern to `accentIsTheMessage`.
- Fonts: text sized at >= 12pt (`shapegrid.EffectiveTextSizePt`), rows sized from `writtenFitHeightPt` with `ctx.themeFonts()`, `MeasureFonts` stamped (expansion does this); `TestPatternExemplarsStoreNoAutofitShrink` and cmd/json2pptx/pattern_autofit_font_sweep_test.go must pass.
- Gaps wrapped in `ctx.Gap()`; filled shapes carry `noLine` (internal/patterns no_outline_test.go).
- Renders on ALL 10 templates including the local gitignored templates/p-style.pptx (abstract has the smallest body, 687x294pt; p-style 899x360pt) with zero refuse-class findings: cmd/json2pptx/template_pattern_matrix_test.go (non-short) is the gate.
- Works alone on a slide AND in split layouts: a horizontal `compose` segment of 50% and 60% width, a vertical segment, and a nested `shape_grid` cell `pattern` (see the split-layout bead). Circles must stay circles there (`fit: "contain"` on the ring cell, lattice edges recomputed from the actual cell).

Render recipe on this Mac (no pptx2jpg): `soffice --headless --convert-to pdf --outdir <dir> <pptx>` then `pdftoppm -r 80 -png <pdf> <prefix>`; private LO profile if soffice hangs (memory: libreoffice-macos-restore-modal-hang). Judge the actual render, including p-style, not green tests alone (memory: layouts-must-not-look-like-ai-html, native-slide-output-standard).

Angles: OOXML preset angles are in 60000ths of a degree, 0 = 3 o'clock, positive = clockwise. `blockArc` adj1 = start angle, adj2 = end angle, adj3 = ring thickness as a fraction of the short side (1/100000); `circularArrow` adj1 = shaft thickness, adj2 = arrowhead end angle, adj3 = start angle, adj4 = arrowhead sweep, adj5 = head width — confirm against ECMA-376 presetShapeDefinitions.xml and pin the chosen values with the golden.

Docs are part of the deliverable, same commit (CLAUDE.md "Skill, Docs, and Code Sync" policy is mandatory): a pattern bead is not done until it has (1) its CLAUDE.md "Named Patterns" table row (TestPatternDocumentationMatchesRegistry), (2) its skills/generate-deck/PATTERNS.md copy-budget paragraph (per item count; no static index — TestAgentPatternGuideUsesLiveCatalog), (3) its docs/PATTERNS.md selection-table row and peer-fill category entry plus any new authoring-contract section, (4) a docs/SCHEMA_CHANGELOG.md entry under the family's SchemaVersion, (5) a docs/wiki/visual-vocabulary.md entry (when to use it, when not, the sibling to prefer) and, where it has a split recipe, a docs/wiki/split-and-complex-layouts.md recipe whose YAML block validates (internal/semantic tests validate wiki YAML blocks), (6) internal/semantic/reach.go entry, (7) recommend.go rules. Anything agent-visible (new override key, new finding, new values field) also lands in skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md or its guide files, within the 100 KiB bundle budget (TestGenerateDeckSkillBudgets — memory: skill-and-tools-list-byte-budgets; trim elsewhere if needed).

Before closing any code bead: `make lint`, `go test ./internal/patterns/... -count=1`, `go test ./cmd/json2pptx -run 'TestPatternDocumentationMatchesRegistry|TestEveryPatternDeclaresMotif|TestPatternReachCoversTheRegistry|TestSchemaMaximaStayReadable|TestRecommendVisualEveryPatternIsAuthorable|TestPatternSmoke_AllPatterns|TestAccentRestraintGallery' -count=1`, then `go test ./... -short -race` (CI shape; see memory ci-differs-from-local-test-run). Any new file in internal/patterns stales templates/previews manifests — run `make template-previews` ONCE at the end of the family (see the docs/previews bead), not per pattern.

title: Margins/grid are engine constants, not template-level; grid alignment check is opt-in
description:
Principle: every element snaps to an invisible grid with consistent outer margins (Duarte slide:ology on grids; '12-column grid… margins of 5-10% from all edges… 30-40% empty space', https://slidebazaar.com/blog/the-invisible-grid-system-that-makes-every-slide-layout-look-intentional/; Gestalt proximity/alignment, https://www.mlcpresentations.com/en/faq/what-are-the-gestalt-principles-and-how-do-they-apply-to-slide-design/). Repo: the content zone is template-derived from placeholders (cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go:141-169), but gutters (`colGap = 8`, `rowGap = 8`, internal/shapegrid/grid.go:22-30), the chrome gap (`gridChromeGapPt = 9.0`, shape_grid.go:587), the title→body gap (`bodyZoneTitleGapPt = 18.0`, title_band.go:30) and the 0.5cm text inset are engine constants; template metadata (internal/types/template.go:24-89) has no margin/grid/column keys and all 9 bundled templates carry only name/description/palette fields; pattern sizing shrinks by hardcoded 0.955 x 0.855 before the zone is known (internal/patterns/content_sizing.go:112-131); the `grid_violation` check (cmd/json2pptx/grid_rhythm.go:323-420) runs only when a `grid` is configured, so by default nothing verifies that titles, content tops and left edges line up across slides. Evidence: p-style vs midnight-blue renders (qbr-p-style/slide-4.png vs qbr-midnight-blue/slide-4.png) show different title-to-content gaps and chart-to-insights gutters because each is a constant applied to differing placeholder boxes rather than a template grid. Why it matters: 'titles should not move when you flip through the deck' (Deckary) — consistency across templates and slides is what separates a system from a collection of patterns.

ACCEPTANCE:
Template metadata gains `grid: {margin_pct, columns, gutter_pt, title_gap_pt}` with engine defaults when absent; shapegrid, patterns and chart frames read gutters/margins from it; `grid_violation` runs by default against the template grid (title baseline, content top, left margin) and is reported in score_deck; docs/TEMPLATE_SPEC.md documents the keys and `examine-template` prints them.

title: Unify the type scale: dead tokens, 17 literal pattern sizes, svggen's own scale, RULES.md table contradicting the 12pt f
description:
Principle: a deck uses one type scale with named roles (display/headline/title/body/label) built from a fixed ratio, and at most ~4 sizes per slide (Material Design 3 type roles, https://m3.material.io/styles/typography/applying-type; modular scale ratios 1.2-1.333, https://typescale.org/; 'four font sizes maximum, built from a single scale', https://www.j-a-b.net/how-to-design-a-google-slides-or-powerpoint-presentation-that-looks-professional-layout-fonts-and-color-rules/). Repo: internal/tokens/typography.go:91-104 defines steps 10/11/12/14/18/28 (+40-48 KPI) whose adjacent ratios are 1.10/1.09/1.17/1.29/1.56 — not a scale; the role tokens in tokens.go:36-90 (GridHeader*, CardTitle*, CardBody*, Footnote*, GridGap*, CellInset*) are read by no non-test code and contradict live values (inset token 8pt vs real 0.5cm = 14.2pt in internal/pptx/shape_text_inset.go:32; card body 9-11pt vs the 11/12pt floors); no file in internal/patterns imports tokens — defaults are literals (`agendaNumberSize = 28`, KPI 36 in kpi_common.go:153 which is outside the 40-48 token range, stathero 120), 17 distinct values across 89 pattern files, snapped down at render time; svggen has its own scale 18/15/13/12/10 (svggen/style.go:563-568) so chart text never sits on the slide scale; line height is the literal 1.2 in ~15 places. Why it matters: cross-slide consistency ('font sizes for same element types must remain identical across all slides', Deckary) is the thing reviewers notice first; today it emerges from snapping rather than design, and chart text visibly differs from grid text on the same slide (compare 'Key Insights' 14pt vs chart title 13pt in qbr-midnight-blue/slide-4.png).

Merged findings from other review areas:
- [agent-guidance] RULES.md typography table (9-11pt body, 7-8pt footnotes) contradicts the 12pt readable floor the engine enforces: skills/generate-deck/RULES.md:21-33 tells agents 'Do not invent font sizes' and lists Card body 9-11pt and Footnote/source 7-8pt as 'the authoritative cross-pattern defaults' (mirroring internal/tokens/tokens.go:51-67). Two paragraphs later (RULES.md:35) the same file says 11pt is the body minimum and 10pt is allowed only in tables; SKILL.md:66-71 says grid text below the 12pt floor is refused as TEXT_BELOW_READABLE_MIN and WORKFLOW.md's rubric fails any text under ~10pt. An agent hand-authoring a shape_grid from the table writes 9-10pt card bodies and 7-8pt footnotes that the engine then snaps or refuses (or, in design_mode free where keepAuthoredTextSizes applies, cmd/json2pptx/defaults.go:62-77, ships as unreadable 8pt text). The guidance should name one scale.

ACCEPTANCE:
One `tokens.TypeRole` table (display, title, lead, subhead, body, caption, kpi) with sizes derived from a documented ratio and `viewing_mode` multipliers; patterns and svggen resolve sizes through it (no numeric literals in `ResolveSize` defaults); dead tokens removed or wired; a test asserts every pattern default is on-scale and that svggen title/body/caption equal the slide subhead/body/caption; RULES.md typography table regenerated from the tokens.
RULES.md typography table lists sizes that sit on the enforced type scale (body >= 12pt in constrained mode, caption 10pt only in tables/dense matrices, source line 9pt) and tokens.go constants/tokens_test.go are reconciled with the readability floor; no shipped doc tells agents to use 7-9pt text.

title: Preview pattern expansion omits template theme used by generation
description:
WHAT
resolveSlidePattern and resolveSlideCompose in cmd/json2pptx/mcp_preview.go construct patterns.ExpandContext without Theme, although previewTemplateContext already holds parsed template theme. Generate supplies patternThemeFromDiag(diagCtx). Content-sized patterns use ctx.Theme.BodyFont for text measurement and may choose different sizes or warnings in preview than generation for templates whose font metrics differ from the fallback.

REPRO
Preview and generate a dense KPI or chevron pattern on a template with a non-default body font. Compare expanded row heights, font sizes, and fit warnings with the generated shape grid.

FIX
Build preview ExpandContext from the same template theme and font data as generation, then add a parity test with a template/body font that changes measured fit decisions.
notes: Preview pattern and compose expansion now receive template theme colors and BodyFont through previewPatternTheme, matching generation. Modern-yellow (non-default Segoe UI body font) parity test compares preview-resolved raw shapes with generation for dense KPI and horizontal compose. Full Go suite, lint, and build pass. Coupled generation BodyFont omission filed and fixed as go-slide-creator-ex74s.
close_reason: Closed

title: Explicit pattern bounds do not inform content-sized expansion
description:
WHAT
PatternInput.Bounds and MaxHeightPct replace the grid's render rectangle after a named pattern has expanded (cmd/json2pptx/pattern_resolve.go). Content-sized pattern decisions still use ExpandContext.LayoutBounds for the full slide content area. A pattern constrained to a shorter or narrower explicit rectangle can therefore choose card height, icon position, or text fit from a box larger than its final render bounds.

REPRO
Render kpi-3up or another content-sized pattern with bounds height 30% or a narrow bounds width on a content slide. Compare expansion row MaxHeight and font-fit decisions with resolveGridBounds of the expanded grid; the decisions use the full layout rectangle while rendering uses the explicit subrectangle.

FIX
Resolve effective PatternInput bounds before content-sized expansion, or expose both the layout content rectangle and the final pattern rectangle in ExpandContext. Preserve documented relative/absolute bounds semantics, then test constrained KPI and flow patterns against actual rendered cell bounds.
notes: expandPattern now resolves author bounds before pattern expansion and passes the effective rectangle, including template content-zone clamping, to content-sized sizing and PostExpandWarnings. Generation, preview, and fit preflight supply the same zone. Compose strips ignored segment bounds before expansion. Regression covers narrow KPI font, 30% KPI/flow row heights and resolved cells, chrome-clamped explicit bounds, compose warning parity, and preview/generation raw-shape parity. Full Go suite, lint, build, and two-slide midnight-blue render pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: recommend_pattern scores arch-stack 0.9 high on 'pricing tiers', and there is no sankey to recommend at all
description:

   The difference is semantic, not structural. Fixing it means tuning the rules table (narrow arch-stack keywords, or add a pricing/plans rule), which wants its own evidence pass over a corpus of intents rather than a guess.

title: agenda-with-images number badges stretch into tall slabs on short agendas
description:
Found while fixing go-slide-creator-jodu (2026-09-20).

WHAT
The number badge cell is a roundRect filled with the accent colour and it fills its whole grid cell. Content rows use AutoHeight with MinHeight 48, so on a short agenda the rows stretch to fill the content zone and the badge stretches with them: on a 3-item agenda on midnight-blue the "01" badge renders ~228x150px — a 3:2 accent slab, not a numbered square. With 5-6 items the rows are short enough that it reads correctly.

Secondary, same slide: the divider rows are GridRowInput{Height: 1}, and internal/jsonschema/shapegrid.go documents Height as a PERCENTAGE of grid height, not points. 1% of the content zone renders as a ~6pt tinted band rather than the hairline the code comment ("thin divider rows") intends. A round-2 reviewer read those bands as stray lines across the slide.

WHERE
internal/patterns/agenda_with_images.go — numberCell construction and the divider row Height.

HOW
Cap the badge to a square: give the number cell a fixed size (or centre a fixed-size badge inside the cell) so it does not scale with row height. For the divider, either express the height in the unit that gives a hairline or accept the band deliberately and fix the comment.

VERIFY
Render a 3-item and a 6-item agenda-with-images on midnight-blue and forest-green: the badge is the same square in both, and the divider is a hairline.

EVIDENCE
/tmp/jodu/after.mb/s-1.png (3 items, slab badges) vs /tmp/jodu/after.mb/s-2.png (5 items, correct)
close_reason:
Fixed in a5c54442 (pushed to main), as far as it can be fixed independently — the residual is go-slide-creator-byr2b, with measurements below.

I FILED THIS BEAD MYSELF AND GOT THE DIRECTION WRONG. I wrote "on a 3-item agenda the badge renders ~228x150px — a slab; with 5-6 items the rows are short enough that it reads correctly". Measured from the renders, it is the opposite: 3 items gives 1.5:1 and 5 items gives 2.4:1. The badge is never square at any count, and MORE items makes it worse. Corrected here so the record is not misleading.

ROOT CAUSE: the badge shape filled its grid cell, and that cell is 18% of the content width by whatever height the row took. Its proportions were the row proportions, never the badge.

FIX: buildAgendaBadgeCell centres the badge in a [gutter, badge, gutter] sub-grid at agendaBadgeWidthPct of the cell width, computed as the estimated row height over the badge column width. At 100% it emits the flat cell with no pointless nesting.

ONLY THE WIDTH IS NARROWED, and that is a proof rather than an omission: for the badge to be too TALL the row would have to exceed 18% of the content width; at this pattern minimum of 3 items the rows are already shorter than that and only shrink as items grow. I implemented the height branch first, then established it is unreachable and removed it rather than ship a branch that cannot run.

A 35% MINIMUM WIDTH WAS IMPLEMENTED AND REMOVED. It bound at 5 and 6 items and reinstated the slab it was meant to prevent — a 6-item badge came out 53x42pt (1.26:1). The test caught it. The badge is square or it is not; the row height already shrinks with the item count.

RESIDUAL, MEASURED, NOT MINE TO FIX HERE: on the generate path ExpandContext carries no LayoutBounds, so contentAreaPt reports the full-slide default rather than the template real content zone. Probed both:
  generate path (no LayoutBounds): content 864x389pt -> col 159pt, row 122pt (n=3) -> width 77%
  true midnight-blue zone:          content 828x308pt -> col 152pt, row  95pt (n=3) -> width 63%
So the badge lands about 20% wider than square on generate. That is go-slide-creator-byr2b exactly; when it lands this becomes square with NO change here, which is why the estimate is written against contentAreaPt rather than hard-coded numbers.

VISUAL EVIDENCE (midnight-blue, soffice + pdftoppm -r 110, 2x crops, all viewed):
  before /tmp/jodu/badges.png        3-item 1.5:1, 5-item 2.4:1
  after  /tmp/jodu/badges-final.png  5-item SQUARE, 3-item 1.3:1 (byr2b residual)

TESTS: TestAgendaBadgeIsNarrowedTowardSquare (aspect within 0.9-1.1 at 3,4,5,6 items against the true zone), TestAgendaBadgeNarrowsAsItemsGrow (monotonic — a non-monotonic rule would hand some count a slab back), TestAgendaBadgeCellIsFlatWhenItFills (no sub-grid when the badge fills, equal gutters when it does not). Four existing tests read the badge through Cells[0].Shape, which is now nested; agendaBadgeShape finds it either way rather than each test knowing the structure.

title: modern-yellow Statement body placeholder cannot hold P3/P4 text-fit content
description:
Split out of go-slide-creator-nlrg (closed): making the preflight and the renderer share the master bodyStyle exposed this.

WHAT
TestTextFitCorpus now fails for templates/modern-yellow.pptx, layout "Statement", placeholder "body":
  level=P3: got severity P4 (FontScale=60000 LnSpcReduction=10000 Overflow=false), expected <= P3
  level=P4: got severity P5 (FontScale=60000 LnSpcReduction=20000 Overflow=true), expected <= P4

WHY IT SURFACED NOW (not a regression)
Before nlrg, a body placeholder whose layout declares no explicit font size reported FontSize 0, and textfit measured it at its own default. applyInheritedBodyText now fills the size (and line spacing, and space-before) from the master bodyStyle, which is what the text actually renders at. The corpus is measuring the truth for the first time; the numbers got worse because the measurement got right, not because the engine did.

OPEN QUESTION, worth answering before "repairing" anything
A "Statement" layout is meant for one short statement. The corpus walks EVERY body placeholder on EVERY layout at six density levels, so it asks a statement placeholder to hold P3/P4 paragraph counts. That may be the corpus over-testing rather than the template under-delivering. Decide which before changing the template: either exempt statement-role placeholders from the dense levels (Role is available on PlaceholderInfo — PlaceholderRole classification), or enlarge/repair the placeholder.

CURRENT STATE
templates/modern-yellow.pptx sha256 2c54ce1839c482ae79350652020c3e7c9242b5465ae926de59fa3d02f808687a is on the text-fit allow-list citing this bead, so the failures are logged rather than fatal. Repairing the template changes its sha256 and automatically restores the gate. The allow-list file comment says the list MUST be empty once go-slide-creator-vqad and its children land — this entry is the only one.

VERIFY
go test ./cmd/json2pptx/ -run TestTextFitCorpus passes with the allow-list entry REMOVED.
close_reason:
Resolved in ad16b8e5 (pushed to main). The bead OPEN QUESTION is answered with measurements: the corpus was over-testing, not the template under-delivering.

THE MEASUREMENT (this is what decided it):
  modern-yellow Statement body: 7118350x2800350 EMU = 560x220pt, sz="quarter", idx=10
  master bodyStyle lvl1: sz=2800 (28pt), spcBef=1000 (10pt), lnSpc=90000
  classification per level: P0->P0  P1->P0  P2->P2  P3->P4  P4->P5  P5->P5
So it holds P0, P1 and P2 CLEANLY and misses only at P3 (8 paragraphs, 590 chars) and P4 (12 paragraphs, 1163 chars). Eight ~70-char paragraphs at 28pt wrap to two lines each in a 560pt-wide box: 8 x 2 x 25.2pt + 8 x 10pt spcBef = ~480pt of text in a 220pt box. That is arithmetic, not a defect. A Statement layout inherits display-sized type from the master precisely so ONE line lands hard.

ALSO MEASURED: modern-yellow is the ONLY bundled template with a statement-tagged layout carrying a measurable body (probed all nine).

FIX (bead option 1, "exempt statement-role placeholders from the dense levels"): collectTextFitFailures now holds a statement-tagged layout to statementMaxLevel = P2 and skips P3/P4. P5 is the deliberate-overflow level and is unaffected.

THE EXEMPTION READS THE TAG, NOT THE GEOMETRY. I considered keying off the inherited font size (a 28pt body is by construction a display surface on any template) and rejected it: a body that merely renders large might be a genuinely MIS-SIZED placeholder, which must still fail the gate. The `statement` tag comes from the template author naming the layout, via internal/template/classifier.go, so the exemption follows a declared intent rather than a guess. Note the bead suggested PlaceholderRole, but there is no PlaceholderRoleStatement — the roles are title/subtitle/eyebrow/section_number/body/image/chart/footer/page_number/date/other — so the layout TAG is the available signal.

NARROWNESS IS PINNED BY TESTS, because an exemption that quietly widens is worse than the failure:
  TestStatementExemptionStaysNarrow  — statementMaxLevel must keep P0-P2 enforced and must not reach P5
  TestIsStatementLayoutReadsTheTag   — tag-driven, table-tested
  TestStatementLayoutsAreStillRare   — asserts exactly ONE bundled template has a statement body, so if a second appears the measurement that justified this gets redone rather than assumed

VERIFY (bead: TestTextFitCorpus passes with the allow-list emptied): all nine templates PASS with "exceptions": [] — abstract, blue-corporate, business-template, forest-green, midnight-blue, modern-template, modern-yellow, modern, warm-coral. allowlist.json is now empty, which is what its own comment requires ("MUST be empty once go-slide-creator-vqad and its children land"); this entry was the last one. TestTextFitCorpus_AllowlistEntriesPointAtRealTemplates skips on an empty list, as designed.

NO TEMPLATE CHANGE: modern-yellow.pptx is untouched, so its sha256 is unchanged. Nothing was "repaired" that was not broken.

NO GOLDEN DRIFT: pre-push rebaseline check produced an empty diff.

DOCS: no agent-visible surface changed — this is a test-gate scoping decision. The reasoning lives in the code comments on statementMaxLevel and isStatementLayout, where the next reader of the gate will find it.

title: heatmap: row labels overlap and column headers clip past the documented cell limit, with no finding
description:
Split from go-slide-creator-vdvs, whose VERIFY covered only the contrast half (now fixed: each cell's value is lt1 or dk1 by measured contrast).

The other half of the charts-diagrams report: a 14x14 heatmap stress case overlaps ALL row labels and clips the column headers, and nothing reports it. The native heatmap builder divides the available height by the row count without a floor, so past a certain density the label boxes are shorter than their text; nothing checks the resulting geometry.

WHERE: internal/generator/heatmap_shapes.go (generateHeatmapGroupXML label placement, heatmapHeaderFontSize), and whatever detector would carry the finding — GRID_DIAGRAM_NARROW is the nearest existing one but it is about cell width, not label density.

HOW (from the bead): truncate or rotate row labels rather than overlapping them, and emit a label-overlap finding above the documented cell limit (the docs state ~200 cells).

VERIFY: a 14x14 heatmap renders with legible, non-overlapping row labels (truncated with an ellipsis is acceptable) and unclipped column headers, OR emits a finding naming the cell count and the limit; a 5x4 heatmap is unchanged and draws nothing.
close_reason:
Fixed in 081c4ba6 (pushed to main).

REPRODUCING TOOK TWO TRIES, WORTH RECORDING: a 14x14 heatmap with ordinary labels ("Workstream A delivery") does NOT reproduce — the labels wrap to two tight lines and stay readable, headers unclipped. The defect needs LONG labels. With "Geschaeftsbereich A Wirtschaftlichkeitsberechnung" x "Lieferantenrahmenvertraege N" it reproduces exactly as reported: every row label wraps to three lines inside a one-line box and renders as overlapping black mush, and the column headers break mid-word and clip ("Lieferan/tenrahm/envertra", the "ege 1" gone). Before: /tmp/heat/stress/s-1.png.

FIX (internal/generator/heatmap_labels.go, new): labels are measured with textfit against the box they will be drawn into and shortened with an ellipsis.
- Registration now resolves placeholderBounds BEFORE encoding the meta, so the fitting happens against real geometry and the shortened labels flow through encodeHeatmapMeta unchanged.
- heatmapGeometryFor is the single definition of the label-band/cell arithmetic; generateHeatmapGroupXML now calls it too, so fitting and drawing cannot drift.
- Binary search over rune count, so a long label costs a handful of measurements.

THE NON-OBVIOUS PART, AND THE TEST THAT CAUGHT IT: my first draft measured against the box HEIGHT and bailed out when nothing fit. In a dense grid the row can be shorter than a single line (14 rows measured 533400 EMU against a 222700 EMU row), so "nothing fits" was the common case and the label was left alone — still wrapping to three lines, still overlapping. The written test failed on exactly this. The budget is now a LINE COUNT with a floor of one line: one line overflows its row a little, three lines overlap the neighbours. heatmapLineBudget is shared by the fitter and the test assertion.

FINDING (bead asked for one naming the cell count and the limit): GRID_DIAGRAM_NARROW is emitted when any label had to be shortened — which is the measured condition, better than a magic ~200. Message names the grid: "heatmap is 14x14 (196 cells), so 28 label(s) do not fit their row/column and were shortened with an ellipsis". fix.kind reduce_text, fix.params {diagram_type, rows, columns, cells, labels_shortened}, action review. Verified reaching the JSON report via generate -json-output-report:
  grid_diagram_narrow /slides/0/content/body  heatmap is 14x14 (196 cells), so 28 label(s)...
  grid_diagram_narrow /slides/1/content/body  heatmap is 20x20 (400 cells), so 20 label(s)...
It is generation-time, consistent with the existing GRID_DIAGRAM_NARROW which docs already state is generate-time because it needs resolved bounds.

VERIFY (bead: 14x14 renders with legible non-overlapping row labels, truncated with ellipsis acceptable, unclipped column headers, OR emits a finding; 5x4 unchanged and draws nothing): all of it, and both halves rather than the OR.
  after 14x14 /tmp/heat/after2/s-1.png — one line per label, no overlap, no mid-word clipping
  after 20x20 /tmp/heat/after2/s-2.png — 400 cells, "Row 1 works..." through "Row 20 work..." all distinguishable
  5x4 control: magick compare -metric AE = 0 against the pre-fix render, and zero findings

TESTS: internal/generator/heatmap_labels_test.go — sparse untouched, dense shortened, a short placeholder shortening the ROW labels specifically, the finding naming the grid, geometry parity between fitting and drawing, and the impossible-box case. The dense/short tests assert the POSTCONDITION (every label fits its line budget) rather than a truncation count, because whether a given label needs cutting depends on the placeholder.

title: Structural fills in dual-org-ladder and process-grid-2row put two unrelated brand hues side by side
description:
Reported with go-slide-creator-ah5s (gallery). ah5s fixed the measurable half — value-chain's highlight is now chosen by contrast — but its sibling report covers two patterns whose structural fills are raw scheme slots:

- dual-org-ladder: org_a header accent1, org_b header accent2. On forest-green that is green beside bright orange (#2E7D32 / #FF8F00); on midnight-blue navy beside red.
- process-grid-2row: row1 accent1 + row2 accent3. On forest-green green + bright blue (#2E7D32 / #1565C0); on midnight-blue blue + amber.

These are not contrast failures — both pairs are perfectly distinguishable. The complaint is harmony: two unrelated brand hues carrying no semantic difference (the two orgs are peers; the two rows are parallel tracks). A tint ladder of ONE accent (accent1 at 100% and at lumMod 60%, say) would read as 'two of the same kind' rather than 'two different brands'.

WHERE: internal/patterns/dualorgladder.go (accent_a/accent_b defaults), internal/patterns/processgrid2row.go (row1/row2 accent defaults).

VERIFY: render both patterns on all four bundled templates; the two structural fills are the same hue at different lightness, still >= 3:1 apart from each other or from their text; no deck that sets the accents explicitly changes.

NOTE: also worth deciding whether dk2-filled structures (a chromatic near-black in three of four templates) should be a neutral instead — the same gallery finding raised it.

Fixed in bdc7bfb5 (pushed to main).

REPRODUCED on all four bundled templates before changing anything (/tmp/at7/before-dual.png, /tmp/at7/before-grid.png), and the bead description is exact:

  process-grid-2row forest-green: green row over bright BLUE; midnight-blue: blue over amber
Confirmed the bead framing too — none of these is a contrast failure. The pairs are perfectly legible. The problem is that two unrelated brand hues say "two different things" about halves that are peers.

FIX: new internal/patterns/peer_fill.go holds the shared convention — peerTone(accent) / peerFillJSON(accent) render the SAME accent at lumMod 65000.
- dual-org-ladder: accent_b defaults to a darker tone of accent_a. The per-row accent BARS follow (an accent bar takes a bare scheme name with no tint, so the peer default reuses accent_a rather than accent2 — the bar marks the same org the header does).

title: Unify degrade advisories under a SEMANTIC_PATTERN_DEGRADED code
description:
Seven slide kinds now report 'you asked for a visual, you are getting bullets' as SEMANTIC_DENSITY: executive_summary, kpi_snapshot, architecture, process, roadmap, chart_insight, comparison, option_matrix. The code is a misnomer for the budget cases — a KPI value of 20 characters is not a density problem — and an agent cannot tell a count advisory from a degrade one without parsing the message.

PROPOSAL (from go-slide-creator-5ok4, whose VERIFY named the code): add diagnostics.CodeSemanticPatternDegraded = 'SEMANTIC_PATTERN_DEGRADED' and move every 'otherwise it degrades to a bullet list' advisory onto it, keeping SEMANTIC_DENSITY for count-range advice that does NOT change the visual. Carry fix.params {from: '<pattern>', to: 'content-bullets', reason} so the agent can act without reading prose.

SCOPE: internal/diagnostics/codes.go (constant + AllCodes + classifyMap), internal/semantic/validate.go (the eight call sites), describe_finding metadata in internal/patterns/finding_meta.go, and docs sync — SKILL.md, skills/generate-deck/FINDINGS.md, docs/SCHEMA_CHANGELOG.md. Tests asserting SEMANTIC_DENSITY on degrade paths must move with it.

VERIFY: every advisory that announces a fallback carries the new code; no advisory that only recommends a count range does; describe_finding('SEMANTIC_PATTERN_DEGRADED') returns remediation steps; the examples corpus validates with no new findings.
close_reason:
Implemented in 5924bd72 (pushed to main).

WHAT SHIPPED
- diagnostics.CodeSemanticPatternDegraded = "SEMANTIC_PATTERN_DEGRADED", registered in AllCodes and the INPUT namespace of classifyMap (envelope.go), with a describe.go entry.
- 25 call sites in internal/semantic/validate.go moved onto it via a new internal/semantic/degrade.go carrying degrade() / degradeFix() plus the target and reason vocabularies. Covers every kind the bead named: agenda, team, stat, architecture, timeline, matrix_2x2, framework, image_case, decision, process, roadmap, executive_summary, kpi_snapshot, option_matrix, chart_insight, comparison.
- SEMANTIC_DENSITY keeps only advisories that do NOT cost the slide its visual: over-wide/over-tall table, a row with fewer cells than its header, an unbalanced comparison a card-grid still draws, a dropped table-highlight badge. Its describe entry was rewritten to say so.

TWO THINGS THE BEAD DID NOT ANTICIPATE
1. Two comparison advisories pick their wording at RUNTIME — "degrades to a bullet list" when no pattern can take the content, "renders as <pattern>" when one can. A code cannot be conditional on a string, so those sites now branch first and emit whichever code matches what actually happens. Existing tests for both still pass on SEMANTIC_DENSITY because their fixtures are the card-grid-rescued case.
2. The bead said carry fix.params {from, to, reason}. The two chart_insight data sites already had a BETTER fix (provide_value with expected_shape/example). Replacing it would have been a regression, so degradeFix merges the three params into whatever fix the caller supplies. Every finding on the code answers the same three questions however it was raised — verified by test.

FIX CONTRACT: fix.kind "restore_visual" (new ADVISORY kind registered in internal/patterns/fix_kinds.go with guidance + alternatives reduce_items/add_items/reduce_text/split_pattern), params {from, to, reason}. to is one of content-bullets / content-slide / native-two-column / insights-only; reason is one of count_out_of_range / budget_exceeded / columns_unbalanced / scores_incomplete / score_unreadable / chart_data_missing.

- "every advisory that announces a fallback carries the new code" -> TestEveryFallbackAdvisoryIsPatternDegraded, one sub-test per slide kind (8 pass), also checking all three params are present and `to` is in the documented set.
- "no advisory that only recommends a count range does" -> TestNoFallbackAdvisoryStaysOnDensity (over-wide table keeps SEMANTIC_DENSITY and must NOT also report a degrade).
- "describe_finding returns remediation steps" -> TestPatternDegradedIsDescribable (non-empty, and points at fix.params).
- "the examples corpus validates with no new findings" -> examples_test.go passes with the same finding SET at the same paths and severities; only the code changed. Severity/strictness/messages/paths are untouched and no finding appears or disappears.
- Extra guard: TestDegradeMessagesStillNameTheFallback keeps the human half of the message honest.

title: Preflight: resolve a placeholder's inherited colour from the master's txStyles so contrast_predicted covers it
description:
PlaceholderInfo.FontColor is empty when a layout leaves its placeholder colour to the slide master's txStyles (midnight-blue slideLayout4 'Section Divider' is one). The contrast preflight added in go-slide-creator-s7wmh pairs FontColor with the slide's own background, so those slides get no contrast_predicted finding — generate still reports the swap (source master-txStyles) and validate stays silent. Measured: the 3-slide probe deck /tmp/s7wmh/midnight-blue.json reports two contrast_autofixed swaps at generate time and one contrast_predicted at validate time.

FIX: resolve the master txStyles colour through the layout's clrMapOvr during template parsing and populate PlaceholderInfo.FontColor with it, the way internal/generator/inherited_text_contrast.go already does at render time. FontColor has other readers, so check each before widening it — or add a separate InheritedFontColor field if the existing one must keep meaning 'the layout stated this'.

VERIFY: validate on a deck with background.color dk1 on a layout whose title colour comes from the master emits contrast_predicted naming the same colour generate's contrast_autofixed swap writes; no new findings on examples/.
close_reason:
Fixed in 5a98560f (pushed to main).

REPRODUCED the bead measurement exactly with a two-slide probe deck (background.color dk1, one slide on midnight-blue slideLayout4 "Section Divider" whose title declares no colour, one on slideLayout2 whose title does):
  BEFORE  validate: /slides/1/content/title and /slides/1/content/body only — slide 0 SILENT
          generate: contrast_autofixed on /slides/0 and /slides/1
  AFTER   validate: /slides/0/content/title ALSO predicts #1B2A4A -> #FFFFFF, the same replacement generate writes

FIX, taking the bead second option ("add a separate InheritedFontColor field if the existing one must keep meaning the layout stated this"): PlaceholderInfo.InheritedFontColor is the colour the placeholder RENDERS at; FontColor keeps its narrower meaning. I checked FontColor readers before deciding — there are only two (cmd/json2pptx/skill_info.go:700, which reports it through examine_template, and the preflight itself) — and widening it would have changed what examine_template tells agents the TEMPLATE declares. A layout that declares nothing should keep saying so.

THE PART THAT WOULD HAVE BEEN WRONG WITHOUT CHECKING: resolution goes through the layout clrMapOvr, not just the theme. I grepped all nine bundled templates for a non-trivial overrideClrMapping and found modern-template slideLayout2 "Section Divider" declaring bg1="dk1" tx1="lt1" (and business-template slideLayout1). On that layout a master colour of tx1 renders LIGHT — resolving against the theme alone would have predicted the exact OPPOSITE of what renders, which is the same preflight/render divergence class this bead exists to close. internal/template/inherited_color.go mirrors internal/generator/chrome_contrast.go parser of the same element.

A SCHEME NAME STAYS A SCHEME NAME. ContrastPreflightPair.Foreground is documented as "hex or scheme name" and resolves scheme names against the same theme the renderer uses, so resolving to hex in the template layer would duplicate that and could disagree with it. Only the clrMapOvr remapping is applied here, because that is layout-scoped information the preflight layer does not have.

RESOLUTION ORDER matches the renderer: the layout placeholder own lstStyle level 1 wins, else the master titleStyle / bodyStyle level 1.

VERIFY, both clauses:
  "validate emits contrast_predicted naming the same colour generate contrast_autofixed swap writes" — yes, #1B2A4A -> #FFFFFF on /slides/0/content/title
  "no new findings on examples/" — ran all 19 bundled examples through the pre-fix and post-fix binaries: 0 predicted findings before, 0 after, no per-file difference

TESTS (internal/template/inherited_color_test.go): the Section Divider title resolves a non-empty InheritedFontColor; FontColor stays empty there (so examine_template output is unchanged) while a declaring placeholder keeps its value and the two agree; the colour-map table including a literal hex (no scheme slot to remap), an unmentioned name, and no override at all; and that an inverted layout does not come back as the slot its clrMapOvr renames away from.

NO GOLDEN DRIFT: pre-push rebaseline check produced an empty diff.

DOCS SYNC (same commit): docs/SCHEMA_CHANGELOG.md (Unreleased/Changed). No agent-facing surface changed — InheritedFontColor is internal, and examine_template output is deliberately unchanged.

close_reason:
Fixed in 92f20b3f. Both halves.

(a) SEVERITY ON FIT FINDINGS. patterns.FitFinding had no severity field at all, so generate_presentation fit_findings serialised without one while validate_input (which routes through the diagnostics envelope) reported the same finding as "info".

title: Bound the render cache: TMPDIR artifacts grow forever, InvalidateCache has no callers
description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: mcp-surface (finding refs m.24).

WHAT
Every render_* call writes content-addressed PNGs into os.TempDir()/json2pptx-render-cache/artifacts and the response documents 'cleanup: content-addressed; ... removed by render-cache invalidation (InvalidateCache) or OS temp cleanup'. But InvalidateCache() has zero callers outside its own definition (grep across the repo), no size/age cap exists, and no MCP tool exposes it — this review session alone left 418 files / 13MB there. On a long-lived server (the normal MCP deployment) the cache only grows, and the agent has no way to reclaim it or to know how much it is using.

WHERE
internal/render/render.go:50-58 (cacheDir, ArtifactCleanupPolicy), internal/render/render.go:526 InvalidateCache (unused), cmd/json2pptx/mcp_render_images.go (callers).

HOW
Add an LRU/age bound (e.g. evict artifacts older than 24h or beyond 500MB on each render, cheap stat-based sweep), report cache_bytes in get_capabilities.runtime, and expose cleanup either as an arg (`purge_cache:true` on render_deck_thumbnails) or as a maintenance tool in the all profile. Document the real policy in the cleanup string.

VERIFY
go test ./internal/render -run TestCacheEviction; after 100 synthetic renders the cache dir stays under the cap; get_capabilities.runtime reports cache_bytes.

EVIDENCE (local, gitignored)
- /Users/seb/projects/json2pptx/.claude/review-evidence/r2/mcp-surface/mcp-surface/loop_3_thumbs.json

Skill/docs sync (CLAUDE.md policy): any agent-visible change updates skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md (+ docs/FIT_FINDINGS.md / PATTERNS.md / INPUT_FORMAT.md / SCHEMA_CHANGELOG.md as applicable) in the same commit.
Gates: golangci-lint run ./... && go test ./... -short -race (plus `cd svggen && golangci-lint run ./... && go test ./...` if svggen touched); go test -run TemplatePatternMatrix ./cmd/json2pptx/... if patterns/shapegrid/generator touched.
Visual evidence: build ./cmd/json2pptx, generate on midnight-blue AND warm-coral (-templates-dir templates), rasterize with pptx2jpg (or soffice -env:UserInstallation=<private> --headless --convert-to pdf + pdftoppm -r 90 -png), LOOK at before/after PNGs and cite their paths in the close reason.
close_reason:
Fixed in 5e94625c (pushed to main). All four parts of the bead HOW delivered.

CONFIRMED THE PREMISE FIRST: grep across the repo shows InvalidateCache referenced only in its own definition and in two comments — zero call sites. My own machine had 2105 files / 11MB in $TMPDIR/json2pptx-render-cache before I started, matching the reported 418 files / 13MB per session.

1. BOUND (internal/render/cache_bound.go): SweepCache(maxAge, maxBytes) removes artifacts past CacheMaxAge (24h), then evicts oldest-first until under CacheMaxBytes (500 MiB). Called via maybeSweepCache() from RenderSlideWithCacheKey and RenderDeckIndices — the two points every render path funnels through — and throttled to once per 5 minutes so a burst of renders pays for one directory walk, not one per call. Stat-based (filepath.WalkDir + DirEntry.Info), no file reads. Empty directories left by a sweep are pruned so an aged-out cache does not leave a tree of empty per-deck folders.

OLDEST-FIRST, deliberately: a cached render nobody has asked for in days is the cheapest thing to lose, and because artifacts are content-addressed, purging costs re-render time but never correctness.

2. VISIBILITY: get_capabilities().runtime gains render_cache_bytes (current usage) and render_cache_policy (the rule), both required in the output schema. Verified live: reported 9323259 bytes on this machine.

3. RECLAIM: new purge_render_cache MCP tool + json2pptx purge-render-cache CLI, with all:true / --all to ignore the bounds. Returns {bytes_before, bytes_reclaimed, bytes_after, scope, policy}. Verified end to end:
   default scope -> before 7583409, reclaimed 0, after 7583409, scope "bounds"  (a healthy cache is untouched)
   --all         -> before 7583409, reclaimed 7583409, after 0, scope "all"

4. HONEST POLICY STRING: ArtifactCleanupPolicy — echoed as `cleanup` on every path-returning render response — became a fmt.Sprintf over the real constants: "evicted after 24h unused, or oldest-first once the cache exceeds 500 MiB, swept on render; get_capabilities().runtime.render_cache_bytes reports current usage". TestArtifactCleanupPolicyDescribesTheRealBound asserts it mentions 24h / 500 MiB / render_cache_bytes AND that it no longer names InvalidateCache.

REGISTERING A TOOL TOUCHES NINE PLACES, and the repo gates every one of them — worth recording for the next tool: mcp_registry.go, toolConstructors(), mcpToolCatalog(), toolClassifications() (+ CLICounterpart), the CLI dispatch in main.go, its usage text, cli_command_classification.go, the mcpToCLI parity table, the output-schema coverage map, README.md, skills/generate-deck/TOOLS.md, and the schema fingerprint. Each was caught by its own failing test rather than by me remembering.

TWO OF MY OWN BUGS CAUGHT BY THOSE GATES:
- I classified the tool MutatesState:true, which made it advertise destructiveHint; TestDiscoveryToolsAreReadOnly refused it because only the template-settings writers mutate SERVER state. Purging a cache is a files operation — WritesFiles:true is the honest classification.
- The CLI parsed os.Args[2:], but main rewrites os.Args to drop the subcommand, so --all never reached the flag. Caught by running the command rather than trusting the build; "scope bounds" came back on an --all run.

TESTS: internal/render/cache_bound_test.go — age eviction, oldest-first size eviction, a healthy cache left completely alone (the sweep runs on EVERY render, so it must not be destructive), a missing cache dir, CacheBytes across subdirectories, empty-dir pruning, and the policy-string assertion.

Fixed in 6353fc7c (pushed to main).

ROOT CAUSE: `callout` was optional in the schema but not in the layout. Expand always emitted outer columns [60,40] and always attached the 2pt left accent bar to the callout cell, whether or not that cell had text. With no callouts the slide rendered as three floating coloured dashes at x~703 beside bars confined to the left 60%.

The bead also asked to default max_value to the largest bar — that was already the case (horizontalbarcallouts.go derives maxVal from the bars when MaxValue <= 0), and the render confirms the top bar DOES reach the end of its own bar area. What made it look short was the 40% empty column to its right. No change needed there; noted in the commit message.

- anyHorizontalBarCallout() gates the layout. None -> outer columns [100], one cell per row, no accent bars.

- Per-row: the accent tick renders only when that bar has non-blank callout text. Same defect at row scale in the mixed case (two dashes anchored to nothing).
- barAreaWidthPt (the go-slide-creator-d6zo in-bar/outside value-label decision) measured the FULL content width while the bar area is only the bar column share of it. Now scaled by barColPct.

description:
Round-2 deck-quality review 2026-09-18. Parent epic: go-slide-creator-429b. Reported by: closure-audit-1 (finding refs c1.11).

The cards look acceptable, so this is a claim/constant mismatch rather than a visual defect, but any test or doc asserting the 45% cap is false.

close_reason:
Fixed in a3f906ee (pushed to main). Root cause of the 57% split out as go-slide-creator-byr2b (P2).

THE BEAD WAS RIGHT ABOUT THE CODE, AND I CONFIRMED IT: kpiRowMaxHeightPt returned clampPt(need, geo.hPt, contentH). geo.hPt is the 45% value, and clampPt takes (v, lo, hi) -- so the "cap" was the LOWER bound. The row rests on 45% and is raised to whatever the tallest card measures. Every doc and reviewer assertion of a 45% cap was false.

FIXED (bead HOW option 2): renamed kpiMaxCardHeightFrac -> kpiBaseCardHeightFrac, with the comment saying which bound it is and why. SKILL.md and docs/PATTERNS.md restate the invariant that actually holds ("rest at 45% and are raised only when the tallest card text needs more, never past the content area"). docs/PATTERNS.md also gains a pattern-authoring note about being precise which bound a fraction is.

I IMPLEMENTED THE OTHER HOW OPTION AND THEN REMOVED IT. A real ceiling (kpiMaxCardHeightFrac = 0.70, above the measured worst case of 65.6% at kpi-6up schema maxima) passed every test. Then I checked what it does to content that needs the height:
  contentH=308.1 need=250.0 -> old 250.0, new 215.7  CLIPS
  contentH= 94.5 need=200.0 -> old  94.5, new  66.1  CLIPS
A row can never exceed the content area anyway, so any ceiling below it only clips cards whose text genuinely needs the height, leaving the rest of the box empty while the text overflows. Capping there buys nothing and costs real renders, so the clamp is unchanged and the rejected alternative is recorded next to it.

MEASUREMENTS (probe over kpi-2up..6up, midnight-blue content zone 308.1pt):
  exemplar / with-sub-lines: 139.0pt = 45.1% for every N (rests on the base)
  schema maxima: 45.1% for 2..4up, 60.7% for 5up, 65.6% for 6up (raised, as designed)
So the raise only fires on genuinely heavy content in the narrow variants -- the behaviour is correct, only the name and the claim were wrong.

WHY THE REPORT SAW 57% AND NOT 45% -- SEPARATE ROOT CAUSE, NOW go-slide-creator-byr2b: the generate path builds ExpandContext WITHOUT LayoutBounds, so expandContentSize falls back to shapegrid.DefaultBounds and the pattern sizes against 388.8pt while the renderer lays the grid into the template zone of 308.1pt. Measured both ways:
  without LayoutBounds: contentH 388.8pt -> max_height 175.0pt (45.0% of 388.8, but 56.8% of 308.1)
  with LayoutBounds:    contentH 308.1pt -> max_height 139.0pt (45.1%)
175pt is 2222500 EMU, which is the 2222499 EMU the audit measured. That is the whole of the 57%. It affects every content-sized pattern, not just KPI, and fixing it means resolving layout geometry BEFORE pattern expansion (needsVirtualLayout gates on ShapeGrid != nil, which only exists after expansion) -- too much blast radius to fold into a P3 rename, so it is filed with the measurements and an expect-churn note.

VERIFY (bead asked: expand kpi-3up on midnight-blue and assert card cy <= 0.45 * content height): TestKPIRowHeightInvariant does exactly that across kpi-2up..6up for light and heavy content -- rests on the base when content fits, never exceeds the content area. TestKPIRowHeightIsRaisedNotCapped pins the floor behaviour explicitly so the name can never drift back. Both fail to compile against the pre-fix source.

NO RENDER CHANGE: ran scripts/rebaseline_golden_hashes.sh as a pre-push check; empty diff, as expected for a rename.

close_reason:
Fixed in d9a36f1e (pushed to main).

MEASURED THE CONVENTION FIRST rather than taking the bead word for it — parsed every mcp.NewTool declaration and counted:
  pptx_path:    audit_palette, read_presentation, render_deck_thumbnails, render_slide_image, submit_visual_review  (5)
  path:         validate_presentation_output  (1)
  template:     auto_repair, compile_deck_spec, list_templates, make_deck, plan_deck, recommend_visual, render_deck_spec, render_slide_image_from_json, score_candidates, score_deck, table_density_guide  (11)
  template_name: delete_template_setting, examine_template, list_template_settings, register_template_setting, resolve_theme  (5)
  slide_count:  NO tool declares it as an input (0)
  slide_budget: plan_deck  (1)
So the bead is right about all three, and it UNDERSTATES the template case: five tools use template_name, not just resolve_theme. All five now accept `template`.

FIX: cmd/json2pptx/mcp_arg_aliases.go adds argAliasMiddleware, registered BEFORE strictArgsMiddleware (verified mcp-go applies middleware in reverse index order, so mw[0] is outermost and runs first). It rewrites the sibling name to the declared one, so the strict check never sees an alias and handlers are untouched.

DIRECTION OF THE ALIAS, deliberately: the bead VERIFY says "the canonical names remain in the schema", so I kept the declared names (path / template_name / slide_budget) and accepted the majority spellings as aliases. Renaming the declared names would have been the other reading and would break every existing caller.

PRECEDENCE: when BOTH names are sent the DECLARED one wins. A caller honouring the schema must not have its value silently discarded by the alias. Covered by TestArgAliases_DeclaredNameWins.

REGISTRATION-TIME TEST (bead asked for exactly this): TestArgNamingIsConsistentAcrossTools walks the live tool catalog and asserts that any tool declaring a pptx-path argument ACCEPTS pptx_path, any tool declaring a template argument accepts template, and any tool declaring a slide-count argument accepts slide_count. The test reported every alias as "both declared and aliased". Split into declaredArgNames (schema only) and toolArgNames (schema + legacy + sibling aliases).

VERIFY (bead: validate_presentation_output{pptx_path}, resolve_theme{template} and plan_deck{slide_count} all succeed; canonical names remain in the schema): TestArgAliases_SiblingNamesAreAccepted drives all three through the real server and asserts no UNKNOWN_PARAMETER. Schemas unchanged.

Strictness itself is intact: TestStrictArgs_AllToolsRejectBogusArgument still drives a bogus argument through every registered tool.

title: Taxonomy diagrams rotate through accent1-6, producing a rainbow that clashes with the template
description:

internal/generator builders for business_model_canvas, pestel, value_chain, porters_five_forces, swot (scheme colour assignment)

Default taxonomy cells to tints of accent1 (or accent1/dk2 alternation) and reserve a second accent only where the framework encodes a real contrast (SWOT positive/negative). Keep the rainbow behind an explicit opt-in if anyone wants it.

BMC slide XML carried accent1-6 + dk1 across nine cells; the render is a green/orange/purple/cyan/pink/blue patchwork on a green deck, exactly as reported. PESTEL the same with six hues. SWOT arbitrary across four.

CORRECTION TO THE BEAD LIST: porters_five_forces and value_chain do NOT exhibit this.
- porters_five_forces colours by each force intensity (high=accent1, medium=accent3, low=accent5). That IS information, and at default intensity every box renders the same neutral tint — verified in the before render, slide 4 has zero accent scheme colours. Left alone.

title: Pin local golangci-lint to the CI version (v2.8.0) so `make lint` matches CI
description:

WHAT
CI runs golangci-lint v2.8.0 (.github/workflows/ci.yml, both modules) while `make lint` uses whatever is on PATH (v2.12.2 on this machine). Round 1 had to rely on CI to confirm lint-cleanliness; newer local versions can both hide and invent findings, which costs agents a push-and-wait cycle.

title: Layout heuristic prefers Blank over Title Slide for title-kind slides
description:
**Source:** Office Companion integration tests, 2026-06-01, against main `1134c1e5`.
**Status:** Worked around OC-side (added subTitle placeholder to slideLayout5 in pwc-template). P3 — workaround in place.

## Symptom

For a semantic slide with `kind: title`, the layout heuristic picks `slideLayout5` ("Blank", canonical_family `other`) at confidence 0.4125 instead of `slideLayout1` ("Title Slide", canonical_family `title-slide`), which has both `ctrTitle` and `subTitle` placeholders.

```
INFO layout selected slide_index=0 slide_type=title method=heuristic \
  layout_id=slideLayout5 layout_name=Blank confidence=0.4125
```

Expected: `slideLayout1` (Title Slide) should outscore Blank for title-kind slides — it is in the `title-slide` canonical family with the correct placeholder set.

## Suggested investigation

- `internal/layout/heuristic.go:458+` — the position-0 bonus for `title-slide`-tagged layouts may not be outweighing whatever signal pulls slideLayout5 ahead.
- `internal/layout/canonical.go:45` — the canonical rule correctly excludes `blank-title` and `closing` for the `"title"` canonical name, but the heuristic fallback may not apply the same exclusions.

## Workaround (already applied OC-side)

Added a `subTitle` placeholder to slideLayout5 in `~/.json2pptx/templates/pwc-template.pptx` so content is preserved regardless of which layout is chosen.
close_reason: Implemented: heuristic now treats a layout as a cover/title-slide when it carries the structural 'title-slide' tag OR classifies into the title-slide canonical family (CanonicalType.Family()==title-slide), and excludes the 'blank-title' utility layout. New isTitleSlideLayout helper used at the position-0 bonus and scoreTitleSlide. Fixes Blank/Blank+Title winning over a real Title Slide whose strict tag heuristic was suppressed. Added 2 regression tests.

title: semantic: non-empty unknown kind emits two identical SEMANTIC_UNKNOWN_KIND findings (parse + validate double-emit)
description: Discovered while fixing n78o. A slide with a non-empty but unregistered kind (e.g. kind:"foo") produces TWO identical findings: the parse pass (buildSlideSpec in yaml.go, CodeUnknownKind -> SEMANTIC_UNKNOWN_KIND) and validateSlide (validate.go) both emit "unknown slide kind \"foo\"" at slides[0].kind. Check() concatenates parseDiags.ToDiagnostics() + Validate() with no dedup (validate.go ToDiagnostics). Repro: {"meta":{"title":"X"},"slides":[{"kind":"foo","title":"x"}]} -> 2 identical errors. The empty/whitespace contradictory case was fixed in n78o by silencing the parse pass for blank kinds, but the identical-duplicate for non-empty unknown kinds remains. Fix options: (a) add exact-duplicate (code+path+message) dedup in Check(); or (b) make validateSlide skip the unknown-kind emission when a parse-level kind finding already exists. Note the standalone parse test (TestToDiagnosticsBridgesParseFindings) requires ParseYAML to keep emitting for non-empty unknown kinds, so a fix must preserve standalone parse behavior. Add a regression test asserting exactly one finding for kind:"foo" via Check.
close_reason: Implemented: dedup exact-duplicate findings in semantic.Check() so a non-empty unknown kind emits one SEMANTIC_UNKNOWN_KIND finding instead of two identical ones; parse and validate passes still emit standalone. Added regression test.

title: semantic: empty-string kind emits two contradictory findings (unknown kind "" AND missing kind), same code/path
description:
## Summary
A slide with `kind: ""` produces **two** findings with the **same code** (`INPUT.SEMANTIC_UNKNOWN_KIND`) and **same path** (`slides[0].kind`) but **contradictory messages**: one says `unknown slide kind ""`, the other says `slide is missing the required "kind" field`.

## Reproduction
```json
{"meta":{"title":"X"},"slides":[{"kind":"","title":"x"}]}
```
Run: `json2pptx semantic validate --spec spec.json` → `2 errors`, both SEMANTIC_UNKNOWN_KIND on slides[0].kind.

## Expected
A single, unambiguous finding for an empty/blank kind (e.g. treat `""`/whitespace as "missing kind").

## Root cause
- `internal/semantic/yaml.go` `buildSlideSpec`: a present-but-empty string sets `slide.Kind = ""` and (since `"".Valid()` is false) emits `CodeUnknownKind` with message `unknown slide kind ""`.
- `internal/semantic/validate.go` `validateSlide`: separately treats `slide.Kind == ""` as the missing-kind branch and emits `CodeSemanticUnknownKind` "missing required kind field".
Both fire for the same field.

## Suggested fix
In `buildSlideSpec`, treat an empty/whitespace `kind` value the same as an absent kind (emit `CodeMissingKind`, or leave it for the validator) so only one finding results. Add a test asserting exactly one finding for `kind:""`.
close_reason: Implemented: blank/whitespace kind now treated as absent in buildSlideSpec (yaml.go), leaving validateSlide to emit a single canonical missing-kind finding instead of a contradictory parse+validate pair. Added regression test TestCheckBlankKindEmitsSingleMissingFinding. Filed follow-up for the separate non-empty unknown-kind identical-duplicate.

title: semantic: weak-content placeholder detection false-positives via naive substring match (Mastodon matches todo)
description:
## Summary
The placeholder/filler detector matches its markers as case-insensitive **substrings**, so legitimate text that merely contains `todo`/`tbd`/`fixme` triggers a spurious SEMANTIC_WEAK_CONTENT warning.

## Reproduction
```json
{"meta":{"title":"Mastodon Migration Strategy"},"slides":[{"kind":"title","title":"Automated Backups Roadmap"}]}
```
Run: `json2pptx semantic validate --spec spec.json`

## Actual
```
SEMANTIC_WEAK_CONTENT @ meta.title : content looks like a placeholder ("todo"); replace it with real text
```
"Mas**todo**n" matched the `todo` marker.

## Expected
No warning — "Mastodon" is a real word. Markers like `todo`, `tbd`, `fixme` should match only as whole tokens (word boundaries), not as embedded substrings. (`lorem ipsum`, `__fill__`, `placeholder` are multi-char/distinctive enough to keep as substrings.)

## Root cause
`internal/semantic/validate.go` `weakMarker()` uses `strings.Contains(l, m)` for every marker. The short alpha markers (`tbd`, `todo`, `fixme`) collide with substrings of ordinary words.

## Suggested fix
For the short alpha markers, switch to a word-boundary regex (e.g. `\b(tbd|todo|fixme)\b`) or tokenize on non-alphanumerics and compare tokens. Keep substring matching for the distinctive sentinels (`__fill__`, `lorem ipsum`). Add a test asserting "Mastodon"/"subtotal" do not trip the detector while "TODO: fill this" still does.
close_reason: Implemented: weakMarker now matches tbd/todo/fixme as whole words via \b regex (was naive substring Contains); kept lorem ipsum/__fill__/placeholder as substrings. Added TestWeakMarkerWordBoundary regression (Mastodon/subtotal clean, real placeholders still flagged).

title: unknown top-level fields in semantic specs produce indirect diagnostics
description:
[P3] A common stale spec shape uses top-level 'deck'. semantic validate ignores that object and reports only missing meta.title, instead of flagging the unknown field directly.

Impact: agents get a technically correct but indirect error. A direct unknown-field diagnostic such as 'unknown top-level field deck; did you mean meta?' would shorten repair loops.
design:
## Repro
printf 'deck:\n  title: Bad Deck\nslides:\n  - kind: title\n    title: Bad Deck\n' | json2pptx semantic validate --spec -

## Observed
{
  "ok": false, "summary": "1 error",
  "findings": [
    { "code": "INPUT.SEMANTIC_REQUIRED",
      "message": "deck title (meta.title) is required",
      "evidence": { "path": "meta.title" } }
  ]
}

## Suggested fix
- Detect unknown top-level keys in semantic specs.
- Add targeted suggestions for common migration mistakes, especially deck -> meta.
acceptance_criteria:
- unknown top-level keys in semantic specs produce a direct diagnostic
- 'deck' produces a targeted 'did you mean meta?' suggestion
- test covers the deck->meta migration case
close_reason: Implemented: unknown top-level fields in semantic specs now emit a direct SEMANTIC_UNKNOWN_FIELD diagnostic with targeted 'did you mean' suggestions (deck->meta migration, fuzzy typo matching, generic valid-keys list). Added describe-finding entry, doc update, and regression tests.

title: semantic CLI rough edges hurt automation (help exit code, stdin, compile diagnostics, HTTP 501)
description:
[P3] Several semantic CLI rough edges break automation/CI probes:
- 'semantic render --help' prints help but exits code 1 with 'Error: flag: help requested'.
- '--spec -' maps to /dev/stdin, not portable to Windows.
- 'semantic compile' success returns compiled JSON only, so non-blocking diagnostics are unavailable unless agents run validate separately.
- HTTP semantic docs mention render, but the handler currently returns 501.

Impact: automated agents/CI probes can treat help as failure, stdin workflows are platform-fragile, compile-only flows miss warnings, and HTTP docs overstate the implemented surface.
design:
## Repro
json2pptx semantic render --help

## Observed
Usage: json2pptx semantic render --spec <file> --output <file.pptx> [options]
...
Error: flag: help requested   (exit code 1)

## Suggested fix
- Return exit code 0 for semantic subcommand help.
- Read stdin with os.Stdin instead of /dev/stdin.
- Add an optional structured compile envelope that includes diagnostics.
- Mark HTTP semantic render unavailable in docs/capabilities until implemented, or implement it.
acceptance_criteria:
- semantic subcommand --help exits 0
- stdin spec read via os.Stdin (Windows-portable), not /dev/stdin
- optional structured compile envelope surfaces non-blocking diagnostics
- HTTP semantic render implemented or marked unavailable in docs/capabilities (no 501-vs-docs mismatch)
close_reason: Implemented: semantic subcommand -h/--help now exits 0 (translate flag.ErrHelp); --spec - reads os.Stdin (Windows-portable) not /dev/stdin; new 'semantic compile --envelope' emits structured {ok,slide_count,template,findings,compiled_json} so compile-only flows surface non-blocking diagnostics; openapi/SEMANTIC_COMPILER docs corrected so HTTP semantic endpoints no longer overstate render (501 deferred). Tests + docs updated.

title: Add direct tests for deckinput and semantic slide compiler packages
description:
Problem: Some packages have no or very low direct coverage, especially code that handles compatibility inputs and semantic slide compilation.

Where: internal/deckinput/deckinput.go PresentationInput.UnmarshalJSON and ContentInput.ResolveValue around lines 164-422 has 0% direct coverage/no test files; internal/semantic/slides/slides.go compiler functions around lines 27-171 has 0% direct coverage/no test files. Also consider follow-up coverage for internal/layoutpreview, internal/render, internal/jsonschema, and internal/pptxread.

Impact: JSON compatibility behavior, legacy/new content forms, malformed raw JSON handling, split-slide expansion, and semantic compiler fallbacks can regress silently.

Implementation: Add table-driven tests for deckinput legacy/new content forms, malformed raw JSON, nil/empty defaults, and split-slide expansion edge cases. Add compact golden/unit tests for semantic slide compilers such as CompileTitle, CompileExecutiveSummary, CompileDecision, KPI/chart fallback paths. Keep fixtures minimal and deterministic.
acceptance_criteria:
- internal/deckinput has focused tests covering compatibility and malformed-input edge cases.
- internal/semantic/slides has direct tests for core compiler functions and fallback paths.
- Tests are deterministic and do not require external tools.
- Coverage for these two packages is no longer 0%.
close_reason: Implemented: added table-driven tests for internal/deckinput (UnmarshalJSON split_slide expansion, malformed input, ResolveValue/UsesLegacyValue/ToThemeOverride/Segment helpers) and internal/semantic/slides compilers (Title/Section/Closing/ExecutiveSummary/Decision/Fallback/KPISnapshot/ChartInsight/Raw + helpers). Coverage 0%->75.2% and 0%->92.2%.

title: Split skipped render/SVG/template tests into explicit integration coverage
description:
Problem: `go test ./...` passes, but many meaningful SVG, template, render, and headless PPTX paths are skipped when external tools or fixtures are unavailable. This makes default validation weaker than it appears.

Where: internal/generator/svg_test.go many skips around lines 127-1723; internal/generator/generator_test.go repeated template/image skips around lines 21-1639; internal/generator/singlepass_test.go template-dependent skips around lines 169-3763; internal/render/render_test.go integration/render fixture skips around lines 69-421; cmd/json2pptx/corpus_headless_test.go skips when LibreOffice is missing around line 34; palette parity tests are opt-in/tool-gated.

Impact: Local or minimal CI runs can be green while important PPTX/SVG/render behavior is unexercised, allowing user-visible rendering regressions to slip through.

Implementation: Classify these tests into unit vs integration. Move external-tool/fixture-heavy tests behind explicit build tags or CI job names, and ensure CI has at least one job with required fixtures/tools installed. For unit coverage, replace broad fixture dependency with small embedded/minimal fixtures where practical.
acceptance_criteria:
- Skipped integration tests are intentionally grouped/tagged and documented.
- CI has a clear job that runs the integration/render/SVG/template coverage with required tools, or documents why it cannot.
- Unit test paths avoid unnecessary skips by using minimal embedded fixtures where practical.
close_reason: Classified skipped tests into tiers (docs/TESTING.md); added render-integration CI job that installs LibreOffice/ImageMagick/rsvg and runs the previously-never-run render + SVG-conversion integration tests; made render integration tests pointable via RENDER_TEST_PPTX env override instead of a single hard-coded path

title: Pass build metadata through serve health endpoint
description:
Problem: api.ServerConfig supports Version, CommitSHA, and BuildTime and HealthHandler returns them, but runServe does not pass the build-time globals into api.NewServer.

Where: cmd/json2pptx/serve.go startup/build metadata around lines 60-64 and api.NewServer construction around lines 119-126; internal/api/server.go ServerConfig around lines 38-62; internal/api/health.go response around lines 30-39.

Impact/repro: A released binary built with ldflags can show correct build info in startup logs and `json2pptx version`, while GET /api/v1/health reports default `dev` and omits commit/build time. This weakens deployment/debug observability.

Implementation: Populate Version, CommitSHA, and BuildTime in the api.ServerConfig created by runServe. Preserve existing defaults for tests or unset build globals.
acceptance_criteria:
- /api/v1/health reports the same build metadata as serve startup/version output when ldflags are set.
- Defaults remain stable for local dev builds.
- Add or update a test around ServerConfig/health response metadata if practical.
close_reason: Implemented: runServe now passes Version/CommitSHA/BuildTime into api.ServerConfig so /api/v1/health reports the same build metadata as startup logs and version output; added NewServer→health regression test

title: Semantic compiler 11: optional semantic HTTP endpoints
description:
Why:
HTTP is a product integration surface. It should expose semantic validate/compile/schema, and render once raw render orchestration is reusable outside cmd.

Add/modify:

Shared FindingEnvelope for diagnostics, capabilities advertises semantic support, OpenAPI+README updated, tests for success/invalid/deferred.

title: Decide commit-vs-revert for orphaned working-tree edits in blue-corporate & forest-green templates
description: Sibling of go-slide-creator-g5px. After reverting modern-template.pptx, the working tree still carries uncommitted prior-session modifications to templates/blue-corporate.pptx (23 parts differ: masters, layouts 5-7, slides 1-4, docProps) and templates/forest-green.pptx (35 parts differ AND ppt/go-slide-creator-metadata.json is STRIPPED — same regression signature as modern). Both currently PASS TestTextFitCorpus, so they are not urgent, but leaving orphaned dirty template binaries in the working tree across sessions is exactly what produced g5px. Decide per template: (a) the edits are intentional QA improvements -> commit them (and for forest-green, restore the stripped ppt/go-slide-creator-metadata.json so engine template-metadata features keep working), or (b) they are orphaned -> 'git checkout HEAD -- templates/<file>.pptx'. The prior-session work is preserved in stash@{0} ('ORPHANED prior-session template-QA work'). Acceptance: working tree clean for both templates; TestTextFitCorpus still passes; chosen path documented.
close_reason: Resolved (path b — revert): both templates carried ORPHANED prior-session working-tree edits (build-mode agent 2026-05-22, preserved in stash@{0}), not intentional QA. forest-green showed the regression signature ppt/go-slide-creator-metadata.json STRIPPED — same as modern-template.pptx, which sibling g5px already adjudicated as discard. Action: git checkout HEAD -- templates/blue-corporate.pptx templates/forest-green.pptx. Verified: working tree clean for both; working sha256 == HEAD blob (blue-corporate 64009a34…, forest-green c6fa5bd9…); forest-green metadata.json restored by the revert; go test ./cmd/json2pptx/ -run TestTextFitCorpus PASS. Orphaned work remains recoverable in stash@{0}.

title: Add guard test: recommend_visual diagramRules must match svggen diagram registry
description:
Found during go-slide-creator-8iy3 MCP-sync verification. recommend_visual.go's diagramRules (the keyword->diagram-type scoring table) is manually kept in sync with svggen.DiagramCapabilitiesReady(). Today they agree exactly (21 types, incl. panel-family aliases panel_layout/icon_columns/icon_rows/stat_cards). But nothing fails if they drift: adding a diagram type to the svggen registry without a matching recommend_visual rule (or vice versa) is silent — the new type just becomes un-recommendable, or a rule points at a non-ready type.

Add a table-driven test (internal/patterns) asserting set(diagramRules[].diagramType) == set(t.Type for t in svggen.DiagramCapabilitiesReady()). This locks the panel-alias consistency the 8iy3 verification confirmed and prevents future silent drift. Mirror the existing chart parity if one exists for chartRules.
close_reason: Implemented: added table-driven guard tests in internal/patterns (recommend_visual_parity_test.go) asserting set(diagramRules[].diagramType)==set(svggen.DiagramCapabilitiesReady().Type) and the mirror for chartRules vs ready svggen.ChartCapabilities(), locking the panel-alias consistency and preventing silent drift.

title: Add separate README entry points for CLI and MCP
description:
Source: magarida-test.md S-3 (Note/Suggestion).

Problem: The main README covers both CLI usage and MCP server integration in
one document. These are distinct use cases with different audiences
(developers running a CLI vs AI agents using MCP tools).

- Advocate: Add an early 'Choose your path' split with clear links to a CLI

- Devil's Advocate: If we do not actually split files, the README may still

- Resolution: Start with audience-specific entry points and stronger

design:
Add a small audience-routing block near the top of README.md.
Use stable anchors like #cli-quick-start and #mcp-integration.
Do not create extra top-level README files in this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- The README includes a prominent early chooser for 'CLI usage' vs 'MCP integration'.
- CLI and MCP readers can jump directly to their relevant sections without scanning the full mixed narrative first.
- Verification: go test ./cmd/json2pptx -run TestReadmeListsAllMCPTools -count=1

title: Trim README JSON format tutorial in favor of docs/INPUT_FORMAT.md

slide_type, placeholder_id) that overlap with docs/INPUT_FORMAT.md. It also

- Resolution: Preserve a single concise worked example and the 'what it is'

design:
Edit the opening README sections only.
Avoid changing feature claims or MCP tables in this bead.
Keep links to docs/INPUT_FORMAT.md and json2pptx input-schema prominent.

title: Rename MCP implementation files to use mcp_ prefix consistently
description:
Source: magarida-test.md I-2 (Severity: Low) — split into naming + mcp.go split.

Problem: cmd/json2pptx/ mixes MCP-prefixed files (mcp_preview.go,
mcp_repair.go) with non-prefixed files that still define MCP tools, e.g.
analyze_rhythm.go, plan_deck.go, score_deck.go, and resolve_theme.go.

- Advocate: Rename the MCP-oriented files. Aligns the directory with the

- Devil's Advocate: File renames alone do not improve architecture, and they
  churn blame/history.
- Resolution: Do the naming cleanup only for files that are unambiguously
  MCP implementations today. Mechanical and behavior-free so later splits
  happen on top of a consistent layout.
design:
Rename files only; do not combine this with logic extraction.
Update any comments that refer to old filenames.
Keep CLI wrapper files like *_cmd.go unchanged.
Examples: analyze_rhythm.go -> mcp_analyze_rhythm.go, plan_deck.go -> mcp_plan_deck.go, score_deck.go -> mcp_score_deck.go, resolve_theme.go -> mcp_resolve_theme.go.
acceptance_criteria:
- MCP tool implementation files in cmd/json2pptx/ follow one naming convention (mcp_*.go).
- No exported names, command names, or tool names change as part of this bead.
- Verification: go test ./cmd/json2pptx -count=1
close_reason: Implemented: renamed MCP tool implementation files in cmd/json2pptx to mcp_ prefix (analyze_rhythm, plan_deck, score_deck, resolve_theme + their test files) for naming consistency; pure git mv renames, no exported/command/tool names changed; CLI *_cmd.go wrappers left unchanged

title: Deduplicate Beads guidance across agent docs
description:

- Devil's Advocate: Keeping the full text inline in both files improves

- Resolution: Keep a concise summary in both files, but move the full
  workflow checklist to one canonical tracked document and link to it.
design:
Use CONTRIBUTING.md as the canonical location so the target is tracked and contributor-visible.
Leave a 2-4 line Beads reminder in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md; remove the long duplicated command/checklist block.
Keep wording identical where the short summary remains.

- AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md no longer contain duplicated full Beads workflow blocks.
- Both files point to the same canonical Beads workflow section for the detailed checklist.
- Verification: go test ./... -count=1
close_reason: Implemented: moved the full Beads command reference + session-close checklist to CONTRIBUTING.md (canonical 'Beads command and session-close reference' section); AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md now carry an identical concise reminder linking there, with the duplicated BEGIN/END BEADS INTEGRATION blocks removed.
