title: [bug] TestSVGFixtures_Sizes/tiny_10x10 fails: 20x20 PNG renders to 99 bytes vs hardcoded 100-byte floor
description: internal/generator/svg_test.go:754 asserts a minimum PNG size of 100 bytes for the tiny_10x10 fixture (10x10 SVG at 2x = 20x20). On macOS (current dev machine) the rendered PNG is 99 bytes, one byte under the floor, failing TestSVGFixtures_Sizes/tiny_10x10. Confirmed pre-existing on a clean tree (git stash) and independent of any diagnostics work. The 100-byte minimum is too tight for a 20x20 raster on this platform/library version. Fix: lower the floor for the tiny fixture or make it platform-tolerant (t.Logf like other font/platform-dependent assertions per CLAUDE.md), or assert a non-zero/valid-PNG-header check instead of a byte count.
close_reason: Implemented: replaced brittle 100-byte floor for tiny_10x10 with a platform-independent PNG-signature check (valid magic header) as the hard correctness gate, plus a tolerantSize flag that demotes the byte floor to t.Logf for the 20x20 fixture. Larger fixtures keep their hard size floors. Fixes macOS 99-byte failure.

title: [bug] svggen module has pre-existing golangci-lint failures (gosec G602/G703, staticcheck QF1012)

title: modern-yellow has untagged orphan layout "69_Custom Layout" that bypasses tag-based selection
description:
modern-yellow.pptx layout dump:
  [title-slide,closing] Closing (slideLayout8)
  [content] One Content (slideLayout3)
  [content,title-at-bottom,section-header] Section Divider (slideLayout2)
  [title-slide] Title Slide (slideLayout1)

  [] 69_Custom Layout (slideLayout4)                  ← no tags, orphan
  [blank] Blank (slideLayout6)

The "69_Custom Layout" has no tags, so tag-based auto-selection (used throughout cmd/json2pptx and internal/pipeline) can never pick it. It will only be reached if a deck explicitly sets layout_id=slideLayout4. That makes it dead weight at best and a source of unpredictable selection at worst — note that slideLayout4 is the ID of "Two Content" / "Closing" in some other templates, so cross-template decks that pin layout_id by index hit the wrong layout.

Root-cause fix: either (a) classify and tag this layout (run internal/template.ClassifyLayout, give it real semantic tags) or (b) remove it from the shipped template if it is unused. Either way, no shipped template should contain a layout with an empty tags slice.

title: Reconciliation doctor: verify SKILL.md finding codes match code emission sites
description:
## Why

The CI heuristic catches new code without skill updates. The opposite drift is just as harmful: SKILL.md (or docs/FIT_FINDINGS.md) describes finding codes that no longer exist, or omits codes the engine actually emits. A periodic reconciliation doctor catches both directions.

## What

A go-test-runnable doctor (e.g., cmd/json2pptx/skill_doctor or a test in cmd/json2pptx/) that:

1. Parses skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md for finding codes (regex over the Finding Codes sections)
2. Parses docs/FIT_FINDINGS.md for the same
3. Greps internal/pipeline/ and cmd/json2pptx/fit_report.go for finding emission strings
4. Asserts:
   - Every code in SKILL.md exists in code
   - Every code in code is documented in SKILL.md AND docs/FIT_FINDINGS.md
   - Severity bands documented in SKILL.md match what code emits (best-effort match)
5. Same idea for OverridesSchema fields: every field documented in SKILL.md / docs/PATTERNS.md must exist in the corresponding OverridesSchema, and vice versa

## Acceptance criteria

- New test or doctor binary runs in `go test ./...` time-budget
- Catches: a code-only finding code (skill doesn't mention it) -> failure
- Catches: a skill-only finding code (code never emits it) -> failure
- Catches: a SKILL.md override field that is not in any pattern's schema -> failure
- Output lists each mismatch with a concrete fix suggestion
- Bypass mechanism for codes intentionally hidden (e.g., internal-only) via a Go-side allowlist with comments

## Dependencies

Related to: the policy bead. Best landed after the heuristic CI check is in place.
close_reason: Implemented reconciliation doctor test in cmd/json2pptx/skill_sync_doctor_test.go with three subtests: FindingCodes (bidirectional code/docs coverage with known-drift baselines and staleness checks), OverridesFields (pattern schema validation), ChartPromotionTable (chart code documentation and promotion-ladder validity)

title: SKILL.md: pattern selection guidance reads show_pattern text_budget_guide
description:
## Why

text_budget_guide ships in show_pattern responses but agents will not use it without the skill explicitly teaching the loop: estimate content volume, read text_budget_guide configurations, pick the configuration whose body_max_chars best matches.

## What

skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md, "Pattern Library" section (or near it):
- Document text_budget_guide block in show_pattern output (target_density + configurations[])
- Add a 'pick a grid configuration' workflow:
  1. Estimate planned content length per cell (chars)
  2. Call show_pattern, read text_budget_guide.configurations
  3. Choose configuration whose body_max_chars is closest to (planned_chars / 0.85) — i.e., aim for ~85% density
  4. Verify post-write with expand_pattern.cell_budgets
- Cross-reference Text Capacity Awareness section
- Note that non-grid patterns (pull-quote, stat-hero, single-cell patterns) have no text_budget_guide; budgeting is per-placeholder via list_templates instead

## Acceptance criteria

- Pattern Library section documents text_budget_guide
- Workflow numbered steps match the actual response shape from the show_pattern bead
- No specific pattern enumerated as example (configurations are template-agnostic)
- Cross-link to Text Capacity Awareness section

## Dependencies

Blocked by: text_budget_guide in show_pattern bead (go-slide-creator-n95z).
close_reason: Documented text_budget_guide block in SKILL.md Pattern Library section with response shape table, 5-step configuration selection workflow, and cross-reference to Text Capacity Awareness

title: SKILL.md: update Color Roles + Layout Discovery for compact list_templates and accent_usage_guide

## Why

It currently does not document how to read template-author-supplied accent_usage_guide (when present), nor how to read the new compact-mode placeholders[] hint. Without skill guidance, the new metadata flows out of list_templates but never reaches agent reasoning.

## What

   - State explicitly: do not assume any accent has a fixed semantic role (positive/negative/neutral) unless accent_usage_guide says so

2. skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md, near "Workflow" Phase 1 PLAN:
   - Document the compact list_templates placeholders[] hint (id/type/max_chars)
   - Use it during pattern selection to size content before calling expand_pattern (rough first pass)
   - Reference full mode for callers who need bounds + font

3. Anti-patterns: do not invent role semantics from accent indexes alone (accent5 is not "subtle" universally — that's per-template)

## Acceptance criteria

- Color Roles section documents accent_usage_guide handling (present vs absent)
- Phase 1 PLAN references compact list_templates placeholders[]

Blocked by: list_templates compact mode + accent_usage_guide bead (go-slide-creator-0o3o).

title: validate-template warns when section-divider layouts have a misnamed decorative number frame
description:
## Why

internal/template/normalizer.go:114 preserves shapes named 'Section Number' as decorative number frames (skipping body normalization). Templates whose section-divider layout has the same visually-large number frame named something else (e.g., 'body') get incorrectly normalized — the large number is treated as body text.

The fix is in place for bundled templates; the project documents this in CLAUDE.md and no specific template is required. The risk is third-party / user-authored templates introducing the same bug.

## What

Extend cmd/json2pptx/validate_template.go (or wherever validate-template lives) with a heuristic warning rule:

For each layout tagged section-header (or whose name matches the section-divider pattern), inspect every body-typed placeholder:
- If the placeholder is small in MaxChars (e.g., < 5 expected chars), large in font size (e.g., > 40pt), and positioned in an upper region of the slide
- AND its name is not 'Section Number'
- Emit a warning: 'Layout {layout_name} has a placeholder that looks like a decorative section number but is named {name}. Rename to "Section Number" so the engine preserves it correctly.'

Pure heuristic — warning only, never error. Tunable thresholds.

## Acceptance criteria

- A template with a correctly-named 'Section Number' frame produces zero warnings
- A synthetic test template with the heuristic shape but a different name produces the warning
- Heuristic thresholds documented in code
- No bundled template required to trigger the rule (use synthetic test fixtures)

## Independence

This bead is genuinely independent of the text-capacity work. Can ship in any order.
close_reason: Implemented heuristic warning in validate-template for section-header layouts with misnamed decorative number frames. Added checkSectionNumberNaming function with documented thresholds (MaxChars<5, FontSize>40pt, upper-third Y position). Full test coverage with 5 test cases.

title: Compute text_budget_guide on demand in show_pattern response
description:
## Why

Agents picking a pattern need a quick reference for typical character budgets per cell at common grid configurations, before they call expand_pattern. A static table baked into the schema (the source TODO's x-ideal-length proposal) goes stale the moment a font or template changes. Computing it on demand from textcapacity.ForResolvedGrid against synthetic exemplars keeps the numbers honest.

## What

Extend show_pattern response (CLI and MCP) with a text_budget_guide block:

```json
"text_budget_guide": {
  "target_density": {"min_pct": 60, "ideal_pct": 85, "max_pct": 110},
  "configurations": [
    {"columns": 2, "rows": 2, "body_max_chars": 95, "header_max_chars": 30},
    {"columns": 3, "rows": 2, "body_max_chars": 65, "header_max_chars": 25},
    {"columns": 2, "rows": 3, "body_max_chars": 70, "header_max_chars": 28}
  ]
}
```

Generation rules:
- Configurations are computed only for grid-shaped patterns where columns/rows are configurable
- Run textcapacity.ForResolvedGrid against a synthetic ShapeGridInput with default font sizes for each common configuration (the pattern declares the configurations to enumerate via a small allowlist, NOT every permutation)
- target_density constants are global (60/85/110), not per-pattern; document them as such
- For non-grid patterns (pull-quote, stat-hero), omit text_budget_guide entirely

DROP x-ideal-length JSON-schema metadata — that proposal is the wrong vehicle (custom schema annotations that vary by computed inputs will lie).

## Acceptance criteria

- show_pattern for grid-shaped patterns emits text_budget_guide with at minimum the three most common configurations for that pattern
- Numbers come from textcapacity (deterministic across platforms) — same package guarantees apply
- Non-grid patterns omit the field
- Tests are parameterized over patterns and configurations — no specific deck or template referenced

## Dependencies

Blocked by textcapacity package bead.
close_reason: Implemented text_budget_guide in show_pattern: added BudgetConfigProvider interface, computeBudgetGuide in textcapacity, card-grid budget configs (2×2, 3×2, 2×3), wired into MCP+CLI handlers, updated output schema and SKILL.md

title: Surface placeholder MaxChars and accent_usage_guide in compact list_templates output
description:
## Why

cmd/json2pptx/skill_info.go:131 skillPlaceholderInfo already exposes MaxChars, Width, Height, FontSize per placeholder when callers request mode=full (buildFullLayoutInfos at :349). Compact / list mode omits this for response-size reasons.

Agents using compact mode for layout discovery currently have no capacity hint and either request full mode (verbose) or guess. A small, structured per-layout summary would close the gap without exploding response size.

Separately: the source TODO proposes accent_usage_guide as a hardcoded string map ('accent1: strong primary content', etc). That intent is template-author territory, not engine logic — different templates have different visual languages. Sourcing it from template metadata (where the template author can override per template) is the durable form.

## What

1. Compact mode placeholder summary
   Add to each layout_summary in compact list_templates:
   ```
   "placeholders": [
     {"id": "title", "type": "title", "max_chars": 120},
     {"id": "body",  "type": "body",  "max_chars": 800}
   ]
   ```
   No bounds, no font — just the single integer agents need to size content.

2. accent_usage_guide
   Source: optional accent_usage_guide map in TemplateMetadata (template authors fill it in). When unset, omit the field entirely from list_templates output. Do NOT hardcode role strings in skill_info.go — that locks every template into one stylistic assumption.

   Per-template override: each bundled template that defines roles ships its own accent_usage_guide values; templates that don't, don't.

## Acceptance criteria

- Compact list_templates includes placeholders[] with id/type/max_chars only
- list_templates includes accent_usage_guide ONLY when the template author supplied it; never synthesized in code
- Bundled templates can opt in by adding the field to their template metadata; the four currently bundled templates may opt in via separate beads / template updates if desired
- Tests assert the field is omitted when metadata absent and present when supplied — no specific template referenced

## Out of scope

The text_budget_guide computed per pattern (show_pattern enrichment) is a separate bead.
close_reason: Implemented: compact list_templates now includes placeholders[] (id/type/max_chars) in layout_summaries; accent_usage_guide sourced from TemplateMetadata and surfaced only when template author supplies it

title: skills/slide-visual-qa SKILL.md: add composition criteria (rhythm, monotony, accent dominance)
description:
**Source**: 2026-05-05 audit follow-up. Memory note: Haiku visual QA agents have ~60% false positive rate on layout issues — they over-flag clipping. They have NO composition signal at all.

**Why agents struggle**: The visual QA agent today only inspects rendered slides for per-slide issues (clipping, contrast). It cannot say 'slide 5 of 10 looks like slide 2 of 10' or 'this whole deck only uses two accents.' Composition flaws are invisible to it.

**Files to update**:
- skills/slide-visual-qa/SKILL.md — add 'Composition criteria' section: pattern_run, accent_dominance, density_variance, narrative_arc (opening + evidence + close). Reference docs/VISUAL_CRITERIA.md.
- docs/VISUAL_CRITERIA.md — add composition section with measurable thresholds (longest_run<=2, accent_dominance<0.7, density_cv>=0.15).
- skills/slide-visual-qa/SKILL.md — instruct the agent to call analyze_deck_rhythm BEFORE per-slide screenshot review, and treat its findings as authoritative for composition issues (do not re-judge from screenshots).

**Acceptance**:
- Visual QA agent run on a known-monotonous deck reports composition issues from analyze_deck_rhythm, NOT from per-slide screenshots.
- False-positive rate on clipping returns to ~normal baseline (composition complaints separated from rendering complaints).
close_reason: Added composition criteria (rhythm, monotony, accent dominance, narrative arc) to SKILL.md and VISUAL_CRITERIA.md. Agent now calls analyze_deck_rhythm before per-slide inspection.

title: grid-rhythm medianInt64 picks upper-middle, biases small layout sets
description:
**Source**: 2026-05-05 audit, R2#11.

**Mechanism**: cmd/json2pptx/grid_rhythm.go:136-149 medianInt64 returns sorted[len(sorted)/2] — for even-length slices that's the upper-middle, biasing inferred title-baseline / content-top toward the lower of two layouts. With 4 layouts in a template, picks element 2 of 4. Combined with extractLayoutDefaults looping over every placeholder of every layout, a single outlier (e.g. section divider with centered title) shifts the deck-wide grid by hundreds of thousands of EMU. detectGridViolations then flags layouts that are CORRECTLY aligned to the master as 'violations.' Agents see noise findings and learn to ignore them.

**Fix**:
- Use canonical mid-pair average for even-length slices.
- Weight by layout usage (which layouts are actually selected).
- Exclude section/title layouts from the title-baseline median (intentionally different).
- Add regression test asserting zero grid_violation findings for a deck using only template-supplied layout placements across all 5 bundled templates.

**Acceptance**: Test passes; existing legitimate violations still detected.
close_reason: Fixed medianInt64 to average mid-pair for even-length slices; excluded section-header/title-slide/closing layouts from grid baseline computation; added regression tests

title: Capability stubs: gate kpi_dashboard, heatmap, pestel, panel_layout behind experimental flag
description:
**Source**: 2026-05-05 audit, R2#12.

**Why agents struggle**: svggen/capabilities.go:347-389 returns kpi_dashboard, heatmap, pestel, panel_layout with Status='stub'. They are visible to agents via DiagramCapabilities() / MCP. An agent that picks kpi_dashboard based on description gets a broken render. 4 of 18 diagram types (22%) are non-functional. Erodes agent trust — they fall back to card-grid for safety.

**Fix**: EITHER (a) finish the stubs:
  - kpi_dashboard reuses kpi-Nup grid + sparkline
  - pestel is a six-cell card-grid variant
  - heatmap exists in internal/generator/heatmap_shapes.go — wire it through
  - panel_layout is icon-row composition
OR (b) gate behind experimental:true flag, exclude from recommend_pattern and default capability listing.

**Acceptance**: Either all four render correctly with golden tests, OR they don't appear in get_diagram_capabilities default response.
close_reason: Promoted kpi_dashboard, heatmap, pestel, panel_layout from stub to ready status — all four have fully functional native OOXML renderers with tests. Added DiagramCapabilitiesReady() filter and include_experimental MCP param for future gating.

title: Detect sparse/underfilled raw shape_grid (extend beyond FillHeight)
description:
**Source**: 2026-05-05 codex audit, finding #5.

**Why agents struggle**: cmd/json2pptx/fit_findings_collect.go:383-389 — sparse-layout detector only runs on FillHeight grids. User-authored raw grids that omit row heights silently shrink to content (internal/shapegrid/grid.go:55-80). The slide visually collapses into small panels with dead space, no diagnostic emitted. This is the per-slide twin of j8rr's deck-level monotony detection.

**Fix**: Run sparse-layout detection on ALL shape_grid outputs (FillHeight=true OR computed bounds < layout content area * 0.6). Emit sparse_layout finding with action=review and Fix.Kind suggesting either explicit row heights or pattern adoption.

**Acceptance**: A raw shape_grid with all row heights omitted that occupies <60% of the layout area emits sparse_layout. Existing FillHeight behavior unchanged.
close_reason: Implemented: extended sparse-layout detection to raw shape_grids with all row heights omitted, emitting sparse_layout when content < 60% of layout area

title: Errors prescribe next_tool_call instead of describing
description:
**Source**: 2026-05-05 audit, R1#11.

**Why agents struggle**: internal/diagnostics/codes.go:13-66 lists 30+ codes. UNKNOWN_PATTERN returns use_one_of with full list (good). But STRICT_FIT, GENERATION_FAILED, INVALID_SLIDE, PATTERN_ERROR return text reasons without next_action hints. A placeholder_overflow finding says 'shrink_or_split' but does not say WHICH tool to call next — repair_slide with which kind? An LLM has to infer protocol from prose.

**Fix**: Add next_tool_call: {tool, args_template} to error envelopes and to fit findings whose action is refuse or shrink_or_split. Example: {tool: 'repair_slide', args_template: {slide_index: 2, fixes: [{kind:'reduce_text', params:{path:'/slides/2/content/body','max_items':5}}]}}. Collapses two LLM turns into one.

**Acceptance**: Every fit-finding with action!='info' returns a populated next_tool_call. Schema validates the template against the target tool's input schema.
close_reason: Added next_tool_call to FitFinding and Diagnostic structs. AttachNextToolCalls populates repair_slide or recommend_pattern suggestions on all actionable findings (action != info). Updated output schemas.

title: list_patterns taxonomy: category, narrative_role, pairs_with, density_class
description:
**Source**: 2026-05-05 audit, R1#8.

**Why agents struggle**: handleListPatterns (cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:1072-1090) returns [{name, cells, use_when}]. No grouping (data-display vs narrative vs structural), no 'good for cover/section/closing', no 'follows well after X.' For an agent building a 10-slide deck, the catalog gives no compositional information. The cells field ('rows x cols') is too abstract.

**Fix**: Extend Pattern interface with:
- Category() string (data-display | narrative | structural | hero)
- NarrativeRole() []string (open | frame | evidence | compare | conclude)
- PairsWith() []string (sibling pattern names that flow well as the next slide)
- DensityClass() string (low | medium | high)
- AccentWeight() string (subtle | normal | strong)

list_patterns groups by category in response. plan_deck (57nl) consumes pairs_with for sequencing.

**Acceptance**: list_patterns response is grouped; agents reading it can plan deck arcs not just slide moments.
close_reason: Implemented: Added PatternTaxonomy struct with Category, NarrativeRole, PairsWith, DensityClass, AccentWeight to Pattern interface. All 17 patterns annotated. list_patterns response now grouped by category.

title: UseWhen contract overhaul: contrastive (when to choose THIS vs sibling) + add not_when
description:
**Source**: 2026-05-05 audit, R1#4.

**Why agents struggle**: PATTERNS.md says use_when must be 'an anti-misuse guardrail,' but actual values are descriptive only:
- cardgrid.go:25: 'NxM titled cards'
- iconrow.go:24: 'Icon + caption row'
- pullquote.go:23: 'Emphasize a single quote or testimonial'
- kpi3up.go:22: 'Three big-number KPIs with short captions'

Only bmccanvas mentions a sibling. Most strings describe WHAT the pattern IS rather than WHEN to choose it over a sibling. Card-grid looks like the right tool for everything >2 items.

**Fix**: Rewrite every UseWhen() to follow the contract: one sentence stating when to choose, plus one phrase stating when to choose a sibling instead. Add a not_when string field returned by show_pattern. Verify with a test that asserts every UseWhen contains 'not'/'unless'/'instead'/'prefer X when' or equivalent contrastive language.

**Acceptance**: card-grid use_when becomes something like 'For 4-9 freeform titled cards. For exactly 3 KPIs prefer kpi-3up; for 2-column tradeoffs prefer comparison-2col; for a 9-block business model prefer bmc-canvas.' Test enforces contrastive form.
close_reason: Implemented UseWhen contract overhaul: all patterns now have contrastive UseWhen text and NotWhen() method. Added enforcement tests.

title: Pattern preview PNGs generated at build time from ExemplarValues
description:
**Source**: 2026-05-05 audit, R2#9.

**Why agents struggle**: recommend_pattern returns shape-grid JSON for each candidate (cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:999-1033 builds previews from ExemplarValues only as raw JSON). Agents do not visualize that JSON; they reason about names. An agent picks card-grid over iconrow because the name is more familiar, not because the rendered preview is better. Commit febc654 added template-layout PNGs proving the team knows preview imagery helps; the same does NOT exist for patterns.

**Fix**: At build time, expand each registered pattern with ExemplarValues() against bundled templates and render to PNG (reuse pptx2jpg). Embed URIs in recommend_pattern MCP response and schema's examples.

**Acceptance**:
- assets/pattern-previews/<template>/<pattern>.png exists for every registered pattern.
- recommend_pattern response includes preview_png_uri[].
- Build pipeline auto-regenerates on pattern code change.
close_reason: Implemented: preview-patterns subcommand generates PNGs for all patterns × templates, preview_png_paths added to recommend_pattern MCP response, Makefile target added

title: Emit validation warning for images without alt-text
description: Now that alt-text flows from JSON through to cNvPr/@descr on all p:pic elements, add a validation warning when an image content item has an empty Alt field. This helps enterprise/public-sector compliance by warning about missing accessibility metadata. Affects `processImageContent()` in `internal/generator/media.go` and the JSON schema validator. Follow-up from go-slide-creator-mled.

This makes grouped shapes edit-friendly in PowerPoint (moving one element moves the group). The low-level `GenerateGroup()` / `GenerateGroupWithChildSpace()` in `internal/pptx/grpgen.go` already exist; the work is to wire a `group` flag from JSON through `shapegrid/types.go` to the shape emission in `cmd/json2pptx/shape_grid.go`. Follow-up from go-slide-creator-mled.

title: P3-51: `added_in` / `removed_in` metadata unpopulated — feature-add and deprecation invisible
description:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `P3`, `api-contract`, `versioning`

**Summary**
`buildDeprecatedFields` (`cmd/json2pptx/mcp_capabilities.go:72-83`) lists two deprecated paths. Both entries have `RemovedIn string` in the struct but neither sets it. No tool advertises `min_schema_version` or `added_in` so an agent using a new server has no way to tell which tools were added recently. When a new placeholder alias (e.g. `section_number` in P1-15) ships, it doesn't surface in `get_capabilities`.

**Fix**
Populate `RemovedIn` on every deprecation. Add `added_in: string` to each entry of `mcpToolNames()` and each field of `capabilitiesFeatures`. Emit `changelog_url` from `get_capabilities` pointing at `docs/SCHEMA_CHANGELOG.md`. Warn in `generate_presentation` responses when a deck uses any field whose `removed_in <= next_minor`.

**Acceptance**
- Every capability field declares `added_in`.
- Every deprecation declares `removed_in`.
- Agent using an old deck against a new server receives warnings for soon-to-be-removed fields.
close_reason: Implemented: added_in on every MCP tool, removed_in on every deprecation, changelog_url in get_capabilities, feature_versions map, deprecation warnings in generate_presentation, read_presentation added to tool catalog

title: P3-50: String-or-object dual parameter pattern doubles tool surface area
description:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `P3`, `api-contract`, `ergonomics`

**Summary**
Every deck-accepting tool declares two mutually-exclusive parameters: `json_input` (string) + `presentation` (object); `values` + `values_object`; `overrides` + `overrides_object`; `cell_overrides` + `cell_overrides_object`; `callout` + `callout_object`. `resolveStringOrObject` is called 14+ times. Doubles the tool schema, doubles error paths (`INVALID_JSON` vs `INVALID_PARAMETER`), and setting both emits an "ambiguous" error that isn't a structured diagnostic. `presentation` object form on `generate_presentation` has no JSON schema attached (`WithObject` with only a description).

**Fix**
Deprecate string forms on a 2.0 bump; keep only object forms. Ship a full JSON schema on every object parameter via `mcp.WithObject(..., mcp.Schema(...))`. Transition: structure the ambiguity error as `Diagnostic{fix: {kind: use_one_of, params: {prefer: "presentation"}}}`.

**Acceptance**
- MCP tool schemas halve in size.
- Every object parameter advertises a full schema.
- Deprecation path documented in `docs/SCHEMA_CHANGELOG.md`.
close_reason: Removed string-form JSON parameters from all MCP tools (json_input, values/overrides/cell_overrides/callout string forms, *_object suffixed params). Only structured object parameters remain. Tool schemas halved. All object params advertise JSON Schema properties. Bumped SchemaVersion to 3.0.0. Updated SCHEMA_CHANGELOG.md, deprecation list, all handlers, CLI wrappers, and tests.

title: P3-49: Non-deterministic `generate_presentation` response (`duration_ms`, no content hash)
description:
**Labels:** `bug`, `P3`, `api-contract`, `idempotency`

**Summary**
Response unconditionally sets `DurationMs: duration.Milliseconds()` (`cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:444-453`), so two identical calls return non-identical responses — defeats content-hash idempotency checks. No documented determinism guarantee for PPTX bytes. No `seed` parameter on tools whose outputs could depend on heuristics. Agents doing retry-on-mismatch or cache-by-input cannot rely on the contract.

**Fix**
- Split volatile metadata out: `diagnostics.performance.duration_ms`, or omit on `deterministic:true` flag.
- Add `build_info.content_hash` (sha256 of output bytes) to the response so agents can compare runs.
- Document in `get_capabilities` whether byte-reproducible output is guaranteed; otherwise publish `{tool_version, template_hash, schema_version}` so agents can detect drift.

**Acceptance**
- Determinism test runs `generate_presentation` twice with identical input; asserts `content_hash` matches.
- Response canonical payload (excluding performance metadata) is byte-identical across runs.
close_reason: Added content_hash (SHA-256) to GenerationResult and JSONOutput response. Verified deterministic output across runs.

title: P3-48: No layout rhythm primitives — slides don't share a consistent grid across a deck
description:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `P3`, `design`, `rhythm`

**Summary**
Each slide's content bounds come from its layout's placeholders, computed independently. Across a deck this means title baselines shift a few px between `slideLayout1` and `slideLayout5`, body content starts at different y-positions on section dividers vs content slides, right margins vary. Viewed as a PDF scroll, this reads as "sloppy" even when each slide is individually fine. No deck-level grid spec.

**Fix**
Deck-level `grid` config validated at generation time:
```json
"grid": {"columns": 12, "gutter_emu": 228600, "title_baseline_pct": 8, "content_top_pct": 15, "content_bottom_pct": 92}
```
Generator snaps pattern `LayoutBounds` to the grid before expansion; emits `grid_violation` fit-findings when layouts can't reconcile.

**Acceptance**
- 20-slide deck exported to PDF — all titles align at the same y, all bodies start at the same y.
close_reason: Implemented deck-level grid config with rhythm snapping, grid_violation fit-findings, validation, and comprehensive tests

title: P3-47: No deck-level visual audit — monotony, color entropy, missing emphasis undetected
description:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `P3`, `feedback-loop`

**Summary**
The ADV deck ended up with 10 consecutive `card-grid` slides because nothing told the agent "you've used card-grid 5 times in a row; vary it." Monotony is a design failure invisible to per-slide validation. No tool reports deck-level metrics.

**Fix**
New `audit_deck` MCP tool (or extension to fit-report) emitting:
- `pattern_histogram` (any pattern >40% of slides → `warning`)
- `consecutive_same_pattern` (>3 → `warning` with suggested alternatives)
- `color_entropy` (too few accent colors → `info`)
- `slide_type_sequence` (no emphasis/stat-hero slide in 10+ slides → `info`)
Feeds into `repair_slide` via P3-12 for automatic pattern-swap.

**Acceptance**
- Audit on the pre-P1-4 ADV deck flags consecutive card-grids and recommends inserting a stat-hero + pull-quote at specific indices.
notes: Sharpened by 2026-05-05 review (3 parallel reviewers). Scope expanded: this is the umbrella for deck-level composition awareness. Subtasks: (1) analyze_deck_rhythm MCP tool returning per-slide {pattern, density_class, accent_role, dominant_visual} + aggregates {pattern_runs, longest_run, repetition_index, accent_balance}; (2) composition_score axis in score_deck separate from correctness — penalize pattern_run>=3, accent_dominance>=80%, density CV<0.15, missing narrative roles (no opening/closing); (3) recommend_pattern must accept recent_patterns[] and prefer_variety bool with decay penalty in scorer (recommend.go:348-406 has no penalty hook today). Refs: cmd/json2pptx/score_deck.go:130-138, internal/patterns/recommend.go:46-267.
close_reason: Implemented composition_score axis in score_deck: runs analyzeDeckRhythm on input slides and emits pattern_run, accent_dominance, density_monotony, and missing_emphasis diagnostics alongside the correctness score. Added CompositionResult types, output schema update, and regression tests.

title: P3-46: Fit-finding `path` grammar undocumented and inconsistent across `repair_slide` kinds
description:
**Labels:** `docs`, `P3`, `feedback-loop`, `api-contract`

**Summary**
Paths in findings look like `slides[2].content.body` (dot+bracket mix). `repair_slide` accepts `path` only on `use_one_of`. For `reduce_text` the target is implicit (slide's first body-ish content). Agents who want to patch "the third bullet of slide 2" have no stable path → fix mapping.

**Fix**
Document the path grammar once (prefer RFC 6901 JSON Pointer: `/slides/2/content/1/bullets/3`). Accept `path` as an optional disambiguator on every `repair_slide` kind; round-trip test it.

**Acceptance**
- `docs/PATH_GRAMMAR.md` published.
- Every fit-finding emits a valid JSON Pointer.
- `repair_slide` accepts `path` uniformly across all kinds.
close_reason: Implemented: JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) path grammar for fit findings and repair_slide. Created internal/slidepath package, migrated all 31 path construction sites from bracket notation to JSON Pointer, added path parameter to reduce_text/shorten_title/split_at_row fix kinds, published docs/PATH_GRAMMAR.md, updated docs/FIT_FINDINGS.md.

title: P3-45: `generate_presentation` response lacks per-slide resolution summary
description:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `P3`, `feedback-loop`

**Summary**
Response (`JSONOutput` at `cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:444-453`) reports `SlideCount` + `FitFindings` array. Doesn't report per slide: which layout was actually used (after resolver fallback), which placeholders received content vs were empty, whether the slide was paginated. P2-11 adds occupancy to `expand_pattern`; the analogous signal is missing from `generate_presentation`. Agents learn occupancy only by calling `preview_presentation_plan` redundantly.

**Fix**
Add to the generate response:
```json
"slides": [{
  "index": 0,
  "resolved_layout_id": "slideLayout5",
  "placeholders_used": ["title", "body"],
  "paginated_from": null,
  "was_synthesized_layout": false,
  "occupancy_pct": 72
}]
```

**Acceptance**
- Agent can audit per-slide resolution without a second tool call.
- Tests assert fields for synthesized layouts, paginated slides, and resolver fallbacks.
close_reason: Added per-slide resolution summary (SlideResolution) to generate_presentation response. Reports resolved_layout_id, placeholders_used, was_synthesized_layout, was_auto_selected, and occupancy_pct for each slide.

title: P3-13: Fit-report should recommend structural fixes, not just text fixes
description:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `P3`, `fit-report`

**Summary**
When `sparse_layout` (P2-10) fires alongside pattern metadata, fit-report should recommend a concrete `swap_pattern` or `reshape_grid` fix kind (depends on P3-12).

**Fix**
Fit-report engine matches `sparse_layout` + pattern name + card count against a recommendation table. E.g. `card-grid` with 3 cells and `filled_pct < 40` → recommend `swap_pattern: kpi-3up`.

**Acceptance**
- ADV AI slide 3 (4 layers, 1 column) emits `sparse_layout` with recommended `reshape_grid: {rows: 2, columns: 2}`.
notes: Sharpened by 2026-05-05 review. Concrete fix kinds to add: (a) pattern_underfilled — when gridOccupancy.filled_pct<50 (already computed in cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:1378-1449 but only emitted in expand_pattern, not fit-stream); (b) pattern_overcrowded — cells > recommended max; (c) split_pattern — for card-grid/iconrow/kpi-Nup/timeline-horizontal, when overflow predicted, emit Fix.Kind=split_pattern with params.first=N1, params.second=N2, params.title_part_2='(continued)'. Currently textfit.go:24-75 only shrinks; no structural-split path. Wire into score_deck and repair_slide.
close_reason: Implemented: sparse_layout now recommends reshape_grid with computed rows/columns when pattern context is available. Added optimalGridDimensions helper. Added reshape_grid to repairFixKinds. Tests cover reshape, fallback, and dimension computation.

title: P3-12: `repair_slide` cannot swap patterns or reshape grids
description:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `P3`, `mcp`, `repair-loop`

**Summary**
`repair_slide` handles text-level fixes (`reduce_text`, `split_at_row`, `swap_layout`) but has no way to change pattern choice or grid shape. When the problem is "wrong pattern chosen," the loop breaks and the agent has to regenerate the whole deck.

**Fix**
New `Fix.Kind` values for `repair_slide`:
- `swap_pattern` — `params: {from: "card-grid", to: "kpi-3up", values: {...}}`
- `reshape_grid` — `params: {rows: int, columns: int|[]int}`
- `set_pattern_style` — `params: {style: "chevron"}` (for P1-7 timeline variants)

**Acceptance**
- Loop can fix sparse_layout → swap to denser pattern without regenerating deck.
- Loop can change timeline style without regenerating deck.
notes: Sharpened by 2026-05-05 review. PREREQUISITE: validate-time wrong-pattern diagnostic must exist first. Today, passing 7 cells to card-grid returns a count error with no swap suggestion (cardgrid.go:194-205 only hints across card-grid/bmc-canvas; kpi_common.go:140-148 only hints across 3<->4). Define ErrCodeWrongPattern; on count/shape failure, run reverse-recommender across the registry against the actual data shape, attach Fix.Kind=swap_pattern with params.suggested=[...] and field mapping. Then repair_slide swap_pattern can act on it. Without the diagnostic, repair has nothing to act on.
close_reason: Implemented swap_pattern, reshape_grid, and set_pattern_style fix kinds in repair_slide

title: feature: get_capabilities MCP tool — schema version and capability negotiation
description:
When SKILL.md drifts from runtime (we1y closed; instant-feedback-audit-2026-04-24 noted this pattern recurs), agents that cached the contract use stale fields silently. A small versioning tool lets agents detect and refresh.

## Tool surface

`get_capabilities() → {\
  schema_version: 'semver string',\
  schema_changes_since: {[from_version]: ['removed:foo', 'added:bar', 'deprecated:baz']},\
  supported_patterns: [string],\
  supported_chart_types: [string],\
  supported_diagram_types: [string],\
  mcp_tools_available: [string],\
  deprecated_fields: [{path, replacement, removed_in?}],\
  features: {strict_fit: ['off','warn','strict'], compact_responses: bool, structured_params: bool, ...}\
}`

## Coordination with tfvv

tfvv (P1, discovery surface convergence) makes skill-info the canonical discovery surface. get_capabilities should either:
1. Be folded INTO skill-info as a new section, OR
2. Live as a thin sibling that skill-info embeds.

Recommend option 1 (folded). This bead becomes 'extend skill-info with version + deprecation + feature-flags' rather than a new tool. If tfvv ships first, this bead's surface area shrinks to a docs+code change inside skill_info.go.

## Why it changes outcomes

- Lets long-running agents detect contract drift without re-reading SKILL.md every session.
- Lets agents gracefully degrade when running against older servers (no compact_responses, no strict_fit ladder, etc.).
- Enables deprecation telegraphing — agents see 'value is deprecated, use text_value' in the response and update their authoring without a forced break (mxec helper).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] schema_version follows semver and bumps on backward-incompatible JSON schema changes.
- [ ] deprecated_fields lists are populated from the same source mxec uses to flag legacy form.
- [ ] Tests: schema bumps require updating capabilities output (lint check).

Effort: small if folded into skill-info per tfvv. Defer until tfvv lands or co-implement.

Found by: agent-native-reviewer + codex-rescue follow-up audit 2026-05-01.
close_reason: Implemented get_capabilities MCP tool with schema_version, mcp_tools_available, deprecated_fields, and feature flags

title: enhancement: expand_pattern MCP tool should run DetectTableDensity on expansion output
description:
The expand_pattern MCP tool returns the resolved shape_grid but does not run pipeline.DetectTableDensity on the expansion. Agents who use named patterns currently must call expand_pattern then validate_input as a second round-trip just to learn the expanded layout is overdense.

Implementation direction:
- After pattern expansion in the MCP expand_pattern handler, run pipeline.DetectTableDensity (or the equivalent shape_grid density check) against the expanded output.
- Append density warnings to the response under a 'density_warnings' field with the same Fix.Kind/Params shape as fit findings.
- Agent gets one-shot feedback: 'this pattern with these inputs will be overdense, here's the row to split'.

Found by: agent-native-reviewer audit 2026-05-01. Closes a top-5 MCP round-trip identified in the audit.
close_reason: Added density check: expand_pattern now runs DetectTableDensity on embedded tables and returns density_warnings in the response

title: enhancement: findings_truncated summary should include top_codes histogram
description:
cmd/json2pptx/fit_findings_collect.go:115-120 emits the truncation summary finding when per-slide budget caps fit-finding output. It currently includes only a Message string ('8 more findings on this slide').

An agent reading this has to set verbose_fit=true blindly to see what was suppressed — burning a round-trip — when the histogram is already computable at truncation time.

Implementation direction:
- At fit_findings_collect.go truncation point, count findings by Code before truncating.
- Emit Params: {top_codes: ['fit_overflow:5', 'density_exceeded:3'], suppressed_count: N} on the truncation finding.
- Agent can then decide: 'oh it's all density_exceeded, I'll split rows' vs 'mixed bag, set verbose_fit=true'.

Found by: agent-native-reviewer audit 2026-05-01. Depends on 8he8 (closed, per-slide budget).
close_reason: Added top_codes histogram and suppressed_count to findings_truncated summary Fix params in both BudgetFitFindings and budgetLocalFindings

title: docs+code: contrast_autofixed finding has no documented Fix.Kind
description:
cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:402 appends contrast auto-fix findings to the result, but docs/FIT_FINDINGS.md 'Fix Kinds' table (around line 202-211) does not list a 'contrast_autofixed' kind. An agent reading the contract cannot programmatically branch on this finding type — it has to fall back to message-string parsing.

Same rationale as d2md (closed): enum completeness matters for agent comprehension.

Implementation direction (pick one):
1. Add Fix.Kind: 'contrast_autofixed' with Params: {original_color, replacement_color, wcag_ratio_before, wcag_ratio_after} and add the row to docs/FIT_FINDINGS.md Fix Kinds table.
2. Or explicitly document that this code emits no Fix (informational only, applied automatically) and update the Fix Kinds doc to call out the no-Fix case.

Recommend option 1 — gives the agent the data to decide whether to override the auto-fix in future revisions.

Found by: agent-native-reviewer audit 2026-05-01.
close_reason: Added contrast_autofixed finding code section and replace_color fix kind to docs/FIT_FINDINGS.md

title: bug: unknown style_id GUID silently accepted by both validate and generate
description:
internal/template/table_style_resolver.go:34-37 deliberately returns unknown table-style GUID values verbatim ('we don't reject unknown values'). cmd/json2pptx/table_density.go:111 already has STYLE_NOT_FOUND machinery for the guide tool, but neither validate (dry_run.go) nor generate uses the index to verify authored style_id against reader.TableStyles().

This is a dual-blind spot, not a validate/generate split — both surfaces equally accept garbage and the agent never learns. PowerPoint may render with a fallback style, hiding the bug from the user too.

Implementation direction:
- Add LookupTableStyleID(authored) (resolved string, *NotFoundError) in internal/template/ that consults the existing tableStyleIndex.
- Call it from validate (dry_run.go) with Code:'unknown_table_style_id', Fix:{Kind:'use_one_of', Params:{available:[...], did_you_mean:'...'}}.
- Reuse the STYLE_NOT_FOUND text already in cmd/json2pptx/table_density.go:111 for messaging consistency.
- Decision needed: should generate also hard-error, or just emit an info-level finding? Recommend hard-error in strict_fit=strict, info finding otherwise (consistent with how layout_id parity works post-fmsh).

Found by: agent-native-reviewer audit 2026-05-01. Lower priority than placeholder_id and fit-report parity because rendering doesn't fail outright.
close_reason: Implemented: unknown style_id GUID now produces structured ValidationError with code unknown_table_style_id and use_one_of fix during validate. Checks both content-level tables and shape_grid tables against template's tableStyles.xml.

title: svggen: JSON Schema authoring for all chart + diagram types (additionalProperties:false)
description: Native pattern schemas enforce additionalProperties:false (internal/patterns/schema.go:48,175; cmd/json2pptx/patterns_cmd.go:457). svggen chart/diagram JSON has zero grep hits for additionalProperties, meaning unknown keys are silently accepted. 15 chart types + 20 diagram types = 35 schemas to author. Strategy: generate schemas from Go struct tags where possible (reduce hand-authoring). Ship incrementally — one or two types per PR — to avoid a 35-file mega-PR. Gated on γ (capability types first) and on the instant-feedback-audit schema-first contract work (go-slide-creator-9dy5, t9zv) landing their JSON Schema foundation.
design: Prefer schema-from-struct-tags generation. Manual schemas only where struct doesn't capture the contract.

- Each chart and diagram type has a JSON Schema with additionalProperties:false

notes: Part of svggen feedback-parity epic. Consensus from 2026-04-24 advocate/devil's-advocate debate over narsil + codex gap analysis. title: feature: MCP list_icons tool (parity with 'json2pptx icons list' CLI)
description:
The 'json2pptx icons list' CLI subcommand returns the icon catalog agents need when setting '"icon": {"name": ...}' on shapes. No MCP equivalent exists — agents in pure-MCP deployments must shell out or guess names.

Agent-native audit 2026-04-24 flagged this as a parity gap (G2). SKILL.md now references 'list_icons' as a target-state MCP tool (see skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md 'MCP Tools' table); this bead tracks shipping it.

## Fix
Add MCP tool 'list_icons' mirroring 'icons list --json' output. Return structured data (category, name, keywords[] for search).

## Sketch
mcp.go: register_tool('list_icons', {category?: string, search?: string})
- No args → full catalog
- category arg → scope to one category
- search arg → substring match across name/keywords

## Acceptance
- Tool registered in mcp.go
- Response schema documented in tool description
- SKILL.md 'Icon Names' section already references this tool; ensure it resolves post-ship

## Why P3
Hygiene / agent-native parity. Pairs with 41ea (table_density_guide). Both gaps flagged together in agent-native audit.
close_reason: Implemented list_icons MCP tool with set and search parameters, mirroring CLI icons list --json output

title: feature: MCP table_density_guide tool (parity with 'json2pptx tables guide' CLI)
description:
The 'json2pptx tables guide' CLI subcommand provides table density reference (font sizes, row counts, width allocations) that agents need to obey Rule 20 (TDR). No MCP equivalent exists — agents in pure-MCP deployments must either shell out or skip the guidance.

Agent-native audit 2026-04-24 flagged this as a parity gap (G2).

## Fix
Add MCP tool 'table_density_guide' mirroring the CLI output. Return structured data (preferred over the CLI's prose format) so agents can key off style_id/template and get back:
- recommended font size range per (rows, cols)
- hard limits (Rule 20: rows<=7, cols<=6, font>=9pt)
- per-template overrides (some templates ship denser default styles)
- warnings / do-not-exceed thresholds

## Sketch
mcp.go: register_tool('table_density_guide', {template?: string, style_id?: string})
- No args → return global TDR table + list of templates
- template arg → return template-specific recommendations + its table_styles[]
- style_id arg → return specific style's density profile

## Acceptance
- Tool registered in mcp.go alongside list_templates / get_data_format_hints
- Response is JSON; schema documented in the tool description
- SKILL.md references the MCP tool (no CLI fallback needed post-ship)
- Test: agent calls with template='midnight-blue' → receives TDR with that template's table_styles

## Why P3
Hygiene / agent-native parity. Not blocking — Rule 20 is already prose-documented in SKILL.md. Closes the last non-icons gap between MCP and CLI introspection surfaces.
close_reason: Added table_density_guide MCP tool returning structured density tiers, TDR limits, and template-specific table_styles. Mirrors CLI 'tables guide' with structured JSON output for agent consumption.

title: docs: HTTP API missing /validate, /skill-info, /data-format-hints + pattern endpoints in docs/api/
description:
Agent-native audit 2026-04-24 found HTTP API lacks agent-native parity with CLI/MCP:

**Code-side gaps (internal/api/server.go:79-89 exposes only convert/templates/patterns/slide-types/health):**

title: investigation: config.Load -config missing-file — clarify intent before hardening
description:
internal/config/config.go:109-118 — os.IsNotExist is explicitly suppressed when loading the -config flag. Defaults are used silently.

Narsil audit 2026-04-24 flagged this as a silent-acceptance gap. Devil's-advocate pushback on 2026-04-24 argued this is likely intentional for Docker optional-mount scenarios (minimal image with config mounted at /etc/json2pptx/config.yaml which may or may not exist).

## Task
Before changing behavior:
1. git blame internal/config/config.go:109-118 — identify the commit and commit message that added the suppression
2. Search issue tracker / commit history for 'docker', 'optional', 'missing config' context
3. Check if the CLI '-config ' empty-string case is handled differently from nonempty-missing case
4. Report findings in this bead's notes

## Possible outcomes
- Confirmed intentional (Docker) → add a doc comment explaining WHY and close with no code change
- Not intentional → file a bug bead with the fix: if -config is explicitly set AND file missing, return error; if -config is empty, use defaults silently

## Why P3
Low urgency. Investigation before code change. Narsil audit 2026-04-24 finding #24.
notes:
## Investigation Findings (2026-04-24)

1. **git blame**: Lines 108-118 are from initial commit (0a53ba1, 2026-04-02). No separate commit with rationale.
2. **Docker evidence**: Dockerfile:84 hardcodes `CMD ["serve", "--config", "/app/config.yaml"]`. If no config is mounted, the file won't exist — the silent fallback lets the container start with defaults.
3. **CLI callers**: generate.go, mcp.go, dry_run.go already gate on `configPath != """ before calling Load. Only serve.go passes `*configPath` unconditionally (defaults to "", so no file read).
4. **No Docker/optional-mount mentions** in commit history or issues — but the Dockerfile evidence is conclusive.
5. **Empty vs nonempty-missing**: `path == """ → skip file read entirely (correct). `path != "" but file missing` → silent defaults (the investigated behavior).

## Verdict
**Confirmed intentional (Docker optional-mount).** Added doc comment explaining WHY. No code change needed.
close_reason: Confirmed intentional: Dockerfile hardcodes --config /app/config.yaml, silent fallback enables Docker optional-mount. Added doc comment explaining why.

title: task: placeholder-not-found drops item silently — emit ValidationError with available[] list
description:

title: task: per-slide fit-finding budget (prereq for render-feedback expansion)
description:
Devil's-advocate debate on 2026-04-24 surfaced a gap in the to8a epic: there is no bound on fit-findings emitted per slide. Without a budget, expanding emit sites to the 14 silent-degradation points in the render path can produce 20-50+ findings per dense deck — the agent burns tokens triaging noise instead of acting.

## Design
- Cap: 5 findings per slide (tunable constant)
- Priority: severity_rank × actionability_rank (errors before warns before hints; findings with Fix.Kind set before those without)
- Dedup axis: (code, slide_index, placeholder) — correct bounded axis, NOT (code, path) which only bounds uniqueness per site
- Overflow handling: emit a summary finding 'truncated: N more findings suppressed, use --verbose-fit to see all' at rank 5
- Opt-out: --verbose-fit flag and MCP capability

## Why this must block the render-feedback expansion
Without this, the payoff from wiring more emit sites is negative: more findings, lower signal-to-noise, agents learn to ignore the channel.

## Acceptance
- Budget enforced in the existing fit-report aggregator (wherever to8a's M2 lands dedup logic)
- Unit test: slide with 20 synthetic findings → response returns 5 + 1 summary, sorted correctly
- Verbose mode returns all findings
- Docs updated in FIT_FINDINGS.md

## Why P3
Blocks Class-A expansion (render-time silent-degradation emit sites) but not P2 contract-side beads. File before starting class-A work.
close_reason: Implemented per-slide fit-finding budget (5/slide default). BudgetFitFindings ranks by severity×actionability, emits findings_truncated summary. Wired into MCP generate/validate + CLI validate. verbose_fit param bypasses. Tests + docs updated.

title: Spike: extend internal/patterns with leaf style-bundle variant
description:
Before creating a sibling internal/stylelib/ registry, prove or refute whether a leaf style-bundle variant can live inside internal/patterns/. Avoid duplicate registries that would fork author mental model and MCP surface.

## What changes (spike only, no commit)
- Sketch a 'pattern kind' dimension on internal/patterns/pattern.go:124-254 registry: existing shape-grid skeleton patterns vs. new leaf style-bundle patterns
- Sketch how list_patterns / show_pattern / expand_pattern (cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go:96-98) would surface both kinds without ambiguity
- Decide: does the leaf variant fit cleanly, or does it fork the schema & validation machinery?

## Acceptance
- Written decision memo in the bead's notes
- Recommendation: extend patterns, OR create new stylelib package, OR reject cross-file entirely and keep deck-local defaults only

## Gate
Cross-deck styles-file work (see deferred bead) depends on THIS spike landing first.

## Anchors
- internal/patterns/pattern.go:124-208 — registry to potentially extend
- internal/patterns/schema.go — hand-authored JSON Schema pattern
- docs/PATTERN_LIBRARY_SPEC.md D13 — schema discipline precedent
notes:
## Spike Decision: REJECT extending patterns with leaf style-bundles

### Analysis

The `Pattern` interface (`internal/patterns/pattern.go:22-54`) is a **shape_grid expansion contract**. Every method is grid-centric:

1. **`Expand() → *ShapeGridInput`** — style bundles do not expand to grids. Returning nil/empty violates the contract.
2. **`CellsHint() string`** — meaningless for styles (no cells).
3. **`NewCellOverride() any`** / `cell_overrides map[int]any` — style bundles have no cells to override.
4. **`Validate(values, overrides, cellOverrides)`** — wrong signature shape; style validation is flat field checking, not cell-count + geometry validation.
5. **`CalloutSupport` / `InlineMarkdownSupport`** — optional interfaces that only make sense for visual grid patterns.

The MCP surface (`list_patterns`, `show_pattern`, `expand_pattern`, `validate_pattern`) all assume grid semantics. Mixing style bundles into `list_patterns` output would confuse agent callers — they expect every pattern to be usable in `slide.pattern.name`.

### What would it take to force-fit?

- Add a `Kind() string` discriminant to Pattern (breaks every existing implementation)
- Make `Expand()` return nil for style kinds (callers must nil-check everywhere)
- Add a parallel code path in `list_patterns` to format styles differently
- Fork validation — styles use flat field checks, patterns use cell-count + geometry
- `CellsHint()` returns "" or "N/A" — confusing in compact discovery

This is exactly the "fork the schema & validation machinery" scenario the spike was designed to detect.

### Recommendation: Keep deck-local defaults; defer cross-deck to a separate mechanism

1. **Single-deck reuse** is already solved by `defaults.table_style` + `defaults.cell_style` (V1, shipped).
2. **Cross-deck reuse** (if token measurement bead `go-slide-creator-09ct` proves material repetition) should use a **file-loading mechanism that feeds into the existing defaults merge path** — e.g., a `-styles <path>` CLI flag or `styles.json` sidecar that loads into the same `Defaults` struct. This is a pipeline concern (load → merge → generate), NOT a pattern concern (name → expand → grid).
3. **Do NOT create `internal/stylelib/`** unless the token measurement shows >30% cross-deck style duplication. The deferred bead `go-slide-creator-g990` already gates on that data.

### Summary

| Option | Verdict | Reason |
|--------|---------|--------|
| Extend `internal/patterns/` with style-bundle kind | **REJECT** | Forks interface contract, validation, MCP surface, and discovery semantics |
| New `internal/stylelib/` package | **DEFER** | Wait for token measurement data (bead 09ct) |
| Keep deck-local defaults only | **CURRENT** | Already shipped; sufficient for single-deck reuse |
| File-loading into defaults merge path | **PREFERRED** (if cross-deck reuse is material) | Reuses existing infrastructure; no new registry |
close_reason: Spike complete: REJECT extending patterns with leaf style-bundles. Pattern interface is a shape_grid expansion contract — forcing style bundles in forks the interface, validation, MCP surface, and discovery. Cross-deck style reuse should use file-loading into existing defaults merge path if token measurement (09ct) shows material repetition.

title: Audit pattern schemas for missing density caps; add only where max_items doesn't already cover
description:
Devil's advocate concern: T5 (per-pattern density caps) duplicates the schema validation patterns already do (max_items etc.). Advocate counter: patterns bypass TDR entirely today; without per-pattern caps, every TDR fix can be defeated by 'pattern: comparison-matrix'.

CONSENSUS: AUDIT first. Walk every pattern in internal/patterns/ and identify which already have density-relevant caps (max_items, max_chars, min_cell_emu) and which don't. Only add caps where they're missing.

## Scope
1. Audit all patterns in internal/patterns/ (card-grid, kpi-3up, kpi-4up, comparison-2col, bmc-canvas, matrix-2x2, icon-row, timeline-horizontal, …)
2. For each, document in a checklist:
   - Has max_items? (or equivalent count cap)
   - Has max_chars per cell? (or equivalent text cap)
   - Has min_cell_emu? (or computed)
   - Has density-equivalent of TDR (rows × cols × font interaction)?
3. For patterns missing one or more: add caps to their schema in internal/patterns/<name>/schema.go
4. Ensure caps emit ErrCodeDensityExceeded (same code as table density schema check)

## Why P3

title: Author→validate→fix loop: NDJSON-driven, anti-thrash cap=2 attempts
description:
Concrete loop semantics for agents using validate --fit-report (go-slide-creator-tme8) to self-correct. NOT a separate binary — this is documentation + a small driver script that any agent harness can adopt.

## Loop
1. Author slide JSON
2. Run validate --fit-report=- (NDJSON to stdout)
3. If any line has action='unfittable':
   a. Filter to failing cells only
   b. Build feedback: filtered NDJSON + 1-line natural-language summary per failing slide
   c. Send back to agent for repair turn
   d. GOTO 2
4. If 2 repair attempts failed for same slide → force split_slide envelope (or downgrade to bullets); do NOT loop further
5. Stop when: zero unfittable AND zero TDR violations AND visual-QA pass

## Why anti-thrash matters
Models will shrink-font→shrink-font→shrink-font forever if not externally capped. AI engineer flagged this explicitly. The cap is a property of the loop driver, not the agent.

## What this bead delivers
- A reference loop driver in tests/quality/loop.go (or scripts/)
- Documentation in docs/ for how to integrate the loop into:
  - claude-code (skill instructs agent to call validate after each slide batch)
  - MCP harness (caller wraps generate + validate in retry loop)
  - CI (pre-commit hook on examples/)
- The loop driver consumes the structured fix.kind from --fit-report

## Acceptance criteria
- Loop driver script that wraps generate + validate + repair signal
- Hard cap of 2 repair attempts per slide
- After cap: forced split_slide injection or fail-loud (configurable)
- Documentation with integration recipes
- Regression test: dense-table-16x6 prompt → 1 author → 1 unfittable → repair → split → valid

## Why P3
Depends on tme8 (fit-report), hbdt (split_slide), eval harness. Document the protocol now so all upstream beads design with this loop in mind.
notes: AI engineer was explicit: 'Models will shrink-font→shrink-font forever; you must externally cap.'

title: Validator: count grid-embedded tables/charts in summary stats
description:
## Problem

Running `json2pptx validate` on a deck with tables embedded in `shape_grid` cells reports `table_count: 0`. Validator counts only top-level `content` array items with `"type": "table"`, not tables inside shape_grid cells. Same likely applies to `chart` and `diagram` cells.

## Impact

- User runs `validate` on a 32-slide PwC deck containing 3 grid-embedded tables → sees `table_count: 0` → assumes deck is clean.
- Skill's Stage 3 "verify tables visually" guidance loses the validator as a signal source.
- The three tables in the deck shipped with truncated rows; validator gave no warning.

## Source

Field report item #18 from PwC deck production, 2026-04-22.

## Fix sketch

- `internal/generator` or wherever the validate summary is computed: walk `shape_grid.rows[].cells[]` and increment counters for `table`, `chart`, `diagram`, `image`, `icon` cells.
- Optionally split the summary: "top-level content: N tables, grid-embedded: M tables".
close_reason: validateShapeGrid now returns gridContentCounts struct with Tables/Diagrams counts. Both validate.go and dry_run.go callers add grid-embedded counts to their summaries.

title: Table: change bandRow default from 0 to 1
description:
When the JSON `style` object is omitted entirely (or `striped: false`), `bandRow` is set to `"0"` in `<a:tblPr>`, disabling row banding. Even if the table style defines `band2H` alternating fills, the table style's banding will not activate.

PowerPoint convention is for tables to band by default unless explicitly disabled.

## Where to change

- `internal/generator/table.go:181-185` in `GenerateTableXML()`:

```go
bandRow := "0"
if config.Style.Striped {
    bandRow = "1"
}
fmt.Fprintf(&xml, `<a:tblPr firstRow="1" bandRow="%s">`, bandRow)
```

Change default to `"1"`. Add an explicit way to disable (`striped: false`) — but this requires changing `Striped bool` to `*bool` in `TableStyle` and `TableStyleInput` to distinguish "unset" from "explicitly false".

## Acceptance criteria

- Tables without a style object: emit `bandRow="1"`
- Tables with `striped: true`: emit `bandRow="1"` (current)
- Tables with `striped: false` (explicit): emit `bandRow="0"`
- Update test `TestGenerateTableXML_StripedRows` at `internal/generator/table_test.go:203`

## Risk

Behavior change: existing decks without explicit striping will start banding. If undesirable, gate behind the new `use_table_style` flag (Issue 4) instead.
close_reason: Changed Striped from bool to *bool to distinguish unset (default banding on) from explicit false (banding off). bandRow now defaults to 1.

title: Spec/code mismatch: INPUT_FORMAT.md documents array chart data format that code doesn't fully support

## Impact
Users following the documented spec will produce broken charts. The integration test fixtures also use this format.

## Fix Options
1. Fix `convertPointArrayToSeriesData` to handle `value` field (see go-slide-creator-bg1j)
2. Update INPUT_FORMAT.md to document the flat map format as primary: `{"Q1": 12, "Q2": 14}`
3. Both: fix the code AND document both formats

## Current State
Example JSONs updated to use flat map format as workaround. INPUT_FORMAT.md still shows array format.
close_reason: Updated INPUT_FORMAT.md to document all four chart data formats: flat map (recommended), array-of-objects, multi-series, and scatter/bubble. Both flat map and array formats are now fully supported by code (via go-slide-creator-bg1j fix).

title: Document shape_grid typography best practices and font size hierarchy
description:
## Problem
No documented typography system for shape_grid slides. Font sizes in examples range from 8pt to 24pt with no consistent hierarchy. This leads to inconsistent, unprofessional-looking slides.

## Proposed Hierarchy (Bain-inspired)
- Slide title: 28-36pt (handled by layout placeholder)
- Grid header/banner: 14-18pt bold, white on accent
- Card title/headline: 12-14pt bold
- Card body text: 9-11pt regular
- Footnote/source: 7-8pt regular, grey

## Action Items
1. Document recommended font sizes in AGENTS.md or skill_info.go
2. Add typography examples to JSON schema documentation
3. Consider adding a "typography_preset" field: {"preset": "header"} → auto-applies size/bold/color
close_reason: Documented shape_grid typography hierarchy in AGENTS.md (quick reference table) and docs/INPUT_FORMAT.md (full best practices section with guidelines and example)

title: Split-column asymmetric layout (text + full-height image)
description:
## Problem
Cannot create Bain slide 8 pattern: left column with text content panels, right column with a full-height dramatic photo. While shape_grid supports 2-column layouts, there's no way to make one column a full-height image while the other has multiple stacked shapes.

## Bain Reference
Slide 8 (Volatility vs Risk): Left = black panel with "Volatility" definition, Right = black panel with "Risk" definition, Bottom left = ocean waves photo, Bottom right = rain/car lights photo.

## Requires
- Image support in cells (go-slide-creator-mc8)
- Row-spanning image cells that fill column height

## Current Workaround
Use row_span on an image cell (once images are supported). The grid system already handles row_span correctly.

## Dependencies
- go-slide-creator-mc8 (image support)
close_reason: Implemented split-column asymmetric layout pattern: added unit test (TestResolve_ImageWithRowSpan) proving row_span + image cell combination works, integration test (TestResolveShapeGrid_SplitColumnImageRowSpan) for JSON-to-domain conversion, and integration fixture (75_sg_split_column_image.json) demonstrating the Bain slide 8 text+full-height-image pattern.

title: Add image-strip layout pattern (Bain slide 14: 5 photos with overlaid labels)
description:
## Problem
Cannot create the Bain slide 14 pattern: a full-width row of 5 photos side-by-side, each with a darkened overlay and category label text. This is an effective visual pattern for showing categories, themes, or risk types.

## Bain Reference
Slide 14 (Myth 3): Full-width strip of 5 photos (UN building, protesters, stock ticker, tech, Arctic ice) with darkened overlay and white text labels below each photo.

## Requires
- Image support in cells (go-slide-creator-mc8)
- Per-cell overlay with alpha (go-slide-creator-ls3)
- Grid row that spans full slide width with image cells

## Proposed JSON
```json
{
  "shape_grid": {
    "columns": 5,
    "rows": [{
      "height": 45,
      "cells": [
        {"image": {"path": "img1.jpg", "fit": "cover"}, "overlay": {"color": "#000", "alpha": 0.4}, "text": "Geopolitical tensions"},
        ...
      ]
    }]
  }
}
```

## Dependencies

- go-slide-creator-ls3 (overlay support)

title: Add accent bar decorative element for section dividers
description:
## Problem
Bain uses thick colored accent bars (red, ~8px wide) on the left side of section divider slides and as visual separators. No native support for decorative accent elements exists in the shape_grid system.

## Bain Reference
- Slide 4: Thick red left bar next to "Resilience" title
- Slide 12: Red horizontal line under "MYTH 2:" label
- Slide 13: Red accent bars under each company logo
- Slide 15: Red accent bars under year labels

## Proposed Solution
Add accent bar support either:
1. As a new shape type: `{"geometry": "accentBar", "fill": "accent1", "position": "left"}`
2. As a slide-level decorator: `{"accent_bar": {"color": "accent1", "width": 8, "position": "left"}}`
3. As a cell border property: `{"shape": {..., "border_left": {"color": "accent1", "width": 4}}}`

## Impact
Low priority but adds significant polish. Section dividers and timeline labels gain visual sophistication.
close_reason: VERIFIED: AccentBarSpec, ResolvedAccentBar, GenerateAccentBarXML implemented. Stress test slide 11 shows all 4 positions (left/top/bottom/right) working.

title: Fix --help flag parsing in templatecaps CLI
description:
cmd/templatecaps treats '--help' as a positional argument (template file path), producing:
  Error opening template: template file not found: --help

## Root cause
The CLI parses positional args before checking for flags. Likely uses os.Args[1] directly without flag.Parse().

## Fix
- Add flag.Parse() before reading positional args
- Or use flag.Usage to provide help output
- Add -h handling via standard flag package (flag.Parse() provides -h automatically)
- Add usage text describing what templatecaps does: "Analyze template capabilities and list available layouts, placeholders, and theme colors"

## Expected behavior
  $ templatecaps --help
  Usage: templatecaps [options] <template.pptx>

  Analyze PPTX template capabilities including layouts, placeholders, and theme.

  Options:
    -json    Output as JSON (default: human-readable)

## Verification
- templatecaps --help prints usage and exits 0
- templatecaps -h prints usage and exits 0
- templatecaps template.pptx still works normally
close_reason: Added flag.Parse() and flag.Usage to templatecaps CLI so --help and -h print usage instead of being treated as a file path

title: Build MCP server for svggen diagram rendering
description:
## Task
Create an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that exposes svggen diagram rendering as AI tools.

## Binary: svggen/cmd/svggen-mcp/main.go

## Approach Decision
Two options were debated:

**Option A (recommended initially)**: HTTP proxy — MCP server wraps the existing HTTP API
- Simpler, no duplicate rendering logic
- Requires svggen-server to be running
- Lower memory footprint (no 32 diagram types loaded in MCP process)

**Option B (later)**: Standalone — MCP server imports svggen library directly  
- Self-contained, no dependency on HTTP server
- Higher memory but simpler deployment
- Better for single-binary distribution

Start with Option B (standalone) since it is simpler for end users (single binary).

## MCP Tools

### render_diagram
Render a diagram to SVG or PNG.
```json
{
  "name": "render_diagram",
  "description": "Render a diagram or chart to SVG/PNG format",
  "inputSchema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "type": { "type": "string", "description": "Diagram type (e.g., bar_chart, org_chart, gantt)" },
      "data": { "type": "object", "description": "Diagram-specific data" },
      "format": { "type": "string", "enum": ["svg", "png"], "default": "svg" },
      "width": { "type": "number", "description": "Output width in pixels" },
      "height": { "type": "number", "description": "Output height in pixels" },
      "style": { "type": "object", "description": "Optional style overrides" }
    },
    "required": ["type", "data"]
  }
}
```
Returns: SVG as text content, or PNG as base64 image content.

### list_diagram_types
List all available diagram types.
Returns: JSON array of type names with descriptions.

### validate_diagram
Validate diagram input without rendering.
Returns: Structured validation result (valid: true/false, errors: [...]).

### get_diagram_schema
Get the data schema for a specific diagram type.
Returns: JSON schema describing the expected data format.

## Pattern Reference
See cmd/json2pptx/mcp.go for existing MCP server pattern in this codebase.

## MCP Transport
- stdio (primary) — for Claude Code, Cursor, etc.
- SSE (optional, later) — for web-based MCP clients

## Acceptance Criteria
- svggen-mcp binary runs as stdio MCP server
- render_diagram produces valid SVG for all diagram types
- list_diagram_types returns complete type list
- validate_diagram catches and reports input errors
- Works with Claude Code: add to .claude/mcp_servers.json and verify
close_reason: Implemented svggen-mcp binary with 4 MCP tools: render_diagram, list_diagram_types, validate_diagram, get_diagram_schema. Standalone stdio MCP server importing svggen library directly. Includes 9 tests covering all tools and error cases.
