title: SKILL.md + repair_slide: capacity-aware repair guidance (paired with reduce_cell_text shipping)
description:
## Why (and why deferred)

When repair_slide reduce_cell_text ships, agents need skill guidance on when to use it vs. rewriting content themselves. Truncation is a fallback; the skill must steer agents toward pre-generation budget awareness as the primary loop and treat repair as a recovery path. Defer in lockstep with the implementation bead.

## What

skills/generate-deck/SKILL.md, "Workflow Phase 4 REPAIR" section:
- Add reduce_cell_text to the repair vocabulary
- Decision rule:
  1. Prefer rewriting content to fit (richer output, preserves meaning)
  2. Only use reduce_cell_text when the agent is content with truncation (e.g., user-supplied text the agent shouldn't rephrase)
  3. After repair, re-validate to confirm zero residual cell_overflow
- Anti-pattern: using reduce_cell_text as a default response to overflow without first considering layout swap or rewrite

## Acceptance criteria

- Phase 4 REPAIR section documents reduce_cell_text with the decision rule above
- No specific deck or content example referenced — generic phrasing
- Cross-link to Text Capacity Awareness for the upstream prevention loop

## Dependencies

Blocked by: repair_slide reduce_cell_text bead (go-slide-creator-qcow).
close_reason: Added reduce_cell_text to SKILL.md Phase 4 REPAIR with decision rules: prefer rewrite > layout swap > reduce_text > reduce_cell_text (last resort for verbatim text). Documented in fix kinds table, common repairs list, and related tools.

title: suggestAlternativeLayout density advisor in expand_pattern response
description:
## Why (and why deferred)

When a pattern's cell density is suboptimal, an agent ideally gets actionable suggestions ('try card-grid 3x2 or kpi-3up'). A small rules table can produce these. Risk: rules tables go stale and need maintenance; the existing pairs_with / SuggestSwap machinery (already present in patterns) covers most of the value.

Defer until we observe via telemetry / agent behavior that the existing density status alone is insufficient.

## What

Add layout_suggestions[] to expand_pattern response when density is suboptimal:

```json
"layout_suggestions": [
  {"pattern": "card-grid", "overrides": {"columns": 3, "rows": 2}, "reason": "smaller cells better match short content"},
  {"pattern": "kpi-3up",   "reason": "fewer items, larger emphasis per item"}
]
```

Rules (initial seed; expand with usage):
- card-grid NxM where all cells <50% density -> suggest smaller grid OR kpi-3up
- card-grid NxM where all cells >120% density -> suggest larger grid OR body_and_bullets
- ~100% density -> empty suggestions (optimal)

Source the rules from a pure Go table colocated with the pattern registry; reuse the existing pairs_with metadata where possible to avoid duplication.

## Acceptance criteria

- expand_pattern response includes layout_suggestions only when at least one cell is non-optimal
- Suggestions reference real registered patterns (compile-time check or test assertion)
- Tests parameterized over density scenarios — no specific deck or template referenced

## Dependencies

Blocked by cell_budgets in expand_pattern response bead.
close_reason: Implemented: layout_suggestions[] in expand_pattern response with rules for card-grid (smaller/larger grid, kpi-Nup) and density-class sibling suggestions for other patterns

title: repair_slide reduce_cell_text — capacity-aware truncation with markdown awareness
description:
## Why (and why deferred)

When cell_overflow findings exist, agents need a programmatic way to reduce cell text to fit. Naive truncation with ellipsis produces ugly output and loses meaning; a proper rewrite is an LLM concern, not engine concern. Defer until we observe whether agents actually need this — they may prefer to rewrite content themselves once cell_budgets are exposed pre-generation.

## What

Add fix kind 'reduce_cell_text' accepted by repair_slide:

```json
{"kind": "reduce_cell_text", "params": {"cell_path": "slides[i].shape_grid.rows[r].cells[c]", "max_chars": 95}}
```

Behavior:
- Read the cell's body paragraph (post-markdown-conversion length)
- Truncate to max_chars - 1 with a single ellipsis character (not three dots — so the displayed length stays predictable)
- If truncation breaks a markdown emphasis pair (e.g., '**bold**' becomes '**bo...'), strip the emphasis markers from the truncated output
- After repair, re-running fit-report on the slide must show zero cell_overflow findings for that cell at the same font size

Truncation is a fallback. Document in the package doc that agents should prefer pre-generation budget awareness via expand_pattern over post-generation repair.

## Acceptance criteria

- Fix kind accepted by repair_slide handler
- Post-repair length matches max_chars (within ±1 char for ellipsis handling)
- Markdown emphasis safely handled across boundary
- Re-running fit-report produces no cell_overflow finding for the repaired cell
- Tests parameterized over content shapes — no specific deck or template referenced
close_reason: Implemented reduce_cell_text fix kind for repair_slide: truncates shape_grid cell text to max_chars with ellipsis, handles markdown emphasis safely across truncation boundary. Tests cover string/object/paragraphs forms, edge cases, and missing params.

title: P4-14: Invert the shape-grid contract (long-term)
description:
**Labels:** `refactor`, `P4`, `architecture`

**Summary**
The all-zero-heights-shrinks-bounds behavior is the source of most sparseness bugs. Retire it permanently.

**Fix**
- `Bounds` is authoritative. Never shrinks.
- Rows declare `min_height`, `preferred_height`, `max_height` (or `flex: number`).
- Engine distributes `Bounds.CY` across rows using CSS-flex-like semantics.
- If content exceeds `max_height`, emit `fit_overflow`.

**Acceptance**
- No pattern needs to know `Bounds.CY` to produce a full-slide layout.
- P1-4 hack is removed.
close_reason: Implemented: inverted shape-grid contract with CSS-flex-like row sizing, authoritative bounds, min/max height constraints, and fit_overflow detection

title: Normalize pattern naming scheme
description:
Registry has inconsistent naming:

- matrix-2x2 (noun-grid)
- comparison-2col (noun-suffix)
- timeline-horizontal (noun-adjective)

Three different conventions for 'N-variant of X'. Consider aliases in registry without breaking existing names. Backlog / low priority — cosmetic.

- Optional: alias table in registry for newer/shorter variants
- Document convention in docs/PATTERN_LIBRARY_SPEC.md
close_reason: Added alias support to pattern Registry (RegisterAlias, ResolveAlias, Aliases methods). Get resolves aliases transparently, List excludes them, Suggest considers them. Registered 4 default aliases (timeline, bmc, matrix, comparison). Documented naming convention in PATTERN_LIBRARY_SPEC.md §1.1.

description:
